AmuletTitan.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Identity "Amulet of Vigor turns every bounce land into a ritual. With two Amulets, a single land drop generates four mana. Primeval Titan finds two more lands on entry and two more every attack. The math gets out of hand very fast." Amulet Titan is Modern's most technically demanding land combo deck. The deck wins by exploiting Amulet of Vigor 's interaction with bounce lands (Simic Growth Chamber, Gruul Turf, Boros Garrison): every tapped permanent entering immediately untaps, so a bounce land that normally costs you a land drop instead produces a net mana surplus. AmuletTitan.mulligan:
Mulligan Framework
Keep
Amulet + Bounce + Land
Any hand with Amulet of Vigor + a bounce land + a second land source is a keep.

engines.title: Titan Haste Kill
engines.body: Cast Primeval Titan (turn 2–4). On entry, fetch Hanweir Battlements + bounce land. Tap Hanweir: give Titan haste. Titan attacks as 6/6 trample. Attack trigger: fetch utility lands — Mirrorpool to create a second Titan token (another ETB trigger, 2 more lands), Boseiju to answer a threat, or more bounce lands for Scapeshift setup. Usually takes 2 attacks to close.

engines.title: Scapeshift
engines.body: Sacrifice any number of lands. Search your library for that many land cards, put them onto the battlefield tapped. With Amulet in play all those lands untap immediately — including bounce lands, which chain to produce massive surplus mana in a single resolution. Four copies ensures you can assemble the Scapeshift line when Titan is answered.

engines.title: Cultivator Colossus
engines.body: When it enters, put a land from hand onto the battlefield tapped, draw a card, repeat. With 6+ lands in hand and Amulet active: each tapped land untaps immediately, produces mana, and the chain draws the next. Creates a massive threat while flooding the battlefield with mana. The GSZ-toolbox line finds it when needed.

engines.title: Amulet + Bounce Lands
engines.body: Each Amulet trigger is a separate untap. Two Amulets + bounce land = 4 mana from one land drop. Three Amulets + bounce land = 6 mana. The bounce land returning a land gives an additional land drop next turn (playing the returned land). This creates mana surpluses that dwarf any other Modern mana source.

engines.title: Highest in Modern
engines.body: CrisMTG77: "The deck has nearly infinite lines of play." Stack triggers correctly (Amulet resolves before bounce return), choose correct lands to fetch, sequence Titan attacks to maximize damage. New pilots cost themselves 20–30% win rate on sequencing alone — this deck rewards hundreds of reps.

engines.title: 3.1% · Specialist Pick
engines.body: Low meta share because the deck requires deep knowledge to pilot. Expert pilots post 55–60% win rates; novices post 40–45%. Best choice for players who commit to learning one deck deeply. March 28, 2026 Challenge first place (8-1 record). Consistent top-table presence at major events.

engines.title: {1} · Artifact
engines.body: Whenever a permanent you control enters TAPPED, untap it. This is a triggered ability — each Amulet is a separate trigger. With two Amulets and a bounce land: play the bounce land (ETB tapped), two Amulet triggers go on stack. Both resolve, untapping the bounce land twice (redundant but both fire). The bounce land's "return a land" trigger is separate — put it on stack after the Amulet triggers, s

engines.title: {4}{G}{G} · 6/6 Trample
engines.body: Whenever this creature enters OR attacks, search library for up to 2 land cards, put them onto battlefield TAPPED, shuffle. With Amulet in play, the lands immediately untap. On entry: fetch Slayers' Stronghold + bounce land (untap both). On each attack: fetch two more lands. This means a Titan that survives to attack multiple times generates 4+ free lands over two turns. The "or attacks" trigger i

engines.title: {3}{G} · Sorcery
engines.body: Sacrifice any number of lands. Search your library for that many land cards, put them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle. With Amulet in play: every fetched land immediately untaps. Fetch bounce lands → each untaps via Amulet, taps for mana, bounce trigger returns a land to hand. A Scapeshift sacrificing 6 lands into the right mix of bounce lands and utility lands can generate 12+ mana in a

engines.title: {1}{G} · Sorcery
engines.body: Look at the top four cards, put one permanent into your hand, put the rest into the graveyard. The key word is permanent — this finds Amulet of Vigor, Spelunking, Arboreal Grazer, Primeval Titan, or any land. Three copies makes the deck remarkably consistent at finding its engine pieces. Discarding the other three also fuels Aftermath Analyst's death trigger, which returns all lands from the GY to

engines.title: {X}{G} · Sorcery
engines.body: Search for a green creature with mana value X or less, put it onto the battlefield, shuffle GSZ into your library. At X=0: finds Dryad Arbor (a 1/1 Forest creature land) — an instant land drop that costs only {G}. At X=3: finds Arboreal Grazer, Aftermath Analyst. At X=6: finds Primeval Titan. Shuffles itself back — effectively a 4th copy of Titan and a 5th copy of Grazer over the course of a game.

engines.title: Bounce Land
engines.body: ETB tapped. When it enters, return a land you control to its owner's hand. The trigger order on stack: Amulet trigger (untap Chamber) is separate from the bounce trigger (return a land). Let Amulet resolve first → tap Chamber for {G}{U} → then the bounce trigger resolves, returning a land. You don't have to return Chamber itself — return a Forest for an extra land drop next turn. This is the funda

engines.title: {2}{G} · Enchantment
engines.body: ETB: draw a card, you may put a land from hand onto the battlefield. Lands you control enter untapped. The "enter untapped" clause applies to ALL your lands, including bounce lands. With Spelunking but no Amulet, your bounce lands still ETB untapped — they tap for mana immediately, and the bounce trigger fires normally. Two Spelunkings means a second effect, but the untap is redundant. Spelunking

engines.title: {0} · Instant
engines.body: Search library for a green creature, put in hand. At beginning of your next upkeep, pay {2}{G}{G} or lose the game. The Pact cost is owed at your NEXT upkeep — if you win this turn, the upkeep never comes. If you Pact for Titan on your turn 3, win via the Titan kill line, you never owe the {2}{G}{G}. DO NOT Pact if you can't pay next turn and don't have a guaranteed kill. Pacting for Dryad or Arbo

engines.title: Amulet + Bounce + Land
engines.body: Any hand with Amulet of Vigor + a bounce land + a second land source is a keep. The Amulet hand snowballs immediately — you're generating surplus mana by turn 2 and have lines to Titan by turn 3. The hand doesn't need Titan, just the mana infrastructure.

engines.title: Grazer + Bounce + Land
engines.body: Arboreal Grazer on turn 1 puts a bounce land from hand directly into play (tapped, triggering Amulet). This effectively gives you two land drops on turn 1. With any green source + Grazer + bounce land + any other card, you're ahead of curve by turn 2. Particularly strong if the bounce land is Simic Growth Chamber (taps for two colors).

engines.title: Summoner's Pact Hands
engines.body: A hand with Summoner's Pact can find any green creature — Dryad, Titan, Grazer, or Colossus. But the {2}{G}{G} upkeep must be paid next turn. Keep only if you can either (a) kill this turn or (b) generate 4 green mana on turn 2 to pay upkeep. Never Pact speculatively on turn 1 without a concrete plan for the payment.

engines.title: No Amulet + No Grazer
engines.body: Hands with only regular green ramp (Dryad, Spelunking) but no Amulet and no Grazer are too slow without the mana engine. These hands develop slowly, hit land drops normally, and cast a turn-4 Titan at best. Mulligan aggressively to find Amulet — the deck is built around the {1} artifact, not around being a standard ramp deck.

engines.title: Turn 3 Kill Available
engines.body: You have Titan + 6+ mana + Hanweir Battlements accessible. Opponents on fair decks haven't set up disruption yet. Execute the haste kill line without hesitation. Don't develop more land or draw cards when the kill is available.

engines.title: Turn 4 Is Safer
engines.body: Against counterspell decks with open mana, develop first: cast Spelunking to cantrip and make lands enter untapped, bounce a land to keep the loop going, and use Urza's Saga to build Constructs. Make them use interaction on non-threats, then jam Titan when they're tapped out.

engines.title: vs Living End / Cascade
engines.body: Against Living End: on the draw, play a bounce land on turn 2, end turn with 8 cards, discard Titan or Colossus at end step. This puts a high-power creature in the GY that Living End would reanimate for them — but more importantly, it extends the game past their turn-3 cascade kill, giving you time to stabilize.

engines.title: T1 Amulet Is the Dream
engines.body: T1 Amulet of Vigor is your highest-impact play. T2 bounce land with Amulet in play untaps immediately and gives you 3 mana on turn 2. That's T3 Titan territory. On the play, mulligan more aggressively for Amulet hands. A hand without Amulet on the play is a T4 deck at best. On the play you want: Amulet + bounce land + any ramp piece.

engines.title: T1 Spelunking Is Fine
engines.body: On the draw you see 8 cards, which finds Amulet more reliably. T1 Spelunking (makes bounce lands enter untapped, cantrips) is a strong draw-side play since it generates card advantage while setting up the bounce engine. Keep slightly looser hands on draw — a Grazer or Malevolent Rumble hand that would ship on the play can keep on draw because you'll find the missing piece.

engines.title: Pivot to Scapeshift
engines.body: Titan countered or removed: count your lands. 7 lands + Dryad of the Ilysian Grove (making all lands Forests/Mountains) = Scapeshift wins immediately. Scapeshift sacrifices all lands, finds 6 Mountains + Valakut — 18 triggers at 3 damage each = 54 damage. You don't need Titan to win. If you have 7+ lands, lead with Scapeshift threat before committing Titan.

engines.title: Dryad + Valakut Plan
engines.body: Damping Sphere or Collector Ouphe hurts the Amulet mana engine. Pivot to the Dryad + Valakut ramp plan: every land you play is a Bolt when Dryad is in play. This is slower (T5–6 kill range) but still wins. Force of Vigor or Haywire Mite answers the hate piece. Spelunking still makes bounce lands enter untapped and cantrips — the engine is slower but functional without Amulet.

engines.title: Urza’s Saga Beatdown
engines.body: Titan answered AND Amulet hated: Urza’s Saga generates 3/3 Construct tokens and tutors for Amulet or Spelunking from the deck. A 3/3 + 3/3 + attack each turn is still a reasonable clock. Green Sun’s Zenith for Dryad makes every land drop a Bolt. This is the slowest mode but it’s real — Amulet Titan can close games with Constructs + land damage.

engines.title: Amulet + Bounce Land
engines.body: The primary speed engine. Amulet of Vigor untaps the bounce land the moment it enters, giving 2 mana from a single land drop. With 2 Amulets, a single bounce land generates 3 mana. This is what enables T3 Titan. Execute this engine first when Amulet is in play. Every land drop with Amulet online should be a bounce land if possible.

engines.title: Dryad + Valakut
engines.body: The damage engine. Dryad makes ALL lands Forests and Mountains in addition to their other types. Every land entering the battlefield triggers Valakut — deal 3 damage to any target. With Titan fetching 4 lands on ETB + attack, that’s 12 damage per Titan swing with Dryad active. Execute this engine when Amulet is disrupted or when Titan is online without haste.

engines.title: Scapeshift
engines.body: The instant-win backup. At 7 lands with Dryad active: Scapeshift sacrifices all lands, finds 6 Mountains + Valakut = 18 triggers at 3 each = 54 damage. Doesn’t need Titan at all. Execute when Titan has been answered twice, when you have 7+ lands and Dryad, or as a surprise finish when they think they’ve stabilised. Don’t Scapeshift below 7 lands.

engines.title: Amulet + Haste
engines.body: T1: Amulet of Vigor. T2: Bounce land (untaps via Amulet = 3 mana). Play a second land. T3: 6+ mana available. Cast Primeval Titan (6 mana). ETB: find Hanweir Battlements + bounce land. Bounce land untaps = more mana. Battlements gives Titan haste. Attack: ETB trigger finds 2 more lands. Swing for 6 + Valakut triggers. Requires: Amulet T1 + bounce land T2 + Titan T3. Real but tight.

engines.title: Spelunking Line
engines.body: T1: Spelunking (makes bounce lands enter untapped, cantrips for a land). T2: Amulet of Vigor. T3: Bounce land + Grazer/ramp piece. 5+ mana available. T4: Primeval Titan. ETB + attack finds 4 lands — Hanweir Battlements, Valakut, bounce land, utility. This is your baseline. Spelunking into Amulet is more consistent than Amulet-first and still enables T4 cleanly.

engines.title: When to Force vs Wait
engines.body: Force T3: Opponent is on a T3 combo (Storm, Goryo’s, Neoform). Race them. Any Titan on T3 is better than a perfect Titan on T4 when they win T3. Wait for T4: They have 2+ open mana and no spells cast (counterspell read). Cast a cantrip on T3 to make them react, then resolve Titan T4 on a tapped-out opponent.

engines.title: Amulet Triggers on Each Bounce Land ETB
engines.body: Each Amulet of Vigor triggers separately when a bounce land enters. Two Amulets in play = two untap triggers per bounce land = net 3 mana from one land drop. The untap trigger goes on the stack before you return the land, so you get the mana even if they respond by destroying the bounce land. Always account for multi-Amulet math before deciding your mana is insufficient for Titan.

engines.title: Dryad Makes ALL Your Lands Mountains
engines.body: Dryad of the Ilysian Grove gives all lands you control every basic land type. This means Urza’s Saga, bounce lands, Amulet fetchlands — they’re all Mountains now. Valakut, the Molten Pinnacle triggers whenever a Mountain enters and you control 6+ other Mountains. With Dryad, every single land drop is a Valakut trigger. This is why Dryad+Valakut wins games without Titan.

engines.title: Titan ETB Finds 2 Lands, Attack Finds 2 More
engines.body: Primeval Titan has two separate land-fetch triggers: ETB finds 2, and attack trigger finds 2 more. That’s 4 total land ETBs in one turn. Find pattern: ETB → Hanweir Battlements + bounce land (untap with Amulet = mana + haste source). Attack → Valakut + another bounce land. With Dryad active, all 4 land entries are Valakut triggers. Calculate your damage before attacking, not after.

engines.title: Titan Keeps Getting Answered
engines.body: Titan has been countered or removed twice. You have 7+ lands in play and Dryad is active (or findable). At this point, Scapeshift wins the game immediately from a tapped-out position. They’ve exhausted interaction on Titan — they may not have an answer for Scapeshift. Cast it as a surprise rather than jamming a third Titan.

engines.title: Amulet Is Hated Out
engines.body: Damping Sphere or Collector Ouphe is in play. Force of Vigor or Haywire Mite didn’t find them. Pivot: Green Sun’s Zenith for Dryad, then play lands. Every land entry is a Lightning Bolt. Spelunking still cantrips and makes bounce lands enter untapped. You can close a game entirely via land-based damage without ever resolving Titan or using Amulet triggers.

engines.title: Everything Is Locked
engines.body: Titan answered, Scapeshift answered, Dryad answered. Urza’s Saga on the battlefield generates a 3/3 Construct each chapter and tutors for Amulet, Spelunking, or any 0/1-mana artifact. Two Constructs attacking each turn is a 6-turn clock — slower but real. This is mode 3, not a concession.

engines.title: T3 Kill Is Available
engines.body: Amulet in play, bounce land in hand, Titan accessible, Hanweir Battlements fetchable. Execute the T3 kill. There is no “better” line. Don’t think about Scapeshift, don’t develop another turn. Amulet Titan’s highest win rate comes from executing the kill the turn it’s first available — not from waiting for perfection.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Midrange-heavy field (Boros Energy, Domain Zoo, Yawgmoth) — your T3–4 kill is faster than their clock. Low Damping Sphere density in expected sideboards (below 15%). Few Chalice of the Void builds in the room. Goryo’s and Storm variants are present — you have good matchups there. You’ve practiced the Scapeshift line so you can switch plans mid-game without thinking.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy Damping Sphere meta — it shuts off multiple bounce land untaps per turn (you can only untap one land per turn while Sphere is in play). Chalice of the Void at 1 shuts off Spelunking and Elvish Reclaimer. High Endurance density hurts Amulet’s GY synergies. You haven’t practiced the Dryad+Valakut line as a backup — you’ll autopilot the Titan plan and lose when it’s disrupted.

engines.title: Amulet of Vigor ×4
engines.body: The deck's namesake and engine. Four copies non-negotiable — Amulet makes your bounce lands tap for mana the turn they enter. Without 4 Amulets, the T2-T3 Titan line is unreliable.

engines.title: Primeval Titan ×4
engines.body: Your win condition. Four copies ensures you see Titan every game. Titan entering finds two lands (Bojuka Bog for GY hate, Cavern of Souls for uncounterable Titan, Vesuva for second Titan activation).

engines.title: Cultivator Colossus
engines.body: 2 as a backup Titan that snowballs with land-play triggers. 1 when your land count is lower and you don't want multiple dead draws. Colossus at 1 copy ensures you find it with Titan but don't see it in opening hands.

engines.title: Force of Vigor (SB)
engines.body: 2 vs Chalice of the Void and enchantment-based hate (Blood Moon, Damping Sphere). Force of Vigor destroys two artifacts/enchantments for free — the pitch cost of a green card is nothing when Chalice is shutting off your deck.

engines.title: Bounce land count
engines.body: 12 bounce lands is the maximum. Cut to 10 when the meta is aggro-heavy and entering tapped matters more than the extra mana. The "Simic Growth Chamber" count adjusts based on whether you need speed or power.

engines.title: Drill the Kill Line
engines.body: Practice T3 Titan kills with different land configurations. If you stumble in G1, it's sequencing.

engines.title: Pact Timing
engines.body: Practice knowing when you can and can't cast Summoner's Pact. One wrong Pact loses the match.

engines.title: G2/G3 Blood Moon Lines
engines.body: They bring Blood Moon. Your basic Forest + Islands still win. Practice finding lines through it.

engines.title: Clock Practice
engines.body: Kill in 20 minutes or time out. Amulet draws can be long — be deliberate and fast.

engines.title: Titan Haste via Hanweir Battlements
engines.body: ETB: fetch Hanweir Battlements + bounce land (both untap). Tap Hanweir: Titan gains haste. Attack. Attack trigger: fetch Mirrorpool + bounce land. Sacrifice Mirrorpool: copy Titan as attacking token. Token ETB fires, fetching 2 more lands. Two 6/6 tramplers = 12 damage + land acceleration.

engines.title: Scapeshift + Amulet Burst
engines.body: Sacrifice 6+ lands via Scapeshift. Fetch bounce lands — each ETB tapped, Amulet untaps immediately, tap for mana before bounce trigger resolves. Generates 12+ mana in a single resolution. Cast Titan off that mana, or finish with a second Scapeshift the following turn.

ARCLIGHTPHOENIX.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "The plan is simple: get Phoenixes in the graveyard early, cast three cheap spells in a single turn, and attack with 3/2 haste fliers that come back every turn. Your opponent needs exile effects. Your spells reload you faster than they can answer." Arclight Phoenix is Pioneer's premier GY-value combo-tempo deck. The namesake card — Arclight Phoenix — is a 3/2 flying haste creature that returns from the graveyard to the battlefield at the beginning of combat if you've cast three or more instant/sorcery spells during your turn. The deck runs 12 one-mana cantrips (Conside
ARCLIGHTPHOENIX.mulligan:
Mulligan
Need: 2 Lands + Cantrips + GY Enabler
Keep: 2 lands, 2+ cantrips, and either Artist's Talent or a way to discard Phoenix (Lightning Axe, Picklock).

engines.title: Consistent T3 Flying Attack
engines.body: Two Phoenixes attacking on T3 is 6 damage. One Cutter-equipped Otter + one Phoenix is another angle. No other deck in Pioneer consistently presents two haste fliers on T3 that come back from the GY for free. The speed and resilience combination is unique.

engines.title: Treasure Cruise at 1–2 Mana
engines.body: Drawing three cards for {U} is what the deck is actually doing. No fair card in Pioneer matches this rate. After one Phoenix recurs and two cantrips fire, your Cruise costs {U} by turn 3. You're drawing 3 cards while they're interacting with one thing.

engines.title: Threats Return From GY Automatically
engines.body: Unlike every other deck, your threats don't die permanently — they come back next turn if you can cast three spells. Single removal spells are tempo-neutral. They kill your Phoenix; you cast three cantrips; it returns. They need exile effects specifically. Most decks don't run enough.

engines.title: Arclight Phoenix — GY Recursion Haste Flier
engines.body: 3/2 flying haste for {3R}. Returns from the GY to the battlefield at the beginning of combat on your turn if you've cast 3+ instant/sorcery spells this turn. You rarely hardcast it — the goal is to discard it via Artist's Talent, Lightning Axe (discard), Picklock Prankster looting, or Consider (surveil). Then cast three cantrips and it's back with haste, attacking immediately. Remove + return cost

engines.title: Treasure Cruise — Draw 3 for {U}
engines.body: Delve: exile cards from your GY, each exiled card reduces the cost by {1}. With 2 Phoenixes and 5 cantrips in the GY (easy by T3), Cruise costs {U}. Drawing 3 cards for 1 mana is the single most efficient draw spell in Pioneer. The tension: exiling GY cards also removes Phoenix — plan which cards to exile (cantrips yes, Phoenixes no).

engines.title: Artist's Talent + Picklock Prankster
engines.body: Artist's Talent: {1U} enchantment, each spell you cast while it's in play loots (draw, then discard). Every cantrip becomes double-filtering. Picklock Prankster's adventure (Pilfer) loots for {U} at instant speed, then you get a 2/2 Flash body. Both put Phoenixes in GY while drawing cards. Together with 12 cantrips, you reliably have Phoenixes in GY by T2.

engines.title: Lightning Axe + Fiery Impulse
engines.body: Lightning Axe: {R}, deals 5 damage to target creature, you discard a card. The discard is a feature — pitch a Phoenix to activate it. A 5-damage instant that also loads your GY is the best tempo play in the deck. Fiery Impulse: {R}, deals 2 damage to target creature (3 with spell mastery — any two instant/sorcery in GY). Your 12 cantrips enable spell mastery by T2.

engines.title: T1–T4 Phoenix Recursion
engines.body: T1: Opt or Consider (surveil/scry, put Phoenix on top or in GY). T2: Artist's Talent, then cantrip (loots — discard Phoenix). T3: Opt + Consider + Sleight of Hand (three spells, Phoenix returns from GY with haste), attack for 3. T4: Treasure Cruise for {U} (5 cards in GY), draw 3, second Phoenix returns next turn. They're at 14 after T3 attack and facing an impossible card-advantage gap.

engines.title: Need: 2 Lands + Cantrips + GY Enabler
engines.body: Keep: 2 lands, 2+ cantrips, and either Artist's Talent or a way to discard Phoenix (Lightning Axe, Picklock). Mulligan: 0 cantrips (can't enable Phoenix recursion), 4+ lands (too slow), or a hand with Treasure Cruise but no way to fill the GY. At 6: 2 lands + 2 cantrips is keepable. At 5: 2 lands + Consider + any spell is fine if you have a Phoenix in hand.

engines.title: Counting to Three Spells
engines.body: Phoenix returns "at the beginning of combat" if you've cast 3+ instant/sorcery spells "this turn." Every cantrip counts. Every removal spell counts. Lightning Axe + Opt + Consider = three spells, Phoenix back. Into the Flood Maw + Sleight + Opt = three spells, two Phoenixes back. Count carefully — going to combat a spell short means Phoenix stays dead that turn.

engines.title: Exile Cantrips, Not Phoenixes
engines.body: When casting Treasure Cruise for delve, choose which GY cards to exile carefully. Exile: spent cantrips (Opt, Consider, Sleight), spent removal (Fiery Impulse), and cards you don't need back. Never exile: Arclight Phoenixes (they need to stay in GY to recur), Lightning Axe (it might be the discard outlet you need). Wrong exile choices cost you a Phoenix activation the next turn.

engines.title: 12 Cantrips + Loot Package
engines.body: 4 Consider, 4 Opt, 4 Sleight of Hand = 12 one-mana cantrips that draw a card and filter your hand/deck. Consider specifically surveil 1 — you can put a Phoenix directly into your GY. Opt scries 1. Sleight sees 2 cards and keeps 1. Together they fill your GY with 4-8 cards by turn 3 while digging toward Treasure Cruise. Every cantrip is also a spell that counts toward Phoenix recursion.

engines.title: 3 Spells = Phoenix Returns
engines.body: Arclight Phoenix returns at the start of combat if you've cast 3+ instant/sorcery spells. Your 12 cantrips + Artist's Talent loots + Picklock's adventure + removal = 25+ instant/sorceries in the deck. Turn 3 onward, three {1} spells means Phoenix attacks with haste. Two Phoenixes in GY: same cost, double the attack. The recursion is free — no mana investment beyond your normal plays.

engines.title: Treasure Cruise at 1–2 Mana
engines.body: After filling the GY in turns 1-3, Treasure Cruise costs {U}. Drawing three cards refills your cantrip chain, finds more Phoenixes for the GY, and maintains pressure long after the opponent has stabilized the board. The recursion loop: fill GY with cantrips → Cruise for 1 → fill GY again → Cruise again. No fair deck can match this card draw rate.

engines.title: Interact and Race
engines.body: Against RDW: Lightning Axe kills Eidolon (5 damage, key target), Fiery Impulse + spell mastery kills most one-drops. Your Phoenix trades unfavorably with combat and comes back; their Swiftspear doesn't. Brotherhood's End (SB) sweeps all their one-drops. You race their clock while removing their threats via your already-necessary spells.

engines.title: Race and Bounce Key Pieces
engines.body: Against Greasefang: race their T3 kill. Into the Flood Maw bounces Greasefang the turn they cast it — the ETB doesn't trigger without Greasefang surviving. Against Lotus Field: apply pressure, Into the Flood Maw bounces Lotus Field or Thespian's Stage. Spell Pierce (SB) counters their setup spells. You're typically faster than Lotus Field.

engines.title: Force Them to Exile
engines.body: Against UW Control: your threats recur from the GY — every removal spell they cast is temporary unless it's exile. Force them to use exile effects (March of Otherworldly Light) early on your smaller threats, then Phoenix dodges the rest. Spell Pierce (SB) answers Temporary Lockdown. Brazen Borrower bounces Teferi at instant speed. Never overcommit creatures into a clear Supreme Verdict.

engines.title: Brazen Borrower ×3
engines.body: 2/1 Flash Flying for {1UU}. The Adventure (Petty Theft) bounces a non-land permanent for {1U} at instant speed. Bounces: Teferi (sends the 5-mana engine back to hand), Rest in Peace (removes GY hate at instant speed), Temporary Lockdown (returning all exiled permanents). The flash flying body also closes games vs a tapped-out control deck. Your best SB card vs any non-creature-based deck.

engines.title: Annul ×2
engines.body: {U} instant that counters target artifact or enchantment spell. In Pioneer 2026: hits Cori-Steel Cutter on the stack (before it transforms), Rest in Peace (before it enters), Monument to Endurance, Artist's Talent in the mirror. The {1} cost is critical — it doesn't break your three-spell chain on mana like a {2} counterspell would. An artifact/enchantment Spell Pierce.

engines.title: Chandra's Defeat ×2
engines.body: {R} instant that exiles a red permanent or red spell (bonus life gain if red creature dies). Hits: Greasefang (the critical threat), other Phoenixes in the mirror, Eidolon of the Great Revel. Exiles rather than destroys — critical for shutting off RDW's persistent threats and preventing Greasefang recursion via Cryptcaller Chariot. At {R} it doesn't interrupt your three-spell chain.

engines.title: Brotherhood's End + Anger of the Gods
engines.body: Brotherhood's End: {1RR} sorcery that deals 2 damage to each creature and each player, or deals 3 damage to each artifact. Anger of the Gods: {1RR} sorcery that deals 3 damage to each creature with toughness 3 or less AND exiles them (preventing recursion). Anger's exile clause is the critical distinction vs Selesnya Company — Voice of Resurgence's token doesn't trigger if the creature is exiled r

engines.title: Fatal Push Ã—2
engines.body: {B} Instant: Destroy target creature with MV â‰¤ 2 (or â‰¤ 4 with revolt). Board in vs Rakdos Midrange (kills their Bloodtithe Harvester, Graveyard Trespasser) and Selesnya Company (kills mana dorks). Revolt triggers off cracking Hearse or fetching. At MV 4 with revolt it kills their Kalitas and Sheoldred.

engines.title: Brotherhood's End Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{R} Sorcery. Mode A: 2 damage to each non-Phyrexian creature/planeswalker. Mode B: Destroy all artifacts with MV â‰¤ 3. Board in vs RDW to sweep their entire creature board simultaneously. Mode A is usually correct â€” it hits Monastery Swiftspear, Goblin Guide, and Eidolon of the Great Revel before they can attack again. Choose your mode BEFORE casting.

engines.title: Duress Ã—2
engines.body: {B} Sorcery: Target opponent reveals hand; you choose and they discard one noncreature, nonland card. Board in vs Lotus Field (strips Hidden Strings or Pore Over the Pages before they combo), Izzet Creativity (strips Indomitable Creativity from hand), Niv-Mizzet Reborn (strips their key multicolor tutor). T1 Duress sets up your entire game plan.

engines.title: Rending Volley Ã—2
engines.body: {R} Instant: Destroy target white or blue creature â€” it can't be regenerated. One mana, instant speed, destroys. Board in vs UR Cutter (destroys their key blue attackers before they swing), Selesnya Company (destroys white lords like Voice of Resurgence). The specific color restriction makes it extremely efficient at answering exactly what threatens you most.

engines.title: Anger of the Gods Timing
engines.body: Anger of the Gods ({1}{R}{R}): deals 3 damage to each creature; they are exiled instead of dying. Your GY-denying sweeper — Arclight Phoenix (2/2) dies to 3 damage AND gets exiled (no return from exile). Board in vs Yawgmoth (breaks Undying chain), Living End (exiles their GY creatures). Mistake: casting Anger when they have 1-2 creatures — wait for 3+ to generate positive card advantage from one

engines.title: 4 Arclight Phoenix
engines.body: The deck's identity card. 4 ensures maximum GY density. More copies in GY = more Phoenix attacks per recursion turn. Never cut any — you need to draw them early to discard them early.

engines.title: 4 Treasure Cruise
engines.body: The most broken draw spell in Pioneer. Fills your hand every turn in the mid-game for {U}. 4 ensures you draw it consistently in the window when your GY is full. Never cut any.

engines.title: 12 One-Mana Cantrips
engines.body: 4 Consider + 4 Opt + 4 Sleight of Hand = the recursion enablers AND the GY fillers AND the draw engine. Below 10 cantrips the deck's consistency collapses. Never cut below 12 total.

engines.title: Picklock Prankster
engines.body: 3 is the reference number. 4 in metas where GY filling speed matters more (GY hate heavy). 3 in metas where the 2/2 Flash body is less relevant. The adventure is always good; the creature side is context-dependent.

engines.title: Into the Flood Maw
engines.body: 2 main is correct in most metas. In UW Control or enchantment-heavy metas go to 3. The bounce is your only main-deck answer to Rest in Peace and Teferi. At 1 you'll frequently not see it when needed.

engines.title: UR Cutter Instead
engines.body: UR Cutter runs a similar engine (Cutter + cantrips + Cruise) without the GY dependency. At ~23% meta share vs Phoenix's 5%, the edge comes from avoiding graveyard hate. If the meta has heavy RIP/Leyline of the Void, seriously consider switching to Cutter.

engines.title: Spell Count Discipline
engines.body: You count your spells every turn before entering combat. Three spells in one turn = Phoenix returns from GY. You pre-identify which three spells you're casting before committing to the attack. You never attack and then realize you're one spell short of Phoenix recursion — you plan the turn before declaring attackers.

engines.title: GY Threshold Awareness
engines.body: You track your GY card count from T1. Below 6: don't cast Treasure Cruise yet. At 6-7: Cruise for {1}{U}{U}. At 8+: Cruise for {U}. You know your GY count without counting — every cantrip puts 1-2 cards in GY, every Lightning Axe + discard puts 2. Running the count in your head is a baseline skill for this deck.

engines.title: RIP Response Protocol
engines.body: When they cast Rest in Peace: you have priority to respond. If Phoenixes are in GY, you cast spells immediately to trigger Phoenix recursion before RIP exiles the GY. After RIP resolves: bounce it with Brazen Borrower or counter it next turn with Annul. You never let RIP sit in play without a plan to answer it.

engines.title: Bounce or Counter First
engines.body: When their GY hate is a permanent (RIP, Grafdigger's Cage): you bounce or destroy it before casting Cruise. When it's a spell on the stack: you counter it. You never cast Cruise into an active RIP — you answer the hate first, then generate advantage.

engines.title: Adding Annul Copies
engines.body: You add Annul copies when the meta has many GY-hate artifacts and enchantments. Rest in Peace, Grafdigger's Cage, and Tormod's Crypt are all answered by Annul at {U}. You run 2-3 copies in heavy hate environments. You add Annul over Spell Pierce when their threats are permanent-based rather than spell-based.

engines.title: Adjusting Brazen Borrower Count
engines.body: You add Brazen Borrower copies (3rd/4th) when control decks dominate your meta. Borrower's Petty Theft bounces Rest in Peace at instant speed AND leaves a 3/1 flash flier. You cut Brazen Borrower when aggro dominates (you need sweepers more than bounce). You adjust based on your expected T3 opponent.

engines.title: Considering Pieces of the Puzzle
engines.body: You add Pieces of the Puzzle in metas with heavy GY hate where Treasure Cruise is consistently answered. Pieces mills five and picks two instants/sorceries — it replaces Cruise's card volume in hate-heavy environments. You run Pieces over Cruise when exile effects are omnipresent.

engines.title: Fatal Push vs Fiery Impulse
engines.body: You adjust your removal suite based on the meta's creature toughness. Fatal Push hits MV ≤ 2 (or ≤ 4 with revolt) — ideal vs small creatures. Fiery Impulse deals 3 damage (kills 3-toughness) — ideal vs medium creatures. You audit which threats dominate and adjust the removal split accordingly.

engines.title: Your Post-Board Shell
engines.body: In game 2, you know their GY hate strategy and adapt. You keep Lightning Axe + discard target (Phoenix) in hand rather than discarding Phoenix to GY when they have hate active. You play as a pure tempo deck until their hate is answered, then pivot back to the Phoenix recursion plan.

engines.title: Your Fastest Win
engines.body: Your fastest win is three Phoenixes in play attacking for 9 flying damage. You work toward this: discard Phoenixes to GY, cast three spells in a turn to return all three, attack. You track your Phoenix count in GY throughout every game.

engines.title: Counter RIP First
engines.body: You always answer Rest in Peace before attempting Treasure Cruise. RIP exiles your GY — Cruise under RIP does nothing. Your priority: resolve the RIP response (Brazen Borrower or Annul), then generate advantage.

engines.title: Three Spells per Turn
engines.body: You track your spell count each turn for Phoenix recursion. Three instants/sorceries in ONE turn = Phoenix returns from GY at EOT. You count before attacking: "Am I casting 3 spells this turn? Yes — attack now. No — hold Phoenix recursion for next turn."

engines.title: Cruise Efficiency Windows
engines.body: You cast Treasure Cruise at 8+ GY cards for {U}. You hold Cruise if you have fewer than 6 GY cards — the mana cost is prohibitive below 6. You build your GY with Lightning Axe discard, Consider mills, and naturally cycling cantrips.

engines.title: Deploy at Their EOT
engines.body: You never deploy Brazen Borrower at sorcery speed unless you need the 3/1 to attack immediately. You flash it at their EOT to bounce their key permanent, then untap and attack. The EOT bounce denies them their main phase without giving them a draw step.

engines.title: G2 Identity Shift
engines.body: In game 2, you shift your identity based on what they boarded. Against GY hate: you board more Brazen Borrower (bounce their hate) and Annul (counter their hate). Against aggro: you board Brotherhood's End. You identify their G2 plan from their G1 play patterns.

engines.title: The Rest in Peace Protocol
engines.body: When they cast RIP: stop and evaluate your GY state. If Phoenixes are in GY, you have until their end step to bounce RIP (Into the Flood Maw) before casting Cruise. Priority: (1) bounce RIP, (2) cast three spells, (3) Phoenixes return, (4) attack. They recast RIP; repeat. Don't cast Treasure Cruise while RIP is in play.

engines.title: GY Count for Cruise Cost
engines.body: Cruise costs {8U} without delve. You need 8 cards in GY to cast it for {U}. Track your GY count from turn 1: each cantrip cycles through 1 card, Talent loots add 1 card to GY, Lightning Axe puts 1 more. By T3 you typically have 5-8 cards in GY. Never cast Cruise before you have 6+ GY cards unless you can afford the extra mana.

engines.title: SB Matches Expected GY Hate Level
engines.body: Heavy GY hate expected (Greasefang/Control): more Annul + Brazen Borrower. Light GY hate (RDW/Selesnya): Brotherhood's End + Anger of the Gods. Your SB is the correct 15 for the current April 2026 meta. Only adjust if you see unusual numbers of Leyline of the Void or Tormod's Crypt.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Godless Shrine = Greasefang (board Chandra's Defeat + Annul G2). Hallowed Fountain = UW Control (board Brazen Borrower + Spell Pierce + Negate G2). Mountain = RDW (board Brotherhood's End + Chandra's Defeat G2). Forest = Selesnya Company (board Anger of the Gods G2). Steam Vents without Phoenix = possibly UR Cutter (board Annul for Cutter).

engines.title: Phoenix Recursion Drill
engines.body: Practice casting exactly 3 instants/sorceries in one turn to return Phoenix. Count your spells: cantrip (1), another cantrip (2), Lightning Axe (3). Phoenix returns. Know this sequence blindfolded.

engines.title: Cruise Timing
engines.body: Practice determining when your GY has 8+ cards for free Cruise. Drill counting: each cantrip puts 1-2 cards in GY, Axe + discard puts 2. Know your GY count without counting cards manually.

engines.title: RIP Protocol
engines.body: Practice the Rest in Peace game state: Phoenix in GY, RIP in play. How do you get Phoenix back? Bounce RIP with Borrower, then cast 3 spells. Practice this line until it's automatic.

engines.title: G2 Hate Reps
engines.body: Practice game 2 with Annul, Spell Pierce, and Chandra's Defeat in hand. Know exactly what each card answers and when to cast it versus holding it.

Floodpits Drowner bounces a permanent on entry and connects for two damage. Aven Interrupter exiles a spell for a turn when it enters. Aang, Swift Savior bounces a creature (yours or theirs) and can airbend permanents to reset value. All w
AZORIUSFLASH.mulligan:
Mulligan Framework
Snap Keeps and Hard Cuts
Snap keep: 2 lands + Voice + any interaction (Seam Rip/Snare/NoMoreLies) + any 3-drop.

engines.title: Deploy on Their End Step
engines.body: Flash creatures can be cast at instant speed — on their end step after they've spent their mana. You untap with your new creature already in play and full mana available. Opponent taps out for their T3 play → you cast Floodpits Drowner at their EOT, bounce their permanent, untap, and attack. They have nothing to show for T3.

engines.title: Always Have Mana Up
engines.body: Because your creatures are flash, you never need to tap out during your main phase to develop your board. Every turn you can hold up Seam Rip, No More Lies, or Spell Snare AND deploy creatures if they don't use their mana. Opponents can never safely tap out against you.

engines.title: High Noon Asymmetry
engines.body: High Noon limits each player to one spell per turn. But your creatures are one spell each — one creature entry puts a permanent on board AND potentially bounces/exiles their permanent. At High Noon parity, your one "spell" does two things while theirs does one. The enchantment is asymmetrically good for you.

engines.title: Aggressive Clock
engines.body: Voice of Victory (2/1 flying lifelink), Floodpits Drowner (3/2 flying), Aven Interrupter (2/2 flying), Aang (2/2 flying). All your threats fly or have evasion. You win through the air while they're stuck blocking or answering ground threats.

engines.title: Permanent Interaction
engines.body: Every creature enters doing something: Drowner bounces, Aven Interrupter exiles a spell, Aang bounces a creature. Plus Seam Rip (counter), No More Lies (counter), Spell Snare (counter 2CMC), Avatar's Wrath (board wipe). You have answers at every point on the curve.

engines.title: Card Advantage Engine
engines.body: Voice of Victory draws on ETB. Enduring Curiosity draws whenever a creature deals combat damage. Wan Shi Tong (SB) draws at EOT if you have the most cards. Ajani, Outland Chaperone generates tokens while gaining life. You never run out of gas because every attack step draws cards.

engines.title: Voice of Victory
engines.body: 2/1 flying lifelink that draws a card on ETB. Every copy is a two-for-one — a body that attacks in the air for 2 damage AND replaces itself in your hand. The lifelink means racing is favored: a stalled board slowly gains you life while you build card advantage. Play this turn 2 on their end step whenever possible.

engines.title: Floodpits Drowner
engines.body: 3/2 flying flash. ETB: target player returns a permanent they control to their hand. This is unconditional permanent removal at instant speed attached to a 3/2 flier. On their end step: bounce their best permanent AND get a 3/2 attacker. Works on any permanent — land, creature, enchantment, planeswalker. The no-gift mode bounces your own permanents (resets Aven Interrupter for another exile).

engines.title: Aven Interrupter
engines.body: 2/2 flying flash. ETB: exile target spell from the stack until Aven leaves play. When Aven dies, the spell goes to the GY (not the hand). This is a Spell Queller — counter their spell AND get a 2/2 flier. Critical: the exiled spell is NOT countered. If Aven dies, the spell resolves. Protect Aven at all costs in control matchups. Don't bounce it with Drowner while it's holding a spell.

engines.title: High Noon
engines.body: Each player can only cast one spell per turn. This is asymmetrically good for you: your one "spell" is a flash creature that does two things on ETB. Their one spell is just a spell. Under High Noon, your Floodpits Drowner = bounce a permanent AND put a 3/2 in play. Their sorcery = just a sorcery. The asymmetry compounds every turn.

engines.title: Establish Presence
engines.body: T1: Land, pass. T2: Their end step → Voice of Victory (2/1 flying lifelink, draw a card). Untap with Voice + 2 mana. T2 on the draw you can play High Noon on your main phase (limiting them to 1 spell per turn immediately). Never tap out on your own turn if you can deploy EOT instead — staying at full mana maximizes your interaction windows.

engines.title: Stack the Board
engines.body: T3 EOT: Aven Interrupter or Floodpits Drowner. Each holds up Seam Rip or Spell Snare backup. T4: If they cast a key spell on T3, Aven Interrupter exiles it (they get it back when Aven dies, but you bought a turn). If they don't, Drowner bounces their best permanent + you now have 4 power flying + mana up for counters.

engines.title: Close with Card Advantage
engines.body: Enduring Curiosity attached to any flier means every attack draws a card. Aang, Swift Savior bouncing your own Voice of Victory resets the ETB draw. Ajani, Outland Chaperone makes Cat tokens + life. The deck doesn't close fast but generates so much card advantage that attrition is impossible. Elspeth, Storm Slayer as the one-of finisher when the board is locked.

engines.title: Snap Keeps and Hard Cuts
engines.body: Snap keep: 2 lands + Voice + any interaction (Seam Rip/Snare/NoMoreLies) + any 3-drop. Mulligan: 0-1 land. 5+ land. All interaction and no threats. All threats and no interaction. You need the threat-interaction balance. Never keep a hand that's pure one type.

engines.title: Your Deployment Rule
engines.body: Your rule: every creature deploys at instant speed on their turn, never your main phase. Voice of Victory at their EOT → you untap and attack T4. Glen Elendra Guardian at instant speed counters their key spell → you keep mana open for more interaction. Spider Manifestation at their combat step creates a blocker before they can attack. You surrender the tempo of sorcery-speed deployment in exchange

engines.title: Your Clock
engines.body: Voice of Victory (3/3 flying, can't be targeted while attacking) is your only clock. You attack with Voice every turn it's in play. Your remaining mana holds Seam Rip (counter their key sorcery), Disdainful Stroke (counter their MV 4+ threats), or Wan Shi Tong activation. Voice demands an answer — board wipe or sacrifice effect. You count their outs before committing Voice.

engines.title: Your Flash Counterspell
engines.body: Aven Interrupter (5/4 flash, ETB counters a spell) is your best single card. You flash it in when they tap for their most important spell — Earthbender Ascension, Sunderflock, Craterhoof Behemoth. Aven ETB counters on resolution, not on the stack — it's a hard counter at instant speed that also leaves a 5/4 blocker. You protect Aven with Tishana's Tidebinder if they try to remove it.

engines.title: Your Counter Priority
engines.body: You maintain a mental hierarchy of counters. First priority: Seam Rip for their key sorcery (the one that wins them the game). Second: Disdainful Stroke for their MV 4+ threats. Third: Glen Elendra Guardian for their key instant. Never waste your best counter on their setup piece when their win condition is still in hand. Identify their win condition and protect that counter.

engines.title: ETB Value Chain
engines.body: Voice of Victory draws on ETB. Aven Interrupter exiles a spell. Floodpits Drowner bounces a permanent. Aang bounces a creature. Every creature entering provides immediate value before combat. The ETB chain compounds: Drowner bounces their threat → your T4 is threat-free → Aven Interrupter deployed safely → exiles their T4 play.

engines.title: High Noon Lock
engines.body: With High Noon in play + 3+ fliers, you're typically at 6/8+ flying power attacking per turn. They can only cast one blocker per turn. Each turn the board state tilts further in your favor. The "one spell per turn" limitation means they can't develop AND interact — they must choose. You choose for them by holding up counters.

engines.title: Enduring Curiosity Combat Loop
engines.body: Enduring Curiosity: whenever a creature with this attached deals combat damage, draw a card. Attach to any flier — Voice of Victory, Drowner, Interrupter. Every unblocked attack is a draw. With 4 fliers and Curiosity, you draw 4 cards per attack step if unblocked. The card advantage in the mid-game is overwhelming.

engines.title: Your Flash-First Rule
engines.body: You never deploy a creature at sorcery speed unless you're closing the game immediately. Every creature you control deploys at their EOT (flash) or in response to their key play. You hold Voice of Victory in hand until T4+ and deploy at their EOT — you untap and attack immediately. Flash discipline is your most important skill; it separates correct play from incorrect play.

engines.title: Your Counter Selection Line
engines.body: You keep the right counter for their deck's specific threats. Against Izzet Spellementals: Tishana's Tidebinder (counter activated ability + remove it). Against Mono-Green: Seam Rip (counter Earthbender Ascension at sorcery speed). Against Jeskai Control: Disdainful Stroke (counter their MV 4+ sweepers). You pre-identify your counter target before the game starts and hold the right mana.

engines.title: Your High Noon Timing
engines.body: You cast High Noon when they're about to cast their key sorcery — the turn they tap for Earthbender Ascension or their board wipe. You don't cast High Noon T3 blindly; you wait for the specific turn it matters. You identify their key sorcery in their deck before round 1 and deploy High Noon specifically when they're about to cast it.

engines.title: Your Wan Shi Tong Activation
engines.body: Wan Shi Tong (5/5 that draws a card when you draw your second each turn): you cantrip on their turn (Opt → draw, second draw triggers Wan Shi Tong → third draw). You generate a 3-card turn without spending your main phase. You protect Wan Shi Tong with Glen Elendra Guardian (counter their removal targeting it). Every cantrip you cast generates one extra draw from Wan Shi Tong.

engines.title: Your Disdainful Stroke Timing
engines.body: You hold Disdainful Stroke ({1}{U}) for their MV 4+ spells: their Sunderflock sweeper, their Craterhoof Behemoth, their Lumra, Bellow of the Woods. You never Stroke their early plays. You identify the one MV 4+ spell that wins them the game and hold your Stroke specifically for that spell. You pre-identify their biggest threat before game 1 and keep {1}{U} open from T4 onward.

engines.title: Your Tishana's Tidebinder Timing
engines.body: Tishana's Tidebinder counters an activated or triggered ability when it enters. You deploy it in response to: Earthbender Ascension's trigger (counter the +1/+1 counter), Lumra's ETB trigger (counter the land returns), or any planeswalker ability. You hold Tidebinder mana ({1}{U}) from T3 onward when their key ability is about to resolve.

engines.title: Tempo Above All
engines.body: Deploy threats while holding up answers. Never tap out completely. Every turn: deploy on their EOT, untap with mana for their turn's interaction. Your threats generate immediate value so you're never "just developing" — every creature is also removing something.

engines.title: Defensive Tempo
engines.body: Against Boros Aggro and Izzet Prowess: lifelink from Voice of Victory gains life while attacking. Avatar's Wrath sweeps their board. Aang bounces their key threat. You're not racing — you're stabilizing. Get to 4 fliers and they cannot attack profitably through your air-defense wall.

engines.title: Aggressive Tempo
engines.body: Against Dimir Midrange and Jeskai Control: you're the aggressor. High Noon limits their development. Aven Interrupter holds their key spell. Drowner bounces their finisher. 12 power flying hits for lethal faster than they can sweep. Counter their sweeper with Seam Rip and win.

engines.title: Tishana's Tidebinder ×2
engines.body: Flash 2/3 that counters a triggered or activated ability and locks it permanently. Use on: Monument to Endurance (locks their recursion), Icetill Explorer (nullifies their combo), Ouroboroid ETB (no 4/4 tokens), Gene Pollinator (no token doubling). This is the most versatile answer in the SB — boards in vs any deck with a key trigger.

engines.title: Avatar's Wrath ×2
engines.body: Sweeper for token and go-wide strategies. Kills all creatures with toughness 2 or less. Main deck already has 2 — SB adds 2 more for aggro matchups. Use on: Boros Aggro (kills their whole board), Izzet Prowess tokens (Stormchaser Talent Otters are 1/1s), Mono-Green dorks (Llanowar Elves 1/1, Badgermole Cub 2/2 survives).

engines.title: Glen Elendra Guardian ×2
engines.body: Flash flying creature that counters spells. The specific counter text matters — check oracle. Boards in vs any spell-based combo strategy and vs aggro decks where you need an extra counter. Provides another flash threat that also interacts.

engines.title: Disdainful Stroke ×2
engines.body: Counter target spell with MV 4 or more for {1}{U}. Efficient hard counter for expensive threats: Monument to Endurance, Sapling Nursery (4 mana), Ouroboroid (4 mana), Brightglass Gearhulk (6 mana), Day of Judgment (4 mana). Boards in vs control, Mono-Green, and any deck whose key plays cost 4+.

engines.title: Settle the Wreckage Ã—2

Board in vs Mono-Red (exile their entire attacking board at instant speed â€” the basic land search is a minor upside for them but completely negates their combat). Exile means no GY recursion and no triggers. Hold up the mana, let them attack, then fire at instant speed.

engines.title: Narset, Parter of Veils Ã—1

engines.title: Linvala, Keeper of Silence Ã—1

engines.title: 4 High Noon
engines.body: The asymmetric lock that defines the deck. Without High Noon, you're just an aggressive tempo deck — still good, but you lose the core identity. Four copies ensures you see it by turn 2-3 consistently.

engines.title: 4 Drowner + 4 Aven + 4 Voice
engines.body: Your 12 flash threats. Each does something on ETB that justifies the tempo play. Below 4 of any of these and the deck's consistency drops dramatically. These are your core — every other slot adjusts around them.

engines.title: Aang, Swift Savior
engines.body: Run 3-4. Four copies gives maximum consistency but you sometimes brick on multiples in hand when you need interaction. Three copies is the floor — Aang's airbend resetting Interrupters is too good to reduce further.

engines.title: Ajani, Outland Chaperone
engines.body: Two copies main is standard. In aggro-heavy metas, Ajani's lifegain and Cat tokens are valuable. In control-heavy metas, cut both — sorcery-speed planeswalkers are slow. Replace with Disdainful Stroke main or Wan Shi Tong main.

engines.title: Seam Rip
engines.body: Three copies main is the consensus. A fourth copy is correct in control-heavy metas where the counter is always relevant. Trim to two in aggro-heavy metas where the 2-mana counter is less impactful than Avatar's Wrath.

engines.title: High Noon Is Underplayed
engines.body: If opponents aren't specifically preparing for High Noon (running enchantment removal or Requisition Raid main), register Azorius Flash. The lock is devastating vs unprepared opponents. If you see a lot of Wistfulness (destroys High Noon) or Reclamation Sage in the expected field, reconsider.

engines.title: High Noon Spell Counting
engines.body: You AND your opponent are limited to one spell per turn under High Noon. Your flash creatures are spells. Casting High Noon + a creature = 2 spells (illegal under High Noon once it resolves). Cast High Noon on T2. Pass. Next spell is on their EOT (different turn). Plan every turn under High Noon carefully.

engines.title: Aven Interrupter ETB Timing
engines.body: Aven Interrupter exiles "target spell" — it can only target a spell on the STACK. You can't cast Aven at sorcery speed and hope a spell was there. Flash Aven in response to their spell: they cast X, you cast Aven in response (on the stack above X), Aven ETB exiles X. Aven resolves, they get X back when Aven dies (to GY).

engines.title: SB Configuration for Meta
engines.body: Heavy aggro (Boros/Prowess): +4 Avatar's Wrath total, +2 Glen Elendra. Heavy control (Jeskai): +2 Disdainful, trim Avatar's Wrath. Heavy Mono-Green: +2 Tidebinder (locks Icetill) mandatory. Confirm your 15 matches the expected room.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Steam Vents/Spirebluff = Izzet (hold Seam Rip for High Noon to resolve). Fabled Passage/Forest = Mono-Green (board in Tidebinder + Disdainful immediately). Watery Grave = Dimir (board in Glen Elendra + Wan Shi Tong). Sacred Foundry = Boros (board in full Avatar's Wrath package).

engines.title: Flash Window Drills
engines.body: Practice deploying at their end step vs your main phase. When do you flash in Glen Elendra Guardian vs when do you commit before they can interact? The answer: always flash unless you need haste.

engines.title: Voice of Victory Attack Lines
engines.body: Practice the Voice lock: they can't target it while attacking. Identify what removes Voice (board wipes, sacrifice effects) vs what doesn't (targeted removal). Know their outs before you commit.

engines.title: High Noon Timing
engines.body: Practice identifying when to cast High Noon. Most effective when they're about to cast their one important sorcery. Too early and they play around it; too late and the damage is done.

engines.title: G2 Counter Wars
engines.body: Practice holding Glen Elendra Guardian + Tishana's Tidebinder + Seam Rip. Know which counter goes on which spell. Wrong counter assignment loses the game.

BANTRHYTHM.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "Every threat generates another threat. Every answer they spend is a two-for-one against them. You never run out of things to do." Nature's Rhythm is the engine. For two mana, it puts a land into play and makes a 1/1 spider token with reach. That's a land drop, a blocker, and a body for Gene Pollinator to trigger off — all from one card. The deck is built around making Nature's Rhythm as explosive as possible, as early as possible. The enablers are Llanowar Elves and Badgermole Cub : one-mana accelerants that let you cast Nature's Rhythm on turn two. From there, Gene P
BANTRHYTHM.mulligan: mulligan or a very slow start.

engines.title: T2 Nature's Rhythm
engines.body: Llanowar Elves or Badgermole Cub into Nature's Rhythm on turn two is the gold standard opener. This puts you two lands ahead of your curve while leaving a blocker. Against aggro, the spider token buys time. Against control, the land advantage converts into more threats every turn.

engines.title: Gene Pollinator Doubling
engines.body: Every token your permanents make is doubled by Gene Pollinator. Nature's Rhythm makes one spider → Pollinator makes it two. Spider Manifestation makes two spiders at instant speed → Pollinator makes it four. The volume of threats overwhelming removal-based decks is the primary win condition against interactive strategies.

engines.title: Card Advantage Top End
engines.body: Quantum Riddler generates card advantage every turn it survives. Mockingbird copies your best creature every attack. Brightglass Gearhulk returns creatures from the graveyard. Against decks that can match your tempo, the top-end card advantage means you win the long game. Ouroboroid is the finisher — two 4/4s from one card is above rate at any stage.

engines.title: Field Is Midrange and Aggro
engines.body: Bant Rhythm's token production invalidates single-target removal. Against Dimir Midrange, every removal spell they spend on a spider token is a two-for-one in your favor. Against Boros Aggro, your board goes wide faster than their threats can kill you. The deck performs best when opponents are leaning on creature removal rather than sweepers.

engines.title: Field Is Heavy Sweepers
engines.body: Mass removal (Day of Judgment, Sunfall, Temporary Lockdown) answers your board comprehensively. If Jeskai Control or Azorius Blink are dominant with multiple sweepers, your token engine becomes less reliable. Also consider alternatives if Torpor Orb is widely played — it stops Gene Pollinator's doubling trigger.

engines.title: Llanowar Elves + Badgermole Cub
engines.body: Both are one-mana green creatures that tap for green mana. Badgermole Cub has the upside of being a 2/2 that can block profitably, while Llanowar Elves is the classic efficient accelerant. Running 8 copies ensures a T2 Nature's Rhythm is consistent. Prioritize keeping hands with at least one.

engines.title: Gene Pollinator + Spider Manifestation
engines.body: Gene Pollinator doubles token creation. Spider Manifestation creates two 1/2 spider tokens with reach at instant speed for 1GG. With Pollinator in play, Spider Manifestation becomes four 1/2 spiders. This combination at instant speed on the opponent's end step, then attacking with eight reach spiders is a common win line.

engines.title: Craterhoof Behemoth
engines.body: One copy as a late-game finisher. When you have 6+ creatures on board, Craterhoof gives everything +6/+6 and trample — this closes the game from almost any board state. Don't rush it out; wait until you have at least 4 creatures for it to be a one-turn-kill threat.

engines.title: Mockingbird
engines.body: Mockingbird becomes a copy of the creature with the highest power when it attacks. In your deck, it most commonly copies Brightglass Gearhulk (returning a creature) or Quantum Riddler (surveil 2 + possible card draw). Three copies is correct — you want to draw it mid-game, not in your opening hand.

engines.title: Mana Dork
engines.body: Llanowar Elves or Badgermole Cub. This is non-negotiable — any hand without a T1 dork is either a snap mulligan or a very slow start. The dork enables every line that follows. On the play, you want this turn one. On the draw, you can consider hands without it if they have enough gas.

engines.title: Nature's Rhythm
engines.body: Tap your land and your dork, cast Nature's Rhythm. You get a land into play and a 1/1 spider token. You're now at 3 lands with a blocker. This is the deck's best turn-2 play. If you don't have it, cast Gene Pollinator (sets up T3 Manifestation doubling) or a second dork.

engines.title: Gene Pollinator
engines.body: With 3 lands and a dork, you have 4 mana. Cast Gene Pollinator. Now every token you make this turn and forward is doubled. If Pollinator is already in hand from T2, you can Nature's Rhythm on T2 then Pollinator on T3 to set up the explosive T4. This is the standard sequencing.

engines.title: Go Wide
engines.body: Spider Manifestation on their end step with Pollinator in play = four 1/2 reach spiders for 1GG. Quantum Riddler starts surveiling and generating card advantage. Mockingbird attacks and copies your best creature. By turn 5 with an uncontested Pollinator, you have lethal on board through most defenses.

engines.title: Prioritize T1 Dork
engines.body: You have the speed advantage — use it. Any opener with a T1 dork into T2 Nature's Rhythm is a keep. You'll be ahead on board by T3. Mulligan aggressively for the T1 accelerant. Don't keep slow hands on the play — your advantage is tempo and you lose it with a slow start.

engines.title: Extra Card Covers for Speed
engines.body: On the draw, you get a free card which offsets being a turn behind. You can keep slightly slower hands because you have more options. A hand with Gene Pollinator + Spider Manifestation (but no T1 dork) is more keepable on the draw than on the play — you have time to cast Pollinator naturally by T3 off two lands and the draw card.

engines.title: Continue Flooding the Board
engines.body: Pollinator is important but not essential. Spider Manifestation still makes two spiders without it. Quantum Riddler still surveils. Nature's Rhythm still ramps. Cast your second Pollinator if you have it, or pivot to casting Mockingbird and Ouroboroid for above-rate threats. Don't slow down — their removal spell bought them one turn, not the game.

engines.title: Rebuild at Natural Pace
engines.body: T1 dork killed means you're back to normal pace. Cast Nature's Rhythm on T3 (their removal + your land on T2). You're one turn behind but still functional. Cast second dork on T2 if you have it to try again. Versus removal-heavy decks, this happens frequently — your engine is resilient enough to function without the dork.

engines.title: Nature's Rhythm + Llanowar Elves
engines.body: Primary engine. T1 dork → T2 Rhythm is 3 lands by T2 plus a spider. Everything else in the deck is enabled by this ramp. Cast this before anything else. This is the sequencing priority above all other considerations.

engines.title: Gene Pollinator + Spider Manifestation
engines.body: Token doubling engine. Pollinator in play means each Manifestation makes 4 spiders instead of 2. Each additional Nature's Rhythm trigger also creates 2 spiders instead of 1. This is the volume engine that buries opponents in bodies.

engines.title: Quantum Riddler + Mockingbird
engines.body: Card advantage engine. Quantum Riddler surveil 2 every turn it attacks — filtering your draws, filling the graveyard. Mockingbird copies Riddler on attack for double surveil. Once these are online, you generate more card advantage per turn than the opponent can burn resources answering.

engines.title: Standard Kill: Turn 5
engines.body: T1: Dork. T2: Nature's Rhythm (3 lands, 1 spider). T3: Gene Pollinator (4 lands). T4: Spider Manifestation EOT → 4 spiders total. T5: Attack with 4 spiders + Pollinator + original spider = lethal vs most life totals. Add Craterhoof for a turn earlier if board is large enough.

engines.title: Craterhoof Kill: Turn 4
engines.body: T1: Dork. T2: Nature's Rhythm (2 spiders with Pollinator on T3 setup). T3: Gene Pollinator + second Nature's Rhythm (2 more spiders = 4 total). T4: Craterhoof with 5 creatures → each gets +5/+5 trample. 4 spiders × 6/7 + Pollinator + Hoof = 40+ damage. This line requires both Natures Rhythms.

engines.title: Nature's Rhythm Puts a Land Into Play Tapped
engines.body: Nature's Rhythm says "search your library for a basic land card and put it onto the battlefield tapped." The land enters TAPPED. You cannot use it the turn you play Nature's Rhythm for mana. Plan your mana accordingly — if you cast Rhythm with 2 mana and need 3 to cast Pollinator immediately after, you're one short. The ramp is for NEXT turn, not the same turn.

engines.title: Gene Pollinator Triggers on Token CREATION
engines.body: Gene Pollinator creates an additional token whenever a non-token creature you control creates one or more tokens. This means: Nature's Rhythm (creates 1 spider → Pollinator creates 1 more = 2 total). Spider Manifestation (creates 2 spiders → Pollinator creates 2 more = 4 total). Pollinator does NOT trigger off tokens you copy or tokens created by the tokens themselves — only from non-token creatur

engines.title: Mockingbird Copies on Attack — Checks at That Moment
engines.body: Mockingbird becomes a copy of the creature with the highest power among creatures you control when it attacks. This is checked at the moment of attack declaration, not at end of combat. If you attack with Mockingbird and a 5/5, Mockingbird becomes a 5/5 copy. If that creature later leaves the battlefield during combat, Mockingbird keeps the copy for that turn. You can attack with Mockingbird befor

engines.title: They Have Open Mana and Cards in Hand
engines.body: Three mana open + two cards in hand vs. your go-wide board = likely Seam Rip for your Pollinator or a sweeper. Slow down, bait the interaction with a lower-value card first, then commit your Pollinator when they've tapped out or used the counter.

engines.title: They've Spent Their Interaction
engines.body: Once they've tapped out or used their last counterspell, go full speed. Cast Pollinator, follow with Manifestation immediately, attack for as much as possible. The window after they've spent their interaction is your strongest attacking position.

engines.title: Oko, Lorwyn Liege ×2
engines.body: Best card in the 15. Comes in vs control and any midrange matchup where Pollinator gets answered repeatedly. Oko generates continuous value, grows your board, and requires multiple answers. Board him whenever you expect a long game.

engines.title: Rest in Peace ×2
engines.body: Vs graveyard-based strategies. NOTE: RiP exiles YOUR graveyard too, shutting off Brightglass Gearhulk's recursion. When boarding in RiP, cut Gearhulk simultaneously. Don't run both in the same configuration.

engines.title: Sage of the Skies ×2
engines.body: Flying blocker and clock. Boards in vs aggro with aerial threats (Izzet Prowess, Boros fliers). Also valuable vs control — they can't counter as efficiently vs two separate threats on sequential turns.

engines.title: Spider-Sense ×2 · Surrak ×1 · Focus Fire ×1
engines.body: Flexible hate. Spider-Sense for interaction-heavy matchups. Surrak, Elusive Hunter gives hexproof to protect your key threat. Focus Fire removes a blocker or walker. Evaluate based on what their deck specifically does.

engines.title: Meltstrider's Resolve
engines.body: Most situational singleton. Only keeps a permanent alive once. Comes out in almost every SB configuration unless you're specifically worried about a single removal spell on a must-protect permanent.

engines.title: Bounce Off
engines.body: Only relevant when you need to protect a key play at instant speed. Out vs aggro (they run out of threats, not spells) and vs heavy removal (too narrow).

engines.title: Llanowar Elves / Badgermole Cub
engines.body: Vs heavy-sweeper control, dorks become liabilities late. They die to sweepers and are bad topdecks. Trim 2–3 copies when boarding expensive threats that don't need T2 acceleration.

engines.title: Pollinator Wasp Synergies
engines.body: Pollinator Wasp creates a 1/1 Insect token each time you create one or more tokens. Your entire token strategy chains through Wasp: Spider Manifestation creates a Spider token → Wasp creates an Insect → both enter → Wasp triggers again for each? No — Wasp triggers once per token-creation event. One Spider Manifestation = one Wasp trigger. You chain: Spider Manifestation (Spider + Insect) → second

engines.title: Seam Rip vs Sorceries
engines.body: Seam Rip ({1}{U}) counters target sorcery spell. Your surgical counter vs sorcery-based win conditions: Earthbender Ascension (MV 2 sorcery), Sunderflock (your own sweeper is a sorcery), Sunfall (opponent sweeper). Crucially, Seam Rip ONLY hits sorceries — it cannot counter instants. Know your targets before boarding: Izzet Prowess runs all instants, so Seam Rip is dead against them.

engines.title: Midrange and Aggro Are Dominant
engines.body: Bant Rhythm is built to beat creature strategies with targeted removal. When the field is Dimir Midrange + Boros Aggro + Mono-Green, you're favored in the two biggest matchups and even in the mirror. Register when you expect a ground-based metagame.

engines.title: Multiple Mass Removal Decks Are Present
engines.body: If Jeskai Control, Azorius Blink, and White Aggro with Temporary Lockdown are all above 15% combined, your token strategy faces multiple angles of sweeper hate. Reconsider or heavily adjust the sideboard for sweeper resilience.

engines.title: Archdruid's Charm
engines.body: Flexible green modal spell — can ramp, remove artifacts, or put a creature directly into play. The 2nd copy of Masaya Hoshino's Top64 Turin list ran 2 copies. Consider adding if control is heavy in your expected field.

engines.title: Keen-Eyed Curator
engines.body: Also seen in Turin Top64 lists. Provides card selection and resilience — if your board gets swept, Curator helps rebuild faster. The 2nd Hoshino list ran 2 copies main. Worth testing if sweepers are prevalent.

engines.title: Ygra, Eater of All
engines.body: Appeared as a 1-of SB in some Turin lists. A powerful top-end threat that generates tokens on creature deaths — both yours and theirs. Excellent in long attrition games. Consider replacing Insidious Fungus or Focus Fire.

engines.title: The 8 Dorks (4+4)
engines.body: The consistency of T1 mana acceleration is fundamental. Dropping below 8 dorks reduces the frequency of the T2 Nature's Rhythm line from high to low. The deck has a specific speed requirement — don't compromise it.

engines.title: Craterhoof Behemoth
engines.body: The 1-of finisher that wins games you otherwise can't. Against decks that can match your token volume, Craterhoof is the trump card that ends the game in one attack. Worth the slot as a singleton.

engines.title: Pollinator Doubling Math
engines.body: Nature's Rhythm + Pollinator = 2 spiders. Manifestation + Pollinator = 4 spiders. Two Manifestations + Pollinator = 8 spiders. One more Nature's Rhythm = 10 total. Know these numbers instantly — they determine combat math every game.

engines.title: Craterhoof Kill Thresholds
engines.body: 5 creatures → each gets +5/+5 trample. 6 creatures → +6/+6. Count it out: 4 spiders (1/2+5/5=6/7) + Pollinator (3/3+5/5=8/8) + another creature + Hoof itself = massive trample damage. Memorize the 5-creature and 6-creature scenarios.

engines.title: Basic Land Count
engines.body: You need at least 5 basics for Nature's Rhythm to reliably find lands. Count your basics: you should have 1 Forest main deck plus basics from Hushwood Verge and Willowrush Verge fetching. Ensure the count is correct before submitting the decklist.

engines.title: SB Configuration for Expected Field
engines.body: Check the current meta breakdown. If Dimir Midrange > 15%: make sure Oko ×2 + Spider-Sense ×2 are in the 15. If Control > 10%: Rest in Peace ×2 + Oko ×2 mandatory. Confirm your 15 matches the expected room, not the average room.

engines.title: Pollinator Token Chains
engines.body: Practice the token chain: each token creates another, which creates another. How many tokens do you generate from a single Pollinator + Spider Manifestation? Count the chain and know it cold.

engines.title: Craterhoof Math
engines.body: Practice Craterhoof lethal calculations. With 5 creatures and Hoof: all get +5/+5 and trample. At 20 life, what board state kills them? Know this without calculating at the table.

engines.title: Spider Flash Timing
engines.body: Practice deploying Spider Manifestation at their end step vs your main phase. When do you deploy early to block vs late to create a surprise blocker? The flash timing is what makes this card good.

engines.title: Grindy Matchup Mode
engines.body: Practice switching to Oko, Lorwyn Liege mode when Pollinator lines are blocked. Oko generates threats passively â€” know when to pivot from aggressive to attrition.

BorosAggro.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Overview "The core plan: play creatures that ping the opponent when other creatures enter, attach Warleader's Call for a +1/+1 anthem and extra ETB pings, and overwhelm them with Warrior tokens before they can stabilize." Boros Aggro (also called Boros Pingers or Boros Tokens) is Tier B at 55.4% win rate across 8,800 BO3 games — the 3rd-most popular deck at 7% meta share. It is the 3rd most common opponent you'll face at Cincinnati. The plan is deceptively linear: every creature that enters the battlefield pings the opponent for 1 damage (or 4 with Ojer Axonil active), Warleade
BorosAggro.mulligan: Mulligan rule: Keep any 7 with a 1-drop + a 2-drop.

engines.title: ETB Damage
engines.body: Shocking Sharpshooter pings opponent for 1 when any creature you control enters. Warleader's Call enchantment does the same (1 damage per creature ETB). Stack both: each creature ETB deals 2 damage (or 8 with Ojer). Fanatical Firebrand entering pings for 2. Then it hasted attacks for 2. Then it dies to trade with a blocker and you {T} sacrifice it to deal 1 more. All noncombat, all going to face.

engines.title: Mobilize + Start Your Engines
engines.body: Voice of Victory Mobilize 2: attacking creates two 1/1 Warriors. Stadium Headliner Mobilize 1: attacking creates one 1/1 Warrior. Howlsquad Heavy creates a Goblin token each combat (Start Your Engines). Each token ETB triggers Sharpshooter and Call. A single attack with Voice + Stadium + Heavy can create 4 creature ETBs dealing 4–16 noncombat damage before a single point of combat damage.

engines.title: Ojer Axonil
engines.body: Ojer Axonil, Deepest Might : 4/4 Legendary God with trample. Red noncombat damage you deal becomes at least 4. One Sharpshooter ping with Ojer = 4 damage instead of 1. Warleader's Call trigger = 4 instead of 1. An attack with 4 creatures creating 4 tokens = 8 ETB triggers × 4 damage = 32 noncombat damage in one attack step. Also: when Ojer dies, it returns transformed as Temple of Power — a land t

The "target opponent" clause means you choose — direct to face. Every token, every creature ETB pings face. Stack Sharpshooter + Warleader's Call: each creature ETB = 2 damage. Stack with Raphael: 3 damage. Stack Ojer: each of those 1-damage instances becomes 4. Multiple S

engines.body: {1}{R}{W} Enchantment. Creatures you control get +1/+1. Whenever a creature you control enters, this enchantment deals 1 damage to each opponent. The global +1/+1 makes all your tokens relevant in combat. The ETB ping amplifies with Ojer — each new creature entering with Warleader's Call + Ojer = 4 damage to face. With 2 Sharpshooters + Warleader's Call + Ojer, each creature entering = 12 noncomba

engines.body: {3}{R} 4/4 Legendary God, Trample. Red noncombat damage sources deal at least 4 instead of less. ETB/ping damage of 1 becomes 4. His death trigger: returns transformed as Temple of Power (land that can untransform with {2}{R}{T} after dealing 4+ noncombat). He's nearly impossible to permanently kill. Even when removed, he comes back as a land that re-transforms on the next attack step where your p

engines.body: Voice: {1}{W} 1/3 Human Bard. Mobilize 2: whenever attacks, create 2 tapped attacking 1/1 Warrior tokens. Opponents can't cast spells your turn. Each attack = 2 Warrior ETBs = 2 Sharpshooter pings + 2 Call pings = 4 noncombat damage before combat. Howlsquad Heavy: {2}{R} 2/3 Goblin.
