engines.body: {1}{R} 1/3 Legendary TMNT. Alliance — whenever another creature you control enters, Raphael deals 1 damage to target opponent. Another ping trigger per creature ETB. With Sharpshooter + Call + Raphael: each creature entering = 3 damage. Stack with Ojer: each creature = 12 damage (3 × 4). The 1/3 body also blocks profitably against aggressive decks and the Alliance trigger is creatures you control

engines.title: Burst Lightning / Torch the Tower / Seam Rip
engines.body: Burst Lightning: 2 damage or 4 kicked. Cheap prowess trigger and removal or reach. Torch the Tower: {R} instant, 2 damage bargained = 3 + scry 1, exile on death. Exiling matters — stops GY recursion and ensures killed creatures don't come back. Seam Rip: {1}{W} enchantment. Exile target nonland permanent with MV ≤ 2 until Seam Rip leaves. The delayed exile that returns when Seam Rip leaves — used

engines.title: Stadium Headliner
engines.body: {1}{R} 1/1 Goblin Warrior. Mobilize 1: whenever attacks, create 1 tapped attacking 1/1 Warrior token. Sacrifice for {1}{R}: deal damage = number of creatures you control to a creature. The token creation triggers Sharpshooter, Call, and Raphael. The sacrifice ability is a significant source of noncombat damage: with 8 creatures and Ojer active, sacrifice Stadium for 32 damage to one creature (or e

engines.title: Dalkovan Encampment
engines.body: Land: enters tapped unless you control Swamp or Mountain. {T}: {W}. {2}{W}{T}: whenever you attack this turn, create two 1/1 red Warrior tokens tapped and attacking. The activated land provides additional token ETBs that trigger Sharpshooter, Call, and Raphael — all without using a card from hand. In mid-game when your hand is depleted, Dalkovan Encampment generates 2 creature ETB triggers per tur

engines.title: Ping Engine Online
engines.body: T1: Fanatical Firebrand (haste 1/1, pings opponent next turn). T2: Shocking Sharpshooter. When Firebrand swings on T2, it pings for 1 (Sharpshooter trigger). Add Warleader's Call on T2 instead for the +1/+1 anthem — now T3 creatures ETB for 2 noncombat damage each. The T2 decision: Sharpshooter (better value with upcoming ETBs) vs Warleader's Call (+1/+1 for faster attacks).

engines.title: Token Generation
engines.body: Voice of Victory attacking creates 2 Warriors (2 ETBs = 2-4 pings). Howlsquad Heavy creates 1 Goblin at beginning of combat (1 more ETB). Stadium Headliner creates 1 Warrior on attack. On T3 with Sharpshooter + Call + all three attackers: 4 ETB triggers = 8 noncombat damage before combat damage. That's often lethal by T4 without Ojer.

engines.title: Ojer or Lethal Math
engines.body: Ojer Axonil on T4: every subsequent ETB ping is now 4 damage minimum. T5 attack with Voice + Stadium + Heavy: 4 ETBs = 16 noncombat damage + combat. Alternatively: at 8 life or less, calculate burn to face. Burst Lightning kicked = 4. Sear = 4. Sacrifice Stadium Headliner: deal damage = creature count. With 8 creatures and Ojer: 8 × 4 = 32 to one creature, or enough to close at face in noncombat.

engines.title: Potential Damage Per ETB
engines.body: Sharpshooter #1: 1→4 damage. Sharpshooter #2: 1→4 damage. Warleader's Call: 1→4 damage. Raphael: 1→4 damage. Total per creature ETB with 2 Sharpshooters + Call + Raphael + Ojer: 16 noncombat damage per creature that enters. This is why Boros Aggro kills out of nowhere — tokens entering the battlefield on the attack step deal 16 damage each before any combat damage resolves.

engines.title: One Attack Step Math
engines.body: Voice attacks → Creates 2 Warriors → Each Warrior ETB deals 4 (Sharpshooter) + 4 (Call) = 8 per token → 2 tokens = 16 damage. Simultaneously: Voice deals its combat damage. Howlsquad creates its Goblin → another 8 damage. Stadium creates its Warrior → another 8 damage. Total noncombat damage from one attack step with Ojer active: 32+ noncombat damage, all going to face.

engines.title: Your T1-T3 Goal
engines.body: You attack on turns 1, 2, and 3. T1: deploy a 1-drop and attack. T2: deploy a 2-drop and attack with both. T3: deploy another threat and attack with everything. You maintain constant attack pressure — if they don't block, you take free damage. If they do block, you trade and deploy your next threat. You never wait for a perfect board state; you attack with what you have.

engines.title: Monstrous Rage Line
engines.body: Your winning burst: Escape Tunnel + Monstrous Rage on your best attacker. Escape Tunnel makes the creature unblockable until EOT. Monstrous Rage gives double strike and +2/+1. A 3/3 with double strike deals 6 unblocked. You hold this combination for the kill — not for tempo trades in the mid-game. Identify the exact life total where this is lethal before committing.

engines.title: Your Aggression Rule
engines.body: You attack every turn with your full attack. You don't block unless taking the damage puts you in a losing position. You don't develop your board at the cost of your attack step. Your clock is faster than theirs — you trade time for damage. Every turn you spend not attacking is a turn they spend drawing answers. You are always the aggressor.

engines.title: Your Reset Protocol
engines.body: After their sweeper, you immediately deploy your next threat. You don't slow down after a wipe — you accelerate. Your hand refills via Sunfall's incubate tokens (you choose which to take). You flip incubate tokens into 2/2 artifacts to re-establish board presence. You treat a sweeper as a speed bump, not a game-ending event. Your deck runs enough threats to rebuild faster than they can re-stabiliz

engines.title: Layer Your Triggers
engines.body: Each trigger source stacks independently. Sharpshooter #1 + Sharpshooter #2 + Warleader's Call + Raphael = 4 separate "1 damage" triggers per creature ETB. With Ojer: 4 triggers × 4 damage = 16 per ETB. The deck plays 4 Sharpshooter and 4 Warleader's Call to ensure multiple trigger sources are in play simultaneously. Even without Ojer, 4 triggers × 1 damage = 4 per ETB is significant across an att

engines.title: Attack-Step ETBs
engines.body: Tokens trigger on ENTERING — not just on ETB from a spell. Mobilize tokens (Voice, Stadium) enter "tapped and attacking" during your attack step. They trigger all ping sources simultaneously as they enter. Howlsquad's "beginning of combat" trigger creates a Goblin before attackers are declared — that Goblin also triggers pings before attacks are declared. Dalkovan Encampment creates more tokens on

engines.title: Go Wide + Ping to Face
engines.body: Their interactive tools (removal, counters) trade one-for-one, but you generate tokens that are inherently two-for-one (a 1/1 token that pings for 4). Deploy the Ojer + pinger + token plan as fast as possible. Force them to spend removal on Ojer and Sharpshooter — their hand empties before you run out of ETBs.

engines.title: Race Noncombat Damage
engines.body: In aggro mirrors, your noncombat damage plan is more consistent than their attack damage plan. Don't overextend into their sweepers — keep 2-3 key pieces rather than flooding the board. A Sharpshooter + Ojer is enough damage output to win the race even if they're trading creatures with you in combat.

engines.title: Activate Encampment → Declare Attackers (Voice)
engines.body: Activate Dalkovan Encampment BEFORE declaring attackers — its activation creates Warriors "whenever you attack this turn," but the activation itself happens before the attack step. Then declare Voice + all attackers. Voice creates 2 Warriors (they can't respond). Encampment creates 2 more Warriors (they still can't respond). That's 4 total ETBs generating 12-16 noncombat damage all while they sit

engines.title: Their Response Windows
engines.body: They must use all removal BEFORE your attack step begins. If they held Floodpits Drowner specifically to tap your board, they need to do it before Voice attacks — once Voice attacks, they can't flash it in. Smart opponents will try to flash in Drowner during your pre-combat main phase (after you've deployed Ojer but before you attack). If you see them leave {2}{U} open, consider not attacking with

engines.title: Heavy Creates Goblin → ETB Pings → Declare Attackers
engines.body: Beginning of combat: Heavy's trigger goes on the stack. Goblin enters. Sharpshooter, Call, and Raphael all trigger (ETB pings). Resolve all triggers. THEN you declare attackers including the Goblin (it has haste from Heavy's "other Goblins have haste"). The Goblin is already in play, already dealt noncombat damage, and it attacks in the same step. This is one ETB trigger PLUS an attacker all from

engines.body: Heavy's Max Speed ability: {T}: add {R} for each Goblin you control. With 4 Goblins in play (including tokens from previous turns), Heavy taps for {R}{R}{R}{R}. engines.title: Voice of Victory count
engines.body: 3 vs 4 is the key question. 4 copies in any field with multiple creature-based decks (Voice attacks through all of them). 3 copies when you expect sweepers from multiple opponents — Voice costs 5 and dies to Sunfall.

engines.title: Monstrous Rage + Tunnel
engines.body: Practice Monstrous Rage + Escape Tunnel kill. Double strike means the creature deals damage twice. Calculate lethal before attacking.

engines.title: T1 Invasion Timing
engines.body: Evaluate: T1 Invasion of Gobakhan vs T1 creature. Against interactive decks: Invasion. Against aggro: creature. Know the default by matchup.

engines.title: Attack Sequencing
engines.body: Lead with your largest threat, not your most important one. Make them commit removal before you attack with your real kill condition.

engines.title: Post-Wipe Rebuilding
engines.body: Practice the Sunfall line: exile their board, take incubate tokens (you pick), flip them into 2/2 artifacts. Re-establish board presence from one sweeper.

matchups.notes: Your pings bypass their flash package. Voice of Victory locks them out of removal during your attack step.

matchups.opponent: You win this matchup because your damage goes around combat entirely. Shocking Sharpshooter, Warleader's Call, and Raphael, Tough Turtle all deal damage when creatures enter the battlefield — their flash blockers (Floodpits Drowner, Tidebinder, Drowner) don't stop those pings because the pings happen on entry, before combat. Dimir's entire defensive plan is built around blocking profitably with efficient flash creatures. Your plan makes blocking irrelevant. The Voice of Victory lock: Voice of Victory reads "your opponents can't cast spells during your turn." When Voice attacks, they cannot cast Lightning Helix, Requiting Hex, Floodpits Drowner — anything — during your attack step. This means your attack with Ojer + Sharpshooter creating Mobilize Warriors deals noncombat damage that they literally cannot respond to. Sequence: activate Dalkovan Encampment ({2}{W}{T}) before Voice attacks to create two more Warriors. They enter, Sharpshooter pings, Call pings — all during your turn, all while they sit with hands full and can't respond. Priority targets for their removal: They will attempt to kill Shocking Sharpshooter first (stops all ETB pings), then Ojer Axonil (stops 4x amplification). Get these threats resolved when their mana is split. Deploy Sharpshooter on T2. If they respond with Requiting Hex ({1}{B}{W}, exile MV ≤ 2), that costs them their entire T3 mana. You untap and deploy Ojer Axonil on T4 into their empty hands. Turn-by-turn plan: T1 Fanatical Firebrand (haste 1/1 — attacks immediately, pings for 1 from Sharpshooter trigger on T2). T2 Shocking Sharpshooter. T3 Voice of Victory + Warleader's Call — now every attack generates Warriors that ping. T4 Ojer Axonil — now every ping is 4. T5 attack: Voice creates 2 Warriors (8 noncombat damage with Sharpshooter + Call + Ojer), all before combat damage resolves. Out In −2 Raphael, Tough Turtle +2 Battle Menu −2 Seam Rip +2 Sear Izzet Lessons Damage Race Unfavorable Their Abandon Attachments hits High Noon. Monument to Endurance gains life faster than you deal damage. Izzet Lessons is your worst post-board matchup in Standard. Monument to Endurance generates life every turn while recurring their threats. Abandon Attachments destroys your High Noon and Inspiring Vantage -dependent setups. Their draw engine ensures they never run out of answers. Priority: Kill them before Monument hits 10 loyalty counters. Go wide, don't go tall — your 1-drop army is harder to sweep than your big threats. If they resolve Monument by turn 4, you need to have them at 8 or fewer life already. Needle: Clarion Conqueror from the SB is your best answer — it copies your next spell and replaces your board after a sweeper. Bring in Rest in Peace to stop Monument's graveyard recursion mode. In Rest in Peace +2 Clarion Conqueror +2 Out High Noon −2 Spectacular Tactics −2 Needle: Deploy Sharpshooter before Ojer — if they Hex Sharpshooter, Ojer lands into a board where his amplification has fewer triggers. But if Sharpshooter sticks and you deploy Ojer on T4, the game state is near-unwinnable for them. Sear (4 damage) handles Cecil, Dark Knight (3/3 deathtouch after flip — if you let Cecil attack and deal damage to Ojer, Ojer dies to deathtouch and Cecil doesn't die). Kill Cecil before he attacks into Ojer. Strategic Betrayal from SB exiles enchantments — hits Enduring Curiosity and Warleader's Call... wait you're running Warleader's Call, not them. Battle Menu is the flex answer: Attack mode creates a 2/2 Knight ETB (triggers Sharpshooter + Call), Magic mode destroys power 4+ creatures (kills Cecil after flip).

matchups.notes: Their Abandon Attachments hits High Noon. Monument to Endurance gains life faster than you deal damage.
Your pings must accumulate 20 damage before their board stabilizes. Exorcise their enchantments and large threats.

matchups.opponent: You lose if you let Sapling Nursery generate Treefolk tokens. A 3/4 reach token blocks your 1/1 and 2/2 Warriors cleanly, and once they have 4+ Treefolk, your attack math is negative — you're trading 1/1 Warriors into 3/4 reach that hits you back for 3 when you block. Your window to win: deal 20 damage via noncombat pings before Nursery resolves on their T3-4, or exile Nursery as fast as possible with Exorcise. Your plan is noncombat first: Sharpshooter + Call pings happen on every creature ETB — including your own Mobilize Warriors. A Voice of Victory attack creating 2 Warriors while Sharpshooter + Call + Raphael + Ojer are all in play = 2 Warriors × 4 triggers × 4 damage (Ojer) = 32 noncombat damage in one attack step. They cannot survive that if Ojer is live. Get Ojer down on T4 and attack immediately. Exorcise handles everything: Exorcise ({1}{W} sorcery) exiles target artifact, enchantment, or creature with power 4 or greater. This hits: Sapling Nursery (enchantment), Mightform Harmonizer (4/4 power), Leatherhead, Swamp Stalker (5/4 power), Mossborn Hydra (power 4+). Bring in both copies G2/G3. Turn-by-turn plan: T1 Firebrand. T2 Sharpshooter — they're likely playing Llanowar Elves T1 and Badgermole Cub T2. Their Cub ETB triggers Sharpshooter (1 ping). T3 Warleader's Call — Cub still on board, pings on every ETB. T4 Ojer Axonil — if Nursery resolved, immediately Exorcise it on your T4 before it generates tokens. Then attack. With Ojer + Sharpshooter + Call, their Elves entering means they take 8 damage from your pings when it entered. Out In −2 Seam Rip +2 Exorcise −2 Raphael, Tough Turtle +2 Battle Menu Needle: Their Archdruid's Charm fight mode kills your key creature AND grows their fighter — don't leave Ojer in a situation where they can Charm-fight it with a creature that has accumulated +1/+1 counters. Ojer has 4 toughness — their Mightform Harmonizer as 4/4 trades equally in a Charm fight. Keep Ojer away from combat damage where possible; his value is the noncombat damage amplification, not as an attacker. Stadium Headliner's sacrifice ability: with Ojer active and 8 creatures, sacrifice Stadium to deal 8 × 4 = 32 damage to their Mossborn Hydra (any size) or directly to their face.

matchups.notes: Magebane Lizard turns their cantrip chain into 10+ damage against themselves. Your noncombat damage ignores their prowess blockers.

matchups.opponent: You win this matchup cleanly when Magebane Lizard (SB) resolves. Their plan requires casting 4+ cantrips per turn — Magebane deals cumulative damage to them equal to the cantrip count: first cantrip deals 1, second deals 2, third deals 3, fourth deals 4. Total: 10 damage to themselves from their own cantrip chain. With Ojer in play, each of those 1-damage Magebane triggers becomes 4 — four cantrips deals 4+8+12+16 = 40 damage. Their entire game plan kills them. Without Magebane (G1): Your noncombat damage from Sharpshooter + Call still bypasses their prowess blockers entirely. Their Eddymurk Crab taps your board on entry — but it enters tapped on your turn, so it can't block. Flash Crab in on their end step taps their creatures, which is a problem — but Ojer's 4/4 body doesn't get tapped by Crab's "tap up to two target creatures" unless they target it. Ojer keeps attacking regardless. Turn-by-turn plan: T1 Firebrand. T2 Sharpshooter. T3 Warleader's Call. T4 Ojer Axonil — now your setup is live. T5 attack: their Slickshot is a 1/2 that gets +2/+0 from spells — with Ojer active, every noncombat damage trigger from Sharpshooter goes to their face, not their Slickshot. Their 7/2 Slickshot attacking you is a concern: Burst Lightning (2 damage) doesn't kill it (2 toughness — actually Burst Lightning does 2 which exactly kills the 1/2). Yes, kill Slickshot with Burst Lightning before it attacks. Out In −2 Seam Rip +4 Magebane Lizard −2 Torch the Tower Needle: Burst Lightning (2 damage) kills Slickshot Show-Off exactly (1/2 toughness). Do it before they attack. Magebane Lizard resolving means their T3-4 cantrip chain deals 10+ damage to themselves — they must kill Magebane before casting spells. But killing Magebane requires spending a removal spell that they normally use for your threats. The tempo trade is your win condition. Trim Seam Rip and Torch (their few ≤ 2 MV permanents aren't worth the slot here).

matchups.notes: Ojer + Sharpshooter generates damage they can't counter. But Inevitable Defeat exiles Ojer uncounterable and Day of Judgment wipes your board.

matchups.opponent: Control has the answers. Day of Judgment destroys your entire board of 1/1 Warriors and key creatures. Inevitable Defeat (uncounterable, instant) exiles Ojer Axonil before he amplifies your pings. Lightning Helix at 4 copies generates 24-point life swings against your early damage. Your path to winning: don't overextend into Day of Judgment, keep 2-3 key pieces rather than flooding the board, and close via Ojer + Sharpshooter noncombat damage that they cannot counter individually — pings resolve on the stack without requiring any spell to be on the stack themselves once Sharpshooter and ETBs are declared. Voice of Victory is critical here: Voice prevents them from casting spells during your turn. When Voice attacks and creates Mobilize Warriors, they cannot cast Lightning Helix or Inevitable Defeat during your attack step. They must deploy all interaction before Voice attacks. Force them to either tap their mana before your attack step (leaving them with nothing for your pings) or hold their mana and take the damage. What they can't stop: Your pings are triggered abilities, not spells. Once Sharpshooter is in play and a creature enters under your control, the ping trigger goes on the stack — they can't counter it with No More Lies or Spell Snare (those counter spells, not triggered abilities). They can kill Sharpshooter in response, but that costs them a card and your creature already entered. Keep the ping engine alive and the noncombat damage accumulates whether they like it or not. Out In −2 Raphael, Tough Turtle +2 Battle Menu −2 Seam Rip +2 Exorcise Needle: They have Mistrise Village ({U}{T}: next spell you cast this turn can't be countered). This means their Inevitable Defeat is occasionally uncounterable even beyond its printed text. Track when they activate Mistrise. Battle Menu's Magic mode destroys power 4+ creatures, which hits their Revelation Monk tokens (1/1 — doesn't trigger Magic mode, they're 1/1). Battle Menu's Attack mode creates a 2/2 Knight ETB trigger for your pingers. Hold 2-3 creatures in hand and don't commit the full board before their sweep resolves — play around Day of Judgment by keeping one good creature in reserve at all times.

matchups.notes: First Ojer + Sharpshooter stack wins. Warleader's Call as the first anthem doubles all your Warriors while halving theirs' effectiveness.

matchups.opponent: Both players are assembling the same engine. The game goes to whoever establishes Ojer + Sharpshooter + Warleader's Call first. Their Sharpshooter triggers YOUR Call (both players' creatures entering deal damage to both players). Be aware: when their creature enters and your Sharpshooter triggers targeting YOU — their Sharpshooter also triggers, targeting THEM. The ping engine runs in both directions once both players have Sharpshooter in play. The race within the race: Kill their Ojer Axonil before he amplifies their pings — Burst Lightning (2 damage) doesn't kill him (4 toughness), need Sear (4 damage) exactly. Stadium Headliner's sacrifice ability deals damage equal to your creature count — with 8 creatures and Ojer, sacrifice Stadium for 32 damage to their Ojer (kills it) or their Sharpshooter (way overkill for a 1/3). Out In −2 Seam Rip +4 Sear −2 Torch the Tower

matchups.opponent: Simic Rhythm mirrors your going-wide strategy but with Badgermole Cub generating +1/+1 counters on their entire board. Their Earthbender Ascension stacks with Cub attacks — they can generate 4-8 power on board by turn 3. Your Monstrous Rage on a key creature into unblockable via Escape Tunnel closes before they can go over your head. Prioritize killing Llanowar Elves on sight — without mana acceleration their curve is much slower. Out In −2 Borrowed Time +2 Sunfall −1 Swamp // Plant + 1 Invasion of Gobakhan Sunfall at 4 damage kills their entire Cub token board and the Cub itself. Invasion of Gobakhan disrupts their hand before Ascension is deployed. Cut Borrowed Time (exile enchantment is too slow) and the flex slot.

matchups.opponent: Dimir Excruciator counters your key threats and bounces your permanents. Their Floodpits Drowner (2/3 flash) bounces a creature on ETB — your small creatures get bounced back to hand indefinitely. The correct play: apply maximum early pressure and close by turn 4 before they stabilize. Monstrous Rage on your unblocked attacker into Escape Tunnel makes their interaction irrelevant if you can land lethal before turn 5. Out In −2 Swamp // Plant +2 Invasion of Gobakhan −1 Borrowed Time +1 Sunfall Invasion of Gobakhan strips their counter from hand before they can use it. Sunfall clears their 2/3 flash blockers. Cut Swamp//Plant (too fair in this aggressive matchup) and Borrowed Time (they have few enchantments to answer).

matchups.notes: Izzet Spellementals builds toward Hearth Elemental and Sunderflock as their payoffs — both...

matchups.opponent: Izzet Spellementals builds toward Hearth Elemental and Sunderflock as their payoffs — both come online turns 3-5. Your clock is faster than their setup. Monstrous Rage into Escape Tunnel on turn 3-4 deals 8+ damage before they can Sunderflock. The critical decision: attack into their 1/1 instants rather than waiting for a perfect board — their Sunderflock sweeper ends games if you let them untap with mana. Out In −1 Borrowed Time +1 Invasion of Gobakhan −1 Swamp // Plant +1 Sunfall Invasion of Gobakhan strips the Sunderflock before they can cast it. Sunfall handles their Hearth Elemental. The core aggressive plan is unchanged — apply pressure early and close before their sweeper.

matchups.notes: Jeskai Control has sweepers, counterspells, and planeswalkers. Their Aven Interrupter coun...

matchups.opponent: Jeskai Control has sweepers, counterspells, and planeswalkers. Their Aven Interrupter counters your key spells (Monstrous Rage, your sorcery-speed threats). High Noon prevents all sorcery-speed plays — your combat tricks still work. Your best path: deploy wide early (pre-High Noon), then attack into their life total before they stabilize with Stormplain Detainment. Every turn they don't have a sweeper is a gift — attack without hesitation. Out In −2 Borrowed Time +2 Invasion of Gobakhan −1 Swamp // Plant +1 Sunfall Invasion strips their key spell from hand before they cast it. Sunfall counters their Voice of Victory lock. Cut defensive flex slots — this is a racing matchup. Apply pressure every turn regardless of open mana.

The core engine is Momo, Friendly Flier : a 1/1 flying lifelink lemur that costs {W} and reduces the cost of each Dragon you cast by {1}. With Momo in play, Clarion Conqueror costs one mana, Magmatic Hellkite costs two, Nova Hellkite costs two. An entire curve of Dragons comes down a full turn early. The Dragon package is brutal: Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant makes every
