Need White Mana T1
Momo requires {W} on T1 — keep hands with Plains, Inspiring Vantage, Sacred Foundry, or Multiversal Passage.

engines.title: One Mana Ahead Every Turn
engines.body: Momo reduces each Dragon's cost by {1}. With Momo on turn 1: T2 Clarion Conqueror for {W} (instead of {1}{W}) + tap their creature. T2 Nova Hellkite for {1}{R} (instead of {2}{R}) + 2 ETB damage. T2 Magmatic Hellkite for {2}{R} (instead of {3}{R}). The acceleration is linear — Momo at 1, Clarion at 0-1, Hellkite at 1-2, repeat. Against Llanowar Elves + Badgermole Cub decks, your T2 Clarion tapping

engines.title: Makes Your Threats Uncounterable
engines.body: Cavern of Souls naming Dragon makes every Dragon you cast off its mana uncounterable. Momo is a Bird — Cavern naming Bird makes Momo uncounterable too. Against Izzet Lessons (Spell Snare, It'll Quench Ya), Jeskai Control (No More Lies), and Azorius Flash (Seam Rip) — your Dragons simply cannot be countered. This is the deck's primary answer to permission-heavy metas.

engines.title: Tutor + Mana Engine
engines.body: Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon is a saga that both tutors for Dragons and provides colored mana. Three copies in the main deck ensures consistent Dragon access even when drawing poorly. It counts as mana fixing, tutor, and threat multiplier in one slot. Against control decks that answer every individual threat, Maelstrom guarantees you always have another Dragon to deploy.

engines.title: Momo, Friendly Flier
engines.body: 1/1 flying lifelink for {W}. Each Dragon you cast costs {1} less. Momo doesn't need to be protected (it's already done its job once you've cast 1-2 discounted Dragons), but it attacks for 1 lifelink every turn which accumulates against aggro. Cavern naming Bird makes Momo uncounterable. With Momo on T1, every Dragon in the deck effectively costs 1 less all game.

engines.title: Clarion Conqueror
engines.body: Dragon creature ({1}{W}{W} normally, {W}{W} with Momo). ETB: tap target permanent. The tap is crucial — it locks their Llanowar Elves before use, taps their Pollinator before it can double tokens, or taps their land to set them back a turn. Clarion comes with a body that attacks. Flying + ETB tap for {0-1}{W}{W} with Momo is one of the best T2 plays in the format.

engines.title: Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant
engines.body: Dragon creature. When Sarkhan attacks, each Dragon you control gains indestructible until EOT. Your entire Dragon board becomes immune to removal during combat. Wrath effects that destroy still kill (indestructible ≠ protection from), but any "deal damage" or "destroy" targeting is blanked. Attack aggressively with Sarkhan each turn to protect your investment.

engines.title: Dragonhawk, Fate's Tempest
engines.body: When Dragonhawk enters, it deals damage to each opponent equal to the highest power among creatures you control, and you exile that many cards from the top of your library, casting one for free. With a 4/4 Dragon on board: 4 damage + exile 4 + cast 1 free. With Sarkhan (power 3 typically): 3 damage + exile 3. This provides both reach damage and card advantage simultaneously.

engines.title: T1 Momo → T2 Discounted Dragon
engines.body: T1: Momo ({W}), 1/1 flying lifelink in play. T2: Clarion Conqueror for {W}{W} (not {1}{W}{W}) — ETB taps their Llanowar Elves or Badgermole Cub before they tap for mana. Now they're at 2 mana on T3 instead of 4. Your T3: two more discounted Dragons. Their T3: scramble to find an answer to 6-8 flying power.

engines.title: Full Curve Beats Too
engines.body: Without Momo, the curve starts T2 Clarion (full cost {1}{W}{W}) or T2 Sarkhan (check cost). Still effective — your Dragons are individually powerful enough without the discount. The deck doesn't require Momo to function; it's a speed amplifier, not a crutch. If Momo dies immediately, continue deploying Dragons at full cost and attack from the air.

engines.title: Need White Mana T1
engines.body: Momo requires {W} on T1 — keep hands with Plains, Inspiring Vantage, Sacred Foundry, or Multiversal Passage. Mulligan any hand with no white source. Hands with Momo + white source + any 2-3 Dragons are snaps. Hands with 5+ Dragons and no Momo or Maelstrom are mediocre — they're castable but miss the power discount. At 6 keep: Momo + 2 lands + any Dragon.

engines.title: Attack Every Turn
engines.body: Sarkhan makes everything indestructible during combat when he attacks. Always attack with Sarkhan first (to trigger the indestructible clause), then declare remaining attackers. This means your Dragons survive damage-based removal and fight effects during combat. In racing scenarios: Sarkhan + 3 Dragons = entire board is indestructible every turn you attack.

engines.title: Momo Cost Reduction
engines.body: Momo reduces every Dragon's cost by {1}. Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon provides additional Dragon mana. Cavern of Souls taps for colored mana on Dragon spells. Result: by T3-T4, you're deploying Dragons that should cost 4-5 mana for 2-3 mana. The curve compression means you always have more threats than they have answers.

engines.title: Sarkhan Indestructible
engines.body: When Sarkhan attacks, ALL your Dragons gain indestructible until EOT. This protects your entire board from removal during combat — fight effects, damage triggers, blocking damage. The key: Sarkhan must attack. Always attack with him unless the life total math doesn't allow it. One Sarkhan attack makes your board completely immune to combat-based removal.

engines.title: Dragonhawk Reach
engines.body: Dragonhawk deals damage equal to your highest-power creature and exiles that many cards. With a 4-power creature: 4 damage to face + exile 4 + free cast. In closing games, Dragonhawk connecting for 4+ damage in the air while also playing your next card for free is an overwhelming value engine. Always aim to have a 4+ power creature in play when Dragonhawk enters.

engines.title: Bigger Fliers Win
engines.body: Against Mono-Red and Boros Aggro: your Dragons are larger and fly. Momo's lifelink + Voice of Victory lifelink means their damage math doesn't work. Clarion Conqueror taps their best attacker before they can use it. You stabilize and attack from the air while they run out of gas. Sarkhan's indestructible ensures your Dragons survive combat.

engines.title: Speed + Disruption
engines.body: Against Dimir, Simic Rhythm, Bant Rhythm: Clarion Conqueror delays their engine (taps Pollinator, Riddler, or dorks). Your Dragons fly over their ground creatures. Cavern names Dragon — their counterspells fail. The race is decided by whether their board can stabilize before you present 12+ flying power.

engines.title: Cavern + Resilience
engines.body: Against Jeskai Control: your biggest weakness. Cavern makes Dragons uncounterable but they have Get Lost, Avatar's Wrath, and efficient exile removal. Deploy one threat at a time, keep one in hand. Maelstrom ensures you always have another Dragon. Dragonhawk provides card advantage to outlast their sweepers. Sheltered by Ghosts (SB) protects a key Dragon.

engines.title: Torpor Orb ×2
engines.body: Artifact that prevents creatures from having "enters the battlefield" abilities. Shuts off Gene Pollinator's token doubling, Clarion Conqueror's tap, Floodpits Drowner's bounce, Nova Hellkite's 2 damage, Aven Interrupter's exile, Voice of Victory's draw. Note: also shuts off YOUR ETBs. Board in only when opponent's ETBs matter more than yours. Vs Simic/Bant rhythm: mandatory.

engines.title: Sheltered by Ghosts ×2
engines.body: Enchantment — Aura. Gives a creature Ward 2 (spells targeting it cost {2} more). Boards in vs control decks with efficient removal. Put on Sarkhan (makes him effectively require {2} additional mana to remove while making the board indestructible) or on a key Dragon to protect the investment. Also provides +1/+1 counter when the enchanted creature attacks.

engines.title: Pyroclasm ×2
engines.body: Deals 2 damage to each creature. Sweeps Izzet Prowess tokens (1/1), Mono-Red 1-drops (1/1, 2/1 dies), Bant spider tokens (1/2 dies to 2). Note: also kills Momo (1/1) and Voice of Victory (2/1). Cast Pyroclasm on THEIR end step before your attack, or after Momo has done its job.

engines.title: Requisition Raid ×2
engines.body: Instant: destroy target artifact or enchantment; if it had MV 4+, draw a card. Destroys: Monument to Endurance (4 MV, draws a card!), Sapling Nursery (4 MV, draws!), Stormchaser's Talent, Enduring Curiosity. The draw trigger on high-MV targets makes this exceptional value. Boards in vs Lessons, Simic, and any enchantment-heavy strategy.

engines.title: Sheltered by Ghosts Ã—1
engines.body: {2}{W} Aura: +1/+1 and ward {2}. Board in vs Jeskai Control when they rely on targeted removal (Seam Rip, spot removal) to answer your key dragons. Ward {2} means they need 2 extra mana to target your creature â€” effectively makes removal cost 4+ on top of their spell cost. Enchant your most threatening Dragon to protect it.

engines.title: Torpor Orb Ã—1
engines.body: {2} Artifact: ETB triggered abilities don't trigger. Board in vs Simic Rhythm and Bant Rhythm when their Earthbender Ascension, Pollinator Wasp, and Beza's ETB triggers are generating massive advantage. Slam this before they deploy their ETB creatures â€” it shuts them ALL off simultaneously. WARNING: also shuts off your Dragon ETBs, so deploy BEFORE your haste-triggering creatures.

engines.title: Pyroclasm Ã—2
engines.body: {1}{R} Sorcery: 2 damage to each creature. Board in vs Izzet Prowess (sweeps their Monastery Swiftspear and DRC before they pump from combat) and Mono-Red Aggro (sweeps their entire board of 1/1s and 2/1s). Cast before your own Dragon if you have one â€” Pyroclasm kills creatures that aren't Dragons. Time it correctly to sweep their board before they attack.

engines.title: Soul-Guide Lantern Ã—2
engines.body: {1} Artifact: Exile target GY at instant speed. Draw a card when it goes to your GY ({B}). Board in vs Izzet Prowess (Phoenix recursion) and Izzet Lessons (GY-based lesson recursion). Never dead â€” in non-GY matchups crack it for the cantrip draw. Crack at instant speed in their upkeep or in response to a GY trigger, never during your own main phase.

engines.title: The Four Fours
engines.body: 4 Momo, 4 Sarkhan, 4 Clarion Conqueror, 4 Magmatic Hellkite + 4 Nova Hellkite. These 20 cards are the engine. Cutting any below 4 reduces the consistency that makes the deck function. Full playsets only.

engines.title: Dragonhawk, Fate's Tempest
engines.body: 2 copies is standard. In control-heavy metas, run 3-4 — the card advantage is critical vs sweeper-heavy decks. In aggro-heavy metas, trim to 1-2 — you don't need the long-game engine as much. Dragonhawk is the late-game punch that the deck needs in grind scenarios.

engines.title: Voice of Victory
engines.body: 3 copies in the March 30 list. Excellent in aggro matchups (lifelink + draw on ETB). Mediocre vs control (dies to everything). In aggressive metas: run 3-4. In control metas: cut entirely and replace with Neriv, Heart of the Storm or another Dragon. Voice is not a Dragon (it's a Warrior?) — check type for Cavern naming purposes.

engines.title: Dragon First, Bird Second
engines.body: Name Dragon on first Cavern, Bird on second (if running 2+ Caverns). Your Dragons are the win conditions — uncounterable Hellkites are the priority. Momo as a Bird is the secondary naming. In highly interactive metas with lots of countermagic, run all 3 Caverns even if it hurts the mana base slightly.

engines.title: Charming Prince (Turin list)
engines.body: The RC Turin 7th place list ran 3 Charming Prince main. Charming Prince (Human, not a Dragon) provides scry 2 on ETB. In a Dragon-dense list, Charming Prince is a non-Dragon way to smooth draws. Some builds prefer pure Dragon density; others value the scry. Test based on how often you flood on Dragons vs need to find them.

engines.title: Simic/Bant + Izzet Lessons Are Top Meta
engines.body: Boros Dragons is specifically built to beat Simic token strategies (Torpor Orb shuts them off) and Izzet Lessons (Cavern + Requisition Raid). If those two archetypes are dominating, register Dragons. Avoid if Jeskai Control is above 10% — it's your clear worst matchup.

engines.title: Haste Sequence
engines.body: You attack with Dragonhawk the turn it enters. You never wait to attack — their flash creatures (Floodpits Drowner, Spider Manifestation) come down AFTER Dragonhawk's haste attack. You declare the attack before they can deploy flash blockers. Haste means your first attack is always free.

engines.title: Worldsoul's Rage Calculation
engines.body: Before casting Worldsoul's Rage: count your lands. 6 lands = 6 damage. 8 lands = 8 damage. 10 lands = 10 damage. You never cast Rage without knowing the exact damage output. You target their creature when the damage kills it AND leaves enough for face damage. You target face when they're at or below your land count.

engines.title: Temur Battlecrier Sequencing
engines.body: You deploy Temur Battlecrier AFTER your Dragon is in play. Battlecrier on an empty board gives +0/+0 to nothing — it's dead. Battlecrier with Dragonhawk in play: Dragonhawk attacks as 5/3 haste flier. You always check: "do I have a Dragon?" before deploying Battlecrier.

engines.title: Devastating Onslaught Kill Math
engines.body: Before casting Devastating Onslaught (+X/+X trample where X = land count): identify your kill target. At 5 lands, Onslaught on Dragonhawk (3/3): it becomes 8/8 trample. That's lethal from 20 with one hit. You know the lethal math at each land count before casting.

engines.title: Worldsoul's Rage Land Count Threshold
engines.body: You track your land count specifically for Worldsoul's Rage efficiency. At 5 lands: Rage kills 5-toughness creatures. At 7: kills 7-toughness. You cut lands only when your curve is low enough to not need the high-count Rage. You run 24+ lands when Rage is your primary removal and win condition.

engines.title: Requisition Raid Flex Slot
engines.body: You adjust your Requisition Raid count based on how often your board gets swept. In wipe-heavy metas: +1 Raid (three bodies from one card rebuilds faster). In creature-heavy metas: -1 Raid (you need more removal). You treat Raid as your resilience card — more against sweepers, less against aggro.

engines.title: Attack Before Blockers
engines.body: You declare attackers with Dragonhawk before your opponents deploy flash blockers. Their Floodpits Drowner comes down at flash speed — but only AFTER you've already declared attackers. Your haste attack happens before any EOT flashing is possible.

engines.title: Dragon First, Crier Second
engines.body: You sequence: Dragon enters → then cast Temur Battlecrier. Battlecrier on an empty board grants +2/+0 to nothing. With any Dragon in play: Battlecrier makes every Dragon attack for +2/+0. You never cast Battlecrier speculatively.

engines.title: Face or Creature?
engines.body: Before casting Worldsoul's Rage, you decide: face or creature? Face: use when their life total is ≤ your land count. Creature: use when their creature's toughness is ≤ your land count AND the creature is blocking your lethal attack.

engines.title: Board State Threshold
engines.body: You cast Pyroclasm ({1}{R}: 2 damage each creature) when they have 3+ creatures with 2 or less toughness. Fewer creatures: hold Pyroclasm. Your dragons (typically 3+ toughness) survive Pyroclasm — you sweep their board while your threats remain.

engines.title: Sarkhan Attack Order
engines.body: ALWAYS attack with Sarkhan first in any combat where you want indestructibility. His trigger fires when he attacks — all your other Dragons get the benefit only if he attacks. Forgetting to attack with Sarkhan means your Dragons die to their burn spells and fight effects. Practice this until it's automatic.

engines.title: Indestructible ≠ Exile Protection
engines.body: Indestructible means your Dragons can't be destroyed. Get Lost exiles — it bypasses indestructible. Avatar's Wrath that says "exile all creatures" bypasses indestructible. Only "destroy" effects are stopped. Know which of their removal effects destroy vs exile before going to combat each game.

engines.title: Cavern Naming Decision
engines.body: Name Dragon on Cavern. Only name Bird if you specifically need Momo to be uncounterable (rare). Default: Dragon = your 4 Sarkhan, 4 Clarion, 4 Magmatic, 4 Nova all become uncounterable. This is worth more than protecting one 1/1 Momo.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Forest = Simic/Bant/Mono-Green — board Torpor Orb and Requisition Raid. Steam Vents = Izzet — board Pyroclasm and Soul-Guide Lantern. Island/Plains combo = Azorius Flash — board Sheltered by Ghosts to protect key Dragon. Mountain or Sacred Foundry = Boros — board Avatar's Wrath and Pyroclasm.

engines.title: Dragonhawk Attack Timing
engines.body: Practice attacking with Dragonhawk the turn it enters before opponents can deploy flash blockers. Know their flash creatures (Floodpits Drowner, Spider Manifestation) and when they're available to counter.

engines.title: Worldsoul's Rage Kill Math
engines.body: Practice calculating Worldsoul's Rage damage at various land counts. At 5 lands: 5 damage face. At 7 lands: 7 damage to their key blocker. Know the math without calculating at the table.

engines.title: Temur Battlecrier Sequencing
engines.body: Practice deploying Battlecrier AFTER your Dragon is in play. Battlecrier on an empty board is just a vanilla creature. Battlecrier on Dragonhawk gives +2/+0 and means Dragonhawk is a 5/3 haste flier.

engines.title: Post-Wipe Recovery
engines.body: Practice the Requisition Raid recovery line after a sweeper. Three bodies immediately puts pressure back on. Know when to rebuild slowly vs go back in immediately.

BorosEnergy.kill_turn: Apply pressure every turn. They cannot block, cannot answer your creatures. Curve one-drop into two-drop into attack.Goblin Bombardment+ full attack should deal lethal before they reach the mana for a lethal Grapeshot chain. Do not tap out for cantrips — always have attackers swinging.
BorosEnergy.game_plan: Chapter 01 Identity & Philosophy "Pressure compounds. Every turn they don't die is a turn you hand them for free." — Core Mantra Boros Energy is an aggressive midrange deck that wins by front-loading pressure and converting early tempo into board-state inevitability. It is not a pure aggro deck — it has real card advantage engines in Guide of Souls , Ocelot Pride , and Ragavan. It is not a midrange deck in the traditional sense — it cannot afford to durdle. It occupies the exact space between those two poles: the deck that is always the beatdown but has the tools to grind when the game goes lo
BorosEnergy.strengths: Consistent — rarely loses to mana. The 21-land base with two-drops means you're never flooded or screwed. Multi-axis pressure — Bombardment reach + combat damage + Phlage escape means opponents can never "stabilize" in the traditional sense. Punishes greedy manabases hard — Blood Moon out of the board shuts down Blink, Titan, Tron, Domain. 17 Top 8s on this build means the lines are documented and proven.
BorosEnergy.weaknesses: Lava Dart kills your best one-drops — Prowess is a bad matchup because of this. Supreme Verdict and Wrath of the Skies can reset a developed board. Sanctifier en-Vec shuts off Galvanic Discharge — must answer immediately. Very fast combo (Neoform, Belcher) can kill before you establish pressure.
BorosEnergy.mulligan:
Mulligan Philosophy

Snap keep: Any hand with Ragavan or Ocelot Pride + 2 lands + at least one removal or interaction spell.

engines.title: The Aggression Package
engines.body: Ragavan generates mana and cards from the first swing. Ocelot Pride builds a scaling cat army that dwarfs the opponent's board by turn 4. Guide of Souls converts that army into energy and life. These three operate as a system: Ragavan opens the door, Pride fills it with threats, Guide converts those threats into resources that fund removal.

engines.title: Galvanic DischargeSystem
engines.body: Discharge scales with energy: 2 energy kills a 2-toughness creature, 4+ kills almost anything in the format. Guide of Souls and Ragavan fund energy passively. The key skill is knowing your full energy pool before spending: Discharge gives you 3 energy on cast, then you deal damage equal to however much you spend. Floor is always 3. With 3 stored you deal 6. Count stored energy + 3 before casting.

engines.title: Goblin BombardmentReach
engines.body: Bombardment converts your board into burn. With 4 cats in play, that's 4 direct damage you can deploy at instant speed before combat is even declared. Opponents constantly miscalculate their safe life total. The highest skill expression in this deck is calculating Bombardment lethal before every combat step — every single turn.

engines.title: Phlage as the Pivot
engines.body: Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury is the late-game inevitability engine. Cast it early for tempo — 6/6 flash — or escape it for the full engine. Once escaped, Phlage recurs every turn, generates energy, and provides reach. Getting to 6 mana to escape Phlage is a priority that overrides other sequencing decisions in long games.

engines.title: What You Do Well
engines.body: Consistent — rarely loses to mana. The 21-land base with two-drops means you're never flooded or screwed. Multi-axis pressure — Bombardment reach + combat damage + Phlage escape means opponents can never "stabilize" in the traditional sense. Punishes greedy manabases hard — Blood Moon out of the board shuts down Blink, Titan, Tron, Domain. 17 Top 8s on this build means the lines are documented and

engines.title: What Beats You
engines.body: Lava Dart kills your best one-drops — Prowess is a bad matchup because of this. Supreme Verdict and Wrath of the Skies can reset a developed board. Sanctifier en-Vec shuts off Galvanic Discharge — must answer immediately. Very fast combo (Neoform, Belcher) can kill before you establish pressure.

engines.title: Ajani, Nacatl Pariah
engines.body: Now a full 4-of. The legend rule means you can only have one in play but running 4 copies maximizes seeing it by turn 2 — the earliest and most impactful deployment. The flip is what you're playing for: Ajani Scattered to the Winds is a game-ender with 3+ cats in play. At 4 cats, a single activation can represent 16+ power on board. Seasoned Pyromancer fills the role of discarding redundant Ajanis

engines.title: Goblin Bombardment
engines.body: You want to draw exactly one per game. Three is the right number — seeing it by turn 3 reliably but not flooding on it. Once Bombardment is down, every creature you deploy has implicit direct damage value. Changes how opponents block, trade, and sequence their answers.

engines.title: Phlage
engines.body: The most underutilized card by newer pilots. Phlage cast as a 6/6 flash on turn 4 is already a strong play. Phlage escaped on turn 6 is a game-ending engine. Know both modes. The escape cost of 3 cards + 5RW sounds expensive but the energy generation and recurring pressure it provides is worth building toward.

engines.title: Seasoned Pyromancer
engines.body: When Seasoned Pyromancer enters, discard up to two cards then draw that many. Each discarded card creates a 1/1 Human token. This is the deck's primary refueling engine — pitch an unneeded land or a Phlage you can't escape yet, draw live cards, and get blockers/attackers simultaneously. When it dies, exile it to create two more 1/1 tokens. Four copies means this deck can outgrind midrange and cont

engines.title: Lead Pressure
engines.body: Ragavan on turn 1 is the ideal start — attack every subsequent turn. If no Ragavan, Ocelot Pride or Guide of Souls . Do not hold a one-drop "for protection." Deploy it. The value compounds. Even a Pride with no immediate trigger is applying pressure and threatening to snowball.

engines.title: Layer Threats
engines.body: Add Guide of Souls or a second Ocelot Pride . Keep attacking with everything. Use Galvanic Discharge to clear blockers — check energy before spending it. Never let them stabilize behind a single blocker for free. If Goblin Bombardment is in hand, resolve it now — it changes the math on every future combat.

engines.title: Generate Inevitability
engines.body: Ocelot Pride should be generating 2+ tokens by now. Guide of Souls is gaining 1 life and 1 energy per creature ETB — and can spend 3 energy when attacking to put two +1/+1 counters and a flying counter on any attacking creature, making it an Angel. That pump changes combat math dramatically mid-combat. Ajani at 3 mana flips cleanly on turn 4 if you attacked on 2 and 3. This is when the Bombardment

engines.title: Ajani Closes
engines.body: A single Ajani flip with 3 cats = each cat gets +3/+3 and creates another cat. From 3 cats you suddenly have 6 attacking for 18+. Do not cast Ajani into open Wrath mana — wait one turn. Either they tap out first, or you attack twice more and have Bombardment reach anyway. Never lose a game because you rushed Ajani.

engines.title: Are They Faster?
engines.body: If yes → you are Tempo Control. Stabilize first. Use Discharge and Wrath of the Skies to buy time. Do not race when you cannot win the race. Every life point matters until you have a stable board.

engines.title: Are They More Powerful Long-Term?
engines.body: If yes → you are Beatdown. Press aggressively. Use Bombardment reach math every turn. Don't give them the turns they need to develop their engine. Close before they get to full power.

engines.title: Is the Board Symmetrical?
engines.body: Mirror situations. Identify the asymmetries — who has Bombardment, who has more pump, whose tokens are bigger. Then make the role decision based on those asymmetries, not on raw position.

engines.title: You're the aggressor when:
engines.body: You've stabilized against aggro at 10+ life. They've used their key disruption pieces. They're on a slow draw. Your board is bigger than theirs and they need to find specific answers to beat you.

engines.title: Hold the line when:
engines.body: Life total is below 8. They have multiple creatures threatening your life. They have untapped mana for burn. You haven't stabilized the board — a dead Ragavan and two tokens is not a stable board.

engines.title: Transition to pure close when:
engines.body: They're hellbent. Bombardment + tokens = lethal in 1–2 turns. Phlage has escaped. Any further development is slower than just attacking and sacrificing everything. Count the lethal, then execute.

engines.title: Maximum Aggression
engines.body: Lead Ragavan, attack into everything. They cannot interact with your board effectively G1. You should be threatening lethal by turn 4 before Archon can enter. Goblin Bombardment on turn 2 converts every subsequent creature into reach they can't block through.

engines.title: RespectThoughtseizeT1
engines.body: They can Thoughtseize you on T1 and take your best card. Prioritize hands with multiple threats so a single discard doesn't brick you. Still very aggressive — one turn behind is fine when they can't interact with the board.

engines.title: White Orchid Phantom
engines.body: Denies a land drop on entry and they blink it repeatedly. If Phantom costs you a land, adjust by playing around their mana rather than developing into it. Don't panic — you still have your existing lands, just count on one fewer.

engines.title: Solitude+Ephemerate
engines.body: Answers two creatures for one card. Stagger your threats — don't deploy two creatures in the same turn if they have 2+ mana up. Force them to choose which threat to answer, then deploy the other one next turn.

engines.title: Ocelot Pride(Theirs)
engines.body: Their Ocelot Pride generates tokens that outpace your reach. Answer it immediately with Celestial Purge (postboard) or Galvanic Discharge . An unchecked Pride on their side is a faster clock than yours and generates lifegain from Blink triggers.

engines.title: Wrath of the Skies
engines.body: Their sweeper. It kills your whole board at X=2-3. Never overcommit — deploy one threat at a time when they have 4+ mana open. Post-board Wrath of the Skies from your own side boards in to clear their token army.

engines.title: Race Pre-Phantom
engines.body: T1 Ragavan, T2 Pride + Guide, T3 Ajani or Goblin Bombardment . You want to have 3+ power attacking before Phantom can land. The more damage you've dealt before they slow you, the more Bombardment reach matters.

engines.title: Respect EarlySolitude
engines.body: They may have Solitude T2 via pitch. Keep hands with 2+ threats so a pitch Solitude doesn't blank your whole turn. On the draw you're slightly behind on tempo — lean on Bombardment reach over combat damage to close.

engines.title: Go Under Dart Range
engines.body: Deploy threats that dodge Lava Dart : Guide of Souls is 2 toughness and survives. Phlage is out of Dart range. Focus on guide + Phlage and use discharge early to kill their prowess threats before they connect.

engines.title: Mulligan Harder
engines.body: Prioritize hands with Guide of Souls , Phlage, and Discharge. Ragavan is a liability here — they will Dart it freely and you fall behind. On the draw, hands without answers to their T1 are mulligans.

engines.title: Establish Bombardment First
engines.body: You have the tempo advantage. Prioritize resolving Goblin Bombardment on T2-3. Once it's down you have the reach advantage regardless of board parity. Attack freely — every unblocked creature is 1 Bombardment damage they can't prevent.

engines.title: Slightly Defensive
engines.body: Ragavan trades unfavorably when they attacked first. Be one turn more defensive — protect your key creatures from trading down. Their Bombardment will be online before yours. Find yours faster — it's your equalizer.

engines.title: Maximum Pressure
engines.body: T1 Ragavan, attack into everything. They cannot interact on T1 without pitch Solitude . Every turn Ragavan connects is a stolen spell and a Gold token. Stolen Counterspells are game-warping. Lead fast, lead relentlessly.

engines.title: One Threat at a Time
engines.body: On the draw they may have T2 Counterspell mana up. Stagger threats — deploy one per turn. Force them to answer each one individually. The more spells they spend answering one-drops, the fewer answers they have for your real threats.

engines.title: Lead the Race
engines.body: You're favored on the play. Your clock is faster than their average draw. Lead aggressively and do not slow down to interact — there's nothing to interact with until they start assembling. Just kill them.

engines.title: Respect T3 Kill
engines.body: On a good Titan draw they can kill T3. You cannot stop this without specific disruption. Play your fastest hand and hope they have a slower draw. The race is the plan — you don't have enough stack interaction to stop their fast kill consistently.

engines.title: Orim's Chant Lock
engines.body: In: +2 Orim's Chant · +1 High Noon · +1 Surgical Extraction · +1 Soul-Guide Lantern · +1 Wear//Tear Out: −2 The Legend of Roku · −2 Phlage · −2 Blood Moon

engines.title: Wrath + GY Hate
engines.body: In: +1 Soul-Guide Lantern · +1 Surgical Extraction · +1 The Legend of Roku · +3 Wrath of the Skies Out: −2 Blood Moon · −4 Ragavan

engines.title: Wrath + GY Hate
engines.body: In: +1 Soul-Guide Lantern · +1 Surgical Extraction · +1 The Legend of Roku · +3 Wrath of the Skies Out: −2 Blood Moon · −4 Ragavan

engines.title: Land Hate Package
engines.body: In: +1 Blood Moon · +2 Obsidian Charmaw · +3 Wrath of the Skies · +1 Surgical Extraction · +1 Wear//Tear Out: −2 The Legend of Roku · −1 Ranger-Captain of Eos · −2 Galvanic Discharge · −2 Phlage · −1 Elegant Parlor

engines.title: Blood Moon + Charmaw
engines.body: In: +1 Blood Moon · +2 Obsidian Charmaw · +1 Wear//Tear Out: −2 The Legend of Roku · −1 Ranger-Captain of Eos · −1 Galvanic Discharge

engines.title: Wrath + Vexing Bauble
engines.body: In: +3 Wrath of the Skies · +1 Wear//Tear · +2 Vexing Bauble · +1 High Noon Out: −1 Ranger-Captain of Eos · −2 The Legend of Roku · −2 Blood Moon · −2 Galvanic Discharge

engines.title: GY Disruption
engines.body: In: +1 Blood Moon · +1 Surgical Extraction · +1 The Legend of Roku · +1 Soul-Guide Lantern Out: −1 Goblin Bombardment · −1 Lightning Bolt · −2 Galvanic Discharge

engines.title: Anti-Combo Package
engines.body: In: +1 Blood Moon · +2 Orim's Chant · +1 High Noon · +2 Vexing Bauble Out: −2 The Legend of Roku · −3 Phlage · −1 Elegant Parlor

engines.title: Ragavan ×4
engines.body: The deck's best T1 play. Four copies non-negotiable — Ragavan connecting generates treasure and steals their spells. Never cut.

engines.title: Phlage ×3
engines.body: Your GY-based reach and finisher. Three copies is the tested number; four floods the hand. Phlage recurring each upkeep after escaping is your late-game inevitability.

engines.title: Ocelot Pride
engines.body: 3 in most metas. Run 4 in creature-heavy metas where the token army dominates combat. Cut to 2 in combo-heavy metas where token generation is irrelevant before they go off.

engines.title: Sanctifier en-Vec (SB)
engines.body: 2 copies vs Grixis Reanimator and GY-heavy metas. 1 copy as a splash. Cut entirely when the meta has no black/red decks to shut off.

engines.title: Goblin Bombardment count
engines.body: 2 vs 3 is the key flex. 3 in grindy metas where the sacrifice outlet generates persistent reach. 2 in fast aggro metas where Bombardment is too slow to be relevant before you win or lose.

engines.title: Ragavan Connection Lines
engines.body: Practice protecting Ragavan in combat. Use removal on their blocker before attacking with Ragavan. Know when Ragavan is worth protecting versus when it can be sacrificed for a free treasure.

engines.title: Phlage Escape Timing
engines.body: Practice evaluating when your GY has 5 cards for Phlage escape. Don't escape Phlage prematurely — the GY cards have value for future escapes. Track your GY count from T1.

engines.title: Energy Tracking
engines.body: Practice counting energy throughout a game. Know your exact energy count at each decision point. Running out of energy mid-combo is the most common mistake with Boros Energy.

engines.title: G2 Sanctifier Lines
engines.body: Practice the Sanctifier en-Vec game state. They cannot target it with black or red removal. Know what CAN remove it: sacrifice effects, exile board wipes, white/blue/green removal only.

matchups.notes: Faster clock — Galvanic Discharge kills their creatures
Race Tron assembly — TKS strips your hand
Kill before they reanimate — Sanctifier immune to Grief
Your clock beats theirs — Sanctifier dodges Grapeshot

DIMIREXCRUCIATOR.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "You're not trying to outgrind them. You're trying to reduce their library to six cards and then mill them out in two attacks." Dimir Excruciator won Pro Tour Lorwyn Eclipsed 2026 in Christoffer Larsen's hands, going 15-4 (78%). The deck is a combo-control shell built around a two-card instant-kill sequence: Doomsday Excruciator + Restless Reef . Doomsday Excruciator is a 7/6 Demon with flash and flying. When it enters the battlefield, both players exile cards from the top of their library until each player has exactly six cards remaining. After Excruciator resolves, R
DIMIREXCRUCIATOR.mulligan:
Mulligan Framework

Keep: Any 7 with 3-4 lands + disruption (Requiting Hex, Deceit) + any combo piece (Excruciator, Spider-Man, or Insatiable Avarice).

engines.title: Excruciator → Restless Reef Attacks → Insatiable Avarice
engines.body: Cast Excruciator (both players go to 6 cards). Restless Reef attacks → opponent mills 4 → they have 2 cards. Cast Insatiable Avarice targeting opponent (draw 3) → they draw 2 then mill 1 with empty library → they lose. Full sequence costs 7 mana total across two turns (5 for Excruciator + 2 for Avarice, with Reef attacking for free).

engines.title: Discard Excruciator → Superior Spider-Man Copies It
engines.body: Use Winternight Stories or Bitter Triumph to discard Doomsday Excruciator to your GY. Cast Superior Spider-Man ({2}{U}{B}) — it ETBs and copies Excruciator's enter trigger using its "if you cast it" clause. Both players exile down to 6. Continue to Line 1. This line costs only 4 mana for the "Excruciator effect" and leaves mana for Avarice the same turn.

engines.title: Midrange Is Dominant
engines.body: Your disruption (Deceit, Intimidation Tactics, Requiting Hex) is excellent against creature and midrange strategies. The combo kills efficiently enough that midrange decks can't race you once Excruciator resolves. Best when the field is Dimir Midrange, Bant Rhythm, and Mono-Green.

engines.title: GY Hate and Flash Creatures Are Prevalent
engines.body: Soul-Guide Lantern exiles your GY (prevents the Spider-Man copy line). Torpor Orb stops all ETB triggers including Excruciator's exile and Deceit's discard. Flash creatures answering your Excruciator at instant speed are also problematic. Verify the field doesn't have widespread Torpor Orb before registering.

engines.title: Disrupt and Survive
engines.body: T1-2: Requiting Hex and Intimidation Tactics remove their early threats. Deceit on T2 strips their best card while leaving a 1/1 body. Stock Up on T2-3 digs for your combo pieces. Goal: be at a comfortable life total with their hand emptied or key threats removed by T4.

engines.title: Set Up the Discard Line
engines.body: Winternight Stories on T3 gives you a discard outlet — use it to bin Doomsday Excruciator from hand. This enables the Superior Spider-Man line on T4: cast Spider-Man ({2}{U}{B}), copy Excruciator's trigger. Both players exile to 6 cards while you have mana up for Insatiable Avarice. Alternatively, cast Insatiable Avarice on T3 to draw 3 and find Excruciator.

engines.title: Execute the Combo
engines.body: Cast Doomsday Excruciator ({3}{B}{B}) or use Spider-Man to copy the trigger. Both players exile down to 6. On your next turn, Restless Reef attacks (flip it into creature mode) → mills them for 4 → they have 2 cards. Cast Insatiable Avarice targeting opponent ({1}{B}: draw 3) → they draw 2 then mill with empty library → they lose immediately.

engines.title: Quantum Riddler Clock
engines.body: When the combo is disrupted (Excruciator countered, Spider-Man killed), Quantum Riddler from the SB serves as a 4/4 that surveil 2 + draws a card every time it attacks. With 2+ instants/sorceries in GY, Riddler generates 1+ card advantage per turn. In long attrition games, Riddler is your backup kill condition — it threatens lethal in 5 attacks and generates overwhelming card advantage.

engines.title: Doomsday Excruciator + Restless Reef
engines.body: Excruciator ETB: both players exile until each has exactly 6 cards remaining. This is symmetrical — you also go to 6. Plan your hand carefully. Restless Reef attacks as a 1/2 and mills 4. After one attack, opponent has 2 cards. Insatiable Avarice (draw 3 targeting them) = they draw 2, try to draw a 3rd from empty library = they lose.

engines.title: Superior Spider-Man + Winternight Stories
engines.body: Discard Excruciator with Winternight Stories. Cast Superior Spider-Man ({2}{U}{B}) — it copies Excruciator's enter trigger because Spider-Man preserves "if you cast it" clauses. Both players exile to 6, leaving you with {B} or {1}{B} for Insatiable Avarice in the same turn. The copy line executes the full combo in one turn for 6 total mana.

engines.title: Deceit + Superior Spider-Man
engines.body: Deceit ({1}{B}) is both Distress (target opponent discards a nonland) and a mini-bounce (return a nonland permanent with MV ≤ 2 to hand) on one card. Superior Spider-Man copies Deceit's ETB — so casting Spider-Man with Deceit in GY effectively gives you a second Deceit effect plus a 4/4 body for {2}{U}{B}. This is why Spider-Man is a 4-of: it's both the combo enabler AND a tempo engine.

engines.title: You Need 5 Black Mana for Excruciator
engines.body: Doomsday Excruciator costs {3}{B}{B}. With 11 Swamps + 4 Watery Grave + 4 Gloomlake Verge (enters untapped with Swamp/Island), you reliably hit double black by T4-5. Don't try to cast Excruciator on T4 with only 1 basic Swamp in play — verify your black mana sources before committing.

engines.title: Restless Reef Needs to Not Have Summoning Sickness
engines.body: Restless Reef is a land that becomes a 1/2 creature when you activate its ability. It has summoning sickness the turn it enters. Play Restless Reef BEFORE casting Excruciator — ideally on T3-4, well before the combo turn. Reef that entered the same turn as Excruciator cannot attack that turn, breaking the two-turn kill.

engines.title: Reactive Control
engines.body: Answer their threats with Requiting Hex and Deceit. Use Harvester of Misery to sweep small boards. Use Bitter Triumph as flexible removal. Build toward the combo with Stock Up and Insatiable Avarice. Don't rush the combo — stabilize first, kill second.

engines.title: Disruptive Combo
engines.body: Strip their hand with Deceit + Superior Spider-Man before executing the combo. Empty their hand of interaction before casting Excruciator. Prioritize Intimidation Tactics to exile their key threat before they can cast it — proactive exile is better than reactive removal.

engines.title: Quantum Riddler Grind
engines.body: When Excruciator is answered or the combo is disrupted, shift to Riddler beatdown. Riddler + Deceit bodies + Harvester tokens close games in 4-6 turns. Deadly Cover-Up as Surgical Extraction disrupts their engine. You can win fair games — you just prefer not to.

engines.title: Duress ×4
engines.body: Your most versatile SB card. Strips countermagic before Excruciator, removes planeswalkers, hits Monument to Endurance, removes High Noon. Board in every non-aggro matchup. The 4-of is justified — you want multiples in the hand before committing to the combo.

engines.title: Quantum Riddler ×3
engines.body: Backup win condition when Excruciator is repeatedly answered. A 4/4 that generates card advantage every attack (surveil 2 + draw 1) is excellent in attrition matchups. Board in: Dimir Midrange, Jeskai Control, mirror. Provides a threat they must answer immediately.

engines.title: Torpor Orb ×2
engines.body: Stops ALL ETB triggers — including Excruciator. WARNING: If you board in Torpor Orb, you cannot use Doomsday Excruciator (no ETB). The Orb is for matchups where you plan to win through fair creature beatdown (Riddler, Deceit bodies) and want to shut down their ETB-based engines (Mono-Green Landfall's Icetill combo, Bant Rhythm's Gene Pollinator). Do NOT board Torpor Orb in matchups where you're st

engines.title: Shoot the Sheriff ×2 + Cruelclaw's Heist ×1
engines.body: Shoot the Sheriff is removal for non-outlaw creatures that Requiting Hex doesn't cover (MV 3+). Board in vs large-creature strategies. Cruelclaw's Heist is targeted exile — removes their key permanent (Monument to Endurance, Restless Reef in mirror, key enchantments) and lets you steal it. One-of flex slot.

engines.title: Requiting Hex Ã—2
engines.body: {B} Instant: Destroy target creature with MV â‰¤ 2; Requiting Hex deals 2 damage to that creature's controller. Board in vs Mono-Red Aggro (destroys their Monastery Swiftspear at instant speed AND deals 2 damage to them â€” a 3-point life swing in one card). At one mana with immediate damage, this is one of your most mana-efficient interactive spells.

engines.title: Cryptic Annelid Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{U} 3/3 that can't be countered. Board in vs Izzet Spellementals and Dimir Midrange when they're holding counters â€” an uncounterable 3/3 forces them to use the exact right answer (removal) rather than their cheapest interaction. If they can't counter it, they need to spend two cards to deal with it.

engines.title: Wistfulness Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{U} Sorcery: Draw three cards. Board in vs Simic Rhythm and Bant Rhythm when you expect the game to go to 7+ turns and raw card advantage decides the winner. Three cards for three mana is extremely efficient at refilling your hand. Deploy after you've spent your hand developing your board.

engines.title: Glarb, Calamity's Augur Ã—2
engines.body: {3}{B}{G} 4/4. Whenever an opponent draws a card, pay {1} + lose 1 life to draw a card. Board in vs Izzet Spellementals (their cantrip chains draw you multiple cards too) and Mono-Red Aggro (every card they draw off their small burn spells draws you one too). At 4 power it's also a meaningful attacker that threatens their life total.

engines.title: Restless Reef + Excruciator + Spider-Man
engines.body: The combo requires both Excruciator (or Spider-Man as the copy) and Restless Reef. 4 Reef ensures you always have it in play. 3 Excruciator + 4 Spider-Man gives 7 ways to execute the exile effect. Don't touch these numbers.

engines.title: Archenemy's Charm: 1-2
engines.body: Flexible removal — modal spell that handles different threats. The single copy in Larsen's list reflects that Requiting Hex and Bitter Triumph cover most removal needs. Run 2 in aggro-heavy metas where the extra flexible removal matters. Cut to 0 vs pure combo where removal is dead.

engines.title: Winternight Stories: 2-3
engines.body: 2 is Larsen's number. Run 3 in metas where the Spider-Man copy line is your primary combo path (vs lots of removal answering Excruciator directly). Winternight discards for multiple turns and generates value beyond just enabling Spider-Man — the life gain from the Stories side is real vs aggro.

engines.title: Harbinger Deployment Window
engines.body: You deploy Harbinger of the Seas on T3 before they've played their fourth land. The earlier Harbinger enters, the more nonbasic land triggers they take. A T3 Harbinger against a 3-color deck means every land they play for the rest of the game enters tapped AND deals damage. You never wait to deploy Harbinger — early is always better.

engines.title: Floodpits Drowner Timing
engines.body: You deploy Floodpits Drowner at their EOT, not your main phase. EOT bounce: they bounce back to hand, lose the tempo, and you untap with a 2/3 flash in play. Main phase bounce: they get a draw step to recast and you've committed to a main-phase play. EOT is always superior.

engines.title: Ascension Trigger Order
engines.body: You cast a cantrip BEFORE playing your Earthbender Ascension. The Ascension trigger fires when you play your SECOND land each turn — you need Ascension already in play for the first trigger. You sequence: play first land → cast Ascension → play second land → Ascension triggers. Never reverse this.

engines.title: Counterspell Priority
engines.body: You counter their win condition, not their setup. Against Izzet: counter Slickshot Show-Off, not Opt. Against Mono-Green: counter Earthbender Ascension (MV 2, Spell Snare), not Llanowar Elves. Against Control: counter their board wipe, not their Narset. You identify the win condition before holding your mana each turn.

engines.title: Harbinger Count vs Greedy Metas
engines.body: You run more Harbinger of the Seas copies in greedy 3-4 color meta. Harbinger makes every nonbasic enter tapped — more nonbasics = more Harbinger value. You cut Harbinger in basic-heavy metas (mono-color heavy) where the nonbasic punishment is minimal.

engines.title: Duress vs Thoughtseize Ratio
engines.body: You run Duress (no life loss) in aggressive metas where 2 life matters. You run Thoughtseize (any nonland) in controlling metas where seeing their full hand is most valuable. In mixed metas: run 2 of each. You adjust the ratio based on whether life pressure or hand quality is your primary concern.

engines.title: Spell Snare in the Main
engines.body: You add Spell Snare to your main deck when the meta is dominated by MV-2 spells. Earthbender Ascension (MV 2), Psychic Frog (MV 1? — check), key 2-drops in the format. Snare is efficient vs MV-2 threats — when the meta rotates away from them, you move Snare to SB.

engines.title: Negate vs Counterspell Choice
engines.body: You run Negate ({1}{U}, hits non-creatures) when the threats you're answering are non-creatures (enchantments, sorceries, planeswalkers). You run Counterspell ({U}{U}, hits anything) when creatures are the primary threat. In balanced metas: Counterspell. In spell-heavy metas: Negate.

engines.title: Wistfulness End Step
engines.body: You cast Wistfulness at their EOT when your hand is below three cards. Refilling at their EOT means you untap with a full hand and your options for your turn are maximized.

engines.title: Hand Information Value
engines.body: Duress shows you their entire hand before you commit your threats. You use the information: if their hand has no answer to your Harbinger, you deploy Harbinger. If they have Counterspell, you hold Harbinger for a safer window. Information from Duress shapes your next three turns.

engines.title: Three Cards at End of Their Turn
engines.body: You cast Wistfulness ({2}{U}: draw three cards) at their EOT to refill your hand after spending your resources. You don't cast it speculatively — you cast it when your hand is running low and you need to dig for your next key piece.

engines.title: Every Nonbasic is a Trigger
engines.body: Harbinger of the Seas makes every nonbasic land enter tapped. Against 3-color opponents: 3 lands per turn enter tapped = 3 triggers per turn. Over 5 turns: 15 tapped-land triggers. Your early Harbinger compounds throughout the game.

engines.title: Deploy Before Their Fourth Land
engines.body: You deploy Harbinger of the Seas on T3 before they've played their fourth land. Earlier deployment = more nonbasic ETB triggers over the game. Every land they play after Harbinger enters potentially triggers the damage/tap effect. Early is better.

engines.title: Their EOT Always
engines.body: You deploy Floodpits Drowner at their EOT, not your main phase. EOT bounce: they lose the tempo of their bounced permanent AND you untap with a 2/3 in play. Main phase bounce: they draw into replacement on their turn.

engines.title: Two Lands Then Triggers
engines.body: Earthbender Ascension triggers when you play your SECOND land each turn. You play land one: nothing. Play land two: Ascension triggers, put a counter on target creature. You need Ascension in play before land two for this to work.

engines.title: Win Condition Not Setup
engines.body: You counter their win condition, not their cantrips. Against Izzet: counter Slickshot Show-Off, not Opt. Against Mono-Green: counter Earthbender Ascension, not Llanowar Elves. Against Control: counter their board wipe, not their draw spell.

engines.title: Take the Uncounterable Threat
engines.body: You Duress away the card you cannot answer with your main deck. Against Mono-Green: take Mossborn Hydra (uncounterable at 7 lands). Against Izzet Prowess: take Slickshot Show-Off. Against Control: take their sweeper.

engines.title: The Kill Sequence Step by Step
engines.body: 1. Restless Reef in play without summoning sickness. 2. Discard Excruciator (Winternight) OR cast Excruciator directly. 3. Spider-Man copies OR Excruciator resolves → both players exile to 6. 4. Reef attacks → mills 4 → they have 2 cards. 5. Cast Insatiable Avarice targeting them → draw 3 → they lose. Know every step before sitting down.

engines.title: Torpor Orb Interaction
engines.body: Torpor Orb stops ALL ETB triggers including Excruciator's exile and Deceit's discard and Harvester of Misery's sweep. If Torpor Orb is in play (yours or theirs), none of these work. Know which cards in your deck are ETB-dependent before boarding Torpor Orb. In the Orb configuration, you win through Riddler and Deceit bodies only.

engines.title: Floodpits Drowner Timing
engines.body: Practice deploying Floodpits Drowner at their EOT to bounce their key creature. The sequence: they tap out, you flash in Drowner, bounce their threat, untap with advantage.

engines.title: Harbinger Timing
engines.body: Practice the T3 Harbinger line. Against greedy manabases, deploying Harbinger on T3 means their T4 land enters tapped â€” they miss their key play. Know when Harbinger is better than Counterspell.

engines.title: Ascension Trigger Sequencing
engines.body: Practice drawing your second card AFTER Ascension resolves. Cantrip â†’ (Ascension ETB) â†’ second draw triggers Ascension. Wrong order = missed trigger.

engines.title: Duress Targets
engines.body: Practice identifying the correct Duress target. Against Izzet Prowess: take their pump spell. Against Jeskai Control: take their board wipe. Against Mono-Green: take Earthbender Ascension. Know the target before casting.

DimirMidrange.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Identity "On the play, develop Kaito and force them to have the answer. On the draw, deploy Enduring Curiosity and punish them for attacking into it." Dimir Midrange is the premier tempo-control strategy in Standard. Every threat in the deck operates at instant speed or generates immediate value on entry — Floodpits Drowner stuns their best creature, Tishana's Tidebinder locks out ETBs and planeswalker abilities, Kaito, Bane of Nightmares becomes a hexproof 3/4 Ninja the moment it resolves on your turn. The opponent is always reacting. You are always the one asking questions. T
DimirMidrange.mulligan: mulligan and sequencing priority signal available.

engines.title: Flash Threats + Card Draw
engines.body: Deploy threats at instant speed on the opponent's end step. Each threat generates value immediately. Enduring Curiosity turns every successful attack into a card. Kaito's 0 ability generates a card every turn. You're always drawing into more answers.

engines.title: Tempo Disruption
engines.body: Tishana's Tidebinder counters their key ability and strips the permanent. Floodpits Drowner stuns their best attacker and threatens to shuffle it away. Azure Beastbinder blanks their best permanent on attack. Every creature is also disruption.

engines.title: Out-Resource + Close
engines.body: Generate card advantage until the opponent runs out of answers, then close with Restless Reef attacks, Cecil transforming into a 4/4 lifelink, or Kaito's emblem making all your creatures bigger. The deck rarely goldfishes — it wins by exhausting opponent options.

engines.title: You Want Flexibility
engines.body: The deck shifts roles game-to-game and even turn-to-turn. Against aggro you're the control deck using flash blockers and removal. Against control you're the beatdown deck attacking through counters and protecting threats. Against midrange mirrors you're the tempo deck with more instant-speed plays. No two games feel the same.

engines.title: You Want Simple Lines
engines.body: This deck has a high decision density. When to deploy Kaito vs. hold mana for Tidebinder. When to attack with Cecil knowing you'll lose life to Darkness. When to promise the fish for Into the Flood Maw. When to blight your own creature for Requiting Hex. Every turn has meaningful choices. It rewards reps.

engines.title: Kaito, Bane of Nightmares
engines.body: In Hand WR: 56.2% · Not In Hand: 45.9%. The largest gap in the deck by a wide margin — without Kaito you're below 50%. Mulligan hardest for this card on the play. Played WR 53.3% is lower than In Hand WR because the games where you play him late are already harder games.

engines.title: The Unagi of Kyoshi Island
engines.body: In Hand WR: 60.2% — but Side-out WR (64.1%) is higher than Side-in WR (57.6%). You win MORE when you take it back out post-board than when you bring it in. Bring Unagi in selectively vs. control only, not speculatively. The field is siding it in against the wrong matchups.

engines.title: Cecil, Dark Knight
engines.body: In Hand WR: 56.6% — higher impact than Enduring Curiosity (+5.6) and Floodpits Drowner (+5.2). Cecil is not a flex slot. His 2/3 deathtouch body plus lifelink transformation carries more measurable weight than the Darkness drain cost suggests. The data confirms keeping 2 copies.

engines.title: Requiting Hex
engines.body: Strong In Hand impact (+3.4 pts) but the field wins 61% of games when they remove it post-board — highest side-out WR in the dataset. Clear signal it's being kept in against the wrong matchups. Take it out aggressively in G2/G3 against any non-aggro opponent. It's an aggro card, not a midrange card.

engines.title: Deep-Cavern Bat
engines.body: 73.4% of Dimir Midrange main decks run Deep-Cavern Bat (+3.9 pts). {1}{B} 1/1 flying — ETB: target opponent reveals hand, you choose a nonland card, that card gains Disguise. Strong hand disruption + evasive threat that the broader field has widely adopted. Zuxas's list skips it — a meaningful departure from the field consensus worth testing.

engines.title: Essence Scatter
engines.body: Side-in WR 51.6%, Side-out WR 55.9% — you win more when it stays out than when it comes in. Lowest differential of any card in the dataset. The matchups it targets either don't come up enough at the RC level or there are better answers. Primary candidate for replacement in the sideboard.

engines.title: Kaito, Bane of Nightmares
engines.body: {2}{U}{B}. Ninjutsu {1}{U}{B} (return unblocked attacker, put Kaito in attacking). During your turn with loyalty counters: 3/4 Ninja with hexproof — opponents have no clean instant-speed answer. 0: Surveil 2, draw a card for each opponent who lost life this turn. That's a free draw every turn you attacked. −2: Tap + 2 stun counters on target creature.

engines.title: Enduring Curiosity
engines.body: {2}{U}{U} Enchantment Creature — Cat Glimmer. Flash. Draw a card whenever any creature you control deals combat damage. When it dies as a creature, returns to battlefield as an enchantment — not a creature, so targeted removal that requires creature type fails. As an enchantment it still triggers. The opponent needs exile to answer it permanently.

engines.title: Floodpits Drowner
engines.body: {1}{U} 2/1 Flash Vigilance. ETB: tap target creature + stun counter (can't untap next turn). {1}{U}{T}: shuffle this creature and target stunned creature into their owners' libraries. Combined: deploy at their end step, stun their best threat, then on your turn pay {1}{U} to shuffle both away. Two-for-one that generates a tempo swing plus library manipulation.

engines.title: Tishana's Tidebinder
engines.body: {2}{U} 3/2 Flash. ETB: counter target activated or triggered ability. If an artifact/creature/planeswalker ability is countered, that permanent loses ALL abilities while Tidebinder is on the battlefield. Hits: any ETB trigger on resolution, a planeswalker's activated ability, any activated ability like looting or sacrifice effects. A resolved Tidebinder is a threat + permanent ability lock in one

engines.title: Azure Beastbinder
engines.body: {1}{U} 1/3 Vigilance. Can't be blocked by power 2+. On attack: target opponent permanent loses all abilities until your next turn; if creature, base 2/2 until your next turn. Blanks their best creature or planeswalker on attack — can't be blocked by most things, turns their 5/5 into a vanilla 2/2, and strips walker abilities. Vigilance means it blocks the turn after too.

engines.title: Cecil, Dark Knight
engines.body: {B} 2/3 Deathtouch. Darkness: whenever Cecil deals damage, you lose that life too. At half life: untap + transform → Cecil, Redeemed Paladin 4/4 Lifelink. Indestructible-granting Protect ability for other attackers. High variance: kills efficiently but drains you. When you flip him at 10 life the lifelink starts recovering it. Best deployed mid-to-late when you can absorb the life loss.

engines.title: Requiting Hex
engines.body: {B} Instant. Additional cost: optionally blight 1 (put −1/−1 counter on a creature you control). Destroy target creature with MV 2 or less. If blighted: gain 2 life. The blight target can be Loch Mare (removing one of its built-in −1/−1 counters) or a creature already at −1/−1 to sacrifice it cleanly. Against Mono-Red: the life gain is critical. Against aggro mirrors: answers all their 1-2 drops c

engines.title: Long Goodbye
engines.body: {1}{B} Instant. Can't be countered. Destroy target creature or planeswalker with MV 3 or less. The "can't be countered" text matters against blue decks — your removal resolves even through their countermagic. Hits Kaito (MV 3), most 2-drops, all 1-drops. Slightly more expensive than Requiting Hex but hits walkers and can't be interacted with by counterspells.

engines.title: Shoot the Sheriff
engines.body: {1}{B} Instant. Destroy target non-outlaw creature. Outlaws (Assassins, Mercenaries, Pirates, Rogues, Warlocks) are exempt — everyone else dies. In practice this means you can't use it on Pirates or Rogues. Most creatures in the format are not outlaws. Note: your own Spyglass Siren (Siren Pirate) is an outlaw — can't be targeted by opponent's Sheriff either.

engines.title: Into the Flood Maw
engines.body: {U} Instant. Gift a tapped Fish: bounce creature (or any nonland permanent if gift promised). The gift mode gives them a 1/1 Fish token. The calculus: no gift → bounce any creature. Gift → bounce any nonland permanent (hits enchantments, artifacts, planeswalkers) but they get a 1/1. Usually worth promising the gift when bouncing an enchantment or planeswalker that would otherwise be hard to answer

engines.title: Phantom Interference
engines.body: {U} Spree. +{3}: create 2/2 Spirit with flying. +{1}: counter target spell unless pay {2}. Can pay both modes simultaneously for {U}+{3}+{1} = {1}{U}{U}{U}. Most useful: the soft counter mode at {1}{U}. Not a hard counter — they can pay {2} to resolve. Best against opponents who are tapped out on their turn. The Spirit mode is too expensive to see regular play.

engines.title: Spell Snare
engines.body: {U} Instant. Counter target spell with MV exactly 2. Niche but powerful — MV 2 is a heavily played slot in Standard right now. Hits most 2-drop threats and interaction. Extremely efficient at {U}. The 1-of count reflects its narrowness — it's dead against control decks and low-curve aggro, but a blowout against midrange 2-drops like Raffine, Fable tokens, or any 2-drop value piece.

engines.title: Setup + First Pressure
engines.body: Turn 1: Fetch untapped dual or play basic. Spyglass Siren for a 1/1 flier + Map token. On the play: Siren → surveil/explore on turn 2 is your fastest start. Cecil, Dark Knight at {B} on turn 1 — instant 2/3 deathtouch but remember Darkness drains you each hit. Requiting Hex held for their turn-2 threat. Spell Snare open if on the draw vs known 2-drop openings.

engines.title: Deploy the Engine
engines.body: On the play: Kaito, Bane of Nightmares — immediately becomes a 3/4 hexproof Ninja. Force them to have an answer before their next turn. On the draw: Enduring Curiosity — flash it at their end step to set up turn-3 attacks that draw cards. Kaito on the draw is also correct if they haven't deployed a threat; the hexproof on your turn means they can't target it at all on your turn.

engines.title: Lock + Close
engines.body: Floodpits Drowner at their end step — stun their attacker, hold shuffle threat. Tishana's Tidebinder in response to any ability. Azure Beastbinder attacks blanking their best permanent while being unblockable by most creatures. Restless Reef activates as a 4/4 deathtouch attacker when you have spare mana. The game typically ends on turn 6-7 with the opponent having exhausted their removal on redun

engines.title: The Turn-3 Choice
engines.body: Play Kaito when on the play — you can deploy him on your turn and he immediately has hexproof while you have priority. Opponents can't answer him at instant speed on your turn. Play Enduring Curiosity when on the draw — you're a turn behind, so flash it in at their end step. Curiosity as a 4/3 enchantment creature is difficult to answer, and the draw engine operates even without attacking. Both pl

engines.title: The Life Math
engines.body: Cecil at {B} is an outstanding rate but every point of damage he deals also comes off your life. Do the math before attacking: if Cecil deals 3 damage to their creature through blocking, you also lose 3. Plan when you want to flip him — at 10 life (half of 20) he transforms into the Redeemed Paladin. Don't flip him when you're already losing — 4/4 lifelink needs attacks to gain life back, and if t

engines.title: When to Promise the Fish
engines.body: No gift: bounce any creature (sorcery speed if they have one). Gift: bounce any nonland permanent AND they get a 1/1 Fish. Always promise the gift when bouncing: enchantments, artifacts, planeswalkers (Enduring Curiosity, a resolved walker). The 1/1 Fish is irrelevant if you're bouncing something worth 3+ mana. Don't promise the gift when the 1/1 Fish is relevant — they're at low life, flood the b

engines.title: Stun First, Shuffle Later
engines.body: ETB stun goes on the stack when Drowner enters. The activated shuffle ability ({1}{U}{T}: shuffle self and stunned creature) is a separate ability. Sequence: Deploy at their end step → stun their threat → on your turn, either attack around the stunned creature or pay {1}{U} to shuffle both away. Don't immediately shuffle — assess whether the stunned creature poses a greater threat than a 2/1 body

engines.title: Flash Drowner → Upkeep Stun
engines.body: On the play you have tempo — use it proactively. If you can hold {2}{U} during their T3 (when Drowner becomes affordable on your end of T2 into T3), flash Drowner during their upkeep before their main phase. Their Llanowar Elves and Badgermole Cub untap at the start of their turn, then immediately get tapped by Drowner before they can use them. They walk into their main phase with zero mana from d

Requiting Hex ({1}{B}{W}) exiles it on ETB before the earthbend resolves. Both answers are available the turn they play Cub on T2 if you kept mana open. Before the earthbend resolves, cast Requiting Hex ({1}{B}{W}, exile target creature MV ≤ 2). Cub is exiled. engines.body: Oracle ruling: Into the Flood Maw's no-gift mode says "return target creature an opponent controls to its owner's hand" — no land restriction. The earthbent land is simultaneously a land AND a creature, so it qualifies as a creature target . You can bounce it. On their T3 (they play Icetill Explorer or Ascension), flash in Floodpits Drowner EOT. ETB taps their Explorer + any other creatures. They untap into a tapped board. Two cards (Hex + Drowner) destroyed two of their turns. Your Kaito on T3 now

engines.title: Let Earthbend Resolve, Then Hex
engines.body: When you let the earthbend resolve first: Cub earthbends onto a Fabled Passage (two landfall triggers happen — they get value). THEN you Hex the Cub afterward. You lose the double-trigger prevention, but you still exile their primary mana doubler. The earthbent Passage returns tapped at EOT anyway. When is this better? When you want to see which land they earthbend (tells you their hand contents —

engines.title: Tidebinder Counters Fabled Passage
engines.body: Sequence: They tap and sacrifice Fabled Passage to activate it (sacrifice is the cost — Passage is now gone). The ability goes on the stack: "Search for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle. Then if you control 4+ lands, untap that land." You flash in Tishana's Tidebinder ({1}{U}{G}), ETB: counter target activated or triggered ability. Target the Fabled Passage activ

engines.title: Activated & Triggered Abilities
engines.body: Tidebinder can counter any activated or triggered ability — not just Fabled Passage: Escape Tunnel unblockable mode — they sacrifice Tunnel to make Harmonizer unblockable. Counter it. Tunnel is gone, creature is still blockable. Combo stops. Mightform Harmonizer landfall trigger — counter the "double target creature's power" triggered ability. Their combo doubling doesn't happen this land drop. Ea

engines.title: Flash During Their Upkeep
engines.body: On the play, their creatures untap at the start of their turn — then during upkeep (before draw, before main phase) you can flash Drowner in. Their Llanowar Elves just untapped. Drowner ETB taps it again before they ever get to use it for mana. They go into their main phase with Elves tapped, Badgermole Cub tapped, anything else tapped. They lose a full turn of mana without being able to respond d

engines.title: Their End Step Drowner
engines.body: Flash Drowner at their end step after they've deployed their board and passed. ETB taps: Icetill Explorer, Badgermole Cub, the earthbent land-creature, Sazh's Chocobo — everything. They pass to your turn with a full board that can't block. You untap, attack freely. The earthbent land is a creature — it's a valid Drowner tap target and also can't generate mana while tapped, cutting off any mana tri

engines.title: Flash During Their Attack Step
engines.body: After they declare attackers, flash Drowner. ETB taps everything that isn't attacking — their non-attackers can't block, Badgermole Cub can't tap for mana this turn, the earthbent land-creature is locked. Their attack is isolated to exactly what they declared. No tricks, no backup, no mana. Block efficiently and swing back with your full board next turn.

engines.title: Return Any Creature (Free)
engines.body: Oracle text: "Return target creature an opponent controls to its owner's hand." No conditions, no cost, no 1/1 fish. Targets any creature they control. This is your primary use case in almost every matchup because the creatures are almost always the more urgent problem: Earthbent land-creature — the no-gift mode targets any creature they control, and the earthbent land qualifies. Bounce it, it ret

engines.title: Return Any Nonland Permanent (They Get a Tapped 1/1)
engines.body: Oracle text (gift promised): "Instead return target nonland permanent an opponent controls to its owner's hand." They create a tapped 1/1 blue Fish token first. Gift the fish when the enchantment or non-creature threat is the actual problem — when a creature bounce doesn't solve what's killing you: Sapling Nursery — bounce it EOT when they're tapped out. They get a 1/1 Fish but lose the tree and m

engines.title: Siren Connects → Kaito Appears
engines.body: T1 Spyglass Siren (1/1 flier, Recon on entry). T2 swing, they likely don't block (1 damage). Ninjutsu Kaito: return Siren to hand, Kaito enters attacking. Bat trigger: look at their hand, exile a nonland card. They've lost their best piece by T2 before they've played a creature.

engines.title: They Must Tap Down to Answer
engines.body: To answer Kaito they need to attack back with power 3+ creature, or use sorcery-speed removal. Both require tapping out. That's your window: hold Requiting Hex or Floodpits Drowner. When they tap for the answer, flash in Drowner EOT to tap everything else. Your next attack with Kaito is free.

engines.title: Kaito Loyalty Builds
engines.body: Each Kaito attack generates a 3/2 Cecil if he doesn't hit, or -2 to look at top 3 and grab a creature. Cecil with Kaito in play: transformed Cecil becomes a 4/4 with lifelink and double strike, which closes fast. The pressure loop forces them to commit resources to deal with Kaito, leaving no mana for disrupting your flash responses.

engines.title: Kaito Is Your Engine
engines.body: You're one turn ahead. The optimal curve is T1 Spyglass Siren or Cecil → T2 hold open for Requiting Hex / interaction → T3 Kaito. Deploying Kaito before their 3-mana interaction comes online means hexproof protects him from anything they could answer with. Kaito on the play generates an average of +10.3 points of win rate. Against aggro on the play, keep Kaito and trim Enduring Curiosity. You can

engines.title: Curiosity Is Your Engine
engines.body: You're a tempo behind. Flash Enduring Curiosity at their end step — it arrives as a 4/3 with the draw trigger active, and you untap with your full turn to attack with it and generate cards. Against aggro on the draw: Curiosity provides a large body that blocks their threats AND draws cards when your creatures connect. The opponent is ahead on board — Curiosity's card advantage catches you up. If C

engines.title: Life ≥ 14
engines.body: At 14+ life, Cecil attacking as a 2/3 deals 2 to them and 2 to you (Darkness), leaving you at 12+ with deathtouch threatening blocks. This is almost always profitable — the damage pressure + deathtouch threat outweighs the self-drain. Attack freely.

engines.title: Life 8–13
engines.body: Danger zone. Ask: "If I take 2 from Darkness AND they burn me for 3 on their turn, am I dead?" Against Mono-Red with 3 cards in hand at 10 life: attacking with Cecil puts you to 8, and two burn spells kill you. Don't attack. Against Midrange at 10 life: no burn in their deck, attack freely. Context is everything.

engines.title: Life ≤ Half (Flip Zone)
engines.body: When you're at half your starting life (10 in Standard), Cecil transforms into a 4/4 with lifelink. The transformation is the payoff — a 4/4 lifelink swings the race by 8 points (4 damage dealt + 4 life gained). The trick: you can manipulate your life total to flip Cecil using shock lands, Multiversal Passage (pay 2 life), or Bitter Triumph (pay 3 life). Sometimes it's correct to deliberately take

engines.title: Library Watch Points
engines.body: Start counting your library when it drops below 15 cards. With Curiosity active and 3+ creatures, you're drawing 4–5 cards per turn cycle (draw step + combat triggers). At 15 cards remaining: you have ~3 attack steps before decking. At 10 cards: ~2 attack steps. If the game is close but not won, consider intentionally NOT attacking with some creatures to reduce draw triggers — a 1/1 Siren not atta

engines.title: Preventing Self-Deck
engines.body: If you're ahead on board but low on library: (1) stop attacking with non-essential creatures — only attack with enough to be lethal in 1-2 turns, (2) use Floodpits Drowner 's shuffle ability — shuffling Drowner and their creature back into libraries effectively adds 2 cards to your library, (3) don't flash in additional creatures if you don't need more attackers — each new creature is another mand

engines.title: Verge Without a Basic
engines.body: Gloomlake Verge taps for {U} unconditionally, but only produces {B} if you control an Island or Swamp. On turn 1 with ONLY Verge in play: you can cast Spyglass Siren ({U}) but NOT Cecil ({B}) or Requiting Hex ({B}). If your hand has Cecil + Verge as your only land: you cannot cast Cecil turn 1. Solution: sequence your land drops so turn-1 Swamp/Watery Grave enables {B}, then Verge on turn 2 produc

engines.title: Multiversal Passage Life Cost
engines.body: Multiversal Passage enters as any basic land type but costs 2 life (enters as a copy of a basic, pays life like a shock land). Against aggro at 12 life: paying 2 to fix your mana puts you to 10 — exactly the threshold where their burn range kills you. Against control: the 2 life is irrelevant. Sequence accordingly: vs aggro, play basics and Verge first, Passage only when necessary. Vs control, Pas

engines.title: Max 4 Cards In/Out
engines.body: In most matchups, board 3-4 cards maximum. The deck's synergies (evasive creatures → Kaito ninjutsu → Curiosity draws) break down when you cut too many pieces. Even against aggro, keep enough creatures to enable your card advantage engines.

engines.title: SBOWR vs SBIWR
engines.body: Side-Board Out Win Rate (SBOWR) vs Side-Board In Win Rate (SBIWR). When a card's SBOWR > SBIWR, you win MORE when it stays out. Example: Essence Scatter has 55.9% SBOWR vs 51.6% SBIWR — you're statistically better leaving it in the board. Track this metric for every SB card.

engines.title: GY Hate vs Non-GY Decks
engines.body: 81.5% of Dimir players bring Soul-Guide Lantern in vs Mono-Green Landfall. The card has a 32.7% side-in WR in that matchup — the worst SB card possible. Lantern does nothing meaningful against Landfall triggers. Only bring GY hate when the opponent's GY is their actual win condition.

engines.title: Draw off Curiosity, Then Deploy
engines.body: You can use Ninjutsu during the end of combat step, AFTER damage has been dealt. This means: attack with Spyglass Siren → Siren deals 1 damage → Enduring Curiosity triggers, draw a card → if you draw Kaito off the trigger → use Ninjutsu to put Kaito in attacking (even though damage already happened) → Kaito can still use an ability post-combat. You effectively got the damage + draw trigger from Si

engines.title: Saving Creatures from Removal
engines.body: When an opponent targets your attacking creature with removal after blocks: if the creature is unblocked, you can Ninjutsu it back to hand in response, dodging the removal AND putting Kaito into play. The removal fizzles (no legal target), and Kaito arrives safely. This turns their removal spell into a 2-for-0 in your favor (they spent a card on nothing, you gained a Kaito). Always hold Ninjutsu m

engines.title: When They Stabilize
engines.body: You started as beatdown vs Control. They stuck a sweeper or stabilized at 8 life with a wall of counters. Don't keep slamming into their shields — transition to Survival mode. Hold your remaining threats, deploy them at instant speed on their end step, and grind through Enduring Curiosity. The worst Dimir play vs Control is "I was beatdown so I'll keep being beatdown" after they've turned the corn

engines.title: When They're Out of Gas
engines.body: You started in Survival vs Mono-Red. You stabilized at 6 life with Cecil on board and Curiosity drawing cards. They're topdecking. NOW transition to Beatdown — attack with everything. Curiosity refills your hand. Every turn you wait gives them draw steps to find burn. Once the aggro player is empty-handed and you have cards, you're the aggressor. Push lethal before they draw out of it.

engines.title: They Hold Mana Open
engines.body: If the opponent passes with {1}{U} open: they likely have a counterspell. Deploy your less important creature first to bait it. If they counter: deploy Kaito next turn when they're tapped out. If they don't counter: they either don't have it or are saving it for something bigger — probe with the smaller threat and hold Kaito.

engines.title: They Attack Into Open Mana
engines.body: When the opponent attacks knowing you have flash creatures available: they either have removal for your flash blocker or they're bluffing. If you've seen their removal suite from Duress: deploy the flash blocker. If you haven't: sometimes it's correct to NOT block with the flash creature and instead deploy it post-combat for value. The 2 damage you take is worth the creature surviving.

engines.title: They Don't Play a Land
engines.body: If the opponent misses a land drop: they're flooding or stuck. Ramp up aggression immediately. Deploy threats on curve rather than holding for value. A mana-screwed opponent can't answer your threats efficiently — every turn they miss is a turn your Kaito generates free cards. Press the advantage before they draw out of it.

engines.title: When to Register Dimir
engines.body: Register Dimir when the field leans toward midrange mirrors, control, and combo. Your card advantage engines outgrind other fair decks. Specifically: when Dimir Excruciator (favorable), Control strategies (favorable ~64%), and midrange mirrors (even ~50%) make up 30%+ of your expected field. Dimir thrives in a thinking-player's metagame where games go long and decision density matters.

engines.title: When to Audible
engines.body: Consider a different deck when Mono-Green Landfall (38% WR), Mono-White Aggro (37% WR), and other go-wide aggro strategies dominate the field above 30% combined. Dimir's removal suite is efficient but limited — when the board floods faster than you can answer threats one-for-one, the deck struggles. If your local meta is 40%+ aggro, Izzet Lessons or Mono-Green may be better positioned.

engines.title: Survival Mode
