engines.body: Prioritize interaction in your opener. Mulligan for Requiting Hex or Shoot the Sheriff. Play Floodpits Drowner to stun their best attacker — a 2/1 with vigilance that also stuns blocks profitably. Hold mana for instant-speed responses. Once you stabilize at 10+ life: Cecil, Dark Knight becomes an option (his lifelink after transformation helps recover). Enduring Curiosity takes over the late game

engines.title: Beatdown Mode
engines.body: You're the aggressor. Deploy threats on the play before their counterspells are online. Spyglass Siren on turn 1 applies pressure before their turn-3 Counterspell mana. Kaito on turn 3 has hexproof — they can't answer it on your turn. Long Goodbye can't be countered — use it to remove their blockers through their own countermagic. Don't give them free turns to draw sweepers.

engines.title: Tempo Mode
engines.body: Role management is the game. Flash in Tidebinder to counter their ETB. Beastbinder blanks their top threat on attack. Hold bounce for their key enchantment or planeswalker. Enduring Curiosity as an enchantment is very difficult for other midrange decks to answer — most don't run enchantment removal main. The first Curiosity that sticks usually wins the resource battle.

engines.title: Disrupt + Clock
engines.body: Apply clock pressure while holding disruption. Spider-Sense counters triggered abilities (Living End, combo resolution triggers). Tishana's Tidebinder counters any activated ability on their combo piece. Duress from the SB hits their setup spells. Soul-Guide Lantern handles GY-based combos. You don't need to stop every piece — disrupting the key one while your clock counts down is enough.

engines.title: Kaito, Bane of Nightmares ×4
engines.body: The deck's identity card. Hexproof on your turn means no clean answer. The 0 ability generates free card draw every turn you attacked. Never board out Kaito — if the matchup doesn't fit, play a different deck.

engines.title: Tishana's Tidebinder ×4
engines.body: Versatile across every matchup — counters ETBs, locks planeswalker abilities, strips abilities from key permanents. There's no matchup where this is completely dead. Maybe trim 1 in pure aggro mirrors but rarely.

engines.title: Floodpits Drowner ×4
engines.body: Flash blocker + stun + shuffle threat. Functions as removal, blocker, and tempo piece simultaneously. The shuffle ability removes opponent's stunned threats from the game entirely. Too versatile to leave out of any matchup.

engines.title: Psychic Frog ×4
engines.body: Your best card. Four copies non-negotiable — the deck is built around Frog connecting and drawing cards. Below 4 and your card advantage engine collapses.

engines.title: Floodpits Drowner ×4
engines.body: Your flash tempo play. Four copies ensures you have the EOT bounce every game. The deck's identity is built around Drowner at their end step.

engines.title: Kaito, Dancing Shadow
engines.body: 2 in fast metas, 3 in slower grind metas. Kaito is your most powerful value engine but costs 3 — too slow against the fastest aggro decks.

engines.title: Into the Flood Maw
engines.body: 1 copy in most builds. 2 copies when you face lots of wide boards where bouncing two creatures is worth 3 mana. Cut to 0 in aggro-heavy fields where tempo is king.

engines.title: Counterspell vs Spell Snare ratio
engines.body: 3 Counterspell + 2 Snare is the baseline. Shift to 4 Snare in Mono-Green-heavy metas (Snare hard-counters both their key MV-2 spells). Shift to 4 Counterspell in control mirrors where MV-2 threats are less relevant.

engines.title: Psychic Frog Attacks
engines.body: Practice evaluating when Frog can attack safely. They need a blocker with 3+ power to kill Frog in combat. Identify their blockers, calculate combat, attack when safe — and keep mana open to protect with Counterspell.

engines.title: Flash Creature Sequencing
engines.body: Practice deploying Floodpits Drowner at their EOT, not your main phase. EOT bounce lets you untap with tempo. Main phase bounce gives them a full draw step to recast the bounced threat — always deploy at their EOT.

engines.title: Counterspell Priority Drills
engines.body: Practice deciding between countering their key spell vs developing your board. The rule: counter the thing that wins them the game, develop when nothing threatens to win immediately. Wrong counter assignment is the most common mistake.

engines.title: Spell Snare Matchup Drills
engines.body: Practice Spell Snare targets by matchup. Mono-Green: Badgermole Cub MV 2 and Earthbender Ascension MV 2 — both hard-countered by Snare for {U}. Know every relevant MV-2 spell in the format and whether Snare catches it.

matchups.notes: Requiting Hex and Shoot the Sheriff are critical. Stabilize, then grind.

matchups.opponent: Mono-Red is your hardest G1. Their aggressive curve (turn-1 threat, turn-2 threat, turn-3 Goblin Bombardment or burn spell) outpaces your 3-drop plan. Requiting Hex at {B} kills their 1-2 drops for nothing — this is your most important card. Prioritize keeping any hand with Hex or Sheriff on the draw. Floodpits Drowner as a 2/1 flash blocker that stuns their threat buys two turns. Mulligan aggressively for interaction — a hand of five 3-drops loses to Mono-Red G1 on the draw. On the play: T1 Spyglass Siren, T2 hold open {B} for Hex, T3 Kaito to force immediate answers. On the draw: Skip Siren, keep Hex + Sheriff, stabilize first, then Enduring Curiosity when they're out of gas. Out In −2 Into the Flood Maw +1 Requiting Hex −1 Spell Snare +1 Bitter Triumph −1 Phantom Interference +1 Day of Black Sun Day of Black Sun at {X}{B}{B}: cast at X=2 to destroy all MV ≤ 2 creatures — wipes their entire early board. Into the Flood Maw is too slow vs their curve. Phantom Interference's soft counter is irrelevant — they're not casting spells you need to counter, they're casting creatures you need to kill. The extra Bitter Triumph answers any threat they might deploy that your cheaper removal misses. Key needle: Cecil, Dark Knight is a liability vs Mono-Red — the Darkness trigger drains you while they're burning your face. Don't attack with Cecil until you're already at half life and ready to flip. If you're at 10 life and Cecil is attacking into a 3/2, the 3 damage you deal = 3 life lost = you're at 7. Dangerous. Either use Cecil as a blocker (deathtouch) or wait to flip safely. % Point Edges +2–3 pts: Play/draw engine split. On the play, keep Kaito — you can T3 deploy before their shields are up and force an immediate answer. On the draw, keep Enduring Curiosity instead — Curiosity flashed on their end step provides a 4/3 body that blocks AND draws when your creatures connect next turn. The wrong engine selection here loses you 2–3 percentage points against aggro. +1–2 pts: T1 Requiting Hex the mana dork. If they open with a 1-drop threat, Hex it immediately. Don't save Hex for their better threats later — in aggro matchups, the tempo gained from killing their T1 play before they untap is worth more than holding for a "better" target. Every turn their clock is delayed is a turn closer to your Curiosity engine. +1 pt: Cecil as deathtouch wall only. Against Mono-Red specifically, never attack with Cecil pre-flip. A 2/3 deathtouch blocker that trades with any attacker is worth more than 2 damage + 2 Darkness drain into their burn range. Wait for flip, then swing with 4/4 lifelink to stabilize.

matchups.notes: 38% WR across 1,900 games. Don't bring Soul-Guide Lantern in. Cecil and Requiting Hex are your best cards.

matchups.opponent: This is your worst common matchup at 38% win rate across 1,900 games (Plat–Mythic BO3). Their large bodies outclass your individual removal cards when they get ahead on board. The key to winning is using your flash package proactively and in the correct windows — on the play, Drowner flashed in during their upkeep taps their Llanowar Elves before they can use it; on the draw, Spell Snare hard counters Badgermole Cub (MV 2) and Earthbender Ascension (MV 2) for one blue mana. Your Tidebinder counters their Fabled Passage activated ability after they sacrifice it (they lose the land AND the Passage), Escape Tunnel's unblockable mode, and Harmonizer's landfall trigger. See the Lines tab for full sequences and timing windows. Data-ranked card impact vs Mono-Green: Deep-Cavern Bat +14.7 pts (not in list — note for future testing), Cecil +14.3 pts, Requiting Hex +13.5 pts, Bitter Triumph +10.6 pts, Kaito +10.6 pts. Spyglass Siren is nearly irrelevant (+1.9 pts). Soulstone Sanctuary and Restless Reef are both negative — don't activate them here, just play lands. Out In −1 Phantom Interference +1 Strategic Betrayal −1 Loch Mare +1 Bitter Triumph DO NOT cut Spell Snare. Spell Snare ({U}) hard counters Badgermole Cub (MV 2) and Earthbender Ascension (MV 2) — their two most important early plays — for one blue mana with no way to pay through it. Phantom Interference ({1}{U}) only soft counters for "pay {2}" which they can often afford off a mana dork. Snare stays in. Phantom Interference comes out — it's a Spree spell whose counter mode is pay-aroundable exactly when they have excess mana from Cub. Loch Mare at 5 mana is too slow for a matchup decided by turn 5 — cleanest cut. DO NOT board in Soul-Guide Lantern — its side-in WR vs Mono-Green is 32.7%, the single worst SB card in this matchup. 81.5% of Dimir players bring it in anyway. They lose. Ghost Vacuum is also bad (37.6%). Duress is a dead card vs a creature deck (45.1% side-in WR). Strategic Betrayal is your best SB option: exiles a creature AND their GY simultaneously. Key needle: Counter Badgermole Cub's ETB with Tidebinder on the stack. Cecil, Dark Knight is your most impactful card in this matchup (+14.3 pts, 71.8% MD inclusion across Dimir builds that run it) — his 2/3 deathtouch trades with everything and the lifelink after flip helps survive their pressure. Don't let Cecil die before he flips if you can avoid it. % Point Edges +3–4 pts: Kill Llanowar Elves on sight, T1. Landfall's explosive turns (Cub on T2 from Elves mana, Ascension T3 ahead of curve) all depend on the mana dork surviving. Requiting Hex for {B} on their Elves before they untap prevents the Cub acceleration entirely. From the RC Vancouver Landfall guide: their pilot called Dimir "preventing the board from happening" as the only way Dimir wins — and that starts with killing the Elves. +2 pts: Tidebinder on Fabled Passage activation. When they sacrifice Fabled Passage, the "search for a basic" ability goes on the stack. Flash Tidebinder in response — counter the search ability. They lose the Passage AND get no land. This is a 2-for-0 that denies a landfall trigger AND a land drop simultaneously. Also works on Escape Tunnel's activated mode. +1–2 pts: Spell Snare hits both Cub AND Ascension. Badgermole Cub (MV 2) and Earthbender Ascension (MV 2) are their two most important early plays. Spell Snare at {U} hard-counters both with no pay-around clause. This is why you NEVER cut Spell Snare in this matchup — it's your most mana-efficient answer to their best cards.

matchups.notes: 44% WR, 1,400 games. Cecil +16.3 pts #1 card. Day of Black Sun best SB bring-in. Don't board Intimidation Tactics.

matchups.opponent: Izzet Prowess (19% meta) wins through efficient spellslinging — cantrips pump their creatures and their burn reaches across the table. Your tempo tools are less effective here because they're not resolving ETBs worth countering. The matchup is won through early pressure (Cecil as a deathtouch wall that trades up) and having enough removal density to answer their threats before they go wide. Data-ranked card impact vs Izzet Prowess (1,400 games): Cecil +16.3 pts, Requiting Hex +10.9 pts, Enduring Curiosity +10.7 pts, Wan Shi Tong +10.2 pts, Tishana's Tidebinder +8.5 pts. Deep-Cavern Bat is -1.1 pts (hurts — their prowess creatures don't care about hand disruption). Bitter Triumph is -1.2 pts and has a 60.2% SBOWR — take it out. Restless Reef is -4.1 pts — never activate vs Prowess. Out In −2 Into the Flood Maw +1 Day of Black Sun −1 Bitter Triumph +1 Duress −1 Loch Mare +1 Annul Day of Black Sun is your best SB card here (+9.7 pts, 72.2% side-in rate). Duress +8.1 pts strips their key spells before they resolve. Annul +8.8 pts — they often run key enchantments or artifacts. Do NOT board Intimidation Tactics — it has -12.6 pts SBOWR, actively losing you games when kept in. Essence Scatter is also weak here (+1.0 pts only). Into the Flood Maw is too slow vs their curve. Bitter Triumph's 60.2% SBOWR means you should be siding it out more aggressively. Key needle: Cecil, Dark Knight is your #1 card in this matchup at +16.3 pts. His 2/3 deathtouch blocks and kills their prowess creatures cleanly. Their pumped creatures all have base power 1 — deathtouch makes Cecil an efficient trade regardless of their pump spells. Keep Cecil in; the Darkness drain is manageable because their burn reach is limited when you're not losing life from combat. % Point Edges +2–3 pts: Duress targeting Stormchaser's Talent. Post-bans (Cori-Steel Cutter gone), Stormchaser's Talent is their key noncreature engine. Duress on T1 stripping Talent before it resolves removes their primary card advantage + token generation axis. Without Talent, their prowess creatures are individual threats that your removal handles 1-for-1. With Talent active, they generate tokens and draw that overwhelm you. +1–2 pts: Annul hits Stormchaser's Talent on the stack. At {U}, Annul hard-counters their enchantment-based engine for one mana. This is the matchup where Annul justifies its SB slot most clearly. Counter Talent on T2 before they have backup mana. +1 pt: Never activate Restless Reef. Reef is −4.1 pts in this matchup — the mana you spend activating it is mana you could have spent on removal or flash threats. Against Prowess, every open mana matters more as a threat of interaction than as a 4/4 attacker.

matchups.notes: Spyglass Siren +13.5 pts — the most impactful evasive threat in the mirror. Don't board Ghost Vacuum (-16 pts).

matchups.opponent: The mirror is a tempo game decided by who deploys the most impactful threat first and protects it. The conventional wisdom ("first Curiosity wins") is supported but incomplete — the data shows Spyglass Siren (+13.5 pts) and Kaito (+11.9 pts) are just as decisive as Curiosity (+0.7 pts, surprisingly low). Enduring Curiosity is nearly neutral in the mirror because both players run it. The differentiating cards are the evasive threats that the mirror opponent can't easily answer. Data-ranked card impact vs Dimir Mirror (1,300 games): Fountainport +15.5 pts (not in your list — worth noting), Spyglass Siren +13.5 pts, Kaito +11.9 pts, Wan Shi Tong +11.0 pts, Cecil +10.9 pts, Tishana's Tidebinder +9.4 pts. Requiting Hex +6.2 pts — still useful as a SB card (SBIWR 59.7%, SBOWR 64.0% — bring it back in). Enduring Curiosity only +0.7 pts in this matchup. Out In −3 Requiting Hex +1 The Unagi of Kyoshi Island −2 Shoot the Sheriff +1 Wan Shi Tong, Librarian −1 Bitter Triumph +1 Kaito, Cunning Infiltrator +1 Requiting Hex (SB copy back in) DO NOT board Ghost Vacuum (-16.0 pts NIHWR diff — worst card you can bring in vs the mirror). DO NOT board Duress (-3.4 pts, negative in mirror — they have threats not spells). Essence Scatter is also -8.1 pts. The SB Requiting Hex has a 64.0% SBOWR — board it back in; when your 3 main deck copies come out, the SB copy fills in. Unagi (+6.7 pts NIHWR) is your best finisher angle vs the mirror opponent's draw-heavy plan. Key needle: Spyglass Siren is your highest-impact evasive threat in the mirror (+13.5 pts). A 1/1 flier that generates a Map token creates repeated pressure the mirror opponent can't efficiently answer. Don't sacrifice Siren early — every hit with her triggers Enduring Curiosity. Fountainport (43% MD inclusion in the broader field, not in your list) being the #1 card suggests the field values the mana sink land as a late-game source of evasive value. % Point Edges +2–3 pts: First Kaito sticking wins the resource war. In the mirror, deploy Kaito on curve and protect him at all costs. The player whose Kaito generates 2+ cards first pulls ahead decisively. If both players have Kaito, the Double-Kaito ninjutsu trick (see Advanced tab) can generate double value in one turn cycle — a mirror-breaking play most opponents don't expect. +1–2 pts: Curiosity is surprisingly neutral in mirror. The data shows Enduring Curiosity is only +0.7 pts in the mirror because both players run it. Don't mulligan aggressively for Curiosity in this matchup — prioritize Siren (+13.5), Kaito (+11.9), and Cecil (+10.9) instead. The evasive creatures that generate Curiosity triggers matter more than Curiosity itself when both sides have access to it. +1 pt: Map tokens from Siren for library manipulation. Siren's Map token lets you surveil 1 — in the mirror where both sides are topdecking for answers, the card selection from Map tokens compounds over multiple turns. Use Maps aggressively to dig for your highest-impact cards rather than holding them.

matchups.notes: 64% WR. Deploy threats before their countermagic is online. Long Goodbye bypasses their counters.

matchups.opponent: You're the aggressor. Control decks have counterspells and sweepers but need time to set up. Spyglass Siren on turn 1 applies pressure before their Counterspell mana. Kaito on turn 3 has hexproof on your turn — they can't answer it while you're taking your turn. Long Goodbye can't be countered — remove their key blockers through their counterspell shields. Enduring Curiosity as an enchantment survives their creature sweepers. Their primary answer to enchantments is bounce or exile. If they have no bounce, Curiosity generates enough card advantage to outgrind any control plan. Apply consistent pressure and don't let them stabilize. Out In −3 Requiting Hex +1 Duress −2 Shoot the Sheriff +1 Spell Pierce −1 Cecil, Dark Knight +1 Disdainful Stroke +1 Kaito, Cunning Infiltrator +1 The Unagi of Kyoshi Island +1 Wan Shi Tong, Librarian Creature removal is dead — trim all of it. The Unagi of Kyoshi Island: {3}{U}{U} 5/5 Flash, ward {4} (opponents need 4+ mana to answer it, which control decks can eventually pay but it slows them dramatically), and whenever they draw their second card each turn you draw two. Against control who draws multiple cards per turn: this generates cascading card advantage. Wan Shi Tong provides a similar finisher angle with flash and flying. Key needle: Deploy threats on the play before they have Counterspell mana. Turn-1 Siren, turn-2 Beastbinder or hold up removal, turn-3 Kaito — this curve forces them to answer threats before their {U}{U} is available. If they take turn 2 off to set up, you've already dealt 3 damage and have Kaito entering next turn. % Point Edges +2 pts: Long Goodbye can't be countered — save it for their win condition. Long Goodbye's "can't be countered" clause means you bypass their entire counterspell suite. Don't waste it on a random threat — save it for whatever creature or threat they're trying to close with. Against Jeskai, that's often a Torrential Gearhulk-style finisher or Sphinx. One uncounterable removal spell at the right moment collapses their entire game plan. +1–2 pts: Enduring Curiosity survives sweepers. Once Curiosity returns as an enchantment, their sweepers (Supreme Verdict, Wrath effects) don't touch it. Deploy new creatures after their sweeper resolves and immediately resume drawing cards. This forces control into an unwinnable loop: sweep → you replay cheap creatures → Curiosity draws you into more → they need another sweeper → repeat until they're out.

matchups.notes: 44% WR. Removal density wins. Hex +15.6, Sheriff +15.2, Bitter Triumph +14.5. Strategic Betrayal best SB card.

matchups.opponent: Boros Aggro applies two-color aggressive pressure with evasion and burn reach. The data is clear on what wins this matchup — removal density above everything else. Deep-Cavern Bat (+0.9 pts) is nearly irrelevant here; Floodpits Drowner (+1.1 pts) is also low-impact. This is a pure reactive matchup where your removal suite is your win condition. Data-ranked card impact vs Boros Aggro (710 games): Requiting Hex +15.6 pts, Shoot the Sheriff +15.2 pts, Bitter Triumph +14.5 pts, Cecil +13.9 pts, Tishana's Tidebinder +12.7 pts, Enduring Curiosity +11.8 pts. Keep all removal. Floodpits Drowner +1.1 pts and Deep-Cavern Bat +0.9 pts — both barely relevant, don't prioritize them in your hand evaluation. Out In −2 Into the Flood Maw +1 Requiting Hex −1 Spell Snare +1 Day of Black Sun −1 Loch Mare +1 Strategic Betrayal Strategic Betrayal is your best SB card vs Boros (+17.5 pts NIHWR diff) — it exiles their best creature AND their GY, removing recursion threats and their best attacker simultaneously. Day of Black Sun sweeps their early board. Duress has -3.6 pts NIHWR in this matchup — they're a creature deck, Duress hits almost nothing relevant. Don't bring it in. Into the Flood Maw is sorcery speed when they have mana to recast bounced threats. Key needle: Don't tap out vs Boros until you're in a safe life position — they hold burn to finish. Cecil transforming into 4/4 lifelink is a legitimate stabilization tool here; his lifelink after flip recovers the Darkness losses quickly. Play to flip Cecil when you're at 10 life — the transformed version swings the race decisively. % Point Edges +3 pts: Strategic Betrayal is your highest-impact SB card (+17.5 pts). Exile their best creature AND their GY in one spell. Against Boros, this removes their recursion angle and biggest threat simultaneously. Always bring Strategic Betrayal in against Boros — it's the single highest differential SB card in any matchup in the entire dataset. +1–2 pts: Day of Black Sun at X=1 is sufficient. Against Boros, most of their early threats are MV 1 (1-drops). Day of Black Sun at X=1 costs only {B}{B} — cheaper than X=2 and still wipes their most dangerous early board. Save the extra mana for a follow-up flash creature to rebuild immediately after the sweep.

matchups.notes: Go under them with Kaito + Curiosity. No GY hate needed — Soul-Guide Lantern is a trap.

matchups.opponent: Dimir Excruciator is a combo-control deck built around Doomsday Excruciator — it exiles both libraries to six cards, then forces lethal draws with Insatiable Avarice . The Pro Tour Lorwyn Eclipsed champion Christoffer Larsen piloted it to the title. Despite sharing your colors, the matchup plays completely differently from the Dimir mirror. Excruciator is slower, more controlling, and relies on assembling its combo. Your role is to go under them with cheap evasive threats and card advantage engines before they can set up. The critical insight (from the Pro Tour 10th-place finisher's guide): you don't need removal or graveyard hate here. They aren't a traditional Reanimator deck — they're a controlling one. Having reactive "do nothing" cards like Soul-Guide Lantern loses you games because they can get ahead on cards easily or use Deceit to discard your action cards. Instead, deploy Kaito on curve, stick Enduring Curiosity, and force them to answer your card advantage engine while their combo pieces rot in hand. Tishana's Tidebinder is excellent here — counter the ETB of Superior Spider-Man copying Excruciator, or counter Stock Up 's triggered abilities. Floodpits Drowner stuns their key blocker while you push through damage. Loch Mare and countermagic round out your disruption — enough to punch holes in their combo sequencing while your clock counts down. Out In −3 Requiting Hex +1 Spell Pierce −2 Shoot the Sheriff +1 Duress −1 Into the Flood Maw +1 Disdainful Stroke +1 Kaito, Cunning Infiltrator +1 The Unagi of Kyoshi Island +1 Wan Shi Tong, Librarian Removal is mostly dead — their creatures are setup pieces for the combo, not beatdown threats. Requiting Hex has no good targets. Shoot the Sheriff hits very little. Instead, bring in countermagic to stop their key spells ( Deadly Cover-Up , Stock Up , Doomsday Excruciator itself) and top-end threats to out-grind their card selection. Duress strips their combo piece or removal before it matters. Disdainful Stroke hard-counters Excruciator (MV 6) and Deadly Cover-Up (MV 5). Key needle: DO NOT bring Soul-Guide Lantern. They put Excruciator in the GY via Winternight Stories or Bitter Triumph discard, then copy it with Superior Spider-Man — but Lantern exiling the GY doesn't stop their main combo line of just casting Excruciator. You're better off with Spell Pierce to counter their setup spells. Apply pressure with evasive threats and force them to have the combo by turn 6 or die to Kaito + Curiosity card advantage. % Point Edges +3–4 pts: Go under, don't interact. From the Pro Tour 10th-place finisher: "I don't think you need removal or graveyard hate. They aren't a traditional Reanimator deck — they're a controlling one. Having reactive 'do nothing' cards like Soul-Guide Lantern is a way to lose." Your role is to deploy Kaito on curve and stick Enduring Curiosity. Force them to answer your card advantage engine while their combo pieces sit in hand. The player who plays proactively wins this matchup. +2 pts: Disdainful Stroke counters their entire top end. Doomsday Excruciator (MV 6), Deadly Cover-Up (MV 5), and Quantum Riddler (MV 5) are all hit by Disdainful Stroke at {1}{U}. One mana-efficient counter for their three most important spells is one of the highest-leverage SB cards in this matchup. +1–2 pts: Kaito is nearly unanswerable for them. Excruciator builds run very few clean answers to planeswalkers. Their removal suite (Requiting Hex, Bitter Triumph, Harvester of Misery) is creature-focused. Kaito's hexproof on your turn means they need to answer him at sorcery speed on their turn — and if they're spending their turn dealing with Kaito, they're not assembling their combo.

matchups.notes: Their efficient interaction and Learn/Lesson engine outgrinds you. Counter their key spells, protect Kaito.

matchups.opponent: Izzet Lessons (9.81% meta share, Tier 1) is one of the format's dominant strategies — an interaction-heavy tempo deck that uses the Learn/Lesson mechanic to tutor answers from the sideboard mid-game. This gives them effective access to 22+ cards in games 2 and 3. Their removal suite is efficient and varied, making your individual threats vulnerable. The matchup is unfavorable because they can match your card advantage while having more flexible answers. Your win condition is sticking Kaito, Bane of Nightmares early — his hexproof on your turn means they need instant-speed answers during their own turn, and most of their removal is sorcery-speed or damage-based (which Kaito's 4 toughness survives). Enduring Curiosity as an enchantment is very hard for Izzet to answer — they typically don't run enchantment removal main. If both engines stick, you can grind through their Lesson advantage. The danger is their tempo: efficient cantrips keep their hand full while their removal picks off your creatures one-for-one. Into the Flood Maw bouncing your key threat after you tapped out is devastating. Hold countermagic for their highest-impact spells and force them to trade down on mana when possible. Out In −2 Requiting Hex +1 Duress −1 Shoot the Sheriff +1 Spell Pierce −1 Cecil, Dark Knight +1 Annul +1 Disdainful Stroke Requiting Hex has few good targets in Izzet Lessons — their threats are typically MV 3+ or noncreature. Shoot the Sheriff is conditionally useful but outclassed by countermagic here. Cecil's Darkness drain is risky when they have burn reach. Instead, layer countermagic: Duress strips their key spell pre-emptively, Spell Pierce catches their cantrips and removal in the early turns, Annul counters any artifact/enchantment payoff, and Disdainful Stroke handles their top-end threats cleanly. Key needle: Protect Kaito at all costs. If Kaito survives two attack steps with the 0 ability, you've drawn 2+ extra cards and the card advantage differential overcomes their Lesson engine. Don't deploy Kaito into open mana if they have {1}{U} available — wait for their end step to flash in a creature, then untap and deploy Kaito when their shields are down. % Point Edges +3–4 pts: Kaito exploits their removal blind spot. From World Championship data: Dimir went 4-1 against Izzet Lessons specifically because Lessons' removal suite doesn't touch planeswalkers. Their Otter tokens can't efficiently pressure a Kaito through a deck full of creature removal. Kaito, Bane of Nightmares is the single most important card in this matchup — it attacks an axis they fundamentally can't interact with. +2 pts: Kill Gran-Gran on sight. Gran-Gran is their primary damage engine — if it connects, their drain triggers from Monument to Endurance create a life advantage that compounds every turn. Shoot the Sheriff, Requiting Hex, any removal — spend it on Gran-Gran immediately. A Gran-Gran that lives for 2 turns generates 4-6 extra damage + drain that puts the game out of reach. +1–2 pts: Curiosity as enchantment dodges their entire answer suite. Izzet Lessons runs almost no enchantment removal main deck. Once Curiosity dies and returns as an enchantment, they have no clean answer outside of bouncing it (and even then, you just replay it). This creates a permanent card advantage engine that their Lesson tutoring can't address — they can Learn for removal all day, but none of it hits an enchantment.

matchups.notes: 37% WR — your worst matchup. Removal only. Almost everything else No Data at 560 games.

matchups.opponent: Mono-White Aggro is your hardest matchup at 37% win rate across 560 games (Plat–Mythic BO3) — narrowly worse than Mono-Green Landfall. Their aggressive white creature package (1/1s with lifelink, Lords, anthem effects) creates a wide board faster than your removal can clear it. The sample size is smaller than Mono-Green, so some variance exists, but the overall WR is consistently sub-40%. Data vs Mono-White Aggro (560 games): Shoot the Sheriff +10.0 pts, Requiting Hex +8.2 pts, Bitter Triumph +5.8 pts, Tishana's Tidebinder +4.8 pts, Floodpits Drowner +5.0 pts. Most other cards show No Data due to sample size limitations. Kaito is only +1.7 pts — their creatures outrace his 3/4 body. Many of your key cards are irrelevant here. Out In −2 Into the Flood Maw +1 Requiting Hex −1 Spell Snare +1 Day of Black Sun −1 Phantom Interference +1 Bitter Triumph Maximum removal density is the only plan. Day of Black Sun at X=2 is your best sweeper for their 1-2 drop board. Annul (+24.9 pts NIHWR diff per the data) and Duress (+18.4 pts NIHWR diff) both show surprisingly high differential, but note that these are NIHWR-based metrics with very small samples — the actual side-in WRs are 50.0% and 48.6% respectively, meaning they're not actually winning you more games when they come in. Don't over-rotate around those metrics. Key needle: This matchup requires Shoot the Sheriff and Requiting Hex in opening hands. Mulligan any hand without at least one piece of interaction at {1} or less. Without turn-1-2 removal, their board snowballs faster than your flash package can manage. Cecil is No Data here — the sample is too small to confirm, but his 2/3 deathtouch probably blocks their 2/2s efficiently. % Point Edges +2–3 pts: Day of Black Sun X=2 is your only board reset. Mono-White goes wide with 1-2 drop creatures and anthem effects. Your spot removal can't keep up with their board development. Day of Black Sun at X=2 for {2}{B}{B} destroys their entire early board — and critically, it strips abilities first (losing indestructible, hexproof) before destroying. This is the one card that resets an otherwise unwinnable board state. +1 pt: Mulligan harder than any other matchup. At 37% WR, this is your worst matchup. A speculative keep with "maybe I'll draw removal" is a loss. Mulligan to 5 if necessary to find Requiting Hex + Shoot the Sheriff. A 5-card hand with 2 removal spells beats a 7-card hand without interaction every time against Mono-White's curve.

matchups.notes: Badgermole Cub + Earthbender Ascension engine. Spell Snare answers both. Race with Kaito.

matchups.opponent: Simic Rhythm plays Badgermole Cub ({1}{G}) into Earthbender Ascension ({1}{G}) — both MV 2, both Spell Snare targets. You have the cleanest answer in the format to their engine. Landing Spell Snare on Cub or Ascension on T2 is worth more than almost any other play you can make. Without their engine they're a pile of medium creatures — Kaito outclasses everything they develop. On the play: Hold {U} on T2 for Spell Snare. Let them play Cub. Deny Ascension. T3 Kaito into draw + Frog pressure closes the tempo gap. On the draw: same plan but with extra card — often you see both Snare and removal. Out In −1 Into the Flood Maw +1 Spell Snare −1 Phantom Interference +1 Requiting Hex Spell Snare at {U} hard-counters Badgermole Cub and Earthbender Ascension — keep all copies. Requiting Hex destroys Ascension and deals 2 damage. Phantom Interference is weak here (they rarely cast noncreature spells that are must-counter).

DimirOculus.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Identity "A Delver deck with a reanimator backup plan. Every cantrip fills the graveyard for three different payoffs. Every discard is both a pump spell and a setup spell. Nothing in this deck does only one thing." Dimir Oculus is Modern's premier tempo-control deck with a reanimator subtheme. It evolved from UR Murktide through three distinct generations: first, Psychic Frog replaced Ragavan as the two-drop engine (MH3, June 2024). Then Abhorrent Oculus replaced Murktide Regent as the primary finisher (Duskmourn, September 2024). Now the deck exists in a mature form where all
DimirOculus.mulligan:
Mulligan Guide
Always Keep
Fetch + Frog + Interaction
Any hand with a fetch-land (for surveil sequencing), Psychic Frog (your primary engine), and at least one piece of interaction (counter, removal, or Force).

engines.title: Psychic Frog
engines.body: {U}{B} · 1/2 Frog. Whenever it deals combat damage to a player or planeswalker, draw a card. Discard a card: put a +1/+1 counter on it. Exile three cards from your graveyard: it gains flying until end of turn. This is the deck's heart. The discard grows Frog AND fills the GY for Unearth/Murktide. The combat draw replaces the discarded card. The flying converts late-game GY resources into evasion.

engines.title: Abhorrent Oculus
engines.body: {2}{U} · 5/5 Eye · Flying. Additional cost: exile 6 cards from GY. At beginning of each opponent's upkeep, manifest dread. The hardcast cost is real ({2}{U} + exile 6), but the primary play is Unearth ({B} sorcery: return creature MV ≤ 3 to battlefield). Oculus is MV 3. Unearth does NOT cast — the additional cost of exiling 6 from GY doesn't apply. A T2 Unearth on a milled Oculus = free 5/5 flying

engines.title: Murktide Regent
engines.body: {5}{U}{U} · 3/3 Dragon · Flying, Delve. Enters with a +1/+1 counter for each instant/sorcery exiled via delve. Whenever an instant or sorcery leaves your GY, put a +1/+1 counter on it. Typically an 8/8 flying for {U}{U}. Demoted to 2 copies in modern builds because Oculus is more efficient, but Murktide is still the best standalone closer. Key tension: Frog exiling cards from GY for flying compete

engines.title: 3 Abilities, All Instant Speed
engines.body: All three abilities activate at instant speed. Combat draw: triggers on damage to player OR planeswalker — relevant when attacking an Oko or Jace. Discard: can discard in response to removal (Frog gets bigger, card goes to GY for later). Can discard multiple cards at once — each discard is a separate activation. Flying: exile 3 cards as one activation. Can activate multiple times per turn (exile 6

engines.title: Every Card Type Behaves Differently
engines.body: Manifest dread: look at top 2, one enters face-down as 2/2, other goes to GY. The face-down 2/2 can be turned face up by paying its mana cost IF it's a creature card. Instant/sorcery manifested: stays face-down as 2/2 FOREVER — cannot be turned face up. Revealing it just shows it's not a creature. Murktide manifested: CAN be turned face up by paying {5}{U}{U} (its mana cost). Delve does NOT apply

engines.title: CRITICAL DISTINCTION
engines.body: Unearth the card ({B} sorcery): "Return target creature card with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield." That's it. No exile clause. No end-of-turn clause. No "if it would leave the battlefield, exile it instead." The creature returns permanently. An Oculus returned via the Unearth card stays on the battlefield forever unless killed/bounced normally. The Unearth keyword (on

engines.title: When Does Exile-6 Apply?
engines.body: Per Scryfall ruling (2024-09-20): "Abhorrent Oculus's additional cost must be paid even if it's cast 'without paying its mana cost' or for any alternative cost." This means: Cascade into Oculus — still pay exile 6. Collected Company hitting Oculus — CoCo puts it onto the battlefield, doesn't cast it, so NO additional cost. Unearth — returns to battlefield, doesn't cast, NO additional cost. Manifes

engines.title: Free Only on Opponent's Turns
engines.body: "If it's not your turn, you may exile a blue card from your hand rather than pay this spell's mana cost." Your upkeep: still your turn — can't free-cast. Your end step: still your turn — can't free-cast. Opponent's upkeep: their turn — CAN free-cast. This means casting spells during your opponent's upkeep dodges their Force of Negation (they can't free-cast on your turn either). Exile clause: FoN

engines.title: Your Own Mana Gets Hit
engines.body: {1}{U}{U} 2/2 Merfolk Wizard. "Nonbasic lands are Islands." ALL nonbasic lands — yours too. Your Watery Graves, Polluted Deltas, Undercity Sewers, Gloomlake Verges = all Islands (only produce {U}). You lose access to {B} from all nonbasics. Only your basic Swamp (1 copy in most lists) produces {B} under Harbinger. Pre-fetch Swamp BEFORE deploying Harbinger if you need {B} for Fatal Push or Bowmast

engines.title: MDFC — Spell and Land in One
engines.body: Front: {1}{U}{U} instant — return target spell or nonland permanent opponent controls to owner's hand. Hits spells ON THE STACK (pseudo-counter that returns to hand) AND permanents in play. Back: Undercity Sewers — land, enters tapped, surveil 1, produces {U} or {B}. The deck counts this as land #20-21 even though it's also interaction. Edge case: If you Sink a spell on the stack, the spell return

engines.title: Second Copy Grows the Existing Army
engines.body: {1}{B} 1/1 Orc Archer · Flash. ETB + whenever opponent draws extra: deal 1 damage to any target, then amass Orcs 1. Amass Orcs 1: if you control an Army, put a +1/+1 counter on it. If you don't, create a 0/0 Orc Army token and put a counter on it. Second Bowmasters: the ETB trigger of the second one grows the EXISTING Army. You don't get two Army tokens. Over a long game a single Army can become a

engines.title: When to Hold Which Counter
engines.body: Counterspell ({U}{U}): hard counter, no conditions. Hold when you need certainty — their must-answer spell resolving loses the game. Requires 2 blue mana, which means T2 at earliest with correct lands. Spell Snare ({U}): counters MV 2 exactly. In current Modern: Bowmasters, Stoneforge Mystic, Wrenn and Six, Lightning Helix, Coppercoat Vanguard, Tarmogoyf. Best on T2 — deploy Frog AND hold Snare wi

engines.title: Controlled vs Random GY Fill
engines.body: Consider ({U} instant): surveil 1 (choose whether top card goes to GY), then draw. You CHOOSE what enters the GY. Use when you need a SPECIFIC card in GY (an Oculus sitting on top). Thought Scour ({U} instant): target player mills 2, draw a card. RANDOM — you don't choose what's milled. But mills 2 vs Consider's 1. Use when you need GY VOLUME (filling for Murktide delve or Oculus hardcast). Sequen

engines.title: You Want Maximum Agency
engines.body: You enjoy making 15+ meaningful decisions per game. You like tracking hidden information (GY contents, opponent's hand after Thoughtseize). You want a deck that rewards knowing every card in the format because your interaction suite needs to answer everything. You find the puzzle of GY resource allocation satisfying. You like winning games by outplaying, not out-topdecking.

engines.title: You Need Autopilot Consistency
engines.body: The deck is unforgiving of mistakes. Wrong land sequencing T1 can cost you the game on T4. Wrong counter target can lose the counter war. Wrong GY management means your Murktide enters as a 4/4 instead of an 8/8. If you're playing on 4 hours of sleep at a day-2 event, the decision fatigue is real. Also: graveyard hate is everywhere in Modern. Nihil Spellbomb, Surgical Extraction, Leyline of the Vo

engines.title: Fetch → Surveil Land
engines.body: Ideal: Fetch-land → crack → find Undercity Sewers (enters tapped, surveil 1). This removes the tapped land from your deck AND fills GY with the surveil. Do NOT lead with Consider or Thought Scour T1 even if you have them — the surveil land is more important because it takes a tapped land out of your deck for future draws. If no fetch: play Gloomlake Verge (untapped, produces {U}). If opening with

engines.title: Frog vs Open Mana
engines.body: Deploy Frog when: you have protection (Spell Snare, Spell Pierce backup), OR they tapped out T1, OR their deck can't efficiently answer a 1/2 (combo, Tron, Storm). Hold open when: they have {1} open for removal (Boros with Galvanic Discharge), OR you have Counterspell + threat for T3, OR you milled an Oculus and can Unearth it this turn instead. T2 Unearth on Oculus: the nut draw. Requires Oculus

engines.title: Discard Oculus → Unearth
engines.body: The standard line: T2 Frog resolved. T3: discard Oculus to Frog (+1/+1 counter, Oculus goes to GY). Cast Unearth for {B} (Oculus returns permanently). Hold {U} for Spell Snare or Spell Pierce. Board state: 2/3 Frog + 5/5 flying Oculus + 1 open mana. Alternative: if no Oculus, T3 hold up Counterspell ({U}{U}) and attack with Frog. Draw a card off combat damage. Rebuild hand for T4 Murktide. Against

engines.title: Fetch + Frog + Interaction
engines.body: Any hand with a fetch-land (for surveil sequencing), Psychic Frog (your primary engine), and at least one piece of interaction (counter, removal, or Force). Example: Polluted Delta, Watery Grave, Frog, Fatal Push, Counterspell, Consider, Thought Scour = snap keep. Even without Oculus or Murktide — Frog generates enough value to find your finishers.

engines.title: Unearth + Mill + Land
engines.body: A hand with Unearth, Thought Scour, and 2 lands is keepable if you're willing to gamble on milling an Oculus or Harbinger. The T1 Scour → T2 Unearth line is powerful enough to justify. But if Scour misses all creatures, Unearth is a dead card until you find another way to fill the GY. Riskier on the draw than the play.

engines.title: No Threat, No Cantrip
engines.body: A hand of 3 lands, 2 Counterspells, Fatal Push, Force of Negation = mulligan. All interaction, no proactive plan. You can't win by countering forever — you need a threat to close. Also mulligan: hands with only Murktide as the threat and no way to fill the GY (no cantrips, no Thought Scour). Murktide without GY fuel enters as a 3/3 for 7 mana — unplayable.

engines.title: Basic Swamp in Opening Hand
engines.body: From MythicMaria's guide: "This is a very awkward hand... mostly because of the basic Swamp. In most cases I don't want to fetch for it, so having it in a starting hand could seriously damage your spell-sequencing." The deck is heavily blue — your T1 and T2 plays are almost always blue. A Swamp in your opener means one of your first two land drops produces only {B}, which can't cast Consider, Thou

engines.title: T2 Frog Is the Line
engines.body: On the play, T2 Psychic Frog is your highest-value action. It comes down before they can assemble interaction, and they have to answer it immediately or lose to the discard-grow loop. Mulligan more aggressively for hands with a T2 Frog play. A hand without Frog or a way to find Frog by T2 is a slow hand that gets outpaced against combo decks.

engines.title: Counter-Mana Hands Are Fine
engines.body: On the draw you see 8 cards and can keep counter-heavy hands (Force of Negation + Counterspell + land) since you have time to deploy them. T1 Spell Snare or Stern Scolding on their T1 threat is a legitimate draw-side opening. Against aggro on the draw, Fatal Push + Shoot the Sheriff hands are keepable even without Frog — you need to survive to T3 before deploying your threats.

engines.title: Murktide as Backup Finisher
engines.body: Frog answered: deploy Murktide Regent as the backup closer. Murktide is effectively a 4/4+ flying for {2}{U} after GY fills. It survives Fatal Push and Lightning Bolt. If Murktide is also unavailable, Orcish Bowmasters + opponent draw triggers creates a drain clock. You have three closing threats — exhaust their answers before scooping.

engines.title: Tempo + Value Plan
engines.body: Nihil Spellbomb or Surgical Extraction is in play. Pivot to Harbinger of the Seas + Bowmasters value: Harbinger locks opponents off multiple islands, Bowmasters generates bodies every time they draw. This plan doesn’t need the GY to function. Sink into Stupor bounces their permanents and generates disruption. You can win without any GY synergies in this mode.

engines.title: Frog + Faithless Looting
engines.body: Discard 2 cards = 2 counters on Frog in one activation. Frog becomes a 3/4 flying on T3 after a T2 deploy + T3 Looting. This is your fastest threat-growth engine. Execute whenever Frog is in play and Looting is in hand. The card selection is a bonus — the primary goal is growing Frog to a size they can’t race.

engines.title: Bowmasters + Opponent Draw
engines.body: Every card they draw creates a Rabbit token and deals 1 damage. Against draw-heavy decks (Storm, UW Control, Living End), Bowmasters generates massive value passively. Deploy Bowmasters before their big draw turn for maximum impact. This engine wins games where Frog has been answered — they can’t stop drawing and the damage accumulates.

engines.title: Harbinger Tempo Lock
engines.body: Harbinger of the Seas makes all islands legendary — opponent can only keep one. Against blue decks, this halves their mana immediately. Deploy when they’re tapped out to maximize the tempo hit. This engine is not a finisher but it creates a window: their mana is restricted, your threats connect. Follow Harbinger immediately with a threat or counter-up to capitalise on the tempo swing.

engines.title: How Fast Does Frog Kill?
engines.body: T2 Frog (1/2 flying). T3 Faithless Looting → Frog is 3/4 flying. T4 swing for 3. T5 another discard outlet → Frog grows, swing for 4+. Starting from T3, Frog closes in 4–5 attack steps without buffs. With additional discard triggers (Sink into Stupor on their EOT), Frog can be 5/6+ by T4 — that’s a 3-turn clock at 20 life.

engines.title: Passive Drain Rate
engines.body: Against draw-heavy decks: T3 Bowmasters. They cast Brainstorm (draw 3, lose 3 life, 3 Rabbits). They cast Preordain (draw 2 more). By T4-5 in a draw-heavy game, Bowmasters has often dealt 8–10 damage passively. Combined with 1/1 Rabbit attacks, this is a realistic 5–6 turn clock that doesn’t require you to ever attack with Frog.

engines.title: When to Hold Mana
engines.body: Deploy T2: They’re on an aggro or combo deck. Frog must hit play before they establish their clock. Hold mana T2: They have 2 open mana and haven’t cast anything — Force of Negation read. Pass T2 with Force up, deploy Frog on T3 when they’ve used mana on their end step.

engines.title: Frog Triggers on ANY Discard
engines.body: Psychic Frog gets a +1/+1 counter whenever ANY card is discarded — including cards you discard to hand size, Faithless Looting’s discard 2, and even opponent’s Thoughtseize stripping your hand. Each individual card discarded is one trigger. Faithless Looting = 2 triggers = 2 counters at instant speed. You can activate this on their combat step to make Frog large enough to survive blocks.

engines.title: Harbinger Applies to ALL Islands
engines.body: Harbinger of the Seas makes ALL islands legendary — including their Hallowed Fountain, Scalding Tarn after fetching, Flooded Strand after cracking, and any island-type dual. If they already have two islands in play when Harbinger resolves, they choose one and the other is sacrificed immediately. This is not a "enters tapped" effect — it’s an immediate sacrifice for the duplicate. Know which of the

engines.title: Sink into Stupor at Their EOT
engines.body: Sink into Stupor / Sinister Monologue is a two-card adventure: cast the adventure first (draw-then-discard + Frog trigger), THEN cast the sorcery next turn to bounce a permanent. You can also hold Sink into Stupor and cast the bounce on your main phase when they’re tapped out for maximum tempo. Casting on your own end step gets you the adventure; saving it for their permanents gets the bounce. Dec

engines.title: Exile Your Own Card to Frog
engines.body: Opponent casts Surgical Extraction targeting Abhorrent Oculus in your GY. Response: activate Psychic Frog's flying ability, exiling Oculus (plus 2 other cards) as COST. Surgical fizzles — its target left the graveyard. The exile is a cost, meaning the opponent can't respond to the exile itself; by the time they get priority, Oculus is already in exile. Frog gained flying as a bonus. Note: this onl

engines.title: Prioritize Unearth Timing
engines.body: If you suspect GY hate: use Unearth BEFORE they get mana to deploy hate. A T2 Unearth on Oculus resolves before their T2 Rest in Peace. Once Oculus is on the battlefield, GY hate doesn't affect it — it's already out. Against Nihil Spellbomb (sacrifice to exile GY): they can fire it in response to Unearth. Counter-play: hold Spell Snare (counters MV 2 artifacts on cast) or Counterspell for their Sp

engines.title: Pseudo-Counter That Returns to Hand
engines.body: Sink bounces a SPELL on the stack back to hand. Unlike Counterspell, the spell was never "countered" — it just returned to hand. This matters against: "Can't be countered" spells: Supreme Verdict says "can't be countered" but Sink doesn't counter it — it returns it to hand. Legal play. Cascade: bounce the cascade spell after Living End resolves (the cascade card goes back to hand, not GY). Suspend

engines.title: Tempo Removal That Dodges Indestructible
engines.body: Sink bounces any nonland permanent opponent controls. This hits: creatures (even indestructible ones), planeswalkers, artifacts, enchantments. Unlike Fatal Push which destroys (stopped by indestructible), Sink returns to hand regardless of indestructible, hexproof, or protection. Best targets: expensive permanents they spent their whole turn deploying (Karn, Primeval Titan, Murktide). Worst target

engines.title: Your Threats Are Answered
engines.body: Frog and Murktide are both answered. Bowmasters is in play. Switch: draw-go with counters + Bowmasters passive drain. Every time they draw a card you advance your position. Hold mana open every turn, counter the important spells, let Bowmasters accumulate damage over 6–8 turns. This is a real win condition.

engines.title: Frog Is Big and They’re Low
engines.body: Frog is 5/6+ flying. They’re below 12 life. Stop developing, stop counterspelling — attack. Two swings with a 5/6 kills from 10 life. Don’t waste mana on extra interaction when the game is already decided by the air. Tap out, attack, hold Priority only to prevent exile effects.

engines.title: Frog + Counter Backup Is Online
engines.body: You have Frog in play, Force of Negation in hand, opponent is at 12 or below. This position wins. Don’t pivot to anything else. Attack with Frog, Force anything that answers it. The counter backup converts a 60% position into a 90% position.

engines.title: Read Their Opening
engines.body: Aggro deck: lead interaction (Fatal Push, Spell Snare), Frog at T2 to block. Combo deck: lead Force of Negation backup, Frog at T2 to race. Control deck: lead Harbinger at T3 to cut their mana, deploy threats when they tap out for a sweeper. The deck changes shape based on what they’re doing.

engines.title: Consign to Memory
engines.body: {U} instant. Replicate {1}. Counter target triggered ability or colorless spell. The most versatile SB card in Modern. Counters: Storm triggers (Grapeshot), cascade triggers (Living End), Karn, Walking Ballista, Chalice of the Void, Thought-Knot Seer ETB, Urza's Saga chapter triggers, Ruby Medallion, The One Ring (if it returns). Replicate means {U}{U}{1} counters TWO things in the same turn. Boar

engines.title: Nihil Spellbomb
engines.body: {1} artifact. {T}, sacrifice: exile target player's graveyard. When it goes to YOUR graveyard from battlefield: you may pay {B} to draw a card. Never dead — against non-GY decks, sacrifice it and pay {B} to draw. Against GY decks: fire in response to their reanimation/Unearth/Living End. The "draw a card when sacrificed" mode means the 3 Spellbombs are essentially 3 cantrips in matchups where GY h

engines.title: Toxic Deluge
engines.body: {2}{B} sorcery. Pay X life: all creatures get -X/-X until EOT. Kills indestructible creatures (doesn't destroy, gives -X/-X). Kills any size creature if you're willing to pay enough life. Against Boros go-wide: pay 2 life for -2/-2 wipes their board of 1/1 and 2/2 tokens. Against Murktide in the mirror: pay 8+ life to kill an 8/8 if necessary. The life payment is real — against aggro this is a las

engines.title: Accursed Marauder
engines.body: {1}{B} 2/1 Zombie Warrior. ETB: each player sacrifices a nontoken creature. Your answer to Sanctifier en-Vec (pro black AND red — untargetable by all your removal), Kaldra Compleat (indestructible), Bogles (hexproof), and any creature that dodges targeted removal. The "each player" clause means you sacrifice too — deploy when you have a manifest token or nothing relevant to lose. Unearthable at MV

engines.title: Harbinger of the Seas (3rd copy)
engines.body: Main runs 2. The 3rd SB copy comes in against any deck with a greedy manabase: Boros Energy (0-1 basics), Domain Zoo (5c), 4C piles, Amulet Titan (bounce lands lose abilities). Turning their nonbasics into Islands locks them off most of their mana. The 2/2 body blocks and attacks. Board in when Harbinger cheese is a realistic game plan — skip against decks with plenty of basics (mono-color, 2C wit

engines.title: Shoot the Sheriff
engines.body: {1}{B} instant. Destroy target non-outlaw creature. "Outlaws" = Assassins, Mercenaries, Pirates, Rogues, Warlocks. Most Modern creatures are NOT outlaws — this hits almost everything. Board in when you need removal density beyond Fatal Push ×4. The "non-outlaw" restriction rarely matters in Modern. Clean answer to any creature Push doesn't cover (MV 3+ without revolt).

engines.title: Orcish Bowmasters (3rd copy)
engines.body: Board in against creature-heavy matchups where the flash + ping + Orc Army matters: Boros Energy, Humans, Prowess, mirror. The 3rd Bowmasters increases your chance of having the flash answer for their T1 play. Remember: second Bowmasters grows the existing Army — you want both copies in play against wide boards.

engines.title: Stern Scolding
engines.body: {U} instant. Counter target creature spell with power or toughness 2 or less. Kills in the mirror: Psychic Frog (1/2), Bowmasters (1/1), Harbinger (2/2). Kills in other matchups: Guide of Souls (1/2), Ocelot Pride (1/1), Stoneforge Mystic (1/2), Ragavan (2/1). At {U} it's the most mana-efficient creature counter available. Board in against any deck with critical small creatures you need to stop be

engines.title: Glistening Deluge
engines.body: {1}{B}{B} sorcery. All creatures get -1/-1 until EOT. Creatures that are green AND/OR white get an additional -2/-2. Total: -3/-3 to green/white creatures, -1/-1 to everything else. Devastating against: Boros (white creatures get -3/-3), Yawgmoth (green creatures), Humans (most creatures are white). Your own Frog (1/2 base, often 3/4+ with counters) survives at -1/-1. The {B}{B} cost requires basi

engines.title: Force of Negation (3rd copy)
engines.body: Board in against combo and control — any matchup where free interaction on their turn is critical. The 3rd Force ensures you statistically have a free answer available in your opener ~35% of games (up from ~24% with 2 copies). Against Storm, Living End, and Belcher: having a Force in your opener is often the difference between winning and losing G1.

engines.title: Spell Pierce
engines.body: {U} instant. Counter noncreature spell unless they pay {2}. Best T1-T3 before they have excess mana. Board in against: control (counter their sweeper/counter), combo (counter their setup spell), any deck with expensive noncreature spells. Falls off hard after T4 when they can always pay {2}. Consider it a T1-T3 tempo piece, not a late-game answer.

engines.title: When You Need an Unkillable Finisher
engines.body: Murktide survives Fatal Push, Lightning Bolt, and most damage-based removal. An 8/8 flying that grows passively is the best standalone closer in the deck. Keep 2 copies when: the meta is midrange-heavy (Murktide outclasses their threats), when GY hate is low (Murktide delve is reliable), or when you need a card that wins the game in 2-3 attack steps without any additional support.

engines.title: When GY Hate Is Everywhere
engines.body: Some builds have dropped Murktide entirely. The argument: Oculus is a better payoff (Unearthable for {B}, doesn't need GY cards to be large), and Murktide competes with Frog for GY resources. In a meta full of Nihil Spellbomb and Surgical Extraction, Murktide often enters as a 4/4 or 5/5 — not the 8/8 you need. Replace with: 3rd Bowmasters + extra interaction, or Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student for a

engines.title: Cheese Angle Without Dilution
engines.body: 2 main means you see Harbinger in ~25% of games. Against the right opponent (Boros, Domain) it's game-winning. Against the wrong opponent (mono-color, 2C with basics) it's a 2/2 for 3 mana. The SB copy comes in when you know Harbinger is live. This split balances the cheese potential against the risk of a dead card.

engines.title: All-In on the Mana Lock
engines.body: In a meta where 70%+ of decks have greedy manabases: 3 main Harbinger increases your odds of the T2-T3 lock. The trade-off is more dead draws against Eldrazi Tron (they run Wastes/colorless basics) and mirror (both players are blue). Only go to 3 main if your local meta is dominated by Boros/Domain/4C and you want to maximize free wins from the cheese angle.

engines.title: Adding a Third Color
engines.body: Some players splash red for Faithless Looting (unbanned Dec 2025): draw 2, discard 2 for {R}. This directly discards Oculus to GY (guaranteeing the Unearth combo) and fills GY faster for Murktide. Also enables Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student flips (draw 3 in a turn). The cost: a third color in a 19-land deck. You need red sources (Steam Vents, Scalding Tarn) which dilute your {U}{B} consistency. Verdi

engines.title: Maximum Consistency
engines.body: The straight UB build never has color issues. Every land produces {U} or {B} or both. You never lose to your own mana. The trade-off: you rely on Thought Scour / Consider / surveil lands / Frog discard to put Oculus in GY — all less reliable than Faithless Looting. Verdict: better for an open field where you can't predict what you'll face. The consistency of never stumbling on mana outweighs the e

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Draw-heavy decks are well-represented (Storm, UW Control, Living End) — Bowmasters generates massive value passively. Many blue decks in the room — Harbinger tempo lock is live in more matchups. Low Surgical Extraction density in expected sideboards. Midrange-heavy meta where Frog is not a known target heading into the event.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy graveyard hate meta — Nihil Spellbomb, Surgical Extraction, Rest in Peace shut off Murktide and GY synergies. Very creature-heavy field where Bowmasters drain is irrelevant — pure aggro decks rarely draw enough to matter. You’re not comfortable with the three-mode role switching — this deck punishes pilots who default to one plan.

engines.title: Frog Beats Plan
engines.body: Practice winning with just Psychic Frog when Archon is answered. It's a real win condition.

engines.title: Solitude Timing
engines.body: Drill Solitude evoke + Ephemerate on the exact right target. Two wrong exiles loses games.

engines.title: G2 GY Hate Lines
engines.body: Practice playing through Rest in Peace and Endurance. These are your hardest post-board situations.

engines.title: Clock Practice
engines.body: Count turns to lethal. Dimir can draw games by overvaluing setup over closing.

matchups.notes: Fatal Push — their creatures are all MV ≤ 2
Counterspell on Ephemerate — denies their engine
Force of Negation — free counter on their combo turn
Fatal Push + Spell Snare on their key pieces
Unearth Oculus T2 — race before Tron assembles
Counterspell on cascade spell — deny the whole combo
Stern Scolding — kills Frog and Bowmasters for {U}
Amulet Titan assembles Primeval Titan + bounce lands by turn 3-4. Your clock is too slow without Frog online. Harbinger ...

matchups.opponent: Amulet Titan assembles Primeval Titan + bounce lands by turn 3-4. Your clock is too slow without Frog online. Harbinger of the Seas is your best card — it makes all nonbasic lands enter tapped, completely disabling their Amulet of Vigor combo. Harbinger deployed on turn 3 before they assemble Tron is a near-auto-win. Out In −2 Spell Snare + 2 Harbinger of the Seas −1 Shoot the Sheriff +1 Nihil Spellbomb Harbinger of the Seas enters tapped lands neutralizes Amulet of Vigor — their bounce lands enter tapped regardless, buying 1-2 extra turns. Spellbomb exiles Spelunking from GY or disrupts their Arboreal Grazer. Spell Snare does nothing here (no MV2 spells that matter).

matchups.notes: Modern Prowess kills on T3 with Slickshot Show-Off + Cori-Steel Cutter + cantrip chains. Your flash creatures plus Count...

matchups.opponent: Modern Prowess kills on T3 with Slickshot Show-Off + Cori-Steel Cutter + cantrip chains. Your flash creatures plus Counterspell are the best interaction suite in the format against this. Force of Negation counters their key spell for free. Frog on T2 into Counterspell open is your ideal G1 line — Frog races their cantrip-buffed creatures through flying. Out In −2 Harbinger of the Seas +2 Stern Scolding −1 Shoot the Sheriff +1 Spell Pierce Stern Scolding hard-counters anything they want to cast that has 2 or less power — DRC (1/1), Swiftspear (1/2), and 1-drops all die to it. Harbinger does nothing to a basic-heavy mana base. Spell Pierce taxes their key pump spells (Mutagenic Growth, Wild Ride) early.

matchups.notes: Thalia, Guardian of Thraben taxes ALL your spells by {1} — your 3-drop plan becomes a 4-drop plan. Counterspell goes fro...

matchups.opponent: Thalia, Guardian of Thraben taxes ALL your spells by {1} — your 3-drop plan becomes a 4-drop plan. Counterspell goes from {UU} to {UU1}. Force of Negation still works free but uses a card. The key: play around Thalia by deploying Frog before it resolves (T2 Frog), then use Frog's flying to kill Thalia in combat. Without Thalia their clock is slow enough that Kaito + Frog wins. Out In −2 Harbinger of the Seas +2 Nihil Spellbomb −1 Phantom Interference +1 Stern Scolding Nihil Spellbomb at {1} enters under Thalia for only {2} total — still efficient graveyard hate. Stern Scolding kills Thalia (2/1) and Meddling Mage (2/2) exactly. Harbinger does nothing to their basic-heavy mana base. Kill Thalia and Meddling Mage the turn they come down.

DomainZoo.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Identity Domain Zoo is Modern's best aggro deck when it draws Leyline of the Guildpact . It's still a solid aggro deck when it doesn't. That's the whole advantage. Domain Zoo plays the longest continuous history of any aggro archetype in Modern — creatures, burn, and land synergies dating back to the format's beginning. What makes the 2025–26 version dangerous is the Leyline of the Guildpact package: a zero-mana enchantment that, when in your opening hand, enters the battlefield before the game begins, instantly giving your lands all five basic land types and making every nonla
DomainZoo.mulligan:
Mulligan Framework

Keep hands that have: at least two lands that together provide multiple land types, and at least two creatures (or one creature + Leyline).

engines.title: Territorial Kavu
engines.body: MV 2, P/T = basic land types you control. With Leyline in opening hand: 5/5 before you've played a land. On attack: must choose — rummage (discard+draw) or exile a GY card. With Scion of Draco : gains hexproof (can't be targeted), lifelink, first strike, trample, vigilance simultaneously.

engines.title: Scion of Draco
engines.body: MV 12, costs {2} less per basic land type. With Leyline: costs {2} (5 types × {2} off = {10} reduction). 4/4 flying. Each of your creatures gets all five keywords when you control all five land types: white=vigilance, blue=hexproof, black=lifelink, red=first strike, green=trample. Hexproof protects all your creatures from targeted removal.

engines.title: Doorkeeper Thrull
engines.body: MV 2, flash 1/2 flying. Artifacts and creatures entering don't cause abilities to trigger. Shuts off: Solitude exile, Overlord of the Balemurk mill, Kappa Cannoneer token, Yawgmoth ETB, Atraxa card-draw ETB. Does NOT stop Ephemerate from blinking — only the triggered ETB ability is silenced. Dies to Lightning Bolt .

engines.title: Leyline Binding
engines.body: MV 6 base, flash. Domain: costs {1} less per basic land type. With full domain: {W}. Exiles any nonland permanent until Binding leaves. If Binding is destroyed ( Nature's Claim , Wear//Tear), the exiled permanent returns. Use to answer Primeval Titan , Murktide Regent , Yawgmoth, anything you can't fight through otherwise.

engines.title: Stubborn Denial
engines.body: MV 1 ({U}). Counter noncreature spell unless pay {1}. With ferocious (4+ power creature): hard counter instead. Territorial Kavu (5/5) and Scion of Draco (4/4) both enable ferocious permanently. Cannot counter creature spells regardless of ferocious. Use to protect Scion or Kavu from removal spells.

engines.title: Psychic Frog
engines.body: {U} 1/1 Frog. Whenever you discard a card, Psychic Frog gets +1/+1 until end of turn and gains flying until end of turn. Pairs with Territorial Kavu 's rummage attack trigger — Kavu attacks, you discard one card, Frog becomes a 2/2 flier and attacks. With Scion in play Frog gains hexproof (blue=hexproof) — it can't be targeted by removal while attacking. The flying evasion is critical for racing;

engines.title: Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury
engines.body: MV 3, 6/6. When enters: {1}{R}{W} cost deal 3 damage to any target and gain 3 life. Escape: exile 5 cards from GY, pay {1}{R}{W}, return from GY. Nearly impossible to permanently answer — recurs from the graveyard. With Scion active: has all five keywords on a 6/6 body.

engines.title: Tribal Flames
engines.body: MV 2 ({1}{R}), sorcery. Deals X damage where X = basic land types you control. With full domain: 5 damage for 2 mana. Kills most creatures, puts opponents on a 4-turn clock. Some lists cut this for additional creatures; include it when you want more direct damage reach.

engines.title: Tribal Flames
engines.body: MV 2 ({1}{R}), sorcery. Deals X damage to any target, where X = number of basic land types among lands you control. With full domain (Leyline in opening hand): 5 damage for 2 mana on turn one. 5 damage kills Primeval Titan (6/6 — no), it kills Ragavan, kills Guide of Souls, kills most two-and three-drops, or deals 5 straight to face. Three copies gives this deck a burn-finisher dimension that pure

engines.title: Leyline in Opening Hand
engines.body: Leyline of the Guildpact + any creature + 2 lands. Leyline enters at start of game. Your Kavu is immediately a 3/3+ and Scion grants hexproof. This is your best draw. Keep any hand with Leyline regardless of land count as long as you have 2 sources and a creature. Scion + Kavu + 3 lands (no Leyline). T1 Kavu, T2 Scion = solid beats plan. Keep.

engines.title: Auto-Ship Conditions
engines.body: No creatures and no Leyline. You have no pressure without creatures and no combo without Leyline. Ship. Five+ lands, no threats. Pure flood hand. Ship even with Leyline — you need T1 threats to leverage it. One land + Leyline. Leyline enters at start but you can’t develop after. Ship vs aggro, conditional keep vs control on the draw.

engines.title: Context-Dependent
engines.body: Two creatures, no Leyline, 3 lands: Keep vs fair midrange (your creatures are good enough), ship vs combo (need Leyline to race). Leyline + 1 land: Keep on the draw (extra card, Leyline buys time). Ship on the play vs aggro (you need T1 development). Four-land Leyline hand: Keep — Leyline makes everything big enough to justify the slow start.

engines.title: T1 Kavu Is Everything
engines.body: On the play, T1 Territorial Kavu is your single most important action. A 3/3+ on T1 with Leyline (or 4/4+ with Leyline + T2 Scion) puts immediate pressure that most decks can’t answer cleanly. Mulligan aggressively for T1 Kavu hands on the play. Missing T1 on the play means your T3 window is tighter and opponents have had time to develop stabilizers.

engines.title: Leyline Hands Are Better
engines.body: On the draw you see 8 cards, which dramatically improves Leyline odds. Keep slightly looser Leyline hands on the draw — even a slow start with Leyline is reasonable because it gives all your creatures hexproof and makes Kavu enormous. T2 Scion of Draco on the draw is a natural curve that still applies pressure on T3 before most opponents have fully stabilized.

engines.title: Pivot to Scion Beats
engines.body: Leyline Binding or Wear // Tear removes Leyline. Kavu and Psychic Frog lose their massive power boosts. Pivot: rely on Scion of Draco’s hexproof grant (creatures with a colour of Scion’s colours have hexproof) and Tribal Flames at full Domain (5 damage to any target). You can still win through raw power — Kavu is still a 3/3 with ferocious counters, Frog still grows on discard. The ceiling is lowe

engines.title: Race with Tribal Flames
engines.body: Scion of Draco removed: hexproof protection is gone. Opponents can now target your Kavu and Frog with removal. Pivot to burn plan: Tribal Flames at 5 damage each + Lightning Bolt is 8 damage from hand. A 3-creature board + 2 Tribal Flames = 21+ damage. Race before they can clear your board. Bring in Consign to Memory post-board to protect your key pieces when they untap with removal available.

engines.title: Leyline + Kavu Combo
engines.body: Leyline of the Guildpact makes all your permanents every color. Territorial Kavu gets a +1/+1 counter for each different color among lands you control — with Leyline and 5 basic land types, Kavu is immediately a 5/5+ or larger. This is your fastest and most dominant engine. Execute by keeping Leyline opening hands and leading Kavu T1.

engines.title: Scion + Hexproof Shield
engines.body: Scion of Draco gives all creatures you control with a matching color hexproof. Under Leyline, all your creatures are all colors — all get hexproof from Scion. This engine is a protection layer, not a damage engine, but it converts a volatile threat board into an untargetable one. Deploy Scion T2 to lock in hexproof before their removal untap.

engines.title: Tribal Flames Reach
engines.body: Tribal Flames at full Domain (5 basic land types) deals 5 damage to any target. Two Flames = 10 damage from hand. At 20 life: two Flames + Kavu attack = lethal from 13+ life. Execute this engine when the game is going long and their life total is in the 10–15 range. Don’t tap out for creatures when you can close with burn from hand — it bypasses their blockers and removal.

engines.title: How Fast Does It Kill?
engines.body: T0: Leyline. T1: Territorial Kavu (5/5+ immediately with Leyline). T2: Scion of Draco (hexproof, flying). T2 swing: Kavu hits for 5+. T3: Lightning Bolt (3) + swing: 8+ per turn. At 20 life, this clock closes in 2–3 swings starting T2. Opponents at 20 life need to have an answer by T3 or the game is over — no time to stabilize.

engines.title: Fair Mode Speed
engines.body: T1: Kavu (3/3 with 3 land types, grows each land). T2: Scion. T2 swing: Kavu hits for 4. T3: Tribal Flames (5 damage) + swing. At 20 life, this is a T4–5 kill. Slower, but still faster than most non-combo Modern decks. The key: Tribal Flames at 5 damage each makes every land drop also threaten the face — opponents can’t just let you develop freely.

engines.title: When to Burn vs Attack
engines.body: Burn face: They have 10 or less life and 2 Tribal Flames in hand = cast both, win. Don’t attack into blockers. Attack: Their board is empty or your creatures have hexproof (untargetable through Scion). Make them use removal on creatures before closing with burn. Mixed: One Bolt + one attack per turn until they’re in Tribal Flames range.

engines.title: Kavu Counts Colors Among Lands You Control
engines.body: Territorial Kavu gets a +1/+1 counter for each “different color” among lands you control — not each land. With Leyline, all your lands become all colors. But Kavu only counts up to 5 (WUBRG). Even with 10 lands under Leyline, Kavu is a 5/5 from the land color ability — not a 10/10. The size comes from other sources (ferocious, exert). Know the ceiling before calculating lethal.

engines.title: Hexproof Doesn’t Stop Sacrifice or Sweepers
engines.body: Scion of Draco grants hexproof to your creatures. Hexproof means they can’t be targeted by opponent’s spells or abilities. It does NOT protect against: Goblin Bombardment (sacrifice effect, no target), Wrath of God effects (doesn’t target), Monstrous Rage targeting itself. Against Boros Energy, always watch for Goblin Bombardment — Leyline Binding is your answer (exiles Bombardment for {W} with Le

engines.title: Leyline Binding Costs {W} Under Leyline
engines.body: Leyline Binding normally costs {5}{W} but has domain: subtract 1 from its cost for each basic land type you control. With all 5 basic land types (via Leyline of the Guildpact), it costs {W} — one white mana to exile any nonland permanent. This is your primary permanent answer. Cast at instant speed during opponent’s attack or in response to ETB triggers. A T1 Binding on their Amulet of Vigor or Ra

engines.title: Board Is Contested
engines.body: They’ve cleared your creatures twice and stabilized at 12 or below. Don’t rebuild the board — two Tribal Flames + Lightning Bolt = 13 damage from hand. Hold mana for burn rather than deploying more creatures into their removal. This plan requires 3 mana and 3 cards but bypasses their entire board.

engines.title: Leyline Combo Is Gone
engines.body: Leyline answered. Your creatures are now fair-sized (3/3–4/4 range). Pivot: deploy one threat at a time backed by Consign to Memory. Use Leyline Binding at flash speed as interaction. Don’t overextend into sweepers — one threat + open mana is the correct posture when you’re in fair mode.

engines.title: Leyline + Scion Are Both Active
engines.body: Leyline in play + Scion in play = all your creatures are hexproof. There is no reason to play around anything — attack with everything. They can’t use targeted removal, they can’t block profitably. This position wins. Commit the board, attack, close.

engines.title: After Each Untap
engines.body: Domain Zoo requires re-identifying its role every turn based on: do I have Leyline? Do I have Scion? What’s their life total? Am I in Tribal Flames range? This deck has three distinct win modes — pilots who autopilot one lose to disruption. Pilots who read each turn and switch cleanly win close games.

engines.title: Leyline of the Guildpact×4
engines.body: Never sideboard out Leylines. The card that makes your deck from "good aggro" to "best aggro" doesn't leave for any matchup. Even in the mirror where both players have Leyline, yours is still symmetrically powering your side.

engines.title: Territorial Kavu×4
engines.body: Your best creature in almost every matchup — 5/5 for {R}{G} that also handles graveyard hate on attack. The only matchup where you might trim one is a pure combo matchup where its attack trigger is irrelevant and you need more interaction.

engines.title: Doorkeeper Thrull/Consign to Memory
engines.body: These come out against matchups with no ETBs to counter. Vs Eldrazi Tron, Ruby Storm, or Tameshi Belcher: Thrull does nothing. Consign to Memory counters triggered abilities — weak when there are none. Cut these first and bring in relevant sideboard pieces.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Midrange-heavy field — no deck can race a T1 5/5 hexproof. Low Wrath density in expected sideboards. Few Leyline of Sanctity builds (it stops Tribal Flames targeting face). Combo decks are present (Tameshi Belcher, Ruby Storm) — your T2 clock outraces them. You have practiced the burn-close line and can calculate lethal from hand before attacking.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy Goblin Bombardment meta — kills through hexproof (sacrifice doesn’t target). Multiple sweeper builds expected (Wrath, Supreme Verdict) — hexproof doesn’t protect from non-targeting sweepers. Leyline of Sanctity density is high — your burn plan is shut off. You haven’t practiced the no-Leyline fair mode — roughly 30% of hands won’t have Leyline.

engines.title: Leyline Binding ×4
engines.body: Your best removal. Free or near-free with a 5-color manabase. Four copies enables the "domain lock" game plan and makes your mana base pay off.

engines.title: Scion of Draco ×4
engines.body: Hexproof 4/4 flier for 2 with a full domain. Never cut — Scion is your most efficient threat and the reward for running five colors.

engines.title: Arid Archon
engines.body: 3 in control-heavy metas where fliers matter. 2 in aggro metas where the 6-drop clock is too slow. Cut to 0 and run more 2-drops in pure aggro fields.

engines.title: Boseiju, Who Endures (SB)
engines.body: 2 copies vs heavy artifact and enchantment metas (Affinity, Amulet Titan). Cut entirely when the field is creature-based.

engines.title: Bring to Light count
engines.body: 3 in combo-heavy metas where tutoring the exact answer is critical. 2 in aggro metas where the 5-drop tutor is too slow to matter before the game ends.

engines.title: Leyline Opens
engines.body: Practice mulliganing for Leyline. Know what a 6-card Leyline hand looks like vs a keep.

engines.title: Domain Math
engines.body: Count your domain before every attack. Know your Kavu's power, your Scion's cost.

engines.title: G2 vs Interaction
engines.body: Drill Stubborn Denial timing — know when you have ferocious and when you don't.

engines.title: Clock Practice
engines.body: Zoo kills T3-4. Practice executing at tournament speed.

matchups.notes: Belcher faster; Stubborn Denial only hope
Kavu exiles GY; Doorkeeper shuts Atraxa
Hexproof protects threats; Doorkeeper shuts ETBs
Storm faster; Stubborn Denial only interaction
Fast clock vs their setup turns
Leyline hexproof; Psychic Frog dismantles hand

EldraziTron.game_plan: Chapter 01 Overview "You don't need to interact with them. You need to be faster than their interaction." Eldrazi Tron is Modern's premier big-mana strategy — a deck that combines the explosive mana acceleration of Urza's Tron lands with the raw power of colorless Eldrazi threats and the flexible toolbox of Karn, the Great Creator .
