When it works, it presents threats on turn 3 that most decks in the format simply can't answer. Thought-Knot Seer strips the opponent's key piece and applies a 4/4 clock. Ugin, Eye of the Storms exiles colored permanents as a cast trigger then again for every subse
EldraziTron.mulligan:
Mulligan Framework

Keep any hand that can assemble Tron by turn 3 OR present a meaningful threat by turn 2.

engines.title: Karn Toolbox + Threats
engines.body: Karn fetches silver bullets from the sideboard for any game plan, while threatening a +1 that turns any artifact into an attacker. The actual threats (Ulamog, Ugin, TKS) close games that Karn stabilizes. Together they form a complete game plan.

engines.title: Three Layers
engines.body: Urza Tron (7 mana when assembled), Ugin's Labyrinth (ETB exile MV 7+ for {C}{C}), and Eldrazi Temple ({C}{C} for colorless Eldrazi). With any two of these plus a Talisman, you can have 5–7 mana on turn 3 without Tron assembled.

engines.title: Karn Static + TKS
engines.body: Karn's static shuts off activated abilities of opponents' artifacts. Thought-Knot Seer strips a card from hand on entry. Together they disrupt nearly every game plan in Modern without spending additional mana after they resolve.

engines.title: Linear Combo Speed
engines.body: Ruby Storm kills turn 2–3. Tameshi Belcher kills turn 4. Simic Neoform kills turn 2–3. Eldrazi Tron's clock is too slow to race these in game 1 without Karn + hate piece. Post-board Disruptor Flute and Trinisphere dramatically improve these matchups.

engines.title: Resilient to Removal
engines.body: Colorless threats are immune to color-based hate. Ulamog has indestructible. Karn's artifacts survive Supreme Verdict. The deck plays through most removal suites by simply casting another threat — the mana is always there to refill.

engines.title: Tier 2 · 5.5%
engines.body: Consistent performer at RCQs. Excellent against midrange and fair blue decks. Struggles against fast combo and Affinity. LucasGiggs' December 2025 run (5 top 8s) validated the Sowing Mycospawn build as optimal for the current meta.

engines.title: {4} · Planeswalker
engines.body: Static: activated abilities of artifacts YOUR OPPONENTS control can't be activated. This shuts Mox Opal (opponent's), Springleaf Drum, Aether Spellbomb, etc. Your own Mox Opal/artifacts still activate normally. −2: reveal artifact from outside the game (your SB) OR choose face-up artifact in exile → put into hand. Karn can fetch artifacts you exiled with Devourer of Destiny, Relic of Progenitus, o

engines.title: {7} · Planeswalker
engines.body: Two exile triggers: (1) cast trigger exiles up to 1 colored permanent, (2) whenever you cast a colorless spell, exile up to 1 colored permanent. Every Eldrazi, every Talisman activation being paid by tapping for colored mana... wait — the trigger says "cast a colorless spell." Talismans aren't spells. But Expedition Map, Kozilek's Command, Thought-Knot Seer, Sowing Mycospawn (devoid = colorless) a

engines.title: Land
engines.body: ETB: you MAY exile a colorless card with MV 7+ from your hand. If you do, {T} adds {C}{C}. Without an exiled card, it only adds {C} — a basic wastes slot. The exiled card can be returned at any time by tapping Labyrinth. Return the card when you want to cast it or to reuse Labyrinth's "exile" slot with a different card. Critically: Ulamog, Ugin, Devourer are all MV 7+ and qualify.

engines.title: {3}{G} · Devoid
engines.body: Devoid = colorless spell (triggers Ugin). When you CAST (not ETB): search library for a land, put it onto battlefield, shuffle. Kicker {1}{C}: when cast if kicked, exile target land. The land search is unconditional — even unkicked, this is a {3}{G} 3/3 that ramps. Kicked, it also permanently removes an opponent's land — stunning in Amulet, Living End, and Storm matchups where the opponent has few

engines.title: {5}{C}{C} · 6/6
engines.body: Reveal from opening hand → at your first upkeep, look at top 4, exile 3, keep 1. The exiled 3 cards go to exile, not hand — Karn can retrieve them with −2 later. When you cast Devourer, exile target colored permanent. Karn can fetch the exiled Devourer-exiled cards back. This creates a two-card loop: Devourer opens exiling their permanent → Karn retrieves useful exile zone cards.

engines.title: {X}{C}{C} · Kindred Instant
engines.body: Choose TWO of four modes: create X Spawn tokens, scry X then draw, exile creature MV ≤ X, exile up to X cards from graveyards. Minimum cost {2}{C}{C} for X=0 (two modes at 0). With Eldrazi Temple: {C}{C} + {2} from land = X=2 on turn 2. Against aggro: X=2 creates 2 tokens (blockers) AND exiles the biggest threat. Versatile removal + ramp + GY hate in one card.

engines.title: Urza's Tron
engines.body: All three Urza lands = 7 mana from 3 land slots. Expedition Map tutors any piece. Assembled by turn 3, Tron enables Karn, Ugin, and Ulamog all in the same turn. Without Tron, the deck is a slower Eldrazi deck. With Tron, it's the most mana-efficient deck in Modern. Always map for the missing piece when you have two.

engines.title: Ugin's Labyrinth
engines.body: Exile a colorless MV 7+ card → {C}{C} per turn. With Ulamog or Devourer of Destiny in opening hand: Labyrinth turn 1 = 2 mana immediately. The exiled card returns to hand when you tap Labyrinth to return it — don't forget this. Sequence Labyrinth before other lands when holding a qualifying card.

engines.title: Eldrazi Temple
engines.body: {C}{C} for casting colorless Eldrazi spells or activating abilities of colorless Eldrazi. Critically: this mana can pay for Kozilek's Command (colorless cost) and for Thought-Knot Seer's {C} requirement. With Temple + a Talisman turn 2, Thought-Knot Seer drops on turn 2.

engines.title: Tron Hands
engines.body: Any hand with 2+ Tron pieces and Expedition Map. Even with slow other cards, the Map finds the third piece on turn 2, enabling Karn/Ugin on turn 3. Karn from turn 3 wins most games singlehandedly — it doesn't need support.

engines.title: Temple + Threat Hands
engines.body: Eldrazi Temple + Talisman + Thought-Knot Seer is a legitimate turn-2 Seer hand. Strip their key piece before they can act. Even if Tron never assembles, a sequence of TKS → Karn → Ugin pressures most decks out of the game.

engines.title: Pure Threat Floods
engines.body: 4+ expensive threats with no acceleration. Ulamog in hand without Labyrinth or Tron pieces means you can't cast it until turn 10. Always ship back hands that can't develop mana — the threats are only good when you can cast them.

engines.title: Karn Hands
engines.body: Karn on turn 3 is often enough to win. Keep if you have 4+ mana available by turn 3 and Karn in hand. Even without Tron, Temple + Talisman + a third source = 4 mana on turn 3. Karn fetching Ensnaring Bridge wins most aggro games immediately.

engines.title: T1 Chalice or Map
engines.body: On the play, T1 Chalice of the Void on 1 shuts down every 1-CMC spell your opponent planned. T1 Expedition Map tutors a Tron piece for T2 assembly. Both are correct depending on their deck — if you saw their hand via T1 Duress in their SB, deploy accordingly. Against aggro: Chalice at 1 immediately. Against combo or control: Expedition Map to race to Tron.

engines.title: Extra Card Finds Tron Piece
engines.body: On the draw you see 8 cards, dramatically improving Tron assembly odds. Keep slightly looser hands on the draw — two Tron pieces + Map is a keep on draw even without a third piece. Against aggro on the draw: Chalice at 1 is urgent — they’ve had a T1 and may have deployed already. Prioritize Chalice over Tron development if their board is ahead.

engines.title: Map + Karn Rebuild
engines.body: Spreading Seas or Blood Moon disrupts Tron. Pivot: Expedition Map finds Eye of Ugin or the missing Tron piece anyway (basic land types don’t apply to colorless utility lands). Karn, the Great Creator fetches any artifact from SB including Ensnaring Bridge or Trinisphere. Eldrazi still cast from colorless mana — you can still function on colorless even without full Tron assembly.

engines.title: Karn Tutor Chain
engines.body: TKS and Ulamog both answered: Karn, the Great Creator’s -2 fetches any artifact from outside the game (your SB). Fetch Ensnaring Bridge to lock out their attacks, Trinisphere to tax their spells, or Relic of Progenitus for GY hate. Karn’s +1 makes their artifacts unable to activate — shut off their Mox Opal, Aether Vial, or Chalice they set against you.

engines.title: Assemble Tron
engines.body: Urza’s Mine + Urza’s Power Plant + Urza’s Tower = 7 colorless mana on T3. This is the foundation of everything. Before deploying threats or interaction, always advance Tron assembly. Expedition Map tutors any land — fetch the missing Tron piece. Ancient Stirrings finds any colorless card including Tron lands. Prioritize assembly over any other action.

engines.title: Karn/Ugin Planeswalker
engines.body: Once Tron is assembled, the T3 play is Karn, the Great Creator or Ugin, the Spirit Dragon. Karn immediately +1s to lock their artifacts or -2s to fetch from SB. Ugin at -X wipes all colored permanents. These are your primary threats and engines — Eldrazi cast alongside them but the walkers generate ongoing value the Eldrazi don’t.

engines.title: TKS / Ulamog Clock
engines.body: Thought-Knot Seer (4 mana) exiles a card from hand and provides a 4/4 body. Ulamog (10 mana) exiles two permanents on cast and attacks with annihilator 4. TKS is your primary disruptive threat and clock. Ulamog is the game-ending threat. Deploy TKS when Tron is online and you need to strip their answer before your Karn resolves.

engines.title: The Dream
engines.body: T1: Expedition Map. T2: Crack Map, find missing Tron piece. All 3 Tron lands in play. T3: 7 mana. Cast Karn (4) or Ugin (8 — needs 1 more land) or TKS (4) + Chalice (1). Karn T3 immediately -2 fetches Ensnaring Bridge or Trinisphere from SB. This is the default goldfish. Any hand with 2 Tron pieces + Map achieves this.

engines.title: Stirrings Line
engines.body: T1: Ancient Stirrings (find Tron piece or Chalice). T2: Deploy Tron piece + Stirrings again. T3: Missing piece found, 7 mana assembles. T4: Ugin (10 mana with 7+3) or TKS + Karn. Without Map, Stirrings is your tutor. Ancient Stirrings finds ANY colorless card including all Eldrazi, walkers, and Tron lands.

engines.title: Chalice vs Tron First
engines.body: Chalice first (T1): Vs aggro (Boros, Prowess, Domain Zoo). Their T1 spells are MV 1 and Chalice stops them immediately. Tron first: Vs combo (Storm, Living End, Amulet). Map T1 to race their kill turn — you need 7 mana before they combo, not just to stop their interaction.

engines.title: TKS Leaving Gives Them a Draw
engines.body: When Thought-Knot Seer enters, it exiles a card from their hand. When TKS LEAVES the battlefield, the opponent draws a card — any card, not the exiled one. Killing your own TKS (sacrifice to dodge removal) gives them a card. Bouncing TKS returns the exiled card AND triggers the draw. Never bounce TKS with a card exiled unless it’s worth giving them a card.

engines.title: Chalice at 1 Stops Your Own Interaction Too
engines.body: Chalice of the Void on 1 counters ALL spells with MV 1, including your Walking Ballista at 0 (pays 0 then enters as a 0/0), your Dismember, and any MV-1 SB card. Set Chalice after you’ve deployed your own MV-1 pieces. Chalice at 0 stops free spells: Force of Negation alternate cost, suspend spells being cast for free. Know what each setting stops before placing.

engines.title: All Is Dust Hits Only Colored Permanents
engines.body: All Is Dust makes each player sacrifice all colored permanents. Your Eldrazi, your lands, your Chalice, your Karn, your Ulamog — all colorless, all survive. Their colored creatures, planeswalkers, enchantments die. This is not a symmetrical Wrath. Cast it when they have a colored board and you have a colorless one. Your colorless board survives their response to it.

engines.title: Their Board Is Faster Than Yours
engines.body: Tron isn’t assembled by T3 and they have a creature board. Karn -2 fetches Ensnaring Bridge immediately. Trinisphere taxes every spell they cast. Chalice at 1 stops their interaction. Switch from developing Tron to deploying hate pieces that slow them enough to assemble on T4.

engines.title: Tron Is Online
engines.body: Tron assembled, 7+ mana available. Stop developing, start threatening. Karn T3, TKS T4, Ulamog T5 if the game goes long. Every turn you have 7+ mana is a turn they should be losing. Don’t pass without casting something impactful.

engines.title: Karn + Empty Hand Available
engines.body: Karn in play + 0 cards in hand = fetch Ensnaring Bridge immediately. This position is often a clean lock — they can’t attack (Bridge), you have Karn generating ongoing value. Execute this line the moment the conditions are met.

engines.title: Race vs Lock
engines.body: Their deck races you (Boros, Prowess, Domain) → Chalice T1, lock them out of interaction. Their deck combos you (Storm, Living End) → Map T1, race to Tron faster than they kill. Their deck controls you (Jeskai, UWC) → TKS T4 to strip counters, Ulamog T5 to close.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Midrange and fair interactive fields — your Tron threats are too large for their answers. Low Damping Sphere density (shuts off multiple untaps per bounce land, but for you: limits to 1 mana per land). Combo-heavy fields (Storm, Living End) — TKS strips their key card. You’ve practiced the Karn SB tutor chains for the top 5 matchups.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy Blood Moon meta — Blood Moon makes all nonbasic lands Mountains, turning your Tron lands into Mountains that produce R, breaking assembly. High Spreading Seas density (turns your land into an Island, breaking Tron). You haven’t practiced the Karn tutor chain for the expected matchups — wrong SB fetch under pressure costs games.

engines.title: Chalice of the Void ×4
engines.body: The whole reason to play Eldrazi Tron. Chalice on 1 shuts off every 1-drop in the format — Ragavan, Spell Pierce, Fatal Push. Never cut.

engines.title: Karn, the Great Creator ×4
engines.body: Your toolbox win condition. Karn finding the exact hate piece for each matchup is what separates Eldrazi Tron from other big-mana decks. Four copies ensures you see it.

engines.title: Reality Smasher
engines.body: 3 in creature-removal-light metas. 4 when you expect lots of midrange where a 5/5 trample haste demands two spells to answer. Cut to 2 when the format is burn-heavy (dies to Bolt + Bolt).

engines.title: Ensnaring Bridge (Karn Wish Target)
engines.body: 1 copy in the sideboard as Karn's best wish target vs creature decks. 2 copies vs heavy aggro metas. Never main deck — only accessed through Karn.

engines.title: Walking Ballista count
engines.body: 2 as a Karn wish target and finisher. 3 in combo metas where pinging for 1 repeatedly matters. Ballista also functions as an answer to 1/1 tokens — increase when tokens are everywhere.

engines.title: T2 TKS Lines
engines.body: Practice assembling T2 Thought-Knot Seer. Sol land + Expedition Map or Eye of Ugin.

engines.title: Chalice Decision
engines.body: Drill setting Chalice at the right number for each matchup. 1 vs most, 0 vs Dredge.

engines.title: All Is Dust Timing
engines.body: Practice when to hold All Is Dust vs deploy it. Sorcery speed = attack first.

engines.title: Clock Practice
engines.body: Tron can flood — count real turns to lethal and commit to the kill.

engines.title: Ensnaring Bridge
engines.body: Empty your hand. Creatures with power greater than hand size can't attack. Fetch immediately on turn 3.

engines.title: Trinisphere
engines.body: All spells cost at least {3}. Ritual chains collapse. Storm can't chain under Trinisphere.

engines.title: Disruptor Flute
engines.body: Choose name. That spell costs {3} more + activated abilities blanked. Name the opponent's win condition.

engines.title: Walking Ballista
engines.body: Cast for X, get X counters, ping for 1 each. Kills Ragavan, Guide of Souls, 1-drops.

engines.title: Damping Sphere
engines.body: Bounce lands produce {C}. Each spell +1 per prior spell. Disrupts Amulet and Storm chains.

engines.title: Grafdigger's Cage
engines.body: Creatures can't enter from GY. Stops Persist, Goryo's, Living End all at once.

Glockulous.game_plan: Chapter 01 Identity & Philosophy "Discard the Archon. Return the Archon. They lose." — Core Mantra Glockulous is a graveyard midrange deck built around one axis: get Archon of Cruelty into the graveyard as fast as possible, then return it repeatedly for 2 mana. The Archon ETB + attack trigger is a 6-point life swing per occurrence — opponent sacrifices a creature or planeswalker, discards a card, loses 3 life; you draw a card and gain 3 life. Against most decks, two Archon triggers is a functional win. What makes Glockulous better than pure Grixis Reanimator is its dual-axis structure . Psychi
Glockulous.strengths: Archon of Cruelty is the single strongest per-trigger effect in Modern — one trigger stabilizes from losing positions. Dual axis: graveyard hate doesn't shut you down because Frog + Emperor win on the fair game. Harbinger of the Seas is the most efficient land hate piece in the format — 3 mana collapses three-color manabases. Thoughtseize clears the path for Persist or Emperor Adapt.
Glockulous.weaknesses: Rest in Peace and Leyline of the Void shut off both Persist and Emperor of Bones entirely — you're forced onto the pure fair axis. Finality counter means Emperor-reanimated Archon goes to exile on death — no second Persist . Fast aggro (Prowess) kills before Archon can stabilize. Galvanic Discharge at 3 energy minimum kills Psychic Frog (2/2) and Emperor of Bones (2/2) cleanly.
Glockulous.mulligan:
Mulligan Philosophy

Snap keep: Any 7 with Faithless Looting (or Thought Scour) + a black source + Persist or Emperor.

engines.title: Archon of Cruelty
engines.body: {6}{B}{B} 6/6 flying. Not legendary — multiple can coexist. Triggers on enter OR attack each time: opponent sacrifices creature or planeswalker, discards a card, loses 3 life; you draw, gain 3. This is a 6-point life swing per trigger, not 7. A Persisted Archon fires the ETB on entry, then again on attack — two triggers from one return, 12 life swings total.

engines.title: Persist
engines.body: {1}{B} sorcery. Return target nonlegendary creature card from graveyard to battlefield with a -1/-1 counter. Archon enters as a 5/5 flier (6/6 base minus -1/-1). Still triggers the full ETB swing at 5/5. Persist is a colored sorcery — Consign to Memory cannot counter it. Only Counterspell , Force of Negation , and similar spell counters can answer it. This matters enormously when planning your pro

engines.title: Faithless Looting
engines.body: {R} sorcery: draw 2, discard 2. Flashback {2}{R}. Primary graveyard filler. The draw and discard are simultaneous in a sense — you draw 2 first, then discard 2. You cannot draw Archon then discard it in the same Looting. Ideal discard: Archon + Troll of Khazad-dûm . Flashback {2}{R} later for additional filtering. One Looting on turn 1 can have Archon in the yard ready for Persist on turn 3.

engines.title: Psychic Frog
engines.body: {U}{B} 1/2. Combat damage to player or planeswalker → draw a card. Discard a card: put a +1/+1 counter on it (activated ability). Exile 3 cards from GY: flying until EOT. The Frog simultaneously draws cards, discards Archon into the graveyard, and grows as a threat. A Frog that connects twice in a game represents both a 3/3+ attacker and two free Archon discards. Its flying ability requires 3 grav

engines.title: Emperor of Bones
engines.body: {1}{B} 2/2. At beginning of combat: exile up to one target card from any graveyard. {1}{B}: Adapt 2 (activated ability). When +1/+1 counters are placed on it, put the exiled creature onto the battlefield under your control with a finality counter and haste. Sacrifice it at beginning of next end step. The Adapt is an activated ability — Consign to Memory cannot counter it. The creature enters with

engines.title: Harbinger of the Seas
engines.body: {1}{U}{U} 2/2 Merfolk Wizard. Nonbasic lands are Islands — continuous static effect, not a trigger. Doesn't destroy or return lands. It changes their subtype. When Harbinger enters, every nonbasic land in play immediately becomes an Island. Sanctifier en-Vec on a board with Harbinger in play cannot generate W from converted nonbasics. Boros Energy loses access to red and white mana from their shoc

engines.title: What You Do Well
engines.body: Archon of Cruelty is the single strongest per-trigger effect in Modern — one trigger stabilizes from losing positions. Dual axis: graveyard hate doesn't shut you down because Frog + Emperor win on the fair game. Harbinger of the Seas is the most efficient land hate piece in the format — 3 mana collapses three-color manabases. Thoughtseize clears the path for Persist or Emperor Adapt.

engines.title: What Beats You
engines.body: Rest in Peace and Leyline of the Void shut off both Persist and Emperor of Bones entirely — you're forced onto the pure fair axis. Finality counter means Emperor-reanimated Archon goes to exile on death — no second Persist . Fast aggro (Prowess) kills before Archon can stabilize. Galvanic Discharge at 3 energy minimum kills Psychic Frog (2/2) and Emperor of Bones (2/2) cleanly.

engines.title: Archon of Cruelty
engines.body: Not legendary — multiple can be on the battlefield. Triggers on enter AND on attack — a Persisted Archon fires ETB on entry (5/5 with -1/-1 counter), then fires attack trigger when it attacks. Two triggers from one return = 12-point life swing in one turn. Each subsequent Persist adds another -1/-1 counter (5/5 → 4/4 → 3/3 etc.).

engines.title: Emperor of Bones
engines.body: The exile happens at the beginning of combat — exile any card from any graveyard, including opponents'. Then Adapt ({1}{B}: Adapt 2) is an activated ability, not a spell — Consign to Memory cannot counter it. The creature enters with a finality counter: if it dies it is permanently exiled, not put in the graveyard. Cannot be Persisted again after Emperor reanimates it.

engines.title: Troll of Khazad-dûm
engines.body: Swampcycling {1}: discard this card from your hand, search for a Swamp card (any Swamp subtype — includes Watery Grave and Blood Crypt ), put it in your hand. This is not drawing a card. With Looting in hand, always discard Troll via Looting instead — you keep the land and get to filter. Only swampcycle when you need a land and don't have Looting.

engines.title: Unearth
engines.body: {B} sorcery: return target creature card with mana value 3 or less from GY to battlefield. Cycling {2}. Targets: Psychic Frog (MV 2) ✓, Emperor of Bones (MV 2) ✓, Harbinger of the Seas (MV 3) ✓. Does NOT target Archon (MV 8), Troll (MV 6). Persist is the card for Archon — Unearth is for your 2-3 mana threats. The cycling {2} lets you pitch it for a fresh draw when the target isn't relevant.

engines.title: Fill or Disrupt
engines.body: Option A: Faithless Looting — draw 2, discard Archon + Troll. Archon is now in the yard with 1 mana spent. Option B: Thought Scour target player — mill 2 (yourself), draw 1. If you mill Archon, even better. Option C: Thoughtseize their removal spell or Solitude to protect your turn 3. Option D: Swampcycle Troll if you need a black source. In order of priority: Looting > Thoughtseize > Thought Scou

engines.title: Deploy a Threat
engines.body: Psychic Frog ({U}{B}) or Emperor of Bones ({1}{B}). Emperor on turn 2 means on turn 3: exile Archon at beginning of combat, Adapt for {1}{B}, Archon enters with finality counter and haste, attacks immediately — two Archon triggers total on turn 3. Psychic Frog turn 2 means turn 3 you attack, deal damage, draw a card, and then Persist Archon — a full midrange turn plus combo payoff.

engines.title: Persistor Emperor Trigger
engines.body: Ideal: cast Persist ({1}{B}), Archon enters as a 5/5 flier, ETB fires. Opponent sacrifices a permanent, discards a card, loses 3. You draw and gain 3. At 17 life with one fewer permanent and one fewer card — the game is nearly won. Attack with Archon on turn 4 for the second trigger. Alternatively: Emperor of Bones Adapt resolves, Archon enters with haste, attacks — both triggers on the same turn.

engines.title: Close or Rebuild
engines.body: Attack with Archon (second trigger if Persisted on 3). If Archon was answered, Psychic Frog continues drawing into the second copy. Faithless Looting flashback ({2}{R}) refills. Unearth returns Harbinger of the Seas (MV 3) at instant speed if needed. Second Persist or second Emperor reanimates again. You have 4 Archons, 4 Persists, 4 Emperors — the redundancy outlasts most hate.

engines.title: T1 Faithless Looting Sets Everything
engines.body: On the play, T1 Faithless Looting mills 2 cards and discards 2 — filling your GY with Griselbrand and the fatties you want to reanimate while finding your reanimation spell. The sooner Griselbrand is in the GY, the sooner you can reanimate it. On the play: Looting > any other T1. Never spend T1 on a land-pass if Looting is in hand.

engines.title: Grief First on Draw
engines.body: On the draw, opponents have had a T1. They may have deployed a threat or GY hate. Consider T1 Grief (evoke for {B}) to strip their Endurance, Relic, or key spell from hand before you try to reanimate T2. The extra card on draw makes Grief+reanimate lines more consistent. On draw vs blue decks: always consider Grief first to clear the counter before attempting reanimation.

engines.title: Fair Mode — Grief + Drown
engines.body: Nihil Spellbomb or Endurance exiles your GY. Pivot: Grief (3/1 menace body), Drown in the Loch (counter or destroy at instant speed), and Unearth targets that aren’t in the GY yet (small creatures). Surveil aggressively to fill GY again for a second reanimation window. Don’t scoop to GY exile — the fair plan is real.

engines.title: Second Target from Hand
engines.body: Griselbrand removed: look for your second reanimation target in hand or GY. Troll of Khazad-dûm is a backup large threat. Persist creatures (Kitchen Finks) generate ETB value. Grief is a 3/1 body. Chain reanimation attempts — you have multiple fatties and multiple reanimation spells. The second reanimation is almost always available.

engines.title: GY Fill + Reanimate Griselbrand
engines.body: Faithless Looting + reanimation spell is the primary engine. Looting puts Griselbrand in GY on T1, reanimate on T2. Griselbrand enters with haste (no — 7/7 lifelink, no haste). Pay 7 life: draw 7. Find your protection (Grief strips their answer). This is the engine that wins in 1-2 turns — execute as fast as possible.

engines.title: Griselbrand Draw Chain
engines.body: Griselbrand in play: pay 7, draw 7. Find Animate Dead, Living End, or another protection piece. Pay 7 again (14 life spent total). Find your next threat. Each activation draws 7 — at 21 starting life, you can activate 3 times for 21 cards. Stop when you have what you need. This engine converts a resolved Griselbrand into an instant-win with enough life.

engines.title: Persist Loop (Backup)
engines.body: Kitchen Finks or other Persist creatures + a sacrifice outlet = recursive life gain and ETB triggers. Finks returns with -1/-1 counter, dies again, counter goes to +1/+1 via Melira (if in build) or just loops for 2 life per cycle. This is the fair backup when Griselbrand is exiled and the GY is empty — grind with Persist until a reanimation window opens.

engines.title: The Dream
engines.body: T1: Faithless Looting — discard Griselbrand + any other fatty. T2: Any reanimation spell targeting Griselbrand. Griselbrand enters (7/7 lifelink). Pay 7 life, draw 7. Find Grief to strip their answer. Pay 7 again. Now at 7 life but with 14 extra cards drawn. Win condition in hand. This T2 line is real and must be answered or they lose.

engines.title: Grief First Then Reanimate
engines.body: T1: Looting or Grief (strip their Endurance/counter). T2: Continue GY fill or second discard. T3: Reanimate Griselbrand or fatty. This is the default vs interactive decks. The extra turn spent on Grief protection converts the coin flip (will they Endurance?) into a near-certain resolution.

engines.title: Blue Mana Check
engines.body: Rush T2: No blue sources visible. Fair deck (Boros, Prowess). Race their clock. Wait for T3: They have open blue mana. T1 Grief strips Endurance or Force of Negation from hand, THEN reanimate T3 safely. The one-turn delay is worth the protection.

engines.title: GY Exile in Response = Fizzle
engines.body: Reanimation spells target a creature card in a graveyard. If the GY is exiled in response — Endurance flash, Nihil Spellbomb, Relic of Progenitus — the target is illegal and the reanimation spell fizzles. Griselbrand does not enter. The spell is countered by rules (illegal target). This is why your Grief must strip Endurance before you attempt reanimation vs blue decks.

engines.title: Griselbrand Draws 7 Can Be Repeated
engines.body: Griselbrand’s ability costs 7 life and has no mana cost. You can activate it multiple times per turn as long as you have 7+ life each time. At 21 life: activate 3 times = draw 21 cards. Use this to find your combo pieces, protection, or second reanimation target. After activation 1, you have 14 life — activate again. At 14: activate again, 7 life left. Optimal: stop at 1 activation if you already

engines.title: Persist/Undying Counters Cancel Each Other
engines.body: If a creature has both Persist (-1/-1 counter on return) and a +1/+1 counter already on it, the -1/-1 and +1/+1 cancel and the creature returns clean without either counter. Kitchen Finks with a +1/+1 counter on it that dies: Persist triggers, returns, the counters cancel = clean Finks. This enables infinite ETB loops with sacrifice outlets: sac Finks (+1/+1 counter), Persist returns it clean, sac

engines.title: No Blue, Fair Deck
engines.body: Boros, Prowess, Domain Zoo: no counterspells or instant GY exile. Race with T2 Griselbrand immediately. Every turn they draw is a turn closer to finding hate.

engines.title: Blue Mana Visible
engines.body: Strip Endurance or Force of Negation T1 with Grief. Reanimate T3 safely. One-turn delay converts a coin flip into a near-certain resolution.

engines.title: GY Locked
engines.body: Multiple hate pieces active. Switch to Grief+Drown value plan. Surveil to rebuild GY for the next reanimate window. Drown kills their key creature or counters their spell.

engines.title: Active Cage or Relic
engines.body: Grafdigger’s Cage = no reanimation. Relic of Progenitus will exile your GY end step. Answer hate pieces with Mystical Dispute or Nihil Spellbomb before attempting reanimation.

engines.title: Looting T1,PersistT3
engines.body: T1 Faithless Looting , discard Archon + Troll. T2 Emperor of Bones . T3 beginning of combat: exile Archon. Adapt: Archon enters with haste. ETB fires, attack trigger fires. They're at 14 life, one card down, one permanent short before turn 4. Apply maximum pressure from the first turn.

engines.title: ThoughtseizeRagavan
engines.body: They'll have Ragavan on turn 1 before you. Thoughtseize it out of their hand if possible, or Fatal Push when it attacks. A Ragavan that connects generates mana + cards that accelerates Goblin Bombardment . Prioritize removing Ragavan even if it delays your Archon plan by one turn.

engines.title: Thoughtseizeon 1
engines.body: Thoughtseize turn 1 to see their hand and take the Solitude or Force of Negation . Then Looting turn 1 if you have it. Emperor turn 2, Archon via Emperor on turn 3. With Solitude gone, Archon enters freely. Their only answer is Consign to Memory — which cannot stop the Emperor Adapt or the Archon ETB itself (only triggered abilities from resolved spells).

engines.title: HoldMystical Dispute
engines.body: They develop Guide of Souls and White Orchid Phantom before you can act. Hold Mystical Dispute for their Counterspell — Dispute counters blue spells for {U} when they control an Island. Counterspell is blue. Force of Negation is blue. One Dispute protecting your Persist resolves the game. Fire it in response to their counter.

engines.title: Race with Max Aggression
engines.body: T1 Looting → Archon in yard. T2 Emperor of Bones . T3 Archon via Emperor with haste — two triggers. Two Archon triggers from a 20-life start puts them at 14 or lower with fewer permanents. Prowess cannot generate lethal from 14 on the board they'll have after sacrificing a creature to the Archon trigger.

engines.title: RemoveDragon's Rage Channeler
engines.body: Their DRC at delirium is a 3/3 flier that must attack — this is the creature that deals the most damage before you can stabilize. Fatal Push kills it cleanly (MV 1, no revolt needed). Priority: kill DRC before it achieves delirium and grows. A 1/1 DRC is a minor annoyance. A 3/3 DRC with delirium deals 9+ damage before you answer it.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Low Endurance density in expected SBs — flash GY exile is the hardest card to play through. Midrange-heavy field where your T2 7/7 is faster than their clock. Few Grafdigger’s Cage builds. Combo present (Storm, Living End) — your T2 Griselbrand is faster. You’ve practiced the fair-mode Grief+Drown game for when reanimate fails.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Multiple Endurance builds expected — flash GY exile in response to reanimation is extremely difficult to beat. High Nihil Spellbomb density. Heavy Grafdigger’s Cage builds. You haven’t practiced the Griselbrand activation count — activating too many times at low life loses games you would have won.

engines.title: Persist ×4
engines.body: Your combo piece. Without Persist, you have no way to reanimate at instant speed. Four copies non-negotiable.

engines.title: Psychic Frog ×4
engines.body: Your best interactive threat and combo enabler. Frog puts cards in GY for Persist and applies a clock. Four copies — the deck doesn't function below 4.

engines.title: Emperor of Bones
engines.body: 3 in metas where ETB triggers matter (it adds a +1/+1 counter each time a nontoken creature enters). 2 when the adapt cost matters less than having more disruption.

engines.title: Nihil Spellbomb (SB)
engines.body: 3 in GY-heavy metas (Living End, Goryo's Vengeance). 2 as a general hedge. The cycling ability means it's never a dead draw — always worth at least one card.

engines.title: Drown in the Loch count
engines.body: 3 in counter-heavy metas where their GY fills quickly, making Drown efficient. 2 in aggro metas where their GY is typically empty early and Drown is a conditional removal spell.

engines.title: Persist Sequencing
engines.body: Practice Thoughtseize → Persist → Archon ETB in one smooth sequence. No pausing.

engines.title: Consign Emperor Trigger
engines.body: Drill countering Emperor's sacrifice trigger. This is the highest-skill interaction in the deck.

engines.title: Fair Frog Plan
engines.body: Practice winning with Frog plan when Archon is answered repeatedly. Know when to pivot.

engines.title: GY Hate Reps
engines.body: Play through Rest in Peace and Nihil Spellbomb. These are your most common post-board obstacles.

engines.title: ThoughtseizeBeforePersist
engines.body: If their hand is unknown and they have UU available, Thoughtseize first. Strip the counter. Then resolve Persist into a clear hand. One Persist countered without a follow-up is close to a game loss.

engines.title: Finality Counter = Permanent Exile
engines.body: Emperor-reanimated creatures go to exile when they die. Never swing Emperor-reanimated Archon into lethal blocks unless the game is won regardless. The ETB already fired — the attack trigger is bonus, not mandatory.

engines.title: PersistCounters Consign — Not Stoppped By It
engines.body: Persist is a black sorcery. Consign to Memory counters triggered abilities and colorless spells. Persist is neither. Play Persist into Consign mana with full confidence. Only Counterspell , Force of Negation , and similar stop it.

engines.title: Nihil Spellbomb— Pop BeforePersist
engines.body: Pop the Spellbomb on their upkeep or end step when Archon is in their yard. Don't wait for them to tap into Persist . The window to deny their return is before they cast it, not in response.

matchups.notes: Reanimate — Persist on 3 before they stabilize
Reanimate — Archon on 3 stabilizes the board
Disrupt + Kill — Thoughtseize then resolve threats
Race + Harbinger — lock their mana, Archon closes
Midrange — Nihil Spellbomb + Frog grind wins
Frog + Emperor win before their artifact engine assembles
TKS strips Persist — Chalice at 1 shuts Looting
Faster clock than your setup — Archon too slow
Graveyard mirror — RiP hurts both, Frog wins fair game
Thoughtseize strips payoff — race with Frog beats Grapeshot

Goryo'sVengeance.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Identity "Two mana instant. Legendary creature from the graveyard. Haste. Exile at end of turn — unless you Ephemerate it first. Then it stays forever. Then Ephemerate rebounds. Then it enters a THIRD time. Atraxa reveals 30 cards. Griselbrand draws 21. Pick your poison." Goryo's Vengeance is Modern's fastest reanimator combo. The namesake card — Goryo's Vengeance ({1}{B}, instant) — returns a legendary creature from your graveyard with haste, but exiles it at end of turn. The trick: Ephemerate ({W}) blinks the creature before the exile trigger, creating a new game object that
Goryo'sVengeance.mulligan:
Mulligan Guide
Snap Keep
Auto-Keep Conditions
Frog + Goryo's + 3 lands.

engines.title: Goryo's Vengeance
engines.body: {1}{B} Instant — Arcane. "Return target legendary creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield. That creature gains haste. Exile it at the beginning of the next end step." INSTANT SPEED. Cast on opponent's end step → creature is on your side for your entire turn with haste. Or cast main phase with Ephemerate backup. Targets LEGENDARY creatures only — Atraxa ✓, Griselbrand ✓, Ulamog ✓. Spli

engines.title: Ephemerate
engines.body: {W} Instant. "Exile target creature you control, then return it. Rebound." This is the card that makes Goryo's broken. Cast before end step → creature blinks → returns as a NEW OBJECT → exile clause from Goryo's no longer applies → creature stays PERMANENTLY. Rebound next upkeep: cast again for free → THIRD ETB. One {W} spell = save your creature + 2 extra ETB triggers. Also combos with Solitude (

engines.title: Atraxa, Grand Unifier
engines.body: {3}{G}{W}{U}{B} 7/7 Legendary Phyrexian Angel. Flying, vigilance, deathtouch, lifelink. "ETB: reveal top 10, take one of each card type (artifact, battle, creature, enchantment, instant, land, planeswalker, sorcery)." Up to 8 cards per ETB. With Goryo's + Ephemerate: 3 ETBs = reveal top 30, take up to 24 cards. Plus a 7/7 with 4 keywords. Hard-cast cost is {3}{G}{W}{U}{B} — irrelevant. You're payi

engines.title: Griselbrand
engines.body: {4}{B}{B}{B}{B} 7/7 Legendary Demon. Flying, lifelink. "Pay 7 life: Draw seven cards." With Goryo's: enter → attack for 7 lifelink (net 0 life) → pay 7 life draw 7 → pay 7 more draw 7 → you've drawn 14 cards and have a 7/7 flying lifelink. Ephemerate before EOT saves it permanently. Griselbrand is the raw power option — draw your entire deck and find whatever you need.

engines.title: Solitude + Ephemerate
engines.body: Solitude: {3}{W}{W} 3/2 Flash, Lifelink. Evoke — exile a white card from hand. "ETB: exile up to one target creature." Evoke Solitude for free → ETB exiles a creature → evoke sacrifice trigger on stack → response: Ephemerate → Solitude blinks → returns as new object → sacrifice trigger fizzles → Solitude stays + SECOND exile trigger → Rebound next upkeep → THIRD exile. Free = exile 3 creatures ove

engines.title: Psychic Frog
engines.body: {U}{B}: Frog enters. Opponent's end step: discard Atraxa to Frog → Frog gets +1/+1 counter, Atraxa goes to GY. You now have the reanimation target ready.

engines.title: Goryo's Vengeance
engines.body: {1}{B} instant: Atraxa enters from GY with haste. ETB #1: reveal top 10, take 4-6 cards. Now hold priority — cast Ephemerate ({W}). Atraxa blinks. ETB #2: reveal top 10, take 4-6 more cards. Atraxa stays permanently.

engines.title: Rebound + Attack
engines.body: Upkeep: Ephemerate rebounds from exile for free. Atraxa blinks AGAIN. ETB #3: reveal top 10, take 4-6 MORE cards. Attack with 7/7 flying vigilance deathtouch lifelink. You've drawn 12-18 extra cards and have an unkillable threat. Game over.

engines.title: Draw Your Entire Deck
engines.body: Goryo's → Griselbrand enters with haste. Attack for 7 lifelink (back to 20). Pay 7 life → draw 7. Pay 7 → draw 7. You've drawn 14 cards and have a 7/7 flying lifelink. Find Ephemerate in those 14 cards → blink Griselbrand → stays permanently. Alternatively: just hold all the answers you drew and win next turn.

engines.title: Frog + Solitude + Ephemerate
engines.body: When combo is disrupted: Psychic Frog grows every turn via discard, draws cards on hit. Solitude evoke + Ephemerate = exile 3 creatures for free. Quantum Riddler draws cards on ETB. You're an Esper control deck with a combo finish that can pivot entirely to fair Magic and still win through card advantage.

engines.title: Auto-Keep Conditions
engines.body: Frog + Goryo's + 3 lands. Full combo in hand. Keep. Frog + Ephemerate + 2 lands. Find Goryo's in 2 draws. Keep. Thoughtseize + Goryo's + Ephemerate + 2 lands. Strip their counter T1, combo T2. Keep.

engines.title: Auto-Ship Conditions
engines.body: No Frog AND no discard outlet. Can't get legendary into GY. Ship. No black source. Can't cast Goryo's. Ship. Only legendary creatures, no setup pieces. Holding targets without enablers. Ship.

engines.title: Context-Dependent
engines.body: Goryo's + 2 lands, no Frog: Keep vs combo/control, ship vs aggro. All disruption, no combo: Keep on draw vs fast decks, ship on play vs midrange. Six-card hands: Keep any 6 with Frog + 2 mana sources.

engines.title: T1 Thoughtseize Window
engines.body: T1 Thoughtseize before they develop. Strip their counterspell or GY hate. Then T2 Goryo’s is uncontested. You see their hand before they deploy interaction. Never skip T1 Thoughtseize on the play.

engines.title: Instant-Speed Everything
engines.body: Can’t Thoughtseize first. Frog discard at their END STEP — never main phase. Minimizes Surgical Extraction window. T1 Frog, discard at their EOT, Goryo’s at their EOT, untap attacking with haste.

engines.title: Pivot to Esper Control
engines.body: Rest in Peace or Leyline in play: combo is offline. Don’t fight through it. Find Wear // Tear and switch. Solitude evoke + Ephemerate to exile threats, Frog for a clock, Riddler for card advantage.

engines.title: Frog Beats Mode
engines.body: Atraxa Surgical’d or Goryo’s countered: lean on Frog. By T4 Frog is 5/6+ flying that draws on every hit. Discard irrelevant legendaries to grow it. A 6/7 flying that draws on damage is a real 3–4 turn clock.

engines.title: Goryo’s + Ephemerate
engines.body: Default. 3 mana = permanent 7/7 with 3 ETBs. Wins games on T2 against any fair deck. If the window is open and you have both pieces, execute.

engines.title: Solitude + Ephemerate
engines.body: Free removal loop. 0 mana + 1 card = exile 3 creatures permanently. Use to stabilize against aggro or buy turns before the combo window opens.

engines.title: Frog Beats
engines.body: Backup win condition. Closes games when other engines are offline. Frog + Ephemerate also generates card advantage (blink on connection = draw).

engines.title: Fastest Line
engines.body: T1 Frog. Their EOT: discard Atraxa. T2 (their EOT): Goryo’s → ETB #1 (reveal 10, take 4–6). Hold priority: Ephemerate. ETB #2 (4–6 more). Atraxa stays permanent. T3 upkeep: Rebound. ETB #3. Cost: {1}{B}{W} = 3 mana. Cards seen: 12–18.

engines.title: Find Anything Line
engines.body: Same line with Griselbrand. ETB #1: pay 7 life, draw 7. Find Ephemerate. ETB #2: pay 7 life, draw 7. Find answer. Cost: 14 life, 14+ cards drawn. Use when you need a specific answer. Atraxa is better when you just need to win.

engines.title: When to Wait
engines.body: T2: Thoughtseize cleared their hand, tapped out, or their EOT. T3: Need Thoughtseize first, or their counterspell mana is up. Don’t rush into open mana.

engines.title: Cast Goryo’s at Their End Step
engines.body: Goryo’s is instant. Cast at their EOT → haste → "exile at NEXT end step" = YOUR end step. You untap, attack, trigger ETBs before exile. You always get a full attack step without Ephemerate. Only use main phase if Ephemerate is in hand.

engines.title: Ephemerate Before the Exile Trigger
engines.body: After Goryo’s resolves, the exile trigger is on stack. Cast Ephemerate BEFORE it resolves. Creature blinks → returns as new object → exile trigger targets the old object (gone) → fizzles. Creature stays permanently.

engines.title: Atraxa Reveals Go to Bottom
engines.body: "Put the rest on the BOTTOM in random order." Gone for the rest of the game. With 3 ETBs you see 30 cards — choose 8–10. The rest are effectively exiled. Choose cards that close the game, not cards you might need later.

engines.title: Frog T1 → Goryo's T2
engines.body: T1: {U}{B} land, Psychic Frog. Opponent's end step: discard Atraxa → Frog gets counter (2/3), Atraxa in GY. T2: Land. Goryo's Vengeance ({1}{B}) → Atraxa enters with haste. ETB: reveal top 10, take 4-6 cards. Hold priority → Ephemerate ({W}) → Atraxa blinks → ETB #2. Atraxa stays permanently. Attack for 7 (flying, vigilance, deathtouch, lifelink). Opponent is down 7 life, you're up 8-12 cards. T3:

engines.title: Thoughtseize T1 → Setup T2 → Goryo's T3
engines.body: T1: Thoughtseize — strip their interaction, gain information. T2: Psychic Frog OR Roiling Dragonstorm. If Frog: discard Atraxa at their end step. If Dragonstorm: draw 2, discard Atraxa. T3: Goryo's + Ephemerate. Atraxa enters permanently with 3 ETBs over 2 turns. You know their hand is safe (Thoughtseize T1). This is the consistent line — it happens in ~40% of games.

engines.title: Do they have GY hate?
engines.body: If you see Rest in Peace, Leyline of the Void, Nihil Spellbomb, or Relic of Progenitus: switch immediately to Esper Control. Don’t fight through GY hate — go around it. Your fair game plan is legitimate.

engines.title: Is Frog already closing?
engines.body: If Psychic Frog is attacking uncontested and drawing cards: don’t slow down to set up the combo. Frog Beats is winning. Discard the legendary creatures to make Frog bigger. Close the game.

engines.title: Is the combo window open?
engines.body: Did T1 Thoughtseize clear their counterspell? Is their hand empty or weak? Is it their end step and they’re tapped out? That’s the combo window. Frog discard + Goryo’s is always instant-speed. Take it.

engines.title: Go Around the Hate
engines.body: They resolve GY hate (any form). Your Goryo’s plan is offline. Immediately cut the combo lines — don’t look for answers, just switch. Your Solitude + Ephemerate package was already in your deck. Deploy it.

engines.title: Let the Clock Run
engines.body: Frog is connecting and growing. They’re spending resources on Frog and have nothing left for Goryo’s. Every card Frog draws improves your position. Don’t interrupt a winning game plan.

engines.title: The Window Opens
engines.body: You’re in Control mode and their GY hate gets answered (Wear // Tear, Prismatic Ending). Their hand is empty. It’s their EOT. The combo window just opened again — take it. Don’t be afraid to switch back.

engines.title: Mid-Combo
engines.body: If you’ve already discarded the legendary creature and are holding Goryo’s + Ephemerate: execute the combo. Don’t second-guess mid-sequence. You committed to this line — run it to completion.

engines.title: Subtlety ×2
engines.body: {2}{U}{U} 3/3 Flash Flying. Evoke — exile a blue card. ETB: put target creature/planeswalker spell on top or bottom of library. Evoke for free by pitching a blue card (Frog, Riddler, Ephemerate). Stops their key creature from resolving. The blue pitch is also useful to feed Frog's GY. Board in vs combo, mirrors, decks with must-answer creatures.

engines.title: Nihil Spellbomb ×2
engines.body: {1} Artifact. "{T}, Sacrifice: Exile target player's graveyard." When sacrificed, pay {B} to draw a card. Nukes opponent's GY at instant speed. Against Living End: crack before Living End resolves → they get nothing. Against Phlage recursion in Boros Energy. Against mirror: exile their Atraxa. The {B} draw clause means it's never dead.

engines.title: Thoughtseize ×2 (extra copies)
engines.body: Additional copies beyond the 3 main. Board in against combo, control, and any deck where information + disruption wins games. 4 total Thoughtseize post-board means you see their hand nearly every game. Against Jeskai Blink: take their Counterspell. Against Storm: take Past in Flames. Against mirror: take their Goryo's.

engines.title: Wear // Tear ×2
engines.body: Wear {1}{R}: Destroy artifact. Tear {W}: Destroy enchantment. Fuse: both. Primary target: Leyline of the Void, Rest in Peace (both shut off your entire combo). Also: Chalice of the Void at 2 (blocks Goryo's), Ensnaring Bridge, Blood Moon. Fuse mode destroys BOTH an artifact and enchantment for {1}{R}{W}. Critical SB card.

engines.title: Celestial Purge ×1
engines.body: {1}{W} Instant: Exile target black or red permanent. Kills Orcish Bowmasters, Fury, any red/black threat — and EXILES them (no GY recursion). Against Dimir decks: exiles their Frog, Bowmasters, or planeswalkers. Clean answer that goes through indestructible.

engines.title: Flare of Denial ×1
engines.body: {1}{U}{U} or sacrifice a nontoken blue creature: Counter target spell. Sacrifice Psychic Frog or Quantum Riddler to counter for free. Against combo: protect your Goryo's by sacrificing a creature. The free cost is critical — you often tap out for Goryo's and need a counter with 0 mana available.

engines.title: Dress Down ×1
engines.body: {1}{U} Enchantment. Flash. ETB: draw a card. "Creatures lose all abilities." Sacrifice at end step. Flash in mid-combat: prowess triggers vanish, Murktide counters don't matter for power, Solitude can't exile. The draw on entry means it's never card disadvantage. Against Affinity: Frogmite dies (0/0 without affinity).

engines.title: Mystical Dispute ×1
engines.body: {2}{U} or {U} targeting a blue spell. Counter unless they pay {3}. Against Jeskai Blink, Dimir Control, mirror: a 1-mana hard counter for their Counterspell, Ephemerate, or Goryo's. The {U} cost when targeting blue makes it the most efficient counter in blue mirrors.

engines.title: Life as a Resource
engines.body: Most lists run 1 Griselbrand. It's the haymaker when you need to draw your entire deck, but costs 7 life per activation. Against aggro-heavy metas: cut to 0. Against combo/control metas: consider 2 (more targets for Goryo's). Griselbrand is your "go nuclear" option — one copy is usually enough because Atraxa is better in most situations.

engines.title: 67% of Lists Run It
engines.body: Emperor provides repeatable reanimation: exile a creature from GY → adapt → reanimate with haste (sacrifice at EOT). Not a Goryo's target (non-legendary). It's a 2-drop that gives you a second axis of reanimation. Run when you expect long games where multiple reanimation effects matter. Cut when you need more interaction or combo speed.

engines.title: 58% of Lists Run It
engines.body: Riddler at Warp {1}{U} = 1/1 that draws a card on ETB. Ephemerate on Riddler = 3 cards. Full cast {3}{U}{U} = 4/6 flying that draws a card + doubles future draws when hand is empty. Run when you want more fair game backup. Cut when the meta rewards pure combo speed.

engines.title: Annihilator vs Card Advantage
engines.body: Ulamog's cast trigger doesn't fire off Goryo's — so you lose the half-library exile. What you get: ward (sacrifice 2), counters from exile, annihilator. Run when: you face decks with indestructible/hexproof threats (annihilator forces sacrifice). Cut when: you need consistent ETB value (Atraxa is better).

engines.title: The Engine Anchor
engines.body: Run 4. Frog is your discard outlet, clock, and card advantage engine in one card. Cutting to 3 weakens both your combo consistency (fewer T1 discard outlets) and the Frog Beats plan. Only cut to 3 if your meta is zero aggro and you need a specific SB slot. In all standard configurations: 4 is correct.

engines.title: Hard Counter for Triggers
engines.body: Standard: 1 main + 2 SB. Consign counters triggered abilities (not just spells) — essential vs Archon of Cruelty ETB (Glockulous), Living End cascade, Emperor of Bones sacrifice trigger. Keep 1 main for G1 combo decks. Go to 3 SB if Glockulous or Living End is above 15% of your field.

engines.title: The Leyline Answer
engines.body: Standard: 2 SB. Wear destroys an artifact, Tear destroys an enchantment. Fused: destroy both for {1}{R}{W}. Primary targets: Leyline of the Void, Rest in Peace, Chalice of the Void, Blood Moon. Go to 3 SB if GY hate is above 20% of the expected field — the third copy is critical when they have multiple hate pieces in G3. Never drop below 2.

engines.title: Free Counter for Creatures
engines.body: Evoke Subtlety: exile a blue card from hand, counter target creature or planeswalker spell for free. Primary use: counter Persist in Living End, opposing combo creatures, Archon of Cruelty. The "free" is critical — using Subtlety on your combo turn costs you zero mana and doesn’t delay Goryo’s. Board in vs any combo or creature-based combo (Living End, Yawgmoth, Titan).

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Midrange-heavy field (Boros Energy, Domain Zoo, Eldrazi Tron) — your combo ignores their interaction. GY hate is below 15% of SB cards in the room. You’ve practiced the role-switching (Combo → Esper Control) until it’s automatic. Fast decks (Prowess, Affinity) are matchups you’ve repped — you know the race timing.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: GY hate is everywhere (15%+ of SBs). Surgical Extraction is common — one copy ends your game without T1 Thoughtseize backup. Heavy Chalice-at-2 meta (shuts off Goryo’s and Ephemerate simultaneously). You haven’t practiced the fair Esper Control plan — you’ll play scared and lose games you should win in the pivot role.

engines.title: Combo Execution
engines.body: T2 Goryo's into Atraxa into Ephemerate. Execute it blindfolded. This is the whole deck.

engines.title: Esper Control Mode
engines.body: Practice playing as pure Esper Control with Frog + Solitude + Ephemerate when GY is hated.

engines.title: Thoughtseize Window
engines.body: Drill seeing their hand on T1 and correctly evaluating whether combo is safe T2.

engines.title: GY Hate Reps
engines.body: Practice playing against Leyline of the Void from T0. Find Wear // Tear before you commit.

matchups.notes: Solitude + Ephemerate exiles their board for free
Your Ephemerate targets are better than theirs
T1 Thoughtseize + T2 Goryo's = faster AND disruptive
Race to T2 Goryo's before their T3 cascade
Solitude + Prismatic Ending answer their threats efficiently
They can't interact with instant-speed Goryo's
Solitude + Ephemerate dominates their small creatures

matchups.opponent: They're faster on raw damage but fragile. Solitude evoke + Ephemerate removes their board for free. Fatal Push kills every creature they run. Psychic Frog blocks profitably (1/2 survives Lightning Bolt). The danger: they can kill you before T3 with a nut draw. Race to Solitude + Ephemerate to stabilize, then combo. Out −1 Griselbrand −1 Ulamog −2 Thoughtseize In +1 Fatal Push +1 Celestial Purge +1 Dress Down Thoughtseize costs 2 life against a deck trying to kill you — too dangerous. Griselbrand costs 7 life per draw — uncastable at low life. More removal to handle their explosive starts. Dress Down turns off prowess mid-combat = their 5/6 Swiftspear becomes a 1/2. % Point Edges +3 pts: Dress Down mid-combat. They cast 3 spells to pump Swiftspear to 4/5 → you flash Dress Down → Swiftspear becomes 1/2 → their combat math is destroyed AND you draw a card. Dress Down sacrifices at end step so your creatures get their abilities back. Yawgmoth Combo Race Unfavorable Race to T2-3 Goryo's before they assemble Yawgmoth Yawgmoth is your hardest non-GY-hate matchup. They combo off T3-4 with Yawgmoth + Undying creatures (Young Wolf, Strangleroot Geist) to draw their entire deck and kill with Zulaport Cutthroat pings. Their clock is steady and they apply pressure while assembling. Your window: T2-3 Goryo's into Atraxa before they find Yawgmoth. Post-board: they bring Endurance (exiles your GY on ETB as a 3/4 reach for free). Subtlety answers Endurance on the stack. Thoughtseize is your best card here — take Yawgmoth himself, not the enablers. Out -2 Spell Pierce -1 Prismatic Ending -1 Solitude In +2 Subtlety +2 Thoughtseize +1 Fatal Push Spell Pierce is too conditional — they have mana by T3. Prismatic Ending can't kill Yawgmoth (MV 4). More hand disruption + Fatal Push for their early undying creatures. Subtlety bounces Endurance before GY exile resolves. % Point Edges +4 pts: T1 Thoughtseize taking Yawgmoth. Without Yawgmoth, their undying creatures are just 1-drops with upside. The entire combo requires the legendary creature. Taking it T1 buys you multiple turns to assemble Goryo's safely. +2 pts: Goryo's before their combo turn. Atraxa on T2-3 draws 6-8 cards and attacks for 7 lifelink. Even if they assemble Yawgmoth after, you've drawn 8 cards and gained 7 life — enough to find your own answer or just close with another attack. Amulet Titan Combo Race Even Thoughtseize their Amulet or Titan on T1 Two of the fastest combo decks in Modern. Amulet Titan can win T2 with the ideal Amulet + Simic Growth Chamber draw; you can win T2 with Psychic Frog into Goryo's. The matchup comes down to who has their hand disruption at the right moment. Thoughtseize T1 strips their Amulet of Vigor (kills their fast combo turn) or their Primeval Titan (removes the finisher). They have minimal interaction with your GY main deck — no counters, no GY hate. Post-board: they bring Endurance (exiles your GY on ETB for free). Answer with Subtlety on the stack. Out -2 Solitude -2 Fatal Push In +2 Subtlety +2 Thoughtseize Solitude exiles creatures — irrelevant until they have Titan. Fatal Push can't kill Primeval Titan (MV 6). More hand disruption and Subtlety to bounce Endurance or Titan on the stack. % Point Edges +3 pts: Thoughtseize taking Amulet of Vigor. Without Amulet, their lands ETB tapped. Their T2 kill becomes a T4-5 fair ramp plan. This converts the matchup from a pure race to a game where your T3 Goryo's is the clear faster line. Death's Shadow Control to Combo Favorable Your threats are larger and your disruption mirrors theirs Shadow mirrors your plan at half-scale. They run Thoughtseize, Fatal Push, and a fast clock — but their threats (4/4 Shadow, Ledger Shredder) are dwarfed by Atraxa's 7/7 flying deathtouch lifelink. Solitude exiles Death's Shadow cleanly — the "controller gains life equal to power" clause benefits you when exiling their 8/8. Fatal Push kills everything they run. Psychic Frog blocks their early pressure profitably and grows. Their Thoughtseize hurts, but you bring more disruption per game and your endgame is more powerful. Out -1 Ulamog -1 Griselbrand -2 Spell Pierce In +1 Celestial Purge +1 Fatal Push +2 Thoughtseize Ulamog and Griselbrand are too slow/life-intensive. Celestial Purge exiles Death's Shadow (black) and Kroxa (red). More Push and Thoughtseize to match their disruption. You want the fastest, most interactive version of your deck here. % Point Edges +3 pts: Solitude exiling Death's Shadow when it's 6+/6+. They lose a 6/6+ body AND you gain 6+ life — a 12+ point swing in one mana. This reverses any pressure they've applied and directly stabilizes the board. +2 pts: Psychic Frog growing faster than their Shadow. Discard excess lands to Frog. Each discard grows Frog by 1/1. A 4/5 Frog with flying outclasses a 4/4 Shadow in combat. They want to go under you — don't let the race happen. Mono-Green Tron Combo Favorable You combo T2-3 before they assemble Tron T3 Mono-Green Tron has no meaningful interaction with your combo in game 1. No counters, no GY hate — just Relic of Progenitus (exiles one card per activation, sacs to exile all GYs). Monitor Relic closely: if they're ticking it every turn, discard Atraxa and cast Goryo's in the same main phase window before Relic gets another activation. Their clock (Karn Liberated, Ulamog) is T3 at earliest. You reliably win T2-3 before they stabilize. Post-board: they bring Grafdigger's Cage (prevents Goryo's from resolving). Wear // Tear answers it immediately — make destroying Cage your first priority before setting up the combo. Out -4 Fatal Push -2 Solitude In +2 Wear // Tear +2 Thoughtseize Fatal Push and Solitude are dead — no creatures until T3+. Wear // Tear destroys Grafdigger's Cage and Relic of Progenitus. Thoughtseize takes Karn (which can exile a permanent immediately) or an assembled Tron piece. % Point Edges +4 pts: T1 Thoughtseize taking a Tron piece. Without all three Tron lands they're a midrange deck with overcosted spells. Taking any one delays their big spells by 2+ turns. Your T3 Goryo's is fast; their T5-6 catch-up is not. +2 pts: Dump Atraxa + Goryo's in one main phase window when Relic is active. Relic exiles from GY on its tap trigger. Discard Atraxa and immediately cast Goryo's before Relic can tap again — one-turn window collapses its effectiveness entirely. Domain Zoo Control Unfavorable Manage their clock with Solitude; Wear // Tear Leyline before combo turn Domain Zoo is your second-hardest matchup. They present a T2 clock (Territorial Kavu, Scion of Draco, Nacatl) backed by Leyline of the Void G0 in some lists — if Leyline resolves on T0, your combo is offline until Wear // Tear arrives. Their threats grow fast (Kavu with domain = 5/5+), and Stubborn Denial becomes a hard counter once they have a 4/4+ creature. Your gameplan: Solitude evoke + Ephemerate buys a turn against their creature-heavy draws. Race to combo before they close. Psychic Frog blocks Nacatl profitably early. Main issue: their T1-2 curve is faster than your combo assembles, and their SB disruption (Leyline, Endurance) attacks both your GY and your rebound plan. Out -1 Griselbrand -1 Ulamog -2 Spell Pierce -2 Thoughtseize In +2 Wear // Tear +2 Nihil Spellbomb +1 Celestial Purge +1 Fatal Push Griselbrand costs 7 life — impossible against a deck dealing 2-3 damage per turn per creature. Spell Pierce doesn't stop their threats. Wear // Tear is your Leyline answer. Nihil Spellbomb preemptively stops recursion angles. Celestial Purge exiles Scion of Draco (multicolored, red+white permanent). % Point Edges +4 pts: Solitude evoke + Ephemerate on their Territorial Kavu. Kavu grows to 5/5+ with full domain. Exiling it for free (Solitude evoke) + Ephemerate rebound means you exile 2 creatures and gain 10+ life. This swing often decides the game on the spot. +3 pts: Wear // Tear on Leyline before your combo turn. If you see Leyline G0, find Wear // Tear on T1-2 before you discard Atraxa. A Leyline that persists until T3 means your entire combo window evaporates. Priority 1 post-board: destroy Leyline before setting up.
