5-ColorHumans.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Identity "Aether Vial at 2. Meddling Mage naming their win condition. Thalia's Lieutenant pumping the whole board. Coppercoat Vanguard giving everything ward. You're deploying threats AND hate pieces simultaneously — no other aggro deck in Modern does this." 5-Color Humans is Modern's original tribal aggro-disruption deck. It applies serious pressure through Champion of the Parish and Thalia's Lieutenant snowball counters while simultaneously deploying hate pieces that break the opponent's game plan. Meddling Mage names their win condition. Thalia, Guardian of Thraben taxes all
5-ColorHumans.mulligan:
Mulligan Guide

The most important card to see in your opener is Aether Vial or Noble Hierarch.

engines.title: Snowball Aggro
engines.body: T1 Noble Hierarch or Champion of the Parish or Aether Vial . T2 Thalia's Lieutenant pumping everything. T3 Mantis Rider or Adeline closing with haste/vigilance. Every Human entering grows your board. By T4 you're swinging with 12+ power across 4 creatures.

engines.title: Disruption While Attacking
engines.body: Meddling Mage names their key spell. Thalia taxes their interaction. Coppercoat Vanguard gives every Human ward {1}, meaning every removal spell costs 1 more. The opponent has to fight through a tax AND answer your clock simultaneously — and you're doing both with the same cards.

engines.title: Critical Mass of Bodies
engines.body: You win through combat damage. Champion with 5+ counters, Adeline creating tokens every attack, Guide of Souls converting energy into +1/+1 and flying on your biggest threat. Mockingbird copies their best creature. There's no combo finish — you out-board them and punch through.

engines.title: You Want Proactive Disruption
engines.body: You like applying pressure while deploying hate. You enjoy naming the right card with Meddling Mage and watching them squirm. You want Aether Vial instant-speed tricks on their turn. You like growing a board that gets harder to answer every turn. High skill ceiling with real racing power.

engines.title: You Want Tier 1 Consistency
engines.body: The manabase is fragile — 19 lands across 5 colors with no fetches. Blood Moon can end you on the spot without Witch Enchanter . You're slower than Boros Energy and less resilient than Jeskai Blink. If you want the highest win rate in an open field, this isn't it. But if you know the deck cold, it punches well above its weight class.

engines.title: T1 Vial, T2 Double Deploy
engines.body: T1: Aether Vial . T2: Tick Vial to 1, cast Thalia's Lieutenant from hand (0 Humans to pump, but she enters). Vial in Champion of the Parish at their end step — Champion gets a counter from Lieutenant entering, Lieutenant gets a counter from Champion entering. T3: Tick to 2. Cast Meddling Mage naming their removal, Vial in Coppercoat Vanguard . Now: Champion is 3/3, Lieutenant is 4/4, Mage has ward

engines.title: T1 Hierarch, T2 Three-Drop
engines.body: T1: Noble Hierarch . T2: Tap Hierarch for mana, cast Mantis Rider (flying, vigilance, haste) — attack for 4 immediately (3 power + 1 exalted). Or T2: Adeline, Resplendent Cathar — she has vigilance, her power = number of creatures you control (2), and she creates a 1/1 Human token tapped and attacking when you swing. T3: deploy 2-drop + attack = Adeline is now a 4/4 making tokens. Snowball.

engines.title: T1 Champion, T2 Mage + Thalia
engines.body: T1: Champion of the Parish (1/1). T2: Meddling Mage naming their best spell (Champion → 2/2). If you have a second land or Hierarch: also cast Thalia, Guardian of Thraben (Champion → 3/3). Now their noncreature spells cost {1} more AND one specific spell can't be cast at all. They're attacking through both a tax and a lock while a growing Champion threatens lethal by T4.

engines.title: T1 Guide, T2 Coppercoat
engines.body: T1: Guide of Souls (1/2). T2: Coppercoat Vanguard — Guide triggers, gain 1 life + {E}. Now every Human entering generates energy + life. T3: Deploy 2 more Humans — Guide now has {E}{E}{E}. Attack, pay 3 energy: put two +1/+1 counters and flying on your best attacker. A 5/5 flying Champion closes games through any ground stall.

engines.title: Vial + 2 Humans + Land
engines.body: Any hand with T1 Vial and at least 2 creatures to deploy is a keep regardless of what else is in the hand. Vial makes your creatures uncounterable and generates instant-speed tricks. The rest of the deck is all 1-2 drops — you'll draw into a curve.

engines.title: Hierarch + 3-Drop + Land
engines.body: T1 Hierarch → T2 Mantis Rider (swing 4) or Adeline is a strong opening. Also keep Hierarch + Lieutenant + Coppercoat — the T2 double-deploy off Hierarch mana is excellent. Any Hierarch hand with a follow-up is keepable.

engines.title: No Accelerant, No T1 Play
engines.body: A hand with 3 lands, 2 Meddling Mages, Adeline, and Witch Enchanter is a mulligan — you can't deploy until T2 and your best cards arrive T3+. Against Boros Energy or Storm, that's too slow. Mulligan to 6 and look for Vial or Hierarch.

engines.title: T1 Thalia or Meddling Mage
engines.body: On the play your T1 matters more than any other decision. Thalia, Guardian of Thraben on T1 taxes every non-creature spell opponents cast for the rest of the game — every Counterspell, Lightning Bolt, and Violent Outburst costs 1 extra. Meddling Mage T1 (via Aether Vial) names their combo piece and locks them out immediately. On the play: always Vial on T1 if it's in hand.

engines.title: Extra Card Finds the Lock Piece
engines.body: On the draw you see 8 cards, dramatically improving odds of finding Thalia + Meddling Mage together. Keep slightly looser hands on the draw if they contain Aether Vial — Vial on T1 lets you deploy multiple creatures per turn without spending mana. Against aggro on the draw, Mantis Rider hands are keepable even without disruption because you need the flying clock more than the tax pieces.

engines.title: Re-tax With Reflector Mage
engines.body: Thalia killed: the tax is gone but Reflector Mage bounces their key creature AND prevents it being recast until their next turn. This gives you one free attack step against the now-tapped opponent. Rebuild Thalia via Chord of Calling or Aether Vial. Humans is resilient because every creature is a threat — you don’t lose when individual pieces die; you lose when the board clears completely.

engines.title: Vial Rebuild
engines.body: Sweeper resolves: count the Aether Vial counters. At 2 counters: Meddling Mage + Thalia re-enter simultaneously next turn. At 3 counters: Mantis Rider closes immediately. The Vial rebuild is faster than topdecking: you can deploy 2 creatures the turn after a sweep. Prioritize rebuilding lock pieces (Thalia, Meddling Mage) over clock pieces (Mantis Rider) after a sweep.

engines.title: Your Explosive Turns
engines.body: Your engine: Champion of the Parish gets +1/+1 for each Human that enters. Thalia's Lieutenant gets +1/+1 for each Human entering AND gives +1/+1 to all Humans when Lieutenant enters. You sequence: T1 Champion → T2 Thalia (Champion 2/2) → T3 Lieutenant (Champion 3/3, all Humans get +1/+1). By T3 you have a 3/3 Champion and 3/3 Lieutenant without casting any pump spells.

engines.title: Your Information Advantage
engines.body: Thalia, Guardian of Thraben taxes all their noncreature spells by {1}. You deploy Thalia on T2 before they've used any mana. Against Living End: their cascade spell costs {1} more — they have to pay {4} for Violent Outburst. Against Izzet Affinity: their cantrips cost {1} more each. Against Storm: their entire combo sequence costs {1} more per spell. Your T2 Thalia often wins the game by slowing t

engines.title: Your Tempo Piece
engines.body: Reflector Mage (3/2 flash) bounces a creature and prevents them from recasting it this turn. You deploy it at instant speed on their T3 when they tap for their most important creature. Mage ETB bounces: Ragavan (removes their mana acceleration), Solitude (removes their removal piece), any combo creature before it activates. You follow Mage with an attack — they're tapped and at a creature disadvan

engines.title: Your Curve Advantage
engines.body: Aether Vial lets you deploy creatures at instant speed by putting them into play without casting them. You activate Vial on their turn to put a creature into play without using your mana — mana you're holding for interaction. Vial at 2 counters lets you instant-speed a 2-drop onto the battlefield, triggering Champion counters, Lieutenant triggers, and ETB effects all at flash speed.

engines.title: Aether Vial + Lock Pieces
engines.body: Aether Vial at 2 counters lets you flash in Meddling Mage or Thalia at instant speed for free. This is your highest-value engine because it produces both disruption and board presence while leaving mana open for other plays. Every turn Vial is in play at the right counter number, you threaten a free creature. Protect Vial over individual creatures.

engines.title: Thalia + Meddling Mage Tax Lock
engines.body: Thalia taxes all non-creature spells by {1}. Meddling Mage names a key spell and prevents it being cast. Together they create a tax + ban wall that forces opponents to either remove the creatures (while you refill from Vial) or try to play through the lock. Against combo, name their win condition. Against control, name Counterspell. Deploy both simultaneously when possible.

engines.title: Champion of the Parish Growth
engines.body: Champion of the Parish gets a +1/+1 counter whenever a Human enters under your control. With a full curve of Humans entering each turn, Champion becomes a 4/4+ by T3 and an 8/8+ by T4. This engine runs in the background while you’re deploying lock pieces — don’t focus on it, but account for it when calculating lethal. A 6/6 Champion + Mantis Rider connecting for 3 is 9 damage in one swing.

engines.title: T3–4 With Champion
engines.body: T1: Champion of the Parish + Aether Vial. T2: Vial in Thalia (Champion +1/+1). Play a second Human. T3: Vial in Mantis Rider. Champion is now 3/3+. Mantis Rider swings for 3 + Champion + others. T4: At 20 life opponent, swing with everything: Mantis 3 + Champion 4+ + others = 10+. Lock clock: Thalia + Meddling Mage means their removal costs extra. They rarely stabilize T3.

engines.title: T4–5 Grind
engines.body: T1: Aether Vial. T2: Meddling Mage (names their key card) + creature. T3: Mantis Rider or Adeline. T4: Full attack with Vial deploying backup. This is the default clock vs interactive decks. The lock pieces slow their answers enough that you connect cleanly by T4–5.

engines.title: Hold Vial, Read Mana
engines.body: Attack T3: They’re on combo (Storm, Living End) — must apply clock before they go off. Hold T3: They have 4+ mana open and haven’t used it — Solitude or Supreme Verdict read. Vial in Reflector Mage instead, bounce their blocker, swing next turn when they tap for the sweeper.

engines.title: Meddling Mage Names on ETB
engines.body: Meddling Mage’s name-a-card ability triggers on ETB. Name the card before any other ETB triggers resolve. You cannot change the named card later. If you Vial in Meddling Mage in response to their spell being cast, the naming happens before their spell resolves — it’s too late to name that spell (it’s already been cast, not yet resolved). Name the NEXT spell they’re going to cast, not the current o

engines.title: Thalia Taxes Aether Vial Activations: NO
engines.body: Thalia, Guardian of Thraben taxes noncreature SPELLS — spells you cast. Aether Vial is an activated ability, not a casting. Vial’s activated ability is not taxed by Thalia. Your opponent’s Vial activations are also not taxed. The tax applies to Lightning Bolt, Violent Outburst, Counterspell, Thoughtseize — anything cast from hand. Activated abilities (Vial, planeswalker +/-) are always free of Tha

engines.title: Reflector Mage’s Return Is Optional
engines.body: Reflector Mage says “return target creature an opponent controls to its owner’s hand” — this is mandatory when it ETBs, not optional. However, the “can’t cast a spell with that name” clause applies until your NEXT turn. If Reflector Mage dies before your next turn, the casting restriction ends. Chain Reflector Mages (Vial deploys one each turn) to perpetually bounce their key creature while they c

engines.title: Your T1-T3 Explosive Sequence
engines.body: Your explosive start: T1 Champion of the Parish (1/1 → 2/2 on T2 Human). T2 Thalia, Guardian of Thraben (Champion → 3/3; Thalia taxes all their noncreature spells). T3 Thalia's Lieutenant (all Humans +1/+1; Champion → 5/5; Lieutenant enters as 2/2). You attack on T3 with a 5/5 Champion and 2/2 Lieutenant against a taxed opponent. This is your ideal opening.

engines.title: Your Aether Vial Line
engines.body: Aether Vial (artifact that adds a counter each turn): T1 Vial (0 counters). T2 Vial (1 counter — can flash in 1-drop). T3 Vial (2 counters — can flash in 2-drop). You use Vial to deploy creatures at instant speed during their turn: Reflector Mage (bounce their key creature) or Thalia's Lieutenant (pump your entire team) without spending your combat mana. Every Vial activation is a free creature de

engines.title: Your Reflector Mage Timing
engines.body: You deploy Reflector Mage ({2}{W}{U} flash 3/2) at their EOT to bounce their most important creature and prevent them from recasting it this turn. Against combo: bounce their key creature. Against control: bounce Teferi. Against aggro: bounce their best attacker before their next turn. You follow with your attack on your turn — they're tapped and a creature short.

engines.title: Your Meddling Mage Lock
engines.body: Meddling Mage (2/2, name a card, they can't cast it): you name their win condition. Against Yawgmoth combo: name Yawgmoth, Thran Physician — they cannot cast their combo piece. Against Living End: name Living End — their entire deck is offline. You deploy Meddling Mage when you already have Aether Vial, reducing the cost of deploying it at flash speed when they try to resolve the named card.

engines.title: Name: Galvanic Discharge
engines.body: Their most efficient removal spell. Stopping Discharge means your board survives longer. Secondary name: Ajani, Nacatl Pariah (stops their best 1-drop from flipping). If you've seen their hand via information: name whatever kills you fastest.

engines.title: Name: Past in Flames
engines.body: Without Past in Flames, their combo is far less reliable. They can still win through Rite of Flame chains, but Past in Flames is the card that lets them rebuild from a disrupted hand. Secondary: Grapeshot (stops the kill itself). Thalia taxing is your primary disruption — Mage is insurance.

engines.title: Name: Ephemerate
engines.body: Ephemerate is their engine — rebuy Solitude, Stoneforge, value creatures. Without it their deck is fair Magic. Secondary: Solitude (stops their free removal). If you have Thalia in play, naming Ephemerate + Thalia tax = they can't blink efficiently at all.

engines.title: Name: Living End
engines.body: They literally cannot win without resolving Living End (or the very rare Grief beatdown). Name it G1 and they need to find Force of Negation or bounce your Mage. With Lavinia from SB: cascade into a free spell = Lavinia counters it. Double lock.

engines.title: Name: Thought Monitor
engines.body: Their draw engine. Without Monitor their deck runs out of gas. Secondary: Sojourner's Companion (stops their biggest free body). Kataki from SB is your primary answer — Mage is supplementary disruption.

engines.title: Name: All Is Dust
engines.body: The sweeper that ignores your entire board. All Is Dust destroys all colored permanents — your Humans, your Vials, everything. Naming it forces them to beat you through creature combat where your disruption and lords shine. Secondary: Karn, the Great Creator.

engines.title: Vial + 2 Champions + 2 Lieutenants
engines.body: T1: Aether Vial. T2: Tick to 1. Cast Champion #1 ({W}) = 1/1. EOT Vial in Champion #2. Champion #1 grows to 2/2. T3: Tick to 2. Cast Lieutenant #1 ({1}{W}). Lt ETB: +1/+1 on each other Human. Champion #1: 3/3 → +1/+1 from Human entering = 4/4. Champion #2: 2/2 → +1/+1 = 3/3. Lt sees 2 Humans = 3/3. Vial in Lieutenant #2. Champion #1: 5/5 → Lt ETB +1/+1 = 6/6 . Champion #2: 4/4 → Lt ETB = 5/5 . Lt

engines.title: Any Vial/Hierarch + Curve
engines.body: T1: Hierarch or Vial. T2: Champion + Lieutenant (3 mana off Hierarch) or Champion + Vial in 1-drop. Champion is 3/3+ after Lieutenant ETB. T3: Deploy 2 more Humans. Board is 4-5 creatures, Champion at 5/5+, Lieutenants at 4/4+. Attack for 11-15 damage. Guide energy at 2-3. T4: Deploy last creatures. Pay 3 energy: +2/+2 flying on Champion. Attack everything. 20+ damage. Lethal. The deck consistentl

engines.title: Combo Opponent
engines.body: Facing Storm, Living End, Neoform, Amulet Titan: abandon the incremental lock plan. Apply the fastest clock possible. T1 Vial, T2 double creature, T3 Mantis Rider for lethal. Use Meddling Mage to name their win condition AND attack. You can’t out-grind them — race them.

engines.title: Removal-Heavy Opponent
engines.body: Facing UW Control or Jeskai Blink: slow deploy mode. Play 2 creatures and hold 2 back. Name Counterspell with Meddling Mage to make their interaction more expensive. Use Vial to flash in creatures at instant speed to avoid sorcery-speed sweepers. Force them to 2-for-1 themselves by answering individual creatures while you rebuild.

engines.title: Always Attack
engines.body: Humans has no draw engine — once the board stalls, you lose the topdeck war. Always attack with something every turn to force blocks and chip damage. A 1/1 that connects each turn deals 10 damage over 10 turns. Passive boards lose. Aggressive boards force mistakes.

engines.title: What Are They On?
engines.body: Combo = name their win con, attack aggressively. Control = deploy in waves, use Vial at flash speed. Midrange = symmetric aggression, protect Champion of the Parish. Identify from their opening land — an untapped Steam Vents is Izzet, a Cavern of Souls is Humans mirror.

engines.title: Kataki, War's Wage ×2
engines.body: {1}{W} 2/1 Human Spirit. All artifacts have "At the beginning of your upkeep, pay {1} or sacrifice this artifact." Devastating vs Affinity — forces them to sacrifice most of their board or go mana-negative. Also hits Amulet of Vigor, Expedition Map, Sigil of Valor. Vialed in at 2. The Spirit type still triggers Champion/Lieutenant because Kataki is also a Human Spirit.

engines.title: Sanctifier en-Vec ×2
engines.body: {1}{W}{W} 2/2 Human Cleric. Protection from black and red. ETB: exile all cards from all graveyards with black or red color identity. Cannot be targeted, damaged, or blocked by anything black or red. Against Boros Energy, Prowess, Dimir, Living End — it's a threat they literally cannot interact with. The GY exile is bonus hate vs recursion. Triple white is castable off Cavern/Courtyard naming Huma

engines.title: Plague Engineer ×2
engines.body: {2}{B} 2/2 Phyrexian Carrier. Deathtouch. As it enters, choose a creature type — creatures of that type opponents control get -1/-1. NOT a Human (Carrier type) — doesn't trigger Champion/Lieutenant. But the effect is devastating: name Goblin vs Goblins, Elemental vs Elementals, Construct vs Affinity tokens. Against token strategies the -1/-1 blanket wipes their 1/1s immediately.

engines.title: Dismember ×2
engines.body: {1}{B/P}{B/P} — pay 4 life to cast for {1}. Target creature gets -5/-5 until EOT. Kills anything with 5 or less toughness at instant speed for 1 mana + 4 life. The life payment is real — against aggro it's dangerous. But against combo and midrange where you need to remove a key blocker or threat, Dismember is the most efficient removal in the format. Castable off any mana source.

engines.title: Reflector Mage ×2
engines.body: {1}{W}{U} 2/3 Human Wizard. ETB: return target creature to owner's hand — its owner can't cast it again until your next turn. The "can't recast" clause is the key — it's not a bounce, it's a full-turn lockout. Against expensive threats (Solitude, Reality Smasher, Primeval Titan): bounce + deny recast = 2 turns of tempo advantage. Vial at 3 for instant-speed deployment. Human — triggers everything.

engines.title: Lavinia, Azorius Renegade ×1
engines.body: {W}{U} 2/2 Human Soldier. Opponents can't cast noncreature spells with MV > lands they control. Whenever an opponent casts a spell with no mana spent, counter it. Blanket-counters: Force of Negation (free), Evoke Solitude/Grief (free), Living End via cascade (free), Manamorphose (net free). Also limits big spells before they have enough lands. Devastating against specific matchups.

engines.title: Gaddock Teeg ×1
engines.body: {G}{W} 2/2 Kithkin Advisor. Noncreature spells with MV 4+ can't be cast. Noncreature spells with {X} in mana cost can't be cast. Stops: All Is Dust, Wrath of God, Supreme Verdict, Past in Flames, Grapeshot (X-spell), Karn, any big planeswalker. Not a Human (Kithkin) — doesn't trigger Champion/Lieutenant. But the static effect is so powerful against the right decks that it's worth the non-synergy s

engines.title: Drannith Magistrate ×1
engines.body: {1}{W} 1/3 Human Wizard. Your opponents can't cast spells from anywhere other than their hands. Shuts down: cascade (Living End, Rhinos), flashback (Past in Flames), escape, foretell, adventure (from exile), Wish effects. Human Wizard — triggers Champion/Lieutenant and gets Coppercoat ward. The 1/3 body survives most damage-based removal.

engines.title: Clarion Conqueror ×1
engines.body: {2}{W} 3/3 Dragon. Flying. Activated abilities of artifacts, creatures, and planeswalkers can't be activated. NOT a Human — doesn't trigger Champion/Lieutenant. But shuts down: Aether Vial (in mirrors), Walking Ballista, Agatha's Soul Cauldron, Karn's Wish, equipment activations. The 3/3 flying body is a real clock. Castable off generic mana or Vial at 3. A narrow but devastating silver bullet.

engines.title: Vexing Bauble ×1
engines.body: {1} Artifact. Whenever a player casts a spell with no mana spent, counter it. {1}, {T}, Sacrifice: draw a card. Redundancy with Lavinia on a different card type — Lavinia is a creature (removable), Bauble is an artifact (harder to interact with for many decks). The sacrifice-to-draw mode means it's never dead: against non-free-spell decks, cycle it for a card. Perfect for Living End, Neoform, Stor

engines.title: When the Meta Is Spell-Heavy
engines.body: Run this when: Storm, Living End, Jeskai Blink, and Dimir Control are prevalent. Noble Hierarch accelerates you past their setup turns. Thalia taxes their noncreature-heavy decks. Coppercoat's ward blanket makes their 1-for-1 removal inefficient. Mantis Rider punishes slow starts. The classic shell excels when the opponent's game plan revolves around noncreature spells you can tax and name with Ma

engines.title: When the Meta Is Creature-Heavy
engines.body: Run this when: Boros Energy, Prowess, and creature midrange dominate. Aang, Swift Savior ({1}{U/W} 2/3 flash flying, ETB airbend bounce a creature/spell) provides instant-speed interaction + evasion that Mantis Rider can't match. Sylvan Safekeeper ({G} 1/1, sacrifice a land: target creature gains shroud) protects your key threats at the cost of lands. Mai, Scornful Striker adds aggressive 2-drop p

engines.title: 2 Witch Enchanter Is Non-Negotiable
engines.body: Without Witch Enchanter, a resolved Blood Moon turns your entire manabase into Mountains that can't cast Humans (Ziggurat, Courtyard, Territory, Cavern all lose their abilities under Moon). 2 copies of Enchanter means you see one roughly 25% of games. The back face being a Plains-type land means you can play it as mana T1 and still have the Enchanter option later — never cut below 2.

engines.title: 2 Plains + 1 Island Minimum
engines.body: Your basics survive Blood Moon. 2 Plains covers your white-heavy creature base (Champion, Lieutenant, Vanguard, Guide, Thalia all have {W}). The single Island enables Meddling Mage ({W}{U}), Mariner ({W}{U}), Mockingbird ({X}{U}). Seachrome Coast adds a 4th "real" dual land. Don't go below 3 fetchable basics — Blood Moon and Path to Exile both punish greedy manabases.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Combo-heavy field (Storm, Living End, Neoform) — Meddling Mage locks them out cold. Midrange-heavy field where your clock is faster than their interaction. Low Supreme Verdict density — Humans folds to sweepers more than targeted removal. You’ve practiced Meddling Mage naming for all expected matchups before the event.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy Supreme Verdict field — sweepers that can’t be Thalia-taxed (Verdict is uncounterable) clear the whole board. Pyroclasm or Anger of the Gods meta — all your creatures die to 2-3 damage. You don’t know the Meddling Mage naming guide for the top 5 expected matchups cold — a wrong name is a 2-mana 2/2 with no text.

engines.title: Vial Timing
engines.body: Every decision about when to tick Vial and when to use it at end step. Drill it.

engines.title: Meddling Mage Names
engines.body: Name 20 matchups, state the correct Mage name immediately. Then state the backup. No pausing.

engines.title: Jirina Sacrifice
engines.body: Drill holding Jirina's sacrifice for the exact right moment. Preemptive sacrifice is the mistake.

engines.title: Tax Stack Math
engines.body: Practice Thalia + Coppercoat + Mariner tax calculations. Know the exact mana cost of opponent's spells.

matchups.notes: Coppercoat Vanguard — ward {1} taxes their cheap removal
Meddling Mage naming All Is Dust
Plague Engineer naming Human (they run Monastery Swiftspear)
Neoform tutors through most interaction — they can combo off turn 3 through a single piece of disruption. Thalia, Guardi...

matchups.opponent: Neoform tutors through most interaction — they can combo off turn 3 through a single piece of disruption. Thalia, Guardian of Thraben on T1 is your best card: it taxes every spell in their combo by {1}. A taxed Neoform costs {3} instead of {2}, which delays their combo turn by a full turn. Thalia also applies immediate clock — a 2/1 first striker attacks past their mana dorks. Out In −2 Reflector Mage + 2 Damping Sphere −2 Kitesail Freebooter +2 Sanctifier en-Vec Damping Sphere shuts off all mana doubling effects — Neoform needs Elvish Spirit Guide, Simian Spirit Guide, and fast mana to goldfish on T2-3. Sphere removes that entire dimension. Sanctifier en-Vec (protection from green/black) is immune to their combo creatures.

matchups.notes: Yawgmoth combo requires two undying creatures + the doctor in play simultaneously. Thalia taxes their tutor package (Eld...

matchups.opponent: Yawgmoth combo requires two undying creatures + the doctor in play simultaneously. Thalia taxes their tutor package (Eldritch Evolution {3} instead of {2}, Chord of Calling costs more). Meddling Mage naming Yawgmoth, Thran Physician turns off the infinite loop entirely — they cannot cast their key card. Keep Mage alive at all costs and name Yawgmoth the moment you resolve it. Out In −2 Reflector Mage +2 Meddling Mage (name Yawgmoth) −2 Mayor of Avabruck +2 Dismember Meddling Mage naming Yawgmoth prevents the loop — they cannot combo without him. Dismember kills undying creatures at instant speed mid-loop. Mayor of Avabruck is too slow for this matchup. The key is stopping the loop before it starts — interact on their combo turn, not after resolution.

IzzetAffinity.game_plan: Chapter 01 Izzet Affinity Pinnacle Emissary changed what Affinity is allowed to do. One card on turn 1 or 2 floods the board with Drone tokens that enable Metalcraft, pay for Improvise, fuel Kappa Cannoneer triggers, and convert into 2-damage Munitions explosions. You are not playing a linear creature deck. You are building a critical mass of artifacts that converts into an unstoppable threat on the same turn it assembles. Izzet Affinity is the highest meta-share deck in Modern at 7.1% and posted a 54.7% win rate across the fall 2025 Regional Championships. The deck won the MIT Championship, t
IzzetAffinity.mulligan:
Mulligan Frameworks

Izzet Affinity mulligans more aggressively than almost any deck in Modern.

engines.title: The Field Is Open
engines.body: Izzet Affinity rewards tight play and punishes unprepared opponents. In open fields where people aren't specifically packing Meltdown, Shatterstorm, or Collector Ouphe, this deck wins through raw speed. It's the best choice when the expected field is creature decks, midrange, and combo — anything that can't answer a Ward-4 threat or a 10-damage EE burst in time.

engines.title: Artifact Hate is Expected
engines.body: Izzet Affinity is glass when hit by mass artifact removal. Stony Silence locks Mox Opal and Springleaf Drum. Collector Ouphe disables all activated artifact abilities. Meltdown at X=2 destroys the entire board for 2 mana. If the expected field includes dedicated artifact hate, the deck's ceiling drops substantially. Jeskai Blink specifically is a hard matchup — Solitude evokes your Emissary for fr

engines.title: Weapons Manufacturing Shell
engines.body: Weapons Manufacturing + Engineered Explosives is the combo finish. Every nontoken artifact creates a Munitions bomb. EE at 0 clears all MV-0 permanents including Munitions, dealing 2 damage per token. Fastest kill, most explosive. Japanese innovation from Pro Tour EOE. This guide is built around this version.

engines.title: Thoughtcast / Thought Monitor Shell
engines.body: Thoughtcast and Thought Monitor provide pure card draw. Slower but more resilient. Less explosive ceiling but grinds better through disruption. Still runs Pinnacle Emissary and Kappa Cannoneer as core win conditions. Less combo-reliant — wins purely on artifact pressure.

engines.title: Ravenous Robots Shell
engines.body: Ravenous Robots ({1}{R}, 2/1) creates a 1/1 Robot token whenever you cast an artifact spell. Doubles token production with Pinnacle Emissary — each artifact spell creates both a Drone (from Emissary) and a Robot (from Robots). Higher token count, faster Improvise payoffs. Some Mar 2026 lists run 4 Robots over other slots.

engines.title: {1}{U}{R} · 3/3 Artifact Creature
engines.body: Whenever you cast an artifact spell, create a 1/1 colorless Drone with flying that can only block creatures with flying. Warp {U/R} (cast for 2 mana, exiled at next end step, can be recast from exile). The Drone trigger fires on CAST — before the spell resolves. This means if the spell gets countered, you still get the Drone.

engines.title: {5}{U} · 4/4 Artifact Creature
engines.body: Improvise — each tapped artifact pays {1}. Ward {4}. Whenever this or another artifact you control enters, put a +1/+1 counter on it and it can't be blocked this turn. The Ward means targeted removal costs 4 extra — opponents spend 5-6 mana to kill it. The enters trigger fires on ALL artifacts: creatures, tokens, equipment, enchantments, Urza's Saga Constructs, Drones. Every artifact that enters g

engines.title: {1}{R} · Enchantment
engines.body: Whenever a NONtoken artifact you control enters, create a colorless Munitions artifact token with "When this token leaves the battlefield, it deals 2 damage to any target." The trigger is nontoken only — Drone tokens and Robot tokens do not trigger it. Your Memnites, Baubles, Mox Opals, Engineered Explosives all trigger it. Each triggers creates one Munitions bomb.

engines.title: {X} · Artifact · Sunburst
engines.body: Enters with charge counters equal to the number of COLORS of mana spent to cast it. {2}, Sacrifice: Destroy each nonland permanent with mana value equal to the number of charge counters. At X=0 with colorless mana: 0 charge counters, destroys all MV-0 permanents. Munitions tokens have MV 0 (no mana cost) — they're destroyed, each dealing 2 damage. Your own Memnites and Ornithopters (MV 0) also die

engines.title: {1}{U}{U} // Land · MDFC
engines.body: Front: Instant — return target spell or nonland permanent an opponent controls to its owner's hand. Back (Soporific Springs): land that ETBs tapped unless you pay 3 life. This is both bounce spell AND land. The flexibility is immense — it's interaction that doesn't cost you a land drop. The 3 life payment is real; track your life total carefully when taking Soporific Springs tapped vs paying 3.

engines.title: Enchantment Land · 3 chapters
engines.body: Ch I: gains "{T}: Add {C}." Ch II: gains "{2}{T}: Create 0/0 Construct that gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control." Ch III: Search library for artifact with MV 0 or 1, put it onto the battlefield, shuffle. The Construct scales with your artifact count — with 12 artifacts, it's a 12/12 the turn it enters. Ch III tutors MV 0-1 artifacts: Mox Opal, Mishra's Bauble, Claws of Gix, Tormod's Crypt, Sp

engines.title: Flood the Board
engines.body: Ideal T1: Island → Mox Opal (Metalcraft not active) → Memnite (free) → Pinnacle Emissary (U/R from Mox). Emissary enters. Now every artifact you cast creates a Drone. Cast another free artifact (Mishra's Bauble, Claws of Gix, Tormod's Crypt) → Drone enters. 3 artifacts on board → Mox Opal is now active for Metalcraft. Kappa Cannoneer can come down T1 if you have enough Improvise fodder.

engines.title: Kappa or Saga
engines.body: With the T1 Emissary board, Kappa Cannoneer drops on T2 tapping Drones for Improvise. It enters as a 5/5+ (counter from entering + the Drones entering). Immediately unblockable this turn. Alternatively: Urza's Saga on T2 means Chapter II Construct production by T3-4, and Chapter III tutors a 0-1 MV artifact. The Saga line is slower but more resilient — Kappa can be countered, Constructs just sit t

engines.title: Weapons Manufacturing Burst
engines.body: Once Weapons Manufacturing is active: every nontoken artifact entering creates a Munitions bomb. By T3-4 with a healthy board, you have 4-8 Munitions tokens. Engineered Explosives at X=0 (cost: {0}, cast with colorless mana from Mox, Fiery Islet, or Claws sacrifice) destroys all MV-0 permanents — including all Munitions tokens, each dealing 2 damage. 6 Munitions = 12 damage. Often lethal from nowh

engines.title: Emry Recursion Loop
engines.body: Emry, Lurker of the Loch mills 4 on entry and taps to cast an artifact card from your GY. With a deep GY and Emry recurring artifacts every turn, the board replenishes through removal. Emry + Weapons Manufacturing = every recurred artifact creates another Munitions. The late game is not about topdecking — it's about using the GY as a second hand.

engines.title: Snap Keep
engines.body: Any hand with Pinnacle Emissary + at least two 0-mana artifacts + a way to cast Emissary (Island/Steam Vents/Spirebluff + Mox Opal or Fiery Islet). This hand floods Drones on turn 2-3 and can drop Kappa Cannoneer by turn 2. The hand wins on its own if not disrupted — it does not need draws.

engines.title: Keep
engines.body: Urza's Saga + a second land + either Springleaf Drum + 0-cost artifact, OR Mox Opal + other artifacts. This generates Construct tokens starting turn 3, creates a growing threat that scales with artifact count, and tutors a key 0-1 MV artifact on chapter III. Slower but self-sufficient — the Constructs win games that get disrupted in the early turns.

engines.title: T1 Mox Opal into Ornithopter
engines.body: On the play, T1 Mox Opal (if metalcraft active) into Ornithopter + Thoughtcast for card draw is your best opening. Deploy as many zero-cost artifacts as possible T1 to build metalcraft. On the play: count your artifact count before tapping Opal. Urza’s Saga on T1 starts its chapter count immediately and generates Constructs by T3.

engines.title: Extra Card Finds Kappa
engines.body: On the draw you see 8 cards, improving odds of finding Kappa Cannoneer + enough artifacts to power it. Keep looser hands on the draw if they contain the artifact mana base. Against removal-heavy decks on the draw: plan around your first Kappa being answered — have a second threat or Urza’s Saga backup ready.

engines.title: Urza’s Saga Backup
engines.body: Kappa Cannoneer removed: Urza’s Saga is your second win condition. Chapter III tutors Shadowspear (trample + lifelink) or Welding Jar (protect an artifact). 3/3 Construct tokens + the tutored equipment close games. Saga generates a threat board even without Kappa.

engines.title: Affinity Beatdown
engines.body: Collector Ouphe or Stony Silence shuts off artifacts. Pivot: affinity creatures still get cost reduction. Thoughtcast still cantrips. Kappa still gets ward from shield counters (not activated). Your creatures are still large — attack with a 6/6 Kappa even without the activated ability generating extra shields.

engines.title: Mox Opal Metalcraft
engines.body: Mox Opal + metalcraft (3+ artifacts) generates free colored mana every turn. This is your primary mana engine — before casting anything, count your artifacts and check if Opal is active. Zero-cost artifacts (Ornithopter, Memnite) plus Opal activate metalcraft on T1 before any land-based mana is needed.

engines.title: Kappa Cannoneer + Shields
engines.body: Kappa gets a shield counter whenever you cast a noncreature spell. Each counter adds Ward 2. Deploy Kappa then chain cheap artifacts and cantrips to stack 2-3 shield counters immediately. A Kappa with 3 counters requires paying 6 or more to target it — effectively unkillable by targeted removal. Build shields before passing.

engines.title: Urza’s Saga Clock
engines.body: Urza’s Saga Chapter I + II generate Construct tokens each upkeep. Chapter III tutors any artifact with MV 0 or 1. Deploy Saga as a backup when Kappa is unavailable — it creates a self-contained clock plus a SB fetch that can answer hate pieces (Cage) or add equipment.

engines.title: Fastest Clock
engines.body: T1: Mox Opal + 2 zero-cost artifacts (metalcraft) + Thoughtcast (draw 2 for {U}). T2: Kappa Cannoneer (4 mana from lands + Opal). Cast a cantrip → Kappa gets shield counter (Ward 2). Kappa attacks as 4/4+ with Ward 2. Kappa closes in 3-4 attack steps from 20 life with growing ward protection.

engines.title: Backup Clock
engines.body: T1: Zero-cost artifacts + land. T2: Urza’s Saga (Chapter I starts). T3: Chapter II → 3/3 Construct. Chapter III next turn → tutor Shadowspear (trample+lifelink for all attackers) or Kappa from hand. Saga provides 2 Construct tokens + a tutor by T4.

engines.title: Kappa vs Saga First
engines.body: Lead Kappa: Vs creature-light decks that can’t block it. Kappa with 2 shield counters is immediately threatening. Lead Saga: Vs removal-heavy decks. Saga’s Constructs are harder to remove than Kappa and the tutor lets you answer their SB hate piece on Chapter III.

engines.title: Kappa Cannoneer Ward 2 Triggers Per Shield Counter
engines.body: Kappa Cannoneer gains Ward 2 for each shield counter on it. Each shield counter creates a separate Ward 2 trigger when Kappa is targeted. Targeting Kappa with 2 shield counters = 2 Ward triggers = pay 2 twice (total 4) or the targeting spell is countered. Ward triggers happen when the target is declared, not on resolution. Counter-spells that don’t target (Cryptic Command tap mode) bypass Ward ent

engines.title: Mox Opal Needs Metalcraft — Count Opal Itself
engines.body: Mox Opal requires metalcraft — 3 or more artifacts in play — to tap for mana. Opal counts itself as one of the 3. With Ornithopter + Thoughtcast + Opal = 3 artifacts = metalcraft active. If you lose one artifact (removal on Ornithopter), metalcraft breaks and Opal goes inert immediately (it’s a static ability check). Rebuild to 3 artifacts before attempting to tap Opal again.

engines.title: Urza’s Saga Chapter III — Know Your Targets
engines.body: Urza’s Saga Chapter III tutors for a creature or artifact with MV 0 or 1 from your deck. Key targets: Shadowspear (1, trample + lifelink for attackers), Welding Jar (0, free regeneration for an artifact), Pithing Needle (1, name a planeswalker ability), Grafdigger’s Cage (1, prevents GY + library-from-other-zones). In the mirror: Saga tutors Cage to lock their GY. Know your target before Saga reso

engines.title: Light on Removal
engines.body: Boros Energy game 1, combo decks, any deck without targeted removal. Kappa’s Ward 2 + shield counters is too expensive for them to answer profitably.

engines.title: Removal-Heavy Opponent
engines.body: Vs Jeskai Blink, UW Control, Dimir Frog: deploy Saga first. It creates multiple bodies and the Chapter III tutor can fetch Pithing Needle to name their key removal spell.

engines.title: Fast Mana Available
engines.body: Three+ artifacts in opening hand including Opal: activate metalcraft ASAP and pour mana into Kappa + cantrips. Speed is your advantage when Opal is active.

engines.title: Kappa Has 3+ Shields
engines.body: Kappa at 3 shield counters = Ward 6+ to target it. Attack every turn. They cannot answer it profitably. Don’t wait for more shields — just attack.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Low Collector Ouphe and Stony Silence density in expected SBs. Midrange-heavy field where your Kappa clock is faster than their answers. Combo decks present — your T2 Kappa races their T3. You’ve practiced the Saga backup plan for when Kappa is answered.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy Collector Ouphe meta — shuts off ALL artifact activated abilities (Opal, Kappa shields, Welding Jar regeneration). High Stony Silence builds. Multiple Whipflare/Pyroclasm decks (kills your artifact creature base). You haven’t practiced the Urza’s Saga-only game plan.

engines.title: Kappa Turn 2
engines.body: Practice the T1 Emissary → T2 Kappa Cannoneer line at tournament speed.

engines.title: Improvise Math
engines.body: Count available Improvise each turn. Know when Rebuke costs {U} vs {2}{U}.

engines.title: Blood Moon Lines
engines.body: Practice what you can cast after Blood Moon resolves. Basic Island gives you {U}.

engines.title: Mirror Sequencing
engines.body: Emissary first wins the mirror. Drill why and practice the priority of deployment.

Solitude bypasses Ward, Wrath clears board, Phelia bounces
Speed race — both kill turns 3-4, their burn ignores Ward
Thoughtseize strips key pieces, Dismember post-board answers
Race Tron assembly — Consign counters Saga and Titan triggers
First Kappa wins — Emissary speed and Ward order matters
Your speed vs their chain — Damping Sphere and FoN postboard
Karn locks artifacts, All is Dust clears board, Chalice at 1
Kappa unblockable, Construct army, Saga tokens + Shadowspear
Fast Kappa + Saga faster than their combo; Thoughtseize hurts
Supreme Verdict clears board; Weapons burst through their sweepers

IZZETCREATIVITY.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "You play control until you're ready. Then you discard Magma Opus, target the Treasure token with Indomitable Creativity, Gearhulk enters, flashes Opus back for free. Their board is gone, you have a 5/6 and four mana worth of effects. The game ends." Izzet Creativity is Pioneer's premier combo-control hybrid. Unlike pure aggro or pure control, it operates from a reactive position until it assembles the two-card combo — then transitions instantly into an overwhelming tempo advantage. The combo is elegant: discard Magma Opus to create a Treasure token (via Fable of the M
IZZETCREATIVITY.mulligan:
Mulligan
Need: Lands + Interaction + Fable/Prismari Path
Keep: 3 lands (including at least one red source for Creativity), 1-2 interaction pieces, and either Fable or Prismari Command.

engines.title: Combo That Doesn't Lose to Removal
engines.body: The Treasure token created by Fable or Prismari Command is not a creature — it can't be targeted by creature removal or killed in combat. Indomitable Creativity targeting a Treasure is effectively uncounterable by creature-based hate. Your combo piece is a non-creature artifact that removes itself when the combo fires. They need to counter Indomitable Creativity itself or have the Gearhulk exiled

engines.title: Fully Interactive Until You Go Off
engines.body: Unlike Lotus Field or Greasefang that are racing on a linear path, Creativity plays real control Magic until it fires. Fiery Impulse, Make Disappear, Divide by Zero, and Prismari Command all answer threats, buy time, and enable the combo simultaneously. You never feel like you're doing nothing — every spell serves double duty as interaction and setup.

engines.title: Magma Opus Is an 8-Mana Spell for {3RRR}
engines.body: Magma Opus at full cost is unplayable at {6UUR}. Cast for free via Gearhulk it's the most broken spell in Pioneer. Dealing 4 damage, tapping four opponent permanents, drawing 2 cards, and making a Treasure while deploying a 5/6 body in one action creates an insurmountable tempo advantage against virtually every deck. Opponents who survive need to deal with both the Gearhulk AND the aftermath.

engines.title: Control Mode
engines.body: Answer early threats: Fiery Impulse kills MV-1 creatures (spell mastery gives 3 damage by T2). Divide by Zero bounces any nonland permanent. Make Disappear is your soft counter — {1U} Mana Leak. Don't deploy Fable yet unless you're sure the board is safe — an early Fable getting answered wastes a critical combo enabler. Play reaction, not action.

engines.title: Fable + Magma Opus in GY
engines.body: T3: Deploy Fable of the Mirror-Breaker. T4 upkeep: Chapter 2 — discard Magma Opus, draw a card, create a Treasure. This puts Opus in your GY and creates the non-creature target for Creativity. Alternatively: Prismari Command on T3 discards Opus and makes a Treasure in one shot. You need Magma Opus in GY + a non-creature token/artifact on board + {3RRR} available.

engines.title: Indomitable Creativity → Gearhulk → Magma Opus
engines.body: Cast Indomitable Creativity targeting the Treasure (or any other non-creature token). Reveal library until you hit a creature — always Torrential Gearhulk (only creature). Gearhulk ETB: cast Magma Opus from GY for free. Tap four opponent permanents (shut down their attacks), deal 4 damage, draw 2 cards. The game is over functionally — they have a tapped board and you have a 5/6 with two cards up.

engines.title: Need: Lands + Interaction + Fable/Prismari Path
engines.body: Keep: 3 lands (including at least one red source for Creativity), 1-2 interaction pieces, and either Fable or Prismari Command. Mulligan: fewer than 2 lands, 0 interaction (you die to aggro before comboing), or a hand with 2+ Magma Opus (dead cards until Fable arrives). At 6: 3 lands + Make Disappear + Fiery Impulse is keepable. At 5: 3 lands + Fable is fine — you find interaction naturally.

engines.title: Fable of the Mirror-Breaker
engines.body: Chapter 1: create a 2/2 Goblin Shaman that makes a Treasure when it attacks. Chapter 2: discard and draw — put Magma Opus in GY and draw a card, OR discard dead cards and draw gas. Chapter 3: transform into Reflection of Kiki-Jiki — copy any nonlegendary creature you control when it enters. Reflection of Kiki-Jiki copying Torrential Gearhulk creates a 5/6 haste that flashes back another Magma Opus

engines.title: Indomitable Creativity → Gearhulk
engines.body: Indomitable Creativity ({X}{R}{R}{R}): for each target artifact/creature you control, exile it and reveal the top of your library until you find an artifact or creature with the same MV or less. Since Gearhulk is the only creature, X=1 always hits it. The Treasure token is the correct target — it can't be killed by creature removal, making the combo resilient. Gearhulk is a 5/6 that flashes back a

engines.title: Make Disappear + Divide by Zero
engines.body: Make Disappear: {1U} counter unless they pay {2} or you sacrifice a creature/artifact. Casualty 1 mode sacrifices the Goblin Shaman token from Fable to hard-counter anything. Divide by Zero: {1U} bounces any nonland permanent with MV 3 or less, then learn (access your lesson cards or draw). Flexible answers that double as card selection in the mid-game. Together they answer any permanent type with

engines.title: Answer Everything, Then Combo
engines.body: Against RDW and Selesnya: use ALL your removal to stay alive. Fiery Impulse + Volcanic Spite kills most threats. Brotherhood's End (SB) sweeps the board. Once stabilized at 6+ life, fire the Creativity combo — Magma Opus taps their remaining threats and the Gearhulk closes. Don't rush the combo while you're dying to their board.

engines.title: Tempo Them Out
engines.body: Against UR Cutter and Dimir Midrange: Divide by Zero bounces their key threats (Vivi Ornitier, Floodpits Drowner). Make Disappear counters their setup spells. Your Fable of the Mirror-Breaker out-values their mid-range plays. Fire the Creativity combo when they're tapped out after deploying a threat — ideally the turn after they play their most impactful card.

engines.title: Bait Counters, Then Resolve Creativity
engines.body: Against UW Control: their Dovin's Veto counters Indomitable Creativity (it's a noncreature spell they can counter). Bait their veto on Fable or a draw spell. Then fire Creativity when their countermagic is spent. Hullbreaker Horror (SB) is your best game 2 threat — it can't be countered by spells and bounces any permanent on each spell you cast.

engines.title: Hullbreaker Horror ×2
engines.body: 7-mana 7/8 with flash. Can't be countered by spells. Whenever you cast a spell, you may return target spell or permanent with MV ≤ 7 to its owner's hand. Against UW Control: Hullbreaker entered at flash speed bounces Teferi before it untaps. Every spell you cast after bounces another permanent. They can't keep anything in play. The uncounterable clause bypasses Dovin's Veto. Hard cast on T7 with m

engines.title: Brotherhood's End + Anger of Gods
engines.body: Brotherhood's End ({1RR}): deals 2 damage to each creature and each player, OR 3 damage to each artifact. Sweeps RDW's one-drops including Eidolon. Anger of the Gods ({1RR}): deals 3 damage to each creature with toughness 3 or less AND exiles them. No GY recursion. Hits Thalia, Llanowar Elves, Voice of Resurgence, Monastery Swiftspear, Kellan. Anger specifically prevents CoCo recursion via Extract

engines.title: Rending Volley ×2
engines.body: {R} instant: destroy target white or blue creature. Can't be countered. Hits Greasefang (white/black 3/3 — wait, Greasefang is a rat which is BW). Actually Rending Volley hits white creatures — relevant vs Selesnya Company (Thalia, Voice of Resurgence, Knight of Autumn) and UW Control threats (Brimaz, Wandering Emperor tokens). For Greasefang specifically, Fiery Impulse at 3 damage (spell mastery)

engines.title: Narset, Parter of Veils
engines.body: 3-mana planeswalker: static ability — opponents can't draw more than one card per turn. Shuts off Treasure Cruise (a {U} spell drawing 3 becomes draw 1), Behold the Multiverse, Consider, Opt. Against UR Cutter and Arclight Phoenix, Narset counters their entire card advantage engine. Deploy alongside interaction — they must answer Narset before drawing any cards. Her -2 looks at top 4 cards and kee

engines.title: Spell Snare Ã—2
engines.body: {U} Instant: Counter target spell with MV exactly 2. Board in vs UW Control (counters their key 2-drops) and UR Cutter (counters their Curiosity or key 2-MV spells). One mana for a hard counter is extremely efficient when you can name their most important two-drop. Board it out in matchups where their key threats are MV â‰¥ 3.

engines.title: Mystical Dispute Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{U} or {U} for blue spells: Counter target spell (or target blue spell for {U}). Board in vs UW Control (cheaply counters their blue spells) and UR Cutter (counters their key blue threats for one mana). Against non-blue decks this is {3} for a Dismiss â€” board it out. Against blue decks this is a one-mana hard counter.

engines.title: Narset, Parter of Veils Ã—1
engines.body: {1}{U}{U} Planeswalker. Opponents can't draw extra cards. âˆ’2: Look at top 4, take a noncreature nonland. Board in vs Lotus Field (shuts off their Pore Over the Pages card draw â€” they can't draw extra cards while Narset is in play, which cripples their combo) and Niv-Mizzet Reborn (shuts off their Niv ETB draw effect).

engines.title: Anger of the Gods Ã—2
engines.body: {1}{R}{R} Sorcery: 3 damage to each creature. If a creature dealt damage this way would die, exile it instead. Board in vs Selesnya Company (exile kills prevent Extraction Specialist recursion) and RDW (exiles their board before they can recurse). The exile clause is critical â€” permanently removes their creatures from GY interaction.

engines.title: 4 Torrential Gearhulk + 4 Magma Opus
engines.body: The combo requires Gearhulk in the library and Opus in the GY. 4 of each maximizes Creativity reliability (always hits) and ensures Opus is available for the flashback every game. Never cut any.

engines.title: 4 Fable of the Mirror-Breaker
engines.body: The primary Opus discard outlet AND the primary Treasure generator AND an alternate win condition. Fable is the reason the deck functions. 4 copies ensures you draw it consistently by T3.

engines.title: Indomitable Creativity
engines.body: 3 is reference. 4 in metas where firing the combo ASAP is critical. 3 in metas where the control shell can win without Creativity (via Reflection of Kiki-Jiki or Hullbreaker). The 3 copies ensure you draw it without the risk of redundant copies in the combo window.

engines.title: Fiery Impulse + Volcanic Spite
engines.body: 7 total removal spells is correct in most metas. In heavy aggro metas, go to 8-9. In control-heavy metas, trim to 5-6 and add more permission. The ratio between removal and counters adjusts to the expected threats.

engines.title: Make Disappear
engines.body: 4 in permission-heavy metas where you need redundant counters. 2-3 in aggro metas where you'd rather have more removal. Make Disappear is weakest against decks that can pay the {2} (control) and best vs combo and midrange.

engines.title: Creature Lands
engines.body: Hall of Storm Giants (3/3 ward when attacking) and Den of the Bugbear (Goblin + Haste) provide resilient win conditions that bypass Creativity entirely. In control-heavy metas where Creativity gets countered, running 2-3 creature lands gives you alternate pressure that works through their interaction.

engines.title: Counter Target Protocol
engines.body: You identify their top 3 threats before round 1 starts and assign the correct counter to each. UR Cutter: Rending Volley for Cutter creature. Greasefang: Dovin's Veto for Greasefang spell. Lotus Field: Damping Sphere before they assemble combo. You know your target before your opponent casts anything.

engines.title: Anger of the Gods Threshold
engines.body: You cast Anger of the Gods when they have 3+ creatures, not 1-2. Against RDW: they commit 3 creatures by T3 — Anger on your T3 is correct. Against Selesnya Company: they commit after a Company resolution. You count creatures before casting and enforce the 3+ threshold.

engines.title: Narset Deployment
engines.body: You deploy Narset when they're about to draw multiple cards. Against Lotus Field: before they tap Lotus for their cantrip chain. Against Niv-Mizzet: before they cast Niv (his ETB draws stop under Narset). Against UR Cutter: when they're about to chain cantrips. You protect Narset with Mystical Dispute.

engines.title: Hullbreaker Sequence
engines.body: You deploy Hullbreaker Horror on T7+ when you have at least one instant available. Hullbreaker enters (uncounterable 7/8). You cast an instant (Spell Pierce, Mystical Dispute): bounce their most expensive permanent. You cast another instant next turn: bounce their next most expensive. Each spell bounces one permanent.

engines.title: Anger vs Brotherhood's End
engines.body: You adjust your sweeper split based on the meta's creature toughness. Anger of the Gods exiles at 3 damage — hits 3-toughness or less AND prevents GY recursion (critical vs Greasefang). Brotherhood's End deals 2 damage — cheaper but misses 3-toughness creatures. You run Anger in GY-heavy metas, Brotherhood's in pure aggro metas.

engines.title: Rending Volley vs Fatal Push
engines.body: Rending Volley destroys white or blue creatures at {R} — specifically answers Greasefang (white) and UR Cutter creatures (blue). Fatal Push destroys any creature at MV ≤ 2 (or ≤ 4 with revolt). You run Rending Volley when the meta has many white/blue creatures. You run Fatal Push when the threats are across all colors.

engines.title: Mystical Dispute Count
engines.body: You add Mystical Dispute copies when blue decks dominate your meta. Dispute counters blue spells at {U} — free against UW Control and UR Cutter. You cut Dispute in non-blue heavy metas where it costs {3} instead of {U}. The Dispute count tracks inversely with your blue opponent percentage.

engines.title: Hullbreaker Horror Count
engines.body: You run 1-2 Hullbreaker Horrors in metas with many control decks that go to the late game. Horror is uncounterable and bounces permanents — ideal vs tap-out control opponents. You cut Horror in aggro-heavy metas where you don't reach 7 mana reliably. Horror is a metagame call, not a staple.

engines.title: Soul-Guide Lantern vs Graveyard Trespasser
engines.body: You run Soul-Guide Lantern (1-mana instant GY exile with cantrip) in light-GY-hate slots. You run Graveyard Trespasser (3/3 creature that exiles GY cards when something dies) in heavier-hate slots. Lantern: cheap and instant speed. Trespasser: body + continuous exile. You choose based on whether you need a threat or just a tool.

engines.title: Narset vs Chandra, Torch of Defiance
engines.body: You run Narset, Parter of Veils when opponents draw many extra cards (Lotus Field combo, Niv-Mizzet). You run Chandra, Torch of Defiance when you need reach (Chandra's +1 deals 2 damage). In metas with heavy draw engines: Narset. In metas where you need extra damage: Chandra.

engines.title: Anger of the Gods Exile Clause
engines.body: Anger of the Gods exiles creatures that would die to it rather than destroying them. This prevents GY recursion: Flamewake Phoenix is exiled, not killed. Arclight Phoenix is exiled, not killed. Monstrous Rage targets die and are exiled. The exile clause is why Anger outperforms Brotherhood's End in GY-heavy metas.

engines.title: Spell Pierce vs Negate
engines.body: Spell Pierce ({U}: counter noncreature unless they pay {2}) is efficient early but falls off late. Negate ({1}{U}: counter noncreature unconditionally) is always relevant. You run Pierce for early counter wars (T1-3) and Negate for late-game insurance. The ratio shifts based on your expected game length.

engines.title: Jace, the Mind Sculptor
engines.body: Jace, the Mind Sculptor (4 mana planeswalker: +2 look at top 2; 0 draw 3 shuffle 2 back; −1 bounce; −12 win) is your most powerful draw engine in long games. You run 1-2 Jace in metas where you reliably reach 4 mana with the board under control.

engines.title: Abrade vs Fatal Push
engines.body: Abrade ({1}{R}: 3 damage or destroy artifact) answers artifacts specifically — Cori-Steel Cutter, Lotus vehicles, any artifact threat. Fatal Push ({B}: destroy MV ≤ 2 or ≤ 4 with revolt) handles small creatures. Your split depends on artifact vs creature density in the expected meta.

engines.title: Thing in the Ice Flip
engines.body: Thing in the Ice (1/4: remove ice counters by casting spells; when last removed, transforms into 7/8 that bounces all non-Horror creatures) is your surprise win condition. You deploy it on T2 and cast 4 spells to flip it. The bounce ETB clears their board when it transforms.

engines.title: Opt vs Consider
engines.body: Opt (scry 1 then draw) vs Consider (surveil 1 — mill or keep — then draw): Consider mills cards into your GY for Treasure Cruise fuel. Opt keeps cards on top for future draws. You run Consider in Cruise-heavy configurations and Opt in pure-control configurations.

engines.title: Negate Slot
engines.body: Negate ({1}{U}: counter noncreature spell) handles their board wipes, their planeswalkers, and their key enchantments. You run 1-2 Negate in metas where their win conditions are noncreature permanents. You cut Negate in creature-heavy metas.

engines.title: Exile vs Destroy
engines.body: Anger of the Gods exiles (prevents GY recursion). Brotherhood's End destroys (they go to GY). You run Anger when their GY matters (Greasefang's Parhelion in GY, Arclight Phoenix). You run Brotherhood's End when GY is irrelevant. Default: Anger for Pioneer's GY-heavy meta.

engines.title: T1 Instant vs White/Blue Threats
engines.body: Rending Volley destroys white or blue creatures at {R}. It's your most efficient answer to Greasefang (white) and UR Cutter creatures (blue). You hold {R} specifically for Rending Volley on T1-2 when you know their key threat is white or blue.

engines.title: Your One-Mana Counter
engines.body: Mystical Dispute counters blue spells at {U}. Against UW Control and UR Cutter, you hold {U} open every turn you have Dispute in hand. You never tap your blue mana for development when Dispute is available and they have blue sources untapped.

engines.title: Never Dead
engines.body: Soul-Guide Lantern exiles their GY at instant speed. Even against non-GY decks: you crack it for {B} to draw a card. You deploy Lantern during their upkeep or in response to their GY trigger — never during your main phase when they might have responses.

engines.title: Three Creatures Always
engines.body: You cast Anger of the Gods when they have exactly 3 creatures with 3 or less toughness. Below 3: use cheaper answers. At 3: Anger sweeps their entire board while exiling to prevent recursion. You count toughness values before casting.

engines.title: Before Their Draw Chain
engines.body: You deploy Narset when they're about to chain draw spells. Against Lotus Field: before Pore Over the Pages. Against Niv-Mizzet: before Niv ETB. Your goal: Narset resolves BEFORE they draw their key cards.

engines.title: One Mana Counter for Blue
engines.body: Mystical Dispute costs {U} for blue spells. You hold {U} open on their turn when you have Dispute in hand and expect a blue spell. You never tap out when Dispute is in hand and their land base includes blue sources.

engines.title: Identify Their Win Condition
engines.body: You identify their win condition before T1 and assign your counters accordingly. Greasefang: Dovin's Veto for Greasefang the creature spell. Lotus: Damping Sphere to shut their combo. UR Cutter: Rending Volley for their key blue attackers.

engines.title: Check Mode Before Casting
engines.body: You decide Brotherhood's End's mode before tapping mana: Mode A (2 damage each creature/planeswalker) or Mode B (destroy MV ≤ 3 artifacts). You commit to a mode based on their board state. You never cast Brotherhood's End without knowing which mode you're using.

engines.title: Trigger Before Casting
engines.body: You crack a fetchland or sacrifice a Soul-Guide Lantern BEFORE casting Fatal Push to trigger revolt (MV ≤ 4 mode). Without revolt, Push only hits MV ≤ 2. With revolt: hits Kalitas, Sheoldred, most of their key threats.

engines.title: The Bait-Before-Fire Protocol
engines.body: Against any deck with countermagic: (1) cast something expendable at end of their turn — Prismari Command, Behold the Multiverse, Divide by Zero. (2) Watch if they counter it. (3) If they counter: their mana is spent, untap, fire Creativity. (4) If they don't counter: the card drew you into Opus/Creativity, proceed. Never fire Creativity into open blue mana without knowing their hand or having bai

engines.title: Magma Opus Four-Tap Priority
engines.body: When Magma Opus taps four permanents, it's often the most important decision in the game. Default priority: (1) their active threats attacking you next turn, (2) mana that enables their key answer, (3) planeswalkers before next activation, (4) anything with a relevant activated ability. Never tap random basics — tap the four things that win them the game if left untapped.

engines.title: SB for Expected Field
engines.body: Heavy control (UW Control): Hullbreaker × 2 + Disdainful Stroke × 2 + Negate. Heavy aggro (RDW, Selesnya): Brotherhood's End + Anger of Gods. Heavy GY combo (Greasefang, Phoenix): Rending Volley + Narset. Confirm 15 cards map cleanly to expected matchups. Creativity's SB is highly flexible — 12 of 15 slots flex.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Mountain = RDW (board Anger of Gods G2). Steam Vents Island = UR Cutter (board Rending Volley + Disdainful Stroke). Godless Shrine = Greasefang (board Rending Volley; protect Divide by Zero for Greasefang bounce). Forest = Selesnya Company (board Anger of Gods + Brotherhood's End). Hallowed Fountain = UW Control (board Hullbreaker + counters). Cycling lands = Phoenix or Lotus Field (board accordin

engines.title: Counter Target Drills
engines.body: Practice identifying the correct counter target by matchup. UR Cutter: counter Cutter. Greasefang: counter Greasefang. Lotus Field: counter Hidden Strings. Know without thinking.

engines.title: Narset Timing
engines.body: Practice deploying Narset at the right moment. Against Lotus: before they tap Lotus. Against Niv: before they cast Niv. Against cantrip decks: on turn 3 before their draw chain.

engines.title: Anger Timing
engines.body: Practice waiting for 3+ creatures before casting Anger. Against RDW: they commit 3 creatures by T3. Against Company: they commit after a Company resolution. Know the correct wait threshold.

engines.title: Hullbreaker Closing
engines.body: Practice the Hullbreaker closing sequence. Cast Hullbreaker, then cast a 1-mana spell to bounce their key permanent, then another to bounce something else. Each spell triggers a bounce.

IZZETELEMENTALS.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "This is not Izzet Spellementals. This is the Incarnation-based Elemental tribal deck. Every creature is an Elemental. Cavern names Elemental. Sunderflock costs zero." Izzet Elementals is the Incarnation tribal variant of the Elemental archetype, distinct from Izzet Spellementals. Where Spellementals uses cantrips and Hearth Elemental to reduce Sunderflock's cost, Elementals uses the Incarnation cycle — Ashling, Rekindled , Flamebraider , Vibrance , Wistfulness — as a suite of hybrid-mana Elementals that each contribute to reducing Sunderflock 's cost by {1} per Elemen
IZZETELEMENTALS.mulligan:
Mulligan
Need Elementals + Throne or Sunderflock
Snap keep: 2+ Elementals + Roaming Throne + 3 lands.

engines.title: Incarnation Tribal Engine
engines.body: Uses Ashling, Flamebraider, Vibrance, Wistfulness as the Elemental package. Each is a hybrid-mana Elemental that enters with an effect. Roaming Throne doubles all their triggers. Sunderflock reduced by 4 with four Elementals = free. Cavern of Souls. More resilient vs removal — the Incarnations replace themselves and generate ongoing value.

engines.title: Spell-Density Engine
engines.body: Uses Hearth Elemental + Eddymurk Crab + cantrips. GY-based cost reduction. More explosive burst potential (free 5/5 Crab with 5 GY spells). Less tribal synergy but faster in specific draws. Izzet Elementals is the more consistent and resilient variant; Spellementals is more combo-capable but less stable.

engines.title: Ashling, Rekindled // Ashling, Rimebound
engines.body: Hybrid {R/U}{R/U}{R/U} Elemental Spirit. Front face: ETB discard any number of cards then draw that many. Back face (Ashling, Rimebound): when it dies, exile it and return to hand. With Roaming Throne: discard/draw triggers twice = cycle 2x more cards per ETB. Front-face Ashling is the card advantage engine. Use Bounce Off or Deceit to return it to hand for another ETB cycle.

engines.title: Flamebraider
engines.body: Hybrid {R/U}{R/U} 2/2 Elemental. Whenever it attacks: create a 1/1 red Elemental token. With Roaming Throne: creates two tokens per attack. These tokens ARE Elementals — they count toward reducing Sunderflock's cost. A T2 Flamebraider that attacks twice creates 2-4 Elemental tokens, rapidly assembling the Sunderflock cost reduction threshold.

engines.title: Vibrance
engines.body: Hybrid Elemental. ETB or whenever you draw a card: do something relevant. With Roaming Throne: the draw trigger fires twice. In the Elementals deck, Vibrance contributes both as an Elemental (reducing Sunderflock's cost) and as a card advantage engine that scales with your draw engine.

engines.title: Wistfulness
engines.body: Hybrid Elemental. Mode 1: Naturalize (destroy artifact or enchantment). Mode 2: Look at top 3 cards, take 1, discard the rest. With Wistfulness in Elementals: the filter mode helps find Roaming Throne or Sunderflock consistently. The Naturalize mode destroys Monument to Endurance vs Izzet Lessons. Play Wistfulness immediately — Abandon Attachments can destroy it.

engines.title: Roaming Throne — Name Elemental
engines.body: Roaming Throne named Elemental: each Elemental you control's triggered abilities trigger an additional time. Ashling's discard/draw ETB fires twice (cycle 2x cards). Flamebraider's attack trigger fires twice (two tokens instead of one). Vibrance's draw trigger fires twice. Sunderflock's ETB (damage to each creature) fires twice with Throne = double the damage. This is the deck's key force multipli

engines.title: Sunderflock — Costs 0 With 4 Elementals
engines.body: Sunderflock costs {X}{U} where X reduces by 1 per Elemental you control. With 4 Elementals in play: X=0, Sunderflock costs {U}. ETB: deals X damage to each creature (where X = number of Elementals you control). With Throne active: deals 2X damage to each creature. Four Elementals + Throne = 8 damage to each creature — kills almost everything in Standard. Cast Sunderflock at your opponent's end ste

engines.title: Deceit — Two Modes
engines.body: Deceit has two modes (like Thoughtseize + bounce): Distress mode (sorcery speed): target player reveals hand, you choose a nonland card, they discard it. Bounce mode: return target nonland permanent with MV ≤ 2 to its owner's hand. Distress strips their key piece before they cast it (Monument to Endurance, Roaming Throne, Sapling Nursery). Bounce mode removes their T1-T2 dorks or resets your own A

engines.title: Winternight Stories
engines.body: Three-chapter saga: Chapter 1 draws a card. Chapter 2 mills 3 then returns up to 1 from your GY to hand. Chapter 3 each opponent discards a card. Three turns of value — card draw, recursion, and hand disruption. Running 3 copies ensures you see it consistently. Chapter 2 can return Ashling from GY to hand, enabling another ETB cycle without casting it from hand. Critical in grindy matchups.

engines.title: Elementals → Throne → Sunderflock
engines.body: T1: Any Elemental (Ashling for {R/U}, Flamebraider for {R/U}{R/U}, etc.). T2: Second Elemental. T3: Roaming Throne (named Elemental). T4: Third Elemental (Throne doubles its ETB) + Sunderflock for free (3 Elementals = free at {0}{U}). Sunderflock ETB deals 3 damage to each creature, Throne doubles it = 6 damage to each. Kills most Standard boards instantly.

engines.title: Four Elementals + Throne = 8 Damage Each
engines.body: With 4 Elementals and Roaming Throne: Sunderflock is free, deals 8 damage to each creature (4 Elementals × 2 from Throne). Every creature in Standard with 8 or less toughness dies. This board wipe is better than Day of Judgment because it also damages large creatures and happens at sorcery speed as part of your own threat deployment. The mana investment: T1+T2+T3 building Elementals, T3 Throne, T4

engines.title: Need Elementals + Throne or Sunderflock
engines.body: Snap keep: 2+ Elementals + Roaming Throne + 3 lands. Keep on 7: 2 Elementals + Sunderflock + lands. Mulligan: all spells and no Elementals, or all Elementals and no Sunderflock/Throne, or 5+ lands. You need the critical mass to generate the free Sunderflock. A hand of Cavern + 4 Elementals + Throne is nearly perfect.

engines.title: Always Name Elemental
engines.body: Cavern of Souls named Elemental makes ALL your creatures uncounterable — Ashling, Flamebraider, Vibrance, Wistfulness, Beza, and crucially Sunderflock (which is an Elemental). This means your entire game plan — every creature AND your board wipe — cannot be countered. Against Izzet Lessons, Azorius Flash, and Jeskai Control this is the single most important decision every game.

engines.title: Elemental Count → Sunderflock Cost
engines.body: Sunderflock costs {1} less for each Elemental you control. 1 Elemental: {2}{U}. 2 Elementals: {1}{U}. 3 Elementals: {U}. 4 Elementals: free! All 20 creature slots are Elementals. This is the deck's combo engine — assembling Elementals is the game plan. Count your Elementals before every main phase.

engines.title: Roaming Throne Doubles
engines.body: Throne named Elemental: each Elemental ETB trigger fires twice. Ashling ETB: discard/draw twice. Flamebraider attack: two tokens. Vibrance trigger: twice. Sunderflock ETB: deals damage TWICE (4 Elementals × 2 triggers = 8 total damage per trigger instance). The Throne-Sunderflock interaction is the deck's game-ending board wipe.

engines.title: Ashling Discard/Draw Loop
engines.body: Ashling's ETB: discard any number, draw that many. Returns to hand when the back face dies. Bounce Off / Deceit bounce mode: return Ashling to hand for another ETB cycle. Winternight Stories Chapter 2: return Ashling from GY. The result: you can cycle Ashling's ETB multiple times per game, finding Throne and Sunderflock through sheer card selection.

engines.title: Assemble and Execute
engines.body: Build to 4 Elementals + Roaming Throne. Cast free Sunderflock for 8 damage to each creature. Attack into the empty board. The entire game is executed in 4-5 turns. Don't deviate from this plan. If the board wipe isn't lethal, follow up with another Sunderflock next turn (only 3 in the main, so use them wisely).

engines.title: Cavern + Resilience
engines.body: Against counterspell decks: Cavern off Elemental = all your creatures and Sunderflock uncounterable. Deploy through their permission. Use Deceit to strip their counterspell from hand before deploying Throne. Winternight Stories draws cards to replace answered threats. You cannot be countered — the control matchup is winnable.

engines.title: Deceit Strips Their Throne
engines.body: Against Izzet Spellementals mirror or any Throne-based deck: Deceit's Distress mode strips their Roaming Throne from hand before it resolves. A Spellementals deck without Throne is much slower. Deceit is your most important card in mirror matchups.

engines.title: Pyroclasm ×3
engines.body: 2 damage to each creature. Emergency sweeper vs aggro when Sunderflock isn't assembled yet. Kills: Izzet Prowess tokens (1/1), Mono-Red 1-2 drops, Boros Aggro creatures, Flamebraider tokens in the mirror. Note: also kills your own 1-2 toughness Elementals — time after you've attacked. Boards in vs all aggro matchups.

engines.title: Spell Snare ×3
engines.body: Counter target spell with MV exactly 2 for {U}. Efficient hard counter for key 2-CMC threats: Badgermole Cub (2 CMC), Flamebraider (2 CMC), Gene Pollinator (3 CMC — doesn't hit), Kaito (5 CMC — doesn't hit). Check MV carefully before boarding in. Best vs decks where their key play is exactly 2 CMC.

engines.title: Soul-Guide Lantern ×2
engines.body: GY hate for Monument to Endurance, Marang River Regent's trigger, any GY strategy. Cheap to deploy alongside your engine. The sacrifice mode exiles their entire GY. Boards in vs Izzet Lessons, Simic Rhythm (Regent), and any GY-dependent strategy.

engines.title: Sear ×2
engines.body: 4 damage to creature or planeswalker. Kills Kaito (loyalty-based), Ojer Axonil (4/4 — Sear does 4 damage exactly), and any 4-toughness creature that Pyroclasm can't reach. Boards in vs midrange decks with medium-size threats and vs any planeswalker-heavy build.

engines.title: Slagstorm Ã—2
engines.body: {1}{R}{R} Sorcery. Mode A: 3 damage to each creature. Mode B: 3 damage to each player. Mode A sweeps Simic Rhythm's Badgermole Cub tokens (all at 2/2 or less at 3 damage) and Mono-Red's board simultaneously. Mode B is rarely used. Board in vs any strategy that floods the board with small creatures that collectively outrace your setup.

engines.title: Into the Flood Maw Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{U} Instant: Return up to two target creatures to their owners' hands. Board in vs Boros Dragons (bounces their key Dragon back before it attacks) and Jeskai Control (bounces their Voice of Victory or Aven Interrupter). Unlike removal, bounce preserves your tempo by making them recast their creature â€” they lose the mana, you keep the board advantage.

engines.title: Glacial Dragonhunt Ã—1
engines.body: {5}{U} Instant: Counter target spell. Draw a card. Board in vs Mono-Green Landfall when the game goes long and you can hold up 6 mana â€” counters their Lumra or Mossborn Hydra while cantripping. Expensive but the draw makes it never a pure tempo loss. Only board in matchups where holding 6 mana open is realistic.

engines.title: Disdainful Stroke Ã—2
engines.body: {1}{U} Instant: Counter target spell with MV â‰¥ 4. Board in vs Jeskai Control (counters their expensive board wipes and walkers) and Mono-Green Landfall (Mossborn Hydra at MV 7, Lumra at MV 7). Hard counter â€” cannot be paid through. Most efficient in turns 4-6 before opponents have excess mana.

engines.title: The Elemental Core
engines.body: 4 Ashling, 4 Flamebraider, 4 Vibrance, 4 Wistfulness, 4 Roaming Throne = 20 locked cards. These are the engine. No cuts below 4 of any of them — the Sunderflock cost reduction requires consistent Elemental density.

engines.title: 4 Cavern of Souls
engines.body: Four copies. The deck cannot function in counter-heavy metas without Cavern. Never cut below 4. The "Elemental" tribal designation means every single card in the 35-nonland slots benefits from Cavern protection.

engines.title: Sunderflock
engines.body: 3 main + 1 SB = 4 total. You want to draw Sunderflock consistently but not flood on it (it's your finisher, not your setup). 3 main is the sweet spot. In aggressive metas where you need the board wipe more urgently, consider a 4th main copy.

engines.title: Deceit
engines.body: 4 main in the March 30 list. Some builds run 3. Deceit's dual function (Distress + bounce) is always relevant. In aggro-heavy metas, trim to 3 and add a fourth Sear or Pyroclasm. In midrange/control metas, 4 Deceit is correct — you need the hand disruption.

engines.title: Bounce Off
engines.body: 3 main in March 30 list. Bounce Off protects Roaming Throne from exile and resets Ashling for ETB cycles. In aggro metas where tempo bounce matters less, trim to 1-2. In control metas, keep 3 — saving Throne from Get Lost is the most important play in those matchups.

engines.title: Creature-Based Metas
engines.body: Izzet Elementals is perfectly positioned when the meta is full of creature strategies. Sunderflock with Throne kills any creature-based board. If the expected field is Simic Rhythm + Dimir Midrange + Izzet Prowess, register Elementals — your board wipe answers all of them.

engines.title: Hearth Elemental Chain
engines.body: You chain cantrips into Hearth Elemental by casting cheap instants/sorceries that reduce Hearth's cost via its ability. With one other elemental in play, Hearth costs {1} less. Two elementals: {2} less. You build your elemental count first, then cast Hearth at reduced cost. Hearth is most efficient when you have 2+ other elementals.

engines.title: Eddymurk Crab Flash Rule
engines.body: You flash Eddymurk Crab at their attack step, never your main phase. The tap-on-ETB prevents their attacker from attacking this turn. Main-phase deployment loses the tap timing. At their attack step: they declare attackers, you flash in Crab, Crab taps their best attacker before it can attack.

engines.title: Sunderflock Threshold
