engines.body: You cast Sunderflock when they have 3+ creatures. One or two creatures: use a cheaper answer. At 3 creatures: Sunderflock at 4-5 damage kills their entire board simultaneously. You calculate: does each creature have toughness ≤ Sunderflock's damage? If yes for all three: cast it. If any survives: hold for a better window.

engines.title: DRC GY Management
engines.body: You never exile a card from your GY when Dreadhorde Arcanist is in play or in hand. Every Opt, every Lightning Bolt in your GY is a free spell on DRC's attack. You keep your cheapest spells in GY and spend your more expensive spells from hand. You sequence: use expensive GY spells first, keep cheap ones for DRC.

engines.title: Sear vs Burst Lightning
engines.body: You run Sear (2 damage or 4 kicked) when your primary targets are 2-4 toughness. You run Burst Lightning (2 damage or 4 kicked for {2}{R}) in the same slot but at different converted costs. Sear's {1}{R} base vs Burst's {R} base — in fast metas, Burst's lower base cost matters more than Sear's middle mode.

engines.title: Glacial Dragonhunt Quantity
engines.body: You run Glacial Dragonhunt in long-game control matchups where you need expensive uncounterable finishers. You cut it in fast metas where you never reach 6 mana. Dragonhunt is a metagame card — run 1 as a finisher in your control matchup slot only when the meta rewards going long.

engines.title: Build Elemental Count First
engines.body: Hearth Elemental costs {1} less for each other elemental you control. With two other elementals: Hearth is free or near-free. You deploy Eddymurk Crab and Dreadhorde Arcanist before Hearth to reduce its cost maximally.

engines.title: Always Flash, Never Sorcery
engines.body: You flash Eddymurk Crab at their attack step. The tap-on-ETB prevents their attacker from swinging this turn. If you deploy at your main phase, they tap you during YOUR turn and you wasted the timing advantage.

engines.title: Confirm All Die Before Casting
engines.body: You cast Sunderflock when ALL of their creatures have toughness ≤ Sunderflock's damage. If any survive, you've wasted the sweeper. You count every creature's toughness before casting and confirm the total wipe before tapping mana.

engines.title: Cheapest Spells Stay in GY
engines.body: Your Dreadhorde Arcanist attacks and casts a spell from GY with MV ≤ Arcanist's power for free. You keep your cheapest spells in GY and spend your more expensive spells from hand. An Opt in GY cast by DRC for free is a cantrip at no cost.

engines.title: Sunderflock Math
engines.body: 3 Elementals = Sunderflock costs {U}. 3 Elementals + Throne = Sunderflock free, deals 6 damage each (3 × 2 triggers). 4 Elementals + Throne = Sunderflock free, deals 8 damage each. Memorize these thresholds. Count your Elementals (including tokens) before every main phase.

engines.title: Cavern Names Elemental
engines.body: Name Elemental on Cavern immediately when it enters. Every creature in the deck is an Elemental. Sunderflock is an Elemental. Cavern named Elemental = your entire game plan is uncounterable. There is no game where you name something other than Elemental.

engines.title: SB Configuration
engines.body: Aggro-heavy field: +3 Pyroclasm mandatory. Control-heavy: +1 Disdainful Stroke + +3 Spell Snare. GY strategies: +2 Soul-Guide Lantern. Izzet Lessons: Wistfulness in main already handles Monument, but Soul-Guide Lantern + Disdainful Stroke are must-boards. Confirm your 15.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Forest = Green deck — assemble freely, use Wistfulness to naturalize their enchantments. Steam Vents / Spirebluff = Izzet — Deceit their Monument or key threat. Island or Plains = Azorius/Jeskai — board Spell Snare, keep Bounce Off for Throne protection. Watery Grave = Dimir — play through their removal, board Spell Snare.

engines.title: Cantrip Chain Drills
engines.body: Practice chaining cantrips into Hearth Elemental. The sequence: Opt (1 mana) â†’ Sleight of Hand (1 mana, reduced) â†’ Hearth attacks. Count your spell count each turn.

engines.title: Eddymurk Crab Flash Timing
engines.body: Practice flashing Eddymurk in at their attack step. The tap-on-ETB taps their attacker before it can attack. This is the card's primary use case â€” always flash, never sorcery-speed.

engines.title: Sunderflock Threshold
engines.body: Practice waiting for 3+ creatures before casting Sunderflock. The 3-creature threshold is when Sunderflock generates positive card advantage. 1-2 creatures = consider a different answer.

engines.title: DRC Attack Drills
engines.body: Practice the DRC attack line: keep instants in GY (Opt, Lightning Bolt) with MV â‰¤ DRC's power. When DRC attacks, cast the best GY instant for free. Know which GY instant to cast each combat.

IZZETLESSONS.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "You win by drawing three cards for one mana, making Treasure tokens to cast more spells, and pinging them for three every turn — all from one artifact." Izzet Lessons won the 2025 Magic: The Gathering World Championship in Seth Manfield's hands and has remained one of the top two decks in Standard ever since. The deck is built around a single artifact — Monument to Endurance — and an engine that makes it work as early as turn 3. The engine: every Lesson subtype card in your graveyard (Firebending Lesson, Abandon Attachments, Combustion Technique, Iroh's Demonstration,

engines.title: Accumulate Wisdom: Draw 3 for Free
engines.body: With 3+ Lessons in GY and Gran-Gran or Artist's Talent active, Accumulate Wisdom ({1}{U} normally) costs {U} or even {0}. Drawing 3 cards for effectively free is Ancestral Recall territory. You hit this condition by turn 3 routinely — your entire spell package is Lessons. Once you can draw 3 per Wisdom cast, you never run out of resources.

engines.title: Monument to Endurance: 3 Damage Per Discard
engines.body: Monument says: discard a card, choose — draw, make Treasure, or opponent loses 3 life. Three discards in a turn = 9 damage. Monument triggers on both players' turns. With Artist's Talent leveled, you discard whenever you cast a spell. A chain of 3 spells on your turn = 9 damage. They untap, you hold up It'll Quench Ya, they cast something = 3 more damage on their turn. Monument kills from full lif

engines.title: It'll Quench Ya + Stormchaser's Talent
engines.body: It'll Quench Ya ({U}, counter unless they pay {3}) protects Monument and Artist's Talent at minimal cost. Stormchaser's Talent provides an alternate win condition — Level 3 creates 1/1 Otters per spell, and with the Lessons engine active you're casting 4-6 spells per turn. Stormchaser's also generates Otters to block early aggression, buying time for the Monument engine to come online.

engines.title: Midrange and Creature Decks Dominate
engines.body: Izzet Lessons is at its best when opponents are leaning on creatures and targeted removal — both of which do nothing against your 30+ noncreature spells. If the field is Dimir Midrange, Boros Aggro, Mono-Green, and Bant Rhythm, you're favored in most matchups and drawing 3 cards per Accumulate Wisdom while they have dead removal in hand.

engines.title: Artifact/Enchantment Hate Is Widespread
engines.body: Annul, Ancient Vendetta, Abrade, and Graveyard exile (Rest in Peace) all hurt you. If the metagame shifts to heavy hate for artifacts and enchantments specifically, the engine is more fragile. Also consider alternatives when the mirror (Izzet Lessons) is above 15% of the field — the mirror is a technical grind that depends heavily on Monument hitting the table first.

engines.title: Gran-Gran
engines.body: Legendary Creature — Legendary {1}{U}. 1/3. When Gran-Gran attacks, you may discard a card. Spells you cast cost {1} less for each differently named Lesson card in your GY (max {3} reduction). T1 Gran-Gran → T2 one Lesson spell → T3 with 3 Lessons in GY, everything costs 2 less. Monument costs {1}, Accumulate Wisdom costs {0}. Gran-Gran is the engine ignition — protect it on turns 1-3 at all costs

engines.title: Monument to Endurance
engines.body: Artifact {3}. {T}: Discard a card, then choose — draw a card, create a Treasure, or target player loses 3 life. The ability triggers ONCE per turn. With Artist's Talent (discard per spell cast), you trigger Monument with each spell. Three spells = three Monument triggers = 9 damage + 3 Treasures + 3 cards drawn. Monument triggers on both turns. Bounce Monument with Boomerang Basics to reset it as

engines.title: Accumulate Wisdom
engines.body: Instant {1}{U}. Draw a card. If you have 3+ Lessons in your GY, draw 3 cards instead. With Gran-Gran + Artist's Talent active (2 discount total) and 3 Lessons in GY: Accumulate Wisdom costs {0} and draws 3. This is Ancestral Recall. Four copies means you draw 12 cards per average game just from this card alone. The condition is trivially met by turn 3 since all your interaction is Lessons.

engines.title: Artist's Talent
engines.body: Enchantment — Class {1}{U}. Level 1: discard a card when you cast a spell. Level 2 ({3}{U}): spells cost {1} less. Level 3 ({5}{U}): each spell also creates a 1/1 Otter. Level 1 is always active from the moment you cast it — every spell triggers Monument. Level 2 stacks with Gran-Gran for up to {2} cost reduction. Level 3 creates an army of Otters from your spell chain. Artist's Talent Level 1 is

engines.title: Lessons (Removal)
engines.body: Firebending Lesson: {R} Lesson — 2 damage to creature or planeswalker. With Gran-Gran at 3 Lessons in GY: free. Combustion Technique: {2}{R} Lesson — 3 damage, scales with Lessons in GY (+1 per Lesson, up to 6). Iroh's Demonstration: {2}{R}{R} Lesson — deals damage equal to Lessons in GY to each creature opponent controls. All three are Lessons, so casting them fuels the discount engine and counts

engines.title: Abandon Attachments
engines.body: Sorcery — Lesson {2}{U}. Look at top 4, put 2 into hand, 2 into GY. A key turn-2 play: cast Abandon Attachments, bin 2 Lessons into GY. Now on turn 3 you already have 3 Lessons in GY (the two from Attachments + Abandon Attachments itself). Gran-Gran full discount is active by turn 3 routinely. Also digs for Monument or missing pieces. Three copies in main, one in SB.

engines.title: Gran-Gran
engines.body: Always T1 Gran-Gran if it's in hand. It's a 1/3 that blocks early aggression, its attack trigger discards to fuel Monument later, and it's the cost reduction engine. Every hand without Gran-Gran T1 is a slower hand. Gran-Gran on T1 means full cost reduction is available by T3.

engines.title: Abandon Attachments
engines.body: Cast Abandon Attachments ({2}{U}, reduced to {1}{U} with Gran-Gran). Look at top 4, bin 2 Lessons. Now you have 3 Lessons in GY (Attachments + 2 binned). Full cost reduction is LIVE on T3. Alternatively: cast Artist's Talent Level 1 on T2 to set up Monument triggers earlier.

engines.title: Artist's Talent + Free Wisdom
engines.body: Cast Artist's Talent Level 1 ({1}{U}, free with Gran-Gran). Every spell now triggers Monument when it resolves. Then cast Accumulate Wisdom for free — draw 3 cards. You're now up 3 cards from Wisdom + maintaining hand size. If you drew Monument, deploy it. If not, hold up It'll Quench Ya or cast Firebending Lesson to keep binning Lessons.

engines.title: Monument + Chain
engines.body: Cast Monument to Endurance ({3}, reduced to {1}). It resolves. Now every spell you cast triggers Artist's Talent (discard) which triggers Monument (choose: draw/Treasure/3 damage). Cast Firebending Lesson (free) → discard → Monument → 3 damage. Cast Combustion Technique (free) → discard → Monument → Treasure. Cast Accumulate Wisdom (free, draw 3) → discard → Monument → 3 more damage. You're doing

engines.title: T1 Gran-Gran is Non-Negotiable
engines.body: On the play, Gran-Gran on T1 means you're one full turn ahead on the engine. T2 Abandon Attachments fills the GY. T3 you have full discount live and can cast Accumulate Wisdom for free. Any hand with T1 Gran-Gran and 3 lands is a keep. Prioritize the T1 Gran-Gran line over any other consideration.

engines.title: Extra Card Buys Flexibility
engines.body: On the draw, you have an extra card — this makes hands without T1 Gran-Gran more keepable. A hand with Artist's Talent T2 + Abandon Attachments T3 still hits the engine by T4. The extra card often means you draw Gran-Gran by T2 anyway. Looser keeps on the draw, but still mulligan hands with 0 or 1 lands.

engines.title: Rebuild Through Artist's Talent
engines.body: Gran-Gran dying is painful but not game-ending. Artist's Talent Level 2 provides cost reduction independently. If you have Artist's Talent Level 2 active, you still get {1} discount per spell. A second Gran-Gran from hand restores the full engine. Don't overextend trying to protect Gran-Gran — let them spend removal on it and rebuild. Their removal is sorcery-speed in most cases.

engines.title: Use Boomerang Basics to Replay
engines.body: If Monument is Annulled or Abrade'd, bounce it with Boomerang Basics before they destroy it — return it to hand as a new object. Recast next turn. If it's destroyed before you can Boomerang it, deploy the second copy. Four copies means you typically have one in hand or draw it quickly. Use It'll Quench Ya to protect Monument resolution.

engines.title: Lesson Accumulation (GY Setup)
engines.body: Priority one is getting 3+ differently named Lessons into your GY. Abandon Attachments bins 2 at once. Firebending Lesson, Combustion Technique, Iroh's Demonstration, Boomerang Basics all count. This is the prerequisite for everything else. Actively cast cheap Lessons early even if they don't do much — you're fueling Gran-Gran and Accumulate Wisdom.

engines.title: Cost Reduction Active
engines.body: Gran-Gran (up to {3} reduction) + Artist's Talent Level 2 ({1} reduction) = up to {4} total cost reduction. In practice with 3 Lessons in GY: {2} from Gran-Gran + {1} from Talent = {3}. Monument costs {0}. Accumulate Wisdom costs {0}. Get both discount engines active before deploying Monument for maximum efficiency.

engines.title: Monument Loop
engines.body: Monument active + Artist's Talent Level 1 + spells in hand = the kill engine. Each spell triggers Talent (discard) which gives you a Monument activation. Three spells = 3 activations = choose from: 9 damage, 3 Treasures (3 mana), 3 cards, or any combination. The correct mode depends on your board state — Treasure when you need mana, damage when they're at 9 or below, draw when you need gas.

engines.title: Monument Deals 18-24 Damage in 2 Turns
engines.body: T4 Monument resolves. T5: Cast Accumulate Wisdom (free, draw 3) → Monument ping 3. Cast Firebending Lesson (free) → Monument ping 3. Cast Combustion Technique (free) → Monument ping 3. Total: 9 damage T5. On their T5 turn they cast something → you hold It'll Quench Ya, they spend {3}, Monument doesn't trigger OR they cast something else → another 3 damage. T6 you cast 3 more spells → 9 more damage

engines.title: Drawing 12+ Cards Per Game
engines.body: 4 copies × 3 cards each = 12 cards drawn from Wisdom alone. With cost reduction active, each Wisdom costs {0}. You can cast multiple Wisdoms per turn when you have the mana or Treasure tokens from Monument. A full Wisdom chain (all 4 copies in one extended game) means you've seen an additional 12 cards — nearly half the deck — in addition to normal draws.

engines.title: Monument Triggers ONCE Per Activation — You Choose the Mode
engines.body: Monument to Endurance's activated ability is: {T}: discard a card, then choose one — draw a card, create a Treasure, or opponent loses 3 life. This is ONE activation per tap. Artist's Talent Level 1 says "whenever you cast a spell, discard a card" — that discard does NOT automatically trigger Monument. Monument requires you to TAP it as an activated ability. Artist's Talent gives you the discard t

engines.title: Gran-Gran Discount Counts DIFFERENTLY Named Lessons
engines.body: Gran-Gran reduces spell costs by {1} for each DIFFERENTLY named Lesson card in your GY. Having 4 Firebending Lessons in GY = {1} discount (they're all the same name). Having Firebending Lesson + Combustion Technique + Iroh's Demonstration = {3} discount (3 differently named). Your 5 Lesson card types (Firebending, Combustion, Iroh's, Abandon Attachments, Boomerang Basics) are all differently named

engines.title: It'll Quench Ya Counters Spells Unless {3} — Not Just {1}
engines.body: It'll Quench Ya! costs {U} and counters target spell unless its controller pays {3}. This is a "soft counter" — opponents CAN pay {3} to get through it. Against Monument to Endurance on T3 (they cast for {3}): hold It'll Quench Ya but recognize they CAN pay {3} to force it through. The best use is against cheap removal like Annul ({U}) or Abrade ({1}{R}) where paying {3} extra is prohibitive. Don'

engines.title: Resource Grind
engines.body: Set up your engine, draw cards, stay ahead on resources. Don't rush Monument — deploy it when you have It'll Quench Ya backup or they're tapped out. You win by having more cards than they have answers. Gran-Gran + Accumulate Wisdom generates 3+ card advantage per turn.

engines.title: Reactive Control
engines.body: Hold Firebending Lesson, Combustion Technique, and Iroh's Demonstration as interaction rather than deploying them for Lesson count. Answer their key threats before they can pressure you. Gran-Gran's 1/3 body blocks early aggression. Iroh's Demonstration wipes token boards.

engines.title: Monument Kill Machine
engines.body: Once Monument is active and they're at 12 or below, switch all Monument modes to Damage. Three activations per turn at 3 damage each = 9 per turn. They die in 2 more turns. Cast spells specifically to generate Monument activations rather than for their effect.

engines.title: They're at 12 or Below With Monument Active
engines.body: Three Monument activations at 3 damage each = 9 damage. From 12 life, two full turns of three activations each = dead. Switch ALL Monument modes to Damage once they're at 12. Don't take Treasure or Draw — every activation must deal damage until they're dead.

engines.title: Aggro Has Early Board Presence
engines.body: When Boros Aggro or Izzet Prowess has a 4-6 power board by T3, don't try to set up your engine. Use your Lesson spells as removal (Firebending Lesson kills 2-toughness creatures for free), use Iroh's Demonstration to sweep their board, and only deploy Monument when the board is stabilized.

engines.title: Pyroclasm + Abrade + Torch the Tower
engines.body: Anti-aggro package. Pyroclasm kills every 1-toughness creature for {1}{R}. Abrade destroys artifacts (hits Monument in the mirror, hits their equipment) or deals 3 damage to a creature. Torch the Tower exiles on death — prevents creature recursion. Board all three vs Izzet Prowess and Boros Aggro.

engines.title: Soul-Guide Lantern ×2
engines.body: Exiles opponent's GY — devastating in the mirror (removes their Lesson discount) and vs any GY-based deck. Also a {1} artifact that can fuel Monument activations. Board in: mirror, any GY deck. Consider vs Dimir Midrange to exile their Enduring Curiosity recursion targets.

engines.title: Negate ×2 + Spell Pierce + Annul
engines.body: Counter package. Negate hits noncreature spells hard — counters Monument, enchantments, sorceries. Spell Pierce is cheap but conditional (pay {2}). Annul is hard-counters artifacts and enchantments for {U}. Board the package vs control and in the mirror where you need stack interaction beyond It'll Quench Ya.

engines.title: Quantum Riddler ×2 + Broadside Barrage
engines.body: Late-game threat package. Quantum Riddler generates card advantage every turn it attacks (surveil 2, draw a card with 2+ instants/sorceries in GY — trivially met). Board vs control and midrange where the game goes long. Broadside Barrage deals 5 damage to a creature/planeswalker for {2}{R}{R} while drawing a card — premium removal for hard-to-kill threats.

engines.title: Abandon Attachments + It'll Quench Ya
engines.body: Abandon Attachments is a slow sorcery-speed card that doesn't interact with their board. It'll Quench Ya doesn't stop creatures. Against fast aggro, these are your weakest cards — out first.

engines.title: Iroh's + Firebending Lesson + Combustion
engines.body: Removal spells are weak vs control (no creatures to kill) and less relevant in the mirror (their only creature is Gran-Gran, 1/3). Cut the lower-impact removal and bring in stack interaction and threats.

engines.title: Gran-Gran + Monument + Accumulate Wisdom
engines.body: The core engine. Never cut Gran-Gran (4), Monument (4), or Accumulate Wisdom (4) in any configuration. These are the reason the deck works. Everything else is support.

engines.title: Pyroclasm Threshold
engines.body: Pyroclasm ({1}{R}) deals 2 damage to each creature. You deploy it when they have 3+ creatures at 2 or less toughness. Your key calculation: which of your own creatures survive Pyroclasm? Your Eddymurk Crab (0/4) survives (4 toughness). Your Artist's Talent (enchantment, not creature) survives. The Pyroclasm threshold is 3 opponent creatures — below that, point removal is more efficient.

engines.title: Field is Creatures and Midrange
engines.body: Izzet Lessons is built to beat creature decks — your 30+ noncreature spells make their removal dead. Dimir Midrange, Boros Aggro, Mono-Green, and Bant Rhythm are all matchups where you're drawing 3 cards for free while they have Shoot the Sheriff in hand with no targets. Register when you expect 60%+ of the field to be creature-based strategies.

engines.title: Mirror and Control Are Heavy
engines.body: In a field heavy with Izzet Lessons mirrors and Jeskai Control, both of which can answer Monument efficiently, your SB needs to be heavily skewed toward the mirror and counter-heavy configurations. This is also when Quantum Riddler becomes more important than Pyroclasm in the 15.

engines.title: Context Dependent
engines.body: Manfield's list runs 1. More copies mean more Monument protection and tempo plays, but the deck needs Lesson density for discount. 1 is the minimum. Run 2 if you expect a lot of Mirror and control. The Lesson subtype matters — each copy in GY counts toward Gran-Gran discount.

engines.title: GY Engine Fuel
engines.body: Manfield's list runs 3 main + 1 SB. 4 main is viable in a wide-open meta where you need the GY setup as fast as possible. 3 is correct when you expect matchups where holding interaction is better than binning cards on T2.

engines.title: Meta Dependent Sweeper
engines.body: Manfield runs 3 main + 1 SB. In aggro-heavy metas, run 4 main. In control-heavy metas, move copies to SB or cut entirely — the sweeper does nothing against noncreature decks. The most meta-sensitive card in the deck.

engines.title: Discount Math by GY Count
engines.body: 0 Lessons in GY: no discount. 1 Lesson: {1} off. 2 Lessons: {2} off. 3+ Lessons: {3} off (max). Monument base cost {3}, at {3} discount = free. Accumulate Wisdom base {1}{U}, at {3} discount = free, draws 3. Firebending Lesson base {R}, at {3} discount = free with red available.

engines.title: Monument Kill Range
engines.body: 3 activations/turn × 3 damage = 9/turn. From 20 life: 3 turns to kill with Monument damage only. From 9 life: 1 activation kills them. Use damage mode when they're at 12 or below AND you have 4+ spells to cast (4 Monument activations = 12 damage = lethal from 12). Know this before game 1.

engines.title: Lesson Count by Name
engines.body: 5 differently named Lesson cards in the deck: Firebending Lesson (4), Combustion Technique (4), Iroh's Demonstration (3), Abandon Attachments (3), Boomerang Basics (1). Maximum Gran-Gran discount = {3} (after 3 different names in GY). You reach this by T3 routinely with Abandon Attachments on T2.

engines.title: SB Configuration
engines.body: Expected field aggro-heavy: +3 sweepers (Pyroclasm, Torch, Abrade) in SB at the expense of Negate/Quantum Riddler. Expected field control/mirror-heavy: +2 Negate, +2 Quantum Riddler, +2 Soul-Guide Lantern priority. Verify your 15 matches the expected meta breakdown before leaving.

engines.title: Talent Leveling
engines.body: Practice the Artist's Talent leveling sequence. Every instant/sorcery levels it up. Know exactly what each level does and when you're one trigger away from the next level.

engines.title: Lesson Selection
engines.body: Practice evaluating which Lesson to take in each game state. Field Trip (land) vs Introduction to Annihilation (exile) vs Expanded Anatomy (buff). The wrong Lesson choice is a subtle mistake that compounds.

engines.title: Accumulate Wisdom Chains
engines.body: Practice the Accumulate Wisdom draw chain. First cast draws 1. Second draws 2. Third draws 3. Know when to hold Wisdom for future casts vs cast it immediately for 1 card.

engines.title: Pyroclasm Windows
engines.body: Practice the Pyroclasm window: 3+ creatures at 2 toughness. Know which matchups generate the right board state and wait for the threshold rather than casting it early.

IzzetProwess.kill_turn: Your kill is faster than their combo assembly in most cases. Their plan requires: (1) pitchAtraxa, Grand Unifieror Griselbrand to Faithful Mending or Tainted Indulgence, then (2) resolve Goryo's Vengeance or Persist. That's a 2-card combo that needs turns 2-3. Your clock kills turns 3-4 consistently. The interaction point:Dragon's Rage Channeler's mandatory surveil mills cards into your graveyard — this also mills their cards if they overfill their hand. DRC with delirium attacks as a 3/3 flier for 3 per turn while they're setting up.
IzzetProwess.game_plan: Chapter 01 Identity & Philosophy "One spell triggers three threats. Two spells end the game." — Core Mantra Izzet Prowess is an aggro-combo hybrid that wins not through any single powerful card but through the density of interactions between cheap threats and cheap spells. Every noncreature spell simultaneously pumps your Monastery Swiftspear via prowess, surv1 sculpts your Dragon's Rage Channeler , advances your Cori-Steel Cutter 's Flurry threshold, and grows your Slickshot Show-Off. A single Lightning Bolt does four things at once. The deck's identity is spell density . You're not trying to
IzzetProwess.strengths: Fastest consistent clock in the format — killing on turn 3 or 4 is normal. Every spell does multiple things — efficient resource conversion per mana spent. Resilient to spot removal — threats replace themselves and chain into more. Expressive Iteration and Preordain provide best-in-class card selection.
IzzetProwess.weaknesses: Sanctifier en-Vec shuts off all red damage spells and makes Swiftspear/Slickshot/DRC ineligible for red-sourced removal. Sweepers ( Wrath of the Skies , Anger of the Gods) reset your board completely. Graveyard exile removes delirium — DRC reverts to 1/1 and Murktide loses counters. Running out of gas is real — the deck is aggressive but not inexhaustible.
IzzetProwess.mulligan:
Mulligan Philosophy

Snap keep: Any hand with 2 threats + 2 spells + 2 lands.

engines.title: The Prowess Package
engines.body: Monastery Swiftspear (1/2 haste, prowess) and Slickshot Show-Off (1/2 flying haste, +2/+0 per noncreature spell) are your primary attackers. Every noncreature spell turns these into serious damage dealers. With two spells in a turn, Slickshot is a 5/2 flying haste — often an 8+ damage swing before blocks are declared.

engines.title: Dragon's Rage Channeler
engines.body: {R} 1/1. Each noncreature spell you cast surv 1 — look at the top card, optionally put it in the graveyard. This actively builds toward delirium while filtering your draws. Delirium active: DRC becomes a 3/3 with flying that must attack each combat. Cannot be held back. Manage your graveyard types consciously.

engines.title: Cori-Steel Cutter
engines.body: {1}{R} equipment. Equipped creature gets +1/+1, trample, haste. Flurry: your second spell each turn creates a 1/1 Monk with prowess — you can immediately attach Cutter to it, giving it +1/+1, trample, haste. That Monk is now a 2/2 trampling haste attacker the same turn it was created, and it has prowess for further pumping. The threshold is the second spell, not the first.

engines.title: Mishra's BaubleSystem
engines.body: {0} artifact: tap + sacrifice to look at the top card of any player's library. Draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep — delayed, not now. Bauble is zero mana, triggers prowess on cast, is an artifact (counting toward delirium), and provides a free delayed card. Four copies means you have four 0-mana spell chains and four guaranteed artifact card types for delirium.

engines.title: What You Do Well
engines.body: Fastest consistent clock in the format — killing on turn 3 or 4 is normal. Every spell does multiple things — efficient resource conversion per mana spent. Resilient to spot removal — threats replace themselves and chain into more. Expressive Iteration and Preordain provide best-in-class card selection.

engines.title: What Beats You
engines.body: Sanctifier en-Vec shuts off all red damage spells and makes Swiftspear/Slickshot/DRC ineligible for red-sourced removal. Sweepers ( Wrath of the Skies , Anger of the Gods) reset your board completely. Graveyard exile removes delirium — DRC reverts to 1/1 and Murktide loses counters. Running out of gas is real — the deck is aggressive but not inexhaustible.

engines.title: Mishra's Bauble
engines.body: {0} artifact: tap + sacrifice to look at top of any player's library. Draw a card at the beginning of next turn's upkeep — not now. The delayed draw means you're always going to be one card ahead the following turn. More importantly: it's zero mana, it's an artifact (delirium card type), and casting it triggers prowess. Four copies guarantees artifact type in graveyard by turn 1.

engines.title: Slickshot Show-Off
engines.body: {1}{R} 1/2 flying haste, +2/+0 per noncreature spell. Plot {1}{R}: pay and exile it from your hand, then cast it as a sorcery on a later turn without paying mana. The Plot mode lets you develop a threat for free on later turns. With delirium active, Slickshot swings in as a 5/2 or larger on the turn you cast just two spells. It attacks the same turn it enters — haste is always on.

engines.title: Murktide Regent
engines.body: {5}{U}{U} with Delve — exile instants/sorceries from your GY to reduce cost. Enters as a 3/3 flier with +1/+1 per instant/sorcery exiled with it. Grows by +1/+1 whenever any instant or sorcery leaves your GY — including cards exiled by Expressive Iteration. A Murktide cast with 5 cards exiled is a 8/8 flier. Even opponent removal triggering Murktide's growth is your upside.

engines.title: Mutagenic Growth
engines.body: {G/P}: pay G or 2 life. +2/+2 until end of turn. This is a free spell in the sense that you're paying life not mana — your mana stays untapped for more spells. Mutagenic Growth in response to removal keeps your threat alive and grows DRC/Swiftspear/Slickshot simultaneously. Never holding mana open for Growth is a common mistake — you can cast it at instant speed on their turn.

engines.title: Deploy + Survey
engines.body: Play a one-drop threat (DRC, Swiftspear) plus Mishra's Bauble if in hand. Bauble costs zero, puts an artifact in the graveyard immediately, triggers prowess, and gives you a card next turn upkeep. DRC surv 1 on Bauble cast starts graveyard sculpting toward delirium. By end of turn 1 you can already have instant + artifact in the yard.

engines.title: Establish Delirium
engines.body: Cast Preordain or Lava Dart to put a sorcery or instant in the yard, cracking a fetchland puts land in the yard. With Bauble already in the yard: artifact + sorcery + land + instant = delirium. DRC flips to a 3/3 flier at this point. Cast Cori-Steel Cutter and equip it to anything — now your attacker has +1/+1, trample, haste.

engines.title: Chain Spells
engines.body: This is the turn you're looking for. Two or three spells in one turn while attacking with a delirium DRC and a Cori-Steel Cutter -equipped threat. Lightning Bolt + Mutagenic Growth + attack = 3+2 from burn plus combat damage from a pumped, trampling creature. Slickshot as a 5/2 flying haste attacker. The chain damage often represents 12+ in one turn.

engines.title: Close or Murktide
engines.body: If the game goes past turn 3, Expressive Iteration refills and Murktide Regent provides a large threat that's hard to remove profitably. Murktide with 4 instants/sorceries exiled is a 7/7 flier for around 3 mana. Any removal they cast on Murktide also triggers its counter from instants/sorceries leaving the graveyard — it grows even as they try to kill it.

engines.title: T1 DRC or Swiftspear
engines.body: On the play, T1 Dragon’s Rage Channeler or Monastery Swiftspear is your highest-value opening. DRC on T1 starts surveiling to build delirium while applying pressure. On the play: always lead with a 1-drop threat. A land-pass on T1 means you’re a full turn behind the tempo game and your spells do less damage without a prowess/surveil trigger magnet on the board.

engines.title: Extra Card Finds the Kill Spell
engines.body: On the draw, the extra card often provides the burn spell that closes the game or the cantrip that finds it. Keep looser hands on the draw if they have a threat + any cantrip. Against aggro on the draw: Fatal Push or Lava Dart hands are keepable even without a T1 threat because you need to survive to T3 before your clock takes over.

engines.title: Burn to Face
engines.body: DRC and Swiftspear removed: pivot to burn plan. Lightning Bolt + Light Up the Stage + any damage spell = 8-10 damage from hand. At 20 life this closes in 2-3 turns without any creatures. The burn redundancy means creature removal never fully answers this deck — they’re only removing 5-6 prowess triggers, not the damage output itself.

engines.title: Rebuild with DRC Surveil
engines.body: Burn spells countered: rebuild via DRC’s surveil triggers. Each noncreature spell surveils 1 — dig through the deck for more threats. Murktide Regent in the GY as a finisher means even a swept board recovers to a 4/4+ flier in 2-3 spells. DRC surveil makes every card you draw a choice, not a topdeck.

engines.title: DRC + Delirium Surveil
engines.body: Dragon’s Rage Channeler with delirium active: surveil 1 whenever you cast a noncreature spell + gains flying and +2/+1. This is your primary engine — DRC surveiling finds threats, fills GY for Murktide, and grows the clock. Get to delirium (4 card types in GY) as fast as possible via fetch lands (land type), spells (instant + sorcery), and DRC itself (creature).

engines.title: Swiftspear + Spell Chain
engines.body: Monastery Swiftspear gets +1/+1 until EOT for each noncreature spell. Chain spells in one turn: Bolt + Dart + Preordain = Swiftspear is 4/5 until EOT. Attack before the chain if you need more power, or attack after to surprise with unexpected pump. Every spell you’d cast anyway grows Swiftspear for free.

engines.title: Murktide Regent Finisher
engines.body: Murktide Regent costs {2}{U} when enough instants/sorceries are in your GY. Each instant/sorcery in GY makes Murktide +1/+1. With 5 instants in GY, Murktide is a 7/7 flying for {2}{U}. This is the inevitability finisher when the early game stalls — survive to T3-4 and Murktide closes 3-4 attack steps from 20 life.

engines.title: T3 Delirium Online
engines.body: T1: DRC. T2: Fetch land (crack it: land type in GY) + Lightning Bolt (instant type). DRC is now 1/2. T3: Preordain (sorcery type) + DRC surveils. Delirium check: creature (DRC), instant (Bolt), sorcery (Preordain), land (fetch cracked). 4 types = delirium. DRC is now 3/3 flying. Swing T3 for 3, chain spells.

engines.title: T3 One-Turn Kill
engines.body: T1: Swiftspear. T2: Light Up the Stage ({R}: reveal cards, cast 2 for free). T3: Chain Bolt + Dart + Preordain + Mutagenic Growth (2 life) → Swiftspear is 5/6. Attack for 5. Bolt face for 3. Dart face for 1. Total: 9 from 20 life. T4 close. The fastest line requires Swiftspear + 4 spells + burn.

engines.title: Race vs Burn
engines.body: Attack aggressively: They’re below 12 life. Swing, chain burn. Finish with Bolt to face. Burn face: They have a 5/5 blocker but 8 life. Don’t attack into it. Dart (1) + Bolt (3) + Light Up the Stage → 2 more damage spells = 6+. Count damage from hand first.

engines.title: DRC Needs 4 Card TYPES for Delirium
engines.body: Dragon’s Rage Channeler’s Delirium requires 4 different card types in your graveyard, not 4 cards. Card types: Instant, Sorcery, Creature, Land, Artifact, Enchantment. The most common gap: you have Instant (Lightning Bolt), Creature (DRC), Land (from fetch) = 3 types. You need a SORCERY — Preordain or Serum Visions. Without a sorcery in GY, DRC is a vanilla 1/1. Surveil aggressively with DRC’s tri

engines.title: Monastery Swiftspear Prowess Triggers Stack
engines.body: Monastery Swiftspear gets +1/+1 until end of turn whenever you cast a noncreature spell. Each spell is a separate trigger. Cast Lightning Bolt + Mutagenic Growth + Preordain in one turn — Swiftspear gets 3 separate +1/+1 triggers = 4/5 until EOT. Triggers can be responded to individually and all still resolve. Chain spells before blocks to maximize Swiftspear’s combat size. Count before declaring

engines.title: Lava Dart Flashback Sacrifices a MOUNTAIN
engines.body: Lava Dart’s flashback cost is to sacrifice a Mountain — not just any land, specifically a Mountain-type land. Steam Vents is a Mountain (it has the Mountain land type). Scalding Tarn after fetching a Mountain leaves no Mountain on board. Basics: only basic Mountain counts. Count your Mountains before counting available Dart flashbacks. Never tap your last Mountain for mana if you need the Dart fla

engines.title: They Have a Clock You Can't Race
engines.body: Opponent presents a threat you can't ignore — a resolved Primeval Titan, a 5/5 Kappa Cannoneer, a Teferi with counters. Stop chaining spells for prowess pumps and deploy targeted removal. Unholy Heat with delirium active (6 damage) is your premium answer. Prioritize surviving over growing your threats.

engines.title: Their Life Total Is in Lethal Range
engines.body: Opponent is below 8 life and you have DRC or Swiftspear with spells in hand. Stop holding back for "better" lines — calculate pump math and attack. Mutagenic Growth + Lava Dart + one spell = 6+ damage from nothing. Commit when the math says lethal is available this turn.

engines.title: Delirium + Open Board
engines.body: Delirium is active, DRC is attacking with surveil, and they have no blockers. This is your highest-value position. Don't switch modes — keep casting spells to trigger prowess, keep flipping DRC to 3/3 surveil 1, keep piling on damage. The tempo advantage compounds with every spell.

engines.title: Read Their Opener
engines.body: Their T1 land tells you a lot: Island = likely counter suite, hold spells until they tap out. Mountain/Plains = aggro mirror or Boros, race them immediately. No land = potential mull to 6, press aggressively. Use this read to sequence your first two spells correctly — the right opener beats good hands by 20%.

engines.title: Race First
engines.body: T1 DRC, T2 Cori-Steel Cutter + spell (Flurry Monk), T3 Slickshot + Lightning Bolt . You're threatening 12+ damage by turn 3. They have to react to you, not the other way around. Keep Bolt for face not creatures unless Bombardment is online.

engines.title: Answer Ragavan
engines.body: They get to attack with Ragavan first. Kill it with Lava Dart (1 damage = dead Ragavan) before it connects and generates mana/card advantage. On the draw you're reacting first. Prioritize Dart on Ragavan over developing your own board.

engines.title: Kill Before Sanctifier
engines.body: You need to be threatening lethal before turn 2-3 when Sanctifier can resolve. T1 DRC, T2 chain spells, T3 attack for 10+. Sanctifier on T2 on the play is their strongest line — race it with maximum aggression.

engines.title: Hold Consign
engines.body: On the draw they may have T1 Guide of Souls + T2 Sanctifier. Consign to Memory counters the Sanctifier ETB triggered ability — when Sanctifier enters, its protection ability is a triggered ability that Consign can counter. Fire Consign to deny the protection, then race freely.

engines.title: Maximum Pressure
engines.body: T1 DRC, T2 delirium active + attack, T3 Slickshot Show-Off + 2 spells = 5/2 flier attacking for 7+. They're dead or nearly dead before Archon can matter. Apply maximum aggression — there's nothing for them to do to stop the clock.

engines.title: RespectThoughtseizeT1
engines.body: They can take your best card T1. Keep hands with 2 threats so Thoughtseize doesn't brick your opening. Even after losing your best card, cast everything else. Your second-best cards are still functional burn clock cards.

engines.title: Chain Into Open Mana
engines.body: They can't hold up Counterspell mana until turn 2. T1 DRC is uncounterable unless they have pitch Subtlety. Develop threats fast, then chain multiple spells in one turn to force them to spend multiple counters or let something through.

engines.title: Hold Consign for Teferi
engines.body: On the draw they hit Counterspell mana on turn 2 first. Develop cheap threats and hold Consign for Teferi, Time Raveler 's ETB bounce trigger — countering it denies both the bounce and the sorcery-speed lock. One Consign in the right moment swings the game.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Fair midrange field — your T1 clock demands immediate interaction. Low life-gain density (Rhox Faith Mender, Leyline of Sanctity shuts off burn). Combo decks present — your T2 DRC races their T3 combo. You have delirium path practiced for the top 5 matchups.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy lifegain meta (Soul-Warden, Leyline of Sanctity) — burn plan fails against life totals 30+. Multiple Supreme Verdict builds where your creature investment gets blanked. You haven’t practiced delirium management (4 card types) and fall behind on clock timing.

engines.title: Monastery Swiftspear ×4
engines.body: Your best T1. Four copies non-negotiable — Swiftspear pumping every spell cast is the engine that makes your clock consistent.

engines.title: Cori-Steel Cutter ×4
engines.body: The centerpiece of the deck. A 1/1 prowess token every turn cycle makes Cutter unkillable as a value engine. Never cut.

engines.title: Slickshot Show-Off
engines.body: 3 in most metas. 4 in control-heavy metas where the plot ability dodges their interaction and the haste attack closes from nowhere. Cut to 2 in aggro mirrors where 3-mana threats are too slow.

engines.title: Dragon's Rage Channeler
engines.body: 3 in metas where the delirium upgrade matters (the 3/3 flier). 2 in faster metas where DRC stays at 1/1 most games — swap for more 1-drop cantrips.

engines.title: Into the Flood Maw (SB)
engines.body: 2 SB copies in creature-heavy metas. Cut entirely in spell-based metas where bouncing creatures does nothing. Flood Maw bouncing two creatures at instant speed is your best tempo play vs wide boards.

engines.title: Spell Sequencing
engines.body: Cast all noncreature spells BEFORE attacking. Practice the order of spells each turn.

engines.title: DRC Delirium
engines.body: Track your GY types actively in every rep. Know when you have delirium and when you don't.

engines.title: Burn Math
engines.body: Count exact lethal from any board state. Know when Dart flashback + attack closes it.

engines.title: G2 Hate Navigation
engines.body: Play through Sanctifier en-Vec and Leyline of Sanctity. These are your worst post-board scenarios.

engines.title: Track Delirium Every Turn
engines.body: Know your graveyard card types at all times. DRC is a 1/1 or a 3/3 flier — that's a 12-point power difference over a game. Never be surprised by your own DRC state.

engines.title: Chain Spells Don't Trickle Them
engines.body: Three spells in one turn is exponentially better than three spells across three turns. The prowess chain compounds. Always look for the turn you can cast everything at once.

engines.title: Lava DartFlashback Costs a Mountain
engines.body: Not free. You lose a land. Count your lands before every Dart flashback. Never flash it back carelessly in turns 1-3 when you need your mana base for spells.

engines.title: Consign Targets Triggers Not Spells
engines.body: Consign counters triggered abilities and colorless spells. Cannot counter Lightning Bolt , Counterspell , or any colored spell. Know your targets before bringing it in.

matchups.notes: Burn Clock — faster than their kill
Spells kill their creatures + grow prowess simultaneously
Chalice at 1 shuts your deck — race before TKS hits
Sanctifier immune to your damage — race their clock
Kill turn 3-4 before reanimation — DRC mills their threats
Speed race — both kill turns 3-4, you're slightly faster

IZZETSPELLEMENTALS.kill_turn: REFERENCEThe Boulder — PT Lorwyn Eclipsed design
IZZETSPELLEMENTALS.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "Your creatures are Elementals and your Elementals care about spells. Every spell you cast does double duty — it's an interaction piece AND a board pump." Izzet Spellementals was designed by The Boulder team for Pro Tour Lorwyn Eclipsed 2026, where it posted an extremely high win rate against Badgermole Cub strategies. The deck sits at 5.26% of Standard and is the premier Elemental-tribal midrange strategy in the format. The core engine: Ashling, Rekindled is a legendary Elemental that triggers on ETB — discard a card, if you do draw a card. With Roaming Throne naming
IZZETSPELLEMENTALS.mulligan:
Mulligan Framework

Keep: Any 7 with Roaming Throne + 2 Elementals + 3 lands.

engines.title: Roaming Throne: Double Elemental Triggers
engines.body: Roaming Throne enters and you choose a creature type — choose Elemental. Now whenever an Elemental you control triggers an ability, that ability triggers an additional time. Ashling's "discard a card, draw a card" ETB triggers TWICE → net: discard 2, draw 2. All your Elemental ETBs double. Sunderflock's damage doubles. Flamebraider's triggers double. Roaming Throne effectively makes every Elementa

engines.title: Sunderflock as a Board Wipe
engines.body: Sunderflock is an Elemental that deals damage to each creature an opponent controls equal to the number of Elementals you control or the number of Elemental spells you've cast this turn. With Roaming Throne doubling the trigger: the damage fires twice. Against go-wide decks, this wipes their entire board while your Elementals survive (they don't deal damage to creatures you control). With 4 Elemen

engines.title: Set Up the Doubler
engines.body: T1: Vibrance or Wistfulness to filter/develop. T2: Roaming Throne (choose Elemental). Throne on T2 means every Elemental you cast afterward has doubled triggers. If Throne isn't in hand, deploy Flamebraider or Wistfulness to build board presence. Cavern of Souls naming Elemental ensures Throne and Ashling can't be countered.

engines.title: Ashling Engine Online
engines.body: T3: Ashling, Rekindled with Throne active → discard 2, draw 2 (double trigger) on ETB. Your hand cycles through itself efficiently. T4: Pay {U} at beginning of first main phase to transform Ashling into Rimebound for additional value. Deploy Flamebraider or more spells to build Elemental count for Sunderflock.

engines.title: Sunderflock Wipe
engines.body: With 3+ Elementals on board, Sunderflock deals 3+ damage to each creature they control. With Roaming Throne: that trigger fires twice → 6+ damage to each creature. Their board is wiped. Your Elementals survive (Sunderflock targets only opponent's creatures). Attack for lethal on an empty board.

engines.title: Deceit + Beza Grind
engines.body: When Sunderflock isn't the right play, Deceit provides early interaction (Distress + bounce). Beza, the Bounding Spring generates creatures and life gain on ETB — with Roaming Throne, Beza's Elemental trigger fires twice. Winter Stories discards to generate advantage. This grindy line wins in attrition matchups where sweepers aren't needed.

engines.title: Ashling + Roaming Throne
engines.body: Ashling ETB: discard, draw. Throne doubles it: discard 2, draw 2. Net: hand stays the same size while cycling your whole hand. You filter aggressively looking for Sunderflock, lands, or key pieces. Deploy Ashling multiple times (bounce with Bounce Off and redeploy) to cycle repeatedly.

engines.title: Sunderflock Sweep
engines.body: Sunderflock deals damage equal to Elementals on board. With Throne: double that. With 4 Elementals: 8 damage to each of their creatures. Their Prowess Otters (1/1-3/3), Badgermole Cubs (2/2), and spiders (1/2) all die. Your Elementals don't. You swing for lethal on an empty board the same turn or next turn.

engines.title: Vibrance + Wistfulness Flood
engines.body: Vibrance and Wistfulness are cheap instants/sorceries that draw cards and/or generate card advantage. They fill the graveyard, enable Eclipsed Realms (a land that does something with instants/sorceries in GY), and keep your hand full. Run all 8 copies to maintain card advantage even without Ashling online.

engines.title: Board Control Then Swing
engines.body: Build your Elemental board, double triggers with Throne, wipe their board with Sunderflock, attack into empty opposition. This is the main win pattern. You're the control player in aggro matchups and the aggro player against control.

engines.title: Ashling Grind
engines.body: When Sunderflock isn't right, grind with Ashling + Throne card advantage. Cycle your hand repeatedly, find your best cards, outvalue their engine. Beza and Winternight Stories contribute to the grind. You win through card quantity.

engines.title: Tempo Through Deceit
engines.body: Strip their key spell with Deceit (Distress mode) or bounce their key permanent (bounce mode for MV ≤ 2 permanents). Use Bounce Off for tempo. Deploy Sunderflock as a threat they have to answer. Sometimes you win through tempo rather than a clean combo.

engines.title: Soul-Guide Lantern ×2
engines.body: Graveyard hate that also cycles. In against Izzet Lessons (Monument to Endurance fuel), any GY-based strategy. The ETB exiles one card; the sacrifice exiles their whole GY. Cheap enough to cast alongside your threats.

engines.title: Disdainful Stroke ×2
engines.body: Counter MV 4+ spells for 2 mana. Hits their sweepers (Day of Judgment, Avatar's Wrath), their Monument to Endurance, their Ouroboroid. Boards in vs any control or combo deck where their key spells cost 4+.

engines.title: Pyroclasm ×1
engines.body: 2 damage to each creature. Sweeps Izzet Prowess tokens (1/1 Otters), Boros 1-drops, Mono-White lifelinkers. Boards in vs any go-wide token strategy. Triggers your prowess creatures if you have any and also counts as a spell for Hearth Elemental's cost reduction.

engines.title: Hydro-Man, Fluid Felon ×2
engines.body: Flexible answer to problem permanents. Boards in vs decks with key noncreature permanents you need to bounce. Check oracle text for exact targeting restrictions before boarding in.

engines.title: Glacial Dragonhunt
engines.body: The narrowest main deck card. A sorcery that deals damage to each creature without flying — useful against ground aggro but too slow against most of the current meta. First card out in almost every SB configuration.

engines.title: Winternight Stories
engines.body: The card advantage enchantment is great in fair matchups but slow against aggro. Trim 2 copies when you need interactive answers. Keep at least 1 in against control for the grind.

engines.title: Spell Pierce
engines.body: Effective early but loses value late. Trim vs aggro (they run few spells you need to counter) and vs decks with cheap spells that pay through easily. Keep vs control and combo.

engines.title: Glacial Dragonhunt Timing
engines.body: Glacial Dragonhunt ({2}{U}) counters an attacking creature until EOT AND you may put a 2/2 flying Dragon token onto the battlefield. You deploy it at their attack step when their biggest attacker is declared. The countered attacker is removed from combat — they don't deal combat damage. You also get a 2/2 Dragon for free. Timing: you must cast it after they declare attackers but before blockers. Y

engines.title: 4 Cavern of Souls + 4 Roaming Throne
engines.body: These are why you play Spellementals over other Elemental strategies. Cavern makes your threats uncounterable. Throne doubles every ETB trigger. The deck doesn't function without both at 4 copies. Any list that cuts either is a different deck.

engines.title: 4 Ashling, Rekindled + 4 Sunderflock
engines.body: Ashling is the engine (ETB: discard 2, draw 2 with Throne). Sunderflock is the board wipe and finisher (doubles with Throne). These are your 8 power cards. Full playset of both is mandatory.

engines.title: Winternight Stories
engines.body: Excellent in fair matchups, slow against aggro. Run 2-3 in control-heavy metas, 1-2 in aggro-heavy fields. The passive card advantage over multiple turns outgrows sweepers.

engines.title: Bounce Off
engines.body: Protects Ashling (draw a card) and provides tempo. Run 2 in metas with high-value permanents to bounce (Sapling Nursery, Roaming Throne in mirror). 1 is fine in aggro-heavy fields.

engines.title: Glacial Dragonhunt
engines.body: Ground creature sweeper with flying exemption. Cut in almost every non-aggro meta. The only reason to run it: a field of Mono-Green Landfall and Boros Aggro where you need another sweeper.

engines.title: Midrange + Control Are Popular
engines.body: Cavern of Souls is at maximum value against Dimir Midrange and Jeskai Control — both rely heavily on counterspells. If the field is these two archetypes plus fair creature decks, Spellementals is well-positioned with free-casting Elementals and Throne doubling everything.

engines.title: Izzet Prowess Is Dominant
engines.body: Your speed disadvantage vs Prowess means a Prowess-heavy field is rough. If more than 15% of the expected field is Prowess, consider Mono-Green Landfall or Izzet Lessons which have better Prowess matchups.

engines.title: Cantrip Chain Efficiency
engines.body: You chain cantrips at instant speed to maximize Hearth Elemental cost reduction. Each elemental in play reduces Hearth's cost by {1}. With Eddymurk Crab + another elemental in play (2 elementals), Hearth costs {2} less. You build elemental count via cantripping into Crab and Dreadhorde Arcanist before deploying Hearth.

engines.title: Sunderflock Timing
engines.body: Your Sunderflock is sorcery speed — you cast it at the beginning of your main phase, never during combat. You wait for them to commit their full board (3+ creatures) before casting. Against token strategies: Sunderflock at 4 damage kills all their 2-toughness tokens simultaneously. You count toughness values before casting.

engines.title: Disdainful Stroke Targets
engines.body: Your Disdainful Stroke hits MV ≥ 4. You know which cards in their deck cost 4+ before they cast anything. Against Jeskai Control: their board wipes and planeswalkers. Against Dimir Excruciator: their Harbinger (MV 3? — check. If MV 3, Stroke misses; use Negate instead). Know your Stroke targets by matchup before game 1.

engines.title: Abrade Mode Selection
engines.body: Your Abrade has two modes: 3 damage to creature OR destroy artifact. You decide which mode before casting — never commit to mode A when mode B is correct. Against Izzet Prowess: mode A kills Monastery Swiftspear (1/2). Against Boros Aggro: mode B destroys their key artifact. Default to mode A unless mode B is clearly superior.

engines.title: Cast Before Hearth Elemental
engines.body: You chain cantrips at instant speed to build your elemental count before deploying Hearth Elemental. With 2 elementals in play, Hearth costs {2} less. Your T3 goal: have 2 elementals → deploy Hearth at {0} or {1}.

engines.title: Sorcery Speed Means After Blockers
engines.body: Sunderflock is sorcery speed — you cast it in your first main phase when their board has 3+ creatures. Never during combat. You commit to Sunderflock when counting their creatures guarantees a full sweep at 4-5 damage.

engines.title: MV 4+ Only
engines.body: Disdainful Stroke counters MV ≥ 4. You pre-identify their MV 4+ threats before game 1: their board wipes, their win conditions, their expensive counters. You never use Stroke on a MV ≤ 3 spell — you hold it for their key MV 4+ card.

engines.title: Check Board Before Casting
engines.body: Mode A: 3 damage to a creature. Mode B: destroy an artifact. You decide before casting based on their board. If they have both a key artifact and a key creature: prioritize the artifact (removal handles the creature). You commit to a mode when you tap mana.

engines.title: Sunderflock Damage Math
engines.body: 3 Elementals + Throne = 6 damage each. 4 Elementals + Throne = 8 damage each. 2 Elementals + Throne = 4 damage each (kills most 4-toughness creatures with a Burst Lightning follow-up). Know these by reflex before sitting down.

engines.title: Cavern Only Protects Creature Spells
engines.body: Roaming Throne is an artifact spell — casting it off Cavern mana does NOT make it uncounterable (Cavern only applies to creature spells of the named type). Cast Throne with open mana to protect it. Bounce Off in response to their counter saves it.

engines.title: Hearth Elemental Cost Reduction
engines.body: Hearth Elemental costs {1} less for each instant/sorcery in your GY. At 4 spells in GY it's {R} — essentially free. Count your GY spells before every main phase to know what Hearth currently costs. Missing a free 3/4 with haste is a significant play error.

engines.title: SB for Expected Meta
engines.body: Check the current meta breakdown. Soul-Guide Lantern in against every GY deck. Annul and Disdainful Stroke in against control. Pyroclasm and Abrade in against aggro. Confirm your 15 before heading out.

engines.title: Cantrip Chain Into Hearth
engines.body: Practice chaining cantrips until Hearth Elemental is in play. The chain: Opt â†’ consider casting efficiency as each elemental reduces costs. Know when you have critical mass.

engines.title: Eddymurk Flash Timing
engines.body: Practice flashing Eddymurk at their attack step. Always flash, never main phase. The tap-on-ETB is the entire value of this card â€” it prevents one attack for free.

engines.title: Sunderflock Decision
engines.body: Practice deciding when to deploy Sunderflock. 3+ creatures at 3 toughness or less: Sunderflock. 1-2 creatures: hold Sunderflock and use a cheaper answer. Know the threshold.

engines.title: Counter Targets
engines.body: Practice identifying the correct Disdainful Stroke target by matchup. Jeskai: board wipe (MV 4+). Dimir Excruciator: Harbinger of the Seas (MV 3... wait, that's not Disdainful). Know the exact MV of their key threats.

JeskaiBlink.game_plan: Chapter 01 Identity & Philosophy "Don't just answer their threats — answer their turns. Every Consign, every Phantom bounce, every Phelia blink steals a turn they never get back." — Core Mantra Jeskai Blink is a tempo-control hybrid that wins by accruing incremental advantages until the opponent runs out of resources — then closing with a board that has quietly outgrown everything they can produce. It is not a combo deck. It is not pure control. It occupies the intersection: proactive enough to pressure combo decks, disruptive enough to grind aggro decks out, and resilient enough to out-value
JeskaiBlink.strengths: High skill ceiling — reps compound into percentage points. Resilient to hate — pivots into fair midrange when graveyard hate lands. Consign to Memory is the most versatile counter in the format. Inevitability in every long game through engine redundancy.
JeskaiBlink.weaknesses: Decision density punishes hesitation and over-thinking. Very fast aggro on stumbles — Prowess can kill before you stabilize. Torpor Orb and Void Mirror shut off ETB engines entirely. Tournament clock — brisk play is mandatory, not optional.
JeskaiBlink.mulligan:
Mulligan Philosophy

Snap keep: Any hand with Guide of Souls or Ocelot Pride + 2 mana sources including white + one relevant interaction piece (Solitude, Consign, Ephemerate).

engines.title: Tempo Denial
engines.body: White Orchid Phantom denies land drops on entry and reblinks to lock mana. Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd exiles a nonland permanent when she attacks — it returns at end of turn, denying it for that combat. Consign to Memory counters triggered abilities and colorless spells — Summoner’s Pact upkeep triggers, cascade triggers, Archon ETB triggers — buying decisive tempo at zero mana cost. You reach int

engines.title: Flexible Interaction
engines.body: Solitude , Prismatic Ending , and Wrath of the Skies answer almost everything in Modern. Solitude + Ephemerate is the premier 2-for-1 — exile two creatures for one card. The interaction suite is never locked into a single axis and can answer any permanent type the format produces.

engines.title: Resilient Engines
engines.body: Guide of Souls + Ocelot Pride generates inevitability that grinds past removal suites. Quantum Riddler and Starfield Shepherd refill the hand. Once engines are live, the deck is extremely difficult to exhaust — they need an answer to the threat and an answer to the refill, simultaneously.

engines.title: Role Flexibility
engines.body: Acts as control vs Aggro (stabilize, then engine), tempo vs Combo (one critical disruption turn then clock), and proactive pressure vs Control (jam threats, force answers). No other archetype in Modern shifts roles this cleanly within a single game state.

engines.title: What You Do Well
engines.body: High skill ceiling — reps compound into percentage points. Resilient to hate — pivots into fair midrange when graveyard hate lands. Consign to Memory is the most versatile counter in the format. Inevitability in every long game through engine redundancy.

engines.title: What Beats You
engines.body: Decision density punishes hesitation and over-thinking. Very fast aggro on stumbles — Prowess can kill before you stabilize. Torpor Orb and Void Mirror shut off ETB engines entirely. Tournament clock — brisk play is mandatory, not optional.

engines.title: Deploy Pressure
engines.body: Guide of Souls or Ocelot Pride on turn 1 or 2. These are not just threats — they are energy and token generators that make every subsequent turn better. Never hold them to "protect" them. Deploy and start accruing. Even a Pride that generates two cats before dying has done its job.

engines.title: Establish the Lock
engines.body: White Orchid Phantom on turn 2 or 3 destroys their best nonbasic land on entry — their controller may search for a tapped basic as replacement. Repeatedly blinking Phantom strips every fetchland and shockland, forcing them onto basics. Against Amulet Titan this collapses their bounce-land mana. Against 3-color decks it cuts off color fixing. If they’re already on basics, use Phantom as a 2/2 flyin

engines.title: Deploy Engines
engines.body: Quantum Riddler and Starfield Shepherd go here. Riddler starts generating card advantage the turn it enters. Shepherd generates Shepherd tokens and refills on blink. The more engines in play simultaneously, the more overwhelming the value generation becomes — they cannot answer all of them.

engines.title: Convert to Inevitability
engines.body: Your engines are now out-generating their answers. Teferi postboard locks them into sorcery speed. Consign holds up as the trump to any free spell or combo piece. At this point in the game, you are winning — the only question is whether you've correctly identified what they need to win and held the right answer for it.

engines.title: T2 Solitude on Their Threat
engines.body: On the play, T2 evoke Solitude to exile their key T1 threat (Ragavan, Thoughtseize target, Swiftspear) is your highest-value early play. Evoke costs only a white card from hand. On the play: always have a Solitude target plan before T2. Follow with Ephemerate in your hand to keep Solitude as a 5/5 and generate a second exile ETB.

engines.title: Hold Ephemerate for Response
engines.body: On the draw, hold Ephemerate mana open through their T2 to respond to whatever they deploy. The extra card on draw often provides the second ETB piece you need. Against aggro on the draw: Solitude T1 (if you can pay the evoke cost) is the priority to not fall behind on board.

engines.title: Switch to Solitude Tempo
engines.body: Teferi killed: opponents can now interact at instant speed again. Shift to reactive mode: hold Solitude + Ephemerate mana, deploy on their turn when they tap out. Without Teferi’s sorcery-speed lock, you play a more traditional draw-go game — your flash pieces still generate value.

engines.title: Rebuild with Teferi
engines.body: Solitude/Restoration Angel removed: rebuild via Teferi’s -3 (return their threat to library) and +1 (draw + sorcery flash). Teferi generates value without creatures in play. A resolved Teferi with no creatures is still a slow clock via loyalty counters and ultimate.

engines.title: Your Core Combo Piece
engines.body: Ephemerate ({W}) blinks a permanent you control (flicker to exile and return immediately) with rebound (cast again for free next upkeep). You blink Solitude on their attack step to remove their biggest creature for free. You blink your own Aven Interrupter to get a second ETB counter trigger. You blink Eternal Witness to recur Ephemerate from GY. One Ephemerate generates multiple triggers.

engines.title: Your Free Path Clearer
engines.body: Solitude ({3}{W}{W}) ETB exiles a creature. You evoke it for free by pitching a white card — Ephemerate, a basic Plains, any white card. Evoking Solitude on their attack step removes their best attacker for zero mana. You follow by attacking into their smaller creatures. The evoke clause makes Solitude your best mana-efficiency play in the format.

engines.title: Your Free Counter
engines.body: Subtlety ({2}{U}{U}) ETB puts a creature or planeswalker spell back on top of their library. You evoke it for free by pitching a blue card. Against their T3 Sheoldred: pitch a blue card, Subtlety ETB, Sheoldred goes to top of their library (not hand — they LOSE the card for a turn). You apply clock while they redraw a card they've already seen.

engines.title: Your Post-Board Mode
engines.body: In games 2-3 you know their hate cards and adapt accordingly. Against Grafdigger's Cage (stops ETB of creatures from non-GY): your Ephemerate still works (flicker doesn't use the GY). Against Leyline of the Void: your Eternal Witness strategy is offline — pivot to Solitude + Subtlety as standalone pieces. Know exactly what each hate card does to your engine before sideboarding.

engines.title: Evoke + Ephemerate Loop
engines.body: Evoke Solitude/Fury + Ephemerate (save creature before sacrifice trigger) = the primary engine. This generates a free exile ETB, keeps a 5/5, and Ephemerate rebounds for a second blink next upkeep. Two exile effects from one evoke + one Ephemerate. Deploy every time you have both pieces and a relevant target.

engines.title: Teferi Sorcery Lock
engines.body: Teferi, Time Raveler on the board locks opponents to sorcery speed. Every spell you cast is immune to instant-speed interaction. +1 draws a card and bounces a noncreature. -3 puts their threat on top of their library. Teferi is simultaneously protection, removal, and a card engine — protect him once he’s resolved.

engines.title: Restoration Angel / Quantum Riddler
engines.body: Restoration Angel blinks any non-Angel creature you control at instant speed, triggering ETBs. Quantum Riddler generates card draw on each blink. These are your value engines in longer games where the evoke combo isn’t available. Chain Angel + blink targets to generate multiple ETBs per turn.

engines.title: T2-3 Tempo Swing
engines.body: T2: Evoke Solitude (exile white card) → ETB exiles their key creature. In response to sacrifice trigger: Ephemerate ({W}) → Solitude exiles, returns at end of step as a 5/5. Rebound next upkeep: Ephemerate blinks Solitude again → second exile ETB. Net: 2 exile effects + a 5/5 for the cost of a white card + {W}.

engines.title: The Grind Finisher
engines.body: Teferi +1 each turn: draw a card. -3 when they develop a threat: put it on top of their library (they re-draw it, gain no tempo). Teferi’s ultimate (−10): for each instant/sorcery in your GY, create a 2/2 Wizard. A Teferi that ultimates wins the game immediately via Wizard tokens. Teferi can also win just by bouncing their threats repeatedly while you draw ahead.

engines.title: Hold vs Deploy Teferi
engines.body: Deploy immediately: Vs aggro or when they have no counterspells visible. Teferi at sorcery speed, protected by open Solitude mana. Hold: Vs heavy counter decks. Wait until they tap out for their own spell, then deploy Teferi into their empty mana. Counter their counter with Consign to Memory.

engines.title: Your Blink Chain
engines.body: Ephemerate ({W}) blinks your permanent (exile and return immediately) with rebound (free cast next upkeep). You target your own ETB creatures: Solitude (second exile ETB), Eternal Witness (returns Ephemerate from GY), Aven Interrupter (second counter ETB). Your payoff: one Ephemerate generates two ETB triggers from one card. The rebound means every Ephemerate generates value again next turn.

engines.title: Your Recursion Engine
engines.body: Eternal Witness (2/1 ETB: return any card from your GY to hand). You blink Witness with Ephemerate: Witness ETB again → returns Ephemerate from GY → Ephemerate rebounds next upkeep → blink Witness again. Your loop: each cycle returns one card from your GY indefinitely. You use this to recur your best counterspell, your best removal, or another Ephemerate. You generate infinite value from a single

engines.title: Your Free Interaction
engines.body: Solitude and Subtlety both have evoke costs (exile a white or blue card respectively instead of paying full mana). You evoke them for zero mana, triggering their ETB effects. Solitude ETB exiles a creature — you exile their best threat for free. Subtlety ETB puts their creature spell on top of library — you counter their best creature for free. Your payoff: you apply interaction at zero mana cost,

engines.title: Your Protection Suite
engines.body: Your counter suite protects your own key permanents as much as it counters their threats. You hold Force of Negation (exile a blue card: counter any noncreature spell) specifically for when they try to answer your resolved Ephemerate engine. You hold Spell Pierce for their key instant-speed interaction. Your payoff: your engine pieces are protected, their answers are countered, and you generate ad

engines.title: Evoke + Ephemerate Saves the Creature
engines.body: When you evoke Solitude, the ETB trigger (exile a creature) goes on the stack. THEN the evoke sacrifice trigger goes on the stack. Before the sacrifice trigger resolves, Ephemerate the creature. Solitude exiles, returns at end of step. The sacrifice trigger resolves but the creature is already in exile/returning — it survives. Solitude returns as a full 5/5 with no sacrifice pending, and Ephemerat

engines.title: Teferi Locks Opponents to Sorcery Speed
engines.body: Teferi, Time Raveler’s static: opponents can’t cast spells or activate abilities except during their own main phase (sorcery speed). This means: no instant-speed removal, no Force of Negation on your spells, no Vial activations at flash speed, no Endurance flash. While Teferi is in play, every spell you cast is protected from instant-speed interaction. Cast your threats on your main phase — they r

engines.title: Prismatic Ending MV Scales With Colors Spent
engines.body: Prismatic Ending’s domain: it exiles a permanent with MV less than or equal to the number of basic land types among lands you control when you cast it. With 3 colors (Jeskai: W, U, R) = exiles MV ≤ 3. Add a green source (Triome) = MV ≤ 4. The land types are BASIC land types, not lands themselves — your Hallowed Fountain counts as Island + Plains. Scalding Tarn fetching basic Mountain adds R type.

engines.title: Your Ephemerate Blink Line
engines.body: You cast Ephemerate ({W}) targeting your own Solitude — Solitude ETB triggers again, exiling another creature. Ephemerate rebounds (cast again next upkeep for free), giving you another ETB trigger. You use Ephemerate on: Solitude (second exile), Subtlety (second bounce), Aven Interrupter (second counter), Eternal Witness (recur Ephemerate again). You chain blinks until their board is empty.

engines.title: Your Evoke Protocol
engines.body: You evoke Solitude ({5}{W}{W} creature, or evoke by exiling a white card) at their attack step when their best creature is attacking. Solitude ETB exiles the attacker. You've removed their best threat for zero mana. You follow with your own attack — you're now ahead in board position. Evoke Subtlety (exile a blue card) on their best creature spell as they cast it. Free counter.

engines.title: Your Eternal Witness Loop
engines.body: Eternal Witness ETB returns a card from your GY. You target Ephemerate. You now have Ephemerate in hand again. You cast Ephemerate on Eternal Witness — Witness ETBs again, returns Ephemerate. With rebound, Ephemerate returns next upkeep. You loop: Witness ETB → recur Ephemerate → Ephemerate Witness → Witness ETB → recur Ephemerate. Each loop generates one free ETB trigger.

engines.title: Your Subtlety Interaction
engines.body: Subtlety ({2}{U}{U} 3/3 flash flying, or evoke by exiling a blue card): ETB puts target creature or planeswalker spell on top of their library (not back to hand — they lose a draw step). You evoke Subtlety in response to their best creature spell. They get it back next turn but you've denied their turn 3 play. You follow with your own T3 play (Solitude evoke or Ephemerate on an existing creature).

engines.title: Are They Faster?
engines.body: If yes → you are Control. Stabilize first. Every life point matters. Don't develop your engine until you've stopped bleeding. Solitude + Ephemerate is your stabilization engine — use it reactively, not proactively.

engines.title: Do They Have a Specific Kill Window?
engines.body: If yes → you are Tempo. Identify the window. Identify the card that creates it. Hold Consign or Orim's Chant for that exact moment. Don't trade resources before it — stay full so you can blow them out at the key turn.

engines.title: Do They Take Longer Than You?
engines.body: If yes → you are Beatdown. Jam Guide + Pride + Phantom aggressively. Use Ephemerate on your own Solitude to exile their blockers. Close before they reach their power level. Do not let the game go to turn 7.

engines.title: You're the aggressor when:
engines.body: You've stabilized vs aggro at 10+ life. You've disrupted combo once and have 4 turns of clock. They're hellbent. They've spent their sweepers and have no answer to your token army.

engines.title: Hold the line when:
engines.body: Life total is still in danger. They have payoffs in hand you haven't answered. You don't have a clock established and they still have lands to develop. One attack without a clock is wasted damage.

engines.title: Go for the jugular when:
engines.body: You've identified their key turn. Consign or Orim's Chant is in hand. You have 2–3 turns of pressure ready. Fire the disruption and immediately convert — don't wait for a "better" window.

engines.title: Phantom on Turn 2
engines.body: T1 Guide of Souls , T2 White Orchid Phantom . Destroying their Sacred Foundry or Inspiring Vantage and replacing with a tapped basic delays their ability to double-spell before Phlage or Ajani comes online. Repeatedly blinking Phantom forces them further onto basics, cutting their energy generation and Discharge efficiency.

engines.title: PrioritizeSolitude
engines.body: On the draw they're one threat ahead. Solitude pitch on their key threat (Ragavan T1 connection is devastating) buys the tempo needed to stabilize. Mulligan for Solitude access — hands without it on the draw are risky into Boros.

engines.title: Race to Sanctifier
engines.body: T1 Guide of Souls , T2 Sanctifier or Phantom. Sanctifier on T2 shuts off their entire damage suite before they've connected enough to matter. You win from here unless they draw into multiple creature attacks that dodge Sanctifier's protection.

engines.title: Mulligan Harder
engines.body: Mulligan to Sanctifier more aggressively on the draw. They get T1 Swiftspear, T2 Cori-Steel Cutter while you're one step behind. Without Sanctifier early, respect the burn clock — Solitude their biggest threats, not the 1/1 tokens. Stabilize life total first.

engines.title: Lock + Hold Consign
engines.body: T2 White Orchid Phantom destroys their best nonbasic land and forces a tapped basic, reducing their mana quality. Hold Consign for Archon of Cruelty’s ETB triggered ability — when Archon enters, its sacrifice/discard/lose 3 life is a triggered ability that Consign can counter. Important: Consign cannot counter Persist the card itself (black sorcery).

engines.title: RespectThoughtseizeT1
engines.body: They Thoughtseize you T1 and take Consign — now you're exposed. Keep hands with 2+ interaction pieces. Solitude answers Psychic Frog and Archon in play. Rest in Peace postboard shuts their entire engine off.

engines.title: Maximum Aggression
engines.body: T1 Guide, T2 Ocelot Pride + attack, T3 Phantom or Phelia. Deploy as many threats as possible before they reach 3 mana for Verdict. On the play you have a full turn ahead of their Counterspell mana — use it.

engines.title: Stagger into Counterspells
engines.body: Deploy one threat per turn. They will Counterspell your best card — bait it with the second best card first. Force them to tap out to answer each threat individually. Your Phantom generating card advantage every turn is harder for them to answer than raw combat threats.

engines.title: Phantom T2 Into Lock
engines.body: T2 Phantom, T3 Phelia to reblink Phantom. They're stuck at 2 lands with no Amulet acceleration. Your engine develops over the next 3 turns while they're locked. This is often a clean win — their deck cannot function without bounce land access.

engines.title: Respect T3 Kill
engines.body: Their fast nut draw (Amulet T1, bounce land T2, Pact T3) kills before Phantom matters. Hold Consign for Summoner's Pact — if you can fire it on upkeep when they can't pay, they die to the Pact trigger. Otherwise, play fastest hand and hope for a normal draw.

engines.title: Teferi on Curve
engines.body: Race to Teferi on turn 3. On the play you can resolve it before they have open mana to Consign it. Teferi locking them out of instant-speed plays is the game-deciding asymmetry. Protect it — don't jam other spells into open blue mana after Teferi resolves.

engines.title: Hold Consign for Their Teferi
engines.body: They're racing to Teferi on the play. Hold Consign for their Teferi specifically — counter it and the game resets to parity. Don't spend Consign on anything else before Teferi resolves. One Consign used on Solitude is one fewer counter for their trump card.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Midrange-heavy field where Teferi + Solitude is faster than their clock. Combo decks present — Consign counters key spells. Low Counterspell density in expected SBs. You’ve practiced the evoke+Ephemerate timing for the top matchups.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy Force of Negation field — your evoke + Ephemerate chain gets countered and you’ve spent 2 cards to resolve nothing. Multiple Harbinger of the Seas builds (cuts your blue mana). You haven’t practiced the Teferi-only grind plan.

engines.title: Ephemerate ×4
