engines.body: The deck's engine. Four copies ensures you have a blink spell every game. Below 4 and the ETB chain collapses.

engines.title: Solitude ×4
engines.body: Your best removal. Evokeable for free by pitching a white card. Four copies gives you consistent access to free interaction.

engines.title: Subtlety
engines.body: 3 in creature-heavy metas where bouncing their threat to library buys a full turn. 4 in combo metas where countering their win condition at instant speed is critical. 2 in aggro metas where their threats are too cheap to be worth bouncing.

engines.title: Dress Down (SB)
engines.body: 2 in ETB-heavy metas (other Blink decks, Neoform). Cut entirely when no opponents generate ETB value. Dress Down on their Archon of Cruelty entry is a 2-mana Counterspell.

engines.title: Teferi, Time Raveler count
engines.body: 2 in the main vs combo and control. 3 when you expect heavy counter mirrors — Teferi making all their spells sorcery-speed and bouncing their permanents wins counter wars. Cut to 1 in pure aggro fields.

engines.title: 20 vs Combo
engines.body: Reanimator, Belcher, Neoform. Drill mulligans and disruption sequencing.

engines.title: 20 vs Aggro
engines.body: Energy, Prowess, Domain. Drill Solitude timing, Wrath sequencing, and the Ocelot kill after stabilization.

engines.title: 20 vs Control / Mirror
engines.body: Practice patience, Ephemerate timing, and Teferi sequencing. Commit threats after Verdict.

engines.title: Clock Practice
engines.body: Play games under 20 minutes. If you're drawing out, it's sequencing — not the deck.

engines.title: Consign Target Pre-Game
engines.body: Know what you're holding Consign for before the game starts. Reanimator: Persist . Titan: Pact trigger. Aggro: board it out. Never figure this out at the table.

engines.title: EphemerateStack Order
engines.body: Never cast Ephemerate first in a stack war. Wait for their response, then respond to theirs. Your Ephemerate resolving last means your blink triggers resolve first.

engines.title: Fetch White First
engines.body: Solitude , Pride, Sanctifier, Wrath all require white. Miss it turns 1–2 and the game is lost before it starts. Almost always fetch white on your opening fetchland.

engines.title: Tournament Clock
engines.body: Find the fastest line to closing in every game state. Jeskai Blink draws matches by generating too many decisions. Identify your win condition by turn 4 and execute toward it.

matchups.notes: Solitude exiles threats — Stony kills the engine
Phelia bounces Chalice — counter their payoffs
Scion hexproof + fast clock — WOP destroys lands
Consign counters Atraxa ETB — TRav locks Goryo's
TRav doesn't help — hold Consign for payoff

JeskaiControl.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Overview "Jeskai Control is an Azorius Control variant that splashes red to take advantage of how valuable that color is in many matchups — particularly the current meta centered around creatures and combat." Jeskai Control runs zero creatures in the main deck — the entire 60 is removal, counters, and card draw. The win condition is Jeskai Revelation, which as an instant bounces a threat, deals 4 damage, creates two 1/1 Monk tokens with prowess, draws 2 cards, and gains 4 life — essentially resetting a board state and refueling simultaneously. Lightning Helix at instant speed d
JeskaiControl.mulligan: Mulligan rule: Keep any 7 with 2 lands + Voice of Victory OR 2 lands + Aven Interrupter + a counter.

engines.title: Lightning Helix
engines.body: {R}{W} Instant. 3 damage to any target + gain 3 life. The best red-white spell in the format. At instant speed, it answers their T1-T3 creatures AND stabilizes your life total. Against Boros Aggro, 4 Helixes = 12 damage absorbed and 12 life gained — effectively a 24-point life swing. Against Prowess, it answers Slickshot Show-Off at any stage. The most important card in the deck against aggro.

engines.title: Inevitable Defeat
engines.body: {2}{B}{W} Instant. Can't be countered. Exile target nonland permanent. Its controller loses 3 life, you gain 3 life. The answer to everything — Ojer Axonil, Mossborn Hydra, Sapling Nursery, Stormchaser's Talent. Can't be countered means it resolves through their Spell Pierce and Get Out. The life swing (+3 / −3 = 6-point swing) is meaningful in close races. 4 copies because this is the primary rem

engines.title: Jeskai Revelation
engines.body: {2}{U}{R}{W} Instant. Return target spell or permanent to hand + deals 4 damage to any target + create two 1/1 Monk tokens with prowess + draw 2 cards + gain 4 life. Five effects in one instant-speed card. Cast at end of opponent's turn after they've tapped out: bounce their key permanent, create two prowess threats, refuel your hand, gain 4 life. engines.title: No More Lies
engines.body: {U}{W} Instant. Counter target spell unless its controller pays {3}. If countered, exile it. The soft counter that's effectively hard when they're on curve. T2 Elusive Otter requires they pay {3} extra = it costs them {U}+{3} = {3}{U}. They can rarely pay {3} extra in the early turns. The exile clause prevents GY recursion for Esper Origins, Wild Ride Harmonize, and any flashback effects.

engines.title: Spell Snare
engines.body: {U} Instant. Counter target spell with mana value 2. Hard counter for one mana specifically targeting the most dangerous turn-2 plays: Stormchaser's Talent, Warleader's Call, Shocking Sharpshooter, Earthbender Ascension. The {U} efficiency means you can hold it while deploying another spell. Only 2 copies because it's dead against 3+ mana threats.

engines.body: Day of Judgment: {2}{W}{W} Sorcery — destroy all creatures. 2 main + 1 SB. The primary board reset. Ultima: {4}{W}{U} Sorcery — destroy all artifacts and creatures, then end the turn (exile all spells/abilities from stack, current player discards to max hand size, damage wears off, EOT effects end). engines.title: Consult the Star Charts / Stock Up
engines.body: Consult the Star Charts: {1}{W} Instant. Kicker {1}{U}. Look at top X cards (X = lands you control), put 1 (or 2 if kicked) in hand. With 6 lands, unkicked = look at 6 pick 1. Kicked with 6 lands = look at 6 pick 2 for {2}{U}{W}. Stock Up: {1}{U} Sorcery — look at top 5, put 2 in hand. Consult at instant speed enables reactive digging — find the sweeper or Helix you need on their end step.

engines.title: Thundering Falls / Mistrise Village
engines.body: Thundering Falls: Island + Mountain, enters tapped, ETB surveil 1. Fixing + library manipulation. Mistrise Village: enters tapped unless you control Mountain or Forest. {U}{T}: your next spell can't be countered. The uncounterable clause on Mistrise is critical in the control mirror — deploy key Revelation or Inevitable Defeat through their countermagic. Note: Ultima can't be countered via Mistris

engines.title: Hold Mana Open
engines.body: Hold Lightning Helix and No More Lies in hand. Deploy land + hold up {R}{W} for Helix response on their attack step. Against aggro: kill their key threats at instant speed (Sharpshooter, Slickshot Show-Off). Against midrange: counter their value engines (Stormchaser's Talent, Sapling Nursery). Never tap out unless you're drawing a land and have nothing to hold up.

engines.title: Sweep + Refuel
engines.body: Once their board is threatening: Day of Judgment to wipe, then Consult the Star Charts kicked to refuel. Inevitable Defeat for their indestructible threats (Ojer Axonil) that Day of Judgment doesn't hit. Stock Up at instant speed on their end step before your turn. The goal: enter turn 7 with 3+ cards in hand and their board clear.

engines.title: Revelation into Monks
engines.body: Cast Jeskai Revelation at instant speed (end of their turn): bounce their key permanent, deal 4 damage, create 2 Monk tokens with prowess, draw 2 cards, gain 4 life. Now you have 2 prowess 1/1 threats on board. Cast Lightning Helix next turn while attacking: each Helix is also +1/+1 on each Monk until EOT. They become 3/3s after one Helix. Win in 2-3 swings.

engines.title: Your Key Plays
engines.body: Your T4 is Voice of Victory. You attack immediately — it can't be targeted while attacking. Your T5 holds Dovin's Veto for their board wipe attempt. Your T6 is Stormplain Detainment if they've developed a wide board. You generate advantage through sustained pressure (Voice) combined with reactive answers (Aven Interrupter, Seam Rip) every turn.

engines.title: Your Interaction Depth
engines.body: Your counters each answer a specific threat type. Seam Rip ({1}{U}): counters sorceries exactly. Aven Interrupter (flash 5/4 ETB): hard counters any instant/sorcery. Dovin's Veto ({W}{U} uncounterable): noncreature spells. High Noon: prevents all sorceries for both players. You hold the right counter for their specific threat — never use Seam Rip on an instant or waste Dovin's Veto on a creature.

engines.title: Your T4+ Win Condition
engines.body: Voice of Victory is your clock. You deploy it at 5+ lands and attack every turn. At 3 damage per turn, you need 7 attack steps to win from 20 life. Their board wipe is the threat — you hold Dovin's Veto specifically for Supreme Verdict. Your Aven Interrupter is your backup counter for whatever their other win condition is. You attack, they spend resources answering, you counter their answer.

engines.title: Your Open Mana Discipline
engines.body: Your most important skill: never tap out. Your T3: one land + {W}{U} open (Dovin's Veto). Your T4: Voice into {W}{U} or {1}{U} open (Seam Rip). Your T5+: hold the most relevant counter for their top 3 plays. You pre-identify what they can cast on their next turn and keep the mana to answer exactly that. Never tap out for development when interaction is available.

engines.title: Lightning Helix / Inevitable Defeat
engines.body: Helix: instant, 3 damage, gain 3 life. Best against 1-3 toughness creatures early (all of Boros' 1/1-2/3 threats, Elusive Otter, Slickshot Show-Off). Inevitable Defeat: exile any nonland permanent, uncounterable. Use for: indestructible creatures, high-toughness threats Helix can't reach (Eddymurk Crab 5/5), planeswalkers, key enchantments. The rule: Helix kills efficiently (2 mana for 3 damage +

engines.body: Inevitable Defeat exiles any nonland permanent — the only main-deck answer to enchantments like Sapling Nursery, Warleader's Call, Stormchaser's Talent. Get Lost: {1}{G} instant — destroy target creature, enchantment, or planeswalker; controller gets 2 Map tokens. The Map tokens are a concession (they get minor card advantage), but instant-speed enchantment removal is critical. Use Get Lost when H

engines.body: No More Lies: soft counter at {U}{W}, hard counter at MV ≤ 3 effectively. Use for key threats you can't answer in play (combo pieces, uncounterable threats, things without answers in your main deck). Spell Snare: hard counter for MV 2 exactly — optimal against Stormchaser's Talent, Warleader's Call, Shocking Sharpshooter. Hold Snare when their T2 play is dangerous. Never tap out to cast a proactiv

engines.body: Day of Judgment: {2}{W}{W} sorcery, destroy all creatures. Use when they have 3+ creatures and Helix can't answer them individually. Ultima: {4}{W}{U} sorcery, destroy all artifacts and creatures, end the turn. engines.title: GY-Based Strategies
engines.body: The main deck has no graveyard hate. Izzet Spellementals using GY for Eddymurk Crab cost reduction, Reanimator returning large threats, Icetill Explorer playing lands from GY — all operate without main deck interference. Plan: counter or exile before they hit the GY. Post-board: Rest in Peace (hard exile everything) and Torpor Orb (stops ETB triggers from reanimated threats).

engines.title: Fast Token Floods
engines.body: A resolved Stormchaser's Talent at level 3 generating tokens per spell is difficult to answer — each Inevitable Defeat on the Talent costs {4} and they've already gotten value. Day of Judgment clears the tokens but not the Talent. Annul from the SB counters it on the way in. Post-board: Annul for Talent, Torpor Orb blanks Crab and other ETB threats. The gap: no instant-speed enchantment removal in

engines.title: Your Uncounterable Clock
engines.body: Voice of Victory (3/3 flying) can't be targeted while attacking. You deploy Voice at 5+ mana and attack every turn. Your payoff: they can't point targeted removal at Voice during your attack step — they must answer it with board wipes or sacrifice effects. You hold your most relevant counter (Dovin's Veto) specifically for their board wipe attempt after Voice resolves. Voice + Veto is your primary

engines.title: Your Flash Counter Creature
engines.body: Aven Interrupter ({3}{W}{U} = 5 mana, 5/4 flash, ETB counters a spell) is your most efficient card. You deploy it in response to their most important noncreature spell — Earthbender Ascension, Sunderflock, their board wipe. Your payoff: their spell is countered AND you have a 5/4 in play. You follow Aven with an attack — they must spend removal instead of advancing their plan.

engines.title: Your Board Lockout
engines.body: Stormplain Detainment ({2}{W}) taps all their creatures until EOT. You deploy it at their attack step when they have 3+ attackers. Your payoff: their entire attack is cancelled, they're tapped down, and you attack freely next turn. You combine it with Voice of Victory attacks: Stormplain taps their blockers, Voice attacks through them. You generate "free" attack steps every turn you cast Stormplai

engines.title: Your Sorcery Shield
engines.body: High Noon prevents all sorcery-speed plays until EOT — for both players. You deploy it the turn before their key sorcery. Your payoff: they can't cast Earthbender Ascension, sweepers, or their key sorcery on their turn. You plan your own sorcery-speed actions for before High Noon resolves. You never cast High Noon blindly; you know their specific sorcery-speed threat first.

engines.title: Life Total Manager
engines.body: Use Lightning Helix at instant speed to both kill threats and gain life. Never tap out when they have open attack mana. Day of Judgment as the reset button. Goal: reach turn 6 with 8+ life, then Revelation stabilizes completely.

engines.title: Answer Engine
engines.body: Inevitable Defeat for their key permanents. No More Lies for their value spells. Counter their draw engines before they generate card advantage. Revelation when they're topdecking — bounce their last threat and refuel.

engines.title: Resource War
engines.body: Hold counterspells for their key spells. Mistrise Village makes your Inevitable Defeat uncounterable — use it to land the uncounterable exile. Revelation at instant speed EOT lets you maintain card parity while generating the Monk clock they can't answer.

engines.title: Your Interaction Hierarchy
engines.body: You pre-establish your interaction hierarchy before each game: Dovin's Veto for their board wipe, Seam Rip for their key sorcery, Aven Interrupter for their key instant, Stormplain Detainment for their wide attack. You never use your highest-priority counter on a lower-priority threat. You identify their top 3 threats and hold the right answer for each. Wrong counter assignment loses games.

engines.title: Your Attack Commitment
engines.body: Once you deploy Voice of Victory, you attack every turn. You never miss an attack step with Voice — every attack is 3 guaranteed damage through targeted-removal immunity. You hold your remaining mana for answers, not attacks. Your threat (Voice) attacks automatically; your job after Voice resolves is holding the right counter for their board wipe attempt.

engines.title: Your Mana Discipline
engines.body: You hold {W}{U} open on their turn every turn from T3 onward. Against a spell-heavy deck: you hold Seam Rip or Dovin's Veto every turn. You tap down to 0 only when you're deploying your own threat AND you have a Veto in hand that will protect it. You never tap out speculatively. Your power comes from untapped mana — every tapped out turn is a turn they can resolve their win condition.

engines.title: Your Sorcery Window
engines.body: You cast High Noon when you've identified the specific sorcery you're stopping. You hold High Noon for the turn before they cast Earthbender Ascension or their sweeper. You don't cast High Noon when they have no sorceries — you save it. Once High Noon resolves, you attack freely knowing they're locked out of their key sorcery-speed play for that turn.

engines.title: Priority Response Mana
engines.body: {R}{W} = Lightning Helix — hold vs any aggro opponent with open attack mana. One Helix per turn is 6-point swing ({R}{W} mana + 3 damage + 3 life). {2}{B}{W} = Inevitable Defeat — hold whenever their key permanent could resolve. Against Dimir: Kaito. Against Boros: Ojer Axonil. Against Mono-Green: Sapling Nursery. {U}{W} = No More Lies — hold vs any key 3-drop you can't let resolve. Counters unles

engines.title: Safe Windows to Tap Out
engines.body: Their end step is your safest window — they've declared no blocks, used their mana, and can't respond to your sorcery-speed cards until their next turn. Use their end step for: Consult the Star Charts (instant — dig for the key card you need), Stock Up on T4+ (sorcery but you're already in their end step... wait, Stock Up is sorcery, you can't cast it at instant speed). Correct: use end step for C

engines.title: Their End Step (After They Pass)
engines.body: They pass priority in their end step. You respond: cast Consult kicked ({1}{U}{1}{W} = {2}{U}{W}). Look at top (lands you control) cards, put 2 in hand. Now you untap with a full hand and full mana. They get no response because it's still their end step — they're not untapping yet. This is the cleanest dig cycle in the deck.

engines.title: X = Lands You Control at Cast Time
engines.body: You look at the top X cards where X is the number of lands you control at the time you cast Consult. With 6 lands = look at 6. With 8 lands = look at 8. This gets dramatically better as the game goes on — by turn 8 you're looking at 8 cards for {2}{U}{W}. Always wait until you have maximum lands before casting Consult for full dig depth.

engines.title: Their Key Permanent When They're Tapped
engines.body: Cast Revelation on their end step when they've spent all their mana. Bounce their most dangerous permanent — not any permanent, the one they relied on most this turn. Sapling Nursery (back to hand, no tokens next turn unless they recast it). Kaito (loses all loyalty counters going back to hand). Enduring Curiosity (stops their draw engine). Time the bounce to the moment they can't immediately reca

engines.title: Two Prowess 1/1s That Grow With Your Spells
engines.body: Your Revelation Monks have prowess — every spell you cast makes them +1/+1 until EOT. Lightning Helix cast while Monks are attacking = both Monks are 2/2. Consult while they're attacking = 2/2. Stock Up + Consult = 3/3. Your instants that you were going to cast anyway are free combat pump on the Monks. Revelation creates a clock that accelerates with your existing game plan.

engines.title: +4 Life at Instant Speed
engines.body: Against any aggro deck, the 4 life from Revelation plus the 3 life from a Lightning Helix in the same turn = 7 life at instant speed. That's often the turn you stabilize from "dead to their next attack" to "comfortable." Don't hold Revelation looking for the perfect bounce target — casting it purely for the life + draw + Monks is often correct against aggressive opponents.

engines.title: Cast Inevitable Defeat During Their Turn
engines.body: Their main phase — after they deploy Kaito but before they end their turn. Or their end step. During their turn Kaito has NO hexproof. Inevitable Defeat: exile him. He's uncounterable (Inevitable Defeat's own text) and instant speed. They can't protect Kaito during their own turn because his hexproof only applies during YOUR turn. This is the single most important interaction rule vs Dimir.

engines.title: Make Defeat Doubly Uncounterable
engines.body: Inevitable Defeat is already uncounterable by its own text. But Mistrise Village ({U}{T}: your next spell this turn can't be countered) adds a second layer. In the control mirror where they might try to counter your Defeat anyway — activate Mistrise first, then cast Defeat. It's now protected by both its own text AND the Village trigger. Use this against any opponent running countermagic who might

engines.title: Cast Ultima When They Attack
engines.body: They declare attackers. You cast Ultima. Their attacking creatures die (destroyed). Their non-attackers die. The turn ends — their attack step is over, they go to their end step with an empty board and no damage dealt. This is the only sweeper in the format that also stops the attack that triggered it. Critical: they don't get to deal combat damage because the turn ending cancels the combat damage

engines.title: Enchantments Survive Ultima
engines.body: Ultima destroys artifacts AND creatures. It does not destroy enchantments. Sapling Nursery survives. Stormchaser's Talent survives. Warleader's Call survives. Earthbender Ascension survives. After Ultima, their enchantments are still in play and will resume generating value next turn. Plan for what survives — if Nursery is in play when you cast Ultima, you've swept their board but Nursery immediat

engines.title: Your High Noon Line
engines.body: You cast High Noon on T3 after identifying their key sorcery. High Noon prevents ALL sorcery-speed plays until EOT. You calculate: if their key play is a sorcery (Earthbender Ascension, their sweeper), you cast High Noon. If their key play is an instant (Counterspell, flash creatures), you hold High Noon. You never cast High Noon blindly — you know their specific threat first.

engines.title: Your Voice + Counter Line
engines.body: You deploy Voice of Victory on T5 with {W}{U} or {1}{U} open (Dovin's Veto or Seam Rip). You attack immediately — Voice can't be targeted while attacking. They must cast their board wipe. You fire Dovin's Veto on their board wipe. If they don't have a wipe, you attack every turn until they're dead. You count their outs before committing Voice.

engines.title: Your Aven Interrupter Flash
engines.body: You hold Aven Interrupter mana ({3}{W}{U} = 5 mana) from T5 onward. You flash Aven in when they tap for their most important non-creature spell. Aven ETB counters the spell. You now have a 5/4 in play. You follow with attack — they must spend removal on Aven instead of advancing their plan.

engines.title: Your Stormplain Detainment Line
engines.body: You deploy Stormplain Detainment ({2}{W}) at their combat step when they declare attackers. All their creatures are tapped until EOT — their attack is cancelled. You untap and attack with your Voice of Victory. They cannot attack back that turn. You reset the board state from "them attacking" to "you attacking" in one instant-speed card.

engines.title: Stormplain Detainment ×4
engines.body: Your most efficient mass answer. Four copies ensures you see it when they commit a wide board. Below 4 and you lose the ability to respond to their T3-T4 explosive turns.

engines.title: Voice of Victory ×4
engines.body: Your clock. No copies = no win condition. Four is the correct number — you need to see it before T5 in most games.

engines.title: High Noon
engines.body: 3 in metas heavy with sorcery-speed combos and sweepers. 2 in faster metas where their key threats are instants. High Noon does nothing if they have no sorceries worth stopping.

engines.title: Aven Interrupter
engines.body: Run 2 as the flash counter. Aven at 5 mana is expensive — 1 copy in pure aggro metas, 2 in spell-heavy metas where the ETB counter is the card that wins games.

engines.title: Dovin's Veto count
engines.body: 2 is the baseline. Run 3 when counter mirrors are common. Veto is uncounterable — it always resolves. The third copy becomes live when you expect multiple counter wars per game.

engines.title: Voice Attack Lines
engines.body: Practice the Voice lock: they can't target it while attacking. Identify what removes Voice — board wipes and sacrifice effects vs targeted removal.

engines.title: Aven Interrupter Flash Timing
engines.body: They cast a key instant: flash Aven in response. Aven ETB counters the spell. Know that Aven's ETB trigger counters on resolution, not on the stack.

engines.title: High Noon Windows
engines.body: Cast it when they're about to cast their key sorcery. Too early = they play around it. Too late = damage is done.

engines.title: Stormplain Detainment Timing
engines.body: They commit creatures to attack: tap them at their declare-attackers step. They can't attack AND they're tapped down for your swing.

matchups.notes: Inevitable Defeat handles Kaito uncounterable. Torpor Orb from SB blanks their entire ETB disruption suite.

matchups.opponent: You are the underdog at 36% — their flash creatures react to your sweeper timing and Kaito has hexproof on your turn. But you have the tools to fight back if you sequence correctly. The matchup is decided by whether you can land Revelation + Monks before they rebuild their hand via Enduring Curiosity. One successful Revelation — bounce their Kaito, deal 4 to their face, create two 1/1 prowess Monks, draw 2, gain 4 — sets you ahead on every axis: card parity, life, and board. Kaito is uncounterable on their turn: Kaito has hexproof during your turn. But on their turn, when they attack with Kaito's minus ability or when Kaito first resolves, you can Inevitable Defeat it — Inevitable Defeat is an instant and doesn't require targeting during your turn. You're exiling "target nonland permanent" which doesn't have the hexproof restriction. Get Kaito off the board with Inevitable Defeat the turn it resolves or the turn after they use his +2 ability. Torpor Orb is your game-winner: Their disruption package is entirely ETB-based: Floodpits Drowner taps your board, Tishana's Tidebinder counters your abilities, Deep-Cavern Bat strips your hand. Torpor Orb ({2} artifact) makes all entering creatures' ETBs do nothing. With Orb in play: Drowner enters as a vanilla 2/5. Tidebinder enters as a 3/3 that does nothing. Bat is a 1/1 flier. Their disruption suite is completely blank. Turn-by-turn plan: T1-T2: play lands, hold mana. T3: Spell Snare their Kaito ({U} counters MV 2 — wait, Kaito is MV 3). Spell Snare counters MV 2 exactly. Kaito is {1}{U}{B} = MV 3. Spell Snare doesn't hit Kaito. No More Lies ({U}{W}) counters Kaito unless they pay {3} — on T3 with only 3 lands, they can't pay {3} extra. Counter Kaito with No More Lies on T3 if they tap for it. T4: if they deployed a creature suite, hold up Inevitable Defeat for Enduring Curiosity (enchantment — Defeat exiles it). T5+: Revelation EOT after they tap for a spell. Out In −2 Day of Judgment +2 Torpor Orb −1 Ultima +2 Wan Shi Tong −1 Spell Snare +1 Tishana's Tidebinder Izzet Lessons Counter + Lock Favorable Your counterspells are better than their draw. Counter Monument to Endurance and you win. Izzet Lessons plays into your gameplan perfectly — they're a spell-heavy deck trying to generate card advantage and you have counterspells to shut down every key spell. Their Monument to Endurance is the single card that beats you; counter it. Everything else they do is manageable. Priority: Counter Monument to Endurance above all else. After that, let their draw spells resolve (Accumulate Wisdom draws them cards but doesn't threaten you) and counter their threats. High Noon slows their spell chains significantly — they can only cast one spell per turn under it. Needle: Don't tap out for your threats until they've spent their Abandon Attachments. Wan Shi Tong generates card advantage faster than their entire draw engine. Establish Wan Shi Tong → High Noon → win. In Disdainful Stroke +1 Wan Shi Tong, Librarian +1 Out Seam Rip −1 Get Lost −1 Needle: Torpor Orb is your best sideboard card in this matchup — deploy it before they can develop their flash package. Wan Shi Tong (3/3 that lets you put cards from hand to bottom of library when you draw) provides a threat that generates card quality in the long game — their attrition plan runs out before your library does. Trim Day of Judgment (they have few creatures) and Ultima (no artifacts to destroy). Keep Inevitable Defeat at 4 — it's your unconditional answer to Kaito and Enduring Curiosity.

matchups.opponent: You are the unfavorable deck here. Stormchaser's Talent at Level 3 generates a 1/1 Otter every time they cast an instant or sorcery — and they cast 10-12 spells per game. Day of Judgment kills the Otters but Talent is still in play generating new ones. Ultima kills the Otters and Talent (as a nonland permanent — wait, Ultima destroys artifacts AND creatures, not enchantments). Ultima does NOT destroy Stormchaser's Talent, which is an enchantment. Your only reliable main deck answer to Talent is Inevitable Defeat — exile it as a nonland permanent. Your kill order: 1. Counter Stormchaser's Talent on entry with Annul ({U}, SB). 2. If Talent resolves, Inevitable Defeat it immediately — don't wait for Level 3. 3. Lightning Helix kills their individual creatures (Slickshot 1/2, Otter 1/1, any 1-3 toughness threat). 4. No More Lies counters Slickshot if they try to deploy it normally (Plot bypasses this — you can't counter a spell cast from exile via Plot... actually you can counter any spell that was cast, including from exile via Plot. No More Lies works on plotted Slickshot). High Noon wins long games: High Noon ({2}{W} enchantment, SB) limits each player to one spell per turn. Their cantrip chain requires casting 4-5 spells in one turn. High Noon makes that illegal. With High Noon in play, they can cast one Opt per turn. Their Stormchaser's Talent Level 3 only generates one Otter per turn instead of four. Pyroclasm sweeps all the accumulated 1/1 Otters for {1}{R} — 2 damage to each creature wipes every 1/1 token on the board while your Revelation Monks (1/1 prowess) also die, which is acceptable if you then recast Revelation. Turn-by-turn plan: T1: land. T2: Lightning Helix on their T1 Otter — 3 damage, gain 3 life, clear the clock. T3: Annul in hand waiting for Talent. If they cast Talent, Annul it for {U}. If they deploy Slickshot instead, hold Helix for it at their attack step. T4: Revelation EOT if they're tapped — bounce their key threat, create two 1/1 prowess Monks (which get +1/+1 when you cast Helix next turn). Out In −2 Get Lost +2 Annul −1 Spell Snare +1 Pyroclasm −1 Ultima +1 High Noon Needle: Annul is your best card in this matchup — hard counter on Stormchaser's Talent for {U}. Keep {U} open every turn on T2+. Pyroclasm at {1}{R} kills all 1/1 tokens and 2/2 creatures simultaneously. Your Revelation Monks die too but that's fine — Revelation immediately recasts for new ones. Trim Get Lost (your only enchantment target is Talent, and Annul is better) and Ultima (doesn't hit enchantments).
