Ojer Axonil — Inevitable Defeat immediately on entry, uncounterable and can't be responded to with Voice (Inevitable Defeat is instant, you can cast it during your turn before their next attack step, or during their main phase before Voice attacks). 2. Shocking Sharpshooter — Helix for 3 (kills the 1/3 exactly with 3 damage). 3. Warleader's Call — Get Lost (destroys enchantment at instant speed). 4. Everything else — Day of Judgment when they overextend. Turn-by-turn plan: T1: land, hold {R}{W}. T2: if they deployed Sharpshooter, Helix it on their end step (3 damage kills 1/3, you gain 3 life). T3: Inevitable Defeat on their Warleader's Call if it resolved. T4: Get Lost on any remaining enchantment OR No More Lies their Ojer if you held up {U}{W}. T5: Day of Judgment on their token flood. T6+: Revelation EOT — bounce their best threat, create two prowess Monks, draw 2, gain 4. You're now ahead on every axis. Out In −2 Spell Snare +2 High Noon −1 No More Lies +1 Pyroclasm Needle: Inevitable Defeat exiles Ojer — when exiled, he doesn't transform into Temple of Power (the death trigger doesn't fire on exile). Get Lost destroys Warleader's Call at instant speed during their main phase before Voice attacks. High Noon limits them to one spell per turn — their attack-step token chain is ETB triggered abilities (not spells), so High Noon doesn't stop Mobilize tokens entering. But it does stop them casting Burst Lightning + Torch the Tower + Seam Rip in one turn to clear your defenders. Pyroclasm sweeps all their 1/1 Warriors for {1}{R}.

matchups.notes: Inevitable Defeat exiles Sapling Nursery. Annul counters it on entry for {U}. Day of Judgment handles their Treefolk board.

matchups.opponent: Mono-Green is unfavorable — Sapling Nursery generates Treefolk tokens faster than you can sweep them, and their combo kill via Icetill Explorer + Mightform Harmonizer + Escape Tunnel creates a one-shot threat you have to respect every turn they have 4+ lands. Your plan: counter or exile Sapling Nursery before it generates tokens, answer the combo pieces individually, and close with Revelation Monks before their board overwhelms your sweepers. The Nursery problem: Sapling Nursery is an enchantment. Day of Judgment doesn't kill it. Ultima doesn't kill it. Your main-deck answers are: Inevitable Defeat ({2}{B}{W} instant, exile any nonland permanent — hits Nursery), Get Lost ({1}{G} instant destroy enchantment — wait, Get Lost is {1}{G}... confirming: Get Lost destroys creature, enchantment, or planeswalker, controller gets 2 Map tokens). Yes, Get Lost destroys Nursery at instant speed. Annul from SB counters it on entry for {U}. The combo threat: Icetill Explorer in play + 4 available land plays + Mightform Harmonizer + Escape Tunnel = one-shot kill. When Icetill is on the board and they have 3+ untapped lands, assume the combo is live. Hold No More Lies for the Escape Tunnel activation (Escape Tunnel's unblockable mode is an activated ability — No More Lies doesn't counter activated abilities, that's Tishana's Tidebinder. No More Lies counters spells. Use Tidebinder from SB to counter the Escape Tunnel activation). Turn-by-turn plan: T1: land + hold {U} for Annul. T2: Helix their Llanowar Elves (1/1, Helix hits creatures — 3 damage kills it, you gain 3 life). T3: if they try Sapling Nursery, Annul it for {U}. T4: if Nursery resolved, Inevitable Defeat it — but recognize this costs 4 mana and puts you behind. Better to Annul it on entry. T5: Day of Judgment on their accumulated Treefolk. T6: Revelation EOT for recovery and Monk clock. Out In −2 Spell Snare +2 Annul −1 Ultima +1 Torpor Orb Needle: Annul counters Sapling Nursery and Earthbender Ascension on entry for {U}. Keep {U} open every turn from T3 onward. Torpor Orb blanks Badgermole Cub's ETB (no earthbend), Fecund Greenshell's ETB (no land), and Leatherhead's hexproof counter entering — but Torpor Orb also blanks your own Revelation Monks' prowess. Your Monks enter as plain 1/1 Monks with no prowess. Factor this in — against Mono-Green the faster clock from Orb blanking their engine is worth losing the Monk prowess.

matchups.notes: Mistrise Village makes your Inevitable Defeat uncounterable. Revelation at instant speed at their end step wins the card parity war.

matchups.opponent: The mirror is pure resource management. Both players hold counterspells and avoid walking into them. The player who makes the first mistake (tapping out when the opponent has countermagic) loses a key permanent and falls behind. Revelation cast EOT when they're tapped out is the single most important play — it draws 2 cards, creates two threats, gains 4 life, and bounces their best permanent simultaneously, all at instant speed while they have nothing open. Mistrise Village is your edge: Mistrise Village ({U}{T}: next spell you cast this turn can't be countered). Activate it before casting Inevitable Defeat to make it uncounterable even beyond its printed text. Against their No More Lies, their Spell Snare, their Get Out — your Defeat resolves regardless. This is the key play to set up in the mirror: Mistrise activation + Inevitable Defeat on their key permanent or their Revelation Monks. Consult the Star Charts at instant speed: Consult ({1}{W} instant, look at top X lands you control, put 1 or 2 kicked) — use this on THEIR end step after they pass priority. You're using their turn to dig for your key cards without tapping out during your own turn. With 6 lands, unkicked Consult looks at 6 cards. Kicked for {1}{U} looks at 6 picks 2. The highest-value use: activate Consult on their end step, find Inevitable Defeat or Revelation for your upcoming turn. Out In −1 Day of Judgment +2 Wan Shi Tong −1 Get Lost Needle: Wan Shi Tong (3/3 that filters your draws — put any card from hand to bottom when you draw) is your threat in the mirror. Control can't efficiently kill a 3/3 without spending valuable removal that they need for Revelation Monks. Trim Day of Judgment (they have few creatures) and Get Lost (no enchantments to destroy — wait, they're running the same deck so they do have enchantments... they have none in the main. Keep Get Lost for their SB Torpor Orbs and enchantment answers).

matchups.notes: Mono-Green Landfall assembles Icetill Explorer + Earthbender Ascension + Lumra for a turn ...

matchups.opponent: Mono-Green Landfall assembles Icetill Explorer + Earthbender Ascension + Lumra for a turn 5-6 kill that goes over your control suite. Counterspell answers their key pieces. Badgermole Cub and Earthbender Ascension are both MV 2 — your Spell Snare hard-counters both for {U}. Mossborn Hydra (7/7, uncounterable at 7+ lands) is their best threat post-board — exile it with Stormplain Detainment or Seam Rip before it hits. Out In −2 High Noon + 2 Spell Snare −1 Aven Interrupter +1 Three Steps Ahead Spell Snare at {U} hard-counters Badgermole Cub and Earthbender Ascension — their two most critical pieces. Three Steps Ahead provides flexible protection. High Noon is wrong here (their key plays are instant-speed ETBs, not sorceries). Cut one Aven Interrupter (5 mana is too slow in this racing matchup).

matchups.notes: Simic Rhythm generates too wide a board for your spot removal to handle. Stormplain Detain...

matchups.opponent: Simic Rhythm generates too wide a board for your spot removal to handle. Stormplain Detainment taps their entire board — deploy it on their attack step when their creatures are untapped. High Noon prevents their sorcery-speed Earthbender Ascension triggers. Your Seam Rip counters their Ascension or Mossborn Hydra (the latter at MV 5 catches Disdainful Stroke). Their Badgermole Cub is MV 2 — Spell Snare handles it. Out In −2 Aven Interrupter + 2 Seam Rip −1 Three Steps Ahead +1 Stormplain Detainment Seam Rip counters Earthbender Ascension at instant speed. Extra Stormplain taps their board mid-attack. Cut Aven Interrupter (too expensive when they have wide boards) and Three Steps Ahead (your tempo package is more important).

matchups.notes: Dimir Excruciator mirrors your counter suite — Counterspell, Floodpits Drowner, Spell Snar...

matchups.opponent: Dimir Excruciator mirrors your counter suite — Counterspell, Floodpits Drowner, Spell Snare. The matchup is decided by who resolves their key permanent first. Your Voice of Victory (3/3 flier that protects itself) is a must-answer threat. Their Floodpits Drowner bounces your Voice when you tap out. Sequence: deploy Voice when they're at 3 or fewer mana, then hold Seam Rip for their bounce. Out In −2 High Noon + 2 Duress −1 Get Lost +1 Seam Rip Duress strips their key counter or Floodpits Drowner from hand before they deploy it. Extra Seam Rip protects your Voice of Victory from bounce. High Noon is wrong — their plays are all at instant speed. Get Lost is weaker when their key permanents are non-enchantments.

matchups.notes: Izzet Spellementals needs to resolve Hearth Elemental to chain free spells. Your Aven Inte...

matchups.opponent: Izzet Spellementals needs to resolve Hearth Elemental to chain free spells. Your Aven Interrupter flashed in while their chain is assembling counters their key spell. Voice of Victory flies over their elemental ground army. Stormplain Detainment taps Hearth Elemental before it can enable more free spells. Their Sunderflock (sweeper) is sorcery speed — Seam Rip hard-counters it for {1U} at instant speed. Out In −2 High Noon + 2 Seam Rip −1 Get Lost +1 Stormplain Detainment Seam Rip counters Sunderflock (their sweeper) and Hearth Elemental's key spells. Extra Stormplain taps Hearth before it can chain. High Noon is wrong here — they chain instants not sorceries. Get Lost is weak (they have no key enchantments).

LivingEnd.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Identity "Living End is the perfect weapon for anyone who wants to play a true combo deck while keeping the ability to interact. When it's working, nothing in Modern feels as clean or as devastating as a turn-3 cascade into a full board wipe and immediate rebuild." — BtB Jericho Living End is a cascade combo deck built around one card: Living End , a sorcery with Suspend 3 and no mana cost. Because it has no mana cost, cascade spells (which look for "a nonland card that costs less" than themselves) will always find and cast it for free. You spend turns 1–2 cycling large creatur
LivingEnd.mulligan: Mulligan rule: Keep any hand with a cascade spell + Living End in GY, or a hand that can cycle to get there.

engines.title: Cascade → Living End
engines.body: Cast Violent Outburst or Ardent Plea (MV 3). Cascade exiles cards until it finds a nonland card costing less than MV 3. Living End has no mana cost — MV 0 — so cascade finds it immediately. Cast Living End for free. Board wipe + graveyard refill.

engines.title: No Mana Cost = No MV
engines.body: Living End has "Suspend 3—{2}{B}{B}" but no printed mana cost at all. Cards with no mana cost have MV 0. The cascade rule says "exile cards until you exile a nonland card that costs less." Less than MV 3 = MV 0, 1, or 2. Living End at MV 0 qualifies. This is why the deck runs ZERO other nonland spells with MV 0, 1, or 2 in the main deck — any such spell could be hit by cascade instead.

engines.title: Violent Outburst EOT
engines.body: Violent Outburst is an INSTANT. Cast it at end of opponent's turn to dodge sorcery-speed hate. Rest in Peace, Relic of Progenitus activations, Grafdigger's Cage — many GY hate pieces can only be deployed at sorcery speed. Casting Violent Outburst at end step also means you hold up mana for Subtlety or Force of Negation on the same turn.

engines.title: Street Wraith — Pay 2 Life
engines.body: Street Wraith cycles for "pay 2 life" — zero mana. On turn 1 with no lands, you can cycle Street Wraith freely if you started at 20 life. Four copies means 8 free life spent cycling by turn 3. This is how the deck fills the GY while still playing on curve. Monstrous Carabid cycles for {B/R} (one mana), Horror for {B}.

engines.title: Zero Sub-3-MV Spells
engines.body: The deck cannot run any nonland spell with MV 2 or less in the main deck — cascade would hit it instead of Living End, wasting the cascade trigger. This shapes every card choice: every noncreature interaction piece (Force of Negation, Subtlety, Grief, Endurance) is either a creature with cycling or a "free" spell that doesn't go in the main cascade sequence.

engines.title: 2.8% · Consistent Threat
engines.body: BtB Jericho: "A rewarding experience for those players who like graveyard and combo strategies alike." Living End is a strong metagame choice when opponents haven't prepared GY hate. The sideboard is heavily tailored to beat GY hate since every opponent brings it in. Expert pilots routinely top8 Modern challenges with the deck.

engines.title: No Mana Cost · Sorcery
engines.body: Suspend 3—{2}{B}{B}. Each player exiles all creature cards from their graveyard, then sacrifices all creatures they control, then puts all cards exiled this way onto the battlefield. The exile and sacrifice happen simultaneously — tokens die, indestructible creatures are sacrificed. The enter triggers (ETBs of returned creatures) all go on the stack after resolution. Note: Grafdigger's Cage stops

engines.title: {1}{R}{G} · Instant MV 3
engines.body: Cascade. Creatures you control get +1/+0 until end of turn. The cascade trigger goes on the stack when you CAST this spell. Cascade exiles from library until it finds a nonland card costing less than MV 3. Casts it free. At end of opponent's turn: Violent Outburst resolves, +1/+0 buff applies to your entering creatures (relevant in combat races). The cascade clause is the reason — cast it at end o

engines.title: {3}{G} · Elemental MV 4
engines.body: When this creature enters, you may destroy target artifact or enchantment. Cycling {G}. Foundation Breaker enters FROM HAND (cast normally) — Grafdigger's Cage does NOT stop it entering or triggering. Even with Cage on board, Foundation Breaker can destroy the Cage on ETB. This is the primary answer to Cage. Cycling it also fills the GY for the Living End (you're cycling a 4-MV creature, which com

engines.title: {2}{U}{U} · 3/3 Flash Flying
engines.body: Evoke — exile a blue card. ETB: choose up to one target creature spell or planeswalker spell. Its owner puts it on top or bottom of library. Subtlety counters creature spells and planeswalker spells — NOT instants or sorceries. Can't counter Living End (it's a sorcery). CAN counter Subtlety, Endurance, Grief cast by opponents. After evoke, Subtlety dies but the ETB trigger already resolved. In Liv

engines.title: {1}{U}{U} · Instant MV 3
engines.body: If it's not your turn: exile a blue card from your hand, counter target noncreature spell. On your own turn: must pay {1}{U}{U}. Force of Negation CANNOT counter creature spells — relevant because Endurance (which shuffles GYs) is a creature spell. You can't Force of Negation an opposing Endurance trying to shuffle your GY. Use Subtlety instead to put Endurance on top/bottom of library before it E

engines.title: {3}{B}{B} · 5/5 Avatar
engines.body: Impending 5—{1}{B}: enters with 5 time counters, isn't a creature until last is removed (end step removes one per turn). When this permanent enters OR attacks: mill 4, then return a creature card from your GY to your hand. Impending means you play it for {1}{B} early, it sits as an enchantment, mills 4 on entry, then becomes a 5/5 creature when counters run out (5 turns later). Mill 4 on entry = 4

engines.title: Grief Disruption
engines.body: Cast Grief (evoke — exile a black card) before cascading to strip the opponent's counter or GY hate piece. Grief ETB: each opponent reveals their hand, you choose a nonland, nonblack card to discard. Stripping a Force of Negation, Rest in Peace, or Teferi before your cascade is often game-winning. Grief dies from evoke but the discard effect already resolved.

engines.title: Hold Up Force / Subtlety
engines.body: Cast Violent Outburst and cascade into Living End. Before Living End resolves, opponents can respond. Hold Force of Negation to counter opposing responses. Subtlety can be cast in response to an opponent's Endurance (trying to shuffle your GY) — Subtlety puts Endurance back on top/bottom of library, protecting your GY before Living End resolves.

engines.title: Instant — Default
engines.body: Always prefer Violent Outburst when possible. Cast at end of opponent's turn — they must hold up interaction during their own turn, can't tap out, can't play sorceries in response. The instant speed is the strongest protection the deck has against sorcery-speed hate.

engines.title: Sorcery — Redundancy
engines.body: Ardent Plea is sorcery speed. Cast on your main phase turn 3 when you have 3 mana. Useful when Violent Outburst is countered or unavailable. The exalted trigger is irrelevant — you're cascading into a mass resurrection, not attacking alone. Running 3 copies ensures consistency.

engines.title: Which Cascade Finds What
engines.body: Both cascades into Living End (the only legal hit in the deck). If you have both, hold Violent Outburst for instant speed. After Living End resolves and you have a second cascade spell: the second cascade finds… Living End again if it's still in the library. If Living End was already cast (it goes to exile via cascade), the second cascade finds nothing above MV 0 and whiffs.

engines.title: Cycle Aggressively T1–2
engines.body: On the play you want to cycle creatures into the graveyard as fast as possible. T1 cycle Deadshot Minotaur or Street Wraith (free cycle). T2 cycle another or cast Violent Outburst if you have 3 mana. On the play: count GY creatures before T3 — you need 3+ for a meaningful Living End. With 5+ creatures you win combat by a wide margin after resolution.

engines.title: Extra Cycle Finds the Cascade
engines.body: On the draw you see 8 cards, increasing cascade spell odds. Keep any hand with 2+ cyclers on the draw even without cascade — the extra card often finds Violent Outburst or Ardent Plea. Against aggressive decks on the draw: Grief hands (T1 discard their key threat) become more valuable since you’re a turn behind on the clock and need to disrupt their development.

engines.title: Second Cascade
engines.body: They counter Living End on the cascade trigger: your creatures stay cycled and you need a second cascade spell. Deploy Grief or Subtlety to attack their hand / remove their next counter. Then Ardent Plea or second Outburst next turn. With 8 cascade spells in the deck, you often have a second line. The key: don’t tap out casting Outburst into obvious open counter mana.

engines.title: Commandeer Their Threat
engines.body: Nihil Spellbomb or Endurance exiles your GY. You have no creatures to reanimate. Pivot: Commandeer steals their best permanent (Titan, Solitude, planeswalker) for free using 2 blue cards from hand. Inevitable Betrayal (suspend) also takes their creature eventually. In the worst case, your Grief and Subtlety bodies are still 3/1 and 3/3 flying threats. You can win fair.

engines.title: Violent Outburst (Instant Speed)
engines.body: Violent Outburst cascades at instant speed on their end step. This is the primary cascade vehicle because they can’t Counterspell at instant speed efficiently and they’re often tapped out. Cast on their EOT for maximum information: you’ve seen their whole turn, they’ve spent their mana. Living End resolves into a defenseless board.

engines.title: Ardent Plea (Backup Cascade)
engines.body: Ardent Plea cascades at sorcery speed but also gives all your creatures exalted. Use when Violent Outburst is unavailable or when you want to cascade on your main phase with open mana backup. The exalted bonus (+1/+1 when attacking alone) is relevant in fair games where you’re winning with Grief/Subtlety bodies instead of a full Living End board.

engines.title: Grief + Subtlety Tempo
engines.body: Grief evokes for {B} — discard a black card, target player discards a nonland card. Subtlety evokes for {U}{U}— put a creature or planeswalker on top of their library. These are your disruption pieces and fair-mode threats. When Living End is shut off, Grief + Subtlety are 3/1 and 3/3 flying bodies. Lead with Grief on T1 to strip their key card, follow with cascade on T2–3.

engines.title: T2 Cascade (7 Creatures)
engines.body: T1: Cycle Street Wraith (free) + cycle Deadshot Minotaur {2}{R/G}. T2: Violent Outburst ({1}{R}{G}) — cascade into Living End. Reanimate 2+ creatures, swing for lethal. Requires: Outburst + 2 cyclers + 3 mana by T2. Rare but real. Even 3 creatures reanimated on T2 is often a winning board.

engines.title: T3 Cascade (5+ Creatures)
engines.body: T1: Cycle Street Wraith (free). T2: Cycle Architects of Will or Architects of Will. T3: Violent Outburst on their EOT. Reanimate 4–5 creatures with flash haste from Subtlety bodies. Swing on T4 for lethal. This is the default. 5 creatures in GY by T3 = dominant board post-LE.

engines.title: Grief First, Cascade Second
engines.body: Cascade T2–3: Fair decks with no interaction in hand. Go as fast as possible. Grief first: They have open blue mana (Force of Negation read) or Endurance visible. T1 Grief strips their counter or GY hate, then cascade T3 safely. Losing a turn is worth it to protect the cascade.

engines.title: Counter the CASCADE Trigger, Not Living End
engines.body: When you cast Violent Outburst, cascade triggers and goes on the stack. You THEN reveal cards until you hit Living End and cast it for free. At this point there are TWO things on the stack: the cascade trigger result (Living End) and the original Outburst. Counter Living End on the stack and the Outburst still resolves as a +1/+1 spell. This is why opponents should counter the cascade trigger, not

engines.title: Living End Returns Your Creatures THEN Kills Theirs
engines.body: Living End has two clauses that happen in order: (1) each player sacrifices all creatures they control, (2) then each player returns all creature cards from their GY to the battlefield. Your creatures come back AFTER theirs die. This means if they have no creatures and you have 5 in the GY, the board is yours cleanly. But if they have creatures, they also die — don’t reanimate into a board where t

engines.title: Grief Evoke Targets Nonland Cards Only
engines.body: Grief’s evoke ability (discard a black card, target player discards a nonland card from their hand) targets a specific player and forces them to discard any nonland card of your choice. You see their whole hand. This is why Grief is your T1 disruption — strip their counter, Endurance, or key combo piece before T2 cascade. Note: Grief’s body is a 3/1 with menace even if you evoke it immediately. Th

engines.title: Each Player Exiles Their GY
engines.body: ALL creature cards from ALL graveyards are exiled simultaneously. Your cycled creatures (Striped Riverwinder, Street Wraith, etc.) are exiled. Opponent's creatures in GY are also exiled. Non-creature cards (instants, sorceries, lands) stay in the graveyard — only creature cards are exiled.

engines.title: Each Player Sacrifices All Creatures
engines.body: ALL creatures in play are sacrificed simultaneously. Your cascade creature (Violent Outburst doesn't leave a body, but Shardless Agent is a 2/2 that dies here). Opponent's entire board is wiped. Sacrifice — not destroy. Indestructible doesn't save them. Death triggers fire (Blood Artist, etc.).

engines.title: Exiled Creatures Return
engines.body: ALL cards exiled in Step 1 enter the battlefield simultaneously. Your 5/5 Riverwinder, 7/7 Waker of Waves, 6/5 Troll, 3/4 Street Wraith — all enter at once. ETB triggers fire (Architects of Will, Foundation Breaker, Grief). ONLY cards exiled in Step 1 return — creatures sacrificed in Step 2 that got exiled by replacement effects (Leyline of the Void) do NOT return.

engines.title: No GY Hate Visible
engines.body: G1, no sideboard: cascade as fast as possible. The correct line is almost always T3 cascade on their EOT. You’re fastest without GY hate and every turn you wait gives them a draw step to find it.

engines.title: Counter or Hate Visible
engines.body: Open blue mana, they held mana for something, you see Endurance or Nihil Spellbomb from a previous game. T1 Grief strips the interaction, T3 cascade safely. Trading T1 for protection is worth it every time.

engines.title: GY Is Exiled
engines.body: Nihil Spellbomb or Endurance cleared your GY and you can’t rebuild in time. Commandeer their best threat. Inevitable Betrayal suspends for a free steal later. Your Grief + Subtlety bodies attack. You can still win — don’t scoop to GY hate.

engines.title: Below 3 Creatures in GY
engines.body: Living End with 1–2 creatures in GY is often a losing play — they return 1–2 bodies and their board may be bigger. Wait until you have 3+ (ideally 5+) in GY before cascading. Cycle aggressively on T1–2 to hit the threshold before committing.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Low Endurance and Nihil Spellbomb density in expected sideboards (below 20% of SB slots). Fair midrange field — your T3 board is larger than anything they assemble. Few Force of Negation builds in the room. Combo mirrors are likely (Storm, Amulet) — you race them. You’ve practiced the Grief setup for counter-heavy matchups.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy Endurance meta — flash GY exile on Living End resolution shuffles your creatures away. High Nihil Spellbomb density — instant-speed GY exile before cascade resolves. Multiple Surgical Extraction builds (strips a key cycler type from your deck). You haven’t practiced the Commandeer pivot game — you’ll concede when you should be stealing their threats.

engines.title: Shardless Agent ×4
engines.body: Your cascade spell. Four copies guarantees you cascade into Living End consistently. Zero wiggle room — the deck needs all 4 to function.

engines.title: Violent Outburst ×4
engines.body: Your instant-speed cascade enabler. Four copies means Living End is always available at instant speed — you can cascade on their end step and swing for lethal on your turn.

engines.title: Street Wraith
engines.body: 4 in fast metas where cycling for 2 life on T1 is worth the life loss (fills GY faster). 3 in slower metas. The free cycle makes it a GY filler that never uses mana.

engines.title: Subtlety (SB)
engines.body: 2 copies when you expect Teferi, Time Raveler (which would make your cascade trigger useless on their turn). Cut to 1 when Teferi isn't widespread.

engines.title: Grief count (SB)
engines.body: 3 vs disruption-heavy metas where clearing their hand before cascading is critical. 2 as a general hedge. Evoke Grief on T0, evoke Grief again off Ephemerate — this is your sideboard "turn 0 combo" vs combo opponents.

engines.title: Cascade Sequencing
engines.body: Cast Violent Outburst, confirm cascade hits Living End, execute the board reset in order.

engines.title: Force Timing
engines.body: Hold Force of Negation for their GY hate, not their cantrips. Drill the prioritization.

engines.title: Post-Board Lines
engines.body: Practice playing through Endurance, Nihil Spellbomb, and Rest in Peace.

engines.title: Clock Practice
engines.body: Living End games are quick. G2/G3 can drag — know your clock.

engines.title: Zero MV ≤ 2 Nonland Spells
engines.body: Cascade finds the first nonland card costing less than MV 3. Living End (MV 0) must always be that card. Any MV 0–2 nonland spell = cascade hits it instead. Zero exceptions. Cycling creatures cost ≥ 3 to cast (not cycle cost — cast cost). Force of Negation is MV 3. Subtlety is MV 4. All legal.

engines.title: T1–T2 Cycle → T3 EOT Cascade
engines.body: Turns 1–2: cycle Street Wraith (free), Horror ({B}), Monstrous Carabid ({B/R}), Curator ({U}), Waker of Waves (cost). T3 EOT: Violent Outburst (instant) → cascade → Living End → hat trick (cycle more on stack) → resolve → 5–7 creature board. Attack for lethal T4.

LOTUS FIELDCOMBO.kill_turn: REFERENCEPro Tour Murders at Karlov Manor — Top4 (Mingyang Chen)
LOTUS FIELDCOMBO.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "This is the only deck in Pioneer that generates unlimited mana with lands alone. Once you have two Lotus Fields and one Hidden Strings, every subsequent turn you can cast every spell in your deck. The opponent is playing a fair game while you break the rules of mana entirely." Lotus Field Combo is Pioneer's most complex and uniquely powerful combo deck. The engine is built around Lotus Field — a land that enters tapped, requires sacrificing two lands when it enters, has hexproof, and taps for three mana of any one color. On its own it's a difficult setup. But with The
LOTUS FIELDCOMBO.mulligan:
Mulligan
Need a Path to Lotus Field by T3
Keep: any hand with Lotus Field, OR Sylvan Scrying/Arboreal Grazer to find it, and 3 lands including one GU dual.

engines.title: Hexproof Lands Can't Be Targeted
engines.body: Lotus Field has hexproof — it can't be targeted by spells or abilities opponents control. Field of Ruin can't destroy it. Single-target removal doesn't exist for it. The primary hate is Damping Sphere (stops multi-mana lands) and High Noon (stops untapping). Most decks have zero maindeck answers.

engines.title: T4–5 Consistent Kill
engines.body: Arboreal Grazer on T1 + Lotus Field on T2 + Thespian's Stage on T3 + Hidden Strings loop on T4 = kill on T4. The combo kills faster than most control decks can marshal answers. Greasefang's T3 is faster, but Lotus beats every non-combo deck before they stabilize.

engines.title: Fae of Wishes is a Toolbox
engines.body: Fae of Wishes's Granted adventure searches your sideboard for any card. This means your 15-card sideboard is a toolbox of every answer, win condition, and backup you could need. Hate card ruining your plan? Granted fetches Boseiju, Who Endures. Need a sweeper? Granted finds it. Opponents must answer both your combo AND your toolbox.

engines.title: Land Assembly + Survival
engines.body: T1: Arboreal Grazer (put Lotus Field from hand onto battlefield tapped) OR Sylvan Scrying (find Lotus/Stage). T2: Play Thespian's Stage. Arboreal Grazer blocks 1-power attackers as a 0/3. T3: Play Lotus Field — sacrifice exactly two non-Lotus lands. Now have one Lotus Field producing {3}. Don't cast Hidden Strings yet — save for the full combo turn.

engines.title: Stage Copies Lotus
engines.body: Tap both Lotus Field + Stage for 6 mana floating. Activate Stage: pay {2}, copy Lotus Field. Stage's ETB as Lotus Field says sacrifice two other lands — sacrifice 2 basics. Now have 6 mana floating and 2 Lotus Fields (both Hexproof). This is the pivotal moment: you now generate 6 mana per turn and the engine is assembled. Use remaining mana for Impulse/Vizier cycle.

engines.title: Hidden Strings → Cipher Loop → Win
engines.body: Cast Hidden Strings, untap both Fields, Cipher on Grazer. Attack with Grazer. Cipher triggers — untap both Fields for free. Use 6 mana for Pore Over the Pages (draw 3, untap Fields again). Repeat 2-3 times. Now have 15-20 mana and enough cards. Cast Dig Through Time (delve, {U}) → find Emergent Ultimatum → win.

engines.title: Need a Path to Lotus Field by T3
engines.body: Keep: any hand with Lotus Field, OR Sylvan Scrying/Arboreal Grazer to find it, and 3 lands including one GU dual. Mulligan: no path to Lotus before T5, hands with 5+ lands and 0 spells, hands with only finishers. At 6: Grazer + Lotus + 2 basics is excellent. At 5: Sylvan Scrying + 2 lands + 1 untap = keepable. At 4: Lotus + Stage + 2 basics + Impulse is functional.

engines.title: Lotus Field × 2 = 6 Mana
engines.body: Two Lotus Fields produce 6 mana of any color. Hidden Strings costs {1U} = 2 mana → net +4. Pore Over the Pages costs {4U} = 5 mana, untaps 3 Fields (or 2 + basics) → net +1 and draws 3. Vizier cycling costs {1G} = 2 mana, untaps one Field → net +1 and draws 1. Every untap effect generates net positive mana when two Fields are in play. Each cycle compounds.

engines.title: Hidden Strings on Grazer
engines.body: Cipher: exile Hidden Strings encoded on Arboreal Grazer. Whenever Grazer deals combat damage to a player, copy Hidden Strings and cast it for free. Each attack: Grazer hits → copy resolves → untap both Fields → 6 free mana. If unblocked, 2-3 attacks generates 18 free mana. Cast Pore Over the Pages (draws 3 + untaps) and Dig Through Time in the same turn to find Emergent Ultimatum and win.

engines.title: Fae of Wishes — Sideboard Access
engines.body: Granted ({2U}) searches sideboard for any card. Your sideboard is split: wish targets (Omniscience, Peer into the Abyss, Oracle, Ultimatum, sweepers, hate answers) + real SB cards. Pre-combo: wish for Depopulate to survive. Mid-combo: wish for Omniscience then cast Peer for free. Post-board: Teferi, Time Raveler prevents their instant-speed interaction during your combo turn.

engines.title: Survive to T5 With Wishboard Sweepers
engines.body: Against RDW, Selesnya: Grazer blocks early drops. Wish for Ritual of Soot (destroys all MV-3 or less creatures) at 5 or fewer life. After sweeping, execute the combo immediately. Leyline Binding exiles Eidolon of the Great Revel. Your only goal is not dying — the combo itself wins the game once assembled.

engines.title: Race Their Threats
engines.body: Against UR Cutter: they can't target Lotus Field (Hexproof). Protect Stage before copying — activate Stage on the same turn you deploy it (they can bounce Stage before it activates). Wish for Teferi, Time Raveler G2 to prevent their instant-speed Into the Flood Maw from bouncing Stage. Execute combo T5 at latest.

engines.title: Answer Their Hate Card First
engines.body: Against UW Control: identify High Noon (prevents land untaps). Destroy it with Blast Zone (MV 2 = activate for {2}) or wish for Boseiju before comboing. Mystical Dispute (SB) counters their blue spells. Teferi, Time Raveler prevents them from casting High Noon at instant speed G2. Don't attempt the combo while High Noon is in play — it's impossible to win through it.

engines.title: Omniscience + Peer + Oracle
engines.body: Omniscience: all spells cost {0}. Cast via Emergent Ultimatum or wish with Granted mid-combo. Peer into the Abyss: target player draws half their deck and loses half their life. Target yourself post-Omniscience — draw 20+ cards. Thassa's Oracle: ETB — if devotion to blue ≥ library size, you win. After drawing your deck via Peer, Oracle wins with one blue mana up. These three form the Ultimatum pac

engines.title: Depopulate + Ritual of Soot
engines.body: Depopulate ({2WW}): exile all creatures. White mana available from Lotus Fields (any color). Ritual of Soot ({2BB}): destroy all MV-3 or less creatures. Your primary survival tools vs aggro — wish for whichever clears their board. Ritual of Soot hits Monastery Swiftspear, Thalia, Llanowar Elves, and Voice of Resurgence (exile rather than destroy via Depopulate prevents recursion). Black also avail

engines.title: Boseiju + Leyline Binding
engines.body: Boseiju, Who Endures ({1G}): instant, destroy target artifact or enchantment. Hits Damping Sphere, High Noon, Rest in Peace at instant speed. Can't be countered (channel ability). Leyline Binding ({5WUBRG}, domain): exile target nonland permanent until Binding leaves. With GU basics in play, costs {1} by T4 effectively — instant speed permanent exile including planeswalkers and artifact-creatures.

engines.title: Mystical Dispute + Teferi, Time Raveler
engines.body: Mystical Dispute ({2U}, {U} if opponent controls blue): counters any blue spell. Best vs UW Control (counters High Noon, Supreme Verdict) and UR Cutter (counters Into the Flood Maw). Teferi, Time Raveler ({1WU}): opponent can only cast at sorcery speed + bounces a permanent. Prevents instant-speed counters during your combo turn. Cast Teferi, then execute the entire combo with no fear of their ins

engines.title: Leyline Binding Ã—2
engines.body: {5}{W} (reducible by basic land types) Instant: Exile target nonland permanent. Board in vs Selesnya Company (exiles their key creature at instant speed), Orzhov Greasefang (exiles Greasefang before it can crew), RDW (exiles their haste threat). With 5 basic land types, this costs {W} â€” virtually free. Exile means no GY recursion.

engines.title: Mystical Dispute Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{U} or {U} targeting blue spells. Board in vs UW Control (one-mana hard counter for all their blue spells) and UR Cutter (counters their key blue threats). The {U} mode makes this your most mana-efficient counter in blue mirror matchups. Board it out vs non-blue decks where it costs {3}.

engines.title: Soul-Guide Lantern Ã—2
engines.body: {1} Artifact: Exile target GY at instant speed. Draw a card when it goes to your GY. Board in vs Orzhov Greasefang (exiles Parhelion II before Greasefang can crew) and Arclight Phoenix (exiles Phoenix before it triggers back). Never dead â€” in non-GY matchups crack it for the cantrip. Always crack at instant speed, never during your main phase.

engines.title: Rending Volley Ã—1
engines.body: {R} Instant: Destroy target white or blue creature. Board in vs Arclight Phoenix (destroys their key white or blue attackers) and Greasefang (destroys Greasefang which is a white creature). One mana, instant speed, destroy â€” extremely efficient at answering the exact creature type that threatens you most in Pioneer.

engines.title: 3 Lotus + 4 Stage + 4 Hidden Strings + 4 Pore
engines.body: The four irreducible combo pieces. 3 Lotus is correct (Stage copies it; 4 is dead draws in multiples). 4 Stage ensures you always find the copy. Hidden Strings + Pore are both mandatory — neither alone generates enough mana for the combo turn. Never cut any of these.

engines.title: 4 Dig Through Time + 4 Sylvan Scrying
engines.body: Dig finds every missing piece at {U} after filling GY. Sylvan finds Lotus or Stage on T2 ensuring the land assembly. Both run as 4-of to maximize the probability of seeing them in the setup turns. Cutting either below 4 makes hands inconsistent.

engines.title: Fae of Wishes
engines.body: 3 is reference. 4 in metas where the wishboard provides essential answers you need early (heavy aggro). 3 in metas where you combo before needing the wishboard. More Fae means more mid-combo wish targets but slower setup turns.

engines.title: Vizier of Tumbling Sands
engines.body: 4 is standard. Can trim to 3 in metas where the cycling is less critical. Vizier provides the "free" untap effect that bridges the gap between Hidden Strings activations. Don't cut below 3 — you need redundant untap effects.

engines.title: Behold the Beyond vs Dark Petition
engines.body: Behold the Beyond is the backup finisher (draw 7 for {5BBB}). Dark Petition is the tutor ({2BBB}, spell mastery adds {BBB} to your mana pool — practically a free spell). In faster metas, cut a Behold for more Dark Petitions (find any card faster). In slower metas, Behold provides more card advantage.

engines.title: Adjust 7-8 Wish Targets Per Meta
engines.body: Heavy aggro: add a second Ritual of Soot or a third sweeper. Heavy control: add Veil of Summer (hexproof for your spells vs blue/black). Heavy GY hate: add Gemstone Caverns for speed or a second Boseiju. The wishboard is your most tunable slot — the best players run the exact 7-8 wish targets for the expected field.

engines.title: The Complete Kill Line
engines.body: Run through the kill line 10 times before each event: T3 Lotus Field (float mana → sacrifice 2 basics → pass). T4 tap Fields → Stage copies Lotus (float 6 → sacrifice 2 more basics) → Hidden Strings untaps Fields → Cipher on Grazer → pass. T5 attack, Cipher triggers × 3 → 18 free mana → Pore Over the Pages → Dig Through Time → Emergent Ultimatum → win. If you can't run this mentally in 60 seconds,

engines.title: Hate Card Matrix
engines.body: High Noon → Blast Zone (MV 2) or Boseiju wish. Damping Sphere → Blast Zone (MV 2) or Boseiju wish. Field of Ruin → deploy Stage and activate immediately. Narset, Parter of Veils → wish for Ugin ({-X exiles} or use Leyline Binding). Thought-Knot Seer → keep redundant combo pieces in hand. Pithing Needle (naming Stage) → play actual Lotus Field + second Stage OR wish for Boseiju. Leyline of the Void

engines.title: Wishboard Matches Expected Field
engines.body: Heavy aggro (RDW, Selesnya): confirm 2 sweeper wish targets + Leyline Binding. Heavy control (UW Control): confirm Teferi, Time Raveler + Mystical Dispute + Boseiju for High Noon. Heavy combo: Leyline Binding for their hate artifacts. 15 SB cards — walk through each card's target matchup before registration.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Mountain only = RDW (wish for Ritual of Soot G1 if life gets low). Godless Shrine = Greasefang (race, board Leyline Binding). Steam Vents = UR Cutter (protect Stage, board Mystical Dispute). Hallowed Fountain = UW Control (target High Noon, board Mystical Dispute + Teferi). Forest = Selesnya Company (Grazer blocks, board Leyline Binding for Damping Sphere).

engines.title: Lotus Setup Drill
engines.body: Practice the Lotus Field setup sequence. T3: play Lotus Field (enter tapped, sacrifice 2 lands). T4: cast Hidden Strings (untap Lotus twice, tap for 6 mana). Execute blindfolded.

engines.title: Stage Copy Timing
engines.body: Practice the Thespian's Stage copy window. Stage must have 3 mana to activate: {3}: copy target land. Know when you have enough mana to copy Lotus AND have Hidden Strings in hand.

engines.title: Damping Sphere Protocol
engines.body: Practice the Damping Sphere game plan. They play Sphere: immediately cast Leyline Binding (for {W} with 5 basic types) to exile it. Know your anti-hate answers before they cast hate.

engines.title: End Step Spells
engines.body: Practice casting key spells at your opponent's EOT. Pore Over the Pages at their EOT: draw 3, untap 2 lands. This lets you tap Lotus for the draw and untap it for your main phase.

engines.title: Lotus Field + Thespian's Stage
engines.body: Lotus Field: taps for {G/G/G} or {U/U/U} or any three of the same color. Hexproof. Enters tapped, sacrifice 2 lands. Thespian's Stage: {T}, pay {2}: becomes a copy of target land. When Stage copies Lotus Field, Stage already entered — no sacrifice trigger fires. You now have two lands that together tap for 6 mana. Cast Hidden Strings for 2. Net 4 mana per cycle. This is Pioneer's only infinite man

engines.title: Hidden Strings + Vizier of Tumbling Sands
engines.body: Hidden Strings: {1U} instant, untap two target permanents. Cipher onto a creature — every time that creature deals combat damage, cast Hidden Strings again for free. Net mana per activation: +4 (tap 6, spend 2 to cast). Vizier of Tumbling Sands: cycle {2U} or pay {T}: untap target permanent. Both untap both Lotus Fields for less than they generate. Chain until you have effectively unlimited mana.

engines.title: Emergent Ultimatum
engines.body: {3BBBGGG} sorcery: search your library for three cards with different names, reveal them, opponent exiles one, you cast the other two without paying their mana costs. Standard lines: (1) Omniscience + Behold the Beyond + Dark Petition — they can exile one; you still cast two that win the game. (2) Peer into the Abyss on opponent — they draw half their library and lose half their life immediately.

engines.title: Fae of Wishes + Granted
engines.body: Fae of Wishes adventure spell (Granted): {1U}, search your sideboard for a card and put it in your hand. Your sideboard is a custom toolbox: sweepers (Depopulate, Supreme Verdict) for aggro, Dovin's Veto for counterspell wars, Boseiju for hate permanents, Ugin as an alternative sweeper/win. Fae of Wishes as a creature provides a 1/4 blocker. Every hate card in Pioneer has a Granted answer in your

engines.title: Get Both Lotuses in Play
engines.body: T1: Arboreal Grazer (put a land from hand onto battlefield tapped), play a land. T2: Play Lotus Field (sacrifice two lands — the Grazer land and your T1 land). T3: Play Thespian's Stage, activate Stage targeting Lotus Field (pay {2} + tap Stage). Stage becomes Lotus Field — no sacrifice trigger. You now have two hexproof Lotus Fields. This is the primary setup path.

engines.title: Generate Unlimited Mana
engines.body: With two Lotus Fields (6 mana per tap): cast Hidden Strings ({1U}), untap both Fields. Net: +4 mana per Hidden Strings activation. Cast enough cantrips and Hidden Strings copies until you have 7+ mana floating ({3BBBGGG}). Vizier of Tumbling Sands cycles {2U} and also untaps a land. Pore Over the Pages ({4U}) draws 3 and untaps two lands. Chain until you have Ultimatum mana.

engines.title: Emergent Ultimatum Lines
engines.body: With unlimited mana and Ultimatum in hand: cast Ultimatum, find Omniscience + Behold the Beyond + Dark Petition. Opponent exiles one. You cast the remaining two for free. Omniscience: all your spells cost 0 mana. Behold the Beyond: tutor three cards to your hand. Cast everything. Alternatively: Peer into the Abyss on opponent (they draw half library, lose half life) ends the game immediately.

engines.title: Need: Lotus Field + Scrying Effect
engines.body: Keep: any hand with Lotus Field OR Sylvan Scrying to find it. Ideal opening: Arboreal Grazer + Lotus Field + Thespian's Stage + Hidden Strings (this is your T4 kill). Mulligan: hands with zero lands, hands with no way to find Lotus Field, and hands with 5+ noncombo cards and no dig spells. Mulligan aggressively — to 5 if needed — for the right combo pieces. 4 Lotus Field + 3 Thespian's Stage means

engines.title: Arboreal Grazer + Sylvan Scrying
engines.body: Arboreal Grazer: {G}, put a land from hand onto the battlefield tapped. Gets you an extra land per turn, specifically putting Lotus Field into play earlier. Sylvan Scrying: {1G}, search for any land and put it in hand. Finds Lotus Field (piece 1) or Thespian's Stage (piece 2). With 4 of each, you find your combo pieces consistently in any opening hand with 3+ cards in it.

engines.title: Hidden Strings + Pore Over the Pages
engines.body: Hidden Strings: untap 2 permanents for {1U}. Net +4 mana per activation with two Lotus Fields. Pore Over the Pages: draw 3, discard 1, untap 2 lands for {4U}. Net +2 mana while drawing. Vizier cycles for {2U} and untaps any land. Together these convert 6-mana output into unlimited mana while simultaneously drawing you through your deck to find Emergent Ultimatum.

engines.title: Emergent Ultimatum Lines
engines.body: Primary kill: Ultimatum → Omniscience + anything (cast free). Secondary kill: Peer into the Abyss on opponent (draw ~30 cards, lose ~20 life). Backup kill (via Fae Granted): Approach of the Second Sun (cast twice with Omniscience). Ugin sweep + Mastermind's Acquisition for remaining pieces. Three separate kill conditions means hate one and you switch to another.

engines.title: Survive to T4
engines.body: Against RDW, UR Cutter, Selesnya Company: your goal is staying alive until turn 4-5 when you execute. Arboreal Grazer provides a 0/3 blocker that stalls attackers. Fae of Wishes fetches Depopulate, Ritual of Soot, or Supreme Verdict from sideboard when you're about to die. Voyaging Satyr can block. Execute before they kill you — your kill is faster than most aggro decks' sustained pressure.

engines.title: Bait Counters, Execute
engines.body: Against UW Control: their High Noon (SB) stops your untap engine. Answer it with Boseiju or Blast Zone. Their Damping Sphere prevents Lotus from tapping for more than one mana — answer immediately via Granted + Boseiju. Hold Hidden Strings until you can chain through their counterspells. Lier, Disciple of the Drowned gives your spells flashback and makes them uncounterable — resolve Lier, then com

engines.title: Race to Your Kill Turn
engines.body: Against Greasefang: they kill T3, you kill T4-5. You lose game 1 if they have their T3 hand. G2-3 you have access to Dovin's Veto (counters their Greasefang) and Necromentia (removes Parhelion II from their deck). Against Phoenix: you're faster. Against other combo: calculate whose kill turn is faster and either race or answer their combo piece via Granted toolbox.

engines.title: Approach of the Second Sun + Omniscience
engines.body: Approach of the Second Sun: the safest win condition vs control. Cast it twice (the second cast wins). With Omniscience in play, you can cycle through your deck finding Approach, cast it, then immediately cast it again from the top. Omniscience (second copy): provides redundancy for the Ultimatum line — if they exile your main-deck Omniscience from Emergent Ultimatum, Granted fetches the second co

engines.title: Boseiju + Blast Zone + Damping Sphere
engines.body: Boseiju, Who Endures: channel for {2G} to destroy target noncreature permanent — cannot be countered. Destroys Damping Sphere, High Noon, Leyline of Sanctity, Rest in Peace. The most important G2-3 Granted target when facing hate permanents. Blast Zone in the sideboard adds redundancy for destroying MV-specific permanents. Damping Sphere in your OWN sideboard: a mirror-specific tool.

engines.title: Depopulate + Ritual of Soot + Supreme Verdict
engines.body: Three sweepers at different mana values: Ritual of Soot ({2BB}, deal 2 to all creatures) for early boards. Depopulate ({2WW}, exile all creatures) for resilient creature decks. Supreme Verdict ({1WWU}, destroy all creatures, uncounterable) for blue matchups. When you're about to die to aggro in G1, Granted for the right sweeper at end of their turn buys a full turn and often wins you the game from

engines.title: Dovin's Veto + Aether Gust + Necromentia
engines.body: Dovin's Veto: hard counter, uncounterable itself. For combo matchups where you need to counter a specific key spell (Greasefang, their Dovin's Veto, Emergent Ultimatum in mirror). Aether Gust: bounces a red or green permanent or counters a red/green spell — primarily for RDW and Selesnya. Necromentia: exile all copies of a named card from opponent's hand, library, and GY. Naming Parhelion II again

engines.title: 4 Lotus Field
engines.body: The deck's engine land. 4 copies ensures you find it consistently in any hand. Cutting even one significantly reduces combo consistency. Never cut any.

engines.title: 4 Hidden Strings
engines.body: The mana loop enabler. Without 4 Hidden Strings you can't reliably chain enough activations to reach Ultimatum mana in a reasonable number of turns. The Cipher ability is also a relevant combat tool.

engines.title: 4 Pore Over the Pages + 4 Sylvan Scrying
engines.body: Scrying finds the combo lands — never cut any. Pore generates mana AND draws toward Ultimatum — 4 is the correct number for combo redundancy. Cutting either reduces kill turn reliability by a full turn on average.

engines.title: Arboreal Grazer
engines.body: 4 main is correct in most metas — accelerates to T4 kill. In heavy aggro metas where blocking matters more than speed, still keep 4 (the 0/3 blocks effectively). Only cut if your meta is 100% control where the blocker doesn't help.

engines.title: Lier, Disciple of the Drowned
engines.body: 1 main is the floor. In heavy control metas go to 2. Lier makes the control matchup from Even to Strongly Favorable. Don't cut it entirely — it's often your G1 control backup plan.

engines.title: Adjust Based on Field
engines.body: Heavy aggro: more sweepers in wish board (3 sweeper effects). Heavy GY: Necromentia becomes more important. Heavy control with High Noon: two Boseijus in wish board. The wish board is the most powerful meta-adaptation tool in Pioneer — rebuild it every week based on the current meta.

engines.title: Kill Turn By Matchup
engines.body: vs Aggro: kill T4 or lose. vs Control: kill T5-6 with countermagic backup. vs Combo: race — know their kill turn and compare. Fastest Lotus kill: T1 Grazer + T2 Lotus + T3 Stage + T4 loop = T4 Ultimatum. Average kill: T5-6. Know which hands achieve T4 vs T5 kills and keep accordingly.

engines.title: The Hate Card Matrix
engines.body: Damping Sphere → Boseiju or Blast Zone. High Noon → Boseiju or Blast Zone. Field of Ruin → affects Thespian's Stage NOT Lotus Field (hexproof). Into the Flood Maw → catastrophic if bounces Lotus. Leyline of Sanctity → Necromentia or Boseiju. Rest in Peace → doesn't affect Lotus combo (no GY dependency). Know which hate cards do what before round 1.

engines.title: Emergent Ultimatum Piles
engines.body: Memorize all three two-card subsets of Omniscience + Behold the Beyond + Dark Petition. Practice the sequence for each one. Know what to fetch if they exile any one of the three. Don't improvise at the table — this costs time and mistakes. Have a backup pile for when they board RIP (fetch Peer into the Abyss instead).

engines.title: Watch for T1 Hate
engines.body: If they play Island T1 + Damping Sphere on T2: fetch Boseiju immediately before continuing setup. Mountain T1 = RDW (fetch Ritual of Soot if needed). Godless Shrine = Greasefang (fetch Necromentia on T3 G2). Forest = Selesnya (block aggressively with Grazer, execute T4). Hallowed Fountain = Control (save Granted for Boseiju when they drop Sphere/Noon).

Mono-GreenLandfall.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Overview "You are a ramp deck that can go both taller and wider than most of the format. You have a solid aggro plan, a built-in combo kill, and a grind mode. The opponent never knows which angle to defend." — January, RC Vancouver 2nd Place Mono-Green Landfall is the Tier A deck in Standard, sitting at 61.3% win rate across 23,000 BO3 games (Plat–Mythic). It is the most popular deck you will face at Cincinnati and DC, and also one of the strongest to pilot — three distinct win conditions that switch dynamically based on what the opponent presents. Against aggressive opponents
Mono-GreenLandfall.mulligan: mulligans aggressively — an opener with no 1-drop or ramp is often wrong.

engines.title: Counter Stack + Trample
engines.body: Sazh's Chocobo enters as a 0/1 but grows a counter every time a land enters — turn 1 Chocobo into turn 2 Ascension means every subsequent land gives +1/+1. Stack trample from Ascension and swing. Effective against any deck that doesn't block efficiently. T1 Chocobo is a clock they must respect immediately.

engines.body: Icetill Explorer + Mightform Harmonizer + Escape Tunnel (or trample enabler) creates one-shot potential from any board state. engines.title: Ramp + Engine
engines.body: Best: T1 Llanowar Elves → T2 Earthbender Ascension (earthbends 2 + fetches a basic). Now every land gives Ascension a quest counter. Also strong: T1 Sazh's Chocobo → T2 Ascension or Badgermole Cub. T1 Chocobo means it's already been growing before Ascension fires. T2 Cub earthbending a fetch = 2 landfall triggers on T2.

engines.title: Deploy Threats
engines.body: Turn 3: Mightform Harmonizer (warp it immediately if removal is likely), or Sapling Nursery (first Treefolk token lands the same turn if you play a land). Turn 4: Icetill Explorer — immediately play your land for turn, mill, and if there's a fetch in the GY you can replay it for a second land drop triggering Nursery + Harmonizer simultaneously.

engines.title: Kill Window
engines.body: Assess which plan is live: board full of Treefolk → swing for lethal with trample from Ascension. Icetill + Harmonizer + evasion piece (Escape Tunnel) → chain land plays, double target creature power, Escape Tunnel for unblockable, deal 20+ damage. Mossborn Hydra with 3+ counters → one more land = 8+ power trampler.

engines.title: What You Need
engines.body: 1. Icetill Explorer on the battlefield (extra land plays + land from GY). 2. Mightform Harmonizer on the battlefield (doubles power on landfall). 3. A creature with at least 2 power (Chocobo with counters, Badgermole Cub, or Harmonizer itself). 4. Multiple land plays available — either fetch lands in hand or GY, and/or Ba Sing Se activation. 5. Escape Tunnel or trample enabler for the creature.

engines.title: Execute the Kill
engines.body: Activate Escape Tunnel targeting your 2-power creature (unblockable). Play any land → Harmonizer triggers, double that creature's power (2 → 4). Play another land (fetch or GY land via Icetill) → double again (4 → 8). Again → 16. Again → 32. Attack with the 32-power unblockable creature for lethal. engines.body: Switch to Nursery plan: When you have 4+ lands and a Nursery on board and the opponent doesn't have a sweeper available. Treefolk tokens with reach block their fliers and attack profitably. Switch to combo plan: When they have a board full of blockers. One unblockable creature bypasses their entire defense. Stay on beatdown plan: Against control with no board — Chocobo + Ascension + attacks is fas

engines.title: Earthbend Caution
engines.body: Earthbending is strong but creates vulnerability: an earthbent land can be stunned (Floodpits Drowner), bounced (Into the Flood Maw), or killed before returning. In those cases you lose mana temporarily. Against Dimir: be careful earthbending when they have {1}{U} open — they can stun your earthbent land in response, leaving it as a dead permanent. Against control with open mana: earthbending is t

engines.body: Sequence: earthbend targets Fabled Passage → Passage becomes 0/0 creature with +1/+1 counter + haste (trigger 1: all your landfall sources fire). When it dies / next upkeep it returns as Fabled Passage → you can then sacrifice it to fetch a basic (trigger 2: all sources fire again). Two triggers from one earthbend. Escape Tunnel works identically as the earthbend target — earthbend it, it becomes

engines.body: Promising Vein: {T} add {C}, {1}{T} sacrifice to fetch basic tapped. Earthbend onto Vein → it becomes a creature (trigger 1). When it returns as Vein → sacrifice it {1}{T} to fetch a basic (trigger 2). Same double-trigger as a fetch. Use this when you've already used your Fabled Passages and Escape Tunnels — Promising Vein is your backup double-trigger earthbend target in the mid-to-late game.

engines.title: What You Need in Play
engines.body: Mandatory: Icetill Explorer (extra land plays, lands from GY). Mandatory: Mightform Harmonizer (doubles a creature's power on each landfall). Mandatory: A creature with power ≤ 2 at the moment Escape Tunnel activates. Mandatory: Escape Tunnel in play (or multiple other land plays available for the doubling chain even without unblockable — use trample from Ascension instead). The power-2 check is c

engines.body: Escape Tunnel activation first — sacrifice Tunnel targeting your 2-power creature (unblockable). Do this before any land drops that would trigger Harmonizer. Play land 1 → Harmonizer trigger: double target creature (2 → 4). Now it has 4 power. Play land 2 (fetch or GY land via Icetill) → Harmonizer trigger: double (4 → 8). Play land 3 → double (8 → 16). Play land 4 → double (16 → 32). Attack with

engines.title: Power Required vs Land Drops Available
engines.body: Starting power determines how many doublings you need: Start at 2 power (bare minimum): 2→4→8→16→32 = 4 doublings = 4 land drops needed. Start at 4 power (Harmonizer itself at 4/4): 4→8→16→32 = 3 doublings = 3 land drops. Start at 8 power (Chocobo with 8 counters): 8→16→32 = 2 doublings = 2 land drops. Count your available land plays before committing to the combo line — Icetill gives 1 extra, eac

engines.title: Hexproof + Trample Instead of Escape Tunnel
engines.body: Leatherhead, Swamp Stalker (5/4, trample, enters with hexproof counter) is the Harmonizer combo piece that doesn't need Escape Tunnel. Leatherhead already has trample — no need for unblockable. She has a hexproof counter — targeted removal can't stop the combo attempt mid-sequence. Start the Harmonizer chain with Leatherhead: 5→10→20→40 with only 3 doublings. The opponent cannot target her to brea

engines.title: Respond to the Sweeper on the Stack
engines.body: They cast Day of Judgment (destroy all creatures). Before it resolves, activate Nursery: exile Nursery, all Treefolk and Forests gain indestructible until EOT. Day of Judgment resolves — tries to destroy all creatures. Your Treefolk have indestructible — they are not destroyed. Day of Judgment is wasted. The two-Nursery bonus: If you have two Nurseries in play, activate one to protect your board,

engines.title: Treefolk AND Forests
engines.body: The ability grants indestructible to two categories: Treefolk (your tokens) AND Forests (your lands). This means: your earthbent Forest that's currently a creature also gains indestructible — it won't die to mass removal even in its creature form. But note: Forests as lands still get indestructible, which is mostly irrelevant against creature sweepers but matters against Destroy target land effect

engines.title: Search Your Library
engines.body: Find any creature or land. Put land into play tapped or creature into hand. Use this to: tutor Mightform Harmonizer for the combo kill when you have the other pieces assembled, tutor Leatherhead as a hexproof trample combo piece, tutor Fecund Greenshell as the 10-land anthem trigger, tutor Icetill Explorer as the engine piece. The tutoring mode effectively makes your deck have more copies of your

Your creature gets the counter first, then the fight damage uses the new power. Use to: kill their Ojer Axonil (your creature gets the counter, fights Ojer — if your creature has 5+ power, Ojer dies), kill their Shocking Sharpshooter (1/3 — any creature with 3+ pow

engines.title: Exile Target Artifact or Enchantment
engines.body: Your only main-deck answer to Stormchaser's Talent, Warleader's Call, Earthbender Ascension (in the mirror), and any other enchantment. Exile is permanent — no returning. Use fight mode on their creatures, exile mode on their enchantments. Don't use the exile mode on a creature when fight mode would handle it — the fight mode also gives your creature a permanent +1/+1 counter as a bonus.

Next turn: play Passage from GY (landfall trigger 1), sacrifice Passage to fetch a basic (landfall trigger 2), basic enters (landfall trigger 3 — wait, fetched basics don't trigger separately, just the basic entering as one event). Actually: Passage's sacrifice + fetch = one landfall event (the basic entering). So replaying Passage from GY = 2 landfall event

engines.body: A "naked" Icetill with no fetches in hand or GY is just a 2/4 for 4 with no immediate value. The correct deployment: T4 Icetill when you can immediately play a land and mill — even milling one card gives you a chance of hitting a fetch. Or deploy when you already have a Fabled Passage in GY (from a previous turn's normal play) — deploy Icetill, play your land for the turn, and immediately replay t

Never deploy Orb before your own key ETB

engines.body: Torpor Orb stops triggered abilities that trigger when creatures enter. It does NOT stop: Icetill Explorer's static abilities (play extra land, play from GY — those are continuous), Badgermole Cub's "tap creature for mana, add {G}" (that's triggered by tapping for mana, not by entering), Earthbender Ascension's landfall triggered ability (triggered by land entering, not creature entering). Orb is

engines.title: Combo Kill Through Flash Package
engines.body: Their flash package (Tidebinder, Drowner) can stun your earthbent lands and counter your ETBs. Don't over-rely on the earthbend plan — they can respond to it. The combo kill via Escape Tunnel bypasses their entire defensive setup: an unblockable threat ignores Floodpits Drowner's stun, Azure Beastbinder's power-2-block restriction, and their entire creature defense. Prioritize assembling Icetill +

engines.title: Race + Sapling Nursery
engines.body: Izzet Prowess races you with spells pumping small creatures. Your larger bodies trade favorably in combat, but their burn can close from long range. Sapling Nursery provides reach blockers that chump their 5/5 prowess creatures. The combo kill is fast enough to race them — assembling the kill on turn 4-5 is usually before they can burn you out. Mossborn Hydra from the SB grows faster than their th

engines.body: The mirror is decided by Mossborn Hydra. Whoever resolves and protects a Hydra first usually wins — one land drop doubles it, so a Hydra at 8 counters with one land in hand = 16-power trample that wins immediately. Sapling Nursery is not the plan here — a wall of 3/4 Treefolk is irrelevant against a 100-power Hydra. Side in the additional Hydra copies. Archdruid's Charm exile mode is excellent — e

engines.title: Sapling Nursery + Surrak
engines.body: Control has counterspells and sweepers but no clock. Sapling Nursery as an enchantment survives most sweepers. Deploy Nursery and let it generate Treefolk tokens faster than they can cast Wrath effects. Surrak, Elusive Hunter from the SB can't be countered and draws a card whenever they target your spells or creatures — forces a no-win situation. Sandman, Shifting Scoundrel from the SB grows to th

engines.title: Torpor Orb (vs Dimir, Reanimator, Spellementals)
engines.body: The most impactful sideboard card against the most popular opponent. Dimir Midrange's entire disruption package is ETB-based — Orb turns all of it off simultaneously. Three copies ensures you draw it G2/G3. Board in whenever you count 3+ ETBs in their key cards.

engines.title: All 4 Mossborn Hydra + Origin of Metalbending
engines.body: The mirror is won by Hydra. Board in all 4 total copies. Origin of Metalbending destroys their Sapling Nursery or Ascension. Board out all 4 Nurseries and Greenshell. The mirror is a pure speed race — slow cards lose.

engines.title: Icetill Explorer ×4
engines.body: Your entire engine. Below 4 copies and your double land drop consistency collapses. Never cut even one.

engines.title: Earthbender Ascension ×4
engines.body: Your scaling threat. Four copies guarantees you see it early. The deck is built around Ascension triggers — without it, your creatures are understatted.

engines.title: Mossborn Hydra
engines.body: 3 in counter-heavy metas (the uncounterable clause at 7 lands is your trump). 2 in aggro metas where 7 lands is too slow. Cut to 1 if the field is all aggro.

engines.title: Lumra, Bellow of the Woods
engines.body: 1 copy is the baseline finisher. 2 copies in control-heavy metas where you need a second win condition after they counter the first Lumra.

engines.title: Spelunking count
engines.body: 2 vs 3 depends on how often you need Lumra. 3 copies when Lumra is your primary win condition and you need to fill GY fast. 2 copies when your creatures carry the game without Lumra.

engines.title: Ascension Trigger Sequencing
engines.body: Practice the Earthbender Ascension trigger order. Play land → Ascension triggers → choose which creature gets the counter. Know which creature to pump for max value.

engines.title: Icetill Explorer Protection
engines.body: Practice protecting Icetill Explorer. Their removal on Explorer = your removal on their threat. Counter their removal before protecting Explorer.

engines.title: Lumra Setup
engines.body: Practice Lumra setup: mill your GY with Spelunking. Count GY lands before casting. Lumra P/T = lands in play; GY lands ETB = more counters.

engines.title: Mossborn Hydra Timing
engines.body: Deploy Hydra at exactly 7 lands. At 7: uncounterable 7/7 trample. At 6: counterable. The one-land difference is critical vs counter-heavy opponents.

matchups.notes: Your 62% WR vs their 38%. Combo kill through Escape Tunnel bypasses their flash package.

matchups.opponent: Dimir Midrange is your best common matchup. Their 38% win rate against you (per Untapped.gg, 1,400 games BO3 Plat–Mythic) reflects their inability to efficiently answer both your Sapling Nursery (enchantment, survives creature removal) and your combo kill (Escape Tunnel bypasses all their blockers). Tidebinder counters Badgermole Cub's ETB — plan for this and don't over-rely on Cub's mana generation. Kaito, Bane of Nightmares as a 3/4 hexproof Ninja is your most problematic creature since he can attack profitably. But your larger threats outclass him quickly. The key insight from Dimir's perspective: their Deep-Cavern Bat is their highest-impact card vs you (+14.7 pts) — it strips your key piece from hand. Be mindful of leaving the combo piece in hand if they have {1}{B} open. Warp Harmonizer proactively to protect it. Out In −2 Mossborn Hydra +1 Surrak, Elusive Hunter −1 Esper Origins +1 Sandman, Shifting Scoundrel −1 Mightform Harmonizer +1 Torpor Orb Izzet Lessons Race Combo Unfavorable They out-draw you with Accumulate Wisdom + Gran-Gran. Your combo must end it by T4. Izzet Lessons is a draw-engine deck that keeps up with your ramp through card quantity. Accumulate Wisdom draws multiple cards per cast, and Gran-Gran provides a recurring card advantage engine. In a long game, they have more answers than you have threats. Priority: Kill them on turn 4 with the Icetill + Harmonizer combo or Craterhoof. Don't let the game reach turn 6. Their Abandon Attachments can remove your enchantments (Earthbender Ascension, Sapling Nursery), so deploy them after they've used it or in a winning position. Needle: Go under their draw engine. If you're setting up the Icetill combo, do it before they have 4 mana open for interaction. Torpor Orb from the sideboard doesn't help here — they don't rely on ETBs. In Meltstrider's Resolve +2 Keen-Eyed Curator +2 Out Torpor Orb −2 Pawpatch Formation −2 Torpor Orb stops their Tidebinder ETB (no ability countered), Floodpits Drowner ETB (no stun), and Kaito's ninjutsu doesn't trigger. A resolved Torpor Orb dismantles their flash disruption package entirely. Surrak can't be countered and draws when they target your spells — forces their Phantom Interference and Spell Snare to blank. Sandman grows to your land count (typically 6-8 lands by the time he's deployed) — unblockable by their small creatures. Key needle: Warp Mightform Harmonizer proactively when Bat is likely. Exile it from hand with the warp cost before they can Bat it away. The combo still works — Harmonizer can be cast from exile on any later turn. Nursery as an enchantment — their removal suite (Requiting Hex, Shoot the Sheriff, Bitter Triumph) does nothing to it. Don't sacrifice Nursery even when ahead.

matchups.notes: They out-draw you with Accumulate Wisdom + Gran-Gran. Your combo must end it by T4.
Race their spell chain with your faster clock. Mossborn Hydra grows faster than their prowess triggers.

matchups.opponent: Izzet Prowess operates by chaining spells to pump small creatures and burn face. Your bodies are larger but their cantrips generate card advantage. The race is close. Sazh's Chocobo on T1 applies clock pressure before their prowess engine is online. Sapling Nursery reach tokens block their pumped fliers and chump 5/5 prowess attackers. The combo kill is fast enough — T5 one-shot before they can burn you from 20 to 0. Out In −2 Sapling Nursery +2 Mossborn Hydra −1 Fecund Greenshell +1 Pawpatch Formation Mossborn Hydra grows exponentially faster than their creatures — one land drop doubles all counters, so a T3 Hydra with T4 two land plays is already a 4/4 that doubles to 8/8 on T5. Pawpatch Formation destroys their flying threats that Nursery tokens can't profitably block. Trim 2 Nurseries because the grind plan is too slow against their burn-reach strategy — you want faster threats. Key needle: Don't let Icetill Explorer sit back waiting for the full combo. Against Prowess, Icetill as an extra land engine that charges your Hydra counters every turn is better than holding for the one-shot. A 32-power Hydra trampling over their board on T5 wins faster than trying to assemble Harmonizer + Escape Tunnel.

matchups.notes: First Mossborn Hydra that connects wins. Archdruid's Charm exile is your answer to their Hydra.

matchups.opponent: The mirror is decided almost entirely by Mossborn Hydra. Both players are doing the same thing — whoever lands a Hydra first and protects it from Archdruid's Charm exile wins when the next land drop doubles it to an unstoppable size. Sapling Nursery treefolk are irrelevant in the mirror — a wall of 3/4 reach tokens does nothing against a 50-power trample Hydra. Recognize this and don't over-invest in the Nursery plan. Harmonizer doubling Harmonizer itself creates an interesting line: Harmonizer is 4 power, one double = 8, two = 16, three = 32. Faster than the Hydra plan with fewer pieces if you have multiple Harmonizers. Out In −4 Sapling Nursery +2 Mossborn Hydra −1 Esper Origins +1 Origin of Metalbending −1 Fecund Greenshell +1 Pawpatch Formation Trim all 4 Nurseries — they win nothing in the mirror. Full Mossborn Hydra count (4 total with SB copies). Origin of Metalbending destroys their Sapling Nursery or Earthbender Ascension if they try to build around those. Pawpatch Formation is the Nursery exile answer. Don't play around their Archdruid's Charm — play fast and force them to react. Key needle: On the Hydra: a Hydra with N counters + 1 land play = 2N counters = 2N power trample. If you have 4 counters and they have an Archdruid's Charm hold, wait for the turn you can play two lands in a row — by the time both land plays resolve the Hydra is at 16 power and they needed the Charm on the first double. Sequence your land plays to bait the Charm on the first double, then immediately play the second land to double to lethal.

matchups.notes: Sapling Nursery generates faster than they can sweep. Surrak can't be countered. Sandman recurs.

matchups.opponent: Control has counterspells and sweepers but no clock. Sapling Nursery as an enchantment survives all creature-based sweepers. With Nursery active, every land drop creates a 3/4 Treefolk with reach — faster than they can spend removal. Their sweep kills the tokens but Nursery is still there to replace them. The indestructible activation protects even the tokens from the next sweep. Time Nursery activations to coincide with their sweeper timing. Out In −2 Mossborn Hydra +1 Surrak, Elusive Hunter −1 Badgermole Cub +1 Sandman, Shifting Scoundrel Surrak can't be countered and punishes them for targeting your permanents — every Time Wipe, Settle the Wreckage, or targeted removal draws you a card. Sandman grows to your land count (8+ power by turn 6), can't be blocked by small creatures, and returns from the GY with a land from the graveyard — effectively immortal as long as you have land recursion. Mossborn Hydra is too fragile against their targeted removal. Trim Cub when they're heavy on ETB counters (Torpor Orb strategies), otherwise keep. Key needle: Hold Archdruid's Charm's exile mode for their key permanent (their planeswalker or Teferi). Don't use it to exile creatures — that's what Meltstrider's Resolve is for. Every Charm activation targeting a creature is a wasted counterspell-protection tool.

matchups.notes: Their burn reach and evasion is faster than your engine. Meltstrider's Resolve blocks key threats.

matchups.opponent: Boros Aggro applies two-color aggressive pressure with flying threats and burn reach. Your large bodies can't block their evasion efficiently, and their burn finishes games you thought you stabilized. The key is deploying Sapling Nursery early — reach tokens block their flying creatures. Fecund Greenshell's reach blocks their 6/6 Dragon. This matchup requires drawing your interaction (Meltstrider's Resolve, Archdruid's Charm fight mode) early. Out In −2 Mossborn Hydra +3 Meltstrider's Resolve −1 Esper Origins +1 Pawpatch Formation Meltstrider's Resolve: Aura ETB fight + enchanted creature gets +0/+2 and can't be blocked by more than one creature. The fight kills their key flier AND makes your threat bigger and resilient. Pawpatch Formation destroys flying creatures outright. Trim all Hydras — they're too slow against burn reach. Trim Esper Origins — 5 mana doesn't matter when they're attacking with 3/3 fliers on turn 3. Key needle: Sapling Nursery's reach tokens are your primary blockers — they chump 3/3 fliers for free and stabilize the ground simultaneously. Prioritize deploying Nursery over the combo plan in this matchup. An active Nursery with 3 Forests represents one 3/4 reach token per land drop — they can't race that with burn alone.

matchups.notes: Their wide board with lifelink and anthem effects is hard to race. Nursery reach tokens are critical.

matchups.opponent: Mono-White Aggro creates a wide board of lifelink creatures with Lords pumping them. Your individual threats trade down against their going-wide strategy. Sapling Nursery's 3/4 reach tokens are your best blockers — they wall off their 2/2 lifelinkers while growing the board for your attack. The combo kill is slower here because their lifelink gains negate some damage. Out In −2 Mossborn Hydra +3 Meltstrider's Resolve −1 Mightform Harmonizer +1 Origin of Metalbending Meltstrider's Resolve fights their key creature (Lord or largest threat) and makes your blocker bigger. Origin of Metalbending destroys their enchantment-based buffs or equipment. Cut Hydras (too slow against their curve) and trim a Harmonizer (combo is slower than they kill). Prioritize Nursery deployment over everything else in this matchup. Key needle: Their lifelink prevents the combo kill from working at full efficiency — you need to deal damage equal to their life total which may have been padded by 4-8 lifelink points. Aim to deal trample damage through their wider board rather than relying on the unblockable one-shot. Earthbender Ascension's trample grant turns your Treefolk tokens into threatening attackers that punch through their wide board.

matchups.opponent: Dimir Excruciator counters your Earthbender Ascension and bounces your Badgermole Cub. Their Floodpits Drowner (flash 2/3) blocks your ground attackers and bounces Cub on ETB — resetting your counters. Icetill Explorer is their most important target: it enables your double land-drop chains. Mossborn Hydra can't be countered once you have 7 lands — time its deployment accordingly. Out In −2 Mossborn Hydra + 2 Vivien Reid −1 Earthbender Ascension +1 Meltstrider's Resolve Vivien Reid fights their creatures (−X/−X) and searches your library for creatures — relevant for finding Icetill Explorer after they've bounced it. Meltstrider's Resolve answers their Floodpits Drowner and grows your creature simultaneously. Move Mossborn Hydra to when you hit 7+ lands reliably — its uncounterability matters then.

matchups.opponent: Simic Rhythm plays the same Badgermole Cub + Earthbender Ascension engine you do, with Icetill Explorer also overlapping. The matchup is won by whoever lands Ascension with more lands already in play. Your Sapling Nursery generates 3/4 reach tokens that block their Chocobo (4/4) — use it as a defensive engine, not just offense. Mossborn Hydra as a 7/7 trample trumps their largest Cub. Get it into play first. Out In −2 Earthbender Ascension + 3 Mossborn Hydra −1 Mightform Harmonizer Mossborn Hydra is the tiebreaker in the counter war — 7/7 trample beats their pumped Cub in combat. Cut one Ascension (you don't need multiples in the mirror where they know to answer it) and Harmonizer (combo kill is slow when they also have landfall pressure).
