matchups.opponent: Bant Rhythm generates tokens with Pollinator Wasp and spider tokens from Spider Manifestation — going wide against your linear single-threat plan. Their Craterhoof Behemoth ends games instantly. Mossborn Hydra as a 7/7 blocker stalls Craterhoof math since you need 7 power to survive a Hoof attack. Origin of Metalbending destroys their Earthbender Ascension or Beza before it generates too many tokens. Out In −2 Mightform Harmonizer + 2 Origin of Metalbending −1 Mossborn Hydra +1 Vivien Reid Origin of Metalbending destroys their key enchantments (Earthbender Ascension, Beza) at {2G} sorcery speed — use it the turn after they deploy. Vivien Reid fights their Pollinator Wasp and Behemoth at -X/-X. Harmonizer combo is too slow in a racing matchup.

MONO-REDAGGRO.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "You don't play around removal. You play faster than they can cast it." Mono-Red Aggro is Standard's fastest deck. Every creature in the 75 has haste or generates immediate value. Emberheart Challenger is a 2/2 haste prowess that grows whenever you target it. Burnout Bashtronaut is a 2/1 haste that copies itself when it attacks — one card becomes two attackers. Nova Hellkite is a 4/4 haste flying dragon that deals 2 damage on entry. Everything attacks the turn it enters. The burn suite closes games that stall. Burst Lightning is 2 damage for {R} or 4 damage with kicker

engines.title: T3–T4 Kill Clock
engines.body: Faster than every other deck in Standard. Against Mono-Green and Simic Rhythm who are setting up their engine, you're attacking for 8+ on turn 3. Against control that's trying to sculpt a hand, you're dealing 20 before they assemble their stabilization tools.

engines.title: All Threats, No Blanks
engines.body: Every card in the main deck is either a hasty threat or a damage spell that kills something. There are no setup cards, no ramp, no card draw that doesn't also deal damage. Every card in your opening hand does something immediately.

engines.title: Burn Goes to Face or Kills Creatures
engines.body: Burst Lightning and Sear are both removal AND reach. A Sear that kills their Gene Pollinator is just as good as a Sear to face. Against decks you can't race, pivot to controlling the board with burn and win with a single unblocked Nova Hellkite.

engines.title: Emberheart Challenger
engines.body: 2/2 haste prowess. Valiant: whenever it becomes the target of a spell or ability you control, it gets a +1/+1 counter permanently. Targeting Emberheart with Burst Lightning, Shock, or Sear triggers Valiant — the counter stacks. A T2 Emberheart targeted by a T2 Shock is a 3/3 haste for an effective 3 mana total. Prowess stacks on top. By T4, this card is often a 5/5+ hasty attacker.

engines.title: Burnout Bashtronaut
engines.body: 2/1 haste. Whenever it attacks, create a token copy of Burnout Bashtronaut that's tapped and attacking. One attacker becomes two. Two Bashtronauts become four. In multiples, Bashtronaut's attack trigger creates an attacking token of EACH Bashtronaut — exponential scaling. A second Bashtronaut's attack creates copies of both, giving you 4 attackers from 2 cards. The ceiling is enormous.

engines.title: Burst Lightning + Sear
engines.body: Burst Lightning: {R} — 2 damage, or {5}{R} — 4 damage with kicker. Sear: {1}{R} — 4 damage to any creature or planeswalker. These are both removal AND reach. At 6 life: Burst Lightning + Sear = 6 damage to face = game. They also trigger Emberheart Challenger's Valiant when targeting your own creatures. Never tap a non-land mana source — 6 lands + kicker Burst Lightning is viable in longer games.

engines.title: Nova Hellkite + Raphael
engines.body: Nova Hellkite: 4/4 flying haste Dragon for 5 mana. ETB: deals 2 damage to any target. Immediately relevant damage on entry + 4 flying damage on attack = 6 damage the turn it enters. Raphael, the Nightwatcher: generates card advantage each turn while applying pressure. Boards in vs control — provides both a 5/4 lifelink body and ongoing resource generation that outlasts removal.

engines.title: T1 Creature Is Mandatory
engines.body: T1: Fanatical Firebrand or Hired Claw. On the play, any hand without a T1 haste creature is a likely mulligan. That one point of damage on turn 1 matters. T2: Emberheart Challenger + Shock targeting Emberheart (prowess trigger + Valiant counter = 4/4 haste effectively). T3: Burnout Bashtronaut (attack with Bashtronaut, token copy of Bashtronaut attacks too). Two creatures have been attacking since

engines.title: Face vs Creature Decision
engines.body: Every burn spell faces this decision: go to face or kill a blocker? Rule: kill the blocker IF killing it lets you deal more damage this attack than the spell to face. Example: they have a 2/4 blocker and you have Emberheart (3/3) + Sear. Sear to face = 4 damage. Sear kills the blocker + Emberheart attacks unblocked = 3 damage. Cast Sear to face. The math governs — always calculate before casting.

engines.title: 7 or 6, Never 5
engines.body: Keep on 7: any hand with a T1 creature + T2 play + lands. Keep on 6: hands with 2 one-drops + burn, or 1 one-drop + Emberheart + burn. Hard mulligan: no T1 creature on the play, 5+ lands, no haste creatures whatsoever. At 5 you need two haste creatures that attack immediately — anything slower is a game loss.

engines.title: Pivot to Pure Burn
engines.body: When blocked by large creatures (Ouroboroid 4/4s, Drowner 3/2s), stop attacking into unfavorable blocks. Burn their life total directly. 3 burn spells = 8-10 damage to face. A Nova Hellkite for 2 ETB + 4 flying = 6 unblocked damage. When the ground stalls, win through the air or through burn to face. Don't attack into large blockers and lose your threats.

engines.title: Burnout Exponential
engines.body: T2: Two Burnout Bashtronauts. T3 attack: each creates a tapped attacking token of itself. You have 4 attackers. Next turn: each of the 4 attacks, creating 4 more = 8 total. The exponential growth means a stalled board is solved in 1-2 turns with Bashtronauts. Opponents must answer each one individually or lose to the math.

engines.title: Emberheart Valiant Stack
engines.body: Emberheart Challenger with 3 Valiant counters is a 5/5 haste prowess. Target it with Burst Lightning (Valiant trigger → 6/6), cast Shock (prowess → +1/+1 until EOT → 7/7 attacking). Two burn spells targeting Emberheart = 7+ damage in one combat. The Valiant trigger is permanent; prowess is temporary but stacks in-combat.

engines.title: Inti + Nova Hellkite
engines.body: Against decks that match your early pressure: Inti exiles top card on attack and lets you cast it for free if creatures attacked. Nova Hellkite provides 6 damage the turn it enters (2 ETB + 4 flying). In slower games after burn runs low, Inti refuels and Hellkite closes without needing to attack through ground blockers.

engines.title: Pure Speed — Race
engines.body: Against Dimir, Simic, Bant — they're setting up engines. You're attacking for 8 before their engine is active. Don't interact with their setup at all. Kill them before Ouroboroid hits. Burn goes face 100% of the time unless killing a blocker creates more damage that turn. Fast and clean.

engines.title: Attack + Block Math
engines.body: Against Boros Aggro mirror or Izzet Prowess — track life totals carefully. Racing math: if you're both at the same life total and you attack into their attack next turn, who dies first? Burnout Bashtronaut tokens give you more attackers than they have blockers. Slagstorm (SB) sweeps their 1/1 tokens.

engines.title: Resilience + Burn
engines.body: Against Jeskai and Azorius Flash — curve out through their counters. Deploy threats every turn until one sticks. Raphael (SB) provides card advantage to rebuild after sweepers. Inti exiles top card for free casts. Keep enough burn in hand to close from 8 life without attacking.

engines.title: Sunspine Lynx ×3
engines.body: Prevents opponents from gaining life. In against: Azorius Flash (Voice of Victory lifelink), Izzet Lessons (Monument to Endurance life gain), any deck with Ajani, Beza, or other life gain. The effect is permanent and applies to ALL life gain including combat damage lifegain. Mandatory in at least 3 of your 8 expected matchups.

engines.title: Slagstorm ×2
engines.body: Sorcery: deals 3 damage to each creature OR 3 damage to each player. The creature mode sweeps Izzet Prowess tokens (1/1 Otters), Boros Aggro 1-drops, Mono-White tokens. The player mode is an additional Fireball effect for 3 to face. Note: sweeper mode also kills YOUR creatures. Plan Slagstorm timing carefully.

engines.title: Twisted Fealty ×2
engines.body: Gain control of target creature until EOT, and it gains haste. Attack with their best creature into their own side, then it goes to your control permanently? (check oracle — may be until EOT only). In against: Mono-Green (steal Harmonizer), Dimir (steal Drowner), Azorius (steal Floodpits Drowner). One card that neutralizes their best threat while giving you an attacker.

engines.title: Ghost Vacuum ×2
engines.body: Artifact that exiles cards from graveyards. In against: Izzet Lessons (Monument to Endurance), Dimir Excruciator (any GY strategies), Simic Rhythm (Marang River Regent death trigger). Cheap enough to cast alongside your threats.

engines.title: Obliterating Bolt Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{R} Instant: Deals 4 damage to target creature or planeswalker; if that permanent would die this turn, exile it instead. Board in vs Dimir Midrange (exile-kills Kaito MV 4, Psychic Frog MV 1+) and Mono-Green Landfall (exile-kills their key creatures). The exile clause prevents GY recursion. At 4 damage it kills most midrange threats that survive Sear.

engines.title: Slagstorm Ã—2
engines.body: {1}{R}{R} Sorcery. Mode A: 3 damage to each creature. Mode B: 3 damage to each player. Board in vs Izzet Prowess (Mode A sweeps their Monastery Swiftspear before they pump) and token strategies (Mode A sweeps their entire wide board). Mode B is almost never correct â€” use Mode A except in rare life drain situations.

engines.title: Ghost Vacuum Ã—2
engines.body: {2} Artifact: {2}{T}: Exile target card from any GY; or exile target card face-down from exile. Board in vs Dimir Midrange when their Kaito and Frog generate GY-based advantage, and vs Izzet Lessons when they run GY-based lesson recursion. The ability to exile face-down exiled cards (like Frog's flying cost) is uniquely powerful.

engines.title: Sunspine Lynx Ã—2
engines.body: {1}{R}{G} 3/3. Whenever an opponent plays a nonbasic land, Sunspine Lynx deals 3 damage to them. Board in vs Azorius Flash (they run many nonbasics), Izzet Lessons (8+ nonbasics), Dimir Midrange (8+ nonbasics). Each nonbasic land they play deals 3 damage â€” they're paying life to play their manabase. Against 4-5 color decks this can deal 12+ damage from land drops alone.

engines.title: 8 Burn Spells Minimum
engines.body: Burst Lightning + Sear at 4 each = 8 burn spells. This is the minimum for reliable reach. Without 8 burn spells, you can't close games from 8 life. The deck requires the burn to be functional — don't cut below 8 total.

engines.title: 4 Emberheart + 4 Burnout
engines.body: The two most powerful threats. Full playsets of both. Emberheart provides the scaling clock (Valiant counters + prowess). Burnout provides the go-wide exponential (token doubling). Missing either reduces your ceiling and floor simultaneously.

engines.title: Raphael + Inti
engines.body: Top-end resilience. In aggro-heavy metas, cut both — they're slow for a race. In control-heavy metas, run 2-3 combined — they provide the inevitability control matchups require. Raphael's lifelink also matters vs Azorius Flash's lifelink strategy.

engines.title: Stingerback Terror
engines.body: The mainboard flex creature. In aggro metas, replace with Fanatical Firebrand × 4 for more T1 plays. In midrange metas, Stingerback Terror's resilience matters. If you're seeing lots of sweepers, cut it entirely for burn spells.

engines.title: 4 Fanatical Firebrand main
engines.body: Some builds run 4 copies main. The T1 1-damage attack matters and the {T}: deal 1 damage activation provides the last point of reach. In fast meta matchups (Prowess, Boros Aggro mirrors), the T1 Firebrand's early damage is decisive.

engines.title: Meta Is Slow + No Lifegain
engines.body: If Izzet Lessons (Monument life gain) and Azorius Flash (Voice lifelink) are below 10% combined, register Mono-Red. If those two are dominant, reconsider — Sunspine Lynx helps but you're still fighting uphill. Best in metas of midrange decks without life gain.

engines.title: T1 Mandatory Creature
engines.body: You keep every hand with a T1 creature. You mulligan any hand without a T1 play. Your T1 creature establishes your clock — every hand without T1 clock is one turn behind schedule, which often means one turn too slow to close.

engines.title: Burn Face Unless
engines.body: You burn their face unless their creature blocks your best attacker AND blocking costs you more damage than the burn would deal face. You calculate: (damage blocked) vs (burn damage to face). Only redirect burn when blocking exceeds face value. Default: burn face.

engines.title: Roiling Vortex Priority
engines.body: You board Roiling Vortex vs any deck with life gain sources. Vortex denies ALL opponent life gain. Against Greasefang: their Parhelion II lifelink gains nothing. Against UW Control: their Absorb gains nothing, their Lyra gains nothing. You deploy Vortex on T1 before any life gain triggers can fire.

engines.title: Kill Math Before Attacks
engines.body: Before your attack step each turn, you add up: (attacking power) + (burn in hand). If that number exceeds their life total, you attack and end the game this turn. If it doesn't, you identify what one card would make it lethal and play toward drawing that card.

engines.title: Rampaging Ferocidon vs Other 3-Drops
engines.body: You run Rampaging Ferocidon (3/3 menace, prevents lifegain, 1 damage per creature ETB) in the SB when your meta has lifegain sources (Selesnya Company, UW Control, Greasefang). You cut Ferocidon in pure aggro metas where lifegain is rare and you want your SB slots for sweepers.

engines.title: Eidolon Count
engines.body: You run maximum Eidolon of the Great Revel (4 copies) when your meta has many low-MV interactive decks. Eidolon damages them for every cantrip, every Fatal Push. You could run 3 Eidolon in heavy aggro metas where both players run low-MV spells and the symmetric damage hurts you equally. 4 copies is the standard configuration.

engines.title: Shock vs Burst Lightning
engines.body: You run Shock ({R}: 2 damage) when speed is everything and your kill happens by T3-4. You run Burst Lightning ({R}: 2 damage or kicked {2}{R}: 4 damage) when your games go to T5+ and the kicked 4-damage matters for closing. In fast metas: Shock. In any metas where you reach 4 mana: Burst Lightning.

engines.title: Count Before Scooping
engines.body: You count your burn before scooping. Often: their life total appears high but your attacking damage plus burn in hand is exactly lethal. You calculate the full kill before conceding. Many games are won by players who didn't scoop too early.

engines.title: Board In. Board Out.
engines.body: You board in your hate cards and remove your weakest cards — never your combo pieces. Against control: Roiling Vortex and Rampaging Ferocidon replace your slowest burn spells. You never remove Eidolon or Swiftspear from your deck.

engines.title: Mulligan Without T1 Creature
engines.body: You mulligan any 7-card hand without a turn-1 creature. Your clock starts on T1. A hand with only T2+ plays is one full damage step behind — against most Pioneer decks, one step is the entire game.

engines.title: Face Unless Math Says Otherwise
engines.body: You burn their face unless their creature would block your best attacker AND the blocked damage exceeds your burn damage. Calculate: (blocked power) vs (burn to face). Burn face unless blocking saves you more damage than you deal.

engines.title: Why You Win the Symmetry
engines.body: Eidolon deals 2 life per spell to BOTH players. You win the symmetry because your spells average MV ≤ 1 (Lightning Bolt, Shock, cantrips) while their answers often cost 2+ mana. At 3 spells per turn, Eidolon deals 6 to them while costing you 6 — but you're ahead on the race.

engines.title: Deploy Before Their Source
engines.body: You deploy Rampaging Ferocidon before their lifegain source enters play. Ferocidon prevents ALL lifegain — but it needs to be in play BEFORE the lifegain source. T3 Ferocidon before T4 Lyra Dawnbringer: Lyra gains 0 life. T3 Ferocidon after Lyra already attacked: you missed the Lyra lifegain trigger.

engines.title: Calculate Before Attacks
engines.body: Before your attack step, you calculate: (attacking power) + (burn in hand). If that total ≥ their life total, you attack and cast burn for lethal. If short by one spell: you identify what card closes it and play toward drawing it.

engines.title: Lethal Math From Common Life Totals
engines.body: 8 life: Burst Lightning (2) + Sear (4) + any 2-power attacker = dead. 10 life: Nova Hellkite ETB (2) + Sear (4) + flying Hellkite (4) = dead the turn Hellkite enters. 12 life: 3 attackers at 4 power + Burst Lightning kicked (4) = dead. Know these numbers by reflex.

engines.title: Slagstorm Kills Your Creatures Too
engines.body: Attack with all small creatures first, then resolve Slagstorm. Never Slagstorm into your own board without attacking. The board wipe hits everything — always attack before wiping.

engines.title: SB Priority for Expected Field
engines.body: Lifegain-heavy field (Azorius + Lessons): max 3 Sunspine Lynx mandatory. Aggro-heavy: max 2 Slagstorm + 2 Abrade. Midrange/control: 2 Twisted Fealty + 2 Ghost Vacuum. Confirm your 15 against the expected field.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Forest = Mono-Green or Simic — go face completely, burn for them if possible. Hallowed Fountain = Azorius Flash — board Sunspine Lynx immediately. Steam Vents = Izzet (Prowess/Lessons/Spellementals) — race or control depending on what they do T1-T2. Watery Grave = Dimir — go wide with Bashtronauts.

engines.title: Turn 4 Goldfish
engines.body: Practice your T4 goldfish kill. T1: 1-drop (deals 2). T2: Eidolon + attack (4+2). T3: attack + burn (6+2+2). T4: attack + Burst Lightning + Lightning Bolt = lethal. Know the sequence.

engines.title: Burn vs Block Decision
engines.body: Practice the "burn face or kill blocker" decision. If their blocker would deal 2 damage to your attacker and your attacker would deal 3, trade is neutral â€” burn face for 3 instead.

engines.title: Goblin Bombardment Sacrifice Timing
engines.body: Practice sacrificing creatures in response to their board wipe. They cast Pyroclasm: before it resolves, sacrifice all your creatures to Bombardment for face damage. Each sacrifice is free damage.

engines.title: Eidolon Damage Tracking
engines.body: Practice tracking Eidolon damage. Every cantrip, every removal spell they cast deals 2 damage to them. Count the Eidolon hits â€” a 5-spell interactive hand deals 10 damage from Eidolon alone.
