The exile clause matters: Greasefang and Monk tokens removed by Hole can't be returned by Extraction Specialist or Goryo's. Mistake: trying to Hole a MV 3+ permanent — it literally can

engines.title: 4 Adeline + 4 Lieutenant + 4 Vanguard
engines.body: These three form the deck's tribal engine. Adeline generates bodies, Lieutenant pumps the team, Vanguard provides +1/+1 and ward to everything. All three at 4 copies ensures you draw at least two of the three in every game. Never cut any.

engines.title: 4 Brave the Elements
engines.body: The deck's primary protection spell and combat trick. Brave is what allows the go-wide Human strategy to work against removal. 4 copies ensures you draw it in most games. Never cut below 4.

engines.title: 4 Thalia, Guardian of Thraben
engines.body: The deck's primary disruption piece. Thalia taxing noncreature spells is what enables the Human aggro strategy against combo and control. 4 is mandatory — finding Thalia consistently on T2 is critical.

engines.title: Recruitment Officer
engines.body: 4 is the reference number. Can trim to 3 in metas where the 2/1 body is less relevant and you need more aggressive one-drops. The mid-game activation is most valuable in long games vs control — if your meta is all aggro mirrors, Officer's activation matters less.

engines.title: Removal (Declaration + Fateful Absence)
engines.body: The removal suite adjusts to meta threats. Declaration in Stone handles go-wide (exiles multiple copies). Fateful Absence handles any creature or planeswalker. In aggro-heavy metas, reduce removal to 2 total and add more creatures. In control-heavy metas, increase to 4 total for more interaction.

engines.title: Castle Ardenvale + Mutavault
engines.body: Castle Ardenvale generates 1/1 Humans at instant speed (enters tapped — doesn't ETB under Mutavault's "land" condition). Mutavault can animate as a 2/2 all-creature and is itself a Human when a creature. 2 of each is the correct ratio. 3+ utility lands risks missing critical Plains for white mana in opening hands.

engines.title: Champion Counter Priority
engines.body: When you have multiple Humans to deploy, you sequence them to maximize Champion of the Parish counters. Deploy Champion first, then Thalia (Champion 2/2), then Lieutenant (Champion 3/3+). You never deploy Humans in random order — you always sequence to maximize the counter cascade.

engines.title: Thalia Tax Math
engines.body: You memorize Thalia's tax impact by matchup. Lotus Field: their Hidden Strings costs {3}. UW Control: their Wrath costs {5}. Greasefang: their Greasefang costs {4}. Every noncreature spell costs {1} more. You know this number before your T2 Thalia resolves, so you immediately understand how much time you've bought.

engines.title: Guardian Response Protocol
engines.body: When you see their sweeper mana up, you hold mana for Guardian of Faith. They tap for sweeper: you flash Guardian in response → exile your board → sweeper resolves → board returns. You practice this response until it's automatic. This is your most skill-intensive interaction.

engines.title: Ossification Targets
engines.body: You board Ossification for their key creature by matchup. UR Cutter: Cori-Steel Cutter. Greasefang: Greasefang the creature. RDW: their key threat. You know the target before game 2 starts, never improvise it at the table.

engines.title: Thalia's Lieutenant vs More 2-Drops
engines.body: You maximize Thalia's Lieutenant copies (4) in Human-dense metas where your curve generates many counter triggers. You run fewer Lieutenant copies when your Human count is inconsistent and the counter generation is unreliable. 4 Lieutenant is standard — you cut it only when your Human count drops below 20.

engines.title: Ossification vs Portable Hole
engines.body: Ossification ({1}{W}) enchants a land and permanently exiles any creature — MV restriction free. Portable Hole ({1}{W}) exiles permanents with MV ≤ 2. You run Ossification when your targets exceed MV 2 (Kalitas, Sheoldred, large threats). You run Portable Hole when your meta is dominated by MV ≤ 2 threats (Monastery Swiftspear, small creatures).

engines.title: Reidane Meta Call
engines.body: Reidane, God of the Worthy makes all MV ≥ 4 spells cost {2} more. You add Reidane copies in metas dominated by expensive spells (UW Control, Lotus Field). You cut Reidane in aggro metas where their spells never reach MV 4. Reidane is a metagame card — 1-2 copies in the SB when your meta rewards it.

engines.title: Wedding Announcement Quantity
engines.body: Wedding Announcement ({2}{W}) generates tokens and eventually becomes a permanent anthem. You run it in grindy metas where you need card advantage and sustained board presence against control. You cut it in fast aggro metas where you need explosive curve, not slow value generation. Run 0-2 based on your expected game length.

engines.title: Guardian of Faith Copies
engines.body: Guardian of Faith (3/2 flash, ETB protects your board from sweepers) is your anti-wipe piece. You run 2+ copies in metas with many sweepers (UW Control, Jeskai Control, any meta with Supreme Verdict). You cut Guardian in aggro metas without sweepers. Guardian is the most metagame-dependent card in your 75.

engines.title: Land Count Adjustment
engines.body: You run 23 lands when your curve tops at Thalia's Lieutenant (2 mana) and your 3-drops are light. You run 24 lands when you have multiple 3-drops (Guardian, Knight of Autumn) you need to deploy reliably. You never run below 22 — missing your second land drop with a creature-heavy deck is a consistent loss condition.

engines.title: Benalish Marshal
engines.body: Benalish Marshal ({W}{W}{W}: 3/3, all creatures you control get +1/+1) is your anthem effect. With Aether Vial at 3 counters, you flash in Marshal for free at their EOT. Every Human you control is +1/+1. A board of 4 Humans with Marshal means 4 extra power and toughness simultaneously.

engines.title: Kytheon Attack Trigger
engines.body: Kytheon, Hero of Akros flips to Gideon, Battle-Forged at EOT if you attacked with 3+ creatures this turn. You sequence your T3 attack with all creatures (including Kytheon) to trigger the flip. A free planeswalker on T3 from a 1-mana investment requires no mana on T3 beyond what you've already spent.

engines.title: Count Before Swinging
engines.body: Before your attack step, you count: (attacking power) + (pump spell in hand). If that total ≥ their life total, you attack for lethal. You never attack without counting — a missed lethal attack adds one more turn for them to stabilize.

engines.title: Two-Power Lifelink
engines.body: Knight of Meadowgrain (2/2 lifelink first strike) gains you life on each attack while winning combat against most 2-drops. Against burn decks: every Knight attack recovers 2 life. Against aggressive decks: first strike means Knight kills their creature before it deals damage.

engines.title: Your Bombs
engines.body: Thalia, Heretic Cathar (3/2 first strike: their nonbasic lands enter tapped, their creatures enter tapped) is your strongest 3-drop. She delays their entire acceleration by one turn — their nonbasic land entering tapped is a free mana tax every turn she's in play.

engines.title: Your Post-Wipe Rebuild
engines.body: After their sweeper, you immediately deploy your next Human. You never slow down after a wipe — you rebuild before their next draw step adds to their resources. Your deck runs 25+ creatures specifically to rebuild faster than they can accumulate advantage.

engines.title: Two Thalias Stack Taxes
engines.body: Two Thalia, Guardian of Thraben in play: their noncreature spells cost {2} more. Their Supreme Verdict costs {6}. You find the second Thalia via Aether Vial (put into play without casting) to avoid paying mana. Double Thalia is often game-ending against spell-heavy decks.

engines.title: Your Early Planeswalker
engines.body: Kytheon, Hero of Akros (1/1 for {W}: if you attacked with 3+ creatures, flip to Gideon, Battle-Forged at EOT) gives you a free planeswalker from a 1-mana investment. T1 Kytheon → T2 two creatures → T3 attack with all three → Kytheon flips EOT. Your T3 planeswalker requires no extra mana.

engines.title: 3/3 Flying Vigilance Haste
engines.body: Mantis Rider (3/3 flying vigilance haste) attacks the turn it enters and blocks without tapping. You deploy Rider via Aether Vial (flash speed, no casting). Rider demands immediate answer — flying means it attacks over most ground blockers.

engines.title: Reidane as a Tempo Piece
engines.body: Reidane, God of the Worthy (2/3 vigilance: MV ≥ 4 spells cost {2} more) is your late-game tax piece. You deploy Reidane when you're ahead on board and want to lock them out of their expensive answers. Under Reidane + Thalia: their MV ≥ 4 spells cost {3} extra.

engines.title: They Must Destroy the Enchantment
engines.body: Ossification exiles the creature and it stays exiled as long as Ossification enchants a land. To get their creature back: they must destroy Ossification. You enchant a fetchland or a basic — fewer ways for them to destroy it. The exile is permanent until they answer your enchantment.

engines.title: Bounce + Can't Recast
engines.body: Reflector Mage bounces their creature AND prevents them from recasting it this turn. You bounce their most dangerous creature at your combat step — they can't recast it until next turn. Your follow-up attack happens against a temporarily reduced board.

engines.title: T4 Board State
engines.body: Your ideal T4 board: Champion of the Parish (4/4+ with counters), Thalia's Lieutenant (3/3+), Thalia, Guardian of Thraben (2/1 first strike), and one more Human. You apply 12+ power of pressure on T4. You build toward this board every game.

engines.title: Champion Before All Other Humans
engines.body: You play Champion of the Parish before other Humans on T1. Every subsequent Human entering gets Champion a counter BECAUSE Champion is already in play. You never deploy another Human before Champion when Champion is in hand.

engines.title: Know Their New Costs Before T2
engines.body: Before deploying T2 Thalia, you calculate their new spell costs. Their Collected Company ({4}): now {5}. Their Supreme Verdict ({4}): now {5}. Their Greasefang ({2}): now {3}. You know the exact delayed turns you're buying with the tax.

engines.title: Creatures at Instant Speed
engines.body: Aether Vial deploys creatures without casting them — they enter at instant speed without paying mana. You use Vial during their end step or in response to their play. Vial-deployed creatures trigger Champion of the Parish, Thalia's Lieutenant ETBs, and all other Human synergies at instant speed.

engines.title: Auto-Respond to Sweepers
engines.body: When their sweeper is on the stack: you flash Guardian of Faith automatically. No hesitation. Guardian ETB exiles your board, sweeper resolves doing nothing, board returns. You practice this until it's a reflex, not a decision.

engines.title: Name Your Target Before G2
engines.body: You identify your Ossification target before game 2 starts. Against UR Cutter: Cori-Steel Cutter. Against Greasefang: Greasefang the creature. Against RDW: their key threat. You never improvise the target at the table — you know it before your opponent picks up their deck.

engines.title: Spells Cost Two More
engines.body: Reidane makes MV ≥ 4 spells cost {2} more. Against UW Control: their Supreme Verdict ({4}) becomes {6}. Against Lotus Field: their expensive spells cost much more. You deploy Reidane on T3 to deny their key T4+ plays. Reidane + Thalia makes almost all expensive spells uncastable on curve.

engines.title: Brave the Elements — Name by Matchup
engines.body: vs RDW: name red — blocks Fiery Impulse, Lightning Strike, Eidolon triggers, and all burn. vs Rakdos Midrange: name black — blocks Fatal Push, Power Word Kill, Dreadbore. vs UR Cutter: name blue — blocks Into the Flood Maw, Make Disappear targeting your creatures. vs UW Control: name white — blocks only their white removal (March of Otherworldly Light); name blue for their counterspells. vs Selesn

engines.title: Sweeper Defense Sequence
engines.body: Supreme Verdict incoming: sacrifice Dauntless Bodyguard targeting Adeline or Lieutenant (indestructible survives Verdict). Alternatively, flash in Guardian of Faith in response, exiling your key creatures before Verdict resolves. Temporary Lockdown (exiles MV≤2): no answer from these creatures themselves — Brave doesn't help, Bodyguard doesn't help. In game 2 vs UW Control, don't overcommit creatu

engines.title: SB Matches Expected Field
engines.body: Heavy control (UW): Wedding Announcement × 2 + Guardian of Faith × 2 + Reidane. Heavy GY (Greasefang, Phoenix): Rest in Peace × 2. Heavy aggro/creature mirrors: Portable Hole × 2 + Ossification × 2. Heavy midrange (Rakdos): Ossification × 2 + Wedding Announcement × 2. The 15-card SB covers all matchups — confirm you know which 4-5 cards come in for each deck you expect.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Mountain = RDW (board Guardian of Faith, hold Brave for red protection). Godless Shrine = Greasefang (race aggressively, board RIP G2). Steam Vents = UR Cutter (board Portable Hole + Ossification for Cutter/Talent). Hallowed Fountain = UW Control (board Wedding Announcement + Guardian of Faith). Forest = Selesnya Company (board Portable Hole + Ossification, name green with Brave in combat).

engines.title: Human Counter Chain
engines.body: Practice the Human counter chain. Champion of the Parish (1/1) â†’ Thalia enters (+1 counter, Champion 2/2) â†’ Lieutenant enters (+2 to all Humans, Champion 4/4, Thalia 3/3). Know the math.

engines.title: Thalia Tax Math
engines.body: Practice evaluating the Thalia tax impact by matchup. Against Lotus Field: their Hidden Strings costs {3} instead of {2} â€” the combo is one turn slower. Against Control: their Wrath costs {5} instead of {4}. Know the impact.

engines.title: Guardian of Faith Sweep Protection
engines.body: Practice the Guardian of Faith response. They cast a sweeper: flash in Guardian â†’ exile all your creatures (including Guardian) â†’ sweeper resolves doing nothing â†’ creatures return end step. Execute without hesitation.

engines.title: Ossification Targets
engines.body: Practice identifying the correct Ossification target by matchup. UR Cutter: Cori-Steel Cutter. Greasefang: Greasefang the creature. RDW: their best threat. Know before sideboarding.

SimicNeoform.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Identity Simic Neoform is Modern's purest kill-you-before-you-react combo deck. One free creature, one two-mana spell, one 12/12 trampler with haste. Turn two. Good game. Neoform 's entire architecture points at a single moment: exile two green cards from your hand, drop Allosaurus Rider for free, cast Neoform or Eldritch Evolution , find Ghalta, Stampede Tyrant or Griselbrand , and close the game before most decks have established anything. The deck competes with Tameshi Belcher for the title of Modern's fastest consistent kill. Unlike cascade-based combo decks, Neoform operat

engines.title: Allosaurus Rider
engines.body: MV 7. Exile two green cards from hand — not pay . P/T = 1 + lands. The MV stays 7 regardless of how you paid. Neoform finds MV 8 (Ghalta, Griselbrand ). Eldritch Evolution finds MV ≤ 9. Always the creature you sacrifice.

engines.title: Ghalta, Stampede Tyrant
engines.body: MV 8, 12/12 trample. ETB: put any number of creature cards from your hand onto the battlefield. Put Xenagos into play → beginning of combat trigger → Ghalta gets haste and +13/+13 ( Neoform adds a counter) = 26/26 trampler. T2 lethal.

engines.title: Xenagos, God of Revels
engines.body: MV 5, indestructible. At the beginning of combat on your turn, target creature gets haste and +X/+X where X = its power. Fires immediately after Ghalta puts him into play. Does not require devotion to trigger — the trigger fires regardless of whether Xenagos is a creature.

engines.title: Planar Genesis
engines.body: MV 2, instant. Look at top 4 — put a land onto battlefield tapped, OR put any card into hand. Does not draw (not a replacement effect). Use EOT to set up combo next turn or find a key piece.

engines.title: Disciple of Freyalise
engines.body: Creature side MV 6: enters, sac another creature → gain X life, draw X cards (X = that creature's power). Land side: Forest — pay 3 life or enters tapped. Both sides count as a green card to exile for Rider. Creature side is a powerful refuel engine after a resolved Ghalta is answered.

engines.title: Bridgeworks Battle
engines.body: Sorcery side: target creature gets +2/+2, fights another. Land side: pay 3 life or enters tapped, {T}: Add {G}. Primarily used as exile fodder for Rider (green card) that can also be played as a land on mulligans with no green sources.

engines.title: Generous Ent
engines.body: MV 6, 5/7 reach. Forestcycling {1} — discard to search for a Forest. Key exile fodder for Rider and a 5-power creature that Disciple of Freyalise loves to sacrifice (gain 5, draw 5). Run 3 in most builds.

engines.title: Hooting Mandrills
engines.body: MV 6, 4/4 trample, delve. In the graveyard-heavy opening, Mandrills can be cast cheaply as an alternative sacrifice target when Rider is unavailable. Can be found with Summoner's Pact .

engines.title: Griselbrand
engines.body: MV 8, 7/7 flying lifelink. Pay 7 life: draw 7 cards. When cheated in, use Nourishing Shoal (exile large green card, gain MV life) to refuel life and keep drawing. Can draw through your entire deck. Backup win over Ghalta when you lack Xenagos in hand.

engines.title: T1 Mana Dork, T2 Kill
engines.body: On the play, T1 mana dork (Birds of Paradise or Ignoble Hierarch) into T2 Neoform is your baseline kill line. Sacrifice the dork, find Grist or Devoted Druid, then find Ghalta and Mavren or the full combo. On the play: always lead mana dork over cantrip. Every turn you delay the T2 line gives opponents an untap step to find interaction.

engines.title: Extra Card Finds Protection
engines.body: On the draw you see 8 cards which dramatically improves finding Pact of Negation backup. Keep slightly looser dork hands on the draw since the extra card often finds the missing combo piece. Against blue decks on the draw: hold Pact of Negation until they try to counter your Neoform, then Pact for free. The extra card makes protection more available.

engines.title: Second Neoform or Eldritch Evolution
engines.body: They counter Neoform: assess your hand. Do you have a second Neoform or Eldritch Evolution? If yes, rebuild the creature base (another dork + any creature) and try again next turn with backup Pact of Negation held. If no second tutor, pivot to fair green value: Grist generates tokens and removal, Devoted Druid combo can still close in fair mode.

engines.title: Green Sun’s Zenith Rebuild
engines.body: Ghalta answered or Grist removed: Green Sun’s Zenith tutors any green creature from your deck directly into play. Zenith for Grist ({2}{G}) reestablishes the combo engine. Zenith for Devoted Druid ({1}{G}) restarts the mana engine. Neoform can still chain through replacements — you have redundancy in both tutors and targets.

engines.title: Neoform Chain (T2 Kill)
engines.body: Neoform sacrifices a creature and puts a creature with exactly 1 more mana value into play from your deck. T1 dork (MV 1) → T2 Neoform → find MV 2 creature → Neoform again → find MV 3+ → chain to Ghalta and Mavren. This is the primary engine. Execute when you have T1 dork + T2 Neoform + blue mana for Pact backup. Every card in the deck supports this chain.

engines.title: Grist + Devoted Druid
engines.body: Grist, the Hunger Tide mills cards and can ultimate for a creature army. Devoted Druid + Vizier of Remedies generates infinite green mana. This is your backup when Neoform is countered — it’s slower (T3–4) but still wins. The Devoted Druid engine requires Druid + Vizier + any outlet. Green Sun’s Zenith finds either piece.

engines.title: Koma Lockdown
engines.body: Koma, World-Eater (SB) comes in vs controlling decks. Koma generates Coil tokens each upkeep and can tap permanents or make itself indestructible. A resolved Koma vs UW Control or Esper Blink is effectively unkillable — they can’t target it, it taps their counterspell lands, and it generates a clock. This engine is the anti-control finisher when the fast combo is disrupted.

engines.title: The Primary Line
engines.body: T1: Ignoble Hierarch or Birds of Paradise (MV 1). T2: Neoform sacrificing the dork → find Grist, the Hunger Tide (MV 3) — wait, Neoform gets MV+1, so dork (MV 1) → finds MV 2. Then chain: find MV 2 creature → Neoform again from hand → find Ghalta and Mavren (MV 7). Ghalta enters with haste (if you have 7+ power in play) and attacks T2. Requires: T1 dork + 2 Neoforms or Neoform chain.

engines.title: Vs Creature-Heavy Boards
engines.body: Same Neoform chain but finding Ureni, Firstborn of Ulamog instead of Ghalta. Ureni is an Eldrazi with annihilator and enters with specific triggers based on board state. Use this route when Ghalta’s haste condition isn’t met or when you need Eldrazi protection rather than pure damage.

engines.title: When to Hold for Pact
engines.body: Go T2: Opponent has no open mana, no blue sources visible, fair deck. Race immediately. Hold for T3: They have 1–2 open blue mana. Pass T2 with Pact of Negation held. On T3, execute the chain with Pact backup. Losing a turn to protect the combo is correct vs any blue deck.

engines.title: Neoform Finds MV + 1 Exactly
engines.body: Neoform says “search your library for a creature card with mana value equal to 1 plus the sacrificed creature’s mana value.” This is exactly MV + 1, not MV + 1 or less. Know every creature’s exact MV before building your chain. Ignoble Hierarch is MV 1 → finds MV 2. A 2-drop dork finds MV 3. Missing the MV by 1 breaks the entire kill line and you’ve sacrificed your creature for nothing.

engines.title: Pact of Negation Has a Payback Trigger
engines.body: Pact of Negation counters any spell for free — but at the beginning of your NEXT upkeep, you must pay {3}{U}{U} or you lose the game. This means if you Pact to protect Neoform on T2 and you don’t win that turn, you need {3}{U}{U} on T3 or you lose. Plan: either win T2–3 OR have the Pact payment ready. Don’t Pact if you can’t pay next turn AND can’t win this turn.

engines.title: Neoform Puts the Creature in Play Directly
engines.body: Unlike Chord of Calling, Neoform puts the creature directly into play — it doesn’t cast it. This means ETB triggers resolve and the creature has summoning sickness (can’t attack) unless it has haste. Ghalta and Mavren has haste if you control 7+ power — calculate your total power before executing the chain. If Ghalta enters without meeting the haste condition, you can’t attack until next turn.

engines.title: Allosaurus Rider for {0}
engines.body: Exile two green cards from hand instead of paying {5}{G}{G}. Rider enters as a 1+*/1+* (1 + lands you control). On T1 with 1 land: it's a 2/2. The exile is an ALTERNATIVE COST, not an additional cost — you choose to pay either {5}{G}{G} or exile 2 green cards. You can exile ANY green cards: lands (if they're green, e.g. Dryad Arbor), creatures, instants. The cards go to exile, not GY.

engines.title: Neoform Rider into Craterhoof
engines.body: Neoform ({G}{U} sorcery): sacrifice Rider (MV 7) → search for creature MV 8 with +1/+1 counter. Eldritch Evolution ({1}{G}{G} sorcery): sacrifice Rider (MV 7) → search for creature MV ≤ 9. Both find Craterhoof Behemoth (MV 8). Neoform gives Craterhoof an extra +1/+1 counter (6/6 base). Evolution exiles itself after resolving.

engines.title: Craterhoof = Lethal
engines.body: Craterhoof enters: "creatures you control gain trample and get +X/+X where X = creatures you control." With just Craterhoof in play: X=1 → it's a 6/6 haste trample (or 7/7 with Neoform counter). That's not lethal alone — you need another creature. With a mana dork surviving: X=2 → Craterhoof is 7/7, dork is 2+/2+ → lethal if opponent is at 20. Multiple dorks = overkill.

engines.title: No Visible Interaction
engines.body: No open blue mana. Fair deck with no counterspells. You have Pact of Negation in hand anyway. They’re on Storm or Living End (must race). Go immediately — waiting only gives them a draw step to find interaction.

engines.title: Counter Mana Visible
engines.body: 1–2 open blue mana, they passed without casting anything — Force of Negation read. Pass T2 with Pact of Negation held. On T3 execute with Pact backup. The delay costs one turn but converts a coin flip into near-certainty.

engines.title: Neoform Countered Twice
engines.body: They’ve countered Neoform twice. Rebuild: bring in Mystical Dispute (free counter vs blue spells for {U}). Cast Dispute on their counter, then resolve Neoform. This mode is slower but converts the permission war in your favor.

engines.title: Fast Combo Is Locked Out
engines.body: Post-board vs heavy interaction decks: Koma, World-Eater on T5+ via GSZ or Neoform chain is effectively unkillable. It taps their lands every Coil token activation, generates a clock, and can make itself indestructible. This is the long-game win condition when T2 is impossible.

engines.title: Consign to Memory(1–2)
engines.body: Consign counters triggered abilities and colorless spells. Against non-blue decks without triggered ability chains (Boros Energy, Domain Zoo, Ruby Storm), Consign is mostly dead. Cut 1–2 copies first.

engines.title: Nourishing Shoal(1)
engines.body: Shoal's purpose is to regain life after Griselbrand activations. Against decks where you're not running the Griselbrand line (most post-board games where Griselbrand is too slow), Shoal is dead. Always the first cut.

engines.title: Planar Genesis/Generous Ent
engines.body: Against heavy interaction, these slow pieces (setup tools that take a turn) become liabilities. Cut them for hard counterspells and threats. Against goldfish matchups keep them — they're your best setup tools.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Low Force of Negation density in expected sideboards. Midrange-heavy field — no deck can interact with a T2 Ghalta. Combo mirror fields (Amulet, Living End) where your clock is comparable and your interaction is better. You’ve practiced the full Neoform chain blindfolded and know every MV in the deck.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy Force of Negation + Endurance builds (Esper Blink, UW Control) dominating the field. Multiple Solitude builds — kills your dork at instant speed on T1 before you can Neoform. You haven’t practiced the Pact of Negation timing windows (when to Pact, when to rebuild). A misfired Pact with no payment costs the game instantly.

engines.title: Neoform ×4
engines.body: Your combo piece. Without Neoform, you cannot find Atraxa. Four copies non-negotiable.

engines.title: Eldritch Evolution ×4
engines.body: Your second set of combo pieces. Four copies of redundancy means your combo line is consistent from hand 1.

engines.title: Atraxa, Grand Unifier
engines.body: 2 is sufficient (you only need to find one). Run 3 as a hedge against Surgical Extraction. The third copy exists specifically because opponents will Extraction the first one.

engines.title: Endurance (SB)
engines.body: 2 copies vs heavy GY metas (Living End, Glockulous). Endurance at flash speed resets their GY. Cut entirely when GY decks are absent from your expected field.

engines.title: Grist, the Hunger Tide count
engines.body: 2 in interactive metas where a planeswalker that finds creatures matters. 1 in fast metas where the 3-drop is too slow. Grist's main role is being findable by Neoform at MV 3.

engines.title: T2 Kill Line
engines.body: Execute the T2 Ghalta line at tournament speed. Allosaurus pitch → Neoform chain → kill.

engines.title: Consign Timing
engines.body: Drill holding Consign for opponent's disruption. Know which spell to counter.

engines.title: Pact Math
engines.body: Practice knowing exactly when you can and cannot cast Summoner's Pact safely.

engines.title: Resilience Lines
engines.body: Practice what you do after T1 interaction hits your setup. The deck has multiple lines.

NIV-MIZZETREBORN.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "This is the toolbox deck. Every slot is chosen to be found by Niv-Mizzet Reborn. Every two-color pair has at least one card. You always have the right answer because you always have access to your entire deck." Niv-Mizzet Reborn (Niv to Light) is Pioneer's five-color midrange toolbox. The two-card engine: Bring to Light is a five-color tutor that also casts the found card for free. It most commonly finds Niv-Mizzet Reborn , the 6/6 flyer whose ETB looks at the top ten cards and puts one card of each two-color guild pair into your hand. With 1-2 copies of each guild pa
NIV-MIZZETREBORN.weaknesses: Rest in Peace doesn't stop Niv. Thalia doesn't stop Niv. Damping Sphere doesn't stop Niv. Because your threats span all five colors and come through creatures, enchantments, and spells, no single sideboard card shuts the deck off. Opponents who sideboard specifically against one thing lose because Niv attacks on every axis simultaneously.
NIV-MIZZETREBORN.mulligan:
Mulligan
Need: Green Source + 3 Lands
Keep: any hand with 3+ lands including at least one green source, a Sylvan Caryatid or Growth Spiral, and any interaction piece.

engines.title: No Silver Bullet Weakness
engines.body: Rest in Peace doesn't stop Niv. Thalia doesn't stop Niv. Damping Sphere doesn't stop Niv. Because your threats span all five colors and come through creatures, enchantments, and spells, no single sideboard card shuts the deck off. Opponents who sideboard specifically against one thing lose because Niv attacks on every axis simultaneously.

engines.title: Niv Draws 4-7 Cards on Entry
engines.body: With 1-2 cards representing each of the 10 guild pairs in an 80-card deck, Niv-Mizzet Reborn reliably draws 4-7 cards when it enters. A 6/6 flyer that draws half a hand is an overwhelming tempo advantage. After a Bring to Light resolving for Niv, you have 10+ cards while they're trying to answer the 6/6.

engines.title: Bring to Light Finds Every Answer
engines.body: Bring to Light ({2WUBRG}) finds and casts any card with MV 5 or less in your library for free. It finds Niv most often, but also finds sweepers (Sunfall), hate (Unmoored Ego to name their combo piece), and specific answers (Valki, God of Lies casting Tibalt). It's the most flexible tutor in Pioneer.

engines.title: Niv-Mizzet Reborn ETB Draws 4-7
engines.body: When Niv enters: reveal top 10, put one card of each two-color pair into your hand. With 1-2 cards per pair across 10 pairs in an 80-card deck, expected hits: 4-7 cards. The 10 pairs (Ravnica guilds): Azorius (WU), Dimir (UB), Rakdos (BR), Gruul (RG), Selesnya (GW), Orzhov (WB), Izzet (UR), Golgari (BG), Boros (RW), Simic (GU). Cards with 3+ colors hit multiple pairs simultaneously. Nicol Bolas (U

engines.title: Bring to Light — Find and Cast
engines.body: {2WUBRG}: search library for a card with MV ≤ 5 and cast it for free. With 5 colors available (guaranteed by Sylvan Caryatid + shock lands), Bring to Light finds and casts: Niv-Mizzet Reborn (usually), Sunfall (sweeper), Omnath (life + card), Valki (Tibalt mode), or Supreme Verdict. The free cast ignores mana costs entirely — Niv costs {4UR} but Bring to Light finds and casts it for {2WUBRG}.

engines.title: Mana Fix + Answer Threats
engines.body: T1: Shock land entering untapped or Triome (cycling if needed). T2: Sylvan Caryatid — a 0/3 hexproof mana dork that produces any color. Crucial: Caryatid is hexproof (can't be targeted by removal) and blocks 1-power attackers. T3: answer their most dangerous threat — Thoughtseize their key card, Abrupt Decay a critical permanent, Dovin's Veto a combo piece. Don't tap out for Niv before the board i

engines.title: Up the Beanstalk + Yorion
engines.body: T4: Deploy Up the Beanstalk — a 2-mana enchantment that draws a card whenever you cast a spell with MV 4 or greater. Every Bring to Light, every Niv, every Sunfall, every Deafening Clarion triggers it. This converts your expensive spells into card draw engines. Yorion (companion) on T5 blinks all your nonland permanents — Sylvan Caryatid untaps and produces mana again, Up the Beanstalk triggers dr

engines.title: Bring to Light → Niv-Mizzet Reborn
engines.body: T5: Cast Bring to Light with all five colors available (Caryatid + shock lands). Find and cast Niv-Mizzet Reborn for free. Niv triggers — reveal top 10, draw one card per guild pair hit. Draw 4-7 cards while deploying a 6/6 flying dragon. Up the Beanstalk also triggers (Niv has MV 6). This single sequence typically draws 5-8 cards and wins the game through card advantage.

engines.title: Need: Green Source + 3 Lands
engines.body: Keep: any hand with 3+ lands including at least one green source, a Sylvan Caryatid or Growth Spiral, and any interaction piece. Mulligan: 1-2 land hands (can't function), hands with 0 green mana (can't cast Caryatid or Growth Spiral which enable all other colors), hands with 4+ of your expensive spells and no ramp. At 6: 3 lands + Caryatid is always correct. At 5: 2 lands + Caryatid + any interac

engines.title: Sylvan Caryatid + Shock Lands
engines.body: Sylvan Caryatid is a 0/3 hexproof creature that produces any color of mana. With 20 shock lands (4 each of WU, BG, BR, GU, GW + 1 each of the others), Caryatid essentially ensures all five colors are available by T3. Triomes provide cycling early and fixing late. The mana base is the most sophisticated in Pioneer — learning the correct land order each game (basics first, then check lands enabled b

engines.title: Niv-Mizzet Reborn ETB
engines.body: Niv enters: look at top 10, put one card of each two-color pair into your hand. With all 10 pairs represented, reliably draws 4-7 cards. Each cast of Bring to Light into Niv effectively draws your hand up from whatever depleted state it's in. The 6/6 flying body also ends games in 3-4 attacks. Casting multiple Nivs in a game (via Kolaghan's Command returning a dead Niv to hand) refills the hand tw

engines.title: Up the Beanstalk + Yorion
engines.body: Up the Beanstalk: draw a card when you cast a spell with MV ≥ 4. Every expensive spell becomes card neutral. Yorion, Sky Nomad (companion for 80-card decks): cast on T5+ to blink all your nonland permanents — Caryatid untaps (mana), Omnath triggers (life gain), Up the Beanstalk redraws. Yorion casting triggers Beanstalk (MV 5). A single Yorion activation with Beanstalk + Omnath + multiple permanen

engines.title: Survive + Sweep + Stabilize
engines.body: Against RDW and Selesnya Company: Sylvan Caryatid blocks early attackers (0/3 hexproof). Deafening Clarion at 3 mana deals 3 damage to all creatures AND gives lifelink to your creatures for the turn — you heal while clearing their board. Sunfall exiles the entire board (uncounterable). Omnath, Locus of Creation gains 4 life on entry. You can survive to T5 in most games and win from there.

engines.title: Card Advantage Through Their Interaction
engines.body: Against UW Control: Thoughtseize strips their Teferi or Supreme Verdict before you're ready to go off. Niv-Mizzet Reborn refills your hand through their one-for-one removal. Dovin's Veto counters their Dovin's Veto (both sides run the same counterspell). After resolving one Niv, the card advantage is too large — you'll have 10+ cards while they're at 4-5.

engines.title: Thoughtseize + Unmoored Ego
engines.body: Against Greasefang and Lotus Field: Thoughtseize strips the key combo piece from hand. Unmoored Ego (via Bring to Light) names their win condition and exiles every copy. Abrupt Decay answers Thespian's Stage for Lotus Field. Against Greasefang: Thoughtseize their Parhelion II, then race with Niv. Against Lotus Field: Bring to Light into Unmoored Ego naming Lotus Field removes their entire engine.

engines.title: Rest in Peace ×2
engines.body: Exiles all GYs and prevents future GY use. Against Greasefang: removes Parhelion II from GY permanently. Against Arclight Phoenix: removes Phoenixes from GY preventing recursion. Against Lotus Field: removes Dig Through Time targets. Note: RIP also exiles your own GY, but Niv to Light doesn't need the GY to win — your engine runs through Bring to Light finding living threats. Cast T2 alongside Car

engines.title: Unmoored Ego + Damping Sphere
engines.body: Unmoored Ego ({1UB}): name a card — all copies are exiled from library, hand, and GY. Finds Lotus Field via Bring to Light (Unmoored Ego is MV 3, castable). Naming Lotus Field removes their entire engine. Naming Greasefang removes the creature. Damping Sphere: each additional spell costs {1} more. Shuts off Lotus Field's Hidden Strings loops and costs Phoenix 2 life per extra cantrip. Two dedicate

engines.title: Mystical Dispute ×2
engines.body: Counters any blue spell for {U} if the opponent controls a blue permanent — otherwise {2U}. Against UW Control and UR Cutter (both heavy blue): effectively a {U} hard counter on Teferi, Supreme Verdict, Treasure Cruise, Indomitable Creativity. Brings in when you need permission to protect your Niv from countermagic or to answer their key spells on budget mana. Synergizes with your five-color mana

engines.title: Sunfall + Deafening Clarion
engines.body: Second copies of main-deck sweepers. Sunfall ({3WW}): exile all creatures + proliferate (puts counters on permanents with counters). Uncounterable as an exile effect. Deafening Clarion ({1RW}): deal 3 damage to each creature + lifelink to your creatures for the turn. Deafening Clarion is better vs tokens (kills everything with 3 toughness or less) and provides life gain. Sunfall is better vs large

engines.title: Mystical Dispute Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{U} or {U} targeting blue spells. Board in vs UW Control (one-mana hard counter for all their blue board wipes and walkers) and UR Cutter (counters their key blue threats). Makes your counter suite dramatically cheaper in blue-heavy matchups. Board it out vs non-blue decks where it costs a full {3}.

engines.title: Unmoored Ego Ã—2
engines.body: {1}{U}{B} Sorcery: Name a card; opponent reveals hand; exile all copies from their hand, GY, library. Board in vs Orzhov Greasefang (name Parhelion II â€” exile all copies permanently) and Lotus Field (name Hidden Strings â€” exile all copies). Unlike Surgical Extraction, Unmoored Ego doesn't need a copy in GY first. Surgically removes their win condition.

engines.title: Damping Sphere Ã—2
engines.body: {2} Artifact: Spells cost {1} more for each spell already cast this turn. Lands only produce {C}. Board in vs Lotus Field (their lands only produce colorless â€” kills their ability to combo), RDW (each burn spell they chain costs {1} more â€” effectively taxes their aggressive draws). Against Lotus Field specifically, the colorless land clause ends their game immediately.

engines.title: Fatal Push Ã—2
engines.body: {B} Instant: Destroy creature MV â‰¤ 2 or â‰¤ 4 with revolt. Board in vs Selesnya Company (kills their mana dorks and Voice of Resurgence) and Rakdos Midrange (kills their 2-drops). Trigger revolt by cracking Soul-Guide Lantern or fetching before casting. Don't cast Push when they have GY recursion â€” their Extraction Specialist or Parhelion will come back.

engines.title: 4 Bring to Light + 4 Niv-Mizzet Reborn
engines.body: The deck's entire identity. Bring to Light is the reason 5-color is viable; Niv is the reason to play all guild pairs. Never cut any copies — 4-of ensures you draw at least one in virtually every game.

engines.title: 4 Sylvan Caryatid + 4 Up the Beanstalk
engines.body: Caryatid is the only hexproof mana dork that fixes all five colors. Beanstalk converts expensive spells into card advantage. Both are mandatory 4-of in any 80-card Niv build. Cutting either collapses the mana or the value engine.

engines.title: Guild Pair Counts
engines.body: The meta call is which guild pairs to emphasize. Heavy aggro: add Deafening Clarion or Assemble the Team (Boros RW). Heavy combo: add Assassin's Trophy or Unmoored Ego. Heavy control: add Dovin's Veto or Thoughtseize. Each meta shift changes 2-4 of the guild pair slots. The core 8 (4×BTL, 4×Niv) never changes.

engines.title: 1 Card of Each Guild Pair
engines.body: Niv draws at most one card per guild pair. To maximize Niv hits, you must have at least one card of each pair in the 80-card deck. If any pair is unrepresented, Niv's ETB misses that slot. At minimum: 1 card of each of the 10 pairs. Budget 2 of the most critical pairs (removal-heavy pairs like BG and BR).

engines.title: Yorion, Sky Nomad — Why 80 Cards
engines.body: Yorion requires 80+ card decks. In exchange, you get a free extra card in hand at the cost of 20 more cards in your deck. In Niv to Light specifically, 80 cards is correct because you need at least 1-2 cards per guild pair (10 pairs = 20 slots minimum), plus the core engine, plus mana. 60 cards would leave guild pairs unrepresented. Yorion is the reason you play 80.

engines.title: Mana Confluence Pain
engines.body: Mana Confluence produces any color but costs 1 life. Against RDW, using Confluence for mana throughout the game costs 3-6 life total. In burn-heavy metas, minimize Confluence activations early — keep life total high enough that burn can't close. Know your life total threshold vs RDW and stop activating Confluence when below 8 life.

engines.title: Niv Draw Calculation
engines.body: You count your color pairs before casting Niv-Mizzet Reborn. WU permanent + WB permanent + WR permanent = you draw for WU, WB, WR = 3 cards. You know the exact draw count before Niv enters. Low draw count (1-2): your board needs more color diversity. Ideal draw count (5-7): cast Niv immediately.

engines.title: Unmoored Ego Target
engines.body: You identify your Unmoored Ego target before game 2 starts. Against Lotus Field: name Hidden Strings. Against Greasefang: name Parhelion II. Against UW Control: name Supreme Verdict. You cast Ego on T2 to permanently remove their win condition before they draw it. Never improvise the name at the table.

engines.title: Fetch Land Sequencing
engines.body: You fetch for the exact color you need at the exact time you need it. T1: fetch for your first missing color. T2: play your next needed dual. T3: have all 5 colors available for Niv or your multicolor spells. You plan your fetch sequence three turns ahead to ensure Niv is castable on T5.

engines.title: Damping Sphere Timing
engines.body: You deploy Damping Sphere against Lotus Field on T2 before they can set up. Sphere makes lands produce only colorless — Lotus Field's tap ability generates {C}{C}{C}, not colored mana. Their entire combo is offline. You deploy as early as possible to deny their setup turns.

engines.title: Unmoored Ego vs Extract
engines.body: Unmoored Ego (name a card, exile all copies from hand, GY, library) is your strongest surgical removal. Extract ({U}: look at their library, exile one copy of a named card) is a cheaper alternative but only removes one copy. You run Ego when your meta has combo decks and permanent removal is worth 3 mana. You run Extract only in testing.

engines.title: Rending Volley vs Aether Gust
engines.body: Rending Volley destroys white/blue creatures at {R}. Aether Gust returns red/green spells to top of library at {1}{U}. You run Volley when your threats are white/blue creatures (Greasefang, UR Cutter). You run Gust when your threats are red/green spells (RDW creatures, Selesnya threats). Your meta split determines which you run.

engines.title: Mystical Dispute for Blue Metas
engines.body: You add Mystical Dispute copies when UW Control and UR Cutter represent 30%+ of your expected field. Dispute at {U} for blue spells is an efficient counter for your specific threats. You cut Dispute in non-blue metas where it costs full {3}. Dispute is metagame-specific, not a staple.

engines.title: Land Base Optimization
engines.body: You run your five fetch lands + five dual lands (one per color pair) + flexible dual lands in your optimal configuration. You minimize basics to the minimum needed for fetch targets (1 each of your five basic types). Your land base can support any color combination for Niv, and you sequence it to always have access to your most-needed colors.

engines.title: Tutor for Niv
engines.body: Bring to Light ({3}{G}{U}: converge — search for a card with MV ≤ colors spent, cast without paying mana cost) finds Niv-Mizzet Reborn at {WUBRG} (5 colors) and casts him immediately. With all 5 colors: Bring to Light costs 5 mana AND casts Niv for free.

engines.title: Color Pair Coverage Before Niv
engines.body: You run two-drop permanents covering distinct color pairs. Each pair covered on your board = one card drawn when Niv enters. Your goal: 5 distinct color pairs in play by T5. Your two-drop selection maximizes non-overlapping color pair coverage.

engines.title: Emergency Sweeper
engines.body: Vanquish the Horde ({6}{W}{W}: costs {1} less for each creature on the battlefield, destroy all creatures) becomes cheap in creature-heavy metas. Against 6 creatures on board: costs {2}{W}{W}. You run 1 copy as emergency reset in token-heavy metas.

engines.title: Five Colors by T5
engines.body: Your mana sequence: T1 fetch (color 1-2 dual). T2 play dual (adds color 3-4). T3 play third dual (adds color 5). T4 access to all five colors. T5 cast Niv-Mizzet Reborn ({WUBRG}). You plan this sequence from your opening hand.

engines.title: Deploy Best Drawn Cards First
engines.body: Niv draws 4-8 cards on ETB. You immediately identify and deploy your highest-priority card from the new hand. You don't think — you snap-play your most impactful card. Usually: your best counterspell or your most relevant threat.

engines.title: On Their Key Threat's Cast Step
engines.body: You cast Aether Gust on their key red/green spell as they cast it — not after it resolves. Gust goes on the stack in response to their spell, their spell is countered (in a sense: it goes back to top of library). You hold {1}{U} specifically for this.

engines.title: Maximize Niv ETB Draws
engines.body: You build your board to maximize distinct color pairs before casting Niv. Each unique color pair (WU, WB, WR, WG, UB, UR, UG, BR, BG, RG) draws one card. You prioritize permanents that cover color pairs your other permanents don't — maximizing non-overlapping coverage.

engines.title: T2 or Never
engines.body: You cast Unmoored Ego on T2 naming their win condition. Against Lotus Field: T2 Ego naming Hidden Strings. Against Greasefang: T2 Ego naming Parhelion II. After T2, they may have drawn into the combo piece — T2 is your optimal window before they draw.

engines.title: Fetch for the Color You Need Now
engines.body: You prioritize your T1 fetch for the missing color you need THIS turn. Not the color you'll need T5 — the color you need T2. You plan three turns of mana ahead and sequence fetches to always have access to your most-needed color.

engines.title: T2 vs Lotus Field
engines.body: Against Lotus Field, you deploy Damping Sphere on T2. Their setup window is T3-4. A T2 Sphere denies their entire setup. A T4 Sphere might miss their T3 setup. You sequence Sphere → Unmoored Ego for maximum disruption density.

engines.title: Use Your Drawn Cards Immediately
engines.body: After Niv ETB draws 4-8 cards, you immediately deploy the most relevant cards from your new hand. You don't wait — you have the mana to cast multiple spells (Niv costs {WUBRG} = 5 mana, you have 5 lands, so you need additional ramp or to wait until T6+ for mana-intensive follow-ups).

engines.title: Bring to Light's 8 Best Targets
engines.body: (1) Niv-Mizzet Reborn — draw 4-7 cards, 6/6. (2) Sunfall — exile all creatures. (3) Deafening Clarion — clear + lifelink. (4) Valki / Tibalt — 8-mana planeswalker free. (5) Unmoored Ego — exile their combo piece. (6) Omnath, Locus of Creation — life + draw. (7) Kolaghan's Command — return Niv + 2 damage. (8) Supreme Verdict — uncounterable wrath. Know which to find before the game starts based on

engines.title: Expected Niv Hits Per Matchup
engines.body: vs UR Cutter: expect to hit 4-6 pairs (Dimir, Izzet, Boros, Azorius, Gruul typically). vs RDW: expect 4-5 pairs (Boros, Rakdos, Gruul are high-impact hits). vs Greasefang: expect Orzhov, Rakdos, Dimir, Golgari hits (black removal). vs Control: expect Azorius, Dimir, Orzhov, Simic hits. Knowing expected hits tells you how many cards Niv draws in each matchup.

engines.title: All 10 Guild Pairs Represented
engines.body: Before registration: count exactly which cards cover each pair. Azorius (WU): Dovin's Veto, Supreme Verdict. Dimir (UB): Thoughtseize (B+). Rakdos (BR): Kolaghan's Command, Dreadbore. Gruul (RG): Growth Spiral (GU, hits Simic). Selesnya (GW): Leyline Binding (W+). Orzhov (WB): Valki. Izzet (UR): none? Add one if missing. Golgari (BG): Abrupt Decay, Assassin's Trophy. Boros (RW): Deafening Clarion.

engines.title: T1 Land Read + Bring to Light Target
engines.body: Mountain = RDW → board Aether Gust, main Deafening Clarion. Steam Vents = UR Cutter → board Mystical Dispute, main Abrupt Decay for Talent. Godless Shrine = Greasefang → board Rest in Peace, hold Thoughtseize for Parhelion. Hallowed Fountain = UW Control → board Mystical Dispute + Teferi. Forest = Selesnya → main Deafening Clarion, board Aether Gust. Cycling land = Lotus Field → board Damping Sphe

engines.title: Niv Draw Calculation
engines.body: Practice counting Niv ETB draws. With a WU permanent, WB permanent, WR permanent: you draw for WU, WB, WR = 3 cards on Niv ETB. Build your board to maximize Niv draws before casting him.

engines.title: Mana Fixing Sequence
engines.body: Practice the mana fixing sequence through fetch lands. T1: fetch for the correct dual. T2: play the next color you need. Know which dual lands cover which colors and find them efficiently.

engines.title: Unmoored Ego Timing
engines.body: Practice timing Unmoored Ego. T2 vs Lotus Field: name Hidden Strings â€” exile all copies permanently. T2 vs Greasefang: name Parhelion II. Know your target before casting.

engines.title: Niv Protection
engines.body: Practice protecting Niv after it resolves. You just drew 5-10 cards â€” now what? Deploy your answers immediately before they can deal with Niv. Know your post-Niv sequence.

ORZHOVGREASEFANG.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "Turn 3 Greasefang is the fastest combo in Pioneer. One card in the GY plus Greasefang equals 13 damage. You don't need anything else." The plan is brutally simple: discard Parhelion II to any of your eight discard outlets on turns 1–2, cast Greasefang, Okiba Boss on turn 3. Greasefang's ETB returns Parhelion II from your GY to the battlefield. Greasefang has power 4, which meets Parhelion II's crew cost. You attack with a 9/9 flying vehicle with first strike, vigilance, and haste — creating two 4/4 Angel tokens with flying and vigilance. That's 13 damage and a follow-
ORZHOVGREASEFANG.mulligan:
Mulligan
Keep: Outlet + Parhelion + Greasefang
Keep: any hand with one discard outlet, Parhelion II (or Monument to find it), and Greasefang, on 2–3 lands.

engines.title: T3 Kill Is Real
engines.body: Eight discard outlets across four cards (Seasoned Hallowblade, Guardian of New Benalia, Fleeting Spirit, plus Monument looting). The combo reliably assembles by turn 3. With Monument mana acceleration, you can threaten a turn-2 Greasefang in nut draws. No other Pioneer deck presents a T3 13-damage attack this consistently.

engines.title: Two-Axis Threat
engines.body: Against GY hate: pivot to Cryptcaller Chariot Zombie tokens + Monument ramp. Against creature hate: Parhelion's Angels close from the air. Against hand disruption: Sheltered by Ghosts protects Greasefang. You're not a one-trick combo deck — you have a legitimate midrange backup that wins games independently.

engines.title: Thoughtseize + Fatal Push
engines.body: The best interaction package in Pioneer. Thoughtseize answers anything before it resolves. Fatal Push hits every relevant creature at one mana. Sheltered by Ghosts gives one of your key pieces protection from a color. You're proactive AND interactive — opponents can't just goldfish past you; you're stripping their answers while assembling your combo.

engines.title: Discard Parhelion II
engines.body: T1: Cast Seasoned Hallowblade or Guardian of New Benalia. Use their activated/ETB ability to discard Parhelion II to GY. Or T2: Monument to Endurance generates mana when you discard — discard Parhelion II for both the GY setup AND Monument value. Parhelion must be in GY before Greasefang resolves.

engines.title: Cast Greasefang, Attack for 13
engines.body: Greasefang, Okiba Boss ETB: return a Vehicle from your GY to the battlefield under your control — it gains haste. Parhelion II enters with haste. Greasefang (power 4) crews it (crew 4). Attack with the 9/9 Parhelion II: deal damage + create two 4/4 Angel tokens with flying and vigilance. Parhelion II returns to GY at EOT. Angels stay.

engines.title: Angels + Repeat
engines.body: Two 4/4 Angels with flying and vigilance attack for 8. If Parhelion is back in GY (it returned at EOT), cast Greasefang again for another 13-damage swing. Total over two turns: 13 + 8 + 13 = 34 potential damage. Most opponents are at 0 by turn 4. The Angels also block during their turn since they have vigilance.

engines.title: Token Flood Without GY
engines.body: Monument to Endurance + Cryptcaller Chariot: each discard triggers Monument (mana) and Chariot (Zombie token). With four discard outlets in hand, flood the board with Zombies in a single turn. This plan bypasses all GY hate — no GY needed, just discards. Against Hearse or RIP, pivot immediately to this gameplan games 2–3.

engines.title: Greasefang, Okiba Boss
engines.body: 3/4 legendary creature for {2}{B}. ETB: return target Vehicle from your GY to the battlefield. That Vehicle gains haste until EOT. At the beginning of your EOT, sacrifice that Vehicle if it's still on the battlefield. Key rule: Greasefang has power 4 — exactly enough to crew Parhelion II (crew 4) by itself. You can play Greasefang, reanimate Parhelion II, and immediately crew and attack, all in th

engines.title: Parhelion II
engines.body: 9/9 Vehicle artifact with crew 4, flying, first strike, vigilance. When it attacks, create two 4/4 white Angel creature tokens with flying and vigilance. The combo attack deals 9 (Parhelion) + creates two 4/4 Angels = 13 total damage potential (Parhelion attacks, Angels are created). Next turn Angels swing for 8. Parhelion returns to GY at EOT — ready for another Greasefang next turn.

engines.title: Monument to Endurance
engines.body: Artifact that triggers whenever you discard a card: add mana (usually {W} or {B}) equal to the number of Monuments you control. The Mycosynth Gardens can copy Monument as an artifact land — stack two Monuments and each discard adds {2}. Four discard outlets in one turn generates enormous mana for Greasefang or other threats. This accelerates your combo turn by a full turn in ideal draws.

engines.title: Cryptcaller Chariot
engines.body: Vehicle artifact. Whenever you discard a card while Cryptcaller Chariot is on the battlefield, create a 2/2 Zombie creature token. Multiple discard outlets + Cryptcaller = a board flooded with Zombies in one turn — no GY required. Greasefang can also reanimate the Chariot itself as a backup attack. Against GY hate (Rest in Peace, Grafdigger's Cage), pivot to this plan immediately.

engines.title: T2 Greasefang
engines.body: T1: Monument to Endurance. T2: Seasoned Hallowblade, activate (discard Parhelion II) — Monument triggers, add {W}. Use that mana toward Greasefang: you now have {1}{W} + {B} from lands = {2}{B} total for Greasefang. Cast Greasefang. Reanimate Parhelion II. Crew, attack for 13 on TURN 2. This is the fastest the deck can kill and it happens often enough to respect.

engines.title: T3 Greasefang
engines.body: T1: Seasoned Hallowblade or Guardian of New Benalia. T2: Activate discard outlet — discard Parhelion II to GY. T3: Cast Greasefang (3 mana). ETB returns Parhelion II. Crew with Greasefang (power 4). Attack with 9/9 flying first strike vigilance + haste. Two 4/4 Angels created. Leave opponent at 7. T4: Angels + Parhelion again = lethal.

engines.title: Monument Backup
engines.body: Opponent kills Greasefang / exiles your GY. Shift to Monument plan. Cryptcaller Chariot in play: discard your whole hand via four outlets = four Zombie tokens in one turn. Monument generates mana with each discard. Build a 4–6 creature board by T4–5 with zero GY involvement. This plan legitimately beats decks that overboard on GY hate.

engines.title: Keep: Outlet + Parhelion + Greasefang
engines.body: Keep: any hand with one discard outlet, Parhelion II (or Monument to find it), and Greasefang, on 2–3 lands. Mulligan: hands without Greasefang AND without a clear path to it by T3. At 6: keep outlet + Parhelion + lands — Greasefang can be found via looting. At 5: only keep if you have Greasefang + Parhelion in hand with 2 lands.

engines.title: Discard → Greasefang → 13 Damage
engines.body: Discard Parhelion II. Cast Greasefang. Reanimate Parhelion II with haste. Crew (Greasefang power 4 = crew 4). Attack for 9, create two 4/4 Angels. Parhelion returns to GY at EOT. This is the fastest kill in Pioneer at 13 damage per Greasefang cast. With two Greasefangs across two turns: 13 + 13 + 8 (Angels) = 34 potential damage.

engines.title: Monument + Mycosynth Stack
engines.body: Monument to Endurance: whenever you discard a card, add {1} (or color-appropriate mana) for each Monument in play. The Mycosynth Gardens copies Monument as an artifact, creating a second copy. Each discard now adds {2}. Four outlets in one turn generates {8} extra mana — enough to cast Greasefang, a spell, and still have gas. This enables T2 Greasefang in nut draws.

engines.title: Cryptcaller Chariot + Outlets
engines.body: Cryptcaller Chariot: whenever you discard a card, create a 2/2 Zombie token. Each of your eight discard outlets creates a Zombie. With Chariot in play, discarding your hand to five outlets creates five 2/2 Zombies in one turn. On your end step using Fleeting Spirit or Hallowblade = Zombies your opponent doesn't see coming before their turn. No GY required — this plan beats every GY hate card in th

engines.title: Race — Priority on Speed
engines.body: Against UR Cutter: they kill on T3–4, you kill on T3. You must go first or match their speed. Don't slow down to use Fatal Push — only kill creatures that would block Greasefang or prevent your attack. Dead aim: assemble the combo as fast as possible. If you're on the draw and they have a board by T2, Parhelion's first strike blocks favorably, buying turns. The 13-damage swing + two 4/4 Angels rac

engines.title: Force Countermagic
engines.body: Against UW Control: they counter Greasefang. Board in Thoughtseize + Duress — strip their counterspell before you cast Greasefang. The correct play: T2 Thoughtseize to see their hand, take their counter or sweeper. T3 Greasefang resolves uncountered. Sheltered by Ghosts on Greasefang after it resolves makes it very difficult to remove. If they sweep, re-reanimate next turn — Parhelion is back in G

engines.title: Combo + Interaction
engines.body: Against midrange: use Fatal Push + Thoughtseize to clear the path for Greasefang. Their removal (Fatal Push, Push) answers your creatures, not your vehicles — Parhelion in GY is safe from most hate. Strip their key disruption pieces (Graveyard Trespasser, their hate bears) before combo turn. The midrange clock is slower than your combo, so you have turns to interact first.

engines.title: Thoughtseize ×4 + Duress ×3
engines.body: Thoughtseize hits any card. Duress hits noncreature spells. Together they strip counterspells before Greasefang, remove combo pieces from opponent's hand, and let you see exactly what disruption they have. Board in vs: control (takes their counters/sweepers), combo (takes their key pieces), midrange (takes their best removal before your combo turn). The best seven cards in your SB by a wide margin

engines.title: Go Blank ×2
engines.body: Go Blank: sorcery, each opponent discards two cards and exiles their GY. This serves two functions: (1) it strips opponents' GY-based threats (Phoenix, Cruise fuel), (2) it exiles their GY in response to their own GY manipulation. Board in vs: Izzet Phoenix, any Treasure Cruise shell. Also excellent vs control to strip their hand further after a Thoughtseize chain.

engines.title: Waste Not ×2
engines.body: Waste Not: whenever an opponent discards a card, get a benefit based on card type (creature = Zombie token, noncreature spell = mana, land = draw). Combine with Thoughtseize + Duress to generate massive resources. Against control: T2 Waste Not, T3 Thoughtseize their hand — each discard creates Zombies and mana. This plan doesn't require GY at all, bypassing hate entirely. Board in when GY plan is

engines.title: Anguished Unmaking ×2 + Reidane ×2
engines.body: Anguished Unmaking: exile any nonland permanent for {1}{W}{B} at instant speed. Answers Graveyard Trespasser, Teferi, planeswalkers, anything. Reidane, God of the Worthy: legendary 2/3 flying creature for {2}{W}. Her god side taxes noncreature spells costing 3 or less — directly hits UR Cutter's entire cantrip suite and Treasure Cruise. Board Reidane vs any cantrip-heavy strategy.

engines.title: Anguished Unmaking Ã—2
engines.body: {1}{W}{B} Instant: Exile target nonland, nontoken permanent. You lose 3 life. Board in vs Rakdos Midrange (exiles their Vein Ripper or Kalitas at instant speed) and Selesnya Company (exiles their key creature). The exile clause means no GY recursion. Three life is the cost â€” board it in only when the permanent being exiled is worth 3+ life.

engines.title: Reidane, God of the Worthy Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{W} 2/3 Vigilance. Spells with MV â‰¥ 4 cost {2} more; snow lands enter tapped. Board in vs RDW (their 4-mana spells cost {2} more) and UR Cutter (their expensive spells become prohibitively expensive). Reidane attacks for 2 with vigilance while taxing their entire mana curve. Particularly effective against decks that need to reach their 4-mana sweet spot.

engines.title: Go Blank Ã—1
engines.body: {2}{B} Sorcery: Target opponent discards two cards. Exile all cards in that player's GY. Board in vs UW Control when they've developed a large hand and you need to both disrupt them and exile their GY simultaneously. Also board in vs any deck that cares about their GY â€” the exile clause is a free Lantern stapled to a Hymn to Tourach.

engines.title: Damping Sphere Ã—1
engines.body: {2} Artifact: Lands only produce colorless; spells cost {1} more per spell already cast. Board in vs Lotus Field (lands produce only colorless, ending their combo immediately). Damping Sphere is the hardest card for Lotus Field to play through â€” their entire strategy requires tapping specific colored Lotus Fields for huge mana, which Sphere prevents.

engines.title: 4 Greasefang, Okiba Boss
engines.body: The entire engine. Finding it consistently on T3 requires four copies. Running three introduces too much variance — games where you don't find it by T4 are almost always losses. Four copies means you find it in your opening 7 about 40% of the time and by turn 3 in the vast majority of games.

engines.title: 4 Parhelion II
engines.body: You must have Parhelion in your GY when Greasefang ETBs. Four copies plus eight discard outlets plus Geier Reach Sanitarium ensures Parhelion is in the GY by T3 consistently. Running three risks games where you have Greasefang but no Parhelion to target — an embarrassing failure state.

engines.title: 8 Discard Outlets (4+4)
engines.body: Seasoned Hallowblade + Guardian of New Benalia form the base. Both are independently powerful two-drops that also crew vehicles and have relevant stats. The two-drop slot must have eight copies to guarantee a T1–T2 discard outlet in opening hands consistently. Cutting to six creates too many slow hands.

engines.title: Monument to Endurance
engines.body: Four copies is standard — the mana acceleration is excellent and it's a payoff for discards you're doing anyway. In very aggro-heavy metas where the Monument plan is irrelevant and speed is everything, trim to two. In slower metas where Monument's ramp and the transformational SB plan are valuable, keep four.

engines.title: Cryptcaller Chariot
engines.body: Four copies is correct in any meta with significant GY hate. If GY hate is light, trim to two — it's the fourth most important piece and draws awkwardly in multiples. Always keep at least two for the backup Zombie plan against hate-heavy opponents.

engines.title: Midrange-Light Metas
engines.body: Greasefang is best when the meta is control or aggro — no disruption to your GY and you race them. It's worst when Rakdos Midrange is over 15% (Thoughtseize + Graveyard Trespasser is a brutal combination). If Rakdos is dominant, shift to a different Pioneer strategy. Otherwise Greasefang is correct at ~11% meta share.

engines.title: Discard Timing Protocol
engines.body: You discard Parhelion II on T2 via your discard outlet (Bitter Triumph, Blood token, Conspiracy Theorist). You never discard Parhelion if they have Soul-Guide Lantern mana open — wait until they tap for something else. You check their available mana before committing Parhelion to GY.

engines.title: Greasefang Blink Line
engines.body: When they have removal available, you protect Greasefang with Ephemerate or Selfless Spirit. Greasefang leaving play means Parhelion returns to GY — the ETB trigger doesn't fire again until Greasefang re-enters. You hold your protection piece and cast it in response to their removal on Greasefang.

engines.title: Go Blank Timing
engines.body: You cast Go Blank (discard 2 + exile their GY) after they've deployed key pieces to their GY but before they can use them. Against UW Control: cast after they've drawn multiple turns to strip their hand. Against mirror: cast after they've discarded Parhelion to exile it permanently. You time Go Blank for maximum impact.

engines.title: Anguished Unmaking Targets
engines.body: You target their GY hate with Anguished Unmaking at instant speed. Lantern activating: respond with Unmaking before the exile resolves. Rest in Peace in play: Unmaking exiles it and their GY reappears. You accept the 3 life cost for instant-speed exile — it's always worth it to enable your combo.

engines.title: Thoughtseize vs Duress Ratio
engines.body: You run Thoughtseize (any nonland, 2 life) in metas where creatures threaten you (Sheoldred, Kalitas, combo creatures). You run Duress (nonland noncreature, 0 life) in metas dominated by noncreature answers (counters, board wipes). In mixed metas: split 3/2 Thoughtseize/Duress. The decision depends on whether creatures or spells threaten your combo more.

engines.title: Anguished Unmaking vs Fatal Push
engines.body: Anguished Unmaking (instant exile any nonland permanent, 3 life) removes any permanent including enchantments. Fatal Push (destroy creature MV ≤ 2 or ≤ 4 with revolt) only hits creatures. You run Unmaking when GY hate enchantments (Rest in Peace) are common. You run Push when their key targets are creatures. In most metas: run both.

engines.title: Never Into Open Lantern Mana
engines.body: You never discard Parhelion II when your opponent has Soul-Guide Lantern mana ({1}) open. You wait until they tap for a spell, then discard. You count their available mana before discarding Parhelion — one wrong discard permanently exiles your win condition.

engines.title: Hold Your Answer
engines.body: When Greasefang is on the stack or in play: you hold your protection piece (Ephemerate, Selfless Spirit) specifically for their removal. You cast protection in response to their removal on Greasefang. Greasefang leaving play before it ETBs means no Parhelion return.

engines.title: Answer Their Permanent Hate
engines.body: When they deploy a permanent that shuts off your combo (Rest in Peace, Grafdigger's Cage): you immediately Anguished Unmaking it. You never wait — the longer their hate is in play, the more likely they sequence additional answers. Unmaking immediately is always correct.

engines.title: T1 Information Advantage
engines.body: You Thoughtseize on T1 in game 1 to identify their GY hate cards. If they have Soul-Guide Lantern: take it and discard Parhelion on T2. If they don't: discard Parhelion on T2 anyway (faster combo). You make the discard decision AFTER seeing their hand.

engines.title: Wait for Full GY
engines.body: You cast Go Blank (discard 2 + exile their GY simultaneously) when their GY has their key card already. Against mirror: wait until they've discarded Parhelion, then Go Blank to exile it permanently. Against UW Control: cast when their hand is large enough to hurt from the 2-card discard.

engines.title: The Kill Sequence
engines.body: Memorize: (1) discard outlet discards Parhelion, (2) Greasefang ETB returns Parhelion with haste, (3) Greasefang crews (power 4 = crew 4), (4) Parhelion attacks — 9 damage + two 4/4 Angels created, (5) Parhelion returns to GY at EOT. You must execute this in under 20 seconds per tournament rules. Practice until it's automatic.

engines.title: Pivot Trigger: Is GY Hate Active?
engines.body: Check at the start of every game: do they have Rest in Peace, Grafdigger's Cage, or Unlicensed Hearse on the battlefield? If yes: go immediately to Cryptcaller Chariot + discard outlet Zombie plan. Do not spend any resources trying to fight the hate piece unless you have Anguished Unmaking. Monument + Chariot + four outlets is a real kill.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Steam Vents = UR Cutter (board Reidane + Thoughtseize G2, race G1). Hallowed Fountain = UW Control (board discard suite, Thoughtseize before Greasefang). Overgrown Tomb = Rakdos Midrange (board Unmaking + Thoughtseize). Forest + land = Selesnya Company (board Thoughtseize + Unmaking). Mountain only = RDW (board Reidane, speed up your clock).

engines.title: Go First or Second?
engines.body: Almost always choose to go first. Thoughtseize on T1 on the draw gets you a card but you're behind on tempo. On the play: T1 outlet, T2 discard Parhelion, T3 Greasefang = fastest possible line. The deck is better on the play than any deck in the format except UR Cutter. Only consider going second if you have a very specific hand that needs the extra card.

engines.title: T3 Combo Drill
engines.body: Practice the T3 Greasefang kill. T1: land. T2: discard outlet (Parhelion to GY). T3: Greasefang enters â†’ ETB returns Parhelion â†’ Parhelion attacks as a 13/13 first strike lifelink. Execute blindfolded.

engines.title: GY Hate Protocol
engines.body: Practice the Rest in Peace game plan. RIP in play = your GY is empty = Greasefang ETB does nothing. Bounce RIP with Anguished Unmaking before comboing. Know your hate answers and when to deploy them.

engines.title: Thoughtseize Targets
engines.body: Practice T1 Thoughtseize targeting. Against UW Control: take their Dovin's Veto (they can't counter Greasefang). Against Mirror: take their Parhelion. Against RDW: take their Goblin Bombardment.

engines.title: Greasefang Blink Timing
engines.body: Practice blinking or protecting Greasefang with Ephemerate or Selfless Spirit if they have removal for it. Greasefang leaving play means Parhelion returns to GY â€” protect it until it attacks.

Sheoldred drains them every draw step. Fable generates two bodies. You never run out of gas." Rakdos Boomer Midrange is the most traditional fair deck in Pioneer. The plan never changes: disrupt with Thoughtseize and Fatal Push , generate value with Fable of the Mirror-Breaker and Bloodtithe Harvester , and close with Sheoldred, the Apocalypse and Graveyard Trespasser . The deck is called "Boomer" because it plays nothing exotic — no combo, no GY s

engines.title: Sheoldred Ends Every Long Game
engines.body: Sheoldred, the Apocalypse deals 2 damage whenever any player draws a card (except the first each turn). In a format where control decks draw 3-4 cards per turn via Teferi and Consult the Star Charts, Sheoldred deals 6-8 damage per turn passively. Removing her costs a removal spell + 2 more life taken to the face first. Opponents who let Sheoldred live die to their own draw steps.

engines.body: A T1 Thoughtseize reveals your opponent's entire hand, lets you strip the most dangerous card, and gives you perfect sequencing knowledge for the next 3-4 turns. Against combo (Greasefang, Lotus Field), strip the key piece. Against control, strip Teferi or their sweeper. Against aggro, strip Eidolon or their combat trick. The information gain is as valuable as the card stripped.

Most opponents can't survive this.

The game's won through incremental advantage: every creature you play generates more value than their single-removal answer. Fable's loot Chapter 2 refills your hand when you'r

engines.title: Need: 3 Lands + Disruption + Threat
engines.body: Keep: 3 lands (including at least one black source), 1 Thoughtseize or Fatal Push, and a 2-3 drop threat. Mulligan: 1-2 land hands (you miss T2 plays which are critical), all threats with no interaction (you die to combo before impacting the board), 4+ lands with nothing to do. At 6: 3 lands + Thoughtseize + any threat. At 5: 2 lands + Thoughtseize + Harvester + any removal.

engines.title: Apply Maximum Pressure
engines.body: Your T3 is Sheoldred, the Apocalypse: 4/5 deathtouch that makes them lose 2 life every time they draw a card. Your T4 is Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet: exiling their creatures and creating Zombie tokens simultaneously. You win the mid-game by forcing them to use removal on your most threatening permanent while your second threat advances your board position.

engines.title: Grind the Win
engines.body: Your late game is defined by Kolaghan's Command's two-for-one modes and Unlicensed Hearse as a 4/4 that exiles their GY simultaneously. You close when their hand is empty (Thoughtseize stripped their threats), their board is cleared (removal handled their permanents), and your Sheoldred or Kalitas has been generating value for 2+ turns. Count their outs before swinging for lethal.

engines.title: Maximize Two-For-Ones
engines.body: Every card you play should generate more than one card's worth of value. Thoughtseize sees their hand AND removes their best card (1 card, 2 effects). Kolaghan's Command destroys their artifact AND makes them discard (1 card, 2 effects). Unlicensed Hearse exiles their GY AND crews as a 4/4 (1 card, 2 effects). You win by chaining two-for-ones until they've run out of resources.

engines.title: Thoughtseize T1 Protocol
engines.body: Your T1 Thoughtseize protocol: look at their hand, identify their win condition, take it. Against combo: take the combo piece. Against control: take their best interaction. Against aggro: take their most dangerous threat. The information alone is worth the 2 life — you know their entire plan. Never take a card you can easily answer — take the card you CAN'T answer easily.

engines.title: Thoughtseize + Sequencing
engines.body: Thoughtseize on T1 reveals their entire opening hand. This information tells you: what's their kill condition, what's their next 3 turns, what's dangerous vs. ignorable. Strip the most important card — usually their combo piece, their sweeper (vs. your threats), their Treasure Cruise (prevents them from refueling), or their best T2 play. The information from Thoughtseize shapes every subsequent de

engines.title: Fable → Reflection of Kiki-Jiki
engines.body: Fable generates value across all three chapters. Chapter 1 (Goblin → Treasure): Treasure enables higher-mana plays earlier. Chapter 2 (loot): dig for Sheoldred, remove lands, put Kroxa in GY. Chapter 3 (Reflection): copy your best nonlegendary creature with haste. Reflection copying Graveyard Trespasser exiles a GY card and drains 1. Reflection copying Bloodtithe Harvester provides removal + Blood

engines.title: Sheoldred, the Apocalypse
engines.body: Sheoldred is a passive win condition that grows more powerful as the game progresses. Early game: a 4/5 deathtouch that demands immediate answer. Mid game: 2 life per opponent draw step turns their card advantage into a clock. engines.title: Your T1 Thoughtseize Protocol
engines.body: You cast Thoughtseize on T1 in over 90% of game 1 situations. You look at their hand, identify their best card, and take it. Against combo: take their win condition. Against control: take their most efficient counter. Against aggro: take the card you least want to face. The information is as valuable as the disruption — you know their remaining hand.

engines.title: Your Sheoldred Deployment
engines.body: You deploy Sheoldred, the Apocalypse on T4 when they don't have 4 mana open for interaction. You hold Duress until T3 to clear their hand of answers before Sheoldred enters on T4. You don't deploy Sheoldred into open mana — you wait until they've tapped down. Once Sheoldred resolves, you apply pressure and let her passive drain win the game.

engines.title: Your Kalitas Line
engines.body: You deploy Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet on T4 when they have key creatures you want to exile. You cast removal in response to Kalitas entering — Kalitas's exile-on-death effect triggers when creatures die from your spells OR combat. You attack with Kalitas into their creature, they block, Kalitas triggers, their creature is exiled (not going to GY), and you create a Zombie token.

engines.title: Your Grind Mode
engines.body: Your late game is pure resource attrition. You've stripped their hand with Thoughtseize, killed their threats with removal, and your Sheoldred or Kalitas has been generating value for 2-3 turns. You swing for lethal when their hand is empty and their board is clear. You never attack into unknown information — you Thoughtseize first to confirm no combat trick.

engines.title: Answer Their Threats, Deploy Yours
engines.body: Against RDW: Fatal Push kills Monastery Swiftspear and Soul-Scar Mage on T1. Bonecrusher Giant's Stomp deals 2 to kill their one-drops (and prevents damage prevention — ignoring protection spells). Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet gains life and exiles their creatures on death. Graveyard Trespasser's drain stabilizes. You can't race burn — answer everything and deploy Sheoldred at 6+ life.

engines.title: Out-Value Their Resources
engines.body: Against Selesnya Company and similar: your 1-for-1 removal trades favorably with their 1/1 Elves. Sheoldred blanks their draw-step value. Graveyard Trespasser with ward forces extra resource spending. Fable's Reflection copying Sheoldred on T5 generates overwhelming advantage they can't answer profitably. You win midrange mirrors by generating more value per card than they do.

engines.title: Strip Key Pieces, Pressure Life
engines.body: Against Greasefang, Lotus Field, and UW Control: Thoughtseize strips the kill piece (Parhelion II, Emergent Ultimatum, Teferi). Dreadbore handles planeswalkers (the only non-blue planeswalker removal in Pioneer). Sheoldred kills control through draw steps. Against combo: don't over-discard — Thoughtseize the ONE critical piece, then race with creatures. They only need one piece to win; you only ne

engines.body: A {B} discard that forces the opponent to reveal their hand and discard a noncreature, nonland card. Against UW Control: strips Teferi, Supreme Verdict, Dovin's Veto, No More Lies.
