engines.body: {2}{B} Sorcery: Target opponent discards two cards. Exile all cards in that GY. Board in vs Orzhov Greasefang (discard 2, exile their GY simultaneously â€” kills their setup and their recursion in one card) and UW Control (forces them to discard two key interaction pieces). engines.title: 4 Thoughtseize + 4 Fatal Push
engines.body: Thoughtseize is the best T1 play in Pioneer across every matchup. Fatal Push kills virtually any relevant creature at {B}. These 8 cards define the deck's identity. Never cut below 4 of either.

engines.title: 4 Fable of the Mirror-Breaker
engines.body: The deck's best card after Thoughtseize. Generates value across all three chapters and transforms into the deck's primary win engine. Always 4 copies — finding Fable consistently by T3 is non-negotiable.

engines.title: 3–4 Sheoldred
engines.body: 3 is the reference number; 4 in control-heavy metas where Sheoldred wins games alone. Sheoldred is legendary so multiples in hand are dead. 3 copies maximizes seeing it in most games without the redundancy problem.

engines.title: Bloodtithe Harvester
engines.body: 4 is standard. Can trim to 3 in metas where the 3/2 body is less relevant (control-heavy). The Blood token provides valuable looting and the sacrifice ability scales with Blood count — more Harvesters = more Blood = better removal. 4 is correct in most metas.

engines.title: Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet
engines.body: 2 in standard builds. The 3/4 lifelink body and exile-on-kill are valuable vs aggro and GY decks. 0 copies vs control (irrelevant). 3 copies in heavy aggro or GY-combo metas. Kalitas is the most meta-dependent slot in the deck.

engines.title: Removal Suite
engines.body: Bonecrusher Giant (Stomp deals 2, prevents damage prevention — runs 3). Dreadbore (kills planeswalkers at sorcery speed — runs 2). Power Word Kill (cheap unconditional creature removal — 1 copy). Adjust the ratio: more Dreadbore vs planeswalker-heavy metas, more Giant vs aggro metas, more Power Word Kill vs wide creature fields.

engines.title: T1 Thoughtseize Always
engines.body: You cast Thoughtseize on T1 in virtually every game 1 situation. The only exceptions: you have a faster clock (T1 Swiftspear) that matters more. You see their hand, identify their win condition, and take it. You never "save" Thoughtseize for a better moment — T1 is always the best moment.

engines.title: Sheoldred Protection
engines.body: You deploy Sheoldred at 4 mana when they're tapped or when you have interaction backup. You protect Sheoldred with Thoughtseize (clear their hand first) or with removal (kill their removal pieces first). Once Sheoldred resolves: each draw they make costs 2 life. Your priority becomes protecting her for 3+ turns.

engines.title: Kalitas Exile Synergy
engines.body: You cast removal when Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet is in play to maximize exile value. Their creature dying to your spell = exile + Zombie token. You sequence: Kalitas enters → opponent plays a creature → you cast Fatal Push (creates exile trigger + Zombie). You never use removal before Kalitas enters if Kalitas is in hand.

engines.title: Kolaghan's Command Modes
engines.body: You select Kolaghan's Command's two modes before casting. Most common combination: "Return target creature from GY to hand" + "Opponent discards a card." Alternative: "Destroy artifact" + "Deal 2 damage." You know both modes for your opponent's current board state before tapping mana.

engines.title: Abrade vs Fatal Push Balance
engines.body: Abrade ({1}{R}: 3 damage to creature OR destroy artifact) handles creatures AND artifacts simultaneously. Fatal Push ({B}: destroy creature MV ≤ 2 or ≤ 4 with revolt) handles small creatures cheaply. You run more Abrade in artifact-heavy metas (UR Cutter's Cutter artifact, Greasefang's vehicles). You run more Push in creature-heavy metas. In most metas: split 2 Abrade / 2 Push.

engines.title: Unlicensed Hearse Count
engines.body: Unlicensed Hearse ({2}: exile GY cards, crew as 4/4) is your GY hate piece. You run 2-3 copies in GY-heavy metas (Greasefang, Arclight Phoenix). You cut Hearse in non-GY metas. Hearse crewing as a 4/4 is a secondary benefit — you run it for the GY exile first, the body second.

engines.title: Kolaghan's Command vs Thoughtseize
engines.body: Kolaghan's Command (2-for-1: return creature + discard, OR destroy artifact + damage) generates card advantage. Thoughtseize (1-for-1: see hand + take card) generates information and disruption. You run more Command in metas where two-for-ones compound advantage. You run more Thoughtseize in metas where specific cards must be stripped from hand on T1.

engines.title: Go Blank Timing and Count
engines.body: Go Blank ({2}{B}: target discards 2 cards + exile their GY simultaneously) is your combo disruption piece. You run 1-2 copies in metas with GY combo decks (Greasefang, Arclight Phoenix). You cast it on T3 when you know their key GY card is already there. You never cast Go Blank blindly on an empty GY — wait for the right moment.

engines.title: Brotherhood's End vs Anger of the Gods
engines.body: Brotherhood's End ({2}{R}: 2 damage each non-Phyrexian creature/planeswalker OR destroy MV ≤ 3 artifacts) is modal and versatile. Anger of the Gods ({1}{R}{R}: 3 damage, exile if it would die) specifically targets GY strategies. You run Anger in GY-heavy metas where exile is critical. You run Brotherhood's End in non-GY metas for the modal flexibility.

engines.title: Collective Brutality Slot
engines.body: Collective Brutality ({1}{B}: choose 1-3 from escalate) drains 2 life, makes them discard, or makes them sacrifice a creature. You run Collective Brutality in burn-heavy metas (RDW) where the 2 life drain matters for the race. You cut it in non-burn metas where the other modes are available but less impactful.

engines.title: Reckoner Bankbuster
engines.body: Reckoner Bankbuster ({2}: artifact Vehicle: tap and add a charge counter; when you add the third counter, crew it as a 4/4 and draw a card) provides card advantage in grindy matchups. You run 1-2 copies in metas where card advantage matters more than speed.

engines.title: Bloodtithe Harvester Utility
engines.body: Bloodtithe Harvester (3/2: ETB creates a Blood token; sacrifice Blood to destroy a tapped creature) provides removal and a Blood token in one card. You use the Blood sacrifice on their tapped creatures after combat — their tapped attacker is destroyed before they can untap. You never forget to use the Blood sacrifice ability.

engines.title: Kalitas Protection
engines.body: You protect Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet with removal on their creatures that threaten to kill Kalitas in combat. Kalitas (4/4 lifelink) trading with a 4/4 would remove your exile engine. You keep smaller removal available to kill their potential Kalitas-attackers before they can swing into Kalitas.

engines.title: Graveyard Trespasser
engines.body: Graveyard Trespasser (3/3: whenever it enters or attacks, exile a card from a GY, and if a Human card is exiled, they discard) is a walking GY-exile engine and discard trigger. Against Greasefang: every attack exiles Parhelion from their GY. You run 1-2 Trespasser as a creature-based GY answer.

engines.title: Kalitas Return Line
engines.body: When Kalitas dies, you use Kolaghan's Command to return him from GY to hand and redeploy on T4+ with mana available. The Command + Kalitas recursion chain generates repeated exile value across multiple turns.

engines.title: Collective Brutality Value
engines.body: Collective Brutality (escalate modes: drain 2, they discard, they sacrifice creature) is your most flexible card in aggro matchups. Against RDW: you escalate all three modes — drain 2 life, they discard their burn, they sacrifice their creature. One card answers three things.

engines.title: Sorin the Mirthless Finisher
engines.body: Sorin, the Mirthless creates 2/3 lifelink Vampire tokens. Against aggressive decks: Sorin at 4 mana creates a blocker that gains you life every combat. You run 1-2 Sorin in the SB for grindy matchups where you need a threat that also stabilizes your life total.

engines.title: Leyline of the Void
engines.body: Leyline of the Void (free if in opening hand: their cards go to exile instead of GY) is your strongest GY hate piece. Against Greasefang: Parhelion II goes to exile, not GY — their combo is permanently offline. You run 2-4 Leyline in Greasefang-heavy metas.

engines.title: Always Trigger First
engines.body: You crack a fetchland or sacrifice a Soul-Guide Lantern BEFORE casting Fatal Push to trigger revolt (MV ≤ 4 mode). Without revolt: Push misses Kalitas (MV 4), misses Sheoldred (MV 4). With revolt: hits everything relevant. You never cast Push without revolt against high-MV threats.

engines.title: Their Draw Step = Your Damage
engines.body: Sheoldred makes them lose 2 life every time they draw a card (including their draw step). A control opponent drawing 6 spells in a game: 12 damage from Sheoldred alone. You protect Sheoldred specifically because her passive drain often deals more damage than your creatures.

engines.title: Know Which to Cast When
engines.body: Duress takes noncreature nonland cards (0 life loss). Thoughtseize takes any nonland (2 life loss). Against combo and control (noncreature threats dominate): Duress is more efficient. Against creature-based strategies: Thoughtseize. You adjust the split based on their deck.

engines.title: Empty Their Resources
engines.body: Your win condition is attrition: Thoughtseize drains their hand, Fatal Push and Abrade drain their board, Sheoldred's drain drains their life. After 4-5 turns of this: their hand is empty, board is clear, and Sheoldred or Kalitas has been accumulating value. You count their remaining cards before attacking.

engines.title: See Their Hand, Take Their Win Condition
engines.body: You cast Thoughtseize on T1 in virtually every game 1. You see their entire plan, identify their win condition, and strip it. Against combo: take the combo piece. Against control: take their best answer. Against aggro: take their most impactful threat. The information gain is as valuable as the disruption.

engines.title: 4 Mana When They're Tapped
engines.body: You deploy Sheoldred, the Apocalypse when your opponent taps out or holds no interaction. You sequence: T1 Thoughtseize (strip their answer), T3 clear board, T4 Sheoldred. You never cast Sheoldred into open counter mana. Wait one turn.

engines.title: Cast Removal After Kalitas Enters
engines.body: You deploy Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet and THEN cast your removal spells. Each creature that dies to your removal while Kalitas is in play: it gets exiled AND you create a Zombie. You maximize Kalitas by sequencing him before your removal spells, not after.

engines.title: Two Modes, Choose Before Tapping
engines.body: You select Kolaghan's Command's two modes before tapping mana. Most common: return creature from GY + opponent discards. Alternative: destroy artifact + deal 2 damage. Rarest: deal 2 damage + opponent discards. You commit to two modes based on their board state BEFORE casting.

engines.title: Attrition Stack Until Empty
engines.body: Your late game: Thoughtseize has stripped their hand, removal has cleared their board, and Sheoldred or Kalitas is generating value. You count their remaining cards before swinging for lethal. Their hand must be empty and board clear before you commit to the killing attack.

engines.title: Thoughtseize Priority by Matchup
engines.body: vs UR Cutter: strip Stormchaser's Talent (their engine). vs RDW: strip Eidolon of the Great Revel (their tax card). vs Greasefang: strip Parhelion II (their kill piece). vs Lotus Field: strip Emergent Ultimatum or Bring to Light. vs UW Control: strip Teferi, Hero of Dominaria (their win condition and draw engine). vs Selesnya: strip Collected Company (their refuel) or Thalia (their tax). vs Phoeni

engines.title: Sheoldred Drain Math
engines.body: With Sheoldred in play: each opponent draw costs them 2 life. Standard draws: 1/turn = 2 life per turn (dies in ~10 turns from 20 life at no draws before). With cantrips: 3 draws/turn = 6 life per turn (dies in ~3 turns from 18 life). Control with Teferi: draws 1+ per turn + untap lands. Know the turn count to death so you know whether to attack or wait. Often: Sheoldred + 2-3 turns is lethal with

engines.title: SB Matches Expected Field
engines.body: Heavy GY (Phoenix, Greasefang): max Unlicensed Hearse + Go Blank. Heavy control: max Duress + Chandra. Heavy aggro (RDW, Selesnya): Brotherhood's End + Extinction Event. Heavy combo (Lotus Field): Duress + Extinction Event for odd-MV creature exiling (Vizier of Tumbling Sands = MV 3, odd). Confirm 15 cards match the expected field before registration.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Steam Vents = UR Cutter (Thoughtseize their Talent). Mountain only = RDW (board Abrade G2, don't Thoughtseize below 14 life). Godless Shrine = Greasefang (Thoughtseize Parhelion II, board Hearse G2). Hallowed Fountain = UW Control (Thoughtseize Teferi, board Duress + Chandra G2). Forest = Selesnya Company (Thoughtseize CoCo). Cycling land / Forest = Lotus Field (board Duress + Extinction Event G2)

engines.title: T1 Thoughtseize Targets
engines.body: Practice evaluating Thoughtseize targets by hand content. Rule: take the card that wins them the game, not the card you most recognize. Unknown cards are often worse than the card you recognize.

engines.title: Sheoldred Math
engines.body: Practice Sheoldred life drain math. They draw their card on upkeep: âˆ’2 life. Each Opt: âˆ’2 more. A control opponent casting 6 spells takes 12 damage from Sheoldred alone. Know when Sheoldred's clock is faster than your creatures.

engines.title: Kalitas Exile Lines
engines.body: Practice Kalitas exile trigger. When their creature dies (to your removal), it gets exiled AND you create a Zombie. Against Greasefang: exile Greasefang. They can't crew Parhelion again from GY. Know this interaction cold.

engines.title: Kolaghan's Command Modes
engines.body: Practice selecting Kolaghan's Command modes. Two modes simultaneously: most common is "return creature + deal 2 damage" or "destroy artifact + they discard." Know your two modes for each board state before casting.

Rakdos Monument is Standard's most resilient aggro-midrange deck. It wins three distinct ways simultaneously: pure aggro pressure from Moonshadow and Marauding Mako, graveyard recursion from Bloodghast and Flamewake Phoenix, and Monument to Endurance converting every discard into 1 damage + 1 life. Opponents who try to answer one axis find themselves losing to another. The deck's defin

The deck now runs 4 Blood Crypt + 4 Blazemire Verge (enters untapped if you control a swamp) + Starting Town (cycles) + Multiversal Passage (flexible MDFC). The two-color mana base is more consistent than three-color Monument variants. Every land enters untapped most of the time.

engines.title: Graveyard Hate, Fast Combo
engines.body: Soul-Guide Lantern exiles Bloodghast and Flamewake Phoenix — your recursion engine turns off. Izzet Prowess races before Monument gets going. Mono-Green Landfall generates boards too large to race through once Earthbender Ascension triggers. Dimir Excruciator can bounce your Monument permanently.

EOT: Monument triggers (discard Flail'd card) — 1 damage + 1 life. T3: Bloodghast returns on land drop (Landfall). Iron-Shield Elf provides a free discard for Monument each turn from here. By T5 with Monument pinging 1 per EOT + M

Bitter Triumph exiles their key permanent. Inti, Seneschal of the Sun generates card advantage whenever you discard. Even without Monument the deck is a legitimate aggro deck — creatures that recur, fly, and generate evasio

engines.body: Keep: any hand with Monument + 2 lands + one discard outlet. OR any hand with 3 creatures + 2 lands (aggro the Monument draws). At 5: 2 lands + Moonshadow + Bloodghast = keep (they recur, you need momentum).

Then choose Damage (deal 1 to opponent + gain 1 life) to accrue reach and life buffer. Treasure only when you need the mana for a key play next turn. engines.title: 4 Monument + 4 Moonshadow + 4 Bloodghast + 4 Bloodthorn Flail
engines.body: These 16 cards are the deck's engine. Monument is the payoff. Moonshadow is the scaling T1 threat. Bloodghast is the free recursive fuel. Bloodthorn Flail is the free discard outlet. Never reduce any below 4.

engines.title: Flamewake Phoenix
engines.body: 3 is correct for most metas. Go to 4 in midrange-heavy fields where your 4-power creature is reliably in play every upkeep. Cut to 2 in aggro-heavy metas where you need more main deck interaction (Tersa Lightshatter counts) rather than recursive threats.

engines.title: Iron-Shield Elf
engines.body: 3 main is the reference. Go to 4 in Monument-centric builds where you want maximum free discard triggers. The indestructible blocker effect is also relevant against creature-heavy fields. Cut to 2 in graveyard-hate-heavy metas where you want faster threats.

engines.title: Sunspine Lynx (0–2 main)
engines.body: 1 main is the current reference. Go to 2 main in metas where 80%+ of decks run 8+ nonbasics (current Standard is close to this). 0 main if you're expecting Boros energy or Mono-Red (basics-heavy). Never more than 2 main — it's a punisher card, not a proactive threat.

engines.title: Inti, Seneschal of the Sun (2–3)
engines.body: 3 is the reference. Cut to 2 in matchups where you want more direct interaction (Bitter Triumph slots). Inti generates card advantage but requires careful tracking. In fast metas where games end T4-5, the impulse draw doesn't have time to generate value — cut to 2 and add Requiting Hex or Tersa Lightshatter.

engines.title: Case of the Crimson Pulse
engines.body: Currently SB only (2 copies). Move 1 to main in control-heavy metas where the sustained Monument fuel across 10+ turns generates crushing advantage. Don't main it in aggro-heavy metas — it's too slow. 2 SB is the right home for most environments.

engines.title: Monument Mode Selection
engines.body: You select Monument to Endurance's trigger mode before declaring which mode. Early game (20+ life): Damage mode (1 damage + 1 life). Mid game (resources depleted): Draw mode (1 card). Late game (closing): Creature mode (4/4 token). You map your life total to the correct mode each turn.

engines.title: Moonshadow Discard Value
engines.body: You discard via Bloodthorn Flail to grow Moonshadow (Ayara) intentionally. Each discard fuels your Moonshadow's power while also creating cards in GY for Flamewake Phoenix's return condition. You discard excess lands and redundant copies — never discard your key interaction pieces.

engines.title: Phoenix Return Threshold
engines.body: You maintain a 4+ power creature every turn for Flamewake Phoenix's return condition. Moonshadow at 5+ power enables Phoenix. If your board drops below 4 power (Moonshadow removed), Phoenix doesn't return next upkeep. You track your largest creature's power every turn.

engines.title: Iron-Shield Elf Protection
engines.body: When they target Iron-Shield Elf with removal: you discard a card to make Elf indestructible until EOT. You do this automatically in response. Elf + discard outlet always in hand means you can protect Elf from removal indefinitely as long as you have cards to discard.

engines.title: Sunspine Lynx Count
engines.body: You run more Sunspine Lynx copies in metas with many nonbasic-heavy decks. Against 3-color metas: 3-4 copies (many nonbasics per opponent). Against mono-color metas: 0-1 copies (few nonbasics to punish). You audit your expected nonbasic count per opponent before each tournament.

engines.title: Pyroclasm vs Slagstorm
engines.body: Pyroclasm ({1}{R}: 2 damage to each creature) handles 2-toughness threats. Slagstorm ({1}{R}{R}: 3 damage or 3 to each player) handles 3-toughness threats but costs more. You run Pyroclasm in fast metas with small creatures (RDW, aggressive tokens). You run Slagstorm in metas with 3-toughness creatures where Pyroclasm misses too often.

engines.title: Nihil Spellbomb vs Soul-Guide Lantern
engines.body: Nihil Spellbomb ({1}: exile target player's GY; when sacrificed, draw for {B}) and Soul-Guide Lantern ({1}: exile target GY; when put in your GY, draw for {B}) have similar effects. Spellbomb targets one player's GY specifically. Lantern targets any GY. You run Spellbomb when you specifically need to exile THEIR GY (not your own). Run Lantern when flexibility matters.

engines.title: Case of the Crimson Pulse Flex
engines.body: Case of the Crimson Pulse fuels Monument every upkeep while generating card draw. You run more copies in control matchup slots where the game going 7+ turns makes Case's slow drip of value profitable. You cut Case in fast matchups where the game ends before Case generates enough value.

engines.title: Iron-Shield Elf Copies
engines.body: Iron-Shield Elf (indestructible via discard) is your resilience piece against removal-heavy metas. You run 3-4 copies in metas with many targeted removal spells. You cut Elf copies in metas where sweepers (not targeted removal) are the primary threat — Elf doesn't survive sweepers. You adjust based on single-target vs sweeper ratio.

engines.title: Roiling Vortex Quantity
engines.body: You run Roiling Vortex in metas with many lifegain sources (UW Control, Selesnya, Azorius). Vortex at {R} denies all lifegain and deals 1 per spell. In non-lifegain metas: cut Vortex from your SB. The card is narrowly metagame-specific — when lifegain is common, run 3-4; when rare, run 0.

engines.title: Disciple of the Vault
engines.body: Disciple of the Vault (1/1: whenever an artifact is put into a GY, target opponent loses 1 life) triggers on each Monument artifact token creation and each Blood token sacrifice. Multiple Disciples create a drain engine: Monument + 3 Disciples + 3 artifact triggers = 9 life drain passively per turn.

engines.title: Monument Synergy Stack
engines.body: Monument to Endurance's Damage mode and your creatures' life drain stack. Monument deals 1 and gains 1 each trigger. Your Flamewake Phoenix is a free recurring threat. Moonshadow's menace forces blocks. All three together make winning through combat or life gain extremely difficult for opponents.

engines.title: Ob Nixilis Finisher
engines.body: Ob Nixilis, the Adversary (planeswalker: casualty 1 copies him; +1 makes them discard; −2 makes Imp token; −7 wins) is your planeswalker finisher. With casualty 1: you sacrifice a small creature to make two Ob Nixilis. Two Ob activations per turn rapidly drains their hand.

engines.title: Tenacious Underdog Cycling
engines.body: Tenacious Underdog (2/3 with blitz: pay {B}{R} to cast as a hasty 2/3 that draws a card when it dies) cycles through your deck at 2 mana. You blitz Underdog when you need a card draw immediately — pay blitz cost, attack, Underdog dies at EOT, draw a card.

engines.title: Rix Maadi Reveler Cycle
engines.body: Rix Maadi Reveler (2/2: ETB discard and draw for each discarded) refuels your hand while triggering Monument damage and growing Moonshadow. With spectacle (paid when opponent lost life this turn): draw 3 instead of 1. You cast Reveler after dealing damage to trigger spectacle.

engines.title: Bloodthorn Flail Activation
engines.body: Bloodthorn Flail equips to a creature and lets you discard for effects. You activate Flail when you have excess lands in hand or duplicate cards. Every Flail activation: grows Moonshadow + fuels Flamewake Phoenix return + creates Monument triggers.

engines.title: Case Solve Trigger
engines.body: Case of the Crimson Pulse solves when you have a creature with power ≥ 4. After solving: you draw a card every upkeep. Your Moonshadow at 4+ power triggers Case solve. Once solved, Case generates one card per turn passively.

engines.title: Ayara Sacrifice Mode
engines.body: Ayara, Widow of the Realm (Moonshadow's other face): you can sacrifice a non-token creature to give target creature −X/−X until EOT where X = sacrificed creature's power. You sacrifice expendable creatures to kill their key threat in a pinch.

engines.title: Kolaghan's Command Recursion
engines.body: Kolaghan's Command's "return creature from GY to hand" mode recurs your key creatures. Against removal-heavy opponents: return Flamewake Phoenix from GY to hand — then discard it to Flail to put it back in GY for haste recursion.

engines.title: Every Turn Adds Up
engines.body: Monument to Endurance's damage triggers stack. At 1 damage per trigger × 1 trigger per turn × 10 turns: 10 accumulated damage before a creature attacks. You think of Monument as a slow but unstoppable clock — your opponent takes 10 damage just from you having Monument in play for 10 turns.

engines.title: Nearly Free Threat
engines.body: Flamewake Phoenix costs {1}{R}{R} initially. After it dies and returns from GY at your upkeep (if you control a 4+ power creature), it's free. A Phoenix that dies in combat returns next upkeep — it's never truly gone. You attack with Phoenix freely because the cost to return it is zero.

engines.title: Track Your Discard Count
engines.body: Moonshadow (Ayara, the Widow) gets larger each time you discard a card. You track your total discard count: each Bloodthorn Flail activation grows Moonshadow by 1. At 5 discards: Moonshadow is a 6+ power menace creature requiring two blockers every combat.

engines.title: Slow But Reliable Draw
engines.body: Case of the Crimson Pulse generates a card draw every upkeep when its condition is met. You deploy Case when you expect the game to go 7+ turns and value card advantage over speed. Against aggressive decks: skip Case and run Pyroclasm instead.

engines.title: Early Damage, Late Creature
engines.body: You select Monument to Endurance's trigger mode before declaring which mode. At 20+ life: Damage mode (accumulate a life buffer). At 10-15 life: Draw mode (find answers). At 8 life or below: Creature mode (4/4 token races the clock). You never default to one mode — you evaluate your life total each trigger.

engines.title: Discard Lands and Copies
engines.body: You discard excess lands and redundant card copies to grow Moonshadow (Ayara). You never discard your interaction pieces or your live threats. Lands after your 5th: always discard. Second copies of Monument: discard if the first is active. You maximize Moonshadow's power through strategic discard.

engines.title: Always Protect In Response
engines.body: When they target Iron-Shield Elf with removal: you discard a card immediately in response to make Elf indestructible until EOT. You never let Elf die to targeted removal — your discard supply is almost always sufficient to protect it. Discard a land, never a threat.

engines.title: Maintain 4+ Power
engines.body: Flamewake Phoenix returns from your GY at the beginning of combat each upkeep if you control a creature with 4+ power. You track your largest creature's power before your combat phase. Moonshadow at 5+ power: Phoenix returns. If Moonshadow was removed: you need another 4+ power creature or Phoenix doesn't return.

engines.title: T3 Before Their Nonbasics
engines.body: You deploy Sunspine Lynx on T3 before they've played their T3 nonbasic land. Lynx must be in play BEFORE their nonbasic land drop to trigger 3 damage on that land. You calculate: how many nonbasics do they have left to play? If 2-3: deploy Lynx immediately for maximum damage.

engines.title: Monument Priority: Draw → Damage → Treasure
engines.body: Internalize this before the event. You will be prompted for Monument's choice dozens of times per round. Default: Draw when hand <3 cards. Damage when hand 3+ cards. Treasure only when you need mana next turn for a specific play. Never take Treasure reflexively — Draw and Damage compound across a game in ways Treasure doesn't.

engines.title: Flamewake Phoenix Return Check
engines.body: At the beginning of EACH of your upkeeps: look at your board. Do you control a creature with power 4+? (Moonshadow with 3+ GY permanents, Marauding Mako, Bloodthorn Flail-pumped creature that survived). If yes AND Phoenix is in GY: announce Phoenix return before any other upkeep triggers. If you miss it, the trigger is still there if noticed before the next step. Don't shortcut upkeep — this matte

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Forest / Stomping Ground = Mono-Green or Temur → board Requiting Hex. Steam Vents / Botanical Sanctum = Izzet → board Soul-Guide Lantern + Pyroclasm. Breeding Pool / Watery Grave = Dimir → board Sunspine Lynx + Vengeful Possession. Swamp only = Dimir Midrange → board Vengeful Possession. Mountain only = Mono-Red Aggro → board Pyroclasm + keep Iron-Shield Elf for blocking. No nonbasics T1 = Boros o

engines.title: Pre-Round
engines.body: Count their nonbasics after G1 — is Sunspine Lynx correct G2? Did they use graveyard recursion G1? → Soul-Guide Lantern G2. Did they have enchantments that mattered? → Requiting Hex G2. Did their creatures have more than 2 toughness on avg? → Pyroclasm is weak, consider Case of the Crimson Pulse instead. Track your own GY carefully — Inti's impulse exile disappears end of next turn.

engines.title: Monument Mode Selection
engines.body: Practice selecting Monument to Endurance's trigger mode each turn. Early game: Damage mode for life buffer. Mid game: Draw mode to dig for answers. Late game: Creature mode for the closing 4/4.

engines.title: Phoenix Return Threshold
engines.body: Practice maintaining the 4+ power creature for Phoenix return. Moonshadow at 5+ power enables Phoenix. If Moonshadow is killed, you need another 4+ power creature by your upkeep for Phoenix to return.

engines.title: Iron-Shield Elf Protection
engines.body: Practice the Iron-Shield Elf indestructible activation. They target Elf with removal: in response, discard a card â†’ Elf becomes indestructible until EOT â†’ their removal does nothing.

engines.title: Sunspine Lynx Timing
engines.body: Practice deploying Sunspine Lynx before they play their nonbasic lands. Deploy on T3 before their T3 nonbasic for maximum damage. Lynx on T5 misses 2-3 nonbasic land drops.

RED DECKWINS.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "Every card does damage. Every creature has haste or a relevant ability. Every turn you're threatening lethal. The question is whether they can answer fast enough." Red Deck Wins is the purest aggro strategy in Pioneer. The plan is the same every game: play one-drop threats, cast burn spells to clear blockers or go face, and end the game before the opponent can stabilize. The deck runs zero cards that don't either deal damage or enable something that deals damage. Monastery Swiftspear is the engine. Every spell cast after Swiftspear gives +1/+1 until end of turn. A sin
RED DECKWINS.mulligan:
Mulligan
Need a T1 Threat + 3 Spells
Keep: any hand with a one-drop (Swiftspear/Soul-Scar/Ghitu) and 3+ burn spells on 2 lands.

engines.title: Fastest Consistent Kill in Pioneer
engines.body: UR Cutter kills on T3 sometimes. RDW kills on T3 consistently. A Swiftspear + Wild Slash + Lightning Strike + Wizard's Lightning hand deals 12 damage by turn 2 with zero creatures from the opponent. The nut draw kills on T2 with any two prowess triggers.

engines.title: No Moving Parts
engines.body: Nothing combos. Nothing needs setup. Every card in the deck works independently. They can take your Swiftspear, your Lightning Strike still deals 3. They can counter your Giant, Stomp already resolved. Every card in your hand is a threat or removal on its own.

engines.title: Eidolon Wins Games by Existing
engines.body: Many opponents can't kill Eidolon without losing 2 more life to it. Against Greasefang: every discard outlet costs 2. Against control: every interaction costs 2. Against UR Cutter: every cantrip costs 2. Some games you just play Eidolon on T2 and watch them die to their own answers.

engines.title: Monastery Swiftspear — Prowess Haste
engines.body: Haste means it attacks the turn it enters. Prowess gives +1/+1 until end of turn for each noncreature spell — in a deck with 22 spells this means every attack turn is a +2/+2 to +5/+5 swing. A T1 Swiftspear + T2 three spells (Lightning Strike + Wild Slash + Play with Fire) attacks for 4 and deals 6 from spells = 10 damage by the end of turn 2.

engines.title: Eidolon of the Great Revel — 2 Per Spell
engines.body: Deals 2 damage to each player whenever either player casts a spell with MV 3 or less. You accept losing 2 per spell yourself; your opponent loses 2 per every answer, cantrip, or interaction they cast. In matchups where they need 4-6 spells to stabilize, that's 8-12 free damage from Eidolon alone. The opponent usually dies trying to remove it.

engines.title: Bonecrusher Giant // Stomp
engines.body: Stomp (the Adventure) deals 2 damage and prevents damage prevention for the turn — critical vs Selesnya Company's protection spells. After casting Stomp for {1R}, cast Bonecrusher Giant later as a 4/3 body. It also has "whenever a spell or ability deals damage to Bonecrusher Giant, counter that spell or ability" — makes it hard to kill with small burn.

engines.title: Wizard's Lightning — {R} with Wizard
engines.body: Normally costs {2R}, but costs just {R} if you control a Wizard. Soul-Scar Mage, Ghitu Lavarunner (when you've cast a spell this turn), and Bonecrusher Giant are all Wizards. In virtually every game, Wizard's Lightning costs {R} by turn 2. A {R} Lightning Bolt effect is the best rate on a burn spell in Pioneer.

engines.title: T1–T4 Kill
engines.body: T1: Monastery Swiftspear (attacks for 1). T2: Eidolon of the Great Revel + one spell — opponent takes 2 from Eidolon, Swiftspear attacks for 3 (prowess). They're at 14. T3: Wizard's Lightning for {R} + two more spells — 3+2+2 = 7 damage. They're at 7. T4: any two spells = lethal. This is a clean T4 kill doing nothing unusual.

engines.title: Need a T1 Threat + 3 Spells
engines.body: Keep: any hand with a one-drop (Swiftspear/Soul-Scar/Ghitu) and 3+ burn spells on 2 lands. Mulligan: all Mountains and no action, hands with 4+ lands, hands with only creatures and no burn. At 6: keep any 1-drop + 2 spells on 2 lands. At 5: keep 1-drop + 2 burn + 2 lands — anything less is too slow.

engines.title: Light Up the Stage for {R}
engines.body: Light Up the Stage costs {2R} normally but {R} with Spectacle — triggered when you deal damage to an opponent. Since Swiftspear attacks T1, Light Up the Stage costs {R} on T2 every game. It exiles the top two cards of your library and you may play them until next turn. This is {R} for two cards — extraordinary value that refuels after the initial burst.

engines.title: The 21st-22nd Point of Damage
engines.body: Ramunap Ruins is a land that can deal 1 damage by tapping and paying 1 life. In many games you win at 1 life by activating it for the last point. More importantly: it makes your "land" draws functional damage sources in topdeck mode. At 4-5 mana with a creature on board and no cards in hand, Ramunap Ruins often represents the final 2 damage they can't see coming.

engines.title: When to Redirect Burn
engines.body: Your default is always: burn the player, not the creature. Redirect burn to their creature ONLY when: (1) their creature is about to block your best attacker and the blocked damage exceeds the burn damage, OR (2) their creature will win the game if it stays in play (e.g., Sheoldred). In all other cases, their life total is your target. Calculate the math before redirecting.

engines.title: Your Best Card in Mirrors
engines.body: Eidolon of the Great Revel deals 2 damage whenever they cast a spell with MV ≤ 3. You deploy it on T2 before they can answer it. Against interactive decks: every cantrip (Opt, Consider) costs them 2 life. Every removal spell costs them 2 life. Against creature decks: every one-drop costs them 2 life. Your Eidolon often deals 8-10 damage before they remove it.

engines.title: Anti-Lifegain Package
engines.body: Your Rampaging Ferocidon (SB) stops ALL life gain by all players. Against Greasefang: Parhelion II's lifelink triggers do nothing. Against Selesnya Company: their Voice of Resurgence lifelink, their Knight of Autumn life gain — all negated. You deploy Ferocidon on T3 after their key life gain source is in play. Menace means they need two blockers for it every combat.

engines.title: Mapping Lethal
engines.body: Before your attack each turn, map your kill. Current damage: Swiftspear (3/4 after pumps) + Goblin Guide (2/2) = 5 attacking. Burn in hand: Wizard's Lightning (3) + Burst Lightning (2) = 5. At 8 or less life: this is lethal. You always know the exact life total where your hand is lethal before you commit to attacking. Never attack without knowing the number.

engines.title: Prowess Burst
engines.body: Monastery Swiftspear and Soul-Scar Mage both have prowess (+1/+1 per noncreature spell). Chain three spells on your attack turn and each creature swings for +3/+3. The burn spells that deal direct damage ALSO trigger prowess — they serve dual purpose as removal/reach AND pump. A hand with Swiftspear + three burn spells presents 15+ damage by turn 3.

engines.title: Eidolon Damage Clock
engines.body: Eidolon of the Great Revel is a passive damage source — every spell your opponent casts costs them 2 life. In most matchups this is 8-16 free damage over the course of a game. The opponent must choose: ignore Eidolon and die to it, or use resources to kill it and die to your burn. Either path accelerates their death. You accept the same tax on yourself, but you deal damage faster.

engines.title: Burn to the Face
engines.body: 22 spells in the main deck, 18 of which deal damage directly. When opponents stabilize the board, you still have direct damage to close. Wizard's Lightning for {R}, Wild Slash, Lightning Strike, Play with Fire — any two of these from topdeck mode close from 6. Ramunap Ruins can contribute the last 1-2 damage without drawing a card. You never truly flood out.

engines.title: Your Free Damage Multiplier
engines.body: Eidolon of the Great Revel makes them pay 2 life per spell they cast with MV ≤ 3. You deploy Eidolon on T2 before they have removal mana available. Your payoff: their Opt costs them 2. Their Fatal Push costs them 2. Their any one-drop costs them 2. Against interactive decks: you deal 10+ damage from Eidolon alone before they finally remove it. You attack aggressively while Eidolon is live — your d

engines.title: Your Primary Clock
engines.body: Monastery Swiftspear (1/2 haste prowess) attacks the turn it enters and pumps +1/+1 for each instant/sorcery you cast. Your pump sequencing: cast burn before attacking → Swiftspear pumps from the spell → attack with buffed Swiftspear. You never attack first and pump second — always cast spells first. At 3 spells in one turn, Swiftspear attacks as a 4/5.

engines.title: Your Anti-Lifegain Package
engines.body: Rampaging Ferocidon (3/3 menace SB): opponents can't gain life AND they take 1 damage whenever a creature enters under their control. You deploy it against Greasefang (no Parhelion lifelink), Selesnya Company (each Company creature entering deals 1 to them), UW Control (no Lyra lifelink). Menace means they need two blockers — your Ferocidon attacks through most defenses.

engines.title: Your Hasty Scout
engines.body: Goblin Guide (2/2 haste) attacks the turn it enters AND reveals their top card (they get a land if it's a land). You attack immediately on T1. Your payoff: 2 damage at haste before they can deploy blockers. Their free land is the downside — you accept it. You never wait to deploy Goblin Guide hoping for a better board state. T1 Guide attacks for 2, and 2 early damage is worth more than any land th

engines.title: Your T1-T4 Sequence
engines.body: You execute your curve on autopilot: T1 Goblin Guide or Monastery Swiftspear (attack immediately). T2 Eidolon of the Great Revel + one burn spell (attack with Swiftspear as 3/3 from prowess). T3 two burn spells + attack (Swiftspear at 4/4). T4 burn any remaining life total. You commit fully to your curve — you never hold spells hoping for a better line.

engines.title: Your Eidolon Priority
engines.body: You deploy Eidolon on T2 before they have removal mana. You never wait for a "better" time — every turn Eidolon lives generates 2 damage per spell they cast. Your primary goal after deploying Eidolon: protect it by pointing their removal at your other threats. You never cast two spells in one turn when you can cast one and hold the other for T3 Eidolon backup.

engines.title: Your Burn-Face Protocol
engines.body: You burn their life total, not their creatures, unless their creature blocks your best attacker AND blocking costs you more damage than the burn would deal. You calculate: if their 3/3 blocks your 4/4 Swiftspear, you're losing 3 damage next turn via their attack. Bolt their blocker instead. In every other case: bolt face.

engines.title: Your Kill Window Recognition
engines.body: You identify your kill window before your attack step every turn. At 8 life: Swiftspear (3) + Goblin Guide (2) + Wizard's Lightning (3) + Burst Lightning (2) = 10, lethal. You count your burn in hand plus your attack damage before swinging. Never attack when counting would reveal you're one spell short — save the attack step for the turn you can definitively close.

engines.title: Race and Apply Eidolon
engines.body: Against Greasefang, Lotus Field: race but add Eidolon. Every discard outlet, every setup spell they cast costs them 2 more life. Rampaging Ferocidon (SB) stops Lotus Field from gaining life. You often win game 1 before they can execute; game 2 Eidolon + Ferocidon is a hard lock on many combo draws.

engines.title: Kill Their Threats, Protect Clock
engines.body: Against UR Cutter: kill their Stormchaser's Talent early, prevent the Monk token engine from firing. Searing Blood (SB) kills a 1-toughness creature AND burns them for 2 more if it dies. Soul-Scar Mage's -1/-1 counters permanently shrink their prowess creatures. Your clock is faster than theirs if you remove their Cutter.

engines.title: Eidolon Wins the Game
engines.body: Against UW Control: play Eidolon on T2 and let them take 4-8 damage trying to answer it. Board in Chandra, Torch of Defiance — a threat they must answer but can't via counterspell without losing more life to Eidolon. Roiling Vortex (SB) prevents lifegain from Teferi, stops White Plains cycles. Every spell they cast is damage.

engines.title: Your Race and Burn Game Plan
engines.body: Against UW Control: you ignore their creatures entirely and burn their face. You deploy Eidolon of the Great Revel on T2 — every Absorb they cast costs them 2 more life from Eidolon. You attack every turn. You never hold burn for their creatures when their life total is 8 or below. Roiling Vortex (SB) negates their Lyra Dawnbringer lifelink — deploy it before they cast their threat.

engines.title: Your Race Line
engines.body: Against Greasefang: you kill them before T3. Your T1-T3 goldfish must put them at 6 or below before their T3 Greasefang + Parhelion combo. Rampaging Ferocidon (SB) prevents all life gain — they can't gain life from Parhelion's lifelink. You deploy Ferocidon on your T3 to stop them from stabilizing if they do survive. You never slow down to interact — you race.

engines.title: Your Eidolon Asymmetry
engines.body: Against other aggressive decks: you deploy Eidolon of the Great Revel and gain the asymmetric advantage. Eidolon hits your own spells too — but your spells cost less on average than theirs. You calculate: if Eidolon costs you 2 damage per spell but costs them 2 damage per spell AND you're applying more spells per turn, you're ahead. You deploy Eidolon in aggro mirrors and win through the life dama

engines.title: Your Ferocidon Line
engines.body: Against Selesnya Company: Rampaging Ferocidon on T3 deals 1 damage for each creature entering (Collected Company puts 2 in — 2 immediate damage from Ferocidon). Your attack plus Ferocidon's combat damage plus each creature ETB damage means you win faster than their wide strategy closes. You never slow down to block their small creatures — you attack face and let Ferocidon damage stack.

engines.title: Rampaging Ferocidon ×4
engines.body: A 3/3 menace for {2R} that prevents ALL lifegain while it's on the battlefield. Every source of lifegain — Scavenging Ooze, Collective Brutality, Sheltered by Ghosts, lifelink creatures — is completely shut off. Additionally, whenever a creature enters the battlefield, Ferocidon can be used to deal 1 damage to that player. It's your best card vs Selesnya Company, Greasefang (Parhelion angels), and

engines.title: Roiling Vortex ×2
engines.body: Enchantment that deals 1 damage to each player during their upkeep, AND prevents lifegain if you control Roiling Vortex and cast a red spell this turn. Shuts off Lotus Field's Abandon Hope lifegain, Teferi's life padding in control, and any other lifegain strategy. The passive upkeep damage is also relevant — 1-2 damage per turn adds up against opponents who stabilize at low life.

engines.title: Chandra, Torch of Defiance ×2
engines.body: Planeswalker that generates {R} mana on +1, deals 2 damage on +1 (alternate mode), and has a ultimate. More importantly: it's a permanent threat they must answer with creatures or targeted removal — neither is easy for UW Control. The mana generation mode helps deploy threats faster; the damage mode ignores counterspells since Chandra herself resolved. Costs 4 mana — bring in only vs control and m

engines.title: Abrade ×2 + Twinmaw ×2
engines.body: Abrade: 3 damage to any creature OR destroy target artifact. Instant speed. Hits Unlicensed Hearse, Treasure Cruise artifacts, CoCo targets. Twinmaw Stormbrood: {2R} creature with flying and "{R}: deal 1 damage to target player or planeswalker" — provides additional reach and evasion in matchups where the board stalls. Also a 3/2 body that attacks past ground blockers.

engines.title: Roiling Vortex Ã—2
engines.body: {R} Enchantment: Each spell deals 1 damage; opponents can't gain life. Board in vs UW Control (they can't gain life from Lyra or Settle the Wreckage; each spell they cast deals 1 damage), Orzhov Greasefang (they can't gain life from Parhelion II triggers). The passive damage and lifegain denial doubles your burn clock passively.

engines.title: Twinmaw Stormbrood Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{R} 2/3 Haste Dragon. When it attacks, deals 1 damage to each creature defending player controls. Board in vs Selesnya Company (the 1-damage ping kills their 1/1 mana dorks and small creatures on attack) and UR Cutter (the ping threatens their small 1/1 tokens). Haste means it attacks the turn it enters, pinging before they can deploy blockers.

engines.title: Rampaging Ferocidon Ã—2
engines.body: {2}{R} 3/3 Menace. Opponents can't gain life; when a creature enters under an opponent's control, Ferocidon deals 1 damage to them. Board in vs Orzhov Greasefang (can't gain life; each creature they deploy deals 1 damage) and Selesnya Company (Company puts two creatures in play â€” 2 damage from Ferocidon alone). Menace means it needs two blockers every combat.

engines.title: Searing Blood Ã—2
engines.body: {R}{R} Instant: Deals 2 damage to target creature. If that creature would die this turn, Searing Blood deals 3 damage to that creature's controller. Board in vs UR Cutter (kills their Dreadhorde Arcanist or key blue creature and deals 3 to them if it dies). The additional 3 damage to their controller effectively makes this a 5-damage spell if the creature dies.

engines.title: 4 Monastery Swiftspear
engines.body: The single best threat in the deck. Haste + prowess makes it impossible to play around. Cutting even one reduces your T1 threat density enough to meaningfully slow the deck's kill clock.

engines.title: 4 Eidolon of the Great Revel
engines.body: Too many matchups are decided by Eidolon alone. 4 copies ensures you draw it early and often. Some pilots cut to 3 to avoid the self-damage, but the win rate data supports 4 copies strongly.

engines.title: 4 Wild Slash + 4 Wizard's Lightning
engines.body: Wild Slash's ferocious mode and Wizard's Lightning's {R} cost are unique to this deck. Both give you burn effects at an efficiency no other deck can replicate. Never cut these.

engines.title: Bonecrusher Giant
engines.body: 2 is the reference number — a strong topdeck and answer to blockers, but the 3-mana cost makes it awkward in some draws. In creature-heavy metas (Selesnya) go to 3-4. In spell-heavy metas (control) trim to 1-2.

engines.title: Light Up the Stage
engines.body: 2 main is a meta call. In open metas where games go to T4+, run 4 for more gas. In fast aggro metas where T3 kills are normal, 2 is correct — you rarely need the extra cards if you're winning that quickly.

engines.title: Lifegain Is Minimal
engines.body: RDW is at its best when opponent lifegain is minimal. If the meta is full of Selesnya Company, go up on Ferocidon (main?). If it's full of control with Teferi, bring Chandra. If it's Cutter and Phoenix, you're favored — just register the reference list.

engines.title: Eidolon Commitment
engines.body: You deploy Eidolon on T2 and never look back. Even if Eidolon damages you (from your own spells), the symmetry favors you because your spells are cheaper on average. A 3-spell turn under Eidolon costs you 6 life but deals you 6 life worth of damage too — on net, you're even on the Eidolon symmetry while your opponent takes the same.

engines.title: Goblin Guide Blocking
engines.body: You never block with Goblin Guide unless you're in lethal danger. Goblin Guide is an attacker — it applies clock. Using it as a blocker delays your damage output by one turn. You accept trading 2 or 3 life to keep Guide attacking. The only exception: blocking prevents lethal damage this turn.

engines.title: Searing Blood Maximization
engines.body: Searing Blood deals 2 damage to target creature — if that creature dies this turn, deals 3 to its controller. You cast Searing Blood on their creature when it's already damaged (from combat) to ensure the death trigger fires. Cast it during combat (in response to blocks) so the creature dies in combat and you get the 3 damage to them.

engines.title: Ferocidon Deployment Timing
engines.body: You deploy Rampaging Ferocidon on T3 before they can gain life from their key source. Against Greasefang: deploy Ferocidon before their Parhelion II enters play. Against Selesnya: deploy before their Company resolves. Ferocidon must be in play BEFORE their life gain source — deploying after misses the trigger.

engines.title: Twinmaw Stormbrood Count
engines.body: Twinmaw Stormbrood (2/3 haste Dragon: when it attacks, deals 1 damage to each creature opponent controls) is your anti-token piece. You run 2-3 copies in token-heavy metas (Selesnya Company). You cut Stormbrood in non-token metas where its combat ping doesn't kill anything. The ping is relevant only when they have multiple 1/1 tokens.

engines.title: Searing Blood Meta Slot
engines.body: Searing Blood ({R}{R}: 2 damage to creature; if it dies this turn, 3 damage to controller) converts your creature removal into additional face damage. You run 2-3 copies in metas with many blockers that must die before you can attack through. You cut Searing Blood in metas where their creatures rarely survive to trigger the 3-damage follow-up.

engines.title: Roiling Vortex Count
engines.body: You maximize Roiling Vortex (3-4 copies) when your meta has multiple lifegain decks. Against a meta with 30%+ lifegain decks: 4 Vortex. Against a meta with 10%: 2 Vortex. You never run zero when the meta has any significant lifegain presence. Lifegain makes your burn math impossible — Vortex is mandatory in those matchups.

engines.title: Deal 2 Plus Get 3 More
engines.body: Searing Blood deals 2 damage to their creature. If that creature dies this turn: deals 3 damage to its controller. You set up the 3-damage trigger by damaging their creature in combat first, then casting Searing Blood — their 2-toughness creature is already damaged, so 2 more kills it and triggers the 3 damage.

engines.title: Two Blockers Required
engines.body: Rampaging Ferocidon has menace — needs two blockers every combat. Against wide boards: they might lack two blockers for Ferocidon while also blocking your other threats. You attack with Ferocidon into boards where they can't profitably double-block it while also blocking your other threats.

engines.title: Mulligan for T1 Play
engines.body: Your only T1 play is a creature. You mulligan any hand without one. The clock starts on T1 — a missed T1 means one fewer attack step and approximately 2 fewer damage over the course of the game. Two fewer damage often equals one fewer kill turn.

engines.title: Burn Before Attacking Always
engines.body: You cast burn spells BEFORE attacking with Monastery Swiftspear. Each spell gives Swiftspear +1/+1 (prowess) until EOT. You cast Lightning Bolt → Swiftspear is 2/3 → declare attack. You never attack first and then pump — the pumped stats apply to the current combat.

engines.title: T2 Before Their Removal Mana
engines.body: You deploy Eidolon of the Great Revel on T2 before they have interaction mana. Against UW Control: they have {W}{U} on T3 for Absorb. Against Lotus Field: they have mana online T3. Your window: T2 Eidolon before they can answer it profitably.

engines.title: Before Their Lifegain Source
engines.body: Rampaging Ferocidon must be in play BEFORE their lifegain source triggers. T3 Ferocidon before T4 Greasefang crews Parhelion: Parhelion's lifelink generates 0 life. If Parhelion attacks first and you deploy Ferocidon: you missed the Parhelion lifelink trigger.

engines.title: Lethal Math by Turn
engines.body: T3 lethal requires ~15-18 damage. Your standard sequence: T1 Swiftspear (attacks 1), T2 spell + Eidolon + Swiftspear attacks for 3 = 4, T3 three spells = 9+ damage. Total: 13-15. Wizard's Lightning for {R} is the card that tips you over lethal. Run these scenarios before each round starts.

engines.title: Eidolon Tax Per Matchup
engines.body: UR Cutter casts ~6-8 spells per game (cantrips + Cruise) = 12-16 from Eidolon. Greasefang runs 8-12 spells including discards = 16-24. Control runs 10+ spells = 20+. Your Eidolon is worth more damage than many of your burn spells. Protect it if they try to remove it without taking meaningful damage.

engines.title: SB Against Field
engines.body: Heavy Greasefang/Lotus: max Ferocidon + Vortex. Heavy control/midrange: Chandra + Vortex. Heavy aggro (Cutter, Phoenix): Searing Blood + Twinmaw. Abrade is for when Hearse or artifact hate appears. Confirm your 15 matches the expected room before registration.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Godless Shrine = Greasefang (board Ferocidon G2). Steam Vents or Island = Cutter/Phoenix (board Searing Blood). Hallowed Fountain = UW Control (board Chandra G2). Forest = Selesnya Company (board Ferocidon + Twinmaw). Mountain only = mirror or aggro (race, no SB changes).

engines.title: T4 Goldfish Kill
engines.body: Practice your T4 goldfish. T1: Goblin Guide (attack for 2). T2: Monastery Swiftspear + burn spell (attack for 6+2=8). T3: burn + attack (16). T4: burn for 4 = lethal. Know the sequence cold.

engines.title: Swiftspear Pump Sequencing
engines.body: Practice casting burn BEFORE attacking with Swiftspear. Cast Lightning Bolt (Swiftspear 2/3), cast Burst Lightning (Swiftspear 3/4), then attack. Never attack first then cast burn.

engines.title: Eidolon Damage Tracking
engines.body: Practice tracking Eidolon damage. Every cantrip, every removal spell they cast deals 2 damage. Count: their hand has 3 spells of MV â‰¤ 3 = 6 damage from Eidolon triggers before their next draw step.

engines.title: Burn Math at Low Life
engines.body: Practice the burn math at low life totals. At 4 life: Lightning Bolt (3) + Burst Lightning (2) = 5, lethal. Know the exact burn hands that close from low life without needing another attack.

RubyStorm.game_plan: Chapter 01 Overview "The deck doesn't care what you're playing. On turn three, it wins." Ruby Storm is Modern's premier critical-mass combo deck. It doesn't set up a two-card lock or assemble a specific combo — it overwhelms the game by chaining cheap spells until the Storm count reaches 20, then wins with a single Grapeshot . The engine has three phases: deploy a reducer, chain rituals and draw spells, then recast everything via Past in Flames . When it works, it's essentially unstoppable. When it's interrupted early, it dies in the water. What separates Ruby Storm from older Izzet Storm buil
RubyStorm.weaknesses: Grafdigger's Cage, Damping Sphere, Deafening Silence, Drannith Magistrate — all hard stops. Opponents bring multiple hate pieces. Ruby Storm pivots via Orim's Chant, Prismatic Ending, and speed before hate can be deployed.
RubyStorm.mulligan:
Mulligan Framework

You need to keep hands that can either (a) resolve a reducer by turn 2 or (b) cast enough impulse draws to find one by turn 3.

engines.title: Critical Mass Combo
engines.body: Not "A+B" combo. Wins by casting ~20 spells in one turn, generating enough storm count that a single Grapeshot deals lethal. No deterministic loop required — just enough mana and draws to keep chaining.

engines.title: Turn 2
engines.body: Turn 1 Strike It Rich → Turn 2: Ritual → Reducer → Ritual → chain draws → Past in Flames → Wish for Grapeshot. The realistic consistent kill is turn 3. Turn 2 requires a very specific hand but is achievable.

engines.title: Heavily Favored
engines.body: Almost every deck in Modern is unprepared for Storm game 1. No main-deck hate, no answers that line up cleanly. The impulse draw spells are 2-for-1s that can't be countered efficiently — opponents run out of answers first.

engines.title: Known Weakness
engines.body: Grafdigger's Cage, Damping Sphere, Deafening Silence, Drannith Magistrate — all hard stops. Opponents bring multiple hate pieces. Ruby Storm pivots via Orim's Chant, Prismatic Ending, and speed before hate can be deployed.

engines.title: Mana Counting
engines.body: The primary skill is precise mana counting before committing to a combo turn. Wasted rituals on aborted turns lose games. The deck rewards players who count to a winning line before spending resources, not those who "feel" their way through combos.

engines.title: Glass Cannon
engines.body: Excellent at unfair tables, poor against players who prepared. RCQ meta is consistently under-prepared for Storm. The deck rewards knowing your metagame: is your room running Cages and Spheres, or hoping their creatures kill you first?

engines.title: {2} · Artifact
engines.body: Red spells you cast cost {1} less. This is a static ability on an artifact — immune to creature removal, not immune to Stony Silence or artifact destruction. It reduces ONLY red spells. Not blue, not colorless. Does NOT reduce Ral, Monsoon Mage (Ral is red but also {1}{R}=2 mana, Ruby makes it {R}). However, Ral DOES reduce Ruby's cast cost from {2} to {1}. These directions are asymmetric — critic

engines.title: {1}{R} · Creature // Planeswalker
engines.body: Front: reduces instants and sorceries by {1}. Flip trigger: after 6 I/S spells during your turn, exile Ral and return him transformed. Back (Ral, Leyline Prodigy): +1 makes I/S cost {1} less until YOUR NEXT TURN — this persists through opponent's turn even if Ral dies. −8 exiles top 8, cast for free. Ral enters with loyalty counters = I/S cast this turn, so flipping early gives immediate -8 access

engines.title: {1}{R} · Instant — Arcane
engines.body: Adds {R}{R}{R}. Splice onto Arcane {1}{R}: when casting any Arcane spell, reveal Desperate Ritual from hand and pay {1}{R} to add its effect. Critically: Pyretic Ritual is NOT Arcane, so splice only triggers off Arcane spells. Always cast Pyretic Ritual first — Pyretic generates mana then the next Arcane spell can splice DR onto it. Incorrect order wastes the splice.

engines.title: {2}{R} · Sorcery
engines.body: Exile top 3, play THIS TURN only. At the beginning of the NEXT end step, cards remaining in exile from this effect go to the GY and create 0/1 Eldrazi Spawn tokens. Critical: cards can't be played next turn like Reckless Impulse — they're gone. Use Glimpse mid-combo only; using it early on a non-combo turn wastes cards unless you can immediately play everything revealed.

engines.title: {3}{R} · Sorcery
engines.body: All instants and sorceries in your GY gain flashback equal to their mana cost until EOT. Flashback {4}{R}. Critical: Grafdigger's Cage says "players can't cast spells from graveyards" — this shuts down ALL Past in Flames flashback. If Cage resolves, hold priority after casting Flames while it's still on the stack to cast instant-speed spells from hand before the Cage resolves. Leyline of Sanctity

engines.title: {W} · Instant
engines.body: Target player can't cast spells this turn. Kicker {W}: creatures can't attack. Requires WHITE mana — that's why Elegant Parlor (ETB tapped, {T}: W) and Sacred Foundry exist in the mana base. On your combo turn, chanting yourself lets you go off without counterplay. Chanting opponent during their upkeep buys one full turn to combo. The mana cost is real: you spend {W} from your non-red mana source.

engines.title: Setup
engines.body: Goal: resolve a cost reducer ( Ruby Medallion or Ral, Monsoon Mage ) and reach at least 3 mana. Without a reducer, winning the same turn requires a near-perfect hand. Use surveil lands and Reckless Impulse effects to find the missing piece. Don't waste rituals trying to "half-combo" — each wasted ritual costs you a full extra mana on the real turn.

engines.title: Threshold
engines.body: Count before you commit: "Do I have enough mana to cast 8+ spells AND find Past in Flames OR flip Ral ?" The Threshold check is mathematical. If the answer is yes with a reasonable margin, go. If no, durdle one more turn. The mistake is going "on feel" and running out of steam at 14 storm count with no Grapeshot.

engines.title: Execution
engines.body: Once off the ground, the deck basically can't be stopped. The draw spells find more mana, the mana finds more draws. Use Wish for the sideboard Past in Flames if needed. Prioritize flipping Ral once Ruby is in play — the -8 casting 8 spells for free essentially wins on the spot. End with Wish → Grapeshot .

engines.title: The Ideal 7
engines.body: 2 lands + 1 reducer + 2 rituals + 2 draw spells. This hand wins on turn 3 almost regardless of opponent's game plan. The mana curves perfectly — T1 land, T2 reducer, T3 ritual → ritual → draw → draw → Past in Flames → Grapeshot. Even if opponents hold up interaction, you can wait or chant through it.

engines.title: The Glass 6
engines.body: 1 land + fetch + reducer + 2 rituals + 1 draw. On the draw, the fetch + surveil land gives 3 looks at a second land (~72% to find it). On the play this drops to 60% — borderline. Keep on the draw, mulligan on the play unless the spells are excellent. The key: with a reducer and rituals, a single topdeck land wins the game.

engines.title: Pure Ritual Hands
engines.body: Hands with 4+ rituals and no draw spells. You make 10 mana and can't find Grapeshot. These hands feel powerful but are fundamentally broken — Storm needs to draw into more spells, not just float mana. Always ship these back.

engines.title: No Reducer
engines.body: A hand with zero reducers and no strong path to finding one by turn 2. The deck can technically win without a reducer but requires ~30+ spells in a turn — essentially impossible. Always mulligan any hand that can't realistically resolve Medallion or Ral by turn 2.

engines.title: Hand Required
engines.body: Turn 1 Strike It Rich → Turn 2: use Treasure + Mountain for RR. Ritual → reducer → ritual → chain. Needs 2 rituals + Manamorphose + Past in Flames or multiple draws to finish. Realistic but requires perfect opening. Primarily relevant to beat removal on the reducer deployment turn.

engines.title: Consistent
engines.body: The bread and butter. T1 land, T2 reducer, T3 go off. At this speed, most decks haven't assembled enough interaction to stop you. Boros Energy might have 4–6 damage in, but Grapeshot at 20 doesn't care. Against control, T3 catches them before they've set up full counter coverage.

engines.title: High Risk
engines.body: If you haven't killed by turn 4, the opponent has set up. Assume: (a) they've found their hate pieces, (b) creature decks have 8+ damage in, (c) combo opponents are also ready to win. Use Orim's Chant on their upkeep if needed to steal the extra turn. Valakut Awakening on turn 3 to cycle bad cards can enable a turn 4 kill instead.

engines.title: T1 Ruby Medallion Is Everything
engines.body: On the play, T1 Ruby Medallion dramatically accelerates your T2-3 kill. Every subsequent red spell costs 1 less. Grapeshot with Medallion in play costs {R} instead of {1}{R}. Past in Flames costs {2}{R} instead of {3}{R}. Mulligan aggressively for T1 Medallion hands on the play — a hand without Medallion or a cantrip to find it is playing a slower version of the deck.

engines.title: Extra Card Finds Missing Piece
engines.body: On the draw you see 8 cards, improving Medallion + kill spell odds. Keep looser hands on the draw — a cantrip-heavy hand without Medallion can keep on draw since you’ll see more cards. Against aggro on the draw: T1 Medallion is still correct over any other play. Against combo mirrors on the draw: Orim’s Chant hands (stop their combo turn) are more valuable since they’re a turn ahead.

engines.title: Second Medallion or Rebuild
engines.body: Medallion removed: assess your mana. Can you still reach kill mana without the discount? If you have a second Medallion in hand, deploy it immediately. If not, your kill turn requires 1 additional mana per spell — count whether you can still chain enough spells at full cost. If not, develop another cantrip turn to find the second Medallion or enough rituals.

engines.title: Empty the Warrens Backup
engines.body: Grapeshot countered: if your storm count was 8+, Empty the Warrens makes 16+ Goblin tokens. Attack on their empty board for lethal next turn. This backup plan requires no additional cards — just a second win condition in the SB. Post-board vs Leyline of Sanctity (stops Grapeshot targeting face), Empty the Warrens becomes the PRIMARY plan since tokens attack, not target.

engines.title: Ruby Medallion + Rituals
engines.body: Ruby Medallion reducing costs + Desperate Ritual/Pyretic Ritual generating mana = the storm engine. Every ritual at full cost generates {R}{R} from {R}. With Medallion, Pyretic costs {R} and generates {R}{R}{R} = net +2 mana. Chain rituals to build storm count. This engine is the foundation: Medallion first, then chain.

engines.title: Past in Flames Flashback Chain
engines.body: Past in Flames gives everything in your GY flashback until end of turn. After PiF resolves, flash back every ritual in your GY for massive mana generation and storm count building. Flash back cantrips for card selection. Flash back a second PiF if available. This engine takes a 3-5 storm count to a 15-20 storm count in one turn.

engines.title: Grapeshot or Empty the Warrens
engines.body: Grapeshot closes when storm count = enough damage. Empty the Warrens closes when facing Leyline of Sanctity or when they’re at 20 life and you can’t reach lethal storm. Calculate before casting: Grapeshot storm count × 1 damage per copy. If that’s not lethal, switch to Empty the Warrens and win on the attack next turn with 16+ tokens.

engines.title: Medallion T1 + Chain T2
engines.body: T1: Ruby Medallion ({1}{R}, now in play). T2: Pyretic Ritual ({R} with Medallion → +{R}{R}{R}). Desperate Ritual ({R} → +{R}{R}{R}). Seething Song ({2}{R} with Medallion = {1}{R} → +{R}{R}{R}{R}{R}). Chain cantrips. PiF ({2}{R} with Medallion). Flash back rituals. Grapeshot when storm = lethal. Requires: Medallion + multiple rituals + kill spell in opening 7.

engines.title: Default Kill Turn
engines.body: T1: Medallion or cantrip. T2: Deploy Medallion (if not T1) + ritual chain begins. T3: PiF + flashback chain + Grapeshot at storm 10+. At 20 life: storm 10 = 10 Grapeshot copies = 10 damage. Need storm 20+ for a clean kill from 20. With 2 Medallions: rituals cost 0 or {R}, chain becomes infinite with enough spells in GY.

engines.title: When to Force It
engines.body: Force T2: Facing Living End, Amulet, Neoform — all T2-3 combo decks. Race them. Any kill on T2 beats their T3. Hold for T3: They have open blue mana. Pass T2 with Orim’s Chant ready. Cast Chant on their upkeep (they can’t cast spells this turn), then chain freely T3 with no interaction possible.

engines.title: Ruby Medallion Reduces Generic Mana Only
engines.body: Ruby Medallion reduces the cost of red spells you cast by {1}. It reduces GENERIC mana only — not colored pip requirements. Lightning Bolt costs {R}: Medallion doesn’t reduce it (no generic). Grapeshot costs {1}{R}: Medallion reduces it to {R}. Past in Flames costs {3}{R}: Medallion reduces to {2}{R}. With 2 Medallions, Past in Flames costs {1}{R}. Calculate mana requirements before starting your

engines.title: Past in Flames Gives Itself Flashback
engines.body: Past in Flames gives all instants and sorceries in your graveyard flashback until end of turn — including itself. After PiF resolves, it goes to your GY. You can then flash it back again from the GY (paying {3}{R} or {2}{R} with Medallion) to give everything in GY flashback again. This means a single PiF can generate multiple copies of your storm pieces if you have the mana. The key: PiF’s flashba

engines.title: Storm Counts Spells Cast This Turn, Not Copies
engines.body: Grapeshot’s storm copies one copy for each spell cast before it this turn. The storm copies themselves are NOT spells cast — they’re copies put directly on the stack. Storm count: every ritual, every Medallion discount trigger, every cantrip, every PiF cast. Grapeshot itself counts as 1 spell. So storm of 10 = 9 previous spells + Grapeshot = 10 copies total. Count carefully before casting Grapesho

engines.title: No Blue Mana Visible
engines.body: Their opening land is not blue. They’ve spent their mana on T1-2. They’re on a fair deck with no stack interaction. Execute the combo as fast as possible. Every turn you wait gives them a draw step to find Force of Negation or Orim’s Chant.

engines.title: Blue Mana Visible
engines.body: Any open blue mana = potential Force of Negation. Cast Orim’s Chant at the beginning of their upkeep — they can’t cast spells this turn. Then combo freely on your turn. Chant is the strongest protection piece in the deck and costs 0 tempo when used optimally.

engines.title: Leyline or Low Storm Count
engines.body: Leyline of Sanctity in play: Grapeshot can’t target them. Switch to Empty. Storm count will be 14+ anyway — 28 Goblin tokens is a 2-swing kill at 20 life. Also switch when your storm count is high but Grapeshot math doesn’t reach lethal.

engines.title: Pre-Chain Calculation
engines.body: Before casting the first ritual in the chain, map your full line: available mana, available GY flashbacks, expected storm count, kill calculation. Committing to the chain without a kill line is a game loss. Calculate — then execute.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Low Force of Negation density in expected sideboards. Midrange-heavy field — no deck can interact with a T2-3 kill at sorcery speed. Orim’s Chant is legal — the event uses proper tournament rules. You’ve practiced counting storm under pressure. You know the Leyline backup (Empty the Warrens) cold.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy Force of Negation + Orim’s Chant mirror (Jeskai and UW builds run Chant post-board to stop you). Damping Sphere builds dominate the field (limits to 1 mana per land + costs 2 more per duplicate spell type). You haven’t tested the Empty the Warrens backup plan vs Leyline decks.

engines.title: Empty the Warrens ×4
engines.body: Your primary win condition. Four copies ensures you always have a finisher after storming off. Never cut.

engines.title: Goblin Electromancer ×4
engines.body: Your cost reducer. With Electromancer, your cantrips cost 0 and your ritual chain extends further. Four copies guarantees you see the reducer.

engines.title: Manamorphose
engines.body: 4 in most lists. Manamorphose fixes mana AND replaces itself AND adds a storm count. 3 copies is the floor — cut to 3 only when you need the slot for hate card answers.

engines.title: Defense Grid (SB)
engines.body: 2 vs heavy counter metas. Grid makes all their spells cost {2} more on your turn — their Counterspell costs {3}{U}{U}. Cut entirely when the field is creature-based.

engines.title: Grapeshot vs Empty the Warrens
engines.body: Grapeshot as your second finisher (1-2 SB copies) vs control where their life total doesn't matter but removing creatures does. Empty is better vs creature-based opponents. Know which finisher closes which matchup.

engines.title: Storm Count
engines.body: Count storm before casting Grapeshot in every rep. Never cast without counting first.

engines.title: Medallion Lines
engines.body: Practice T3 kills with and without Medallion in play. Know the mana difference.

engines.title: PiF Timing
engines.body: When do you cast Past in Flames? Practice identifying the right moment — not too early.

engines.title: Hate Navigation
engines.body: Play through Damping Sphere, Eidolon of the Great Revel, and Thalia. These are common post-board.

engines.title: White Mana Ready?
engines.body: Confirm you have Elegant Parlor + Sacred Foundry in your SB build for Orim's Chant. If you don't have white mana sources, Chants are dead cards. Check your land count: you need 20 lands total. Confirm fetch targets exist (Sacred Foundry for W/R).

engines.title: Know Your SB Targets
engines.body: Prismatic Ending hits MV 1 (Drannith Magistrate) with {W} or MV 2 (Damping Sphere, Cage) with {W}+another color. Brotherhood's End mode 2 destroys artifacts MV ≤ 3. Abrade is instant. These are not interchangeable — know which removal piece to bring for which hate piece before each round.

SELESNYACOMPANY.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "Every creature enters doing something. Thalia slows them down. CoCo refills your board at instant speed at the end of their turn. They never have a clean window to answer everything." Selesnya Company is Pioneer's premier creature-based midrange deck. The strategy is built around three interlocking pieces: mana acceleration through early elves, disruption through taxing creatures, and explosive board refills via Collected Company . No individual card is overwhelming, but the combination of consistent threat density, instant-speed surprise hits, and difficult-to-answer
SELESNYACOMPANY.mulligan:
Mulligan
Need a Mana Elf in Every Opening
Keep: any hand with a mana elf + 2-3 lands + at least one two-drop or CoCo.

engines.title: Board Wipes Don't End the Game
engines.body: Against a traditional midrange or aggro deck, a sweeper ends the game. Against Selesnya Company, a sweeper is answered by a CoCo end of their turn and two creatures entering play. Extraction Specialist returns another creature from your GY. Your opponent needs multiple sweepers in sequence to contain the board, and control decks rarely have that.

engines.title: Thalia Slows Every Deck
engines.body: Thalia taxes all noncreature spells {1} extra. In a format where UR Cutter runs 20+ noncreature spells, Greasefang depends on discards, and control relies on cheap interaction, Thalia's tax generates 4-8 extra mana worth of tempo over the course of a game. She makes every opponent's turn more awkward from turn 2 onward.

engines.title: T2 Three-Drops Every Game
engines.body: Eight mana dorks make T2 three-drops consistent. A T1 elf into T2 Thalia or Voice of Resurgence is a strong clock. T3 Collected Company (hitting two creatures) puts you at 4-5 creatures on the board by turn 3. No other midrange deck in Pioneer can deploy this much threat volume this early while also disrupting the opponent.

engines.title: Collected Company — Instant-Speed Two-for-One
engines.body: Cast at end of their turn for {3G}: reveal top 6, put up to two creatures with MV ≤ 3 into play. With 28 creatures (MV 1-3) in the deck, expected hits: 2 creatures roughly 85%+ of the time. The instant speed is the key advantage — they can't tap out for a four-mana spell at end of their turn safely when you have {3G} available. Always ask: what's the best time to CoCo? Usually end of their turn 3

engines.title: Thalia, Guardian of Thraben — {1} on Everything
engines.body: All noncreature spells cost {1} more for both players. Against UR Cutter: Vivi Ornitier, cantrips, and Treasure Cruise all cost more. Against Greasefang: Monument looting, discard outlets, everything costs more. Against control: counterspells, removal, and wraths cost more. Your deck runs almost entirely creatures — Thalia taxes them asymmetrically. The 2/1 first strike body is also difficult to p

engines.title: Kellan, Daring Traveler — Draw on Attack
engines.body: 2/1 for {1G} that draws a card when it deals combat damage to a player. With mana elves enabling T2 Kellan, you often draw your first card on T2. Every time Kellan connects you pull ahead on cards. He's your card advantage engine in creature mirrors where both sides are trading resources. Small enough to CoCo into, large enough to trade with most one-drops.

engines.title: Extraction Specialist — Return + 3/2 Body
engines.body: 3/2 for {2W}. When it enters, return a creature with MV 2 or less from your GY to play (tapped). This means your Llanowar Elves, Thalia, Voice of Resurgence, Kellan, and Skrelv never truly die — Extraction Specialist loops them back. It creates a recursive engine where removal never permanently answers your threats. A key CoCo hit in any late-game scenario.

engines.title: T1–T4 Board Dominance
engines.body: T1: Llanowar Elves or Elvish Mystic. T2: Thalia (tapping the elf) + Voice of Resurgence. Opponent is now taxed and facing a 2/2 + 2/1 first strike. T3: Attack for 4, then cast Collected Company on their end step, hitting two creatures from 6. T4: Untap with 5 creatures, attack for lethal or near-lethal. This is a T4 kill doing nothing unusual.

engines.title: Need a Mana Elf in Every Opening
engines.body: Keep: any hand with a mana elf + 2-3 lands + at least one two-drop or CoCo. Mulligan: hands with zero mana dorks (you're a turn behind every other Pioneer deck without acceleration), hands with 5+ lands, and hands with CoCo but nothing to accelerate into it on T3. At 6: elf + land + any two-drop is keepable. 5-card hands: elf + land + Thalia is correct.

engines.title: End of Their Turn, Not Your Main Phase
engines.body: Always cast Collected Company at the end of the opponent's turn unless you need the creatures to block immediately. Waiting for their end step means: (1) you untap with the creatures, (2) they couldn't interact during their turn with full mana up, (3) they committed resources assuming you had no action. The surprise factor of instant-speed creatures is a major part of the deck's strength.

engines.title: Force Them Off Instant-Speed Interaction
engines.body: Voice of Resurgence creates an Elemental token when either player casts a spell during your turn. It punishes instant-speed interaction during your main phase — if they counterspell or remove a creature on your turn, they give you a token. This forces them to let your spells resolve or pass without interaction. Against control, Voice completely warps how they can deploy answers.

engines.title: Eight Mana Dorks
engines.body: 4 Llanowar Elves + 4 Elvish Mystic = eight unconditional T1 one-mana green creatures that produce {G}.
