The math: with 8 elves in 60 cards and 28 creatures total, you have a ~78% chance of having a mana dork in your opening 7. Without them, you're a turn behind on every curve — with them, you're deploying three-mana threats on turn two consistently.

engines.title: Thalia + Voice Tax Package
engines.body: Thalia taxes noncreature spells. Voice of Resurgence punishes instant-speed interaction on your turn. Together they create a zone of control: opponents must cast spells at sorcery speed (to avoid Voice tokens) but Thalia's tax means those sorceries cost more mana. The two-card combination warps opponent sequencing more than either card alone.

engines.title: CoCo + Extraction Loop
engines.body: Collected Company refills your board from your library at instant speed. Extraction Specialist refills your board from your graveyard. Together, they make your threat supply essentially infinite in longer games. A sweeper leaves them tapped out; CoCo on your end step puts two more into play. Extraction Specialist on the following turn returns the best MV-2 creature from the GY.

engines.title: Clock + Disruption
engines.body: Against Greasefang and Lotus Field: deploy Thalia early to tax their setup, apply clock with creatures, and win before they execute. You're not trying to interact with the combo — Thalia buying one extra turn is often enough. Leyline of Sanctity (SB) prevents Thoughtseize from disrupting your hand. Rest in Peace (SB) shuts off Parhelion II recursion.

engines.title: Outclass Their Board
engines.body: Against RDW: your creatures are larger and you have Knight of Autumn for lifegain. Gaining 4 life from Knight stabilizes against burn. Lathiel, the Bounding Dawn generates +1/+1 counters on life gain — a board that gains life and grows is difficult for burn to close against. Against UR Cutter: your bodies block their Monks profitably; Thalia slows their cantrips.

engines.title: Play Around Wraths
engines.body: Against UW Control: deploy two threats, hold CoCo in hand. When they tap out for a wrath, CoCo their end step. Never overcommit more than 3-4 creatures unless you're killing them that turn. Voice of Resurgence makes them choose between tapping out for a sorcery-speed wrath or holding mana for interaction — either path benefits you.

engines.title: Leyline of Sanctity ×3
engines.body: Prevents you from being targeted by discard spells, burn, and other targeted effects. Against Greasefang, Thoughtseize is their primary disruption — Leyline in your opening hand completely blanks that plan. Notably, Leyline is free if in your opening 7, making it perfect against hand disruption strategies that would normally strip your combo answers before you can cast them.

engines.title: Rest in Peace ×2
engines.body: Enchantment that exiles all GY cards and exiles everything going to the GY afterward. A T2 Rest in Peace completely answers Greasefang (no Parhelion II to return), Arclight Phoenix (can't return from GY), and any other GY-based strategy. Your deck doesn't use the GY in game 2-3 after boarding — Extraction Specialist is cut. Rest in Peace is a one-sided lock in most GY matchups.

engines.title: Damping Sphere ×2
engines.body: Artifact that makes lands only produce {C} if they produce more than one mana, and spells cost {1} extra per spell cast by that player this turn. Shuts off Lotus Field's mana generation completely. Also relevant vs any storm-style combo. Comes in alongside Thalia's tax for a double-disruption package against mana-intensive combo decks.

engines.title: Shapers' Sanctuary ×2
engines.body: Enchantment: whenever a creature you control becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, draw a card. Against UW Control and any targeted removal deck, this converts their interaction into card draw for you. They can't answer Shapers' Sanctuary with their removal (it's an enchantment), and every removal spell they cast draws you a card. Creates an insurmountable card advantage g

engines.title: Damping Sphere Ã—2
engines.body: {2} Artifact: Spells cost {1} more per spell already cast this turn; lands produce only colorless. Board in vs Lotus Field (lands produce only colorless â€” their entire combo is offline), UR Cutter (each spell after their first costs {1} more â€” slows their free-spell chains significantly). The colorless land clause is the critical mode vs Lotus Field.

engines.title: Shapers' Sanctuary Ã—2
engines.body: {G} Enchantment: Whenever a creature you control becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, draw a card. Board in vs UW Control (every time they target your creature you draw) and UR Cutter (every Bolt or target draws you a card). Makes their removal draw you cards â€” they effectively pay life for the privilege of removing your creatures.

engines.title: Rest in Peace Ã—1
engines.body: {1}{W} Enchantment: All GYs are exiled as they fill. Board in vs Orzhov Greasefang when their Parhelion II GY plan is a key threat. RIP permanently exiles everything â€” their GY never exists while it's in play. Warning: Also exiles YOUR GY â€” don't board it in if your own Extraction Specialist recursion plan matters.

engines.title: Skrelv, Defector Mite Ã—1
engines.body: {W} 1/1 Toxic 1. {W}: Target friendly non-Mite creature gains protection from colors of your choice until EOT and can't block. Board in vs UW Control (give your key creature protection from blue and white â€” immune to their Supreme Verdict and removal) and RDW (give protection from red â€” immune to all their burn). A mana-efficient protection piece.

engines.title: 4 Llanowar Elves + 4 Elvish Mystic
engines.body: Eight mana dorks is the minimum for consistent T2 three-drops. Cutting to 6 noticeably reduces your acceleration consistency, which is the entire reason to play this deck over a non-CoCo GW midrange build.

engines.title: 4 Thalia, Guardian of Thraben
engines.body: Your best card in 4 of 5 matchups. First strike makes her difficult to kill in combat. 4 copies is mandatory — you need her in your opening hand or on T2 consistently.

engines.title: 4 Collected Company
engines.body: The deck's entire late-game identity. CoCo is why you play 28 creatures instead of a more interactive build. Cutting even one reduces the frequency of your most powerful plays.

engines.title: Voice of Resurgence
engines.body: 4 in creature-heavy or control metas. Can go to 2-3 in combo-heavy metas where the token creation is less relevant. Voice's anti-counterspell property is best vs control and tempo decks.

engines.title: Commune with Spirits
engines.body: Pure card selection that finds either a creature or CoCo. Increase to 4 in metas where finding CoCo consistently is critical (control-heavy). Decrease to 2 in metas where raw threat density matters more (aggro-heavy).

engines.title: Lathiel, the Bounding Dawn
engines.body: Best when burn (RDW) or lifegain matters. Grows your board with +1/+1 counters whenever you gain life. Cut entirely in metas where lifegain isn't relevant. Add copies when facing heavy burn or aggressive strategies.

engines.title: Company Timing
engines.body: You cast Collected Company at their EOT when they're tapped. You never cast Company during your main phase unless you need the creatures immediately for a block. EOT Company: you untap with two new creatures ready to attack. Main phase Company: you deploy creatures but they're summoning-sick. EOT is almost always correct.

engines.title: Voice Trigger Sequencing
engines.body: You cast your spells on THEIR turn to trigger Voice of Resurgence. Voice ETB effect: when they cast spells on your turn, you create an Elemental. You invert this: you cast on their turn (instants/flash), they cast on their turn (their spells), and Voice triggers off their casts. You sequence instants during their turn to avoid giving them Voice triggers.

engines.title: Knight of Autumn Mode
engines.body: You identify which Knight of Autumn mode you need before Collected Company resolves. If you're below 10 life: take life. If their artifacts/enchantments are threatening: take destroy. In most other cases: take +1/+1 counters. You call your mode before flipping the top 6 cards — never improvise.

engines.title: Damping Sphere Lotus Lock
engines.body: Against Lotus Field: Damping Sphere makes their lands produce only colorless. Their Lotus Field's {B}{B}{B} becomes {C}{C}{C} — useless for their combo. You deploy Sphere on T2 before they can set up. You fetch it with Fauna Shaman or find it naturally. The Sphere lock is your primary win condition in this matchup.

engines.title: Collected Company Count
engines.body: You run 4 Collected Company and never cut it. Company at instant speed is your most efficient card — 4 mana for two creatures is above-rate. The only reason to cut Company is if your creature count drops below 25, making misses too frequent. You keep creature count at 25+ specifically to maximize Company hit rate.

engines.title: Shapers' Sanctuary Meta Call
engines.body: Shapers' Sanctuary ({G}: whenever a creature you control becomes the target of a spell/ability an opponent controls, draw a card) is your draw engine vs removal-heavy decks. You run 2 copies in metas with many targeted removal spells. You cut it in wipe-heavy metas where the draw trigger requires targeted removal to fire.

engines.title: Burrenton Forge-Tender vs Leyline of Combustion
engines.body: Burrenton Forge-Tender (sacrifice: prevent all damage from a red source this turn) stops Anger of the Gods and red sweepers. Leyline of Combustion (whenever a red spell targets you, it deals damage to its controller) punishes red burn spells. You run Forge-Tender against single-sweeper red decks. You run Leyline against burn-to-face red decks.

engines.title: Extraction Specialist Count
engines.body: Extraction Specialist (3/2: ETB returns creature MV ≤ 2 from GY to play — it can't attack or block until your next turn) generates recursion value. You run 3-4 copies in metas where your small creatures die often and recursion compounds advantage. You cut Specialist in wipe-heavy metas where your entire board dies simultaneously, making single-creature recursion insufficient.

engines.title: Noble Hierarch Ramp
engines.body: Noble Hierarch provides exalted and {G}, {W}, or {U} mana. You use Hierarch to reach Company on T3 instead of T4. A T3 Company is approximately one full turn ahead of schedule.

engines.title: 25 Creatures for 79% Hit Rate
engines.body: You run 25+ creatures to maintain Collected Company's hit rate. With 25 creatures in 60 cards: Company hits 2 creatures approximately 79% of the time. With 22 creatures: hit rate drops to ~65%. You count creatures when building and sideboarding.

engines.title: Instants on Their Turn
engines.body: You cast all your instants on their turn to trigger Voice of Resurgence properly. Voice triggers when they cast spells on your turn — but you want to CAST on their turn to deny them the trigger. You invert: your turn is attack-only, their turn is cast-spells.

engines.title: Recur Your Best MV ≤ 2
engines.body: Extraction Specialist returns a MV ≤ 2 creature from GY to play. You target your most valuable creature: Voice of Resurgence (ETB token + Elemental synergy), Scavenging Ooze (GY hate + grows), or another Specialist (double recursion). You pre-identify the target before Specialist enters.

engines.title: Almost Always Their End Step
engines.body: You cast Collected Company at their EOT in 90%+ of situations. The exceptions: you need the creatures to block on your turn (0.5%) or you need the ETBs immediately (Knight of Autumn's life gain to survive their burn). Outside those exceptions: always EOT.

engines.title: Cast Instants on Their Turn
engines.body: Voice of Resurgence triggers when opponents cast spells on your turn. To avoid triggering Voice for them: you cast your own spells on THEIR turn. Your instants and flash spells go on their turn. You only cast sorceries on your turn when Voice isn't relevant.

engines.title: 25+ Creatures Required
engines.body: You run 25+ creature cards to maintain Company's hit rate. With 24 creatures in a 60-card deck: Company hits 2 creatures ~79% of the time. Below 24: hit rate drops unacceptably. You count your creature count when building and sideboarding.

engines.title: Return Your Best MV ≤ 2 Threat
engines.body: Extraction Specialist returns a creature with MV ≤ 2 from your GY to play. You use it on your best value creature: Voice of Resurgence, Scavenging Ooze, or another Specialist. You pre-identify your recursion target before Specialist resolves.

engines.title: T2 vs Lotus Field
engines.body: Against Lotus Field: you deploy Damping Sphere on T2 before they set up. Sphere makes their lands produce colorless only — their Lotus Field generates {C}{C}{C} instead of colors. The combo is offline. You find Sphere via Fauna Shaman if you don't draw it naturally.

engines.title: CoCo Hit Rate Math
engines.body: With 28 creatures in 60 cards and 6 cards revealed: expected 2-creature hits ~85%, 1-creature hits ~13%, 0 hits ~2%. Practical note: never mulligan a hand just because you don't have CoCo — you hit often enough that having acceleration + threats is correct. At 26 creatures, hit rate drops slightly (~80% for 2). Keep creature count at 26+.

engines.title: Thalia's Tax Per Matchup
engines.body: UR Cutter: 6-8 spells per game × {1} = 6-8 free mana of tempo. Greasefang: 4-6 discard/Monument activations × {1} = 4-6 tempo. UW Control: 6-10 interaction spells × {1} = your clock advantage. Calculate this at game start — knowing Thalia generates 6+ free mana of tempo tells you how aggressive to be with your clock.

engines.title: SB Matches Expected Meta
engines.body: Heavy GY (Greasefang, Phoenix): max RIP + Leyline. Heavy combo (Lotus Field): Damping Sphere + Knight destroy mode. Heavy control: Shapers' Sanctuary + Declaration in Stone. Heavy aggro (RDW): Burrenton Forge-Tender + Skrelv. Confirm 15 matches the room before registration.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Steam Vents/Island = UR Cutter (board Portable Hole, Shapers'). Mountain only = RDW (board Forge-Tender, Skrelv). Godless Shrine = Greasefang (board RIP, Leyline). Hallowed Fountain = UW Control (board Shapers', Declaration). Watery Grave = Phoenix (board RIP). Forest = possible mirror or Lotus Field.

engines.title: Company Target Selection
engines.body: Practice evaluating which two creatures you want to hit with Collected Company. Know your top 6 and the probability of hitting your target. Knight of Autumn (4-of) vs Fauna Shaman (2-of) â€” know your hit probability.

engines.title: Voice Trigger Timing
engines.body: Practice identifying when to trigger Voice of Resurgence. Opponents must cast spells on YOUR turn for the trigger. Know your sequencing: if you need to cast a spell, cast it on their turn. If they need to cast, wait.

engines.title: Knight of Autumn Mode Selection
engines.body: Practice the Knight of Autumn mode decision. At low life: take life. Vs aggro: take counters. Vs Rest in Peace: take destroy. The wrong mode against a Rest in Peace means your GY strategy is offline.

engines.title: Extraction Specialist Chains
engines.body: Practice the Extraction Specialist recursion chain. Specialist enters â†’ returns a MV â‰¤ 2 creature from GY â†’ that creature ETBs and triggers its effect â†’ recurse again next turn. Know your recursion targets.

SIMICRHYTHM.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "Every card in this deck is either a threat or ramp. There is no interaction, no counters, no removal — just an unstoppable sequence of power cards." Simic Rhythm is the pure expression of the Nature's Rhythm ramp shell. Where Bant Rhythm adds white for Seam Rip and tempo tools, Simic doubles down on the power plan: Ouroboroid at four copies instead of two, Quantum Riddler at four copies instead of three, and top-end threats like Marang River Regent and Abhorrent Oculus that Bant doesn't have room for. The deck's identity is acceleration into unanswerable threats. Llan
SIMICRHYTHM.mulligan: Mulligan aggressively for the T1 accelerant.

engines.title: Raw Power + Consistency
engines.body: 4 Ouroboroid (vs 2). 4 Quantum Riddler (vs 3). Marang River Regent as a death-replacement engine. Abhorrent Oculus as an 8/8 Ward 2 that replaces itself. Better mana base (no tri-color). More consistent opening hands — every card either ramps or threatens.

engines.title: Tempo and Interaction
engines.body: Seam Rip (main deck counterspell). Bounce Off (tempo). Beza, the Bounding Spring (life gain). Meltstrider's Resolve (protection). You have zero main deck interaction. If they land a key permanent on turn 3, you cannot answer it — you can only race past it.

engines.title: Field Is Aggro-Heavy
engines.body: Against aggro, your large bodies (Ouroboroid 4/4, Abhorrent Oculus 8/8) wall everything. Without needing interaction, your streamlined plan operates at full speed. Marang River Regent replaces your creatures when they die, giving you inevitability vs removal-based aggro.

engines.title: You Expect Midrange Mirrors
engines.body: Simic out-threatens every other midrange deck. Ouroboroid × 4 means 8 bodies from one card type. Quantum Riddler × 4 generates card advantage faster. If you're expecting Dimir Midrange and Bant Rhythm mirrors, Simic's sheer power level wins those.

engines.title: Control Is Prevalent
engines.body: Against Jeskai Control, Seam Rip protecting your key threats is the difference between winning and losing. If sweepers are common, Bant's interaction buys the turns you need. Simic cannot interact with a Sunfall or Day of Judgment.

engines.title: The Primary Win Condition
engines.body: Ouroboroid creates two 4/4 Serpent tokens when it enters or cycles. At four copies you reliably see it by turn 4. Unlike Bant's two copies, you can chain multiple Ouroboroids — two in one turn from the ramp acceleration means 4 immediate 4/4s for 8 mana. The cycle mode (discard + draw) keeps the hand live when you draw multiples.

engines.title: Marang River Regent
engines.body: Whenever a non-token creature you control dies, Marang River Regent creates a 4/4 Dragon token with flying. This makes your entire threat base resistant to single removal — every Llanowar Elves that dies becomes a 4/4 flier. Against removal-heavy decks, Regent turns their entire removal suite into advantage for you.

engines.title: Abhorrent Oculus
engines.body: 8/8 for five mana. Ward 2 (must pay 2 or the targeting spell fails). When it enters, you mill 4 cards. The milled cards feed your graveyard. Most importantly: it's an 8/8 that survives most targeted removal (Ward 2 + 8 toughness). Against decks without exile effects, Oculus resolving is usually game over.

engines.title: Wistfulness
engines.body: The Simic elemental incarnation: one mode destroys an artifact or enchantment (Naturalize), the other filters draws (look at top 3, take 1, discard the rest). In Simic Rhythm, the filter mode smooths your curve — discard excess lands or redundant threats. Note: the discard feeds Marang River Regent's death trigger if you discard creatures.

engines.title: Establish the Engine
engines.body: T1: Llanowar Elves or Badgermole Cub. T2: Nature's Rhythm (with dork mana) — ramp a basic, make a spider. T3: Gene Pollinator (all subsequent tokens are doubled). This is the non-negotiable opening. Any hand deviating from this sequence needs to have a very good reason.

engines.title: Threats Into Empty Air
engines.body: T4: Ouroboroid for two 4/4s (+ Pollinator doubles spiders from Rhythm if Rhythm was T3 instead). Alternatively: Spider Manifestation EOT for 4 spiders with Pollinator, then Quantum Riddler. T5: Craterhoof with 6+ creatures for 30+ trample damage, or second Ouroboroid for 4 more 4/4s, or Abhorrent Oculus for the 8/8 follow-up.

engines.title: Speed Is Your Weapon
engines.body: Any hand with T1 dork + T2 Nature's Rhythm is a keep. You'll be two turns ahead on board development. On the play you should have Craterhoof lethal available on turn 5 consistently. Mulligan aggressively for the T1 accelerant.

engines.title: The Extra Card Covers
engines.body: On the draw you can keep slightly slower hands — the extra card offsets being a turn behind. A hand with Pollinator + Ouroboroid + 3 lands is keepable on the draw even without a T1 dork. You'll deploy everything one turn later and that's fine. Don't over-mulligan trying to find the perfect draw-7.

engines.title: Ramp Chain
engines.body: Llanowar Elves / Badgermole Cub → Nature's Rhythm → Hushwood Verge / Willowrush Verge untapped. The ramp puts you at 5-6 effective mana by turn 3, enabling Ouroboroid or Abhorrent Oculus ahead of curve. Without the dork, Rhythm is a T3 play and you're one turn behind.

engines.title: Token Flood
engines.body: Gene Pollinator doubles all token creation. Nature's Rhythm = 2 spiders. Spider Manifestation EOT = 4 spiders. Two Manifestations + Pollinator = 8 spiders in one turn cycle. Ouroboroid creates two 4/4s normally, but doesn't trigger Pollinator (Pollinator only triggers from non-token creature ETBs — Ouroboroid creates tokens directly, not via a non-token creature ETB).

engines.title: Card Advantage Loop
engines.body: Quantum Riddler surveil 2 on attack, draw if 2+ instants/sorceries in GY. Mockingbird copies the highest-power creature when it attacks. Marang River Regent makes 4/4s whenever your non-token creatures die. Wistfulness filters. By turn 5, each creature you deploy generates more resources, making attrition impossible.

engines.title: Ramp Into Power
engines.body: Get dork → Rhythm → Pollinator → Ouroboroid down in order. You're not trying to interact. You're not trying to be clever. You're putting the biggest threats on the table at the fastest possible speed and daring them to have an answer for each one sequentially.

engines.title: Grind with Regent
engines.body: When they have removal: use it. Every non-token creature they kill triggers Marang River Regent for a 4/4 Dragon. In matchups with 6+ removal spells (Dimir Midrange, Jeskai Control), you want them to spend every removal spell — each one generates a 4/4 flier. Play Regent early so death-triggers start immediately.

engines.title: Overwhelm with Hoof
engines.body: Save Craterhoof for when you have 6+ creatures. Count power: 6 creatures × (power+6) + trample = usually 40+ damage in one attack. Don't cast Hoof until the math is lethal — it's a sorcery and they untap after a non-lethal Hoof. With Regent generating fliers and Ouroboroid making 4/4s, reaching lethal Hoof math is fast.

engines.title: Surrak, Elusive Hunter ×2
engines.body: Gives hexproof to target creature you control until EOT. Protects Marang River Regent, Gene Pollinator, or Quantum Riddler from targeted removal at instant speed. In vs any removal-heavy deck. The most flexible protection piece in the 15.

engines.title: Keen-Eyed Curator ×2
engines.body: Tutors for your top-end threats. Against control where you need Ouroboroid or Craterhoof to close, Curator digs and finds it. Also boards in vs mirrors where knowing your win condition is in hand matters.

engines.title: Soul-Guide Lantern ×2
engines.body: GY hate. In vs Izzet Lessons (Monument to Endurance), Dimir Excruciator, and any GY strategy. Cheap enough to cast alongside your threats without disrupting your curve.

engines.title: Meltstrider's Resolve ×2
engines.body: Protects a permanent from being destroyed until EOT. In vs aggro that kills your Pollinator or vs spot removal decks. Note: doesn't stop exile effects (Get Lost, Torch the Tower). Cheapest protection available.

engines.title: Archdruid's Charm Ã—2
engines.body: {G}{G}{G} Instant. Choose one: Search for a basic land; Destroy target artifact or enchantment; Put target creature card from a GY onto the battlefield under your control. Board in vs Bant Rhythm (destroy their Earthbender Ascension or Beza enchantment) and Dimir Excruciator (destroy their Torpor Orb). The reanimate mode is your Plan C â€” use it to steal their key creature from their GY.

engines.title: Unable to Scream Ã—1
engines.body: {B} Instant: Target creature can't activate abilities until EOT; it can't block this turn; tap it. Board in vs Mono-Green Landfall (tap their Icetill Explorer before their attack, preventing its search ability) and Dimir Excruciator (tap their Floodpits Drowner before it can bounce your key creature). A one-mana instant that both taps and shuts off abilities.

engines.title: Disdainful Stroke Ã—2
engines.body: {1}{U} Instant: Counter target spell with MV â‰¥ 4. Board in vs Jeskai Control (counters their expensive board wipes and walkers) and Izzet Lessons (counters their Sunderflock or expensive payoffs MV 4+). Hard counter for high-cost spells that your combat damage plan can't race through. Particularly effective in turns 4-6.

engines.title: Soul-Guide Lantern Ã—1
engines.body: {1} Artifact: Exile target GY at instant speed. Draw when it goes to your GY. Board in vs Izzet Lessons when they run GY-based lesson recursion. The cantrip clause makes it never truly dead â€” always crack it for value in non-GY matchups.

engines.title: 8 Dorks + 4 Rhythm
engines.body: 4 Llanowar Elves + 4 Badgermole Cub. Full playset of both. The T2 Nature's Rhythm requirement is too important to compromise. Dropping below 8 accelerants makes the deck function like a normal midrange deck at 3-mana-on-turn-3 pace — you lose the speed advantage entirely.

engines.title: 4 Ouroboroid
engines.body: This is the key distinction from Bant Rhythm. Four copies means you see it consistently by T4 and can chain multiples. If you cut Ouroboroid to 2 you're playing Bant Rhythm without white, which is just a worse Bant. The full set is the reason to play Simic.

engines.title: Wistfulness
engines.body: Excellent in control matchups (Naturalize mode on Monument) and for card filtering. In aggro-heavy metas, cut to 0 — you don't need GY hate or filtering, you need speed. In control-heavy metas, run the full 2. In mixed metas, 1 is the compromise.

engines.title: Spider Manifestation
engines.body: Four copies is the norm for its role as a flash board-builder. Some builds trim to 2 in the maindeck and rely more heavily on Ouroboroid tokens. Cutting Manifestation makes you more vulnerable to aggro (no instant-speed reach blockers) but more powerful in midrange/control matchups.

engines.title: Mockingbird
engines.body: Copies the highest-power creature on attack — typically Abhorrent Oculus (8/8) or Quantum Riddler. At 3 copies, you see it mid-game. Some builds run 2, preferring a second Marang River Regent or an additional Abhorrent Oculus. The sweet spot depends on how much you need the card advantage engine in your expected matchups.

engines.title: Archdruid's Charm
engines.body: Flexible green modal spell seen in Turin Top64 Bant builds. Can ramp (search land), remove artifacts/enchantments, or put a creature into play directly. Worth testing 1-2 copies main in control-heavy metas where the removal mode (killing their sweeper-enabling enchantments) justifies the inclusion.

engines.title: Craterhoof Math
engines.body: 6 creatures: each gets +6/+6 trample. 8 creatures: +8/+8. A standard board of 4 Serpents (4/4) + Pollinator (3/3) + Elves (1/1) = 6 creatures → each becomes 10/10+ with trample. Count it out before every potential Hoof turn. Never cast it without lethal math confirmed.

engines.title: Pollinator Trigger Conditions
engines.body: Pollinator triggers when a non-token creature you control creates tokens. In Simic Rhythm, Nature's Rhythm and Spider Manifestation are spells not creatures — they do NOT trigger Pollinator. Only actual creature ETBs that create tokens trigger it. Know this before game 1.

engines.title: SB Configuration
engines.body: Check expected field. Izzet Lessons above 10%: Soul-Guide Lantern mandatory. Jeskai Control above 5%: Keen-Eyed Curator and Vivien Reid in. Mono-Green above 10%: Unable to Scream, Get Lost, Reclamation Sage for the combo. Confirm your 15 matches the room.

engines.title: T1 Land Identification
engines.body: Breeding Pool or Spirebluff Canal = Izzet variant (Prowess/Lessons/Spellementals) — go fast, spiders at EOT T3. Fabled Passage or Forest = Mono-Green — board in Unable to Scream for game 2. Island or Watery Grave = Dimir — play Regent early, let them spend removal.

engines.title: Badgermole Cub Counter Tracking
engines.body: Practice tracking Badgermole Cub's counters. Each creature that attacks generates one counter per Cub. With 3 creatures attacking: Cub gets 3 counters per combat. Know the math at each board state.

engines.title: Earthbender Ascension Trigger
engines.body: Practice the Ascension trigger sequence. Play first land: nothing. Play second land: Ascension triggers. Each subsequent land: another trigger. Know the land count before deploying Ascension.

engines.title: Mossborn Hydra Timing
engines.body: Practice deploying Mossborn Hydra at exactly 7 lands. At 6 lands: Hydra is counterable. At 7: uncounterable. Count your lands throughout the game and know when the uncounterable window opens.

engines.title: Spider Manifestation Defense
engines.body: Practice flashing Spider Manifestation at their attack step. A 1/4 reach blocker at instant speed stops their fliers and provides ground defense simultaneously.

engines.title: Consult the Star Charts

engines.title: Removal Suite (Sear / Soul Immolation)

engines.title: 30 Lands Is Correct
engines.body: High land count is mandatory — Lumra's P/T = lands in play. More lands = bigger Lumra. 30 lands in a 60-card deck means 50% of your deck is lands. The deck wants to find land every turn. Never cut below 28, optimal is 30-31 depending on the number of cycling/fetch lands.

engines.title: Sazh's Chocobo as Backup Threat

engines.title: Obliterating Bolt Count

engines.title: Canyon Crab as Meta Call
engines.body: Canyon Crab (0/4 flash: tap a creature on ETB) is your defensive piece. You run 2-3 Crabs in metas with many aggressive threats. engines.title: Overwhelm Through Lands
engines.body: Your win condition is a board state so large that no individual answer matters. 12 lands in play means Worldsoul's Rage deals 12 face damage. Lumra as a 12/12 means combat is impossible. You win by making the game reach a point where the size of your board is unjawnable.

engines.title: Turn 7 Board State

engines.title: Spelunking Active Early

engines.title: Finding Your Missing Piece

engines.title: When Combo is Disrupted

engines.title: Exile over Destroy
engines.body: Obliterating Bolt exiles the creature instead of destroying it when it would die. This is critical against decks with GY recursion. You use Bolt over other removal when your target has GY recursion potential — the exile clause prevents any comeback.

engines.title: Lumra on the Battlefield
