Cast Opt on their end step after already casting a spell earlier and you get a free Monk that untaps ready t

engines.title: Treasure Cruise — Draw 3 for {U}
engines.body: Each cantrip you cast or mill via Consider fills your GY. By turn 4–5, Treasure Cruise costs {U} and draws three cards. This is Pioneer's best card advantage spell in this shell. Critical rule: Delve exiles cards from YOUR GY to pay for generic mana costs. Each exiled card = {1} paid. With 7 cards in GY, Treasure Cruise costs {U}. Counts from the GY only — no GY, no discount. Don't over-Delve earl

engines.title: Opt + Consider + Sleight of Hand
engines.body: 12 cantrips is not an accident. Every cantrip is: (1) a Cutter trigger if it's your second spell, (2) a prowess pump on Vivi/Stormchaser, (3) Delve fuel for Treasure Cruise, (4) card selection to find your kill. Opt and Consider are instant-speed — they trigger Cutter on your opponent's turn. Sleight of Hand is sorcery — cast it on your main phase before combat. Always count your cantrips: two = C

engines.title: Vivi Ornitier + Stormchaser's Talent
engines.body: Vivi Ornitier (FINAL FANTASY): when it enters or whenever you draw your second card each turn, it gets +1/+1 permanently. Combined with Treasure Cruise (drawing 3 = triggering Vivi twice), a freshly cast Vivi can be a 3/3 or larger immediately. Stormchaser's Talent: creates a 1/1 Otter with prowess for {U}, then grows it whenever you draw your second card each turn (+1/+1 permanently). Both scale

engines.title: T1–T3 Kill Setup
engines.body: T1: Stormchaser's Talent ({U}) — Otter token in play. T2: Cori-Steel Cutter ({1}{R}) + Opt ({U}) — Cutter Flurry triggers, second Monk created, Cutter attaches to it. Two creatures attacking for 2+2 before pumps. T3: Sleight of Hand + Consider + Fiery Impulse — each spell pumps all creatures +1/+1 via prowess. Three spells = four triggers total (three prowess on each creature). Board presents 12+

engines.title: Pure Prowess Beats
engines.body: Even without Cutter, Vivi Ornitier and Stormchaser's Talent are strong standalone threats. Vivi grows permanently every time you draw your second card per turn — a Treasure Cruise immediately makes Vivi a 3/3. Chain cantrips freely. Stormchaser's Otter also grows permanently. The creatures are not just Cutter payoffs — they win independently if Cutter is removed or countered.

engines.title: Need Threat + Cutter + Cantrips
engines.body: Keep: any hand with a T1–T2 threat (Stormchaser/Vivi), Cori-Steel Cutter, and 2+ cantrips, on 2 lands. Mulligan: all lands and no spells, all spells and no lands, no Cutter and no way to find it quickly. At 6: keep threat + Cutter + 1 cantrip on 2 lands. At 5: need Cutter + 2 spells + 2 lands — anything less is too slow.

engines.title: Cruise Into the Win
engines.body: When your hand empties after the initial burst, check GY count. 7 cards = Treasure Cruise for {U}. Draw three, reload, attack again. The second wave of spells pumps your existing board AND creates more Monks via Cutter. This is why the deck beats fair midrange: they answer your initial threats and then die to the reload. Keep 2 lands up post-combat for Cruise + one more spell.

engines.title: Cutter Token Factory
engines.body: Every spell past the first each turn = new 1/1 Monk with prowess + Cutter attached. A turn with four spells creates three Monks (second, third, fourth spell each trigger). Each Monk pumps +1/+1 for every additional spell cast that turn. With three existing Monks and three spells: 9 prowess triggers across the board. The math compounds fast.

engines.title: Delve Loop
engines.body: 12 cantrips fill your GY every game. Consider mills one additional card on resolution. By T3–T4 you routinely have 5–8 cards in GY. Treasure Cruise for {U}–{2}{U} draws three new spells. Those three spells create more Monks, fill the GY further, and enable the next Cruise. You can cast two Cruises in a game and win from an empty hand.

engines.title: Vivi + Stormchaser Scaling
engines.body: Vivi Ornitier grows permanently when you draw your second card per turn. A Treasure Cruise drawing three cards triggers Vivi twice in one spell (you draw cards 1, 2, 3 — second draw triggers, done). A single Cruise can put +2/+2 on Vivi permanently. After 2–3 Cruises, Vivi is a 5/5 or larger. Stormchaser's Otter scales the same way. These aren't 1/1 jokes late in the game.

engines.title: Race — All In
engines.body: Against Greasefang, Lotus Field, Niv: you are faster. Go all in on the clock. Don't hold up Spell Pierce preemptively — cast it as another spell for Cutter triggers and save counters only if their combo is resolving. Goldfishing at maximum speed is correct. A turn-3 kill doesn't care about Parhelion II.

engines.title: Race With Disruption
engines.body: Against Rakdos Midrange: apply pressure while holding Into the Flood Maw for their key threat. Don't let Thoughtseize strip Cutter — lead with a creature threat if you have both. After the first wave is answered, Treasure Cruise reloads. Their removal is 1-for-1 and you have twelve cantrips — eventually you run them out of answers.

engines.title: Slickshot Plan B
engines.body: Against UW Control: they sweep your Monks. Board in Slickshot Show-Off. Plot it early, resolve it after their sweeper, attack for lethal with the Plot attack triggers. Into the Flood Maw bounces their Teferi before they can -3. Force them to have every answer — you have more threats than they have answers in post-board games.

engines.title: Slickshot Show-Off ×3
engines.body: Plot Slickshot for its plot cost, exile it face down. After their sweeper resolves (or at any convenient moment), pay {1}{R} to deploy it without casting from hand. It attacks and gets +2/+0 for each instant/sorcery you cast this turn. Board in against: UW Control, Esper, any deck with Anger of the Gods or Extinction Event. The sweeper-proof threat that wins the attrition game.

engines.title: Unlicensed Hearse ×2
engines.body: Artifact that exiles X cards from any GY (X = number of creature types among exiled cards). Against Greasefang: activate immediately to exile vehicles and Greasefang from their GY. Prevents any reanimation. Against Phoenix: exiles Arclight Phoenix from GY so it can't recur. Hearse itself becomes a creature equal to the number of exiled cards. A 5/5 Hearse is also a win condition.

engines.title: Spell Pierce ×2 + Annul ×2
engines.body: Spell Pierce counters noncreature spells unless they pay {2} — counters Collected Company, Greasefang's setup, control sweepers on T2–T3. Annul counters artifacts and enchantments — hits Cori-Steel Cutter in the mirror, Stormchaser's Talent, Wilderness Reclamation, and key artifacts. Stack both vs combo decks where their key pieces are artifacts or enchantments.

engines.title: Abrade ×2 + Color Hate ×2
engines.body: Abrade: 3 damage to any creature OR destroy target artifact. Instant speed. Hits Collected Company targets and artifacts. Aether Gust: counter or put on top of library any red or green spell or permanent — counters RDW threats, GW creatures, Collected Company targets. Chandra's Defeat: exile a red permanent for {R} — efficient answer to mirror Vivi Ornitier or red threats.

engines.title: Aether Gust Ã—2
engines.body: {1}{U} Instant: Put target red or green spell/permanent on top of owner's library. Board in vs Selesnya Company (puts their Collected Company or key green creature back on top â€” delays their draw) and RDW (puts Monastery Swiftspear or their key red threat back to the top). "On top of library" means they keep the card but lose a draw step. Cast on their attack step for maximum disruption.

engines.title: Annul Ã—2
engines.body: {U} Instant: Counter target artifact or enchantment spell. Board in vs UW Control (counters their Rest in Peace or Temporary Lockdown before it enters) and Selesnya Company (counters their Collected Company if it's classified as... wait Collected Company is neither, but counters their key artifacts like Smuggler's Copter). Pure hard counter at one mana.

engines.title: Chandra's Defeat Ã—1
engines.body: {R} Instant: Exile target red permanent or red spell. Board in vs RDW (exiles Monastery Swiftspear or Goblin Guide from the battlefield â€” exile means no triggers or GY recursion) and Orzhov Greasefang if Greasefang is red. One mana exile at instant speed is the most efficient possible answer to red permanents. Always use Defeat proactively.

engines.title: Unlicensed Hearse Ã—1
engines.body: {2} Artifact: {T}: Exile two target cards from any GY. Can be crewed as a 4/4. Board in vs Orzhov Greasefang (exile Parhelion II from GY before Greasefang can crew it â€” their combo is offline without Parhelion). Each activation permanently removes their key combo piece. Crew it as a 4/4 when GY hate isn't needed to maintain board pressure.

engines.title: 4 Cori-Steel Cutter
engines.body: The entire engine. Four copies ensures you find it by T2 consistently. Running fewer makes the deck dramatically worse — you become just a mediocre Prowess deck rather than the format's dominant aggro-combo strategy.

engines.title: 12 Cantrips (4+4+4)
engines.body: Opt + Consider + Sleight of Hand. The Delve fuel, the Cutter triggers, the card selection. Any cantrip cut reduces the consistency of Treasure Cruise AND the Cutter token engine simultaneously. 12 is the right number.

engines.title: 4 Treasure Cruise
engines.body: The refuel that makes the deck unbeatable in attrition. Four copies ensures you draw it after the first burst. Running fewer means opponents stabilize and you can't reload. The best card advantage spell in this shell by a massive margin.

engines.title: Into the Flood Maw
engines.body: 2 main is standard. In aggro-heavy metas, cut entirely — it's slow for creature racing. In midrange/control metas, run 3–4. The loot + bounce is excellent tempo vs Rakdos and control. Also fills GY for Delve.

engines.title: Slickshot Show-Off (SB)
engines.body: 3 copies is correct for any meta with UW Control or significant sweeper strategies. If your meta is creature-heavy (RDW, Selesnya), trim to 1–2 and add more removal. Slickshot is your Plan B, not your Plan A.

engines.title: Any Non-Hate Meta
engines.body: UR Cutter is correct whenever the meta isn't specifically targeting it with sweepers and counterspells. If UW Control is dominant (above 15% meta), consider switching to a more resilient strategy. Otherwise, register Cutter — 23% meta share doesn't happen by accident.

engines.title: Cutter Crew Commitment
engines.body: You crew Cori-Steel Cutter only when you have a plan. Either: (1) you have pump spells to protect the attacker, or (2) Cutter's attack is lethal this turn. You never crew Cutter into unknown information — you check their mana and calculate whether they can block or remove your crewing creature before committing.

engines.title: Slickshot Plot Timing
engines.body: You plot Slickshot Show-Off at their EOT, not during your main phase. Plotting at their EOT: you plot for {1}{R}, exile Slickshot face-down, then your next turn chain cantrips (each gives +2/+0) before deploying Slickshot from exile. You time the plot to align with your highest-spell-density turn.

engines.title: Free Spell Identification
engines.body: You know your free spells by memory: Mutagenic Growth (pay 2 life, no mana), Force of Negation (exile blue card), Mishra's Bauble (0-mana artifact). Before combat, you count your free spells and add their prowess triggers. Free spells chain into each other — each one makes your Cutter crew deal more damage.

engines.title: Arcanist Attack Sequence
engines.body: You attack with Dreadhorde Arcanist and immediately know which GY spell you're casting for free. You build your GY specifically for this trigger — T1 Opt goes to GY, T2 DRC enters, T3 DRC attacks and casts Opt from GY for free. You never attack DRC without knowing the GY spell you're casting.

engines.title: Annul vs Spell Pierce Balance
engines.body: Annul ({U}: counter artifact or enchantment spell) is narrow but powerful against permanent-based threats. Spell Pierce ({U}: counter noncreature spell unless they pay {2}) is broader but falls off late. You run 2 Annul / 2 Pierce in balanced metas. In enchantment-heavy metas: 3 Annul. In counter-war metas: 3 Pierce.

engines.title: Slickshot Show-Off Copies
engines.body: Slickshot Show-Off (plot, then attack as a huge evasion creature) is your primary sweeper-proof threat. You run 3-4 copies in your SB specifically for control matchups. You cut Slickshot copies in aggro-heavy metas where you need more interactive pieces and the sweeper-proof threat is less relevant.

engines.title: Chandra's Defeat Quantity
engines.body: Chandra's Defeat ({R}: exile target red permanent or red spell) is your efficient answer to red threats. In RDW-heavy metas: 3-4 copies. In non-red metas: 0 copies. You never run Chandra's Defeat when less than 20% of your expected field is red — the card is too narrow to dilute your SB otherwise.

engines.title: Know Your Plan Before Crewing
engines.body: You crew Cori-Steel Cutter only with a complete plan: pump spell in hand for protection OR the attack is definitively lethal. You check their available interaction before committing your crewing creature. You never crew into unknown counterspell mana.

engines.title: Plot at Their EOT Only
engines.body: You plot Slickshot Show-Off at their EOT, paying {1}{R}. Your next turn: chain cantrips (each gives +2/+0 from Slickshot's ability) before deploying Slickshot from exile. You plot exactly one turn before you intend to attack with Slickshot.

engines.title: Count Zero-Mana Spells Before Combat
engines.body: Before your attack step: count your free spells (Mutagenic Growth, Force of Negation, Mishra's Bauble). Each free spell triggers prowess on each creature and gives Slickshot +2/+0 when it attacks. Your free spell count determines how large Slickshot gets.

engines.title: Keep Cheap Spells in GY
engines.body: Dreadhorde Arcanist attacks and casts a GY spell with MV ≤ Arcanist's power for free. You keep MV ≤ 1 spells in GY (Opt, Lightning Bolt) and spend expensive spells from hand. You never exile a GY spell when Arcanist is in play or in hand.

engines.title: Put on Top of Library Not Hand
engines.body: Aether Gust puts target red/green spell on top of their library — not back to their hand. This costs them their next draw step (they draw back the same card). You cast Gust at their end step when they've tapped for their key red/green threat, putting it back on top before they get a natural draw.

engines.title: Cutter Triggers Every Turn
engines.body: Before each turn cycle ask: how many spells have I cast? If zero, next spell is free — second spell triggers Cutter. If one, next spell triggers Cutter. Practice tracking this across both turns automatically — you should never miss a trigger.

engines.title: GY Count → Cruise Cost
engines.body: Count your GY at the start of your main phase every turn. 7 = Cruise for {U}. 5 = Cruise for {2}{U}. 3 = Cruise for {4}{U}. Know the threshold and play toward it. Don't Cruise at {4}{U} when passing and Opting on their end step gets you to {2}{U}.

engines.title: SB vs Expected Field
engines.body: Heavy GY decks (Greasefang, Phoenix): max 2 Hearse. Heavy control (UW): max 3 Slickshot + 2 Pierce. Heavy red: Chandra's Defeat + Torch. Mirror: Annul + Abrade for their equipment. Confirm your 15 matches the room.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Godless Shrine = Greasefang (race, board Hearse G2). Steam Vents + Island = UR Cutter mirror or Phoenix (board Annul). Hallowed Fountain = UW Control (board Slickshot G2 immediately). Forest = Selesnya Company (board Annul + Gust). Mountain only = RDW (board Torch + Defeat).

engines.title: Cutter Crew Timing
engines.body: Practice identifying when to crew Cutter. Crew only when you can protect the attacker OR when Cutter attacking is worth the risk. Know which creatures have 2+ power for crewing.

engines.title: Slickshot Plot Sequence
engines.body: Practice the Slickshot attack line. Plot EOT â†’ T+1: cast cantrip (+2/+0), cantrip (+2/+0), Slickshot attacks as 7/4 evasion. Know the exact spell count needed for lethal.

engines.title: Free Spell Chain
engines.body: Practice identifying your free spells and chaining them. Mutagenic Growth (free), Force of Negation (free), Mishra's Bauble (free ETB draw). Know exactly which spells are free and when to chain them.

engines.title: Arcanist GY Management
engines.body: Practice building the correct GY for Arcanist attacks. Keep MV â‰¤ 1 spells in GY (Opt, Lightning Bolt). Don't exile them with fetchlands or Mishra's Bauble. Know your GY targets before each combat.

UWBlink.game_plan: Chapter 01 Identity & Philosophy "Don't just play more cards — play more turns." — Core Mantra UW Blink is a tempo-control hybrid that weaponizes time. It is not all-in combo, and it is not pure control. It plays like disruptive midrange — stall, interact, then snowball with repeatable ETB value until inevitability takes over. The deck's strength lies not in any one card, but in the synergy between cheap interaction and recursive ETBs . Every Ephemerate rebound, every Phelia trigger, every Starfield Shepherd warp opens multiple lines of play. Core Axes Axis 01 Tempo Denial Phelia time-walks by
UWBlink.strengths: High skill ceiling — reps compound. Resilient to hate — pivots into fair midrange. Powerful bullets that are tutorable. Inevitability in every long game.
UWBlink.weaknesses: Decision density punishes mistakes. Very fast aggro (Burn, Prowess) on stumbles. Torpor Orb / Void Mirror require full pivots. Tournament clock — brisk play is required.
UWBlink.mulligan:
Mulligan Rules

The single most important skill in this deck.

engines.title: Tempo Denial
engines.body: Phelia time-walks by blinking threats. Phantom destroys nonbasics. Consign buys entire turns. You are always reaching into the opponent's next turn and stealing it.

engines.title: Flexible Interaction
engines.body: Solitude, Prismatic Ending, and Wrath of the Skies answer almost everything in the format. The deck is never locked into a single answer type.

engines.title: Resilient Engines
engines.body: Guide + Ocelot generates inevitability. Riddler and Shepherd refill your hand. Once engines are live, the deck is very hard to exhaust.

engines.title: Role Flexibility
engines.body: Acts as control vs Aggro, tempo vs Combo, and proactive pressure vs Control. No other archetype in the format shifts roles this cleanly.

engines.title: What You Do Well
engines.body: High skill ceiling — reps compound. Resilient to hate — pivots into fair midrange. Powerful bullets that are tutorable. Inevitability in every long game.

engines.title: What Beats You
engines.body: Decision density punishes mistakes. Very fast aggro (Burn, Prowess) on stumbles. Torpor Orb / Void Mirror require full pivots. Tournament clock — brisk play is required.

engines.title: Ephemerate
engines.body: The heartbeat of the deck. At floor: reuse an ETB. At ceiling: counterspell, Time Walk, 4-for-1. Never fire for small gains when a big moment is coming.

engines.title: Phelia, Ex. Shepherd
engines.body: A Time Walk stapled to a blink engine. Use on opponents' permanents first — blink Atraxa, blink Titan, blink walkers. Offensive value comes only once you're ahead.

engines.title: Solitude
engines.body: Free removal + lifegain + lifelink clock. Save it for their payoff — never pitch early to a setup creature. With Ephemerate it becomes 2–3 removals + 6–9 life.

engines.title: White Orchid Phantom
engines.body: Mana denial disguised as a 2/2 flier. On the play + Ephemerate = triple Stone Rain by T3. Strongest vs greedy mana bases (Tron, Titan, Domain).

engines.title: Ocelot Pride
engines.body: Lifegain factory + token engine. Once Ascend is online, every end step generates exponential board presence. Cannot lose a board stall once this is live.

engines.title: Quantum Riddler
engines.body: Deploy when nearly hellbent — every draw becomes +1. A 4/6 flyer that closes in 5 turns and buries Control once it sticks. Sandbag cheap spells to maximize it.

engines.title: Snap Keep
engines.body: 2 lands + Ephemerate + Solitude or Phelia or Phantom. Any opener with Sanctifier or Mistcaller vs known combo. Guide + Ocelot + any interaction.

engines.title: Snap Mull
engines.body: 0–1 landers, 5+ lands. Hands with only Shepherd/Riddler/Mockingbird and no interaction. Any hand that doesn't clock by T4 and doesn't disrupt by T3.

engines.title: Watch For
engines.body: Mockingbird in opener without another 2-drop. RIP in opener vs unknown G1. Value-only 7s vs combo (Reanimator, Belcher, Neoform).

engines.title: T2 Solitude on Their Threat
engines.body: On the play, T2 evoke Solitude to exile their key threat or T3 Restoration Angel sets up the blink loop. On the play you dictate tempo — evoke Solitude + Ephemerate on T2 converts your 2-card investment into a 5/5 body and 2 exile effects before they’ve developed. This tempo advantage compounds with Teferi’s sorcery lock on T3.

engines.title: Hold Ephemerate Open
engines.body: On the draw, your extra card gives you more Ephemerate / Solitude coverage. Hold Ephemerate mana open on their T2 and T3 to respond to their threats in real time. Against aggro on the draw: Solitude T1 evoke (pay white card) to stop their T1 deployment is the highest-priority play.

engines.title: Reactive Ephemerate Mode
engines.body: Teferi removed: opponents interact at instant speed again. Switch to reactive: hold Ephemerate + Solitude mana open every turn. Deploy threats during their end step or in response to their attacks. Without Teferi’s lock, you play draw-go but your flash pieces still generate value without the sorcery-speed protection.

engines.title: Angel + Riddler Rebuild
engines.body: Solitude countered or removed: rebuild with Restoration Angel (blinks any non-Angel creature you control) and Quantum Riddler (draw on each blink). Chain Angel + creature ETBs to refill hand and rebuild board. Teferi’s +1 continues generating card draw. You can win entirely through Teferi + Angel value without ever resolving another Solitude.

engines.title: Evoke + Ephemerate ETB Loop
engines.body: Evoke Solitude (exile white card) + Ephemerate (in response to sacrifice trigger) = 2 exile ETBs + a permanent 5/5. Ephemerate rebounds: second blink next upkeep = another exile. This loop is the highest-value engine and should be executed every time you have Solitude + Ephemerate + a relevant target.

engines.title: Teferi + Sorcery Flash
engines.body: Teferi, Time Raveler locks opponents to sorcery speed while +1 draws cards. His +1 also enables sorcery-speed flash for Restoration Angel and other creatures (not directly useful since Angel is already instant-speed, but applies to other sorceries). Each Teferi +1 is +1 card and the sorcery-speed lock continues. Protect him once resolved.

engines.title: Quantum Riddler Blink Draw
engines.body: Quantum Riddler draws a card each time you blink a permanent. With Ephemerate + Restoration Angel chains, Riddler generates 2-4 cards per turn. This card advantage engine makes your late game inevitably better than any fair opponent. Deploy Riddler once Teferi is in play to protect the blink chain.

engines.title: T2 Double Exile
engines.body: T2: Evoke Solitude (exile a white card) → Solitude ETB exiles their threat. Evoke sacrifice trigger on stack → Ephemerate Solitude ({W}) → Solitude exiles, sacrifice trigger fizzles, Solitude returns at end of step as 5/5. Ephemerate rebound next upkeep → blink again for second exile ETB. Cost: 1 white card + {W}. Return: 2 exiles + permanent 5/5.

engines.title: T4 Value Acceleration
engines.body: T4: Restoration Angel (flash) → blinks Quantum Riddler → Riddler ETB draws a card. Flash Angel at instant speed during their EOT. Riddler drew a card. Next turn: Ephemerate Angel → blinks Riddler again → another card drawn. Chain generates 2-3 cards from 2 pieces.

engines.title: Teferi + Creatures Clock
engines.body: Teferi (3/4) + Solitude (5/5) + Restoration Angel (3/4) = 11 attack power. From 20 life: 2 attack steps while using Teferi +1 to bounce their blockers. With Teferi’s lock active, they can’t flash in blockers. The clock is fast enough that you don’t need a dedicated finisher — the value pieces are also the damage.

engines.title: Ephemerate Rebounds at Your Next Upkeep
engines.body: Ephemerate exiles the creature, which returns at the beginning of the next end step. On your turn: exile + return at YOUR end step, then rebound copy at YOUR NEXT upkeep = exile + return again at your next end step. Total: 2 ETB blinks from one Ephemerate. On opponent’s turn (cast during their attack): exile + return at THEIR end step, rebound at YOUR upkeep = exile + return at your end step. Same

engines.title: Evoke + Ephemerate: Keep the Creature
engines.body: Evoke Solitude: ETB trigger (exile target creature) and evoke sacrifice trigger both go on the stack. Ephemerate Solitude in response to the sacrifice trigger: Solitude exiles before being sacrificed. Sacrifice trigger resolves with no target. Solitude returns at end of step as a full 5/5. Ephemerate’s rebound blinks it again next upkeep — another exile ETB. Two free exile effects from Solitude +

engines.title: Restoration Angel Cannot Blink Angels
engines.body: Restoration Angel says target non-Angel creature you control. This restriction means: you cannot blink another Angel with it, and you cannot blink itself. In practice this rarely matters for UW Blink but know it so you don’t target an Angel creature incorrectly. All your value creatures (Eternal Witness, Wall of Omens, Recruiters) are non-Angel and are valid targets.

engines.title: Are they faster?
engines.body: If yes → you are Control. Stabilize first, then pivot. Every life point matters until you have an engine online.

engines.title: Are they more powerful long-term?
engines.body: If yes → you are Beatdown. Jam Ocelot/Phantom aggressively. Use Ephemerate offensively to push damage.

engines.title: Neither?
engines.body: You are Tempo. Buy one critical turn with Consign, Phelia, or Phantom — then race with your modest clock before they rebuild.

engines.title: You're now the aggressor when:
engines.body: You've stabilized vs aggro at 10+ life. You've disrupted combo once and have 4 turns of clock available. They're hellbent and rebuilding slowly.

engines.title: Hold the line when:
engines.body: Life total is still in danger. They have payoffs in hand (Titan, Atraxa) you haven't answered. You don't have a clean clock established yet.

engines.title: Aggro-Disruption
engines.body: Aggressive hands (Guide + Ocelot) force defensive reanimates. Sanctifier priority. Pressure lets you play more proactively.

engines.title: Disruption First
engines.body: They can Atraxa as early as T3. Always prioritize Consign or Solitude over clock cards. Mulligan harder.

engines.title: The Draw Engine Count
engines.body: Most lists run 3. At 4: more consistent draw engine, but Riddler at Warp is slow against fast aggro and clogs blink lines. At 2: leaner, more room for interaction or Mockingbird, but you see it less in grind games. Run 4 if your meta is heavy on control or mirror. Cut to 2 if Prowess or Burn is above 15% of the room — their clock is faster than Riddler can generate value.

engines.title: The Mirror / Flex Creature
engines.body: The 1-copy is standard. Mockingbird at X copies any creature with MV ≤ X — at 2 mana it's your best mirror tool (copies their Phelia or Riddler for immediate ETB value). Cut to 0 against aggro-heavy metas where you need more interaction. Go to 2 in mirror-heavy tournament environments. Never go above 2 — dilutes your main engine density.

engines.title: The Main Deck Counter
engines.body: The current shell runs 1 main + 3 SB. The 1 main copy is primarily for triggered ability counters you need in G1 — Archon ETB in Glockulous, Pact upkeep trigger vs Titan. Cut the main copy if your expected field has no combo. Keep it if you expect Glockulous, Neoform, or Amulet Titan above 10% combined. The 3 SB copies are non-negotiable regardless.

engines.title: The Speed Caverns
engines.body: Currently 1 SB copy. Caverns enters with a luck counter if it's in your opening hand (exile any other card) — you gain a free mana on turn 1 on the draw. Board in vs any combo matchup where being "on the play" for the first spell matters — Neoform, Glockulous, Storm. Consider main decking if your local meta is more than 30% combo. Never go above 1.

engines.title: Flex Hate Bear Slot
engines.body: Currently 1 main. Sanctifier has protection from black and red (can't be targeted/blocked/damaged by either). In a meta with Boros Energy and Prowess it's a free threat that turns off their removal suite. Cut it to 0 main in control-heavy metas where it does nothing G1. Never cut the 2 SB copies — they're mandatory for aggro matchups.

engines.title: The Board Wipe Count
engines.body: Currently 2 SB. X-cost sweeper that hits creatures with power ≤ X. At X=3 it clears most boards without hitting your own Kappa or large Constructs (but does hit your Phelia/Guide). Consider going 1 SB if your matchup spread has little aggro. Go 3 SB if token-wide decks like Boros Energy or Jeskai Blink are prevalent — the extra copy improves your ability to find it in G2 without Shepherd.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: The meta is creature-based (Boros Energy, Prowess, Zoo) — your free removal and token generation outperform. Mirror matchup is high — your blink loops generate more value than anyone else. No heavy GY-hate meta that would blank your ETB loops.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy combo meta above 25% — your disruption is tempo-based, not lock-based. Mass land destruction strategies (your Phantom is symmetric — opponent can also use Flagstones lines against you). Teferi, Time Raveler is at 15%+ of the meta (locks your instant-speed blink loops).

engines.title: 20 vs Combo
engines.body: Reanimator, Belcher, Neoform. Drill mulligans and disruption sequencing. Practice keeping vs shipping with a timer running.

engines.title: 20 vs Aggro
engines.body: Energy, Prowess, Domain. Drill Solitude timing, Wrath sequencing, and the pivot to Ocelot Ascend kill after stabilization.

engines.title: 20 vs Control / Mirror
engines.body: Practice patience, Ephemerate timing, and Teferi sequencing. Learn the exact turn to commit threats after Verdict.

engines.title: Clock Practice
engines.body: Play games under a 20-minute timer. Track kill turns. Aim for 4–6 postboard. If you're going to time, the problem is usually sequencing, not the deck.

UWCONTROL.game_plan: Chapter 01 DECK IDENTITY "You never tap out. Every turn ends with mana available. Every threat they present gets answered. When Teferi resolves, the game is functionally over." UW Control is Pioneer's premier permission-and-sweeper control deck. The plan is consistent regardless of the matchup: answer every early threat with removal, hold up counterspells every turn, sweep the board when they overcommit, and win by resolving Teferi, Hero of Dominaria and protecting it until the ultimate ends the game. No other deck in Pioneer can match the card advantage Teferi generates each turn. The interac
UWCONTROL.mulligan:
Mulligan
Need: Land + Interaction + Draw
Keep: 3-4 lands, at least 2 interaction pieces, at least 1 draw spell.

engines.title: Teferi Wins Every Long Game
engines.body: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria draws a card and untaps two lands every turn. In a control shell, this means you draw a card and still have two mana available for a counterspell. No fair deck in Pioneer can outgrind this engine. Once Teferi resolves and survives a turn, your hand size and mana advantage grow exponentially.

engines.title: Every Threat Has an Answer
engines.body: Temporary Lockdown for go-wide. Supreme Verdict for go-tall. March of Otherworldly Light for individual threats. No More Lies for spells on the stack. Dovin's Veto for must-counter spells. Farewell for GY-based strategies. Each layer addresses a different axis of attack — the deck has no unwinnable matchup.

engines.title: Wandering Emperor at Instant Speed
engines.body: The Wandering Emperor is a flash planeswalker — you can cast it at any time. This means you never need to tap out on your own turn. Deploy Wandering Emperor at end of their turn, untap, and continue holding up interaction. The Emperor creates tokens, exiles tapped attackers, and protects your life total without ever requiring you to spend your turn proactively.

engines.title: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria
engines.body: 5 mana. +1: draw a card, untap two lands. This means after playing Teferi you can +1 and still leave {U}{U} up for a counterspell. Every subsequent turn: draw a card AND maintain countermagic. -3: put a nonland permanent on top of its owner's library — answers anything that slipped through. Ultimate: each turn exile 3 target permanents. Games where Teferi untaps are almost unlosable.

engines.title: The Wandering Emperor
engines.body: 4 mana Flash. +1: creates a 2/2 vigilance Samurai token. +1 (alternate): put a +1/+1 counter and first strike on target creature. -2: exile target tapped creature, gain 2 life. Cast at instant speed at end of their turn. Never tap out for this — it functions exactly like passing the turn with a threat ready. Against aggro the exile mode stabilizes the board. Against control the token threatens let

engines.title: Temporary Lockdown vs Supreme Verdict
engines.body: Temporary Lockdown: 3 mana enchantment, exiles all nonland permanents with MV 2 or less until it leaves. Cheaper, hits non-creatures, and handles token boards. Use for wide aggro. Supreme Verdict: 4 mana sorcery, destroys all creatures, can't be countered. Use for larger creature threats or when you need an uncounterable effect. Know which to cast when — Lockdown is usually correct against most Pi

engines.title: Dovin's Veto vs No More Lies
engines.body: No More Lies ({1U}) is your soft counter — counters unless they pay {3}. Perfect for early game when mana is tight. Dovin's Veto ({WU}) is the hard counter — counters and can't be countered itself. Reserve Dovin's Veto for: Teferi-level threats, their sweepers vs your board, combo-critical spells (Greasefang ETB trigger). No More Lies is the free-roll counter; Dovin's Veto is the nuclear button.

engines.title: Survival Phase
engines.body: Your only goal in turns 1-3 is to not die. March of Otherworldly Light removes early threats at any mana cost. Consult the Star Charts draws cards and sculpts your hand. Temporary Lockdown on T3 sweeps MV-2 or less permanents. Never commit a threat — hold all your mana for answers. The opponent is trying to establish pressure; you're answering everything.

engines.title: Transition to Control
engines.body: T4: Supreme Verdict or Temporary Lockdown wipes whatever survived. Wandering Emperor at end of their T4 stabilizes. T5: Teferi with a counterspell backup in hand — this is your target state. Playing Teferi at 5 mana while holding No More Lies means: deploy Teferi, they try to answer it, you counter their answer. Teferi survives and your lead is permanent.

engines.title: Inevitability Phase
engines.body: Once Teferi is active: +1 every turn draws a card AND leaves 2 mana up. Each turn your hand grows, your options expand, and their resources deplete. Use Teferi -3 to send their threats back to their library one at a time. If they ever cast a creature, Wandering Emperor exiles it tapped. Memory Deluge at instant speed refuels if Teferi dies. The game ends when Teferi ultimates or they concede.

engines.title: Need: Land + Interaction + Draw
engines.body: Keep: 3-4 lands, at least 2 interaction pieces, at least 1 draw spell. Mulligan: fewer than 3 lands (you can't play on curve), 0 interaction pieces (you die to aggro), or hands with 2+ Teferi and no way to survive to T5. You can keep 2 lands if both are dual lands and you have Consult the Star Charts to find more. At 6: keep 3 lands + 2 interaction. At 5: 3 lands + 1 instant-speed removal + 1 coun

engines.title: Deploy Your Threat
engines.body: Your T4 play is Teferi, Hero of Dominaria. You plus Teferi, untap two lands, and immediately have mana open for interaction on their turn. Teferi generates card advantage (+1 draws a card) while keeping counterspells available. Your T5 is Absorb if they threaten to resolve something critical, or another Teferi activation for another draw. You win by generating more cards than they have answers.

engines.title: Seal the Game
engines.body: You win in the late game by having more interaction in hand than they have threats in theirs. Supreme Verdict refills your threat count from zero. Brimaz, King of Oreskos creates Cat tokens each time it attacks or blocks — your board goes wide faster than they can answer individual pieces. You close with Brimaz beats while holding Dovin's Veto for their board wipe attempt.

engines.title: Open Mana on Their Turn
engines.body: Your most important skill is managing your mana to hold interaction open on their turn. Leave exactly the mana you need for your most relevant counter: {W}{U} for Dovin's Veto, {1}{W}{U} for Absorb, {3}{W}{W} for Supreme Verdict. Never tap out unless you're winning immediately. Your power comes from untapped mana — never waste it.

engines.title: What Are You Answering?
engines.body: Before each of their turns, ask: what are the three most dangerous things they could cast? Know your answer for each. If they cast A, you counter. If they cast B, you march it. If they cast C, you Verdict. Having a pre-planned answer for their top 3 plays means you never hesitate when they tap mana.

engines.title: Spot + Sweeper Layering
engines.body: March of Otherworldly Light exiles at instant speed. Get Lost answers anything at sorcery speed for 2 mana. Temporary Lockdown blanks boards at 3 mana. Supreme Verdict wipes boards at 4 mana. Farewell is the reset button for GY and artifact-heavy strategies. Each answers a different threat width — never be caught with the wrong tool by understanding each card's specific role.

engines.title: Hard + Soft Countermagic
engines.body: No More Lies counters early (soft — {1U}, unless pay {3}). Dovin's Veto counters critical spells (hard — {WU}, can't be countered). Three Steps Ahead is flexible: copy, counter, or draw 2. Together they cover every threat type: early creatures, high-impact spells, and uncounterable threats (Dovin's Veto handles their Dovin's Veto; Supreme Verdict can't be countered back). Always know which counter

engines.title: Consult + Memory Deluge + Teferi
engines.body: Consult the Star Charts at 2 mana filters draws. Memory Deluge at 4 mana (or flashback for 5) draws 3-4 cards. Teferi draws a card AND untaps 2 lands every turn. The draw engine ensures you never run out of answers — every turn your hand replenishes while opponents' hands empty. At Teferi mana you're typically drawing more per turn than you're spending.

engines.title: Your Card Advantage Loop
engines.body: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria generates +1 card per activation while untapping two lands for free. Your loop: Teferi plus → draw a card → untap two lands → use those lands to hold Dovin's Veto open → their turn ends → repeat. You generate one card per turn cycle while maintaining interaction capability. You protect Teferi with Dovin's Veto on their answers to him.

engines.title: Your Uncounterable Shield
engines.body: Dovin's Veto ({W}{U}) is uncounterable. You use it to protect your key plays from their counters and to stop their key noncreature spells. You hold it specifically for Supreme Verdict (their board wipe), Indomitable Creativity (their combo), or their most impactful noncreature answer. You never use Veto on a creature spell — Absorb handles those for 3 life gain.

engines.title: Your Self-Generating Army
engines.body: Brimaz, King of Oreskos creates a 1/1 Cat with vigilance every time he attacks or blocks. You attack every turn with Brimaz and generate one Cat token per combat. After 3 attacks: Brimaz 3/4 (with vigilance, untaps after attack) + three 1/1 Cats. Your board multiplies without additional card investment. You protect Brimaz with Dovin's Veto on their board wipe.

engines.title: Your Alt Win Condition
engines.body: Approach of the Second Sun ({6}{W}): you cast it, pay 7 life, it goes to your library 7 from the top. Next turn you draw 7 cards down, find Approach, cast it again — you win instantly. Your Approach line: survive to T7 (hold interaction throughout), cast Approach with Veto backup, survive their response turn, draw and cast Approach again T8. You win on the spot when Approach resolves the second ti

engines.title: Your T4 Teferi Line
engines.body: You reach T4 with {1}{U}{U} open and Teferi in hand. You cast Teferi, Hero of Dominaria: draw a card, untap two lands. You immediately have {W}{U} or {1}{U} open for interaction on their turn. You never cast Teferi into open mana — you wait until they've spent their interaction or until you have Dovin's Veto backup.

engines.title: Your Supreme Verdict Line
engines.body: You hold Supreme Verdict until they have 3+ creatures. You never Verdict into 1-2 creatures. After Verdict resolves, you immediately deploy Brimaz, King of Oreskos — your board goes from 0 to 1 creature with a Cat token the turn he attacks. You follow Brimaz with Dovin's Veto backup for their sweeper response.

engines.title: Your Narset Line
engines.body: You deploy Narset, Parter of Veils when they are about to draw — their upkeep, or in response to their cantrip. Under Narset: their Opt draws 0 extra cards, their Collected Company hits but draws 0. You follow Narset with a clock (Brimaz) so they must spend removal on Narset instead of advancing their own plan.

engines.title: Your Dovin's Veto Line
engines.body: You save Dovin's Veto for their uncounterable board wipes (Supreme Verdict from opponents, Anger of the Gods) or their most critical noncreature spell. You never use Veto on a cantrip or a small creature spell — you reserve it for the one spell that wins them the game. Veto is uncounterable itself, so you hold it until it must go on the stack.

engines.title: Survive to T4 Wrath
engines.body: Against RDW, Selesnya Company: your goal is staying alive until Temporary Lockdown or Supreme Verdict clears the board. March of Otherworldly Light removes early threats. Beza (SB) gains life. Wandering Emperor exiles key attackers in combat. Your life total is a resource — don't spend it to stop irrelevant damage. A wrath on T4 followed by Teferi on T5 wins the game.

engines.title: Counter Their Key Piece
engines.body: Against Greasefang: counter or remove Greasefang itself on the stack (the ETB trigger is the kill). Rest in Peace (SB) answers the GY recursion. Against Lotus Field: Field of Ruin destroys Lotus before it doubles. Get Lost answers Thespian's Stage. High Noon (SB) stops them from untapping lands to generate explosive mana.

engines.title: Win the Permission War
engines.body: Against UR Cutter and Dimir Midrange: play around their interaction by baiting counters on expendable spells before deploying Teferi. Against the UW mirror: the first Teferi to resolve often wins — hold Dovin's Veto for their Teferi, deploy yours when they're tapped out. Wandering Emperor at instant speed functions as a threat that never exposes you to their interaction window.

engines.title: Brimaz + Caracal + Kaheera
engines.body: Brimaz, King of Oreskos is a 3/3 first strike for {1WW} that creates a 1/1 Cat Warrior token whenever it attacks or blocks. Regal Caracal is a 3/4 for {3WW} that creates two 1/1 Cat tokens with lifelink and gives all your Cats +1/+1 and lifelink. Kaheera, the Orphanguard as companion (no non-Cat creatures) gives all your non-Cat Companions +1/+1 and vigilance. Board this package in vs creature dec

engines.title: Beza, the Bounding Spring ×3
engines.body: Beza enters tapped and generates a Forest land plus gains life. As a 2/4 body it blocks efficiently. Primary value: lifegain stabilization vs RDW and aggressive strategies. You have 1 in the main and 2 more in the sideboard. Bring in all 3 vs burn-heavy matchups to stabilize your life total. The body is also a legitimate blocker in creature-heavy matchups.

engines.title: Rest in Peace ×2
engines.body: Exiles all GYs and prevents future GY use. Primary target: Greasefang (Parhelion II can't return), Arclight Phoenix (can't come back from GY), and any recursion strategy. Note: RIP also exiles your own GY, so Wandering Emperor's token creation and your own Memory Deluge flashback are unaffected (they don't use GY). Cast on T2 before they set up their discard outlet.

engines.title: High Noon ×3
engines.body: Enchantment: players can't untap more lands than they had at the start of their turn. Destroys Lotus Field combo — their entire plan involves untapping Lotus with Hidden Strings. Also relevant vs any land-untap effect. Comes with 1 in the main and 2 more in the sideboard. Board all 3 copies vs Lotus Field. The 3 total copies with the SB pair ensure you draw it in G2-3 with a sculpted hand.

engines.title: Regal Caracal Ã—2
engines.body: {3}{W}{W} 3/3 Lifelink. Other Cats you control get +1/+1 and have lifelink; create two 1/1 Cats with lifelink. Board in vs Selesnya Company (three lifelink bodies from one card completely stabilizes the life race) and RDW (3 lifelink tokens generate 3+ life per attack, racing their burn). A total of 5 lifelink power from one card in difficult racing matchups.

engines.title: Dovin's Veto Ã—3
engines.body: {W}{U} Instant: Counter target noncreature spell â€” THIS SPELL CAN'T BE COUNTERED. Board in vs Orzhov Greasefang (uncounterable counter on their Greasefang or their key spell), Lotus Field (counters their key combo spell, and they can't counter it back), UR Cutter (counters their key threat while they can't respond). The uncounterable clause makes this strictly better than Negate in a counter war

engines.title: Beza, the Bounding Spring Ã—1
engines.body: {4}{G}{W} 4/4. When Beza or another creature with a +1/+1 counter enters under your control, you gain 2 life and draw a card. Board in vs RDW when you need additional lifegain that also generates card advantage. A 4/4 body that generates 2 life and a card draw on entry is efficient. Can also serve as a must-answer threat that replaces itself if removed.

engines.title: Rest in Peace Ã—1
engines.body: {1}{W} Enchantment: All GYs are exiled as they fill. Board in vs Orzhov Greasefang (their Parhelion II GY plan is offline â€” no GY ever exists while RIP is in play) and Arclight Phoenix (exiles Phoenix before it triggers back). WARNING: Also exiles your own GY â€” don't board it in if your own Church of Dusk or similar GY-matters cards are part of your plan.

engines.title: 4 March of Otherworldly Light
engines.body: The most flexible removal spell in Pioneer — instant, any MV, exiles. Hits creatures, enchantments, artifacts, and planeswalkers. Never cut below 4. The exile clause is critical vs GY strategies.

engines.title: 4 No More Lies
engines.body: The best early counterspell available. Counters anything for {1U} when opponents are mana-constrained (turns 1-4). Never cut to fewer than 4 — your early permission suite depends on it.

engines.title: 2 Teferi, Hero of Dominaria
engines.body: Your primary win condition and draw engine. 2 copies ensures you draw it in most games without flooding. 3 copies is too many — Teferi is dead in hand before T5 and bad when you draw multiples.

engines.title: Dovin's Veto
engines.body: 2 main is correct for most metas. In heavy-blue or mirror-heavy metas, move to 3 main. In aggro-heavy metas, trim to 1 and move the rest to sideboard where they arrive with a plan.

engines.title: Temporary Lockdown
engines.body: 3 main in aggro-heavy metas. 2 in balanced metas. The card is too narrow vs control and combo to run 4, but too powerful vs creature decks to run fewer than 2.

engines.title: High Noon
engines.body: Main-deck when Lotus Field is popular (prevents the land-untap combo). Board it out in control-heavy metas where it does nothing. The main deck 1 is a hedge — if you never face Lotus, it's a low-impact card that at worst draws off Consult.

engines.title: Mana Open Discipline
engines.body: You leave the correct mana open on their turn every turn from T3 onward. T3+: hold {W}{U} for Dovin's Veto. T4+: hold {1}{W}{U} for Absorb. T5+: hold {3}{W}{W} for Supreme Verdict. You pre-plan which counter you're holding before their turn starts. You tap out ONLY when you're winning immediately.

engines.title: Supreme Verdict Threshold
engines.body: You cast Supreme Verdict at exactly 3 creatures. Below 3: use smaller answers (March of Otherworldly Light, Absorb). At 3: Verdict. You enforce this threshold strictly. Verdicting into 1-2 creatures wastes 4 mana on inefficient removal.

engines.title: Brimaz Bravery
engines.body: You attack with Brimaz every turn, regardless of their board. Brimaz 3/4 with vigilance (untaps after attack) creates a 1/1 Cat on attack. You attack into their 3/3 — Brimaz blocks back with vigilance. After 3 turns of Brimaz attacks: you have 3 Cat tokens and Brimaz untapped. You never hold Brimaz back.

engines.title: Dovin's Veto Reserve
engines.body: You save Dovin's Veto for the specific spell that wins them the game. You identify that spell before T1. Against Lotus Field: Veto on Pore Over the Pages. Against Greasefang: Veto on Greasefang the spell. Against RDW: Veto is wrong (they cast creatures) — use March instead. You match Veto to the correct target.

engines.title: Lockdown vs Verdict Decision Tree
engines.body: Temporary Lockdown: vs MV-2-or-less dominated boards (RDW, Selesnya elves, tokens). Supreme Verdict: vs boards with MV-3+ creatures (Bonecrusher Giant, Voice of Resurgence Tokens that are big, or any board where Lockdown misses something important). Farewell: vs GY-heavy or artifact-heavy situations, or as a hard reset when nothing else cleans up.

engines.title: Counter Priority Hierarchy
engines.body: Use No More Lies on: early creatures and spells when opponent has limited mana. Use Dovin's Veto on: Teferi (mirror), their Dovin's Veto, combo kill spell, sweeper that would destroy your board. Use Three Steps Ahead on: copy a planeswalker ability if you need its effect, counter if flexible, or draw 2 in late game. Never waste Dovin's Veto on a creature.

engines.title: SB vs Expected Field
engines.body: Heavy aggro (RDW, Selesnya): max Beza + Brimaz + Caracal. Heavy combo (Greasefang, Lotus): RIP + High Noon. Heavy blue (Cutter, mirror): Dovin's Veto + Brimaz for clock. Confirm your 15 matches the room. UW's sideboard is versatile — no matchup is unwinnable after siding.

engines.title: T1 Land Read
engines.body: Steam Vents/Mountain = UR Cutter or RDW (Lockdown G2). Godless Shrine = Greasefang (board RIP G2). Forest = Selesnya Company (board Brimaz, extra Lockdown). Island/Hallowed Fountain without Plains = potentially Dimir Midrange. Urborg = Lotus Field (board High Noon G2). Opponent mulliganing aggressively = likely Lotus Field or Greasefang setting up a specific hand.

engines.title: Teferi + Mana Management
engines.body: Practice the Teferi plus-untap sequence. Plus Teferi â†’ untap 2 lands â†’ hold them open for interaction. Know which 2 lands to untap for maximum flexibility on your opponent's turn.

engines.title: Supreme Verdict Timing
engines.body: Practice identifying the Supreme Verdict threshold. 3+ creatures is the default. Against Company: wait for their Company resolution (they can't counter Verdict), then sweep the board.

engines.title: Counter Priority
engines.body: Practice selecting the correct counter for each threat. Dovin's Veto vs noncreature. Absorb vs anything (3 life gain). Know which counter applies to their specific threat before holding up mana.

engines.title: Brimaz Board Building
engines.body: Practice the Brimaz board building sequence. T3 Brimaz â†’ T4 attack (2/3 + 1/1 Cat blocker). T5 attack again (two 1/1 Cats + Brimaz). Know the exact board state after 3 turns of Brimaz attacks.

AzoriusControl.game_plan: Chapter 01 Overview & Philosophy "Answer everything. Win with the last card in hand." — Core Mantra Azorius Control is a meta-dependent pick . It is not the best deck in every room — it is the best deck in the right room. That room is heavy on midrange and combo, light on fast aggro. When the RC field skews toward Jeskai Blink, Glockulous, Amulet Titan, and other fair/combo decks, UW Control is the highest equity register — specifically the Scepter-Chant lock variant that punishes interactive fields hardest. The philosophy is simple: every opponent card that resolves is a mistake. Counterspell
AzoriusControl.mulligan:
Mulligan Philosophy

Snap keep: 3–4 lands (including at least one blue source), one Counterspell or Solitude, and either Stock Up/Tune the Narrative to refuel or a second interaction piece.

engines.title: Teferi + Counter Backup
engines.body: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria resolves with Counterspell or Force of Negation in hand. +1 every turn draws a card and untaps two lands — maintaining counter backup while accruing card advantage. The game ends when they run out of resources and Teferi's emblem exiles the final permanents.

engines.title: Narset + Day's Undoing Lock
engines.body: When the Scepter lock is disrupted, Narset, Parter of Veils + Day's Undoing generates +6 net card advantage in a single action — you draw 7, they draw 1. Narset's static cannot be responded to. The game typically ends on the spot from the resulting hand disparity.

engines.title: Card Quality + Volume
engines.body: Every spell is an answer or a card draw engine. No dead cards. No situational threats. Pure card quality — every card in the 60 either stops their plan or draws more cards. Tune the Narrative banks energy passively while cantripping.

engines.title: Control — Always
engines.body: This deck never willingly becomes the beatdown. The exception: when Teferi, Time Raveler resolves, you briefly switch to pressuring them at sorcery speed while they can't respond. Otherwise: hold mana open, answer spells, generate cards, close with Teferi Hero.

engines.title: Best-in-Class At
engines.body: Best deck against combo — hard counters answer any key spell. Isochron Scepter + Orim's Chant lock completely prevents the opponent from casting spells or attacking. Supreme Verdict is the cleanest sweeper in the format — cannot be countered. Deep format knowledge produces meaningful edges in every interaction decision.

engines.title: Vulnerable To
engines.body: Boros Energy and Prowess apply pressure faster than your reactive plan sets up — aggro is a bad matchup. Tournament clock: UW games run long. RC day is 9 rounds. Slow play is a real concern. Counter wars vs Jeskai Blink require precise threat assessment — one wrong counter is often fatal. Mana base pain adds up — fetchland + shockland hits matter against aggro.

engines.title: Orim's Chant+Isochron Scepter

engines.title: Never Tap Out
engines.body: Fetchland into Island. Spell Snare open if applicable. Pass. The exception: if they are on a deck with known T1 mana dorks or cantrips that need to be answered, Prismatic Ending for {W} on a one-drop is correct. Otherwise, observe and identify their deck.

engines.title: Answer or Develop
engines.body: Counterspell their key two-drop. Or Prismatic Ending (converge 2 = hits MV 2 or less). Or Spell Snare their Counterspell if in a blue mirror. If their board is empty: Teferi, Time Raveler applies the sorcery lock at minimal cost. Never tap out below 3 mana unless the answer is worth the risk.

engines.title: Assert Control
engines.body: Teferi, Time Raveler if the coast is clear — the static sorcery lock immediately prevents their instant-speed responses. Or Supreme Verdict into a wide board. Or deploy Isochron Scepter to set up the Chant lock beginning turn 3. This is the critical turn where you establish who controls the game.

engines.title: Teferi Hero
engines.body: Deploy Teferi, Hero of Dominaria when you can hold up countermagic. +1 immediately: draw a card. At the beginning of the next end step, untap up to two lands — use those untapped lands to hold counters on their turn. Each turn Teferi survives is a +1 card advantage and threat to their entire board.

engines.title: T1 Interaction, T4 Teferi
engines.body: On the play, your T1 is interaction: Spell Snare up, Brainstorm to fix hand, or simply pass and hold mana. On the play you’re dictating tempo — pass T1 with Spell Snare mana and counter their T2 spell while developing your land base. Teferi on T3 (with mana available) locks them down before they assemble their plan.

engines.title: Extra Card Finds Force of Negation
engines.body: On the draw you see 8 cards, dramatically improving Force of Negation odds. Keep looser hands on the draw if they have 3 lands + 2 interaction pieces. Force of Negation on the draw is most valuable in the early turns when you’re behind — free counter of their key spell while developing.

engines.title: Snapcaster Rebuys
engines.body: Teferi killed: opponents interact at instant speed again. Hold Cryptic Command mana open (tap all their creatures before their attack step). Snapcaster Mage rebuy Counterspell or Day’s Undoing for hand refill. The control plan still functions without Teferi — it just requires more mana efficiency.

engines.title: Brainstorm + Force Holds
engines.body: Blood Moon or Spreading Seas disrupts your mana. Pivot: Force of Negation handles the key threats for free. Brainstorm shuffles bad draws away. Keep basic lands in hand until Blood Moon is answered with Prismatic Ending or Cryptic Command bounce.

engines.title: Your Reactive Stance
engines.body: You hold up interaction every single turn. Dovin's Veto ({W}{U} uncounterable noncreature counter), Absorb ({1}{W}{U} counter + 3 life), and Temporary Lockdown ({2}{W} exile MV ≤ 2) are your primary three plays. Your game plan is: answer their threat, hold mana open, untap, answer their next threat. You never commit a threat you can't protect until you're ahead on resources.

engines.title: Your Resource Denial
engines.body: Narset, Parter of Veils prevents opponents from drawing additional cards. You deploy Narset when they tap for their draw-heavy spell (Collected Company, Pore Over the Pages). Under Narset: their Opt draws 0 extra cards, their Company hits but draws 0, their Pore draws only their main card. You follow Narset with a threat they must spend removal on instead of their draw engine.

engines.title: Your Card Engine
engines.body: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria pluses to draw a card and untap two lands — you end up with +1 card AND more mana than you started with. Each Teferi activation draws you deeper while maintaining interaction. Your T5+ is: Teferi plus → draw card → two lands untap → hold mana for counter. You generate advantage while keeping interaction open simultaneously.

engines.title: Your Reset Button
engines.body: Supreme Verdict ({2}{W}{W}) can't be countered. You deploy it when they have 3+ creatures and you need a clean board. After Verdict resolves, you untap with an empty board and (usually) a full hand. You immediately deploy your first threat after Verdict — Brimaz if you have him, or Teferi if you need more resources first. Their board is zero; yours is about to be something.

engines.title: Teferi + Sorcery Speed Lock
engines.body: Teferi, Time Raveler’s static locks opponents to sorcery speed. While Teferi is in play: deploy your sorceries (Supreme Verdict, Day’s Undoing) at instant speed during their end step. +1 bounces their permanent. Protect Teferi as your primary engine — every turn he survives is a free card advantage and tempo loss for them.

engines.title: Cryptic Command Value Chain
engines.body: Cryptic Command with 2 modes (counter+draw, tap all+draw) is your primary card advantage and board control piece. Counter their best spell AND draw a card. Tap all their creatures before attacks AND draw a card. Use Snapcaster Mage to flash back Cryptic for a second set of 2 modes. The Command + Snapcaster chain generates +2 cards per cycle.

engines.title: Day’s Undoing + Teferi
engines.body: Day’s Undoing: each player shuffles hand + GY into library and draws 7. THEN the turn ends. With Teferi in play: cast Undoing during their turn (Teferi gives you flash for sorceries until your next turn). You draw 7, the turn ends before they can cast anything with their new 7 cards. This is the game-winning draw refuel when your hand is empty.

engines.title: Full Refuel at Instant Speed
engines.body: Teferi in play (gives sorceries flash until your next turn). Their turn: cast Day’s Undoing at instant speed. Both players shuffle and draw 7. End step occurs (Day’s Undoing ends the turn). They have 7 new cards but no mana. You have 7 new cards going into your untap. This is a complete hand refuel with no opportunity for them to use their new hand.

engines.title: Sweeper at Instant Speed
engines.body: Teferi in play. Their attack step: wait until they declare attackers. Cast Supreme Verdict at instant speed (sorcery, but Teferi gives flash) before damage. Sweeper resolves, all creatures die including your own (but you have no creatures). This timing denies them combat damage AND sweeps at instant speed. Standard UW Control sequencing.

engines.title: How Fast Do You Win?
engines.body: Celestial Colonnade (3/4 flying creature land): attacks for 3 every turn. From 20 life: 7 attack steps. That’s your default clock. With Day’s Undoing refueling, you can protect Colonnade for 7 attacks. Accelerate with Teferi ultimate: −10 creates 2/2 Wizard tokens for every instant/sorcery in your GY.

engines.title: Your Card Engine
engines.body: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria pluses to draw a card and untap two lands simultaneously. Your payoff: you end each Teferi turn with more mana available than you started with. You generate card advantage while maintaining interaction capability. Your loop: Teferi plus → draw → untap two → hold {W}{U} open for Dovin's Veto on their response → repeat. You protect Teferi and generate advantage until your b

engines.title: Your Resource Denial
engines.body: Narset, Parter of Veils prevents opponents from drawing additional cards. You deploy Narset when they're about to draw multiple cards (their Collected Company triggers, their draw engine). Your payoff: their Opt draws 0 extra, their Company hits creatures but draws 0. You protect Narset with Absorb or Dovin's Veto on their removal. The Narset lock combined with Teferi advantage wins through pure c

engines.title: Your Sustain Counter
engines.body: Absorb ({1}{W}{U}) counters any spell AND gains you 3 life. You use Absorb on their most threatening non-creature spell when the 3 life matters for your survival math. Your payoff: you counter their spell AND sustain your life total simultaneously. You never Absorb a cantrip — you Absorb their best spell. The 3 life from Absorb is often the margin that lets Teferi tick up one more time.

engines.title: Your Board Clear
engines.body: Supreme Verdict ({2}{W}{W}) can't be countered AND destroys all creatures. You deploy it when their board has 3+ creatures threatening lethal. Your payoff: clean board + they can't counter it. You immediately deploy your first threat after Verdict (Brimaz, Teferi, or Narset). You never Verdict into 1-2 creatures — you wait for the threshold where Verdict generates card advantage.

engines.title: Force of Negation is NOT Free On Your Turn
engines.body: Force of Negation can only be cast for its alternate cost (exile a blue card) if it is NOT your turn. On your own turn, you must pay {1}{U}{U}. This is the most common rules error with Force. If you’re in your own main phase or combat, Force costs full mana. This means you cannot Force your opponent’s response to your own Wrath of God on your turn — you’d need to pay {1}{U}{U}. Hold Force for thei

engines.title: Teferi +1 Lets You Cast Spells at Flash Speed
engines.body: Teferi, Time Raveler’s +1 says "until your next turn, you may cast sorcery spells as though they had flash." This lets you cast Supreme Verdict, Day’s Undoing, and other sorceries at instant speed until your next turn. Cast Verdict during their end step after they’ve committed their board. Cast Day’s Undoing during their upkeep when they have no mana. The +1 also bounces a noncreature, nonland per

engines.title: Cryptic Command: Use the Return Mode
engines.body: Cryptic Command’s 4 modes: counter spell, return permanent, tap all creatures, draw a card. The return mode is the most underused: Counter + Return bounces your own Snapcaster Mage to rebuy a spell AND counters their response in one Cryptic. Tap All + Return resets their board AND bounces a threat. Return your own Vendilion Clique mid-combat to get another ETB (see their hand again). Know all 6 tw

engines.title: Your Dovin's Veto Timing
engines.body: You save Dovin's Veto for their uncounterable threats: Supreme Verdict (their board wipe), Indomitable Creativity (their combo piece), any spell that wins them the game on resolution. You never Veto a cantrip or a creature — Absorb handles those. You identify their key spell and keep {W}{U} open specifically for it. Veto is uncounterable itself — it always resolves.

engines.title: Your Narset Lock
engines.body: You deploy Narset, Parter of Veils when they're about to draw extra cards. Their Opt draws nothing extra. Their Pore Over the Pages draws nothing extra. Their Company hits creatures but draws nothing. You protect Narset with your remaining interaction. The lock combined with a clock (Teferi, Brimaz) closes the game while they can't draw into answers.

engines.title: Your Teferi Minus Line
engines.body: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria's −3 puts a permanent on top of their library. You use the −3 on their most dangerous permanent: Sheoldred, Kalitas, a resolved Creativity threat. "On top of library" means they draw it next turn — not back to hand. You follow the −3 with your own clock (Brimaz attack). They must redraw the removed permanent and cast it again.

engines.title: Your Approach Closing
engines.body: Approach of the Second Sun ({6}{W}): you cast it first (costs 6). Next turn, you draw and cast it again for 7 life gain. Your goal: cast Approach on T7, survive one more turn, draw and cast Approach again on T8. You protect yourself with counters during the intervening turn. You never cast Approach unless you can cast it again next turn — never waste the first cast.

engines.title: Scepter Lock Is Online
engines.body: Isochron Scepter with Orim's Chant imprinted and Teferi, Time Raveler in play: stop drawing and passing. Deploy your win condition — Teferi Hero, Jace, Wan Shi Tong. Tap Scepter each upkeep to prevent their main phase. The lock is established, now close the game before they draw Force of Vigor.

engines.title: They Have Answers in Hand
engines.body: You know they have Force of Negation or Consign to Memory from a Thoughtseize or scry. Hold Teferi Hero until they tap out on their turn. Use Teferi Time Raveler +1 to set up sorcery-speed Wrath timing. Don't walk your win condition into open mana — one free counter ends the game.

engines.title: Their Hand Is Unknown
engines.body: You've had no information on their hand since T1. They've been drawing and holding. Scry before deploying Teferi Hero — a Day's Undoing or cantrip first to see what's coming. Deploying a 5-mana threat into a completely unknown hand is the most common loss condition for UW Control pilots.

engines.title: Combo Deck Across the Table
engines.body: Facing Storm, Living End, Neoform, Amulet Titan: abandon the draw-go plan. Lead Chalice of the Void at 0 (stops cascade) or Vexing Bauble early. Deploy Orim's Chant each turn. Force every spell they try to resolve. Tap Scepter on their upkeep. The prison is your gameplan vs combo — not the control gameplan.

engines.title: Spell Snare/Tune the Narrative
engines.body: Both flex based on the meta. Spell Snare : powerful vs midrange and mirrors (stops 2-drop threats). Swap up when blue decks dominate. Tune the Narrative : energy banking for Wrath of Skies, doubles as a cantrip. Swap more in when combo is present. (hits Counterspell , Teferi TRav, Expressive Iteration). Swap toward Snare when blue decks dominate. Currently: 2 of each is the balanced call.

engines.title: Consign to Memory/Wrath of the Skies(SB) Count
engines.body: Consign to Memory (3x SB) is for combo and triggered-ability-heavy fields (Glockulous, Titan, Affinity). Wrath of the Skies (2x SB) is for creature and artifact flood. Currently 3+2 split. If artifacts aren't present, add a second Vendilion Clique or Celestial Purge (exiles red/black permanents including Archon of Cruelty ). Meta-read this every RC cycle.

engines.title: Subtlety / Lórien Revealed
engines.body: Subtlety ({3}{U}{U}, pitch blue card, evoke: return target noncreature nonland spell to owner's hand) delays key spells and provides a 3/3 flash body. Testing it when combo is light and ETB denial matters less than hand disruption. Lórien Revealed ({3}{U}{U}: draw 3, can be cycled as an Island) is pure card selection — testing as a 1-of over second Tune the Narrative for additional non-redundant c

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Fair interactive field where Supreme Verdict and Teferi invalidate their gameplan. Combo decks present (Storm, Living End) — Force of Negation + Day’s Undoing generate inevitability. Low threat density — Celestial Colonnade clock reaches lethal without racing pressure. You’ve practiced the Day’s Undoing + Teferi timing for all expected matchups.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy Blood Moon field — your nonbasic lands become Mountains, breaking blue mana. Multiple Amulet Titan builds (T3 kill is faster than your Teferi on T3). Very fast aggro field where 5-toughness threats come down T1-2 and Supreme Verdict is too slow. You haven’t practiced the Cryptic Command mode selection for specific matchups.

engines.title: Verdict Backup
engines.body: Practice never tapping out before T4. Every rep: hold mana, hold Verdict, hold Verdict.

engines.title: FoN Targets
engines.body: Drill which spells deserve Force of Negation. Counter the win condition, not the setup.

engines.title: TRav Deployment
engines.body: Practice when to deploy TRav vs hold up countermagic. One-sided sorcery lock is strong but you need mana.

engines.title: G2 RiP Timing
engines.body: Drill playing Rest in Peace the first safe turn. Late RiP loses to rebuilt graveyards.
