GolgariYawgmoth.game_plan: Chapter 01 Deck Identity "The deck has two modes: fair creature midrange that grinds with Collected Company and Chord of Calling, and an infinite combo engine that kills on the spot. You're always one Chord of Calling away from either finding the missing combo piece or closing the game." Golgari Yawgmoth is a creature combo deck built around Yawgmoth, Thran Physician and the undying mechanic. The infinite loop requires Yawgmoth, two creatures with undying (like Young Wolf + Geralf's Messenger), and Melira, Sylvok Outcast : Melira prevents -1/-1 counters from being placed on your creatures. Und
GolgariYawgmoth.mulligan:
Mulligan Framework
Keep
Tutor + 2 Lands + Creatures
Any hand with a Chord of Calling, Eldritch Evolution, or Collected Company + 2 lands + early creatures is a keep.

engines.title: Yawgmoth + Melira + 2 Undying
engines.body: Yawgmoth + Melira + Young Wolf + Geralf's Messenger + Blood Artist. Sacrifice Wolf: -1/-1 counter prevented (Melira), Wolf dies with no counters, returns (undying). Draw a card. Target opponent with -1/-1. Sacrifice Messenger: same. Repeat infinitely. Blood Artist drains 1 per death = infinite life loss.

engines.title: Melira + 1 Undying = Infinite
engines.body: With Melira in play, even ONE undying creature is enough for the infinite loop: sacrifice it, -1/-1 counter is prevented, it dies with no counters, returns with +1/+1 (undying), sacrifice again. Each loop: draw a card, place -1/-1 on a target. You need a drain outlet (Blood Artist) to convert this into a kill. Without a drain outlet, you can draw your whole deck.

engines.title: Chord + Evolution + CoCo
engines.body: Chord of Calling (instant, convoke) finds any creature at sorcery speed. Eldritch Evolution (sorcery) sacrifices a creature to find one with MV ≤ sacrifice MV + 2. Collected Company hits up to two creatures with MV ≤ 3 at instant speed. The density of creature tutors makes the combo reliably findable by turn 3–4 even without opening the pieces.

engines.title: Beats Without Combo
engines.body: When the combo is disrupted, the deck plays fair: Young Wolf and Geralf's Messenger are resilient threats (undying makes them permanent value). Hapatra, Vizier of Poisons creates Snake tokens when -1/-1 counters are placed. Yawgmoth's protection from Humans makes him hard to answer with the most common removal. The midrange plan is often enough to win against unprepared opponents.

engines.title: Protection From Humans
engines.body: Yawgmoth has protection from Humans — not from creatures in general, not from black. Many players incorrectly try to target Yawgmoth with Solitude (exiles a creature) or Swords to Plowshares (exile a creature). Protection means: can't be blocked, targeted, dealt damage, or enchanted by Humans. Solitude and StP are Human spells/effects from non-Human permanents — they CAN target Yawgmoth.

engines.title: 2.0% · Resilient Specialist
engines.body: Golgari Yawgmoth has been a Modern staple since Yawgmoth's printing. Low meta share reflects the narrow meta slot but consistent performance. Strong against creature-based midrange, weak against Clarion Conqueror (shuts activated abilities) and fast combo that kills before the loop assembles. A skilled pilot wins matchups others lose.

engines.title: {2}{B}{B} · 2/4 Legendary
engines.body: Protection from Humans. Pay 1 life, sacrifice another creature: put a -1/-1 counter on up to one target creature and draw a card. {B}{B}, discard a card: proliferate. The sacrifice ability is an ACTIVATED ability (cost: pay life + sacrifice). Clarion Conqueror shuts this off completely. Yawgmoth can activate the turn he enters — no summoning sickness on activated abilities. Protection from Humans:

engines.title: {1}{G} · 2/2 Legendary
engines.body: You can't get poison counters. Creatures you control can't have -1/-1 counters placed on them. The "can't have counters placed" clause is what enables the loop — when Yawgmoth tries to place a -1/-1 counter on the undying creature (as part of his activation cost — wait, the counter IS placed on a target creature, not on the creature being sacrificed). Key: Yawgmoth places -1/-1 on "up to one targe

engines.title: Returns With +1/+1 Counter
engines.body: When this creature dies, if it had no +1/+1 counters on it, return it to the battlefield under its owner's control with a +1/+1 counter on it. In the loop: the undying creature is sacrificed to Yawgmoth (not targeted, just sacrificed). Yawgmoth places a -1/-1 counter on a target (which can be the opposing creature, or another target). The undying creature died with no counters (Melira blocks -1/-1

engines.title: {1}{B} · 0/1 Vampire
engines.body: Whenever this creature OR another creature dies, target player loses 1 life and you gain 1 life. Blood Artist triggers on ANY creature dying — including your own undying creatures. Each infinite loop iteration: one creature death = Blood Artist trigger = 1 life loss for opponent. Infinite loops = infinite drain. With two Blood Artists: 2 life per loop. Compare Zulaport Cutthroat: triggers only on

engines.title: {1}{G}{G} · Sorcery
engines.body: Sacrifice a creature. Search for a creature with MV ≤ sacrifice MV + 2. Sacrifice Young Wolf (MV 1): find MV ≤ 3. Can find Melira (MV 2), Hapatra (MV 2), Grist (MV 3), Bloodline Cultivator (MV 3). CANNOT find Yawgmoth (MV 4). Sacrifice Geralf's Messenger (MV 3): find MV ≤ 5. Can find Yawgmoth (MV 4), Nissa (MV 4), or Endurance (MV 3). The tutor chain: Evolution on Wolf → Melira. Evolution on Messe

engines.title: {1}{B}{G} · Legendary Planeswalker
engines.body: Grist is a creature in all zones except the battlefield. This means Chord of Calling and Collected Company can find him (both look for "creature cards"). Grist's +1: each opponent mills 1, you create a 1/1 Insect if a creature was milled. −2: destroy target creature with MV ≤ number of Insects you control. −5: each opponent loses life equal to the number of creature cards in their GY. A planeswalk

engines.title: Tutor + 2 Lands + Creatures
engines.body: Any hand with a Chord of Calling, Eldritch Evolution, or Collected Company + 2 lands + early creatures is a keep. The tutors find any missing combo piece by turn 3–4. You don't need to open with all 4 combo pieces — you just need the infrastructure to find them.

engines.title: Wolf + Messenger + Yawgmoth Line
engines.body: Wolf T1 + Messenger T3 + Yawgmoth (from Evolution on Messenger) T4 is the baseline gold standard. If your hand has the first two pieces and 4 mana available (Eldritch Evolution on Messenger costs {1}{G}{G} + 3 lands to cast Messenger), this is a clean line.

engines.title: No Tutors + No Undying
engines.body: Hands with Yawgmoth + Melira but no undying creatures and no tutors cannot win — they need the undying part of the combo. Hands with all undying but no Yawgmoth and no tutors are just attacking with small creatures. Both are mulligans.

engines.title: Prioritize Disruption Hands
engines.body: On the draw against known fast combo (Ruby Storm, Living End, Amulet Titan): keep hands with Thoughtseize (SB) or disruption. Post-board, disruption hands take priority over pure combo speed — the opponent is likely faster than you in game 1 if you're drawing second.

engines.title: Auto-Keep Conditions
engines.body: Undying creature + black source + any tutor. Young Wolf or Strangleroot Geist + Evolution/Chord/CoCo = you can assemble the combo. Keep. Two undying creatures + 2 lands. You’ll find the tutors. Keep. CoCo + 3 lands + undying creature. Blind CoCo hits Melira + Yawgmoth often enough. Keep.

engines.title: Auto-Ship Conditions
engines.body: No undying creatures AND no tutors. You can’t assemble the combo without an undying creature. Ship. No black source. Can’t cast Yawgmoth, Evolution, or Thoughtseize. Ship. No creatures at all. Tutors without bodies to find are dead cards. Ship.

engines.title: Context-Dependent
engines.body: Yawgmoth + 2 lands, no undying: Keep vs slow midrange, ship vs aggro (need the blocker on T1). All tutors, no threats: Keep on draw (extra card finds the body), ship on play vs aggro. Six-card hands: Keep any 6 with undying + tutor + 2 mana sources.

engines.title: T1 Wolf, T4 Combo
engines.body: T1 Young Wolf establishes the blocker and combo piece simultaneously. T2 Bloodline Cultivator (mana filter). T3 Evolution into Geralf’s Messenger (3/2 zombie = more undying bodies). T4 Chord for Yawgmoth. This is your cleanest line. On the play: never skip T1 Young Wolf if it’s in hand — it’s too important for blocking AND combo.

engines.title: T1 Wolf Still Correct
engines.body: The extra draw can find Melira, Blood Artist, or a missing combo piece. T1 Wolf is still correct. On the draw: you can keep slightly more speculative hands (6-land hands with CoCo) since you see more cards. T2 CoCo is a strong line on draw — you’ve seen 8 cards and CoCo hits roughly 60% of the time with the right deck configuration.

engines.title: Rebuild via Chord
engines.body: They Solitude or Path your Yawgmoth: don’t immediately recast. First assess: do you have 2 undying creatures and Melira still in play? If yes, Chord for Yawgmoth again next turn. If no, spend the turn rebuilding the creature base with CoCo or Evolution before tutoring Yawgmoth again.

engines.title: Pivot to Beatdown
engines.body: Rest in Peace or Grafdigger’s Cage shuts off undying. Pivot to CoCo fair value plan: undying creatures still attack and block profitably. Yawgmoth is still a 2/4 that draws cards. Melira + Blood Artist can race in this mode. Find Haywire Mite from SB to clear the hate piece before going back to combo.

engines.title: Full Combo Loop
engines.body: Yawgmoth + Melira + 2 undying + Blood Artist. This is the win condition. Execute the loop: sacrifice undying creature → puts -1/-1 on opponent → Blood Artist drains 1 → undying returns → repeat. Infinite life drain, infinite -1/-1. If you have all four pieces, execute. Don’t wait for a “better” turn.

engines.title: Yawgmoth Draw Engine
engines.body: Yawgmoth + 2 undying creatures (no Blood Artist yet). Sacrifice undying → draw a card → undying returns → sacrifice again. This cycles through your deck for Blood Artist or Melira. You’re not winning yet but you’re finding the missing piece. Activate this as soon as Yawgmoth is in play with 2 undying bodies.

engines.title: Fair Creature Plan
engines.body: CoCo or Chord for value creatures when the combo is disrupted. Undying creatures still attack and block profitably. Yawgmoth is a 2/4 that draws a card per {1}{B} activation. Melira + Blood Artist generate incremental drain. You can win games entirely fair. This is not a surrender — it’s a different route to the same destination.

engines.title: Evolution Chain
engines.body: T1: Young Wolf. T2: Bloodline Cultivator (filter {G} to {B}). T2 also: discard to get Messenger in GY (if CoCo plan). T3: Eldritch Evolution sacrificing Wolf → find Geralf’s Messenger (3/2 undying). Evolution again → find Melira. Chord → find Blood Artist. Needs: Evolution + Wolf T1 + Messenger + Melira + Blood Artist accessible. Rare but real.

engines.title: The Default Line
engines.body: T1: Young Wolf. T2: Bloodline Cultivator. T3: Eldritch Evolution sacrificing Wolf → find Geralf’s Messenger. OR CoCo for Melira + undying. T4: Chord for Yawgmoth ({4} with 4 creatures) OR second Evolution → Melira → Chord → Yawgmoth. This is your baseline. If you can’t kill T4, something went wrong or they disrupted.

engines.title: When to Wait
engines.body: Rush T3: They’re on Storm, Amulet Titan, or Living End — any deck that wins T3 themselves. Force the issue. Wait for T4: They have open mana for Solitude or Force of Negation. Cast Thoughtseize T3 to clear the counterspell, then execute T4 cleanly. Don’t walk Chord into Solitude.

engines.title: Exiled Creatures Don’t Trigger Undying
engines.body: Undying triggers on death — meaning the creature goes to the graveyard. Solitude, Path to Exile, and Prismatic Ending EXILE the creature. Exiled creatures skip the graveyard, so undying doesn’t trigger. Your Young Wolf stays dead permanently when Pathed. Galvanic Discharge deals damage (they die normally, undying works). Know the difference.

engines.title: Yawgmoth Can Target ANY Creature
engines.body: Yawgmoth says “target creature.” That’s any creature — yours OR theirs. You can put -1/-1 counters on their creatures by sacrificing one of your undying creatures. Kill their 1/1 tokens. Run a 3/3 down to a 2/2 before blocks. Draw a card doing it. This is not a rare line — use Yawgmoth actively to answer their threats while assembling your combo.

engines.title: Protect Melira — She’s the Loop
engines.body: Melira prevents -1/-1 counters on creatures YOU control. If Melira is removed between loop activations, the next undying creature returns WITH a -1/-1 counter and immediately dies as a 0/0, breaking the loop. Protect Melira above Yawgmoth. A Melira + 2 undying board without Yawgmoth still wins with one Chord. A Yawgmoth board without Melira is just a draw engine.

engines.title: Yawgmoth + 2 Undying Creatures
engines.body: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician in play. Two undying creatures — typically Young Wolf (1/1) and Strangleroot Geist (2/1 haste). One has a +1/+1 counter from undying, one doesn't. Sacrifice the creature WITHOUT the counter. Put the -1/-1 counter on the creature WITH the +1/+1 counter. Counters cancel via CR 122.3. The sacrificed creature returns via undying with a fresh +1/+1. Repeat. Each cycle: draw 1

engines.title: Blood Artist / Zulaport / Geralf's Messenger
engines.body: With Blood Artist : each sacrifice = opponent loses 1, you gain 1. Life gain offsets Yawgmoth's payment. Draw your entire deck, opponent loses life = your starting total. With Geralf's Messenger as an undying creature: each return = "target opponent loses 2 life." Messenger enters TAPPED (can't block), but drain stacks infinitely. With Zulaport Cutthroat : same as Artist but "each opponent" — can'

engines.title: Combo Window Is Closed
engines.body: Yawgmoth has been answered twice. They have Solitude + open mana. GY hate is in play and you haven’t found Haywire Mite. In these scenarios: CoCo for value, undying bodies in combat, Yawgmoth draw engine (not loop). You can still win — just differently.

engines.title: The Window Re-Opens
engines.body: GY hate gets answered (Haywire Mite / Force of Vigor). Their hand is empty from your Thoughtseizes. They tap out for a threat. When the window opens again, immediately pivot back to assembling the 4-piece loop. Don’t stay in fair mode out of habit — the combo is always the better line when available.

engines.title: You Have 4 Pieces
engines.body: Yawgmoth + Melira + 2 undying + Blood Artist all in play. Execute the loop. There is no scenario where you should delay the win — they can draw Solitude on their next draw step. Activate Yawgmoth on your main phase, drain them to 0.

engines.title: Opponent Is Faster
engines.body: Storm goldfishes T3. Amulet Titan goldfishes T3. Living End goes off T3. When facing decks that win T3, don’t wait for the perfect hand. Chord for Yawgmoth on T3 with whatever you have and hope for the best. A 60% T3 kill is better than a 95% T4 kill when they’re T3 themselves.

engines.title: Green Lights
engines.body: Midrange-heavy field (Boros Energy, Domain Zoo, Amulet) — you combo through their interaction. Exile-based removal is below 15% of SB cards in the room (Path, Solitude). No Surgical Extraction in the metagame. You’ve practiced the T3 execution blindfolded. The field has few Grafdigger’s Cage or Leyline of the Void builds.

engines.title: Red Lights
engines.body: Heavy exile removal in the field (Solitude and Path on every SB). Surgical Extraction is common — one copy targeting Young Wolf ends your game. Chalice of the Void at 1 shuts off Young Wolf, Haywire Mite, and Chord. You haven’t practiced the draw-engine line (Yawgmoth without Blood Artist) — you’ll mismanage your undying creature count under pressure.

engines.title: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician ×4
engines.body: Your entire combo engine. Four copies non-negotiable — the deck is named after this card.

engines.title: Young Wolf ×4
engines.body: Your Undying enabler. Young Wolf + Yawgmoth + another Undying creature generates infinite loops. Four copies ensures the combo is online.

engines.title: Strangleroot Geist
engines.body: 3 in most metas. 4 when you need faster aggressive starts — Geist as a 2/1 haste with Undying applies early pressure. Cut to 2 in slower metas where its haste is irrelevant.

engines.title: Thoughtseize (SB)
engines.body: 2 in combo-heavy metas where stripping their key piece T1 wins the game. Cut entirely in creature-based metas where their threats are on the board, not in their hand.

engines.title: Grist, the Hunger Tide count
engines.body: 2 as a findable threat via Chord of Calling. Grist's -1 kills a creature AND mills a card (helping fill GY for Yawgmoth). 3 in grindy metas where card advantage matters more than speed.

engines.title: Combo Loop
engines.body: Drill the Yawgmoth loop until it's mechanical: sacrifice, -1/-1 counter, draw, undying returns, loop.

engines.title: CoCo Timing
engines.body: Practice casting Collected Company at opponents' EOT. Know exactly what you can and can't find.

engines.title: Protect Yawgmoth
engines.body: Practice keeping disruption specifically for Yawgmoth protection. He's the only piece that matters.

engines.title: G2 Hate Lines
engines.body: Practice through Grafdigger's Cage (stops Persist/CoCo), Solitude, and Endurance.

engines.title: Yawgmoth + Melira + Undying + Drain
engines.body: Yawgmoth (activated ability: pay life, sacrifice, -1/-1, draw) + Melira (prevents -1/-1 on your creatures) + 1 undying creature (Young Wolf, Geralf's Messenger) + Blood Artist or Zulaport Cutthroat. Missing any one = no infinite loop. But missing just Melira = still functional midrange.

engines.title: Wolf → Melira → Chord → Yawgmoth
engines.body: T1 Young Wolf. T3 Eldritch Evolution (sacrifice Wolf MV1 → find Melira MV≤3). T4+ Chord of Calling X=4 with convoke from tapping creatures → find Yawgmoth. Blood Artist in play = combo active. Instant-speed Chord at EOT is the clean kill line.
